- If the interface is missing a menu such as Manage programs or Growth, the account may be in a Google test. Contact Merchant Center support, state the missing menu, and ask to be removed from the test or shown where to find it. (2023) [L0970.119]

#### Fields in About your business
- The About your business page contains: Business display name, Business address (Address line 1, Address line 2, City, State/Province, Postal/ZIP code, Country), Phone number, Website, and Customer service contact (URL, E-mail, Phone). (older, 2021-22) [L0730.020, L0727.026]
- Click Save after entering the address. Complete the phone verification and customer service contact in the same tab. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.020]
- The page for Shopping ads customer service contact fields is: Website, E-mail and Phone. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.006]

#### Business display name
- Keep the business name equal to the store name, and do not change it. [L0729.005]
- Changing the business display name requires re-submitting product data before the new name takes effect. (older, 2021-22) [L0727.027, L0730.021]

#### Business address
- The registered business address must match where the business is actually set up. A sole proprietor uses their home address, while an LLC may enter a business address. The address is not shown to customers. [L0729.006]
- **Sources differ:** L0729.006 and L0181.008 accept a home address for a sole proprietor. A 2020 unit reports that a residential home address on a Merchant Center account or website may cause problems, with one reported case asking for photos of a warehouse. The cause is not confirmed, so use a commercial address such as a UPS store address where possible. (older, 2020) [L0729.006, L0181.008, L1111.177]
- The business address entered in Business information must match exactly the address shown on the website. A mismatch can lead to a Merchant Center suspension. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.001]
- The address in Merchant Center must be the same as the address shown on the Shopify store and on the business documents. (2024) [L0971.066]

#### Phone number
- The phone number entered in Merchant Center must match the number on the website and must be verified. An unverified number can lead to a Merchant Center suspension. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.002]
- Enter the business phone number under Business information, which must match the phone number on the website. (older, 2021-22) [L0727.015]
- After a phone number is entered, it shows an **Unverified** label until verified. The **Verify number** button starts the process. The phone field uses a country code prefix (for an Australian store, +61), and the example format is (02) 1234 5678. The verification method screen has a **Change my number** link to correct the number before a code is sent. The website URL also shows an **Unverified** label. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.022]

#### Customer service contact
- For Shopping ads, enter the contact-us page URL, the customer service email and the business phone number. The phone number should match the one on the website. (older, 2021-22) [L0727.016]
- The Customer service contact for Shopping ads (Business information > Customer service contact) takes the contact-us page URL, a support email and the verified business phone number. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.006]

#### Consistency across the store
- Information entered in Merchant Center (prices, tax, shipping, contact details, policies) must match the website exactly at all times. If it does not match, Google can suspend the account. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.003]
- Merchant Center tax rate, shipping policy, return policy and contact information must match what the store shows. Mismatches can lead to limited performance or suspension for misrepresentation. (2023) [L0804.047]

### Phone verification

Steps (older, 2021-22):
1. Open Business information > About your business and click **Verify number**. [L0730.003]
2. Choose **Voice call** or **Text message**. For most phone providers, choose **Voice call**, because text messages often do not reach business numbers. [L0730.003]
3. The automated call reads a verification code. Enter the code in the field, then click **Continue**. The status changes to Verified. [L0730.003]
4. Enter the code exactly as heard. The code is a six-character code of letters and digits, not only digits. [L0730.005]
5. Enter the business phone number under Business information, then click **Verify number**, choose **Voice call** (text messages often do not work for business numbers), then enter the six-digit alphanumeric code from the automated call. [L0727.015]

Why it matters:
- Google verifies the phone number so it can confirm the business is reachable through the customer service number and that the account owner is genuine. Skipping verification makes Google suspect the account owner is not the real business owner. (older, 2021-22) [L0730.004]
- Phone verification confirms the business owner and ensures customer contact works. (older, 2021-22) [L0727.015]

### Branding

- Branding is optional. Leaving it empty does not cause suspension. [L0727.028, L0730.008]
- If you fill it in, the main color should match the background color of your logo, and the accent color should differ from the main color. [L0727.028]
- Logos only appear after Google approves them, and only in some Shopping ad placements, not all. [L0727.028, L0730.008]
- Branding is found under Business information > Branding. [L0730.008]
- Set up branding: open Branding, upload the logo, choose the accent color, and upload the square logo and rectangular logo. Shopping actions branding is not needed while Shopping actions is not used. [L0728.016]
- Merchant Center preferences: enable receiving opportunities to get Google's improvement suggestions. You can also upload a business logo, which Google may show during shopping sessions. [L0732.012]

Branding requirements:

| Element | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Square logo format | PNG or SVG | L0727.017, L0730.008 |
| Maximum file size | 5 MB | L0727.017, L0730.008 |
| Dimensions | Minimum 500 x 500 pixels, maximum 2,000 x 2,000 pixels | L0727.017, L0730.008 |
| Ratio, square logo | 1:1 | L0727.017, L0730.008 |
| Rectangular logo | Also uploaded; appears on small screens | L0730.008 |
| Main color | Matches the logo background color; hex format (for example #FFFFFF) or rgba | L0730.008, L0727.028 |
| Accent color | Optional; must differ from the main color | L0730.008, L0727.028 |

(older, 2021-22 for all rows above except where noted in the source list; the L0728.016 and L0732.012 units are undated or from Source A)

### Tax

- Enter your tax configuration under the tax section, using the tax categories that match your situation. The setup depends on where you are registered and sell. [L0732.010]
- Tax setup: go to the tax section and choose **Configure no nexus for all states**, then click **Save**. Choose this only if the business is not set up with tax nexus in its registered state. The tax setup should mirror the tax settings configured in Shopify. [L0728.003]
- For Google Shopping tax, set your store and Merchant Center tax rates to zero if the business is incorporated outside the US, so the product price does not appear higher than competitors' taxed prices. (2023) [L0964.063]
- **Sources differ:** L0728.003 sets no nexus when the business has no nexus in its registered state and mirrors Shopify. L0964.063 sets zero rates when the business is incorporated outside the US. Both apply to their own situation as stated. [L0728.003, L0964.063]
- Tax and shipping are labelled optional in the free listings setup, but for this business model they were treated as required. The steps are completed in order, with Website and Products following tax and shipping. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.009]

### Shipping

#### Shipping service setup
- Shipping setup: click the plus icon, enter a shipping service name (for example "domestic shipping"), select only the countries you ship to, set the order cutoff time, and set the handling time. [L0728.005]
- Set the handling time in Eastern time. For free shipping, enter a service named free shipping as well. It is required even when shipping is free. [L0728.005]
- **Sources differ on time zone:** L0728.005 gives Eastern time for handling time in the example. L0728.020 says the cutoff is set in the time zone used for the account, and L0726.005 says the time zone is the business's. [L0728.005, L0728.020, L0726.005]
- Enter shipping information even when shipping is free, because a shipping setup is mandatory for Shopping ads eligibility. [L0728.006]
- Set the shipping rates for each destination, set shipping time zones and whether shipping is free. Shipping settings are found in the shipping section of Merchant Center. [L0732.011]
- A default shipping rate must be set up for every country you sell to, and a default shipping method must be selected. Merchant Center shows a warning when a country has no default shipping rate. [L0732.009]

Procedure to set up a shipping service (older, 2021-22):
1. Click **Add shipping service**. [L0731.010]
2. Enter a name for the service (for example Australia shipping or US shipping). [L0731.010]
3. Select the country. [L0731.010]
4. Select the service area, which is the delivery destination (the customer's address). [L0731.010]
5. Select the currency, matching the currency used for the business and the delivery location. [L0731.010]
6. Click **Next**. [L0731.010]
7. Enter the order cutoff time (optional), handling time and transit time under Delivery times. [L0731.010]
8. Click **Next**. [L0731.010]
9. Keep the default free shipping rate. [L0731.010]
10. Click **Save**. [L0731.010]

#### Choosing the countries
- Select only the countries where you actually sell in Merchant Center. Shipping and return details are then set up for each selected country. [L0729.007]
- Select only the countries in the shipping destination list that you actually ship to, because the setting controls where Shopping ads may be shown. [L0728.007]

#### Handling and transit times

Sources give different values for different cases. Use the case that matches the store.

| Case | Handling time | Transit time | When it applies | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Example store (policy: processing 3 to 5 days, maximum 5; typical delivery 3 to 7 days, up to 12) | 1 to 5 days | 1 to 12 days | The store's own policy text, entered manually | L0729.009 |
| Print-on-demand products | 2 to 4 days, Monday through Saturday | Not stated | Print-on-demand fulfilment | L0728.008 |
| Free shipping (2023) | 1 to 2 days | 5 to 7 days | Free shipping set in Merchant Center | L835.064 |

Notes:
- Enter order cutoff time, handling time and transit time so they match the shipping policy page. [L0729.001, L0181.008]
- Handling time is the time from order to dispatch. [L0728.008]
- The order cutoff time sets the time of day after which an order counts as shipping the next day. Choose a cutoff that matches the store's real dispatch routine. [L0728.020]
- Automated shipping rules from carriers such as UPS or FedEx are not used in this setup. Delivery times are entered manually, so they must be kept up to date when the policy changes. [L0729.010]
- Cross-check the shipping and return fields against the policy pages, as follows: [L0729.018]
  1. Open the shipping policy page and note the stated order processing time, typical delivery time and maximum transit time. [L0729.018]
  2. In Merchant Center, enter the order cutoff time, handling time and transit time so they match those figures. [L0729.018]
  3. Open the return policy page and copy its URL into the return policy URL field. [L0729.018]
  4. Compare the accepted return conditions (defective and non-defective products) and whether exchanges are accepted with the page text. [L0729.018]
  5. Enter the return window, return method, party paying return shipping, restocking fee and refund processing time exactly as the page states them. [L0729.018]
  6. Before clicking Save, check the summary against both pages. [L0729.018]
- Merchant Center shipping and return values must match the policy pages word for word in substance. A mismatch, such as choosing exchanges when the policy refuses them, causes Google to flag the account. [L0729.008]
- The shipping policy link in the product data section needs the exact URL of the shipping policy page on the store. Save it after the shipping page has been created. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.018]

#### Free shipping
- If the store offers free shipping on all orders, setting the shipping rate to 0 for all orders in Merchant Center is sufficient. No other shipping options need to be added. Paid shipping options are only added when the store charges for shipping. [L0728.011]
- Create a shipping rate named free shipping with a single rate for all orders and a fixed rate of 0, then click **Continue** and **Save**. [L0728.010]
- Choose free shipping for all customers with no conditional values, then click **Save**. (older, 2021-22 for the source's procedure) [L0729.001]
- Keep the default free shipping rate. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.010]
- Advanced shipping settings include free shipping thresholds (for example free shipping from a minimum order value) and holiday shipping exceptions. These are optional and only needed if the store uses them. [L0728.009]
- The shipping settings in Merchant Center must match what the Shopify store charges at checkout. If the store offers free shipping on all orders, the Merchant Center shipping rate must also be 0. A paid shipping option should only be added when the store charges for shipping. [L0728.019]
- Showing free shipping in Merchant Center while charging shipping at checkout can trigger warnings or suspensions, because Google bots crawl stores and test the cart. (2024) [L0360.046]
- Merchant Center shipping settings must match the Shopify shipping settings exactly. Mismatches can trigger warnings or a suspension, because Google bots check the two against each other. (2022) [L1092.070]
- To show free shipping on the Google ad label, set shipping prices in Shopify and then set the same shipping prices in the Merchant Center settings. [L0941.073]
- The estimated delivery date shown under a Shopping ad is set in the shipping section of Merchant Center. (older, 2021) [L0671.079, L0671.215]

#### Special shipping cases
- For Black Friday with a flat shipping fee for one supplier only, create the matching shipping rate in Shopify and set the same rule in Merchant Center. Free shipping for all other products can stay as is. (2022) [L1092.071]
- Heavy items can be shipped curbside and advertised on Google Shopping with free shipping. The shipping approach should still be checked against Merchant Center policies and confirmed with Google if a policy seems to restrict it. (2023) [L0835.066]
- For items whose shipping cost depends on destination (LTL or freight items), contact Google Merchant Center help through the help page and describe the issue. Save the conversation or the answer in case the question comes up again. (2023) [L0835.067]
- When Google Merchant Center asks for a ship-from address, enter your own business account address rather than each supplier's warehouse address. Supplier warehouse locations do not need to be listed separately for every supplier. (2022) [L0854.112]
- Warehouse locations need to be entered in Merchant Center only if you calculate shipping rates using zip codes. (2023) [L0835.064]

### Returns

- Return settings in the example store: return window 30 days, return method by mail with a return label, return shipping paid by the customer only if the policy says so, no restocking fee if none exists, and refund processing time 7 days after the return is received. [L0729.011]
- Return settings in the sign-up sequence: paste the Returns & Refunds policy URL, select the countries you accept returns from, confirm acceptance of defective and non-defective products, enter the return window (example: 30 days), select **mail** as the return method, specify return shipping responsibility, select **No cost** for restocking fee if applicable, and enter refund processing time. [L0181.008]
- Enter the return window, return method, who pays return shipping, restocking fee and refund processing time to match the policies, then click **Next**. Check whether exchanges are accepted. [L0729.001]

### Google Ads linking

- Do not link Google Ads to your Merchant Center account during initial setup. Google Ads will be configured later after your products are approved. [L0181.007]
- Do not link a Google Ads account to Merchant Center until your products have been approved for the first time in Merchant Center. [L0729.012]
- **Sources differ:** L0181.007 and L0729.012 say to link only after first approval. L1165.001 lists a linked Google Ads account among the requirements the account must meet before products can be submitted. The sources do not state how to reconcile the two. The first two are the step order of the setup flow, and L1165.001 is a checklist of what must be in place before submission. [L0181.007, L0729.012, L1165.001]
- Before products can be submitted to Google Merchant Center, the account needs taxes, shipping rules, a verified store URL and a linked Google Ads account. Only the product data is missing at that point. [L1165.001]

Linking procedure (older, 2021-22):
1. In the Merchant Center linking step, select the Google Ads customer ID that should be used and click **Link**. [L0731.029]
2. In Google Ads, go to Tools and settings > Linked accounts. [L0731.029]
3. Find Google Merchant Center and click **Details**. [L0731.029]
4. Click **View details** on the pending request, check the Merchant Center ID and website, then click **Approve**. [L0731.029]
5. Refresh Merchant Center and confirm the link status shows as active. [L0731.029]

Linking steps from other sources:
- Link Google Ads to Merchant Center: in Merchant Center, click **Link**, sign in to the Google Ads account with the same email, and approve the linking request that appears in Google Ads. Linking happens automatically after approval. [L0728.017]
- Link Merchant Center to Google Ads under the account linking section by clicking **Link account**. Once linked, Merchant Center can be used for daily feed management while campaigns run in Google Ads. [L0732.016]
- Link the Merchant Center account to Google Ads and select the correct Merchant Center account when adding products to the campaign. [L0743.012]
- Link Merchant Center to Google Ads: open the cogwheel settings in Merchant Center and choose **Linked accounts**. Without this link you cannot create campaigns that include your products. [L1145.044]

### Programs: free listings and Shopping ads

- In Merchant Center, go to Growth > Manage Programs and enable both Free listings and Shopping ads. These are the two channels that display your products to shoppers. Shopping ads must be enabled here before you can run Shopping campaigns in Google Ads. [L1145.042]
- Select the programs that fit your goals when creating the account. Shopping actions is optional and needs more business history and product understanding. [L0728.002]
- The free listings setup has Tax and Shipping items, which are optional, and the steps are completed in order. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.009]
- Free listings show products in Google surfaces without paid ads, but bring limited traffic. (older, 2021-22) [L0731.001]
- Merchant Center Buy with Google listings are optional. Disapprovals there are not a cause for concern if Shopping ads and dynamic remarketing are active without error. (2022) [L0969.070]

### Country availability

- Across every surface, Google Merchant Center can be used only in the United States and India. In New Zealand the sole option offered is Google Ads, which means Google Shopping cannot be operated there in the identical manner. (older, 2020) [L0961.061]
- Select only the countries where you actually sell. [L0181.008, L0729.007]
- Set shipping and return details for each selected country. [L0729.007]
- Set a default shipping rate for every country you sell to. [L0732.009]
- Shopping Actions in the US market in 2020 had its own dedicated ad space. (older, 2020) [L0738.015]

### Product source control and avoiding duplicate feeds

- To stop Google from importing products on its own, go to Settings > Data sources, open **Actions**, and choose **Hide all automatically found products**. Products then come through the "Provided by you" source, which you control. [L0729.013]
- Hide automatically found products in Settings > Data Sources by locating **Found by Google** and clicking **Hide all automatically found products**. This prevents Google from pulling products without your control. Your products will be submitted under "Provided by you." [L0181.006]
- Hiding automatically found products reduces your visibility in the Shopping tab, Google Maps and YouTube. This is accepted because you then control which products are submitted, and the feed is the source of your product data. [L0729.014]
- Duplicate-prevention checks: [L1114.071, L0731.016, L0731.017, L0731.040]
  - One Merchant Center account per store.
  - One website per account; a second website requires an advanced account. (older, 2021-22)
  - Claiming the website stops other accounts from using the same URL. (older, 2021-22)
  - Confirm the correct Google Ads customer ID before linking. (older, 2021-22)

### Starting the feed

- You can start a Google Shopping feed with about 30 products, but keep adding products continuously. Starting early lets data and sales begin to build while the catalog grows. (older, 2020) [L0358.008]
- If Merchant Center has a feed issue, check the product data first: correct product data is the basis of approval. (older, 2020) [L1087.006]

### Pay button and payment methods

- Enabling the Google Pay button in Merchant Center: if using Shopify Payments, Apple Pay and Google Pay are usually enabled by default. If not, enable them in Shopify payment settings. (2025) [L0255.044]
- The Add to checkout feature in Merchant Center is not recommended for dropship products due to lower conversion rates. (2025) [L0255.045]
- In Merchant Center, under payment method settings, check the boxes for all payment methods accepted on your site (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Shop Pay, credit cards). This must match what is enabled in Shopify. (2025) [L0255.046]

### Shopping Actions and Buy on Google

#### What it is
- Google Shopping Actions, also called Buy on Google, are product ads that let shoppers complete a purchase on Google without visiting the merchant's website. The format changes quickly, so the rules described for 2020 should be verified against current Merchant Center documentation before making decisions. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.001]
- Buy on Google is a checkout feature that lets people buy without leaving Google Shopping. It is a separate policy and is not the same as the standard Google Shopping setup. (2023) [L0835.068]
- Shopping Actions ads carry a Buy on Google icon over the product image, and often an Add to cart button. Clicking adds the item to the shopper's Google cart and leads to a checkout hosted by Google, which sends the order and payment to the merchant to process. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.019]
- In the Google Shopping tab, a Buy it on Google filter can appear on many results. Shoppers who apply it see only Shopping Actions ads, and all pay-per-click ads are hidden. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.021]
- Do not let customers buy directly through Google. Use free Google product listings but send shoppers to your own store for checkout. (2021) [L0962.071]

#### History and cost
- Shopping Actions developed from Google Express, an app-based Google marketplace that was not adopted by customers. Google then moved the same buy-on-Google ads into its existing Search, Images, Shopping, Discover and Lens interfaces. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.002]
- Originally Shopping Actions were not cost-per-click ads. The merchant paid a commission only on completed sales, similar to Amazon or eBay. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.004]

| Period | Cost to merchant | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Before mid-2020 | Commission on completed sales; averaged about 12%, varied by product type and category, ranged from roughly 8% up to above 12% | L0738.004 (older, 2021-22) |
| From mid-2020 | No commission; selling became free. Google presented this as a COVID-19 measure for advertisers, and it also increases the number of users on the platform | L0738.006 (older, 2021-22) |

- Shopping Actions listings are not pay-per-click ads, but they sit in the same ad slots as paid Shopping ads, so they push paid listings down. Even first position among ads may not be the first thing the shopper sees when Shopping Actions appear above it. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.020]
- Shopping Actions listings appear in the same positions as paid Shopping ads, in Search, Image search and other placements. As they grow, they take space from pay-per-click listings and can push them lower. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.013]
- Merchant Center renamed the Shopping Actions labels: Shopping Actions became Buy on Google listings, surfaces across Google became free listings, and local surfaces across Google became free local listings. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.033]

#### Control and placement
- With Shopping Actions, the merchant has little control over the checkout experience or the ad placement, and there is no optimisation tool. Google's aim of keeping users on its own properties means fewer visits to the merchant's own website, which weakens a sales funnel that depends on site traffic. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.003]
- Merchants cannot optimise Shopping Actions ads. They can only submit an additional feed on top of their existing Merchant Center feed, and Google decides whether and when the products are shown. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.007]
- In 2020, Shopping Actions listings could appear on Google Search, Google Images, the Shopping tab, Google Discover, Google Lens, the online Google Shopping homepage and the Google Shopping app (formerly Google Express). Google decides where each listing is shown, and the merchant cannot select individual placements. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.036]
- Shopping Actions ads only display when at least one competitor for the same product is also participating. If no competitor in the market has joined, a merchant will see no Shopping Actions ads even when approved. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.037]
- Large national retailers that sell high-ticket products, such as Walmart, Costco and Target, can occupy Shopping Actions slots if they join. Their entry can push smaller high-ticket dropshipping listings further down in the same results. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.038]
- Google's algorithm ranks and promotes sellers according to their seller score. A low score reduces traffic and sales, which leaves fewer orders to rebuild the score, so the damage compounds. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.017]

#### Risk and decision
- Shopping Actions requires more business history and a deeper product understanding than standard Shopping ads, so it is not a starting priority. Selecting it in the program choice is optional and can be ignored. (Source A, undated) [L0728.018]
- Stock shortages, which were common for high-ticket dropshippers during COVID-19, make Shopping Actions risky because delivery time commitments are hard to keep. Do not join while order fulfilment times are unpredictable. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.012]
- Start with Shopping Actions when you can reliably meet your delivery times, because the platform is useful for getting into the program. If stock and delivery are unpredictable, wait, but monitor the channel because it is expected to become more important. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.018]
- If traditional Shopping ads become harder to get seen, a merchant may be forced to use the Shopping Actions interface. This is both a risk and an opportunity when competitors are not using it. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.014]
- In the US market in 2020, when few competitors take part, a merchant can gain extra ad positions by joining. (older, 2020) [L0738.015]

#### Setup and reporting
Procedure (older, 2021-22):
1. Check whether Shopping Actions is visible as an option in Google Merchant Center. [L0738.022]
2. If it is not visible, submit the Google application form linked from Google's Shopping Actions page and describe the business. [L0738.022]
3. Wait for Google's approval. After approval, the Shopping Actions sections are added to Merchant Center. [L0738.022]
4. Submit the additional feed data through the Feeds for Google Shopping app in Shopify and switch on Google Shopping Actions in that app's menu. [L0738.022]
5. Only after approval, install the Order Sync for Google Shopping app so orders are brought into Shopify. [L0738.022]
6. Manage the orders in Shopify, where they are synced, and fulfil them. [L0738.022]

- Shopping Actions reporting is under Performance > Dashboard > Shopping Actions. Retailer Standards and Shopping Actions promotions are under Performance, and disapproval details are under Diagnostics > Products after changing the destination to Shopping Actions. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.025]
- The Merchant Center Overview page (merchants.google.com) includes a Shopping Actions box that shows how many products in the feed are approved for Shopping Actions. It is listed separately from the boxes for Shopping ads, Dynamic Remarketing and surfaces across Google. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.039]
- The Growth tab's Shopping Actions insights were in beta and added little value at the time. Promotions can be attached to Shopping Actions listings to highlight sale events on particular items. (older, 2021-22) [L0738.034]

### Why Merchant Center Comes First

- Google Shopping ads cannot run without a product feed created in Google Merchant Center. [L1287.037]
- The Shopping campaign pulls its products from that feed, so Merchant Center must be set up before the Shopping campaign. [L1287.037]
- Google Merchant Center receives the store's product feed and is needed before products can appear in Google Shopping. [L1437.014]
- Submit the feed right after uploading products, because approval takes time. [L1437.014]

### Setup Sequence

Source C procedure:

1. Create a free Google Merchant Center account. [L1251.027]
2. In Shopify, install the Google sales channel and follow its step-by-step setup, which takes about 10 minutes. [L1251.027]
3. Wait about 3 to 5 days while Google audits the products, which is required for a new account. [L1251.027]
4. In Google Merchant Center, open linked accounts and link your Google Ads account. [L1251.027, L1251.028]
5. Once linked, run the campaign hands-off with Performance Max. [L1251.027]

Source A procedure:

1. Upload all products to the store. [L1437.015]
2. Submit the store's product feed to Google Merchant Centre. [L1437.015, L1437.014]
3. While the feed is waiting for approval, launch Search text ads so the store can start getting sales. [L1437.015]

Sources differ on sequence and campaign type:

| Point | Source C [L1251.027] | Source A [L1437.015, L1287.037] |
|---|---|---|
| When Google Ads is linked | After the Merchant Center audit is complete [L1251.028] | Not stated as a linking step; Search text ads launch while the feed waits for approval [L1437.015] |
| Campaign type named | Performance Max, run hands-off once linked [L1251.027] | Shopping campaign, which pulls products from the feed [L1287.037] |
| Shared point | Merchant Center feed comes first [L1287.037, L1437.014] | Merchant Center feed comes first [L1287.037, L1437.014] |

### Linking Merchant Center to Google Ads

- Connect the Google Ads account under Google Merchant Center > Linked accounts, after the Merchant Center audit is complete. [L1251.028]
- The link lets Google Ads use the product feed for Shopping and Performance Max campaigns. [L1251.028]

### Audit and Approval Timing

- A new account needs an audit of about 3 to 5 days before the link step. [L1251.027]
- Approval of the feed takes time, so the feed is submitted right after products are uploaded. [L1437.014]
- Waiting time for feed approval can be used to launch Search text ads. [L1437.015]

### Verifying Shipping and Tax Settings

- The shipping and tax rate calculator in Merchant Center previews the rates that will show for a product delivered to a chosen destination. [L1170.043]
- Use it to verify shipping and tax settings before the feed goes live. [L1170.043]
- Older source (Source B, 2021-22): treat this as older advice and check it against the current Merchant Center interface. [L1170.043]

#### Further details

- All shipping and return settings must match exactly what is stated on your website policies. If settings do not match, Google may reject your products. [L0181.005]

- Fill in company information and shipping information in your Google Merchant Center account when setting it up. [L0671.066]

- Fill in company information and shipping information in your Google Merchant Center account when setting it up. [L0671.203]

## Product Feed Setup and Feed Apps

### Choosing a Feed Route

- Google's official Shopify app manages your product feed for Google Merchant Center and syncs the store with it automatically. [L0049.001]
- In the Google Shopify app, sync either all products or only products from a specific collection. [L0049.002]
- The Google Shopify app shows each product as `published` (synced successfully) or `warning` (has sync issues), so you can find and fix feed problems. [L0049.003]
- Symprosis Google Shopping Feed is a Shopify app starting at $4.99/month, with a free trial. It gives granular control over the product data sent to Google, far more than Shopify's free Google & YouTube app. Choose it when scaling a store. [L0182.001]
- Do not use Shopify's free Google & YouTube app for the product feed if you plan to scale. It offers limited manual control and restricted feed customization, so it suits only beginners who will not optimize or scale beyond initial listings. [L0182.002]
- The built-in Google & YouTube app is free but gives less manual control over the feed. Once a store grows and needs frequent feed edits, a dedicated feed app such as Symprosis is the better choice. As of 2026, the built-in app was judged far less advanced for this purpose. [L1168.002]
- Free plugins that push a feed to Merchant Center are a starting point. Feed tools go further, aiming for more traffic through optimized titles, distribution to secondary and tertiary channels, and product-level performance views across platforms. [L0454.027]
- A Google Shopping feed app gives far more control over feed fields than the default Shopify sales channels. You can change titles, images and other feed data without editing each product page. [L0965.009]
- A free Google Sheets feed is static and updated by hand for every new product. It suits only a small catalogue that rarely changes, because new suppliers and products would otherwise never reach the feed. [L1165.004]

#### Single feed or several feeds

- Starting setup: keep one feed. Do not run two Google product feeds at once, such as the Shopify Google channel and the Feed for Google Shopping app. Disconnect the Shopify Google channel and keep only one feed. [L0801.076]
- Starting setup: use one product feed and one Shopping campaign setup, with product titles, brands and SKUs complete, because the feed determines what Google displays. [L0962.072]
- Scaling setup: you can run several feeds at once, for example one free-listings feed with all products and one paid feed with only the most profitable products. Link the paid feed to the paid campaigns and the free feed to free listings. [L0965.010]
- The single-feed rule applies to the initial setup. The multi-feed setup applies once a store is scaling and separates products by profitability. [L0801.076, L0962.072, L0965.010]
- Create a separate feed for each channel, such as Instagram Shops, so product descriptions can be limited or customized per platform instead of sending identical content everywhere. [L1283.040]

#### Google & YouTube app versus dedicated feed app

- Install the Google & YouTube app to connect GA4 and Google Ads conversion tracking, but submit the product feed through a separate dedicated app. [L0856.032]
- In Shopify, Apps > Google & YouTube is used only to connect GA4 and optionally to track sales. Disconnect Merchant Center feed submission there and set it up through a separate Merchant Center feed app. [L0856.033]
- If the Google & YouTube app is connected to Merchant Center, it submits a second feed alongside the Google Shopping feed app. This causes daily "please review your file format" emails, even when all products are accepted. [L1116.023]
- Do not activate Shopify's built-in Google sales channel for Shopping. It lacks features, gives weaker results, and if set live after the feed setup, it duplicates the product feed. [L0731.019]
- Do not check the box that submits products to Merchant Center through the Google sales channel, because it duplicates the feed from the feed app. Keep the Google sales channel installed, but leave the product submission option unchecked. [L0835.065]

##### Procedure: Remove a duplicate feed [L1116.024]

1. Open the Google & YouTube app in Shopify. [L1116.024]
2. Go to Settings. [L1116.024]
3. If it shows it is connected to Merchant Center, click Disconnect. [L1116.024]
4. Keep the Google Shopping feed app as the only product feed sent to Merchant Center. [L1116.024]
5. Keep the Google & YouTube app installed, because it is used to connect Shopify to Google Analytics. [L1116.024]

### Connecting Shopify to Merchant Center

#### Before connecting

- The Google Merchant Center account must already exist before the Symprosis setup wizard can link it. [L1168.004]
- Create the Google Merchant Center account first, because the app's setup wizard links to an existing account. [L1168.003]
- Do not submit demo or test products to a live Merchant Center account, because they create product warnings. Use a store that is already linked to a real Merchant Center account for demonstrations. [L1168.005]
- The tax and shipping details in Merchant Center must exactly match your Shopify settings. [L1145.040]

##### Setting: Shopping ads setup in Merchant Center [L0731.027]

- Adult content: disabled.
- Country of sale and language: select the country and English.
- Destinations: Free listings and Shopping ads.
- Name the feed (for example, "shopify feed") and click Create feed.

#### Setup with the Google Shopping feed app

##### Procedure: Symprosis setup, short version [L0182.004]

1. In Shopify Admin, go to Apps. [L0182.004]
2. Search for "Symprosis Google Shopping Feed". [L0182.004]
3. Click Install. [L0182.004]
4. Access the app from your Apps list. [L0182.004]
5. Follow the guided setup wizard. [L0182.004]
6. Connect your Google Merchant Center account (select the account from the previous lesson). [L0182.004]
7. The app automatically pulls in all Shopify products. [L0182.004]
8. Products initially show as Pending, which is normal. [L0182.004]

##### Procedure: Symprosis setup, detailed version [L1168.003]

1. Create the Google Merchant Center account first, because the app's setup wizard links to an existing account. [L1168.003]
2. Install Symprosis Google Shopping Feed on the Shopify store by searching its name and clicking Install. It then appears in the store's Shopify apps. [L1168.003]
3. Open the app and follow its setup wizard. [L1168.003]
4. In the wizard, choose the Merchant Center account that was created, using the Google login that is already active. [L1168.003]
5. Let the app pull in all products automatically. [L1168.003]
6. Check the Google product category of each product and correct any that are wrong. The category is set inside the product view of the app. [L1168.003]
7. Fill in custom attributes or detailed product characteristics only where needed. Detailed characteristics are mainly used for apparel. [L1168.003]
8. Leave custom labels empty for now. [L1168.003]
9. Wait 2 to 4 days, up to about four, until every product changes from Pending to approved with a green check. [L1168.003]
10. Only after approval, move on to setting up Google Ads. [L1168.003]

#### Data the app submits

- Default fields submitted from Symprosis to Google are Brand name, MPN, and GTIN/SKU number. These are the standard values and should be checked if settings are changed later. [L1168.009]
- Symprosis submits these attributes to Google Merchant Center:

| Attribute | Notes |
|---|---|
| Brand name | From product data |
| MPN | Manufacturer Part Number |
| GTIN | Global Trade Item Number, if available |
| SKU | Stock Keeping Unit |

  [L0182.006]
- Symprosis automatically creates a Content API feed and sends it to Merchant Center. This is why the store's products appear under "Provided by you", and the feed label usually matches the store. [L1168.013]

#### Setup with the Google Shopify app

- Set up the app's feed settings: review the sync options (which products to sync, title and description formats). Most stores can keep the defaults. Enable "Submit additional image" for products whose variants use different images, then click sync to generate the feed. [L1165.008]
- Clicking sync pulls all products from Shopify into the feed app. This can take only moments for a small store; one example store had 27 products. Products can then be edited inside the app, including Google product category and promotions. [L1165.009]
- After the app is connected, Google Merchant Center creates a feed named "Content API" automatically. The seller does not need to add or edit it manually. [L1165.016]
- Once the feed app is connected, Merchant Center checks the domain and shipping setup automatically. Both should show as verified. Run the product sync only after these checks pass. [L0731.039]

##### Procedure: Publishing a product through the feed app (older method) [L0664.059]

*Older advice (2020):*

1. Open the product in the Shopify admin. [L0664.059]
2. Under product availability, check the box for Google Shopping. [L0664.059]
3. Use the Shopify Google Shopping app so the product is published to the Merchant Center. [L0664.059]

##### Procedure: Connecting the Google sales channel and feed app (2023) [L0835.061]

1. In the Google sales channel, connect your Google account and set emails from Google to off. [L0835.061]
2. Set up only the link, and do not click the Google Merchant Center listing option in the Google sales channel. [L0835.061]
3. Install the feed for Google shopping app. [L0835.061]
4. Use the app to connect to Merchant Center and submit your product feed. [L0835.061]
5. Set the feed to pull and update products from your store every 24 hours, so changes appear in Google within that window. [L0835.061]
6. Set variant submission preference to all variants if each variant should be its own listing. [L0835.061]
7. Keep only one product feed in Merchant Center when starting. [L0835.061]

#### Google Sheets feed (free, manual)

- Google Sheets feeds suit only a small, rarely changing catalogue. Manual spreadsheet uploads are not updated in real time and drift from the store, so connect the store through the API instead. [L1165.004, L0801.075]

##### Procedure: Building a free feed from a Google Sheets template [L1165.023]

1. Click add product data. [L1165.023]
2. Open primary feeds and click the plus button. [L1165.023]
3. Turn off Shopping actions if you do not plan to use them. [L1165.023]
4. Click continue. [L1165.023]
5. Choose to make the product feed from Google Sheets, give it a name and click continue. [L1165.023]
6. Generate a new Google spreadsheet from the template, click create and grant the requested permissions. [L1165.023]
7. Click open to edit the spreadsheet. [L1165.023]

##### Template columns [L1165.024]

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| Product ID | Unique identifier of each product |
| Title | Product name |
| Description | Product description |
| Link | URL of the product page |
| Condition | Product condition |
| Price | Product price |
| Availability | Stock status |
| Image link | URL of the product image |

- The template can be filled in by hand, or by pasting a product CSV exported from the Shopify store into the matching columns. It includes example rows and instructions that show how a completed sheet should look. [L1165.025]

### Sync Frequency and Updates

#### Refresh intervals

Sources agree on a 24-hour cycle. Use the manual update button only when a change must go live immediately.

- Google Merchant Center syncs products from Shopify once every 24 hours. Pricing changes are also synced every 24 hours. [L0255.038]
- The Google Shopping feed refreshes automatically every 24 hours with current product information from the Shopify store. [L0276.023]
- Products sold through the feed app should be updated automatically every 24 hours, so changes to descriptions or new products appear in Google within 24 hours. [L0835.062]
- In the feed app, set the update frequency (for example every 24 hours), and use the manual update button when you need changes live. [L0801.074]
- The refresh schedule controls how often products are resubmitted to Merchant Center, often every 24 hours. Find it in the app's sync or Google Shopping settings and change it there. [L0965.011]
- Connect the product feed through an app that refreshes it every 24 hours. Do not rely on manual Excel exports, because a price change not updated in the feed causes mismatches. [L0671.221]
- In Google Merchant Center, set the product feed to auto-update, so price and stock changes on the store sync automatically. [L0671.065, L0671.202]
- Feeds connected through the Content API update automatically, so the last upload date stays current. Use the Merchant Center feeds section to confirm updates are running. [L0732.019]
- Any edit made to a product inside the Symprosis app is automatically submitted to Google Merchant Center. No manual upload is needed after changing categories or attributes. [L1168.011]
- Manual Excel or spreadsheet product feeds are no longer needed for Merchant Center. Use an automated feed solution, usually an app connected to the store. [L0732.005]
- Manually maintained feeds were a major problem, because they often missed Google's requirements. Price changes on the website were not reflected in the listings, since every update had to be copied into the feed by hand. [L0762.012]
- Do not upload product data to Merchant Center by hand through spreadsheets, because those files are never updated in real time and will drift from the store. Connect the store through the API. [L0801.075]
- Connect the feed from Shopify to Merchant Center using the Feed for Google Shopping app, through the API connection. [L0801.074]

#### Settings checklist for the Feed for Google Shopping app [L0276.056]

- Feed refreshes every 24 hours.
- Brand field is mapped to the Shopify brand data.
- Old or broken product URLs are removed.

#### Meta fields changed outside Shopify

- The Feed for Google Shopping app does not pick up custom label changes made in Shopify automatically. Its meta fields must be synced manually from Settings > Sync Settings From Shopify after any custom label update. [L0402.006]
- The same applies to other meta fields such as SEO title, SEO description, age group and gender that are changed via CSV. [L0402.006]

#### Timing after a fix

- Shopify product data syncs to Merchant Center automatically every 24 hours. Allow 24 to 48 hours for changes to go through. [L1115.049]
- After the first sync, Merchant Center can take up to 10 hours to show products for Google, and up to 4 hours for Facebook. The product section shows "no data" during this time, so wait until active items appear before setting up campaigns. [L0731.028]

#### Standard flow

- Under the standard setup, new products and changes to existing products, including price, description and variants, flow automatically from Shopify to Google Merchant Center and then to Google Ads. If campaigns are split by brand or price, check that each product is present in the campaigns. [L1097.031]
- The feed determines the data Google reads: price, photo, product link, description and title for each product. Google uses it to understand what you sell and to show products in Shopping ads. [L0762.009]
- Shopping ad elements such as the product image, title, price, sale price, compare-at price, seller name, shipping cost and tax information all come from the Merchant Center feed, not from Google Ads. Merchant Center data must be set up correctly before any Shopping campaign can work. [L0731.002]

### Product Identifiers

#### Priority: which identifier to submit

Sources differ by year and by emphasis. Use the supplier's GTIN or UPC when one exists, MPN when none exists, and a self-made MPN only when the supplier provides neither.

| Situation | Identifier to submit | Source and status |
|---|---|---|
| Supplier provides a GTIN, UPC or EAN | Supplier's barcode | Current advice [L0470.039, L0934.069, L1115.048, L0971.065] |
| Supplier provides no barcode, but has an MPN | MPN | Current advice [L0468.186, L0803.044, L0984.006, L1105.015] |
| Supplier has no SKU, GTIN or MPN | Self-made MPN | Current advice [L1115.048, L1113.062] |
| MPN preferred over GTIN for fewer approval issues | MPN | *Older advice (2021):* [L0270.011] |
| MPN used instead of UPC | MPN | *Older advice (2022):* [L0272.034] |
| GTIN is not required; MPN is sufficient | MPN | *Older advice (2018):* [L1109.054] |

- Use the GTIN when a supplier provides one, because Google uses it to match the product to other listings. If no GTIN exists, use the MPN from the manufacturer. SKU is an internal stock code. ISBN applies only to books. UPC is one common product code format. [L0470.039]
- Use the supplier's UPC as the product identifier when it has one, because it helps Shopify and Google Merchant Center match your product with identical products. If there is no UPC, use the MPN instead. [L0934.069]
- For Google Shopping, UPC codes give an advantage if the supplier has them. If not, use the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead. [L0971.065]
- For Merchant Center product identifiers, use the supplier-provided GTIN if available. If no GTIN exists, use MPN instead. If the supplier provides neither, create your own identifier and use the SKU as the MPN. [L1115.048]
- Google Shopping supports GTIN or SKU. A store does not need both. Either identifier is enough for listing products. [L0429.061]
- Merchant Center accepts the manufacturer part number (MPN) as a product identifier, and it matters most when a product has no GTIN. Provide the brand and MPN for products that lack a GTIN, following Google's guidance. [L1105.015]
- In Google Merchant Center, an MPN is used as a product identifier when a product has no GTIN, so enter it for branded products that lack a GTIN. [L0984.006]
- MPN identifiers are valid to use when suppliers have no SKU or GTIN, because Google documents when MPN is used. Check competitors' Google Shopping listings to see which identifiers they use before creating your own. [L0856.028]
- Use an MPN when a GTIN is not available. MPNs can be used alongside or instead of GTINs in Google Merchant Center. An internal code such as AB1 or AB2 can serve as the MPN for tracking. [L0803.044]
- Products that have no GTIN can be listed with their MPN, and Google does not penalize this. Check Google's MPN documentation to see the situations in which an MPN should be used. [L0965.088]
- GTIN numbers missing or incorrect in the feed cause a low quality score and lower ad rank. Add GTINs where available. If not available, use UPC, EAN or ISBN equivalents. [L0274.052]
- Complete product identifiers in the feed, such as brand, GTIN (barcode number) and manufacturer part number, help Google match your product to the right searches and to competitor listings. Missing identifiers weaken that matching. [L0739.008]
- Some products require a GTIN, a unique product identifier such as a barcode. Products without a valid GTIN can be disapproved, so ask your feed app provider how to add GTINs to your products. [L0732.013]
- Provide identifiers in the feed for paid advertising. Barcodes must be entered whenever a supplier provides them, though a missing barcode is not a problem. [L1163.006]
- Google Merchant Center approval can be delayed when product identifiers are missing from the feed. Submit an MPN for every product, and check the feed if a review drags on. *Older advice (2018):* [L1109.053]

#### Barcodes and suspension risk

- Products that have a barcode (UPC, GTIN or EAN, depending on the country) must include that barcode number in the product feed. If the supplier provides no barcodes, the product does not need one and should not cause suspension. Missing barcodes on products that have them can lead to individual product or full account suspension. [L0727.004]
- If a product has a barcode and it is missing from the feed, Google may find it and suspend the product until the barcode is added. Supplying barcodes where they exist tends to increase impressions and can improve ranking. [L1170.009]
- Barcodes are registered in central databases that Google can query, and each barcode links to product information. A valid barcode helps Google match the product more accurately and use its historical performance data. [L1170.008]
- UPC is the common term in the US, EAN in Europe, and GTIN is the general term. All three describe the same barcode number. Supply a barcode only if the product actually has one. [L1170.007]
- Never buy UPC codes. If a product has no UPC or SKU, use the MPN identifier in Google Merchant Center. *Older advice (2020):* [L1277.069]
- If a supplier does not provide a barcode, a competitor's listing or an online barcode search can reveal the product's GTIN. Use this as a fallback when the supplier does not respond. [L0807.021]

##### Procedure: Fixing missing barcodes [L0727.005]

1. Check the Merchant Center product data diagnostics for missing or invalid GTIN issues. [L0727.005]
2. Contact the supplier and ask whether they have barcode numbers for the products, and request them. [L0727.005]
3. Enter the barcode in Shopify and make sure the supplier information matches. [L0727.005]
4. Let the feed update Merchant Center automatically. [L0727.005]

#### Custom products

- Mark a product as custom only if it truly has no identifiers, such as a self-made product or a unique bundle, or if you are the only seller of it. Marking a product as custom to avoid competition is not a valid reason. [L1170.018]
- Marking a product as custom while a barcode exists reduces its impressions. Google then ranks it below competitors who supply identifiers, so it rarely helps. [L1170.019]
- Create product bundles as custom products when you sell a combination no other seller offers. This is the main valid use case for custom submission. [L1170.036]
- For a self-made bundle or custom product, Google does not require a barcode. In the Shopping feed you can mark it as a custom product. Bundles built from the same base product still compete for the same clicks, so the cost per click for the same search stays the same. [L1456.011]
- A product with no unique identifiers is submitted with identifier_exists set to FALSE, as shown in the options table below. [L1170.035]

##### Product identifier management options in the feed app [L1170.035]

| Option | What is submitted | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| Submit Brand Name, MPN (SKU) and GTIN (Barcode) | All three identifiers; any missing value is not submitted | Products have correct, unique identifiers that match other merchants for the same product or variant |
| Submit Brand Name and MPN (SKU) | Brand and MPN only; GTIN is ignored | No valid barcode exists; this may limit performance |
| Submit Product as Custom Product | No unique identifiers; identifier_exists set to FALSE | You are the only advertiser of the product, e.g. a self-made bundle |
| Check "Adult-oriented" | Flags the product as adult-oriented | The product contains adult merchandise or sexually explicit content |

- The identifier setting in the Google Shopping feed app controls how brand, MPN, SKU and GTIN are submitted. Keep the option that sends brand name, MPN, SKU and GTIN enabled, so a product without a GTIN falls back to its MPN or SKU. Check this setting before troubleshooting missing identifier warnings. [L0855.175]
- The app's settings control how product identifiers are submitted to Google, and must be checked when GTIN codes are missing. [L0855.023]
- If the supplier provides no identifiers, the product can be set up to submit identifiers from the feed app's default identifier option. [L1165.011]

##### Procedure: Setting default product identifiers in the feed app [L1165.011]

1. Open the default product identifier management option. [L1165.011]
2. Choose the option that submits brand name, MPN (SKU number) and GTIN (barcode) together. [L1165.011]
3. If some identifiers are missing, the feed still works and submits the ones available. [L1165.011]
4. Click save, then confirm with yes, save. [L1165.011]
5. Click sync again so the feed modifiers link to the products from the store. [L1165.011]

### Identifier Fallbacks and Errors

#### Resolving a GTIN error

- If a product returns a GTIN error, enter the manufacturer part number (MPN) in the MPN column instead, because MPN values are usually approved more easily than GTINs. *Older advice (2019):* [L0357.035]
- When a product has no GTIN, Google Merchant Center can accept manufacturer part numbers (MPN) instead. Use MPNs as the fallback identifier when Merchant Center reports a missing GTIN error. *Older advice (2020):* [L0468.186]
- A product flagged for missing GTIN should be listed with an MPN instead, leaving the GTIN field empty. Google documentation explains the required fields when the MPN is flagged as not one of a kind. [L1283.037]
- To fix invalid GTIN errors in Merchant Center, correct the product page on Shopify or disable GTIN in the product feed settings. [L1115.049]
- If Google reports a GTIN as having too few digits, add leading zeros in front of it until it reaches the full required length. This is the fix Google itself suggests. [L0470.040]
- GTINs must be unique for each product. Do not use the same value, such as the brand name, for several products. [L0964.062]
- Product variations that are multipacks of one item cannot share the same GTIN. Give each variation a unique identifier, or sell the item only as bundles. [L1281.109]

##### Procedure: Resolving Merchant Center GTIN errors [L0469.093]

1. Remove the barcode if it duplicates the SKU, and keep only the SKU value. [L0469.093]
2. Resubmit the product feed and check whether the errors clear. [L0469.093]
3. If the SKU does not resolve the error, use the MPN (manufacturer part number) instead. [L0469.093]

- You do not need every product identifier. Using the same value in multiple fields, such as SKU and barcode, can trigger duplicate-value errors in Merchant Center. [L0469.094]

#### Fixing missing identifiers

*Older advice (2020):*

##### Procedure: Fixing missing product identifiers in Merchant Center [L1088.038]

1. Check Merchant Center for products flagged with missing values, since they can be limited. [L1088.038]
2. Ask the supplier for SKU numbers first, or find them on the price sheets they sent. [L1088.038]
3. If no SKU exists, use the manufacturer part number (MPN). [L1088.038]
4. If neither exists, create your own consistent naming and numbering convention. [L1088.038]
5. After the fix, confirm impressions rise before raising the budget. [L1088.038]

#### Creating your own identifiers (MPN)

- Create your own MPNs only for suppliers that lack SKUs, UPCs and MPNs, or when private labeling. [L0247.046]
- When private labeling, create your own identifier, such as a brand name plus a number, to use as the MPN instead of the supplier's SKU. This stops Google from matching your products with the supplier's other listings. *Older advice (2021):* [L0247.045]
- To make MPNs, make up a consistent code from the brand's name, for example the brand initial followed by the product letters and a sequence number. Use the same logic for every product. *Older advice (2020):* [L1277.070]
- Use a consistent MPN format per supplier. For example, take the supplier's product reference number or SKU, create an internal prefix from the brand name (such as the first letters of the brand), and join them with an underscore, as in FOV_12345. Apply the same format to every product from that supplier. *Older advice (2018):* [L1109.056]
- Around 99% of suppliers have no UPC, based on nearly 1,000 suppliers worked with. If a supplier does provide a UPC, GTIN or its own MPN, use the supplier's identifier instead. *Older advice (2018):* [L1109.055]
- When a product has no GTIN, use the MPN field in Google Merchant Center. If the supplier has no MPN either, create one from the brand initials plus a sequence number, such as AP-1 and AP-2. [L1113.062]
- A custom identifier can be built from brand initials plus a product descriptor, such as AS-blue-one for a blue surfboard. This ensures uniqueness without relying on supplier identifiers. *Older advice (2020):* [L0245.014]
- Use MPN (Manufacturer Part Number) as a unique product identifier when UPC numbers are unavailable or do not exist. You may create MPN numbers if the supplier does not provide them. *Older advice (2020):* [L0245.013]
- Never invent a SKU to fill the identifier field, because SKUs are retailer-specific and are not universal product identifiers. Use a UPC or MPN from the supplier instead. [L0934.070]

### SKU Rules

- Do not invent SKUs. If a brand's products already have SKUs and you sell under that brand, use the supplier's SKU. *Older advice (2021):* [L0247.046]
- Keep SKUs in the product feed as best practice, even if they cause products to appear among competitors in Google Shopping comparisons. Removing them is not the recommended fix. [L0470.037]
- Product SKU numbers from the feed can match buyer searches, so you do compete with other sellers on those SKUs in the Google auction. Treat SKUs as part of your competitive exposure. *Older advice (2021):* [L1090.097]
- Listing a product's SKU and barcode in the same identifier fields can trigger duplicate-value errors. See the duplicate-value rule above. [L0469.094]
- The Shopify SKU field on the product page is an internal management field and has no effect on Google Shopping. Google uses the MPN and UPC, which can only be set through a shopping feed app or a CSV upload, not on the Shopify product page. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L1456.012]

### Variants

- Sync all variants in the Shopping feed when variants differ in color or similar attributes. Sync only the first variant when variants do not need separate listings. *Older advice (2021):* [L0247.059]
- When each variant should appear as its own product in Google, set the variant submission preference to all variants in the feed app. Choose first variants only if you want a single listing per product. [L0835.057]
- Set variant submission preference to all variants if each variant should be its own listing. [L0835.061]
- Upload every product and every variant to Google Merchant Center as its own item. Each variant can match a different specific search term, such as material or size. *Older advice (2022):* [L1092.058]
- Product variants set up in Shopify, such as colors, are picked up by the feed if all variants are included. Each variant can then appear for searches that include its attribute, such as a particular color. [L1170.031]
- For apparel with several sizes or colors, each variant is normally a separate row in the Google feed. Use the item group ID column to group the variants under one product, so Google can show color filters on Google Shopping. [L1328.032]

### Google Product Category and Shopping Attributes

#### Setting the category

- Set the Google product category for every product in the feed. A default can be set for the whole feed, but per-product assignment is better when the store carries several product types. [L0879.017]
- Google Product Category must be set manually for each product in the feed app. Choose the most specific and closest match from Google's predefined taxonomy, for example Hardware > Plumbing > Plumbing Fixtures > Shower Stalls & Kits. The category also influences US tax calculation and campaign targeting. [L1170.029]
- Default Google product category: in the feed app settings, choose a top-level category that matches the main niche (for an apparel store, a top-level clothing category). This default applies to products without a more specific category. [L1165.010]
- Product categories and other attributes can be set in bulk by category. This saves time when a catalogue has many products, instead of editing each product separately. [L1165.015]
- More product data, such as categories, age group and gender, helps Google classify products and match them to more relevant searches. Filling in every detail is not necessary; titles, descriptions and the keywords shoppers use are the priority. [L1165.014]
- The Shopping tab lets shoppers filter results by price range, category, brand, type and capacity. Which filters a product can appear in depends on the product data sent to Google, so complete and accurate attributes matter. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L0741.022]

#### Custom attributes

- The feed app's Custom Attributes section lets you enter Color, Size, Material, Pattern and COGS. These values are submitted to connected channels but do not write back to Shopify. They apply only when the same attribute is not already defined in Shopify. [L0879.019]
- For clothing, size and color must be entered in the feed, because ads cannot run without them. Standardized size values matter because customers compare products on size. [L0879.020]
- For non-clothing products, the Size field means a size category such as small, medium or large, not dimensions. Consistent size values help customers compare products, even though variant setups differ across stores. [L0879.022]
- Custom attributes are usually not required for high-ticket products, unlike clothing. [L0879.018]

#### Detailed product characteristics

- Set Condition to New for all high-ticket dropshipping products. Set Age Group to Adult unless the product is for children, in which case use Kids, Infant, Toddler or Newborn as appropriate. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L1170.032]

### Age, Gender and Adult Attributes

- For most high-ticket products, set gender to unisex, age group to adult and condition to new. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L0879.018]
- For unisex products, where any age is not an option, select Adults in the age group setting per product in the feed app. [L1165.012]
- Age group describes who the product is for. The Adult-oriented checkbox is only for products containing adult merchandise or sexually explicit content. Do not confuse the two. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L1170.033]
- Set Gender only when the product is made specifically for one gender, such as men's apparel, footwear, fashion items or gender-specific makeup. For most products, including those used mainly by one gender, choose Unisex. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L1170.034]
- Check the Adult-oriented box only when the product contains adult merchandise or sexually explicit content, such as nudity, sexually suggestive content, or products intended to enhance sexual activity. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L0879.021]

### Custom Labels, Shipping Labels and Feed Modifiers

- Ads Label and Ads Grouping have no real use in current Google Ads. Custom Labels structure campaigns, and the Shipping Label links a product to a specific shipping rate in Merchant Center. *Older advice (2021-2022):* [L1170.037]
- Google Shopping product tags can be generated by the Google Shopping feed app. When using it, take tag problems to the app developer. [L0971.060]
- The Google Ads Shopping feed must include each product's price. Google Ads does not require a separate price field for shipping costs when the cost is included in the product price. [L0971.081]

##### Procedure: Setting product-level shipping costs in Shopping feeds [L1170.038]

*Older advice (2021-2022):*

1. Create a shipping label in Merchant Center for each rate you charge, for example a flat 20 USD rate. [L1170.038]
2. Enter that exact label in the Shipping Label field of each product that uses the rate. [L1170.038]
3. Confirm that the shipping rates charged on the site match the rates advertised in the feed. [L1170.038]

### Which Products to Include

#### Inclusion and exclusion

- The feed app's product inclusions and exclusions let you select products under $200 and remove them from campaigns, so they receive no spend. Setup takes about 10 to 15 minutes. [L0748.008]
- In Google Merchant Center, you can set the feed to sync only the products from a specific collection. [L0049.002]
- Exclude unwanted categories, such as accessories, by manually removing them from your product feed or campaign product selection, not via negative keywords. Shopping campaigns do not respond to negative keywords the same way Search does. *Older advice (2020):* [L0268.070]
- Products must have a live product page and a valid URL. Remove old or broken product URLs from the feed. [L0276.056]

#### Products that must be in stock

- Listing products you do not have in stock can lead to a suspended Google Merchant Center account. A student reported this after selling a product that was not in stock. Keep product availability accurate before running Google Shopping. [L0502.041]

#### Feed preparation before the first sync

- Optimize the product titles in your Shopify store so they contain the core keywords and the real search terms customers use and convert with. Then set up Merchant Center, install a product feed app for Google Ads, connect it to your store, and let the app keep the feed updated daily so stock, prices, images and titles stay current. [L0762.013]
- Clicking sync pulls all products into the feed app. Products can then be edited inside the app. [L1165.009]
- Enable "Submit additional image" for products whose variants use different images, then click sync to generate the feed. [L1165.008]
- Recheck the feed when identifiers are missing or products are flagged, rather than launching new feeds. Google Shopping's standard reach is only as good as the feed. [L0855.017]
- A product feed is the list of product data Google reads. It contains the price, photo, product link, description and title for each product. [L0762.009]
- Fill in custom attributes or detailed product characteristics only where needed. [L1168.003]
- Most fields filled in when creating a product in Shopify, including product type and brand, are passed to the feed. For most stores the feed needs checking rather than rebuilding. [L1170.004]
- A Google Shopping product feed is the structured product data you send to Google Merchant Center, usually through a connector or API. Google uses it to fill Shopping ads and to decide which search terms each product matches. [L1170.001]
- Google Shopping product approval can be affected by feed quality. Check the feed when the review drags on. [L1109.053]

#### Ongoing product feed changes

- Changes in product or shipping details in Merchant Center should be checked to confirm the feed is not duplicated. Deleting and re-adding a feed can create a duplicate, so confirm there is only one feed from the feed app. [L0835.063]
- Changing product IDs after the feed has been approved makes products count as new, requires re-approval that can take 3 to 5 days, and wipes the performance history of the feed. Do not change the product ID format after approval. [L0731.026]
- Never change product IDs once ads are running. Google treats a changed ID as a new product, and the historical data for the old product is lost. The only exception is when performance is very poor. [L0747.010]

### Verification and Approval

- Verify products are correctly submitted to Google Merchant Center: go to Merchant Center, navigate to Settings > Data Sources, and confirm products appear under "Provided by you" with the feed source showing as "Content API" (created automatically by Symprosis). No products should appear under "Found by Google". [L0182.007]
- In Google Merchant Center, go to Settings > Data sources and look at the section "Provided by you". It shows a Content API source with the store's products, instead of the "Found by Google" products that appear with the built-in app. [L1168.012]
- For a US-based store, the Content API source under Settings > Data sources > Provided by you usually has the feed label US. The app sets this label automatically when it creates the feed during setup. [L1168.015]
- Wait 2 to 4 days, up to about four, until every product changes from Pending to approved with a green check. Only after approval, move on to setting up Google Ads. [L1168.003]
- Google Merchant Center's product section shows "no data" for up to 10 hours after the first sync for Google, and up to 4 hours for Facebook. Wait until active items appear before setting up campaigns. [L0731.028]
- Once the feed app is connected, Merchant Center checks the domain and shipping setup automatically, and both should show as verified. Run the product sync only after these checks pass. [L0731.039]

### Feed Mistakes to Avoid

- Do not run two feeds at once without a deliberate plan, such as the Shopify Google channel and the Feed for Google Shopping app. [L0801.076]
- Do not submit demo or test products to a live Merchant Center account, because they create product warnings. [L1168.005]
- Do not activate Shopify's built-in Google sales channel for Shopping. It duplicates the product feed if set live after the feed setup. [L0731.019]
- Do not check the box that submits products to Merchant Center through the Google sales channel. [L0835.065]
- Do not connect the Google & YouTube app to Merchant Center alongside the feed app. [L1116.023]
- Do not list products you do not have in stock. [L0502.041]
- Do not change product IDs after approval or once ads are running. [L0731.026, L0747.010]
- Do not mark a product as custom to avoid competition, and do not mark a product as custom when a barcode exists. [L1170.018, L1170.019]
- Do not invent SKUs or use the Shopify SKU field expecting it to reach Google. [L0934.070, L1456.012]
- Do not rely on manual Excel or spreadsheet uploads for a growing store. [L0801.075, L0732.005]
- Do not use the same GTIN for several products. [L0964.062]
- Do not use negative keywords to remove categories from Shopping campaigns; remove them from the feed or the campaign product selection. [L0268.070]

#### Further details

- To remove a brand entirely from Google Product Listing Ads, use your Shopify-to-Google feed app (e.g., EasyTabs or similar), sort products by brand, uncheck all products from that brand, save settings, and Google Merchant Center will exclude them on next feed pull. [L0245.024]

## Feed Optimization: Titles, Images, Descriptions and Promotions

### Feed Control and Launch Sequence

- The product feed is the only controllable input for Shopping Actions, so titles and descriptions should be optimised. This is the same work as regular Google Shopping and should be done anyway (older advice, 2021-22). [L0738.009]
- Shopping campaigns match searches using the product data sent from Merchant Center, which is built from titles and descriptions. Product data quality therefore determines which searches a product can appear for, and changes to titles and descriptions change ad reach. [L1097.048]
- Feed quality determines how well Google understands a product. Inaccurate or thin data makes ads appear for less relevant searches (older advice, 2021-22). [L1170.002]
- Optimise the feed before running Shopping ads. If ads already run, review the feed regularly to find fields that can be improved (older advice, 2021-22). [L1170.003]
- Focus feed work on three fields that carry most of the effect on Shopping performance (older advice, 2021-22):
  - Product title (most important)
  - Product description
  - Barcode (GTIN, UPC or EAN) where one exists [L1170.005]
- Upload supplier product descriptions and images as received and get Google Ads running for every product. Optimise the best performers later, because the top 20% by impressions, clicks and sales usually drive most results (older advice, 2020). [L0664.061]
- Standard Shopping setup uses the product images from your product pages, so no separate ad creatives are needed to start. [L0972.064, L0247.047]
- Title determines whether the product appears; image determines whether the shopper clicks. Title is the single highest-impact lever for search reach, but all feed elements (images, product types, attributes) feed the same system. [L0220.026]
- Shopping and search campaigns work differently. In search, ad text and keywords are separate. In Shopping, the product title is the keyword, and Google reads titles to assign products to queries. [L0220.011]
- Where a product is approved in Merchant Center but gets few organic Shopping impressions after months:
  1. Confirm some impressions occur. This shows the feed works. [L0837.001]
  2. Treat the remaining problem as visibility. [L0837.001]
  3. Fix it with product page SEO, which improves regular Google organic results and organic Google Shopping listings. [L0837.001]
- A title optimised for paid Shopping usually also helps organic product results, so one shared title can save time. The exception is when organic shoppers search with different, non-commercial terms, which could lower organic traffic. [L0510.030, L0762.016]

### Title Structure and Keyword Placement

#### Core rules

- Product title structure determines search visibility. Weak titles with no keywords, or with brand names crowding out search terms, reach fewer searches, which leads to low CTR and wasted impressions. [L0220.014]
- Core keywords must appear in product titles, because Google scans titles to decide which searches trigger ads. Use terms that actually convert for your store, not only terms that sound good. [L0762.014]
- Google reads the title from left to right and gives the first words the most weight. Keyword importance decreases along the title, so place the most important search term first. [L1170.010]
- Titles are the largest-impact element of a feed, because shoppers compare them side by side with competitors in product listing ads. A study cited in the source found that optimised titles produced more clicks and more impressions. [L0762.015]
- The first words of a title matter most, because the results page often shows only the start of a long title. [L0510.017]
- Put customer search terms into the Shopping title, because matching what shoppers type increases clicks and CTR. [L1031.024]
- Titles should reflect how buyers search. Google Shopping ads are triggered by buying-intent terms, so words such as `buy` and `online` in product titles can increase Shopping impressions. The benefit comes from matching searchers close to purchase. [L0575.030]
- Do not place promotional phrases such as `free shipping` at the start of a title. Customers do not search that way, and the phrase pushes relevant keywords toward the end. [L1170.020]
- Do not copy competitors' product titles, even if they look good, because competitors often have weak quality scores too. Write titles that stand out while still including searched terms. [L0510.021]
- Broad category searches are top of funnel. Send them to an educational category page rather than a single product page. Use product pages for buyers who already know the product they want. [L1170.021]
