- Placements let you choose specific websites where your ad appears, for example sites your customers already read. This works as a targeting method alongside search. [L0720.009]
- Demographic segments can receive different ads rather than one message for everyone. Examples include households in the top versus bottom income bracket, or senior citizens versus people under 30 who are actively searching. [L0720.025]

**Launch order**

1. Launch targeting methods in order of how well they convert: start with the methods that convert best most often, then move up the funnel to methods that reach earlier-stage audiences. [L0720.020]
2. Do not activate all methods at once. [L0720.020]

**Finding placements and interest ideas for YouTube**

1. Browse YouTube channels in the category (e.g. furniture) and check whether their audience matches your customers. [L1510.031]
2. In Google Analytics, use the Interests report (Overview and Affinity categories) to find audience categories, then search for them in Google Ads. [L1510.031]
3. Use placements only when the audience is large enough. For smaller audiences, do not narrow the targeting too much. [L1510.031]

### Competitor and top-of-funnel YouTube

- YouTube allows targeting competitor audiences by selecting specific channels or videos (e.g. a competitor channel), so that a discovery or in-stream ad appears as a suggested video next to that content. Facebook restricts such page-level targeting, while YouTube does not restrict it in the same way. [L1510.008]
- On YouTube you can target specific channels and specific videos, including videos made by competitors. This lets you reach an audience that already watches content close to your offer. [L0720.014]
- Use YouTube targeting to reach viewers of specific competitor channels or videos only when that content is relevant to your buyers. The goal is to draw part of that audience's attention toward your offer. [L0720.023]

**Top-of-funnel campaign for competitor fans**

- Principle: copy the retargeting campaign and modify it. Exclude the website visitors audience (so only new people are reached), and target competitor channels or videos under placements (e.g. competitor YouTube channel) so the ad appears as a suggested video next to their content. Pause the retargeting ad groups if they are not needed. [L1510.035]
- The first touch should use a top-of-funnel video and offer. Users then flow into retargeting campaigns. The purpose of this campaign is to build a list of people to retarget later, so track cost per view against how many enter the funnel. [L1510.037]

**Build procedure**

1. Copy the existing campaign and paste it. [L1510.036]
2. Rename it to "top of funnel views". [L1510.036]
3. Replace the visitors-who-haven't-converted audience with a competitor-channel audience, by adding placements with YouTube channels or videos. [L1510.036]
4. Keep the website visitors audience as an exclusion. [L1510.036]
5. Repeat the same changes for the discovery ad group. [L1510.036]
6. Pick the funnel offer. [L1510.036]
7. Measure cost per view to see whether it pushes visitors into the funnel. [L1510.036]

### When YouTube makes sense

- YouTube ads are not a starting point for a new store. They suit sellers who are already doing well, want to grow further, and are comfortable with video. [L1088.046] (older, 2020)
- YouTube ads are not needed early on because they take considerable effort to get right and easier gains exist elsewhere. Consider them only when a store already does multiple millions of dollars in sales per year and needs more growth. [L0968.108] (older, 2021)
- Invest in Google Ads (search, shopping, Performance Max) for strong returns over 2-3 years. Reserve YouTube ads for retargeting only, because YouTube reaches video viewers rather than search-intent customers. [L0324.043]
- The sources differ on cold use. The retargeting-only rule [L0324.043] applies by default. The cold top-of-funnel build [L1510.035, L1510.036] applies only once the store has passed the starting stage described above [L1088.046, L0968.108]. [L0324.043, L1510.035, L1088.046, L0968.108]
- YouTube ads can serve two purposes: warming up past visitors to raise conversion rate (retargeting), and introducing the brand to cold users who search for the product but have not seen the store yet. The same setup works for both audiences. [L1510.005]
- YouTube can create ad tools through Google Ads, and a Google support document covers the setup process. It is a separate ad format to consider alongside Shopping and Search campaigns. [L1093.003]
- YouTube ads can target any channel regardless of its size, unlike Facebook, where targeting is limited to certain page types. [L0510.028]
- A YouTube channel that drives zero direct-attributed conversions may still deliver value through brand awareness, audience building for retargeting, and pixel/cookie placement. Measure its indirect impact using assisted conversions in Google Ads. [L0257.016]

**How a view is counted and billed**

- Sources describe the counted view in two ways. A view counts when the viewer watches 15 seconds, or the whole video if it is shorter, and these views are relatively cheap. [L0510.028] A view counts when the viewer watches a significant portion of the ad or clicks it, and skipping before that point is not billed. [L1510.006]
- On YouTube you pay per view, and a view only counts when the viewer chooses to watch a significant portion of the ad. Facebook can count a mere impression as a view. Skipping an in-stream ad costs nothing. [L1510.004]

**Format definitions**

- In-stream ads (pre-roll) are charged only when a viewer watches a significant part of the ad or clicks it. [L1510.006]
- Discovery ads appear as suggested videos in the sidebar, on the YouTube homepage, or in the search results for a keyword. [L1510.007]

### Display Network: reach and when prospecting makes sense

**Reach figures (older, 2021-2022 source; verify current values)**

- The Google Display Network can reach about 97% of internet users. This is a reach figure for the whole network and does not mean those users are relevant buyers for a given product. [L0725.001]
- At the time of the source, Google's own reach figure for US internet users on the Display Network was 92% across millions of sites, videos, and devices. The source said the figure was higher by then. Treat it as a dated figure for the US and check the current value in Google's tools before using it. [L0725.004]
- Around 2021 to 2022, websites monetized through the AdSense publisher network had about 204 million visitors per month combined in the US. This is a dated US figure and should be verified before use. [L0725.005]
- At the time of the source, YouTube had over 1 billion video views per day, and Google properties accounted for about 5% of all online time spent. These are dated global figures that show the scale of Google-owned placements. [L0725.006]
- The DoubleClick Ad Exchange connects hundreds of premium content publishers that offer hundreds of millions of ad placements every day, according to a 2021 to 2022 figure that should be verified before use. This exchange is one of the three groups of properties that make up the Display Network. [L0725.016]
- YouTube was described as the second largest search engine in the world around 2021 to 2022, with over 1 billion video views per day. Video placements on YouTube are therefore a large Display Network inventory, but the figures are dated and should be checked in current Google sources. [L0725.017]

**Where display ads run (older, 2021-2022 source)**

- Display ads run on third-party websites and apps monetized through the AdSense publisher network or the DoubleClick Ad Exchange, and also on Google-owned properties such as YouTube, Gmail, Google Maps, Blogger, and Google Finance. They do not appear in the main Google search results. [L0725.003]
- Search network ads reach people who are actively looking for something, so their intent is visible from the search terms. Display ads interrupt people while they browse other content, similar to Facebook ads, so their intent is much weaker. [L0725.002]
- The Display Network contains a large share of irrelevant traffic. The source estimates that roughly 99% of available impressions will not match your market. Relevant audiences can still be reached, but only through careful targeting. [L0725.015]

**When to use display (older, 2021-2022 source)**

- For a high-ticket dropshipping store, the Display Network is best used for retargeting ads (static and dynamic) and targeted lead generation ads. Using it for cold prospecting is an advanced strategy. [L0725.007]
- Display prospecting should only start once the business is already profitable from other traffic sources, such as Google Shopping, search text ads, and organic search. Retargeting can and should run from the start. [L0725.010]
- Cold display audiences are usually far from the bottom of the sales funnel, so a direct offer for an expensive product such as a $4,000 item rarely converts from a first impression. People need time and a reason to trust before they buy. [L0725.008]
- Cold display traffic has a longer gap between the first click and the purchase, so ad spend must continue for a long time before returns come in. Only businesses with cash to keep investing should attempt this. Businesses running on thin margins should first improve the sources they already have. [L0725.011]
- A lead generation approach to cold display traffic depends on having useful content on the website to send visitors to. Without content pages, the funnel has nowhere to move the visitor next. [L0725.012]

**Cold display procedure for a high-ticket store (older, 2021-2022 source)**

1. Run a lead generation ad that sends cold visitors to a content page or lead page on your website. [L0725.009]
2. Retarget those visitors with display ads (static and dynamic) for product pages, content pages, and collection pages. [L0725.009]
3. Get visitors to opt into your email list and deliver value through content before making a sales pitch for an expensive product. [L0725.009]

**Mistakes to avoid (older, 2021-2022 source)**

- Display ads from large brands for expensive products, such as car makers in major newspapers, are usually branding campaigns with budgets in the millions and no direct tracking. A small store cannot copy this approach, so its own display plan should be built around direct response and sales within a reasonable time frame. [L0725.013]
- Before copying a competitor's ad strategy, check what kind of company it is and how much money it can spend. Results that work for a different business model or budget are not a reliable guide for your store. [L0725.014]
- One advertiser can fill several ad slots on the same large news page at once, which signals a very large budget. A small store cannot copy this kind of placement and should judge display placements by the advertiser's size and goal before treating them as a model. [L0725.018]

**Sidebar and footer testing**

- If a site shows Google-served ads in its sidebar or footer and offers no direct ad deal, you can still test ads there by running Google display ads that appear only on that website. [L0528.029]

### Display ad formats and CTA

- On the Google Display Network, the same ad can use a plain text-based link-style CTA or a button-style CTA. Keep the same image and headline when switching between the two styles. [L0415.008]

### Shopping showcase ads

- Showcase ads in Shopping campaigns show searchers a swipeable carousel of brands and products, leading to a brand store-style page and then to single products. The lesson reports a very high CTR and says the first click is free. Verify that billing claim in current Google Ads terms before relying on it. [L0712.002]
- Product showcase ads require uploaded images: a logo, a header image, and a lifestyle photo, such as a model wearing or using the product outdoors. The lifestyle photo works best as the top photo of the set. Product images can be added as well. [L0712.003]
- The product showcase description is limited to 120 characters. [L0712.005]

**Create a product showcase ad**

1. Create a new campaign and choose the goal Shopping. [L0712.004]
2. Select your merchant feed and go to the next screen. [L0712.004]
3. Enter a campaign name and click Save and continue. [L0712.004]
4. On the showcase format screen, choose to show a selection of products and put your top products first. [L0712.004]
5. Upload the header image, the logo and, if used, the product images. [L0712.004]
6. Enter the display URLs the ad should lead to. [L0712.004]
7. Write a headline and a description of up to 120 characters. [L0712.004]

### Demand Gen

**Why Demand Gen matters**

- A Google Shopping listing shows only an image, a title and a price, so the image is one of the main reasons a shopper clicks. Demand Gen native image ads run in browsing placements such as YouTube in-feed and Google Discover, where images also drive the ad. [L0882.001]
- Brands scaling through Shopping and Demand Gen spend about 10,000 to 40,000 US dollars per day across both channels, according to the lesson. Demand Gen image placements are described as one of the most under-used scaling options. [L0882.002]

**Assets**

- A Demand Gen ad can use up to 20 images, up to 5 headlines and up to 5 descriptions. Google combines these assets into different ad combinations, so each asset should work with any other asset. [L0882.019]

**Image sizes**

| Format | Aspect ratio | Pixel size | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Landscape | 1.91:1 | 1200 x 628 px | YouTube in-feed |
| Square | 1:1 | 1200 x 1200 px | Works across both placements |
| Portrait | 4:5 | 960 x 1200 px | Discover |

[L0882.021]

**Channels**

- To choose where a Demand Gen ad runs, open the ad group settings and go to Channels. Select All Google channels to run everywhere eligible, or select Let me choose and tick the channels to use, such as YouTube in-stream, YouTube Shorts, Discover, Gmail, Google Display Network or Maps. [L0882.020]
- YouTube in-stream and YouTube Shorts run on YouTube surfaces. Discover shows ads in personalized content feeds on Google mobile apps. Gmail shows ads inside users' Gmail inboxes. Google Display Network runs ads on third-party sites and apps and may modify the ad to fit each publisher's format. Maps shows ads on Google Maps and is labelled NEW in the interface. [L0882.035]
- Before saving a Demand Gen ad group, the Channels panel shows an estimate of conversions and impressions for the channels currently selected, plus the total available ad group impressions. Checking these estimates while ticking channels helps compare which placements will bring volume before publishing. [L0882.037]

**Ad group page**

- Above the Channels section, the Demand Gen ad group page has Ad group name, Locations and Languages fields. The example uses United States (country) and All languages. [L0882.036]
- The page is saved with the buttons Save all changes, Duplicate ad group and Discard all changes at the bottom. [L0882.036]

### Pinterest and secondary formats

- Pinterest promoted pins were in beta at the time of recording and were billed on a cost-per-click basis. You only pay when a user clicks through from the pin to your website. [L1136.028]
- Pinterest ad targeting uses search keywords, which are displayed as separate keyword segments in search results, plus location, language, device and gender. Choose the keywords that match what users search for, then select the audience filters before paying. [L1136.029]
- Promoted pins often earned free repins more easily than they earned paid clicks back to the store in the speaker's tests. Repins still spread the content and can later lead to purchases or viral reach. [L1136.030]
- Pinterest promoted pins are new, so there is little public data on the best way to use them. Traffic from them tends to be browsing traffic, so the store needs a strong funnel with retargeting and an email opt-in to capture it. [L1136.031]

### Measurement across channels

- Switching on a Google Ads search campaign raised overall website traffic, even though the campaign running at that time was a YouTube video campaign that sent no visitors directly to the site. Track total site traffic alongside per-campaign clicks to see this kind of cross-channel lift. [L1142.002]
- Targeting an interest category with a highly relevant video ad can produce very cheap views, because relevance drives down cost per view. Relevance of message, audience and timing matters more than budget size for this effect. [L1142.004]
- Brand recognition built up by earlier video ads raises the click-through rate of later search ads, because searchers already recognize the brand. Plan search ads as a follow-up to awareness campaigns, not only as standalone direct-response buys. [L1142.005]

**Campaign- and ad-group-level video cost check**

1. Open Supermetrics and choose the last 30 days. [L1236.016]
2. Add cost, clicks and cost per view. [L1236.016]
3. Split the rows by campaign name and ad group. [L1236.016]
4. Apply the cost-per-view KPI of 0.05 USD and conditional formatting that turns cells yellow when they are greater than 0.05. [L1236.016]
5. Drag the formula down for all campaigns and check for flagged rows. [L1236.016]

- In a YouTube awareness campaign, the ad group for retargeting pre-roll and awareness showed a cost per view above the 0.05 USD threshold. Breaking it down by video title identified the specific video and audience combinations that were not performing, which pointed to exactly which ads to change. [L1236.017]

## Performance Max and Automation

### Performance Max and Automation

### Humans and Machines

- The effective approach combines humans and machines. The marketer sets goals, campaign structure, tests and feed quality, while automation calculates bids across many dimensions. Manual control alone leaves dimension value untapped, and trusting automation blindly leaves no check on results. [L0454.009]
- Systems that learn from outcomes can find patterns that rules written by humans miss. An early drop in ROAS during the learning phase is normal and should not trigger an immediate reversal. Judge automated bidding only after it has had time to learn. [L0454.013]
- Keep a human in control of bids, budgets and structure, and use AI mainly for research and analysis. Do not hand a live Google Ads account to an AI agent to run unattended. [L0876.001]
- Errors compound at scale: one bad bid or budget change applied across an account can burn a lot of money before anyone notices. Some account mistakes take weeks or months to repair. [L0876.002]
- Current AI models handle short, single tasks well but fail on long chains of steps, repeated tasks and tasks requiring exact steps. They may skip a step or enter details incorrectly, which is costly in a live ad account. [L0876.004]

### Account Maturity and Starting Point

- Standard Shopping is preferred over Performance Max for most merchants. Performance Max gives Google full control of targeting, placements and bidding with less transparency. (Older, 2022.) [L0272.033]
- Standard Shopping campaigns are preferred over Performance Max for non-impulse products because they provide control over keywords and clear data on what is performing. [L0255.041]
- Standard Shopping stays the core of the account. Performance Max, if tested, sits beside it. [L0854.051, L0969.056, L0941.070]
- For most new stores, start with Alpha Beta standard Shopping campaigns and run Performance Max alongside them rather than replacing them. (Older, 2022.) [L1113.057]
- In a new account with no conversion history, do not use Smart Shopping for all products. Use standard Shopping campaigns with individual bids until Google has conversion data. (Older, 2021.) [L1112.014]
- Smart Shopping and other automated bidding are not recommended for new accounts, because Google has no store data yet and will spend money broadly. Start with manual bidding and controlled setup, then consider automation once the account has a history of profitable data. (Older, 2021.) [L1090.095]
- Automated bidding works best when the account already has a large history of conversions, since the platform then knows which clicks are likely to buy. Without that history, automation mainly spends on random clicks. (Older, 2021.) [L1090.096]
- For most accounts, scaling manual campaigns gives a higher return on ad spend more easily than experimenting with smart campaigns. Scaling the manual campaigns is therefore the default choice. (Older, 2022.) [L0963.003]
- Switching a working account to Smart Shopping while raising budgets can make the numbers unreadable. If an agency did this during a scale-up, revert to manual campaigns and scale there. (Older, 2022.) [L0963.007]

Prerequisites named in the sources:

| Campaign or step | Condition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Performance Max | Start after about 30 to 40 sales; before that, begin with Search and Shopping campaigns around the product keywords | L0788.014 |
| Performance Max | Needs at least 50 conversions to optimize well | L1213.003 |
| Performance Max | Use only with a store already profitable on standard Shopping | L0969.056 |
| Performance Max | Test only if Smart Shopping already worked profitably for the account (older, 2022) | L0272.032 |
| Performance Max | Works well only with a large history of past conversions | L0970.116 |
| Smart Shopping rollout, per brand | Brand has more than 20 conversions per month and 100 or fewer products | L0454.036, L1033.005 |
| Smart Shopping, per product group | Product groups hold 100 or fewer products, and each small group generates more than 20 conversions per month | L1033.005 |
| Smart Shopping | Most worth running when the account already has a high impression share | L1033.006, L0454.036 |

### Performance Max: Behavior and Decline

- Performance Max campaigns initially target the hottest existing audiences, people who visited the store, and produce high ROAS. As these audiences see the ads repeatedly and become exhausted, Google expands targeting to wider, colder audiences who are less likely to convert, so ROAS drops significantly. Performance Max, including feed-only campaigns, often performs well for a few weeks or months and then return on ad spend drops sharply, because it increasingly retargets existing visitors until those audiences run out. When this happens, add other Google traffic sources. It typically starts strong, first remarketing heavily to the warmest visitors, and it is not recommended as a core approach. [L0255.040, L0667.006, L0965.006, L1015.007]
- As of April 2025, Performance Max campaigns are not recommended. They show strong performance initially but decline over time as audiences exhaust. [L0255.039]
- Performance Max remains a black box. Remarketing lists inflate its early results before performance slows once those lists max out. [L1283.032]
- Performance Max is not recommended for dropship products. The lack of data visibility and declining performance over time make it unsuitable. [L0255.042]
- Use Standard Shopping rather than Performance Max for Google Shopping campaigns, because Performance Max has not shown consistent results. [L1115.038]
- Performance Max results are inconsistent: some accounts lose money with it. It is not recommended for this store model. [L0855.016]
- Performance Max is not recommended for this business model, because it did not perform consistently across several accounts where it was tested. A campaign that is getting impressions can still produce poor-quality traffic, since impressions alone do not show whether they lead to sales. [L1015.006]
- Performance Max is not recommended for the store types taught in the course as of March 2023. Standard Shopping campaigns outperform it, so do not run Performance Max. [L0964.051]
- Performance Max was not used by the team because results were inconsistent across stores. The team uses Shopping Alpha/Beta and other campaign types instead. [L0971.058]
- Performance Max is a newer Google campaign type that Google pushes heavily. It does not replace standard Shopping campaigns, so test it with about 10% of the budget only and keep the proven Shopping campaigns as the main spend. (Older, 2022.) [L0854.051]
- Performance Max results vary widely, and there is no fixed set of rules that works in all accounts. Creating more asset groups segmented by product category, brand or best-selling products is the most reliable adjustment seen so far. (Older, 2022.) [L1281.101]
- Performance Max has not replaced Standard Shopping in the owner's accounts. It sometimes targets people who click a lot but do not buy, so stick with Standard Shopping unless tests show otherwise. [L0941.070]
- Performance Max shows products across Google Shopping and other Google inventory such as YouTube and Gmail, and uses built-in AI to choose placements. It helps control spend because the system places ads where it expects a return. [L1508.005]
- After moving from Smart Shopping to Performance Max, one seller reported sales from YouTube and Gmail placements that the earlier setup did not bring in. Performance Max therefore added incremental sales through Google's other channels. [L1508.017]
- Google Shopping moved from regular Shopping, where higher bids raised placement, to Smart Shopping, which balanced toward a target return, and now to Performance Max. Shopping-based campaigns are still described as the strongest return on ad spend among Google formats. [L1508.004]
- Performance Max automatically handles retargeting. After setup it needs little work once it has been given enough time, which the mentor said could be more than two weeks. [L1107.016]

### Performance Max: Results Seen in Sources

- Performance Max campaigns across several accounts returned about 6 to 9 in return on ad spend. Results were not clearly better than manual campaigns, so underperforming campaigns were turned off and the others kept running. [L0970.117]
- An agency-managed Google Ads account with Performance Max returned about 4x to 5x ROAS, with the main returns coming from that campaign type. [L1213.009]
- Performance Max worked for some accounts but failed for others with the same setup. (Older, 2022.) [L1113.057]
- A Google Ads account was shown with about 450,000 spend over several years in Performance Max campaigns; the speaker estimated the spend at about 450,000 in the shown view. [L1440.034]
- In an already optimized Performance Max campaign, add budget to scale. Remove products that keep consuming spend without producing sales. (Older, 2022.) [L1113.058]

### Performance Max: Brands, Negatives and Setup

- Google Ads for brands (not dropshipping) works best when there is branded search intent. Performance Max campaigns received most of their sales from brand search terms, so they had to be adjusted. [L0577.051]
- Performance Max negative keywords cannot be added directly. You need to contact Google support to add them manually. Brand-term share can be checked under Insights, which only looks back 28 days. [L0577.052]
- For a product store on Google, use Performance Max rather than standard Shopping or Smart Shopping campaigns. Performance Max pulls from the shopping feed and runs across Search, Display, YouTube and Shopping. [L1251.023]
- Once Performance Max and the Google Merchant Center feed are set up, the campaign runs largely hands-off, because Google handles much of the optimization. The main work is in the initial setup and the assets. [L1251.025]
- Start Google Ads for e-commerce with Performance Max, since it automates distribution across Search, Shopping, YouTube and Display from Google data. It needs a week or two before manual changes, and it needs consistent budget to optimize. [L1440.032]
- Performance Max is harder to set up for beginners because it needs money to optimize. Do not micromanage it the way TikTok or Facebook is managed. Search and shopping ads are harder to run than Performance Max for beginners. [L1440.033]
- Performance Max is an AI-driven campaign type that needs a couple of weeks before its results can be judged. Once it runs, the main job is to adjust budgets every one or two weeks. [L0694.037]
- Start Performance Max only after the account has about 30 to 40 sales. Before that, begin with Search and Shopping campaigns using keywords around the product. [L0788.014]
- Performance Max needs at least 50 conversions to optimize well. The account also needs about two weeks to collect data and warm up before results stabilize. [L1213.003]

### Smart Shopping: Status and Campaign Types

- Smart Shopping campaigns were sunset by the end of Q3 2022. Merchants migrated to either Standard Shopping or Performance Max. [L0272.031]
- Smart Shopping is being sunset and replaced by Performance Max. Standard Shopping is the campaign type taught as the core. (Older, 2022.) [L0969.057]
- Smart Shopping campaigns are generally not recommended. Performance Max may be tested with about 10% of the ad budget, but it only works well with a large history of past conversions. [L0970.116]
- Shopping campaign types include standard Shopping, Dynamic ads on the Google network, YouTube shopping, Gmail shopping and product listing retargeting on the display network. Smart Shopping is Google's automated campaign type and automatically includes retargeting, dynamic retargeting, YouTube ads and Gmail ads. [L0454.033]
- Smart Shopping is most worth running when the account already has a high impression share. It covers Shopping, retargeting, dynamic retargeting, YouTube ads and Gmail ads, and is valued for simplicity, performance and reach. [L1033.006]
- Smart Shopping gives little control. You cannot see placements, performance by dimension such as gender, location or income, or the split between cold and retargeting traffic, and negative keywords are not available. Placement exclusions can only be set at the account level. [L0454.034]
- Smart Shopping works best with one brand per campaign. Product groups should contain 100 or fewer products, and each small product group should generate more than 20 conversions per month. [L1033.005]

### Smart Shopping: Learning Time and Stability

- Pausing a new Smart Shopping campaign before it has enough conversions cuts off its learning. Google suggests giving it about one month to learn. Judge it only after that period. [L0454.035]
- Frequent changes to Smart Shopping campaigns disrupt the automated learning, so settings should be left alone for a stable period. Make adjustments deliberately rather than on a daily basis. [L1033.007]
- The lesson estimated Smart Shopping succeeds about 50 to 60% of the time. Sometimes it performs very well, sometimes it needs more learning, and sometimes it must be turned off in favor of Alpha Beta. Plan for all three outcomes. [L0454.037]
- Automated Google recommendations and Smart features mainly raise spend rather than performance. For high-ticket dropshipping, managing settings manually performs better, so use your own judgment. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0742.016]

### Smart Shopping Rollout Procedure

Procedure to roll out Smart Shopping safely [L0454.036, L1033.005]:

1. Start with one brand at a time.
2. Exclude that brand from the standard Alpha Beta campaign.
3. Place the brand in a Smart Shopping campaign.
4. Prefer brands with 100 or fewer products, since smaller sets are easier for Google to learn.
5. Confirm the brand already has more than 20 conversions per month.
6. Prioritize brands that already convert well and have a high search impression share, because they gain the most clicks and conversions.
7. Do not change the campaign frequently; allow about one month for learning.

Build the shopping structure in a hierarchy: keep Alpha Beta as the baseline, peel one brand into Smart Shopping, then test Bing, other product listing ads, YouTube shopping ads and Gmail shopping ads. Compare each new element against the Alpha Beta baseline before expanding it. [L0454.039]

### Testing Automation Safely

Procedure to test a change safely with Drafts and experiments [L0454.023]:

1. Open Drafts and experiments in the left sidebar of Google Ads.
2. Create a draft from the campaign; the draft lets you change the campaign without affecting live traffic.
3. Make the changes to test in the draft, for example grouping products instead of segmenting by product ID, turning on automated bidding, or adding negative keywords.
4. Run an experiment from the draft.
5. Set how much traffic or budget goes to the test, for example a 50/50 split or a smaller share of 20, 30 or 40%.
6. Compare the results and decide based on the experiment outcome.

Procedure to test automated bidding on an existing Shopping campaign [L1033.003]:

1. In Google Ads, open Drafts and Experiments.
2. Create a draft from the original campaign.
3. In the draft, turn on bid automation.
4. Run the draft as an experiment against the original campaign and compare the results.

An experiment tests automated bidding on a share of traffic instead of the whole campaign. If the automated version wins, the test shows where to scale; if the manual campaign wins, that result confirms the existing setup beats automation. Either outcome is useful. [L0454.024]

A couple of years before the lesson, automated bidding beat manual setups only about 10 to 20% of the time, and that share was rising. Test automated bidding on your own account instead of assuming either outcome. [L0454.025]

With a large amount of account data, a smart campaign can be tested at a small budget in parallel with the manual campaigns. The manual campaigns stay switched on during the test. (Older, 2022.) [L0963.002]

### Case: Switching a Shopping Account to Smart Shopping

A client's Shopping product listing ads were slowly declining. The campaign manager switched the account from the standard Alpha Beta shopping setup to Smart Shopping. Afterwards the chart showed large daily swings, with revenue peaks around $25,000 on some days and a reference line near $12,500 that many days exceeded. Cost and conversions were high but volatile, and the recent period clearly outperformed the older period on sales and ROI. [L0454.049]

### AI for Keyword and Search Term Work

- Use AI for keyword research, search term analysis and negative keyword lists rather than for managing the ad account itself. These tasks carry the least risk and give the biggest time saving. [L0876.005]
- Any large language model can be used for the negative keyword and search term prompts. The lesson used Gemini in a browser chat for these tasks. [L0876.030]
- For a large search terms export, attach the full file to an AI chat together with the audit prompt and wait for it to finish. A file of about 13,000 rows took a few minutes to process in Gemini, so review the output only after the run is complete. [L0876.038]
- AI generates plausible-looking keywords without knowing whether anyone searches for them, so it can produce long lists of terms with zero search demand. Never build campaigns on AI keyword ideas before validating their search volume. [L0876.007]

Keyword validation procedure [L0876.006]:

1. Use AI to generate keyword ideas and group them by theme and intent.
2. Take the keyword groups into Google Keyword Planner.
3. Check each group for real average monthly search volume and keep only terms that people actually search.
4. Feed the validated set back to the AI as seed keywords to find more ideas, then validate again.

Keyword and campaign prompt [L0876.008]:

```text
Act as a senior Google Ads strategist working for eCommerce and DTC brands.

1. Business summary from the website alone: Describe what the company sells, its main product category, the problems its customers face, its core benefits and unique selling points, its trust signals, current offers, pricing and guarantees, and any compliance limits (claims that cannot appear in ads).

2. High-volume keyword themes: Using that summary, group keyword themes by product sold, priority and search intent. Keep each ad group narrow enough that matching ad copy can be written for it. For every theme, state its intent stage and priority. Never invent keywords nobody searches for. Mark every theme that still needs search volume confirmation.
```

## Microsoft/Bing Ads

### Role of Microsoft Ads in the account

- Microsoft Advertising, formerly Bing Ads, is Microsoft's paid search platform and an alternative to Google Ads. Its ads mainly appear on bing.com. [L1034.001]
- Roughly one in three web searches takes place on Bing, so it is a sizeable additional traffic source next to a Google Ads account. [L0866.001]
- Microsoft Ads is an advanced paid search channel to add later, not part of the core setup. It only makes sense once Google Ads is maxed out. [L0544.005]
- Pause Bing Ads until Google Shopping is profitable, then move the proven campaigns over to Bing. [L0804.078]
- Microsoft and Bing ads should not take part of the starting budget. Add them once campaigns are profitable and profits are being reinvested. [L0360.034]
- Bing produces real sales with a good return on ad spend, but it is weaker than Google. Focus on Google first and add Bing once Google performs. [L0855.019]
- Much of Bing's search volume likely comes from people who kept the default search engine preinstalled on a new PC and never changed it. Paid reach on Bing is therefore smaller but still profitable. [L1034.004, L1034.003]
- Bing works almost like a copy of Google Ads. Account structure, campaign logic and optimization habits transfer directly, so little new learning is needed. [L0866.002]
- Product feed, conversion tracking and campaigns move to Bing as one set with the same logic. The existing Google setup does not need to be rebuilt from zero. [L0866.010]
- Google and Microsoft do not share data. Past results on one platform do not show what Google will do. [L0472.009]
- If an account that sold well on one platform gets very few conversions on Google from thousands of clicks, the setup or traffic type is likely wrong. [L0472.009]

### Account setup

#### Sign-up (detailed route, ads.microsoft.com)

1. Open ads.microsoft.com and click `Sign up now`. If you already have an account, log in. If not, click the option to create one. [L1035.002]
2. Enter an email address. Use the same email address as your Google Ads account. [L1035.002, L1035.003]
3. Set up the account, then click `switch to expert mode`, as in the Google Ads setup. [L1035.002, L1035.004]
4. Enter your business information. Set the primary use of the account to `promote this business` (your own business). [L1035.002, L1035.005]
5. Accept the Terms and Conditions (a link to read them is provided) and click `create account`. [L1035.002]
6. On the next screen, do not import from Google yet. Click `skip campaign creation`. It sits at the top of the page. [L1035.002, L1035.011, L1035.006]
7. Enter your business location (address) and tax information, then enter your billing information. [L1035.002]
8. In the billing options, choose `Post-pay`. Post-pay means you pay after you have spent money on ads. [L1035.002, L1035.008]
9. Select `Credit or debit card` as the payment method and enter your card details. [L1035.002, L1035.009]
10. Confirm. The new account screen opens. It is empty at this stage, which is expected. [L1035.002]

#### Sign-up (short route)

1. Search for Bing Ads and go directly to the Bing Ads site. [L0866.003]
2. Click to sign up and create an account. [L0866.003]
3. Verify the email address, then complete the captcha. [L0866.003]
4. Enter the company name. [L0866.003]
5. Enter a business phone number. [L0866.003]
6. Select the option to manage your own accounts. [L0866.003]

#### Setup rules

- Use the same email address for Microsoft Advertising as for Google Ads, so both accounts stay linked to one identity. [L1035.003]
- Entering business address, tax and billing details does not charge anything, because no ads are running yet. [L1035.007]
- Microsoft Advertising offers `Post-pay` or `Prepay`. Choose `Post-pay` as described above. [L1035.008]
- The Bing Ads campaign screens can still look like the old AdWords layout after an import. This is cosmetic and does not mean the import failed. [L0866.005]
- Bing may ask for a credit card during account setup. It can be skipped for now while the imported campaigns are still set up. [L0866.004]
- Setup order: sign up for Bing Ads, Bing Webmaster Tools and Merchant Center, then create the first Bing Shopping campaign. [L0393.014]
- Bing Webmaster Tools and Merchant Center are set up alongside Bing Ads. Merchant Center supplies the product data that Bing Shopping campaigns use. [L0393.015]
- Next step after the account exists: create the Microsoft Merchant Center account. Products are submitted there before any Google Ads campaigns are imported. [L1035.012]

#### Sign-up import option: sources differ

- Source A says that during Bing account setup you should use the import-from-Google option so the existing Google campaigns appear inside the Bing account. [L0866.004]
- Source B says to skip campaign creation at first setup, because importing from Google requires logging in to Google and only works correctly after Microsoft Merchant Center is set up and products are submitted. [L1035.006, L1035.011]
- When each applies: use Source B if Merchant Center is not yet set up. Use Source A's import option once Merchant Center is in place and you are importing. [L0866.004, L1035.006]

#### Vouchers and credits

- Microsoft Advertising sometimes offers voucher codes that give new accounts ad credits. Availability changes, so search for current `Microsoft advertising vouchers` on bing.com. [L1035.001]
- Older advice (2020): Microsoft Advertising offered a $100 credit for new accounts. Search for the current version of the offer, since the URLs change often. [L0852.070, older 2020]

### Microsoft Merchant Center

#### What it is

- Microsoft Merchant Center is the Microsoft counterpart to Google Merchant Center. It holds store information and the product feed used by Microsoft Shopping ads on Bing. [L1037.004]
- Microsoft Merchant Center is where products must be set up and submitted before importing Google Ads campaigns into Microsoft Advertising for Shopping. [L1035.010]
- The Merchant Center setup follows the same logic as Google Merchant Center: store details and shipping first, products after. The product feed is only submitted once the account is complete. [L1037.005]
- A Microsoft Advertising account must exist before a Merchant Center store can be created, because the Merchant Center link is opened from inside that account. The new store is attached to the main Microsoft Advertising account. [L1037.014]

#### Store creation procedure

1. Log in to the Microsoft Advertising account and click the Merchant Center link in the header menu. [L1037.001, L1037.002]
2. On the empty welcome screen (no stores yet), click `Create store`. [L1037.001]
3. Enter the store name. [L1037.001]
4. For domain validation, select the Bing Webmaster Tools account that already holds the store's destination URL. [L1037.001]
5. Add a store description. [L1037.001]
6. Answer yes to secure checkout and click `Next`. [L1037.001, L1037.007]
7. Select `Block` for aggregators and click `Next`. [L1037.001, L1037.009]
8. Choose the language and enter the store's contact email. [L1037.001]
9. Answer no to best-practice emails if the main account email already receives them, then click `Create store`. [L1037.001, L1037.011]
10. Open the store's settings from the main account, go to shipping settings, turn on free shipping, enter a minimum purchase price (0 if there is none), and click `Submit`. Products are not uploaded in this step. [L1037.001, L1037.002, L1037.012, L1037.013]

#### Store settings details

- Store description works like a short About Us page. It tells shoppers what the store is and who runs it. The field shows a remaining character count. A real business should use more of it to explain what it sells and what makes it different. [L1037.006]
- Turn on secure checkout when creating the store. [L1037.007]
- Aggregators collect product offers from many often unrelated businesses. By default they can include your product feed in their ads. Blocking aggregators keeps your products out of their Bing ads. [L1037.008]
- Block aggregators during store setup. The extra explanation is available by hovering over the question mark next to the option. [L1037.009]
- Use a dedicated support email address on the store's own domain as the contact email. [L1037.010]
- Set the minimum purchase price for free shipping to 0 if there is no minimum order value. Free shipping is switched on in the store's shipping settings. [L1037.012]
- Do not upload products during Merchant Center setup. The account must be complete first, and the feed is submitted afterwards. [L1037.013]
- Right after the store is created, it appears under the main account with no items listed. The list stays empty until a feed is submitted, so an empty store at this stage is normal. [L1037.015]

#### Product feed for Bing

- Sources differ on whether the Bing merchant account carries over from Google. Source A says it does not and must be created again from scratch, because assuming it comes across leaves Shopping ads without a working feed. [L0866.006]
- Source B says one feed app connection can supply products to both Google and Bing. The connection screen lets you pick an existing Merchant Center store or create a new one from inside the app. [L1036.011, L1036.012]
- When each applies: if you have no Microsoft Merchant Center store, create one (Source A). If you do, pick it in the app's connection screen (Source B). [L0866.006, L1036.012]
- Before connecting a Shopify store to Bing Shopping through the feed app, a Microsoft Advertising account and a Merchant Center store should already exist. [L1036.012]
- Feed procedure:
  1. Use the same process that was used to create the Google Shopping feed. [L0866.007]
  2. Open a Shopify app that builds the feed inside the store. The same feed app serves Google Shopping and Bing Shopping. [L0866.007, L1036.011]
  3. Log in to the app and set up the feed. [L0866.007]
  4. In the app, go to `Settings > Bing Shopping Settings`. The only option that needs changing is the `sale price with price` checkbox, which must be checked. Leave the other Bing Shopping options at their defaults. [L1036.014]
  5. Sync the feed with Bing Ads. [L0866.007]
  6. Check that the product feed is now available in Bing Ads. [L0866.007]
- After a successful import, products show the status `pending`. This alone is not an error and confirms that the feed was received. [L1036.010]

### Store verification

Procedure for verifying the store for Bing:

1. When Bing asks for the store name, first set up the store in Bing Webmaster Tools. [L0866.009]
2. Return to Bing Ads once the store is set up there. The remaining fields fill in automatically. [L0866.009]
3. When Bing asks for the product feed, select the feed that was already created. [L0866.009]

- Domain validation in Merchant Center uses the Bing Webmaster Tools account that already holds the destination URL. [L1037.001]
- Bing Webmaster Tools and Microsoft Merchant Center support the Bing Shopping campaign, which runs alongside Google. [L0532.018]
- Bing Webmaster Tools also shows organic Bing search terms. [L0834.072]

### Import from Google Ads

#### Why import, and what not to do

- Existing Google Ads campaigns can be imported into Microsoft Advertising. This takes much less work than building them from scratch. Budgets are then set lower than on Google. [L1034.002]
- Do not use Auto Import when importing campaigns from Google Ads to Microsoft Advertising. Auto Import copies everything in your Google account and becomes unmanageable once you have many campaigns. [L0302.001]
- Use `Import Specific Campaigns and Ad Groups` to choose exactly which campaigns to copy. [L0302.001, L0302.003]
- Sources differ on ongoing sync. Source A says Auto Import should not be used (above). Source B says below about $5,000 monthly ad spend, export the Google Ads campaigns straight into Bing Ads, because later changes in Google Ads are then updated automatically in Bing Ads. [L0302.001, L0866.011]
- When each applies: the import settings in the procedure below cover the choice of campaigns. Source B's automatic updates depend on `apply updates to existing items` being checked (the import option in step 12). The sources do not give a threshold for Auto Import itself. [L0302.005, L0866.011]
- Above about $5,000 monthly ad spend, do the initial import and then optimize Bing Ads using its own performance data. Repeated imports from Google Ads become less useful once Bing has enough data of its own. [L0866.012]
- Example signal that Bing has enough own data: a Bing conversion rate of around 1% combined with regularly around 100 clicks. Then optimizing on Bing's own numbers can replace constant importing from Google Ads. [L0866.013]

#### Import procedure

1. Log in to Microsoft Advertising. [L0302.010]
2. Click `Import` in the header menu. [L0302.010]
3. Select `Import from Google Ads`. [L0302.010]
4. Sign in to the Google account linked to your Google Ads account. [L0302.010]
5. Click `Continue`. [L0302.010]
6. Change `Schedule` from `Auto` to `Once` and set the time to `Right Now` (your timezone). [L0302.010, L0302.002]
7. Click `Customize Import`. [L0302.010]
8. Select `Import Specific Campaigns and Ad Groups`, not `import all existing and new campaigns`. [L0302.010, L0302.003]
9. Search for and select the campaigns you want to copy (for example, your Alpha and Beta campaigns). [L0302.010, L0302.003]
10. Click `Next`. [L0302.010]
11. Uncheck `account level URL options`. [L0302.010, L0302.004]
12. Check the three sync options: sync items not previously added to your Microsoft account, apply updates to existing items, and remove items from Microsoft Advertising if they were deleted from Google Ads. [L0302.010, L0302.005]
13. Select your UET tag from the Google Shopping app, so conversion data from Bing Shopping feeds into your Microsoft Advertising account. [L0302.010, L0302.006]
14. Uncheck the bid and budget minimums options (`Increase any of our bids to reach minimums for Microsoft Advertising`, `Update Bid Strategies`, `Increase Campaign Budgets to the minimum`). [L0302.010, L0302.007]
15. Select `Customize Budgets for Microsoft Advertising` and reduce by 80%. [L0302.010, L0302.008]
16. Click `Next`. [L0302.010]
17. Name the import (for example, Alpha Beta Import). [L0302.010]
18. Set it to email on errors. [L0302.010]
19. Click `Run Import Now`. [L0302.010]
20. Wait for product feed approval in Microsoft Merchant Center. It may show pending while images are crawled. [L0302.010, L0302.011]
21. Once approved, check the account weekly to review numbers, add negative keywords and adjust bids. [L0302.010, L0302.012]

#### Import settings explained

- Uncheck account level URL options. Leaving it checked transfers URL tracking from Google to Bing, which incorrectly attributes Bing sales to your Google Ads account. [L0302.004]
- The UET tag must be connected to the Google Shopping app in the Microsoft Advertising Conversion section. Select this tag during import setup. [L0302.006]

#### Pending approval

- Do not expect imported Bing campaigns to run immediately while the feed is pending approval in Merchant Center. The feed may show `pending according to image crawling` until Microsoft approves all product images and data. [L0302.011]
- Campaigns show Delivery errors until approval completes. Wait for the feed status to turn green before expecting ad delivery. [L0302.011]

#### Other import routes

- To set up Bing ads from an existing Google setup:
  1. Import your campaigns from your Google account to Bing. [L0972.065]
  2. Lower the budget for the Bing campaigns. [L0972.065]
  3. Keep using the product images from your product pages. No separate assets are needed. [L0972.065]
- To launch Bing Shopping from an existing Google feed:
  1. Submit the same product feed you use for Google to Bing Ads. This can be done within about an hour if it is already clean. [L1328.034]
  2. Import your Google Shopping campaigns into Bing Ads. The platform supports this with one action. [L1328.034]
  3. Review the imported bids and segmentation before turning the campaigns on. [L1328.034]
- Remarketing audiences must be created inside Microsoft Ads. Shopping campaigns can be transferred from Google Ads without creating new audiences. [L1283.028]
- Older advice (2022): if import errors occur:
  1. Open the Microsoft Merchant Center account in Microsoft Ads. [L1092.073, older 2022]
  2. Delete the existing Google Ads integrations, but do not delete the accounts themselves. [L1092.073, older 2022]
  3. Re-add the integrations and confirm the correct Merchant Center accounts are selected, since linking the wrong account causes data errors. [L1092.073, older 2022]

### Budgets relative to Google

Sources agree that the Bing budget should be lower than the Google budget. They give different ratios because each uses a different base.

| Starting point | Bing budget | Base | Year of advice | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| First import of Google campaigns | Reduce imported budgets by 80%, which leaves 20% | Imported Google budgets | Undated | L0302.008, L0302.009, L0302.010 |
| Import into a new Microsoft account | About 75% lower, which is 25% of Google | Google daily budget | 2024 | L0666.040 |
| Launch with Google daily budget | 25% of the Google Ads daily budget | Google Ads daily budget | 2026 | L0808.032 |
| Ratio by search volume | About 25% of Google budgets | Google alpha and beta budgets | 2021, older | L0671.092, L0671.229 |
| Shopping budget | 15 to 20% of Google Shopping daily budget. Bing can be left unfunded at first | Google Shopping daily budget | 2023 | L0855.018 |
| Proportional to traffic | About 25% to 30% of Google's traffic. Google keeps the larger share | Traffic that Bing brings | 2022, older | L0854.043, L0854.118 |
| Total ad budget | Start with about 10% of total ad budget, optimize there, then scale | Total ad budget | 2024 | L0856.034 |
| Secondary platform | $15 per day. If it does not pay off, drop to about $5 per day to keep visibility | Fixed daily amount | 2024 | L1285.052 |
| Troubleshooting unprofitable traffic | Cut the total budget to about $10 until settings are fixed | Fixed total | 2025 | L0857.009 |
| Unfunded start | No budget until Google is profitable | Google profitability | 2023, 2024 | L0855.018, L0360.034, L0855.019 |

Examples:

- $100 per day on Google becomes $25 per day on Bing. [L0666.040, L0671.093, L0671.230]
- $100 per day on Google Shopping gives $15 to $30 per day on Bing. [L0855.018]
- Setting Bing to $400 with a $100 Google budget would skew results. [L0671.093, L0671.230]

Rules for picking a value:

- For a first import, start with the 80% reduction. The procedure's test is whether Bing delivers any impressions and clicks before committing larger spend. [L0302.008, L0302.009]
- The 80% reduction leaves 20% of the Google budget, which is the top of the 15 to 20% range given for Shopping. [L0302.008, L0855.018]
- The 25% figures (2026, and the 2021 volume ratio) and the 15 to 20% figure (2023) use different bases. Use the one that matches how your budget is set. [L0808.032, L0671.092, L0855.018]
- If the budget is set as a share of total spend, start at about 10%. [L0856.034]
- If Microsoft spends more than Google despite higher Google budgets, the Google daily budget is not being spent. See Bids and CPC below. [L0837.021]

Cuts and pauses:

- If Microsoft Ads costs are high while its sales are low compared with Google, cut its budget sharply or turn it off. Focus on Google Shopping first. [L0854.118, older 2022]
- Restart Microsoft Ads only once the Google campaigns are profitable. Size its budget in proportion to the traffic it brings, which is typically about 25% to 30% of Google's. [L0854.118, older 2022]
- Traffic relation: Microsoft Ads usually brings about 25% to 30% of the traffic that Google brings. Its spend should be proportional to that, and Google should get the larger share because it typically has the better ROAS. [L0854.043, older 2022]
- Share of searches: roughly one in three web searches takes place on Bing. This is a share of all searches, not a share of Google's traffic. [L0866.001]

### Bids and CPC

- Launch Microsoft Ads with 25% of your Google Ads daily budget. Set the cost-per-click to match your Google Ads cost-per-click, and adjust it as data comes in. [L0808.032]
- Older advice (2021): a Bing account received advice to raise every CPC to $2. The better approach was a small increase of about 5 cents, because Google campaigns already produced clicks at 60 cents. [L0962.061, older 2021]
- If Microsoft Ads spends more than Google Ads despite higher Google budgets, the Google daily budget is not being spent. This usually means the default CPC is too low. Raise the Google Ads default CPC by about 10 cents. [L0837.021]
- Older advice (2020): if Google impressions are low while Bing shows many impressions for the same products, check the keyword triggers and product matches in both accounts. Bing clicks are often cheaper, so raising the Google cost per click can increase impressions. [L1111.105, older 2020]
- Bing clicks cheaper than Google is part of why Bing can add impressions at low cost. Keep the bid adjustments small and check results after each change. [L1111.105, L0962.061]

### Targeting

- Bing Ads supports the same geo-targeting options as Google Ads and Meta: individual zip codes, whole states, or a radius around a city. Use these instead of a country-wide target when a supplier's shipping cost makes distant customers unprofitable. [L0942.030]
- Before adding budget to a campaign with traffic but no sales, check its location and other settings. A campaign with about 5,944 clicks from very low spend and zero sales points to the wrong traffic, often from targeting many countries where clicks are cheap. [L0857.008]

### Suspensions and reinstatement

#### Why it happens

- New Microsoft Ads accounts are often suspended automatically within a day or two of creation, sometimes on the same day, for a vague policy reason with no specific details. [L0373.004]
- This happens even when the store is compliant. A suspension alone does not mean the advertiser did something wrong. [L0373.004]
- A new account may be suspended the next day with a notice citing an egregious policy violation and a list of possible causes, without saying which one applies. Treat this as a common platform issue and appeal it, rather than assuming the store broke a rule. [L0373.022]
- Microsoft Ads commonly suspends new accounts. Resolve any Google issues first, then pursue the Microsoft suspension. [L0855.146]

#### Appeal procedures

Procedure A (if a new account is suspended):

1. Check the store against a platform compliance checklist. [L0373.005]
2. Submit an appeal through the account. [L0373.005]
3. Wait for a human reviewer to visit the site, which usually leads to reinstatement. [L0373.005]

Procedure B (reinstatement after an immediate suspension, 2024):

1. Visit the Microsoft support page every two to three days. [L0360.051]
2. Request help, say that the store follows all policies, and ask for a human review of the store. [L0360.051]
3. Keep repeating until a reviewer who can look at the store is reached (about one week in one case). [L0360.051]

Procedure C (new account closed automatically without a clear reason, 2023):

1. Set a daily reminder for the same time each day. [L0804.113]
2. Send a message to Bing support every day. [L0804.113]
3. Try live chat and open support tickets as well. [L0804.113]
4. Keep following up until a human reviews the account, because new accounts are often flagged by automated checks. [L0804.113]

- For repeated suspensions, request live chat again and ask for a different representative. [L0855.146]

#### Merchant Center flags

- Older advice (2022): Microsoft Merchant Center can flag a store for professional services or unallowed characters in product data. Tobacco or e-cigarette ads are also flagged. [L0803.102, older 2022]
- Some flags cannot be appealed from inside the account. Contact Microsoft support directly and ask for a manual review. [L0803.102, older 2022]

#### Using Microsoft as a backup

- Older advice (2022): if Google Shopping is blocked by a suspension, use Microsoft as a backup traffic source:
  1. Set up a Microsoft store. [L0963.159, older 2022]
  2. Create a Microsoft Shopping campaign. The traffic volume is smaller, but the campaign can still be profitable. [L0963.159, older 2022]
- Case (Google account suspended): a Shopify store open since January with over 100 orders sold only through Microsoft Ads. Net profit was about 10 to 15%, around $2,000 in September. [L1116.062]
- Case (Merchant Center and Google Ads suspended): a store with about 200 products from seven brands ran Alpha and Beta campaigns on its full catalog across Google and Microsoft. Microsoft received about twice the spend of Google. See Optimization for the outcome and advice. [L0941.074]

### Ad formats and tracking

- Microsoft Advertising offers search text ads, the Bing counterpart to Google search text ads. They carry a small `Ad` label above the listing. [L1034.007]
- Microsoft Advertising offers Shopping ads, the Bing counterpart to Google Shopping. They show when a user searches for a product, or a keyword related to a product sold in the store. [L1034.008]
- Microsoft Shopping ads work the same way as Google Shopping. Set up Shopping ads after the search text campaigns and the organic webmaster setup. [L1034.011]
- Older advice (2020): Bing Ads offers search text ads and other formats that copy Google's types. Import the Google campaigns into Bing and check Google first if Bing shows errors. [L0468.119, older 2020]
- Conversion tracking is set up by adding Microsoft tags to the site as described in the Microsoft setup section of the advanced ads material. [L0855.147]
- Connect the UET tag to the Google Shopping app in the Microsoft Advertising Conversion section. [L0302.006]
- Bing search terms appear in the Microsoft Advertising dashboard. [L0834.072, older 2021]

### Optimization

#### Core rule

- Optimize Bing Shopping campaigns weekly when first starting. Review performance numbers, identify negative keywords to add, and adjust bids up or down based on results. Treat Bing management the same as Google Ads optimization after import. [L0302.012]
- Microsoft Ads is optimized with the same actions as Google Ads: search term review, negative keywords and budget changes. Only the interface differs, so the Google Ads workflow can be applied directly. [L0807.019]
- The same optimization rules used for Google Ads also apply to Microsoft Ads (Bing). [L0857.007]
- The same Google Ads campaign optimization steps also apply to Microsoft Ads (Bing). The same tweaks can be made on both platforms before raising bids. Microsoft Ads should still be left out of the starting budget until campaigns are profitable. [L0360.088]
- Microsoft Ads responds to the same optimization as Google Ads, so apply the same Google Ads optimization process to Microsoft campaigns. [L1116.031]

#### Negative keywords (older advice)

- On Microsoft Ads, removing negative keywords has a different impact than on Google Ads. If you have high impression share but low CTR and want to improve visibility, remove some negative keywords on Microsoft specifically before increasing bid. [L0272.059, older 2022]

#### Troubleshooting an unprofitable campaign

- A Bing campaign that sends unprofitable traffic should be cut to about $10 in total until the settings are fixed. [L0857.009]
- Check the campaign's location and other settings before adding budget. [L0857.008]

#### Case: lowering spend on a losing account

- Case (2025): the owner of a store with over 100 orders feared paying too much per click and had not raised spend. The account had about 1,100 clicks from about 75,000 impressions on $650 of spend, on a shared $20 daily budget that was always maxed out. [L1116.062]
- Advice given: do not raise the budget yet. Review which products and keywords convert profitably and which do not, move budget toward the profitable ones, let the account run for a couple of weeks, confirm that return on ad spend rises, and only then increase the budget. [L1116.062]
- No final result was reported in the call. [L1116.062]

#### Case: Microsoft spend exceeded Google's return

- Case: Microsoft received about twice the spend of Google, yet Google had the better return. Google had four conversions from 566 pounds of spend, and total sales were reported around 4,400 pounds from 10 conversions. [L0941.074]
- Advice given: keep Microsoft off until extra profit covers it. Run Google only, review which products already sold, and lower CPC on products that spent at least 50 without converting. [L0941.074]

### Scaling

#### Scale only when proven

- Bing Ads should be added after the core setup and only when Google performs. [L0855.019, L0544.005]
- Pause Bing Ads until Google Shopping is profitable, then move the proven campaigns to Bing. [L0804.078]
- Older advice (2022): restart Microsoft Ads only once the Google campaigns are profitable. [L0854.118, older 2022]

#### Stepwise scaling procedure

1. Check which products and keywords convert profitably and which do not. [L1116.033]
2. Move budget away from non-converting or unprofitable keywords and products toward the most profitable ones. [L1116.033]
3. Let the adjusted account run for a couple of weeks. [L1116.033]
4. Confirm that return on ad spend improved. [L1116.033]
5. Only then increase the daily budget. [L1116.033]

- Increase budgets gradually. If results are positive after the 80% test, raise budgets step by step. [L0302.009]
- Start with about 10% of the total ad budget, optimize there, and only then scale. [L0856.034]

#### Scaling by account spend

- Below about $5,000 monthly ad spend, export Google Ads campaigns straight into Bing Ads, and later changes in Google Ads update automatically. [L0866.011]
- Above about $5,000 monthly ad spend, do the initial import and then optimize Bing on its own data. [L0866.012]
- Signal that Bing has enough own data: around 1% conversion rate with regularly around 100 clicks. [L0866.013]

#### Case: restarting after losses

- Case: a store with about 200 products restarts at about 30 per day on five to ten proven products. [L0941.074]
- It improves product pages, expands the product list later, and adds Microsoft back at a much smaller budget. [L0941.074]

#### Secondary platform budget

- A secondary search platform such as Bing can run at $15 a day. If it does not pay off, drop it to about $5 a day to keep visibility until profits can support more spend. [L1285.052]

### Market background data

Dated figures from older sources, to be used as background only:

- As of 2015 (older data): about one in three US searches happened on Bing, and Google had about 65% of US search share. Google and Bing together reached about 95% of the US market, so skipping Bing meant missing a large share of buyers. [L1328.033, dated 2015]
- For the period around 2018 (older data): Bing Ads ad spend grew 32% year over year in Q4. Bing handled about one in three US searches. [L1455.010, dated 2018]
- For the same period (older data): audience-based Google search ad clicks grew 34% year over year, so audience targeting became a larger part of search campaigns. [L1455.010, dated 2018]

## Account Suspensions, Appeals and Google Support

### Why Accounts Get Suspended

#### Merchant Center: Misrepresentation and Data Mismatches

- Google suspends Merchant Center accounts mainly for five reasons: business information that does not match the website, incomplete product data, missing required business information on the website, incomplete Merchant Center settings, and products in prohibited categories. A suspension is not a deletion; the account is only blocked from use. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.002]
- Suspensions often carry the reason misrepresentation, which means Google believes some information is missing or wrong. Suspension notices arrive by email to the business email address set up for the account. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.008]
- A suspension is a legitimacy check, not a final verdict. Google suspends to protect searchers and to screen out scam or low-quality stores. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.025]
- New accounts are checked most strictly and are often suspended almost immediately. Established accounts can also be suspended after two years or more of trading. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.025]
- Google tightened account security after the e-commerce boom in 2020, so suspensions can also hit legitimate sellers. A suspension can be reversed, so fix the cause and request reinstatement rather than panic. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0731.004]
- Common causes of suspension are shipping or tax information in Merchant Center that does not match the Shopify store, product prices in the catalog that do not match the store, missing contact information, and a missing privacy policy. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0801.072]
- Missing or inconsistent contact details can cause a contact-information suspension. The contact page should offer at least two contact methods, such as a phone number, an email address or a contact form, plus a privacy policy. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0801.071]
- A currency mismatch, missing contact details or a missing privacy policy can flag an account. Fix these and then appeal. *(Older advice, 2020.)* [L0468.118]
- A missing or unverified business phone number in Merchant Center is a recurring trigger for misrepresentation. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0247.060, L0962.067, L0429.080]
- Shipping costs, the shipping policy and the privacy policy URLs in Merchant Center must match what appears in the Shopify store, because Google bots add products to cart to check this. [L0856.035]
- Footer social links that point to Shopify social pages or to platform home pages, instead of your own profiles, were a known cause of a Merchant Center suspension. Change them to your own profiles or remove them, then resubmit. *(Advice from 2023.)* [L0934.072]
- Misrepresentation often comes from missing policy pages and content. Make sure the store has all required policies and pages. *(Older advice, 2022.)* [L1281.107]
- Vague or missing wording in shipping and return policies is a common cause of a suspension without a clear reason. Check that both policies are clear and complete. [L0808.025]
- Never invent a GTIN or enter a third-party GTIN that does not belong to the product. Google treats a mismatched GTIN as misrepresentation, which can lead to suspension. [L1283.038]
- A missing GTIN alone does not cause a misrepresentation suspension. The problem arises only when a wrong identifier is placed in the GTIN field. [L1283.039]
- A contact detail or policy that differs even slightly from the Merchant Center entry can trigger misrepresentation. Example: a suite number written differently. Compare address, phone, email and every policy character by character with the store. [L1283.045]
- A Merchant Center suspension can have many causes. Check the GTIN, verified phone number, shipping, return and privacy policies, and product detail content, and use the full checklist before escalating to support. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0469.095]
- Installed dropshipping apps alone were not considered a cause of account rejection. The likely trigger is a red flag on the store that a Google bot detects as dropshipping. [L0577.054]
- Blocking Google's checkout crawler to hide abandoned checkouts also leads to automatic feed suspension. Do not try to block it. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1170.040]
- Test ads with fake URLs or non-existent websites can get a Google Ads account suspended. Ads must point to the business website linked to the account. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.012]

#### Google Ads: Account-Level Reasons

- Google Ads accounts are suspended for specific reasons: incorrect business information; multiple Google Ads accounts tied to the same business or personal information, including old dormant accounts after a prior suspension; a payment method flagged as fraudulent or previously bounced; and ads that point to a URL other than the business website or to a website that does not exist. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.009]
- A Google Ads suspension applies to the whole advertiser account and every related account. While suspended, you cannot open new accounts, and ads stop running on Search, search partner sites and the Display Network at the same time. A store that relies on one paid channel can lose all paid traffic at once. [L0380.033]
- Google can flag an ad account as restricted in a country where the advertiser does not sell or advertise. This is usually an automated error. *(Older advice, 2022.)* [L0803.103]
- For suspected bot clicks, contact Google support by live chat for the recommended course of action before relying on a click-blocking tool alone. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L1279.068]
- A Google Ads suspension for suspicious payment activity is usually caused by billing details that do not match the account, which is covered in the appeal steps below. [L0806.067]

#### Circumventing Systems and Linked Accounts

- The circumventing systems suspension usually occurs when Google believes a new account was opened after a previous account was closed. [L1283.043]
- The circumventing flag often appears when a previously suspended account used the same billing address, credit card or website as a new account. Creating a new account to get around a policy triggers this flag. [L0857.014]
- Google can link new ad accounts to earlier ones through IP address, cookies, name, address and card details. Creating a new ad account after a suspension therefore usually fails. *(Older advice, 2022.)* [L0963.019]
- A suspension on one platform does not automatically affect other platforms. Accounts on Microsoft, Facebook, TikTok, Pinterest and Instagram can keep running. *(Older advice, 2022.)* [L0963.020]
- Using agency accounts to circumvent bans on Google Merchant Center is not recommended. It can lead to a cycle of banned accounts and costs a lot of money. [L0577.050]
- Only use.com domains for the store. Do not switch to a.store or.us domain to fix a Google Ads policy problem, because changing domains to get around a flag can look like circumventing systems. [L0857.012]
- The circumventing flag can be a false flag when a new account was opened after a previously closed account. If you never had an earlier account, appeal the suspension instead of creating a new one. [L0965.007]

### Response Procedure After a Suspension

#### First Steps

1. Do not reply immediately, and do not reply in anger. [L0727.013]
2. Read the suspension reason in Google's email. It may be a warning giving 7 days to fix the issue, or an immediate suspension. [L0727.013]
3. Check that the business information in the account is complete. [L0727.013]
4. Make sure the website follows the business launch checklist. [L0727.013]
5. Check product data in the feed for disapproved products and missing attributes. [L0727.013]
6. Make sure shipping, tax, phone number and other account information match the website exactly. [L0727.013]
7. Delete old, unused Google Ads accounts. [L0727.013, L0727.009]
8. Submit a detailed, neutral response through the form or avenue in Google's email, explaining what was checked and changed and asking for a review. [L0727.013]
9. Expect a review within one to two days, sometimes up to a week. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.013]
10. Unsuspension responses must be neutral and factual. An angry or terse reply makes the problem worse and delays the review. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0727.014]
11. When a Merchant Center issue is unclear, respond calmly, check the official Google policy pages, and ask an expert or coach rather than attempting a risky fix alone. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0730.018]

#### Merchant Center Recovery (Current Method)

1. Read the compliance checklist lesson and confirm every recommended setting is in place. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L1279.067]
2. Log in to Merchant Center and click through all settings, making sure each is complete. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.068]
3. Check the phone number under contact info in Merchant Center settings. [L1279.067]
4. Check whether the business phone number is verified. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.068]
5. Verify the phone number. Depending on what Merchant Center offers, use the verification by text message [L0247.060], the automated call [L0962.068], or the PIN sent by phone call [L1279.067]. *(Older advice, 2021.)*
6. Reply to Google's suspension email and request a review. In the source example, reinstatement came the same day. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.068, L0962.067]
7. Follow up with Google until the account is reinstated. [L1279.067]

#### Merchant Center: Full Review Request

1. Log in to Google Merchant Center. [L1094.042]
2. Add the return policy and make the other changes Google asked for. [L1094.042]
3. Find the request review option, which may appear in the first email Google sent. [L1094.042]
4. Submit the request. After the first few reviews, Google may impose a waiting period of about one week before the next submission. [L1094.042]
5. Before requesting review, correct all mismatches. The first suspension round is usually handled by an algorithm, and a human reviews the store only after a manual review request. [L1283.046]
6. Read the reason Google gives and fix the mismatched item. [L1283.044]
7. Check that every setting and policy in Merchant Center matches the store exactly. [L1283.044]
8. Submit for a review. If suspended again, request a manual review. [L1283.044]
9. In the manual review request, list each correction you made and state that you checked all Google policies. [L1283.044]
10. Do not request a review again until the problems are fixed. [L0962.069]
11. After a Merchant Center suspension is fixed, wait for Google's review result before changing other platforms. Once confirmed, make sure the same errors do not repeat on Microsoft, Bing or Meta. [L0934.073]
12. Prepare the fix before appealing, so the first appeal succeeds. A failed appeal can be resubmitted. [L0934.074]
13. Manual review requests for suspended products are typically decided within 24 to 48 hours. Use them when a flag appears to be an algorithm misreading rather than a true violation. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1170.045]

#### Merchant Center: Standard Template

Use this message when requesting a Google Merchant Center account review after a suspension. Replace each bracketed placeholder with the real information and keep every sentence in the same order:

```
To whom this may concern,

We are submitting our store for review after our account was initially suspended for [reason] on [date]. We understand that our initial submission was missing [issues]. All of these issues have now been addressed in their entirety. After reviewing all of the Google Merchant Center terms of service, we now believe our site is in full compliance with your policies. [List each change you made to meet compliance.]

Thank you for your time and review.
```
[L1094.043]

#### Google Ads: Response Routine

1. Identify the suspension reason first by contacting support. Do not create a new Google Ads account with the same email, card on file or URL. [L0278.005]
