2. Look at posts with millions of views and note their intros, hooks and how they grab attention. [L0561.008]
3. Filter results by most likes or views for a keyword, such as lamps, and study what the top posts do. [L0561.008]
4. Pull relevant niche hashtags and follow trending sounds. [L0561.008]
5. Copy the structural style, such as transitions, hooks or controversy, not the exact content. [L0561.008]

### Creative Center and Video Ideas

- The TikTok Creative Center is a tool for seeing what ads and creatives other brands run on TikTok. [L0577.047]
- The Creative Center includes a video ideas section next to the search for top-performing ads in a niche. Use it for filming ideas after you have identified the winning hooks. [L1374.034]

### Checking Whether a Competitor Still Sells

Judge a competitor's TikTok product by its latest video, not its most-viewed one. [L0656.031]

1. Open the seller's most recent video, not the one with the most views. [L0656.031]
2. Read the comments in order of date and focus on those from the last week. [L0656.031]
3. Look for buying signals such as "where can I buy this", "I just bought one", "I placed an order" or "I really want one". [L0656.031]
4. Look for complaints such as "where is my order" or "why hasn't my order shipped", which point to fulfillment problems. [L0656.031]
5. Treat recent buying signals as evidence that the product is still selling, even if view counts are low. [L0656.031]

### Building a Research Feed on TikTok

Use a separate account for product discovery, not your business account. [L0708.032, L1444.024]

**Procedure A (hashtag-based feed):**

1. Create a new TikTok account for research only. [L0708.032]
2. Search and follow pages for hashtags such as tiktokmademebuyit, Amazon finds, exposing dropshippers, Etsy finds and eBay finds. [L0708.032]
3. Like and comment on the content to show TikTok your interest. [L0708.032]
4. The For You page fills with similar product content over time, which turns the account into an organic research feed. [L0708.032]

**Procedure B (daily engagement feed):**

1. Create a new account that is separate from your business account. [L1444.024]
2. Like, share, comment on and engage with product videos every day. [L1444.024]
3. Keep doing this until the For You page of that account is filled with product content. [L1444.024]
4. Use this account to spot new trends, and keep it separate from your business account. [L1444.024]

### Spying on TikTok Ads

- Sellercount and PPAds are spy tools for TikTok ads. [L0708.033]
- PPAds has a different library than Sellercount, so using both gives better coverage. [L0708.033]
- Use these filters in Sellercount or PPAds:

| Filter | Setting | Reason | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Post duration | 2, then 3, then 4 weeks | Many advertisers are moving from Facebook to TikTok | [L0708.034] |
| Engagement | 50k plus to 100k plus impressions | Proof of concept | [L0708.034] |

- An ad with 50k to 200k plus impressions suggests the advertiser has been spending roughly 500 to 1,000 dollars, which usually means the product is profitable for them. [L0708.035]
- Products with no clear profit signal should not be assumed profitable. [L0708.035]

### Finding Products That Sell Without an Audience

- The Low-Follower Sales Videos filter shows videos that sell even though the creator has few followers. [L1479.009]
- A product that sells this way does not depend on an existing audience, which makes it a stronger test candidate. [L1479.009]

### TikTok Shop and Video Reuse

- For a TikTok Shop video, the Magic AI search looks for Facebook ads that repurpose the same video, sorted by thumbnail similarity. [L0892.031]
- If no similar ads appear, it is unlikely that anyone has reused the video in paid ads. [L0892.031]
- The Videos & Ads view lets you download all listed videos with one button. [L0892.032]
- The lesson uses this to save a whole competitor video set at once. [L0892.032]

### Reach Signals

- TikTok open targeting reaches an audience of roughly 500 million to 800 million, sometimes up to about 1 billion people. [L0895.034]
- Because of this reach, high ad impression counts for a product are a positive sign for a seller. [L0895.034]

### Facebook Ad Library Cross-Checks

**When to use both platforms:**

- The Facebook Ad Library is not the only source of product video inspiration. TikTok searches can find better-performing videos for the same product. [L1172.045]
- Use both to find strong creatives. [L1172.045]

**When to skip the Facebook checks:**

| Check | TikTok product lists | Replacement rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Page creation date | Skip | None | [L1183.022] |
| Ad library scaling stages | Skip | None | [L1183.022] |
| Ads created within the last 14 days with strong likes and plays | Use | Treat as proof the product works | [L1183.022] |

- For TikTok product lists, skip the Facebook checks because TikTok has no equivalent ad library page. [L1183.022]
- List at least about 10 products to rank. [L1183.022]

### Saving Viral Videos

- Save the link, a screenshot and the view count of every viral video you research as soon as you see it. [L1385.022]
- Save immediately because the creator can later set videos to private or delete them. [L1385.022]
- A previously working link that now fails, combined with a changed account name or domain, signals that the account has pivoted. [L1385.022]

### Case Studies

#### Case 1: Two Look-Alike Bottle-Opener Stores

**Starting point:** A bottle-opener product was promoted by two TikTok accounts with about 41,000 and 19,000 followers. Each was linked to a Shopify store on a different domain, and the two stores looked almost identical. [L0656.032]

**Evidence that one operator ran both:**

- Store checks found no Terms of Service, no Privacy Policy and no full Contact Us page. [L0656.032]
- Both stores used a free default Shopify theme with default colors. [L0656.032]
- The product cost about 5 USD with shipping from AliExpress. [L0656.032]
- Both stores listed the same contact email. [L0656.032]
- Both accounts posted at the same times with the same clips, so the presenter treated them as one operator. [L0656.032]

**Timeline and sales estimate:**

- The older account began posting in June. The newer one began on 14 July, and about two weeks later one of its videos reached 1.7 million views. [L0656.032]
- The operator posted roughly once a day with gaps. [L0656.032]
- The presenter estimated sales only as a range of about 1,000 to 10,000 USD, since exact revenue cannot be seen from outside. [L0656.032]

**Store issues:**

- A leftover footer code line was visible. [L0656.032]
- The header was changed, but the default theme colors stayed in other sections. [L0656.032]
- There was no Shop Now button. [L0656.032]

#### Case 2: Drinks Product With Gaps in Posting

**Starting point:** A seller of a drinks-related product started posting on 26 April, first with two or three videos a day. [L0656.033]

**Posting pattern and results:**

- After 27 April there were no uploads until 11 May. [L0656.033]
- A video that reused a clip from an earlier post got only about 600 views. [L0656.033]
- The seller's best video reached 700,000 views, and a second one reached 500,000 views. [L0656.033]
- The account had only a few tens of thousands of followers at most, yet it kept posting about twice a day. [L0656.033]
- Comments asking where to buy the product suggested sales were still coming in. [L0656.033]

**Store issues:**

- The store had a visible HTML/CSS footer code line. [L0656.033]
- It had several pop-ups and heavy use of GIFs. [L0656.033]
- It used dark black and silver colors and lowercase brand lettering. [L0656.033]
- There was no Shop Now button, so buyers had to add to cart and then open a separate cart page. [L0656.033]
- The profile image did not show the product, which made the account look like a bot. [L0656.033]

**Conclusion:** The seller was probably still earning some sales despite low view counts. A new seller could beat those results with better consistency and cleaner content. [L0656.033]

## Hooks, Scripts and Video Structure

### Hook Design and First Seconds

#### The Opening Hook

- The first five seconds decide whether viewers keep watching; a weak opening makes people swipe away, so the hook must grab attention immediately [L0820.005].
- Retention rate is treated as the most important signal for pushing a video, so the first seconds deserve the most effort. Some early drop-off is normal, but the goal is to make the curve as flat as possible [L1186.024].
- Viewers often read on-screen text or an emoji in the first seconds before deciding to keep watching. A short caption with a visible emoji in the opening frame can hold attention for the hook [L1444.073].
- TikTok hooks need to be more shocking than standard ad hooks and should create curiosity that keeps the viewer watching. Other hook formats that work include before-and-after and point-of-view (POV) shots [L1427.007].
- A hook must promise something specific that the video then shows, so viewers stay to see whether it works [L1444.028].
- Proven hook structures can be borrowed from product videos in other niches, because the same opening works across different products. Copy the structure of the hook, not its exact wording, and adapt the content to your product [L1384.055].
- Virality depends more on video quality than on luck. An engaging hook, such as a surprising question that makes viewers want to finish, is a key driver [L1429.042].
- On TikTok, going viral depends on the hook, the wording, the angles and the sound choices in the video. Once these are found, they can be repeated across new videos [L1469.011].

#### Hook Pattern for a Short Product Video

Pattern: open with a short statement in the first seconds that makes viewers curious about a clear visible result, and keep the total length around seven seconds to raise watch time [L1444.028].

Example patterns to adapt to your own product:
- "Your phone screen is dirtier than you think, see it clean in 7 seconds." [L1444.028]
- "This drawer organizer fits any kitchen sink, watch it fit in one try." [L1444.028]

#### Hook Types and Examples

| Hook type | Use | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Controversial or provocative opener | Drives comments and organic virality | L0561.009 |
| Shocking or surprising ending near the end | Encourages rewatches; cut slightly short after the twist | L1384.019 |
| Cliffhanger that leaves a question open | Pushes viewers to the end | L1384.016 |
| Wait-for-result hook (e.g. "I won't buy until you do it") | Very high watch time | L0657.007 |
| Foreshadow: most interesting moment in the first second | Used when the video runs about 15 seconds | L0764.011 |
| Before-and-after and POV shots | Alternative hook formats | L1427.007 |

- Controversial hooks and openers that provoke comments can drive organic virality. One video that went viral this way was driven by comments reacting to a provocative caption [L0561.009].
- A hook that makes viewers wait for the result (for example "I won't buy until you do it") can produce very high watch time. High watch time keeps the video in circulation and gives viewers a reason to watch again [L0657.007].
- A shocking or surprising ending placed near the end of the video encourages viewers to rewatch. The video can be cut slightly short right after the twist to increase rewatches [L1384.019].
- A very short video that ends on a cliffhanger, around 5 seconds long, can produce a high rewatch rate and a strong completion percentage. Leaving a question open pushes viewers to watch to the end [L1384.016].

#### Hook Example from a Beauty Demo

- A demonstration video for a beauty product that goes viral shows the product being used on screen, for example applying lashes to one eye while the other eye stays bare for a side-by-side comparison. Viewers keep watching to see the result, which holds attention better than talking about ingredients or specifications [L0820.051].

### Native and Raw Entertainment Style

#### Core Principles

- TikTok creatives perform when they feel native and raw and trigger an emotion, rather than reading like a sales pitch. The same content principle can be applied to Facebook [L0363.051].
- On TikTok, content is judged as entertainment rather than as advertising. Viewers leave quickly if something looks like an ad, so hooks should lead with value or entertainment and the product should appear inside that content, not be the focus of it. Skits with the product woven in tend to outperform straight product ads, while direct response styles that work on Facebook often fail here [L0819.001].
- TikTok functions as an entertainment platform rather than a social network. Users come to be entertained, so a hook must either create aspiration or entertain before any product is shown. Ads that open with features or selling points are skipped quickly [L1374.001].
- Content on TikTok should deliver one of three forms of value: aspiration, entertainment, or education. The ad must lead with one of these, otherwise viewers feel sold to and leave [L1374.002].
- Virality depends more on video quality than on luck [L1429.042].

#### Clean Versus Wild Style

- Unconventional or overly wild video styles can go viral without converting well, because viewers enjoy the spectacle but do not buy. Clean, professional-looking videos that show what the product does usually convert better [L0657.015].
- Talk-heavy or dialogue-driven videos often get views but convert less than videos that show the product clearly. Use a talking-to-camera opening only when it leads into a demonstration [L0657.012].

#### Sound, Satisfaction and Creative Angles

- Colorful, satisfying visuals with ASMR-style sound performed well on TikTok organically, especially with younger audiences. In one comparison, a candy-like colorful product outperformed a healthy-looking one [L0657.023].
- Look for creative advantages in each product: ASMR-style sound, recreating a sound better than the original, cool transitions, a clear wow moment, and relevant trends. Use these to stand out from similar videos [L0764.015].
- A simple pencil product (Infinity pencil) went viral on TikTok although it is not a high-converting product. Its success came from a trending sound used at the right time, a well-executed video with a good, aesthetically pleasing background, and a sound that matched the video. The same product with a plain background would likely have performed much worse [L0821.021].

#### Case: Phone Case Demonstration

- A phone case ad that works on TikTok can show the case being knocked, clicked and removed, with satisfying ASMR sounds and no on-screen text or spoken sales pitch. The features are visible through the demonstration alone, so the viewer does not feel sold to [L1374.035].

### Video Length and Clip Pacing

#### Length Targets

| Context | Length | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum recommended length for TikTok videos | At least 6 seconds | L0764.003 |
| Target for creators new to video | 7 to 12 seconds | L0764.004 |
| Starting point for a new account, then extend | Around 6 seconds, then gradually to about 10 seconds | L1384.011 |
| Hook-focused short product video | Around 7 seconds | L1444.028 |
| Dropshipping ads on TikTok | 15 to 30 seconds, never more than one minute | L1374.017 |
| Long video, foreshadow applied | Around 15 seconds | L0764.011 |
| Very short cliffhanger video | Around 5 seconds | L1384.016 |
| Fake conversation video | Around 15 seconds if the story is engaging | L1384.022 |
| Clip that holds well with strong visuals | About 5 seconds | L0530.037 |

- Keep TikTok videos at least 6 seconds long. Anything shorter usually causes a large drop in retention and makes it harder for the platform to find the right audience, although very short videos can work occasionally [L0764.003].
- Shorter videos are easier to keep viewers watching and hit higher watch-time percentages. Start with videos around 6 seconds, then gradually extend to about 10 seconds once you are comfortable with retention [L1384.011].
- A clip of about five seconds can still perform well when it has strong visuals, clear sound and a styled background, because the short length raises watch time and replays. This format works best when the product is satisfying to watch and the video loops easily [L0530.037].
- Video length for dropshipping ads on TikTok: aim for 15 to 30 seconds, and never exceed one minute. Two-minute ads only work for big brands with a famous founder who already has trust [L1374.017].
- Making videos that run a minute or longer lowers average watch time, because viewers swipe away within seconds. Overly long videos are a common reason for weak retention [L1384.014].
- Fake conversation videos, such as a customer and company exchange, work because viewers stay to see how the story ends. A longer video of around 15 seconds can raise watch time when the story is engaging [L1384.022].

#### Pacing Rules

- Remove every dead moment and keep TikTok videos fast paced. Clips or sections under 3 seconds work well, though the right length depends on where each clip sits in the video [L0764.001].
- Dull moments drive viewers to swipe away, so remove any pause or slow scene, even half a second. Longer videos should be edited down aggressively without removing the key content [L1384.013].
- Change the camera angle, scene or use case every 2-3 seconds to hold attention. A clip that stays visually unchanged for more than two to three seconds causes people to scroll away [L0398.009].
- When a video has longer clips, place them toward the end rather than the beginning so viewers are eased into the pace. Starting with long clips tends to lose attention early [L0764.002].

#### Clip Length Ladder

Increase the clip length step by step. Jumping straight from a 2-second clip to a 6 to 7 second clip makes viewers lose interest [L0764.012].

| Clip | Length |
|---|---|
| 1 (hook) | 2 seconds |
| 2 | 3 seconds |
| 3 | 4 to 5 seconds |
| 4 | 5 to 6 seconds |

#### Editing Procedure for Trimming

1. Cut every dull moment from the video, even if it is only a fraction of a second [L1384.012].
2. Trim longer videos by keeping only the key content; a 20-second video may be cut to about 12 seconds [L1384.012].
3. Open with a strong hook and avoid slow scenes that let viewers swipe [L1384.012].
4. Have someone else or yourself rewatch the cut to find slow parts and make split-second edits [L1384.012].

### Standard Product Video Structure

#### Structure for a 7 to 12 Second Product Video

1. **Hook clip, 1 to 3 seconds, ideally 1.5 to 2 seconds:** on-screen text plus an unexpected background action [L0764.010].
2. **Product show clip:** hold the product and spin it so viewers know what they are looking at [L0764.010].
3. **Demonstration clip:** use the product on screen for about 2 to 3 seconds [L0764.010].
4. **Second demonstration clip:** show the product in a different way, for example a different use or a different feature, for about 2 to 3 seconds [L0764.010].
5. **Further demonstration angles:** keep adding demonstration angles so no single clip stays on screen too long and viewers do not swipe away from boredom [L0764.010].

#### Longer Videos with a Foreshadow

- If a video runs long, around 15 seconds, play the most interesting moment in the first second as a foreshadow. That opening clip must be very satisfying, because it makes viewers stay to see the full payoff [L0764.011].

### Loops and Rewatch Logic

- A seamless loop, where the end flows back into the start, raises watch time. It is harder and more time-consuming to edit, so make it when the edit allows [L0764.014].
- A video with a clear, satisfying ending that flows back to the start rewards rewatching; combine with a loop where the edit allows [L0764.014].
- Re-watches and full completions matter more than likes for virality, because a high rewatch rate pushes distribution further even when the like-to-view ratio is modest [L0820.007].
- A shocking ending near the end encourages rewatches [L1384.019].

### Retention and Distribution Logic

- TikTok shows a video to a small test audience first and only expands distribution if watch time passes the threshold, so watch time and full completion are the key performance signals [L0820.006].
- Watch time strongly affects reach and sales. High watch time keeps the video in circulation and gives viewers a reason to watch again [L0657.007].
- Retention rate is treated as the most important signal for pushing a video [L1186.024].
- Re-watches and full completions matter more than likes for virality [L0820.007].
- Reusing the same intro and video structure over and over lets viewers recognize the content, and views drop over time. In the case described, repeated intros eventually caused an account to get almost no views [L1444.029].

### Script and Story Formats

#### Story Script Template (Comment-Driving)

Template: write a short-video story script that makes viewers comment at the end. Structure it in this order:

1. HOOK (face to camera, intense eye contact): one bold opening line that challenges the advice most people around you give.
2. CONFLICT: what you saw around you that made you doubt the common advice, and what happened when you shared your own goal.
3. TURNING POINT: the decision you made and how you began learning the skill.
4. CALL TO ACTION: ask viewers to comment a specific keyword, such as their country code, and promise to send them a free guide.

Use my story: [describe your background, location, starting situation, what you did and what changed]. Keep the tone emotional but humble, avoid bragging and close with the message that the goal is possible.

Write two completely different versions:
Version 1: emotional, personal 'mini series' style that emphasises pain, rebellion and redemption and builds emotional connection.
Version 2: bold, punchy, controversial 'debate starter' style that is faster paced, opinionated and built to trigger comments and shares, with a hook that challenges a common income benchmark.

[L0887.027]

- Story-based scripts that end with a comment request get more replies when the call to action asks for one simple keyword and promises something specific in return. The hook and conflict should create tension first, so viewers want to see the outcome [L0887.028].

#### Debate-Starter Hook Formula

Pattern: name a common income figure that people use to judge what is realistic, reject it as the limit of someone's goals, and set it against a dream worth protecting. It works because it creates immediate tension and gives the viewer a position to agree or disagree with, which drives comments and shares [L0887.032].

Examples in this pattern:
- "Don't let a $35K paycheck decide how big your store is allowed to grow." [L0887.032]
- "Stop taking money advice from someone who has never built anything they own." [L0887.032]

#### Story and Scenario Videos

- Story-based or scenario videos can drive virality for a product, and viewers respond to relatable situations more than to plain product demonstrations [L0656.005].
- Products applied to the face require the creator to show the face or part of it, which limits who can film the product comfortably. Account for this before choosing a face-care product for a faceless or privacy-focused account [L0657.047].

### Talking-Head Videos

- For talking-head videos, prop the phone up and film as if you were on a FaceTime call with a friend. Formats that suit this approach include a day-in-the-life clip, a founder routine, or answers to frequently asked product questions [L0576.003].
- Talk-heavy or dialogue-driven videos often get views but convert less than videos that show the product clearly. Use a talking-to-camera opening only when it leads into a demonstration [L0657.012].

### Scenario and Demonstration Examples

- For a product meant for a pet or a baby, a stuffed animal or a doll can stand in for the real subject in short demonstration videos. This keeps the demo realistic while avoiding the need for a live child or animal [L1380.059].
- Products applied to the face require the creator to show the face or part of it. Account for this before choosing a face-care product for a faceless or privacy-focused account [L0657.047].

### Product-Specific Creative Angles

- Look for creative advantages in each product: ASMR-style sound, recreating a sound better than the original, cool transitions, a clear wow moment, and relevant trends. Use these to stand out from similar videos [L0764.015].
- Colorful, satisfying visuals with ASMR-style sound performed well on TikTok organically, especially with younger audiences [L0657.023].
- Products whose use is visible through hands-on action, such as the phone case knocked, clicked and removed, can carry the video without speech or on-screen sales text [L1374.035].
- A viral beauty demo applied lashes to one eye while the other stayed bare, giving a side-by-side comparison that holds attention [L0820.051].
- A simple, visually styled product can go viral through a trending sound used at the right time and an aesthetically pleasing background [L0821.021].

## Filming, Editing and Sound

### Filming Practice and Locations

- Leave room around the subject when framing, because footage framed too tightly limits zoom, pan and transition options. [L0341.037]
- Film in varied real locations, such as a car, outdoors or while out and about. These look more engaging than the same indoor setting, such as a dining table or living room. Avoid glare from strong light. [L0656.004]
- Use sound-led footage where it fits. ASMR content, such as the sound of opening a soda bottle, can make a bottle opener product more engaging on video. [L0656.007]

### Phone-First Workflow

- Draft and edit on the phone. Desktop cannot reliably add text, sounds or some editing features, so keep the phone as the main device for all TikTok work. [L1380.002]
- Do not edit in the TikTok studio or in-app editor. The original file is lost and cannot be reused in another edit. Use TikTok only for sounds, hashtags, text and text-to-speech. [L1380.022]
- Follow this production sequence:
  1. Record the video on the phone in 4K at 60 fps (1080p is acceptable). [L1380.021]
  2. Edit the video in an external app such as Splice, keeping the original file. [L1380.021]
  3. Export the finished video. [L1380.021]
  4. Upload it to TikTok. [L1380.021]
  5. In TikTok, add on-screen text, text-to-speech, music, filters and hashtags. [L1380.021]
  6. Save as a draft or post, and keep several drafts queued for the upcoming days. [L1380.021]
- To add music, tap upload, pick the video, then tap the music icon at the top center of the screen and search for a sound. Trending and copyright-cleared sounds are only available on a personal account. [L1380.026]
- Many TikTok sellers execute products poorly. Cleaner editing, better hooks and removal of dull moments can win views over competitors, which makes this an opportunity for a clean, careful creator. [L1380.050]

### Editing Tools

| Tool | Role in this workflow | Units |
|---|---|---|
| Premiere Pro (desktop) | Vertical sequence, fast cutting of dead time, TikTok-style text | L0343.044, L0343.045, L1427.035 |
| CapCut (mobile) | Keyframes and easing, ratio setup, reframing, TikTok-style text, combining footage with A-roll audio | L0343.048, L1403.024, L1427.038, L1427.070, L1427.074 |
| Splice | Edit before upload, royalty-free sounds for ads, aligning re-created sounds, layering sound effects | L1380.021, L1383.019, L0764.035, L1384.057 |

#### Premiere Pro

- For 9:16 video, keep a separate vertical sequence or workspace rather than cutting vertical clips in a landscape sequence. The sequence takes its frame ratio from the first clip, so set the ratio before adding footage. [L0343.044]
- Press C to switch to the Razor tool and cut a clip at the point you click. This is a fast way to remove dead time from raw footage. [L0343.045]

#### CapCut

- Combine the recorded footage with the A-roll audio and create the final short video from the phone. [L1403.024]

#### Splice

- Use Splice to edit videos before upload. [L1383.019]
- Use Splice to add custom sound effects after the video edit is finished, layering recorded sounds over the cut. [L1384.057]

### Keyframes and Transitions

- A keyframe stores a value such as scale or position at one point in time, and the editor generates the change between two keyframes. Movement only appears when at least two keyframes with different values are set. [L0343.046]
- Make zooms and moves long enough to show the change in speed and blur before judging the result. Very short transitions hide easing and motion blur, so the effect looks weak or goes unnoticed. [L0343.047]
- In CapCut, set the transition curve between keyframes to a preset ease-in, ease-out or bounce option, or shape it in a graph. Start with the presets, because a hand-shaped bell-style ease curve is harder to get right. [L0343.048]
- Use transitions and trend formats that are current, such as a soft music intro that cuts into a fast track with a transition. Spend time inside the platform each day to see what is trending. [L1077.023]

### Vertical Framing and Reframing

- A TikTok-style vertical ad uses a frame of 1080 x 1920 pixels, a 9:16 aspect ratio. [L1427.021]
- After switching to a vertical frame, footage downloaded from TikTok can look smaller in the frame because TikTok has compressed it. Scale the clip back up to fill the frame. [L1427.022]
- In CapCut's main menu, the Ratio option sets the project frame, for example 1:1 for a square Instagram-style ad. After changing the ratio, resize the footage so it fills the new timeline frame. [L1427.070]
- Reframe horizontal footage for a vertical or square ad:
  1. Import the horizontal clip and place it on the timeline. [L1427.074]
  2. Scale the clip up until the subject fills the vertical or square frame. [L1427.074]
  3. Wait until the subject is clearly visible, then add a keyframe on position. [L1427.074]
  4. Move the position keyframe so the frame follows the subject to the next keyframe. [L1427.074]

### TikTok-Style Text

- In Premiere Pro, set the text color to black, add a white background box, add padding around the text and round the corners of the box. [L1427.035]
- Add TikTok-style text in CapCut:
  1. Tap Text and add your text. [L1427.038]
  2. Open Style and tap Canvas to create an instant background. [L1427.038]
  3. Set the background to white and the text to black. [L1427.038]
  4. Make the text bold. [L1427.038]
  5. Pinch the text to resize it, and adjust the background height and width. [L1427.038]
  6. Animate the text, for example with a bounce-in, if needed. [L1427.038]

### Sound Design and ASMR

- Ambient ASMR sound, aesthetic backgrounds and colorful visuals keep viewers engaged and help videos become memorable. Satisfying sounds, such as unwrapping or peeling, were cited as especially effective. [L1384.017]
- Recording your own sound effects, such as a stretching or pulling sound for a product, can beat stock audio. Original satisfying sounds were reported to perform better than generic sound effects. [L1384.018]
- Record your own satisfying sounds, for example a product being stretched or pulled, and place them on the edit to give the video original audio. [L1384.057]
- Follow this sound production procedure for product videos:
  1. Record the product's natural sound with the microphone as close as possible while filming. [L0764.034]
  2. If the natural sound does not come out as wanted, record it again separately, for example on a voice memo. [L0764.034]
  3. Recreate the sound after the video is done, and import it into Splice. [L0764.034, L0764.035]
  4. Align the recording to the exact clip and frame where the sound happens. [L0764.034, L0764.035]
  5. Balance the levels: keep the product sound audible over the background music. For ASMR-focused content, lower the music and raise the original audio, or the other way around depending on the goal. [L0764.034]
- Splice is used to import a separately recorded sound and align it to the matching frame of the video clip, so a re-created product sound fits the action. [L0764.035]
- Video has two sound layers to balance: the background music or trending audio, and the product's own sound. In ASMR-style videos, the product sound should stay clearly audible without being drowned out by music. [L0764.036]

### Trending Sounds

- Trending sounds can drive large organic reach because videos using a rising sound are shown to people searching that sound. Find trending sounds early by opening a trending song and reviewing its top posts, which can show product videos already using it. [L0655.011]
- Hop on a new trending sound quickly. A sound and its hashtag can grow from thousands of users to hundreds of thousands or millions within a short time, and early adoption gives the best chance of being shown first in search. [L0655.012]
- An early video can rank near the top of the sound's page. As more users adopt the sound, that video is recommended first. The owner reported one video reaching 20 to 30 million views this way. [L1077.024]
- Hop onto a trending sound or hashtag early, while it is still growing. [L1077.024]
- Use trending sounds from the For You page rather than the viral tab, since sounds that are already viral are often used by many accounts. Use a sound from the For You page only if it fits the video and the product. [L0372.035]
- Sounds taken from the For You page are often better than trending chart sounds, which saturate quickly. Choose sounds that are still in use but not yet overused. [L1383.048]
- Adopt a trending sound early, before many product accounts use it, because a format that is already common among sellers gets less reach. Only use the sound if its meaning fits the product. [L0657.045]
- Trending songs tend to rise quickly and fade within days. If you plan to use a trending sound, post while it is still climbing, not after it has peaked. [L0706.018]
- Trending audio helps videos get found. Using a sound that is already trending places your video among the first ones shown for that audio. Dialogue or theme music from a trending series can be used with the lines shown as on-screen text. [L0764.033]
- Organic TikTok growth depends on riding sounds before they peak. Jump onto a trending sound early so viewers who click the sound also watch the other videos in that trend. [L0819.002]
- Cutting clips to the beat of the audio is a meaningful editing technique on TikTok, since sound is on by default. This differs from Facebook, where most viewers watch muted. [L0819.002]
- Trending sounds are a key factor in going viral. Check which sounds are currently trending and use them in your own videos, provided the sound matches the video and is used while it is still popular. [L0821.013]
- Choose music whose beats or pauses line up with your transitions, and that matches the product and the timing of the video. A trending sound that has no relation to the product is unlikely to help. [L0372.034]

### Music Rules and Copyright

- When a creator video runs as a TikTok paid ad, use only audio from TikTok's commercial soundtrack library. Regular artist music in paid ads can lead to copyright problems. [L0784.014]
- For a video that will run as an ad, download royalty-free sounds from a free library, add them in Splice, then upload. [L1383.019]
- If a trending sound is copyrighted, find a bootleg or re-uploaded version that sounds nearly identical and use that instead. Sounds that complement the product also help the video. [L1383.020]
- Conflict: L1383.020 suggests bootleg substitutes for copyrighted trending sounds, but L0784.014 requires the commercial library for paid ads. For paid ads, follow L0784.014. The source only describes the bootleg substitute for organic use. [L0784.014, L1383.020]
- Trending and copyright-cleared sounds are only available on a personal account. [L1380.026]

### Text-to-Speech

- Hook videos can be voiced with TikTok's built-in text-to-speech using the "Jesse" voice, which keeps the hook from sounding flat. [L1383.055]
- Use the same voice across hook variations so the format stays consistent for testing. [L1383.055]
- Add text-to-speech inside TikTok after uploading the exported video. [L1380.021, L1380.022]

## Replicating, Remixing and Refreshing Viral Content

### Principles of Replicating and Remixing

- Start from what already works. Copy the winning angle and format first, and change angles only after the product shows traction and converts well. [L1380.049]
- Copying a successful competitor's video closely, even frame by frame, can still produce a viral result, which suggests that video structure drives performance more than timing alone. [L1429.043]
- A viral video with weak sharpness and audio can still succeed on its concept. You can beat it by keeping the concept and improving image sharpness and sound quality. [L0657.046]
- Reposting other creators' videos is risky because TikTok increasingly detects reused content, and the account can suffer. Recreate the concept with your own footage instead. [L0657.018]
- Study the top videos of a successful account closely, including frame changes, splits, sounds, transitions, recording style and editing pace. Then recreate the structure with your own product rather than copying the content. [L0657.017]
- Use competitor accounts in the same niche as inspiration. Borrow the theme or structure, then improve it or change it entirely. [L0764.045]
- Study a proven viral video from another account and recreate its structure in your own way, using the same type of music, hook and context. Copying the core format while filming your own version is the approach that produced the first sales. [L0821.004]
- To learn what works on TikTok, spend regular time on the platform looking at which videos go viral and which sounds they use. Then replicate those sounds and formats in your own videos. [L0821.014]

### Remixing a Winning Ad or Viral Video

#### Remixing a Winning Ad

1. Start from the winning ad's angle and script. [L0341.035]
2. Open with a big benefit shot, such as a phone that sticks anywhere. [L0341.035]
3. Find footage that shows each benefit and cut it into short clips. [L0341.035]
4. Adjust clip audio and volume as needed. [L0341.035]
5. Add text in a TikTok-style layout using Open Sans, scale it down to fit, and set the text background to white at 100% opacity. [L0341.035]

- One clip is rarely enough to modify a winning video ad well, so gather a full set of footage before cutting. This prevents a copy that looks exactly like the original. [L0341.038]
- On TikTok, change the clip roughly every 2-3 seconds when remixing competitor videos, so the video is not flagged as a duplicate. Mixing hooks from several winning videos into one new edit is a common method. [L0637.051]

#### Replicating a Viral TikTok Video

- Keep the same filming style and footage approach, but make slight variations of the spoken text or on-screen words, and cut any weak moments (for example, shorten a 10-second video to 8 seconds). [L0501.006]
- Judge each variation against the original. If it performs worse, work out whether the words, the angle or the length caused it. [L0501.006]
- Do not repost the same video. Make a new variation of the same style (same filming approach, different wording or cut), and reuse trending sounds that worked on your best video. [L0501.016]

#### Repurposing Viral Footage into a Facebook Ad

1. Write a script with ChatGPT based on the footage and the product's problem and benefits. [L0524.052]
2. Record a voiceover, or generate one with ElevenLabs. [L0524.052]
3. Cut the footage to match the voiceover and add on-screen text. [L0524.052]
4. Test the cut as a Facebook ad against a version with a fresh opening. [L0524.052]

#### Copying a Viral Product's Video Approach

1. Identify the viral video and its trending sound while the trend is still active. [L0655.014]
2. Copy the video's format, structure, and sound closely rather than inventing a new angle. [L0655.014]
3. Ensure your product link is working before publishing. [L0655.014]
4. Add a clear call to action and urgency to the video text and description. [L0655.014]
5. Post while the sound is still trending, ideally within days of the viral peak. [L0655.014]

#### Recreating Your Product Cleanly

- Learn the structure of successful competitor videos, then rebuild it with your own footage, so the content is yours even when the format is copied. [L0657.017, L0657.018]
- Remove watermarks and create original footage. Reused clips with watermarks can signal low quality and lead to lower distribution. [L1384.046]

### Content Mix and Testing Volume

| Videos per day | Mix |
|---|---|
| 3 | About two videos in a style that already works, and one riskier new angle [L0501.017] |
| 4-5 | Two or three proven styles, one or two variations, and one new risky angle [L0501.017] |

- Keep testing new angles constantly, because the same content gets harder to keep relevant over time. [L0501.017]

### Trends, Sounds and Hashtags

- Trend-based videos are easy to produce and are worth doing even if a trend does not last, as long as the product fits naturally into the trend format. An example is listing benefits over a trending sound on a product-style video. [L0655.013]
- Trends can be used to reach new audiences from the For You Page. Include your product in a current video trend, filter, or trending sound instead of relying only on your own content format. [L1384.029]
- A trend can be used without showing your face. Put the product into a current video trend, a filter or a trending sound. Keep the product presentation within normal limits and avoid anything too revealing. [L1384.054]

#### Organic Replication of a Viral Video

1. Use the same trending sounds, the same hashtags, and a very similar text-to-speech voiceover as the viral video. [L1429.017]
2. Upload two to three more similar videos after the viral one. [L1429.017]
3. Leave at least 2 hours between uploads. [L1429.017]
4. Vary posting times, including unusual hours such as 2 am, so different time zones and regions see the content. [L1429.017]

### Reusing Your Own Old Videos (Repurposing)

#### Eligibility Rules

- Only repurpose content on an account that has been posting for several weeks or months and already has a large library of videos. Do not repurpose on a new account. [L0795.008]
- Only consider re-uploading a video that is at least about one month old, and only when it previously performed well. [L0795.009]
- Use repurposing sparingly. Repeating it too often stops it from working. [L0795.010]

#### Procedure

To repurpose an existing video:

1. Take a video that already performed. [L0820.016]
2. Change the hook or the opening. [L0820.016]
3. Slightly alter the video file itself. [L0820.016]
4. Re-upload it so TikTok does not treat it as spam. [L0820.016]

#### File Differences

- A re-uploaded video must differ in its file content, for example through a small trim of a second or a changed frame, even if it looks the same to the viewer. [L0795.011]
- Re-uploading the identical file is risky, and a viewer who has already seen it will swipe past. [L0795.011]
- Viewers who have already seen a video on a large account may swipe past it when it reappears, which can lower its performance. This is a reason to avoid identical re-uploads even when a restriction is not triggered. [L0795.012]

#### Changing the Fingerprint

- To change a video's fingerprint before re-uploading it as an ad, speed it up by 1.01x to 1.05x in a video editor or speed tool. Combined with swapping the hook of one video onto the body of another, this creates variants that TikTok may treat as new videos, which can lower CPM. [L1377.063]

### Metadata and Meta Refresh

- The aim of a meta refresh is to make TikTok treat a re-uploaded ad as new content rather than an old video, so it gets fresh reach. [L1436.030]
- A metadata-changing method can be used to refresh a copied video so the platform treats it as a new upload. In one test a third-party website was used for this, and the effect lasted only about one day. [L1177.057]
- The metadata that can be changed for a refresh includes coding, dimensions, length, timing, and playback speed. Changing these helps the platform treat a reused video as a new ad. [L1382.026]

#### Meta Refresh Procedure

1. Start with the video at its original 1080 x 1920 (9:16) dimension. [L1382.024, L1436.029]
2. Change the dimension to 1920 x 1080 (16:9) in an editor such as CapCut, Sony Vegas Pro or Premiere Pro. [L1382.024, L1436.029]
3. Export the video and re-import it into the editor. [L1382.024, L1436.029]
4. Change the dimension back to 1080 x 1920 (9:16). [L1382.024, L1436.029]
5. Change the coding and other metadata of the video, such as speed or timing. [L1382.024, L1436.029]
6. Export the final video and use it for the new ad. [L1436.029]

#### Results Benchmark

- After using the meta refresh method on competitor videos, a CTR of 1.52 percent was reached on TikTok, which is very high. [L1382.025]
- A CTR of about 0.7 to 0.8 percent is considered good on TikTok. The 1.52 percent is a single test result, and 0.7 to 0.8 percent is the general benchmark. [L1382.025]

### Downloaders, Watermark Removal and Editing Tools

- Snap Tick (snaptick.app) and SnapTik are web tools that download TikTok videos without the TikTok watermark. The clean file can be posted on Instagram Reels or YouTube Shorts without visible TikTok branding. [L0795.032, L1186.039]
- Use the downloader to get a clean file before re-uploading, since the watermark suppresses reach on other platforms. [L1186.039]
- To reuse existing TikTok content, download the source video with SnapTik, then edit it into your own custom ad in CapCut, which is also available as a mobile app for editing on the phone. [L1183.023]

### Video Replies

- For a video reply, pick a high-liked comment as the hook. The selected comment appears in the top left corner of the reply video, where it works as a strong hook. [L1429.040]
- Video replies that respond to a viral video with traction can compound reach, because each reply can ride the momentum of the earlier viral video. The top comments on a new reply then supply topics for the next replies in the same chain. [L1429.054]

### Case: Replication That Produced the Breakthrough

- A dropshipper started about 20 months before the interview, initially doubting that dropshipping could be profitable until a friend began making sales. [L0821.022]
- He tested 6 to 7 products before finding a hit. [L0821.022]
- For the hit, he noticed another account getting tens of millions of views within a day, bought one unit on Amazon that arrived the same day, and filmed many videos that copied that account's format, music and hook in his own execution. [L0821.022]
- He posted 4 to 5 videos per day for two weeks, was about to stop just before the breakthrough, and then gained 1,000 followers in 15 days, then 10,000, and about 20,000 as one video reached roughly 10 to 15 million views and earned about $1,000 within 2 hours. [L0821.022]
- The same product then kept getting about 4 million views per day for roughly a month. The overall path from the first dropshipping attempt to the win took about a year. [L0821.022]

### Procedures by Source Unit

#### Competitor Analysis to Recreation

1. Find the largest accounts selling the product. [L1380.048]
2. Collect their most viral videos. [L1380.048]
3. Note the hooks, transitions, and formats such as ASMR. [L1380.048]
4. Remove dull moments and shorten each video. [L1380.048]
5. Recreate the best videos using your own footage and improve the weak parts. [L1380.048]

#### Further details

- Reusing the same video clip across several posts or across a second account hurts reach. Posts with identical clips tend to get very few views, so new videos should use fresh footage. [L0656.002]

## Posting Cadence, Timing and Hashtags

### Posting Cadence and Volume

- Cadence matters more than volume. One video per week posted consistently beats ten videos in one day or one burst per month followed by inactivity. Choose a cadence you can sustain. [L0915.013]
- Organic short-video accounts should post at least once a day, even when older videos still generate sales. Views keep growing from earlier uploads, but regular new posts keep reach and sales from declining. [L0387.038]
- Organic growth depends on consistent posting over time rather than on one video. Early results, such as about 1,200 views and 18 new followers after two days, are best treated as a test of how steady the output is. Plan a regular posting rhythm from the start. [L0888.033]

### Posts per Day by Phase

| Situation | Posts per day | Conditions | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organic minimum | At least 1 | Applies even when older videos still sell | [L0387.038] |
| Organic testing, per account | About 3 | Content must differ between accounts, not be duplicated | [L0561.006] |
| Testing, standard | 3-5 | Use days 3-7 to find which videos work and replicate them | [L0501.005] |
| Testing, active | 2-3 | Post in bursts followed by gaps | [L0820.015] |
| Early account stage | 3-4 | Spaced 4-6 hours apart | [L1077.027] |
| Peak hours, especially first week | About 3 | Keep posting even if early views are low | [L1383.029] |
| Video going viral | 5-6 | Go up to 5-6 when a video is viral | [L0501.005] |
| Video going viral, alternative aim | 4-5 | Space uploads about 2 hours apart | [L0706.042] |
| Upper limit | About 9 | Never exceed about 9 per day; risks hurting the account | [L0501.005] |
| Q4 holidays | 3 | Raise from 1-2 to 3 per day | [L0820.042] |

- The sources give different numbers because they describe different goals. The 1-per-day floor keeps an established account active. The 2-5 range fits testing. The 5-6 range applies only while a video is viral. The 9 cap is an upper limit that should not be exceeded. [L0387.038, L0501.005, L0706.042]
- The viral figures differ slightly: one source aims for 4-5 and allows 5-6 when a video is viral, so treat 4-5 as the target and 5-6 as the ceiling during a spike. [L0706.042, L0501.005]
- The "about 3 per account" figure applies to organic testing across several accounts, and each account needs its own content. [L0561.006]

### Bursts, Gaps and Spacing

- During active testing, post in bursts followed by gaps between posts. [L0820.015]
- Upload in volume and in batches. One video in a batch can go viral while the others do not. One account in the slipper case uploaded about three to six times per day, and one of its many videos produced most of the views. [L0657.019]
- Viral success depends on volume. Several uploads a day raise the chance that one video breaks through. The hosts emphasized that a single successful video can drive most of an account's results. [L0657.020]
- While a video is viral, space uploads about two hours apart to avoid being flagged as spam. [L0706.042]
- On an early account, space posts four to six hours apart. [L1077.027]

### Consistency and Patience

- A viral video can take up to two weeks to appear after an account starts posting. An account that posts irregularly may take longer to break through, and consistent uploading shortens that wait. [L0656.003]
- Going viral usually requires sustained posting, because reach often disappears for stretches and then returns. Do not conclude after a dry period that the account is shadow banned. Keep publishing consistently. [L0819.003]

### Best Posting Hours

Each example below comes from one account or one audience. Use them as starting slots to test, not as fixed rules.

| Example | Times | Time zone | IDs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product test, conversion | Around 12:00, around 16:00, 18:00-19:00 | Not stated; 18:00-19:00 showed the highest conversion | [L0764.031] |
| Account test | 11:00, 15:00, 18:00 | Not stated; confirm with your own analytics | [L0795.035] |
| Channel routine | 11:00, 15:00, 19:00 | GMT+2 | [L1131.054] |
| Early account example | About 6-7 a.m., about 11-12, 3-4 p.m., plus a later evening slot | Not stated | [L1077.027] |
| Eastern Time example | 3 p.m. and 9 p.m. ET (= 12 p.m. and 6 p.m. PT) | ET / PT | [L1381.018] |
| Trainer's account | About 10:00-12:00, 15:00-17:00, 18:00-21:00 | Trainer's own time zone | [L1383.028] |
| US audience | 7:30-8 p.m. PT, 11 a.m. PT; 3 a.m. PT for a personal account | PT | [L0820.014] |

- Align posting with US waking and lunch hours, since the US audience is the reference for these peaks. [L0820.014]
- Avoid posting near midnight. [L0795.035]
- Sources differ on the early-morning slot. A seller's 3 a.m. ET uploads performed well because the audience was awake at that hour in another time zone. A personal account did well at 3 a.m. PT. The midnight warning and these early-morning examples do not conflict, because they describe different accounts and audiences. [L1381.019, L0820.014, L0795.035]
- In one account, a video posted around 6:30 a.m. ET got about 170 views, while videos posted around 12:00-13:00 ET got about 300-400 views. Compare view counts across your own upload times before settling on a schedule. [L1383.057]
- Always test upload times against the time zone of the target audience, and test more than three upload times on a new account. [L1381.019, L1381.018]
- Varying upload times diversifies who sees the content, because viewers in other regions may be awake at unusual hours. Posting late at night in one region may still need local engagement first. [L1429.018]

#### Procedure: Finding the Best Posting Time for a Product

1. Use different devices and accounts.
2. Post the same product content at different hours of the day.
3. Compare views and engagement by time slot to find the best window.

[L0561.057]

### Drafting and the Content Pipeline

- Draft at least 3 to 5 days of videos ahead of posting day instead of creating them on the day. A buffer of drafts makes consistent uploading possible. [L1380.019]
- Drafting regularly signals to TikTok that the creator is a consistent, valuable uploader, which tends to lead to more reach. Edit everything on the phone so the workflow stays quick. [L1380.023]
- For steady output while busy, use this routine:
  1. Produce three to nine videos per day in advance.
  2. Keep drafts a day ahead.
  3. Upload one per scheduled slot.

  [L0820.017]
- The two figures describe different levels of the pipeline. The one-day-ahead draft rhythm is the daily working routine, and the 3-5 day buffer is the reserve kept on hand. [L0820.017, L1380.019]

### Scheduling

- The TikTok desktop uploader lets you set a scheduled upload time, which separates posting from phone activity. It offers fewer editing options than the app, so add music and text before uploading from the computer. [L1186.041]
- TikTok Shop now lets creators and brands schedule shoppable videos ahead of time, so shoppable content can be planned and published at set times. [L1504.012]

### Hashtags

- Hashtags are not the main reason a video goes viral. If no specific hashtag comes to mind, broad tags such as fyp, viral or asmr can be used, but the video itself matters far more. [L0764.037]
- Use no more than six hashtags per post: about two niche, two broad and two trending. A very large set can send a video to unrelated audiences. [L1077.025]
- For a new account with a target audience, use two niche hashtags, one of which names the target audience. [L1077.025]
- Test with and without hashtags, because their effect varies. [L1077.025]
- A typical set uses about five hashtags: the product hashtag, about two niche hashtags, one broad hashtag such as "satisfying", and one hashtag for the problem or complaint the buyer has. Every hashtag should be relevant, because irrelevant hashtags narrow the audience to the wrong group. [L1381.020]
- The two counts differ. Six is the maximum for a post, and about five is the typical structure. Stay at or below six, and aim for about five. [L1077.025, L1381.020]

### Captions and Search Terms

- TikTok search autocomplete suggestions can reveal what users want within a niche. Using them in captions and content is an early SEO tactic on the platform. [L1077.026]

### Trend Monitoring

#### Procedure: Daily Trend Monitoring

1. Spend about 30 minutes a day on the For You feed to see what is trending.
2. Note the popular music, sounds and formats that repeat across several videos.
3. When you find a trending audio, open its sound page to see the top videos using it.
4. Use the same audio in your own video, ideally soon after it starts trending.

[L0764.032]

#### Procedure: Finding Trending Audio and Formats

1. Spend regular time on TikTok analyzing what is trending.
2. Spot trends one to two weeks before they reach the viral charts when possible.
3. Use the trend format with your product. Older trends, even a few months old, can still perform well.

[L0795.030]

### Seasonal and Q4 Planning

- Consumer spending increases visibly around October 12-15 every year. Spending stays high despite economic downturns because consumers rely on credit cards and buy-now-pay-later schemes. Plan inventory and campaign capacity for a volume surge in this window. [L0309.015]

#### Procedure: Preparing for the Q4 Holidays

1. Raise posting from one or two to three times per day.
2. Watch for trending sounds, hashtags and filters starting about 24 to 48 hours before Thanksgiving and the Friday after.
3. Use them in your videos.

[L0820.042]

### Handling Viral Momentum

- While a video is viral, upload more good-quality content, aiming for four to five videos, and space uploads about two hours apart. [L0706.042]
- When a video is gaining momentum, post several times a day. The example was four uploads on the first day, followed by continued consistency. [L1444.025]
- Keep posting during the peak first week even if early views are low, because one video can break out and lift the rest. [L1383.029]
- A viral spike usually fades within 24 hours to a few days. A strong video can stay elevated for about a week, but only if you keep adding actions that reach new viewers. [L1429.001]
- A video that does not go viral on day one can still gain views later, because TikTok sometimes reruns or pushes older videos. One reported video went from 14 million views to 20 million and then to 30 million through reruns. [L1444.026]

## Organic Testing Protocol and Reading Results

### Test Setup and Account Plan

- Test one product at a time. Put all energy into that product instead of running several at once. [L0309.025]
- Keep one testing account per product. Do not reuse a product's account for a different product unless the niche is the same. [L0501.007]
- Once a proven winner works on one account, repeating it on a second account is valid, because competitors copy visible winners, so capture the market while it works. [L0501.015]
- Judge a product only after a sustained posting period, not after a few videos. [L0821.006]

**Accounts per product, by approach**

| Approach | Number of accounts | Condition | Source ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spread output across many accounts | 5 to 10 accounts, posting on all of them | Standard organic test of one product. A single account rarely gets enough distribution for the platform to show the product. | L0561.001 |
| Single testing account | 1 account per product | Keeps each product's account separate. Each new account's first videos usually get little reach, so post before the new-account advantage ends. | L0501.007 |
| Two-phone setup | 2 accounts on separate phones | Post the product video organically and track its views. | L1186.025 |
| Replacement account | 1 new account (new email) | Performance stalls by day 3 to 4. Repeat until one account gains traction or the product is confirmed as not resonating. | L0309.026 |
| Replacement account, no traffic | 1 new account | No organic traffic despite reasonable creative quality. Use the new-account advantage instead of continuing on a shadowbanned or under-performing account. | L0309.035 |

- Relying on one account and posting only a few videos per product is the main reason organic reach stays at roughly 500 to 1,500 views. [L0561.010]
- A new account may need about 9 to 12 uploads before a video takes off, so do not judge it after a few posts. A breakout can come on day four after a steady routine. [L0372.045]

### Test Duration and Patience

**Duration by situation**

| Situation | Duration | Source ids |
|---|---|---|
| Kill check: no meaningful results at all (no views, engagement or conversions) | Run the test for 3 to 5 days, then kill | L0309.025 |
| Standard product judgment | About 2 to 3 weeks per product | L0820.001 |
| Standard product judgment, applied to a trending-product test | Two weeks of posting before judging | L0821.005, L0821.006 |
| Organic test, minimum patience | About two weeks or more. A few days of low views is not a reliable verdict. | L0561.007 |
| Early viral window | Most content goes viral within the first week, usually 3 to 7 days, and can take up to two weeks | L1429.035 |
| Hook and angle testing when videos show zero views | About two months before videos begin to go viral | L1469.012, L1469.013 |

- Sources disagree on how long to wait. The 3 to 5 day rule applies only when nothing happens at all. The 2 to 3 week rule applies when you have some signal and need sustained output before judging. The two-month rule applies when zero-view results come from creative problems and the team is still testing hooks, wording, angles and sounds. [L0309.025, L0820.001, L0561.007, L1469.012, L1469.013]
- Do not treat early zero-view results as proof that TikTok cannot work for the product. [L1469.013]
- Posting only five videos and then expecting views is not enough. Upload consistently over days and weeks before judging a product. [L1383.030]

### Phase 1: Days 1 to 2

1. Upload 3 videos on day 1 and reply to every comment. [L0501.001]
2. Follow back and engage with accounts that liked or followed you, and with similar accounts in your niche, because mutual follows make TikTok more likely to show your videos. [L0501.001]
3. On day 2, keep replying to all comments, fix any mistakes in the account, and keep posting 3 to 5 videos per day while the new-account advantage lasts. [L0501.001]
4. Use video replies on relevant comments, ideally on the top 5 to 10 comments of a viral video, so new viewers who read the comments land on your newer video. [L0501.001]
5. In the first few days, use the story/dialogue scenario format (for example "follow me for a chance to win") to grow followers faster. It works with almost any niche or personal brand. [L0501.001]

### Phase 2: Days 3 Onward

**Posting volume**

Sources give different volumes. Use the one that matches the test:

- 3 to 5 videos per day for a single product on a test account. [L0309.025, L0501.001]
- 2 to 5 short videos per day across TikTok and Instagram Reels, with about 2 to 3 weeks per product. [L0820.001]
- 4 to 5 videos per day for about two weeks on a trending product. [L0821.005]
- When running several products on one account, 3 to 5 videos per week or per day per product, logged in a spreadsheet. [L0561.013]

**Stall check and replacement**

1. Upload 3 to 5 videos to a TikTok account for organic testing. [L0309.026]
2. Within the first 24 to 48 hours, look for at least 500 to 1,000 views across videos. [L0309.026]
3. If a video reaches 10,000+ views by the end of day 1, it signals strong potential. [L0309.026]
4. If performance stalls by day 3 to 4, create a new account (new email) and test the same product again. Repeat until one account gains traction or you confirm the product does not resonate. [L0309.026]

**Product test procedure (short)**

1. Upload 3 to 5 videos per day to a test account. [L0309.025]
2. Run this test for 3 to 5 days. [L0309.025]
3. If no meaningful results appear (no views, no engagement, no conversions), kill the product and move to the next one. [L0309.025]
4. Do not run multiple products simultaneously. [L0309.025]

**Creative angle testing before abandoning a product**

Content quality and creative angle are separate variables. One failing does not mean the product fails. [L0309.040]

1. Test six angles before dropping a product: problem-solution framing, lifestyle, emotion, social proof, benefit statement, comparison. [L0309.040]
2. If one angle performs poorly, test two to three different angles with the same product before moving to a new product. [L0309.040]

**Trend-based product start**

1. Find a product that is getting strong views on other TikTok accounts. [L0821.005]
2. Buy the product quickly so you can film with it. [L0821.005]
3. Create several videos for that product using the trending sound and a hook in the style of the viral video, adding your own execution. [L0821.005]
4. Post 4 to 5 videos per day. [L0821.005]
5. Keep posting this way for about two weeks before judging the result. [L0821.005]

- The referenced case reached first real traction only after about two weeks of 4 to 5 posts per day. [L0821.006]

### Week-Two Cycling

1. Run cycles in which a few broad-view videos build reach first. [L0501.018]
2. Follow them with higher-converting videos that carry the momentum into sales. [L0501.018]
3. When views drop, go back to broad-reach videos. [L0501.018]
4. Re-introduce high-converting videos once views recover. [L0501.018]

### View Benchmarks

| Benchmark | Value | Meaning | Source ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Early reach across videos | 500 to 1,000 views within 24 to 48 hours | Minimum early signal | L0309.026 |
| Strong day-1 signal | 10,000+ views by end of day 1 | Strong potential | L0309.026 |
| First-week range | 1,000 to 10,000 views | Expected range for the product video in its first week | L1186.025 |
| Stalled account | 500 to 1,500 views | Typical reach of one account with few videos per product | L0561.010 |
| Growth to keep a product | Steady growth, for example 1,000 to 5,000 views | Keep the product; remove it after a set number of posts without growth | L0561.013 |
| Pivot trigger | 50,000 to 100,000 views with clear interest in another topic | Enough reason to pivot | L1429.023 |
| Viral | More than 1 million views | Definition of viral | L0795.017 |
| Meaningful sales threshold | 1 million to 10 million organic views | Needed before a product produces meaningful sales | L0706.067 |

- A converting video at small scale: one video at around 40,000 to 60,000 views produced four to six sales, which was the breakthrough point for a seller who had tested for about two months. [L1469.012]
- These two values describe different things. The 40,000 to 60,000 view figure is a converting video early in the testing phase, and the 1 to 10 million figure is the general organic threshold for meaningful revenue. [L1469.012, L0706.067]
- Views of 500 or more with strong engagement but no conversions point to product-market fit or the landing page, not the creative. [L0309.035]

### Judging a Product

**Check the signals that matter**

- Judge a TikTok account by video performance and conversion, not by follower count. [L0657.029]
- Followers on TikTok carry less weight than on other platforms: they do not guarantee views or sales. [L0657.029]
- One account with about 1,000 followers produced 56 store sessions in its first few days, while its average video reached about 5,000 views. Store sessions were the clearest signal of audience response. [L0352.002]
- Check how consistently the seller posts, not only the view count. A seller who posts at least daily and keeps uploading is usually still getting some sales, even when individual videos stall. [L0656.001]
- Read the comments for buying intent. Phrases like "where can I buy this", "I just bought one", "I placed an order" or "I want one" signal interest and possible sales. Complaints like "where is my order" signal fulfillment problems. [L0656.006]
- Use views only as an early signal and compare them with actual orders before scaling. [L0372.049]

**Check conversion before scaling a product**

- If a product gets good organic traffic (500+ views, strong engagement) but no sales, check product-market fit and the landing page before changing the creative. [L0309.035]
- If a product gets no organic traffic despite reasonable creative quality, create a new account rather than continuing on a shadowbanned or under-performing one. [L0309.035]

### Kill and Pivot Decisions

**Kill rules**

- Kill a product if a 3 to 5 day test shows no meaningful results (no views, no engagement, no conversions). [L0309.025]
- Kill a product when, after several days, the view count stays flat. Keep products whose views grow steadily and remove the product after a set number of posts without growth. [L0561.013]
- Do not kill a product on zero-view results alone when the creative is the likely cause. Test angles and hooks first. [L1469.012, L1469.013, L0309.040]

**Procedure for several products on one account**

1. Post each product on a per-post basis, roughly three to five videos per week or per day. [L0561.013]
2. Log engagement and views for each product in a spreadsheet over time. [L0561.013]
3. Keep products whose views grow steadily, for example from 1,000 to 5,000. [L0561.013]
4. After a set number of posts without growth, remove the product from the account. [L0561.013]

**Testing a product before paid ads**

- Post organic content to see which products gain traction in views and comments before investing in paid ads. Kill those that do not grow. [L0561.012]

### Comment-Driven Pivots

**Principles**

- Comments are the best feedback on what an audience wants to see. When one reference keeps repeating, pivot the whole angle toward it. [L0764.017]
- A small change of angle can turn a weak account viral. Recognise when to change the content completely. [L0764.047]

**Procedure: audience feedback**

1. Read the comments on every video, especially the top comments. [L0764.016]
2. Look for the same reference, theme or question appearing repeatedly. [L0764.016]
3. Reply to the top comment with a video reply that uses that theme. [L0764.016]
4. If the reply performs well, go hard on that theme and keep repeating it across uploads. [L0764.016]
5. If the existing angle keeps underperforming after a few days, change the content completely instead of waiting. [L0764.016]

**Procedure: pivot from an unrelated trend in the comments**

1. Check videos with real views but weak engagement, and read the comments for a different topic or interest. [L1429.021]
2. Find comments on that topic that have many likes, which signal real interest. [L1429.021]
3. Make a video reply on that topic and connect it to your product. [L1429.021]
4. Take the top comments of the new video and make further video replies from them. [L1429.021]
5. Use trending sounds or trends on that topic, and create your own sounds if that helps. [L1429.021]

**Reference case**

- A product had been tested on TikTok for six to seven days. About three days in, one video reached about 50,000 views, but its comments were about an unrelated trend instead of the product. [L1429.022]
- A video reply on that trend, connected to the product, reached about 250,000 views within 24 hours and about 1 million in total. Its top comments led to further video replies that generated about 3 million additional views. [L1429.022]
- The video was then completely reworked around that interest using a trending sound and custom sounds. It grew from about 200,000 to over 1 million views. [L1429.022]
- Later videos regularly reached over 100,000 views, several about 250,000, and others about 800,000. [L1429.022]
- Moderate view counts of 50,000 to 100,000 are reason enough to pivot when comments show clear interest in something else. Follow the audience's interest instead of the original plan. [L1429.023]

### Views Versus Sales Reality

- A large view count does not guarantee sales. One product video with about 15 million views produced only about 25 orders and under 500 dollars in sales for the store. [L0372.049]
- A viral video's sales usually peak for about 24 hours. After that they decline gradually or sometimes drop sharply. [L0706.041]
- One viral video in a referenced case reached roughly 10 to 15 million views and produced about $1,000 in sales within about 2 hours. [L0821.008]
- A product in the same referenced case kept getting around 4 million views per day for about a month after one video went viral. A single winning video can keep producing sales over an extended period. [L0821.010]
- Videos keep generating views and sales long after you stop posting. A product account with a strong video can keep earning for weeks without new uploads. Count older winners as ongoing revenue when judging an account. [L1384.056]
- Plan for roughly 1 million to 10 million organic views before a product produces meaningful sales. Products reaching only a few thousand views rarely create enough revenue to matter. [L0706.067]

### Retention and Traffic-Source Analytics

**Retention**

- Low average watch time means the video does not hold viewers long enough. Make the editing faster and the pacing tighter. [L1186.018]
- The retention chart shows the second where viewers leave. A sharp drop in the first seconds means the hook is failing and needs rebuilding. [L1186.019]
- Example: a retention curve falling from 100% to 87% and then to about 34% shows a weak hook followed by a steep loss of viewers. That curve needs a new opening. [L1186.020]
- A second drop later in the video points to a specific segment that viewers found boring or confusing. Fix that segment in the next edit so the curve flattens out. [L1186.021]
- Watch time drives distribution. Videos viewers watch to the end keep getting shown. [L1381.007]
- A low-performing video often reflects weak content rather than restriction. Identical copies of a video can still perform very differently, with one example reaching 17 million, 4 million and 2 million views. [L1381.007]

**Traffic source**

- Check the traffic-source split. A For You share of 98% shows the algorithm is pushing the video. [L1186.022]
- A split such as 54% For You and 42% Following suggests weak distribution and may point to a shadow-ban risk. [L1186.022]

### Profile and Engagement Tactics

- Pin up to three videos on the profile, because pinned videos are seen first. They should be professional, high-converting videos, especially when running Spark Ads. [L1381.011]
- Start Spark Ads on a video once it passes about 10,000 views in its first week. [L1186.025]
- Use trending sounds and hooks in the style of a viral video, adding your own execution. [L0821.005]
- Avoid watermarks on re-uploads. In one case, re-uploads that still carried a watermark signalled low quality from the start. [L1384.058]
- Reply to every comment in the first days, and use video replies to lift the newest videos. [L0501.001]
- A product was tested as a quick experiment, with the account uploading for about two to three weeks and then being left with little attention. One video reached 9.5 million views. A YouTube video featuring the same clip produced a visible surge in engagement on the day it was published. The store was closed only a few days before the call, yet earlier videos kept bringing in sales for more than two weeks without new uploads. [L1384.058]

### Common Mistakes

- Relying on one account and posting only a few videos per product keeps reach at roughly 500 to 1,500 views. Spread output across multiple accounts. [L0561.010]
- Posting only five videos and then expecting views is not enough. [L1383.030]
- A seller tested many videos with no views, and accounts were banned, shadow-banned and videos removed on the first day. After about two months of testing hooks, wording, angles and ASMR-style sounds, a video converted at around 40,000 to 60,000 views with four to six sales. From then on, the team could reproduce viral results consistently. [L1469.012]
- Expect a testing phase of about two months before videos begin to go viral. Do not treat early zero-view results as proof that TikTok cannot work for the product. [L1469.013]

## Engagement, Comments and Driving Traffic to the Store

### Followers Versus Sales

- Below 1,000 followers, direct sales from TikTok profile traffic are small, because new viewers rarely trust a small account. Sales typically pick up after the account passes 1,000 followers, and a single video with roughly 5,000 to 10,000 views can be enough to reach that number. [L1380.015]
- Free-product and giveaway-style angles grow followers and views fast, but the audience that responds mostly wants free items and rarely buys. Use them to build early momentum, not as the main sales angle. [L0352.001]
- Giveaway posts grew the follower count quickly but mostly attracted people who wanted free items, not buyers. Sales-focused videos that followed stayed under 5,000 views and drew little traffic. Keep the content aimed at people who want the product, and use giveaways only when the audience matches the product. [L1077.054]
- Engagement drives distribution. When viewers like, follow, watch to the end and comment, the platform sends the video to a larger audience. Ads optimised for viewers who engage and finish watching the video tend to scale better. [L1383.054]

### Audience Matching and Steering

- Engaging with similar creators (liking, commenting and following in your niche) increases your exposure to the audience of those creators. [L0915.011]
- Steer the audience away from kids after a viral video attracts the wrong viewers:
  1. Find another viral video for a similar product and identify its angle. [L0706.053]
  2. Test new content angles that appeal to adults. [L0706.053]
  3. Use hashtags that adults engage with. [L0706.053]
  4. Once an adult-focused angle goes viral, replicate it and reduce the youth-focused content. [L0706.053]
- Redirecting an existing audience with coins is risky because it can drive away current viewers. Use it only when comments show a clear buying segment, such as all male commenters, and target that segment or an age group expected to buy. [L1429.014]

### Comments and Engagement

- Reply to as many comments as possible. Long comment sections raise watch time, and TikTok then pushes the video further. Replying to comments with new videos and asking questions in comments drives engagement. [L0501.035]
- To reply to a comment with a video, tap the comment under your viral video and choose **Make video**. The original comment then appears in the top-left corner of the recording screen, and you place your reply video there. [L0501.036]
- The TikTok video reply lets you answer a specific comment with a new video. Using it on a top comment that shares a theme can pull in viewers who are already engaged with that topic. [L0764.018]
- When a viral video's comment thread is building around its angle, a follow-up video that responds to those comments can extend reach while the trend is active. Only use this if the product really works, because a retraction-style follow-up can backfire. [L0655.028]
- Controversial content that prompts argument in the comments raises engagement and watch time, because the video keeps playing while people read and reply. Some creators deliberately point viewers to the comments to drive interaction. [L1384.025]
- Small deliberate imperfections in a video or caption, such as a visible slip, can draw comments and boost engagement. Keep them mild, because extreme behaviour can backfire on the account. [L0501.043]
