- Do not share your own video by copying its link and sharing it on your own account, because TikTok can detect self-spam. Share actions should come from genuine viewer behaviour, not self-promotion. [L1384.026]

### Calls to Action and Links

#### Calls to action

- Calls to action can boost engagement by asking viewers to comment, share, save or tag. Examples include asking viewers to save the video for later, send it to a gym partner, or tag a friend who needs the product. [L1384.024]

#### Link rules

- Do not put link in bio or any direct link call-to-action in captions or on videos. TikTok is believed to penalise it. If a product link must be shown, a friend or second account can comment that they just bought it and that it is in the description, and the comment can be pinned to the top of the comment section. [L0501.009]
- Excessive use of link in bio calls on TikTok tends to end in a sharp drop-off after an initial viral spike, and shadow bans after large follower counts have been reported. Play it safe with links and do not risk an account that has reached a large following. [L0501.010]
- Avoid tricks such as misspelling link in bio in organic comments to get around algorithm limits. The effect is uncertain, and a mistake can damage an account that took a long time to build. [L0706.028]
- For commenters asking where to buy, redirect them to the link without using the standard link in bio wording. Keep the product visible in the video so viewers have a reason to click. [L0352.005]
- Comment template for redirecting commenters:

```
Hey guys, if anyone is asking, you can find it in the product description. I just bought one, and it's in the description if you want one too.
```
[L0501.037]

#### Comment placement for the store link

- TikTok removed the option to pin comments, so the store link cannot be pinned any more. Instead, be the first to comment or comment under the most-liked comment, pointing viewers to the store. [L1381.021]
- A creator comment placed under the most-liked comment is shown above the other comments. This makes it a reliable place to point viewers to the store. [L1381.022]

#### Product link flagging

- TikTok can flag a product page link when its URL has too many characters, so the link may be blocked or fail. Shortening the product page URL by removing characters can make the link work again. A link problem can also be fixed in the Shopify store settings or at the domain provider, such as GoDaddy. [L1385.015]
- A product link that TikTok flags or that fails may work on mobile while failing on desktop. Test the product page link on both device types before concluding it is broken. Long URLs with many characters are a common cause of flagging, and shortening the product page URL can restore the link. [L1385.020]

### Giveaways

#### Giveaway format

- A giveaway format can drive comments by promising a free product to a commenter whose comment gets no likes within 24 hours. Viewers often like each other's comments to avoid being the winner, which keeps the comment section active. [L1384.028]

#### Fulfilment rule

- Running giveaways you do not actually fulfil, such as promising a free product to a commenter, damages trust and can lead to reports and violations, even if the giveaway drives comments. If you run a giveaway, deliver the prize as promised. If a giveaway is promoted, the prize must be delivered exactly as promised. [L1384.027, L1384.059]

#### Running a giveaway for an account

1. Post a link with a set entry date, here the 10th, for participants. [L0352.045]
2. Participants click or react to the link to enter a random wheel. [L0352.045]
3. The wheel selects a winner, and the result is announced on the set date, here the 15th. [L0352.045]
4. The winner receives the login details and can change the username, password and branding. [L0352.045]

#### Account as prize

- A giveaway account offered as a prize had more than 10,000 followers in the personal care category and was about two to three weeks old. Its followers were reported as organic and real, which makes the account a stronger prize than a bought one. [L0352.046]

#### Case: giveaway growth without sales

- A store was open for one week after a TikTok video went viral. The owner posted three to four videos a day spaced four to six hours apart, mostly giveaway content meant to grow the account from zero toward 1,000 followers, and the account reached about 35,000 followers. One video reached 22 million views within about 36 hours. The store received about 1,220 sessions in the week, with 57 add-to-cart events and 47 checkouts and zero sales. The owner attributed the failure to low-relevance traffic from curious viewers and to the product itself, then stopped posting and closed the store. [L1077.055]

### Monetisation Programmes

#### Creator Next

- Creator Next is accessed via the top-right icon on the profile tab. The course states these requirements: 1,000 followers, 1,000 views in the last 30 days, at least 3 posts in the last 30 days, and age 18 or older. Confirm the view requirement in the app, as the transcript is unclear. [L1380.027]
- The sources give a different follower figure for the shop playlist. At 10,000 followers, apply for TikTok's creator program (transcribed as Creator Next) to get access to a shop playlist, which lets viewers see a shop-now option. Use 1,000 followers as the stated Creator Next requirement and 10,000 followers as the course's point to apply for the playlist. Check current eligibility in the app. [L1381.017, L1380.027]

#### Creator Fund

- Eligibility conflicts across sources. One source reports that the Creator Fund requires at least 1,000 followers, but an account with 10,000 followers was still rejected in one case, and support replies were slow. Verify the eligibility criteria yourself and do not expect automatic approval. [L0372.030]
- Other sources state 10,000 followers as the requirement. Use 10,000 as the planning figure. [L1380.029, L1383.037]
- Payouts: the Creator Fund was estimated at about 30 dollars per million views, so 40 million views would be worth about 1,200 dollars. This is only an estimate from community experience and should not be used as a fixed revenue forecast. [L0372.031, L1381.015]
- The range given in the course is about 20 to 40 dollars per million views. It only pays meaningfully for accounts with large view counts. [L1380.029, L1381.015]
- Product accounts can earn about 1,000 to 3,000 dollars per million views through product-linked content, which is worth much more than the Creator Fund. [L1380.029]
- Sources disagree on whether product accounts should apply:
  - For product accounts whose goal is sales, the course advises avoiding the Creator Fund. It risks view suppression that can hurt sales. [L1380.029]
  - For accounts with about 10,000 followers whose videos already perform well, the course advises applying for the Creator Fund and turning on sponsorships, and continuing to upload well-performing videos even without direct sales. [L1383.037]
- Late-year payouts may slow down because the fund runs out, which can reduce views for creators in the fund. Treat this as a risk to plan around rather than a reliable income source. [L1380.030]
- Some sellers avoid the Creator Fund because they believe it limits organic views. This is an unverified belief. One seller estimated that a viral account could have earned about 30,000 to 40,000 dollars from it but never applied. [L1381.016]

#### Creator Marketplace

- Creator Marketplace offers brand sponsor deals and is not usually used for product accounts. Large accounts have been offered around 2,000 to 3,000 dollars per sponsored video, so it is worth checking as a later revenue option. [L1380.031]

#### Programme comparison

| Programme | Stated requirement | Payout or use | Fit for product accounts | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creator Next | 1,000 followers, 1,000 views in last 30 days, at least 3 posts in last 30 days, age 18+ | Gateway to the app programmes; confirm view requirement in app | Check eligibility | L1380.027 |
| Creator program with shop playlist | Apply at 10,000 followers | Shop-now option for viewers | Use for store traffic | L1381.017 |
| Creator Fund (reported) | 1,000 followers, but 10,000 in other sources; no automatic approval | About 30 dollars per million views (estimate); 20 to 40 dollars range | Avoid for sales-focused product accounts; see conflict above | L0372.030, L0372.031, L1380.029, L1381.015 |
| Creator Fund (accounts with strong organic videos) | About 10,000 followers, apply and turn on sponsorships | Income from well-performing videos | Applies to accounts already performing without direct sales | L1383.037 |
| Product-linked content | Not a programme; earnings from product-linked content | About 1,000 to 3,000 dollars per million views | Preferred for product accounts | L1380.029 |
| Creator Marketplace | Brand sponsor deals | About 2,000 to 3,000 dollars per sponsored video (large accounts) | Later option, not usually for product accounts | L1380.031 |

## Shadowbans, Restrictions and Account Health

### Symptoms of a Restriction

- A restriction shows up as a sudden drop in views compared with recent videos, and several consecutive uploads stay at a similar, very low level. Example: one video at 5,000 views followed by repeated uploads near 80 views is a strong sign of restriction. [L1381.003]
- Judge restriction by views relative to follower count, not by one low result. Views in the thousands on a small account can be normal, while an account with about 100,000 followers that gets only a few hundred views is likely restricted. [L1381.005]

### Diagnosis Before Assuming a Shadowban

1. Check whether the problem is platform-wide. Analytics and Creator Fund issues can affect many accounts and are not specific to yours. Before assuming a shadowban, check whether other accounts report the same delays or problems. [L0372.033]
2. For a new account whose videos get almost no views, check the account setup and VPN use before blaming the content. [L0501.041]
3. If a video stays in review for a long time, check its upload status with the Copy link step before assuming it failed. [L0501.042]

### Causes

- A glitching VPN or other account-level problem can get a new TikTok account shadow banned. [L0501.041]
- Removing several videos in one day may trigger a restriction. [L1381.008]
- Videos from new accounts can be shadowbanned or removed quickly if they contain risky content. [L0372.036]
- Posting a private copy and then publishing the same video again from the same account is risky, as TikTok may see the duplication as a problem. [L1444.030]
- Competitors can file reports against successful accounts, and enough reports can lead to flags even without a violation. [L1384.031]
- Most account removals happen after multiple violations or reports, not after a single incident. [L1384.032]

### Durations

The sources give different values. Read them together.

| Source | Duration | When it applies |
|---|---|---|
| Restriction in general | Usually one to two days; the longest observed lasted about two weeks. [L1381.004] | Ordinary restriction |
| Shadow ban in the described cases | Typically about 14 days before it lifts. [L0819.004] | Shadow ban; the length varies with the content posted during that time. [L0819.004] |
| Several videos removed in one day | Views stayed very low until the account recovered after about one to two weeks of waiting and re-uploading. [L1381.008] | Case of mass removal |

- Expect a few days for an ordinary restriction, and plan for up to about two weeks. [L1381.004, L0819.004]

### Recovery

When an account seems shadow banned:

1. Keep posting about once a day on that account. [L0819.028]
2. Run a new account in parallel. [L0819.028]
3. Expect the shadow ban to usually lift after about 14 days in the cases described, but note that the duration depended on the content being posted. [L0819.028, L0819.004]

- After mass removal, wait about one to two weeks and re-upload videos. [L1381.008]
- A single restriction usually recovers within a short period after a successful appeal. [L1384.032]
- Recovering from a shadow ban can cost weeks of work. [L1444.031]

### Appeals and Review

- Appeals are typically resolved in about 24 hours, sometimes three to four days when TikTok is backed up. [L1384.031]
- A video removed at least once may cause later uploads to go into review more often. [L0501.042]

### Reports and Violations

- Videos that violate Community Guidelines are not pushed to the For You Page and are shown only to the creator's own followers. [L1384.030]
- Repeated violations can lead to a permanent ban. Removal of an account means losing its followers and income. [L1384.030]
- Enough reports can lead to flags even without a violation. [L1384.031]

### Guidelines and Risky Content

- Keep the first videos of a new account safe and avoid borderline jokes until the account is stable. [L0372.036]
- Videos that break the rules lose their reach, so check every video against the Community Guidelines before posting. [L1384.030]

### Deletion Rules

- Never delete a video, because TikTok treats deleted videos as failed. [L1444.027]
- If a video is bad or has an editing mistake, set it to private instead. [L1444.027]
- Do not publish the same video again from the same account after posting a private copy, because TikTok may see the duplication as a problem. [L1444.030]
- If an account stops performing, test the same content on a new account, which is the safer option. [L1444.030]
- Removing several videos in one day may trigger a restriction. [L1381.008]
- Do not delete accounts that have brand, business or personal value right away. [L1381.009]

### Keeping or Abandoning Accounts

- A restricted account with thousands of followers can be kept. [L1381.009]
- For product accounts, a new account is often easier to make go viral than reviving an old one. [L1381.009]
- A large follower count builds credibility with shoppers, so an account with tens of thousands of followers is worth keeping as the main brand account even when its organic views drop. [L1381.010]
- Shoppers who click a Spark Ad often look at the profile first, which is why the follower count matters. [L1381.010]

### Account Roles and Separation

- Keep a separate account for paid ads and for testing new products. [L1381.012]
- Keep the personal account separate from ad and test work. This protects the main account and keeps the work organized. [L1381.012]
- The sources use "main account" in two senses. In L1381.010 it means the high-follower brand account that you keep. In L1381.012 it means the account kept personal and separate from ads and tests. Keep both roles apart. [L1381.010, L1381.012]

### Platform Rule Changes

- Platform rules and TikTok features change often, so check the current rules before relying on any setting or program. [L1380.051]
- Changes are a recurring reason setups fail. [L1380.051]

### Risk Principles

- Keep the risk of account bans low, because a ban can wipe out the views and progress of accounts on the same device. [L1444.031]
- Avoid the mistakes that trigger shadow bans, since recovering from a shadow ban can cost weeks of work. [L1444.031]

## TikTok Ads Account Setup, Pixel and Tracking

### Account Types and Target Countries

- Personal ad accounts showed higher CPMs than agency accounts running the same ad setup. The course attributes this likely to trust factors. [L0296.007]
- Each target country generally needs its own TikTok ad account registered in that market, because an account from one country usually cannot target audiences in another. Plan separate accounts for Australia, New Zealand, the UK or European markets before launching tests there. [L1377.001]
- TikTok Ads Manager only lets advertisers target their own country. A UK advertiser who wants US ads has to use a VPN on a computer to access a US-region ads account. This setup was described as unreliable and prone to issues, so use it only for ads and not for organic accounts. [L1186.034]
- Run ads activity from a desktop computer rather than the phone, because the phone version of Ads Manager does not work for this setup. Keeping ad activity on desktop also keeps the phone separate from the ad account. [L1186.035]

### Browser, Email and Payment Settings

- Create and run new TikTok ad accounts in Safari or another privacy-focused browser rather than Google Chrome, because the course operator saw more account suspensions when using Chrome with extensions. Use a different browser for each new account you set up. [L1377.059]
- Use a new email address for each new TikTok ad account rather than one that has already run ads on TikTok. In the course's experience, TikTok sent verification codes to the email address and not by text message. [L1377.061]
- Browser advice differs by source and case:

| Source | Browser | When it applies | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Safari or another privacy-focused browser, not Chrome with extensions | Each new account in its own browser | General account creation | [L1377.059] |
| Brave instead of Google Chrome | Different from your usual browser | Self-created account after the old one is blocked | [L0562.033] |
| Google Chrome, fully quit and reopened | Chrome, with any TikTok sales channel removed first | US targeting from a blocked location such as India | [L1440.024] |

### Creating an Account Yourself

- Use this procedure to create a new TikTok ad account yourself when the old one is blocked:
  1. Connect a VPN set to the target country, such as the United States.
  2. Log in with a different browser from your usual one, such as Brave instead of Google Chrome.
  3. Create a new TikTok ad account from that browser session.

  [L0562.033]

- Use TikTok sales channel in the US by:
  1. Delete the sales channel integration.
  2. Clear browser cache or use incognito mode.
  3. Open NordVPN and connect to a US server.
  4. Download and add TikTok sales channel again.
  5. Create a new ad account.

  This workaround allows non-US users to run ads to US audiences. [L0309.028]

- Creating a TikTok ads account for US targeting when the business is based in India or another blocked location: Add TikTok as a sales channel in Shopify, creating a new advertising account, enter a US phone number, and connect a PayPal account for payment. The VPN must be set to the US and Chrome must be fully quit and reopened, with any TikTok sales channel removed first. [L1440.024]

### Creating an Account Through a Provider

- Litfix.com is a provider that creates TikTok ad accounts in a chosen country with your email and payment details, then sends you the login. It is used to get an ad account in a target market, such as the United States, Europe or Australia, without setting one up yourself. [L0562.034]
- A TikTok ad account created by a provider in a chosen country, such as the US, can be logged into from the seller's own location without a VPN, because the country is fixed when the account is created. Providers usually sell separate accounts per market, such as US, Europe or Australia, so each new target market needs its own account. A self-created account instead requires logging in through a VPN set to the target country. [L0562.039]
- For TikTok ads from a country where you cannot create ad accounts, a third-party service can create a TikTok ad account for a chosen country (US, Australia, or EU, where the whole of Europe can be targeted). Choose ad account currency US dollars and pay via automatic payment. [L1184.038]
- Third-party account creation steps:
  1. Open the third-party TikTok ad account service.
  2. Choose the ad account type: US, Australia, or EU.
  3. Enter a new email address (a new Gmail account per ad account is recommended, since a password is required).
  4. Enter the store URL.
  5. Enter a phone number to receive an SMS.
  6. Select the currency (US dollars) and the payment method.
  7. Pay; the account is confirmed by email within two days.

  [L1184.039]

### Business Documents

- For a US TikTok ad account, the operator reported that few strict business documents were needed, and the store name could be entered as the business name. Requirements for Australian accounts were not confirmed, so check which business fields are mandatory before creating the account. [L1377.062]

### Ads Manager Setup with Shopify

- Creating a TikTok Ads account and connecting it to a Shopify store with a pixel, in order:
  1. Go to ads.tiktok.com and click Create.
  2. Fill in the personal information and accept the policy.
  3. Choose the payment method: Manual Payment (top up the ads account with a budget) or Automatic Payment (card is charged automatically when a threshold is reached); Automatic Payment is the recommended choice.
  4. Click Go to Ads Manager.
  5. Optionally use the Dashboard to review settings and the business overview.
  6. Change the business or user settings via the account icon at the top right (User Settings: email, username, password, notifications).
  7. Open Tools > Events > Manage Web Events.
  8. Click Create Pixel and choose Partner Setup, then Next.
  9. Select Shopify as platform, open the Shopify app and install the TikTok app in the store.
  10. Scroll down, check that everything is done and click Add Sales Channel.
  11. Click Setup Now and connect the business account via Connect Business Manager.
  12. Set Data Sharing to Maximum, check that the pixel is shown as created, then click Confirm.
  13. Click Finish Setup.
  14. Wait for the review, which takes up to 24 hours.
  15. When activated, the status shows 'TikTok Marketing' as Active.

  [L1373.001]

- In TikTok Ads Manager, the account icon at the top right opens User Settings, where you can edit the email address, username, password and notifications. If the account holds several business accounts, the business can be switched from the same top-right area. [L1373.007]

### Shopify and Pixel Connection

- Install the TikTok Pixel Helper Shopify app and set up TikTok as a sales channel, which connects the pixel automatically; then connect the pixel to the store and to the TikTok Business Manager ad account. [L1376.007]
- Sources disagree on linking the ads account to the Shopify store:

| Position | Advice | When it applies | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Link the account | Add TikTok as a sales channel and connect the pixel, as in the setup steps | Standard path for connecting the pixel to Shopify | [L1373.001, L1376.007, L1440.024] |
| Do not link the account | One seller saw a sudden decline in views after linking and then kept accounts unlinked, creating a second account when a link was needed | Experience of one seller; weigh it against the standard path | [L1381.035] |

### Pixel Creation and Renewal

- When testing TikTok ads with a new product, create a new pixel for each product. Even for running products, change the pixel every three to seven days, because TikTok pixels wear out after a few days. [L1440.027]
- The connection of pixels to a store is not reliable any longer: a strategy of not connecting the pixel is considered outdated and not working as well as it used to. [L1440.028]
- A new pixel gets a grace period in which early traffic is cheaper, so performance can look better briefly. Renewing pixels every day is not a sustainable approach. [L1440.030]

### Backup and Multiple Accounts

- For TikTok ads, several ad accounts can be run from the same registered company setup by creating a new account with a different email address. The Shopify connection is changed in the same way, and the business entity itself does not need to change. [L1440.057]

### Ban Risks

- TikTok ad accounts created from a foreign location via a new device and VPN can get flagged. The lesson's phone-verification workaround with random US numbers or US number services at 2-3 USD per month also carries a risk of account restriction. [L0363.052]
- Logging into a TikTok ad account from a country different from the one it was set up in can cause shadow bans and suspensions again. Use a VPN in the target country or a provider-set account, matching the login location as closely as possible. [L0562.035]
- A prepaid card from the target country can be used to pay for ads from a country where the store is located; the presenter mentions this as a workaround but notes it is not recommended. [L1184.042]

## Coins, Spark Ads and Paid Boosting of Organic Videos

### Choosing between organic testing and paid boosting

- Test the product with organic content first. Create organic TikTok videos and measure product performance over 3 to 7 days. [L0309.021]
- Boost only a video that is already performing. A video with strong engagement and views can be converted into a Spark Ad that runs from that organic video's URL. [L0309.021]
- Spark Ads typically outperform ads made from scratch because they use authentic engagement signals. [L0309.021]
- A two-day test with a small budget indicates whether a product gets sales and is likely to receive organic sales once views come in. [L1376.022]
- Coins help a new account's video reach the right audience faster, so organic reach can follow. The paid portion lets TikTok learn the audience early, and the organic portion can be much larger. [L0501.014]
- Coins are most useful once the content format already works and when you run multiple accounts on the same product. [L0501.014]
- For a product that has already produced proven sales, the approach is to start a new TikTok account for it, spend on coins only during the first few days so TikTok finds the right audience faster, and avoid overspending by limiting boosts to that window. [L1376.027]

**Procedure: accelerate organic reach for a product that already sells** [L1376.027]

1. Choose a product that has already produced proven sales. [L1376.027]
2. Start a new TikTok account for it. [L1376.027]
3. Spend on coins (paid boosts) during only the first few days so TikTok finds the right audience faster. [L1376.027]
4. Use the new account advantage during that window. [L1376.027]
5. Do not overspend on coins; limit the boosts to the first few days. [L1376.027]

**Example (one case, not a guaranteed result):** A product that had already passed six-figure sales was pushed on a new account with paid coins. The new account's video went viral with millions of views within three days. This suggests the early paid boost can compound with the new account advantage. [L1376.028]

### Timing: when to boost

- Spark Ads on a viral organic video are usually run after the viral effect has passed, once the video has slowed down. The video then carries social proof. [L1376.023]
- Organic reach on TikTok is inconsistent. Videos can reach very high views in the first hour and then stop. Whether running ads stops organic growth is unproven, so test it yourself. [L1376.024]
- Some videos go viral repeatedly. One reported video gained another 5 million views every few months. Such videos are good Spark Ad candidates after their viral phase has passed. [L1376.031]
- If a viral video's views start declining, wait a day or two, then add coins to it. [L1429.011]
- Use coins or Spark Ads on a video that is growing but not yet getting sales only after the audience has been checked. [L1429.011]
- A Reach campaign can kick-start a new account by putting a test video in front of many people in the target audience. If those viewers watch to the end and engage, average watch time rises and the platform distributes the video to larger groups. Use this to accelerate organic growth during testing. [L1383.005]

**Procedure: Spark Ads trigger for a test video** [L1186.026]

1. Pick the best organic video from the first days. [L1186.026]
2. If it reaches roughly 1,000 views on day two or three, set up a Spark Ads campaign for it. [L1186.026]

### Buying coins

**Where and how to buy**

- Buy coins on desktop, not on the phone. Desktop is cheaper and gives more coins per dollar. Promote the video afterward from the phone app. [L0501.011]
- Coins bought on the phone cost about 31% more for the same amount. Coins bought on the TikTok desktop version cost about 31% less than on mobile. [L0706.048, L1429.007]
- Price points cited:
  - 1,000 coins cost about 10 USD and fund about 2 days of promotion. A thousand coins is a good starting amount. [L0501.011]
  - On desktop, $14.80 buys 1,400 coins, described as roughly three days of testing. [L0706.049]
- TikTok sometimes sends notifications with coin promo deals of around 20% off. Check these before buying at full price. [L0706.051]
- If you use a VPN, buying coins on desktop may cause problems. Try the purchase in the phone browser instead, and avoid the in-app purchase, which costs about 31% more. [L0706.068]

**Procedure: buy coins on desktop** [L0706.050]

1. Log in to TikTok on desktop using the QR code login. [L0706.050]
2. Open the coin purchase page and select the 1,400-coin package for $14.80. [L0706.050]
3. Complete the purchase, and the coins are added to your account automatically. [L0706.050]

**Login tip:** Log into your TikTok account on desktop, using the QR code login for faster sign-in if needed. [L1429.008]

**Return to the app:** Buy the coins on desktop, then return to the phone app, where the coins boost prompt appears automatically. [L1429.008]

### Coins: setup, objective and audience

**Procedure: coins setup, in this order** [L1429.009]

1. Buy coins on the desktop version of TikTok, which is about 31% cheaper than mobile. [L1429.009]
2. Go back to the phone app; the coins prompt appears automatically. [L1429.009]
3. Choose the goal: More video views, More website visits, or More followers. [L1429.009]
4. Choose the audience: TikTok's automatic targeting, or Custom. [L1429.009]
5. For Custom, select interests, the age range, and gender (male, female, or both). [L1429.009]
6. Choose the button call-to-action, such as Shop now, and enter the website URL. [L1429.009]
7. Set the daily amount and number of days, for example $10 per day for 4 days = $40 total, and check the estimated click range shown before confirming. [L1429.009]

**Objective**

- Choose the coins promotion objective before setting the budget. Website visits send paid traffic to your store. Video views only increase reach. [L0501.040]
- Use website visits once the store is ready to take visitors. [L0501.040]

**Age targeting**

- When targeting coins by age, exclude 13 to 17 year olds because they rarely buy. Typical adult ranges are 18 to 45 or 18 to 54, combined with a gender choice. [L1429.010]
- You can target audiences aged 18 and up when boosting with coins. [L0706.047]

**Review and link rules**

- TikTok reviews coin-boosted videos before promotion. Campaigns aimed at views face fewer restrictions than campaigns that add a website link, so keep links out of boosts when possible. [L0706.046]
- Views-based objectives are more lenient than traffic objectives that include a link. [L0706.047]

**Audience finding through comments**

**Procedure** [L1429.013]

1. Read the comments from people who say they want to buy the product. [L1429.013]
2. Open those commenters' profiles and look at their photos and videos to identify who they are, for example a mom account. [L1429.013]
3. Find other accounts that look similar to define the group you want to reach. [L1429.013]
4. Set the age range and audience of your coins or Spark Ads to match that group. [L1429.013]

### Coins: budget, duration and music

- Coins promotion budget can be as low as 5 USD per day per video. [L0501.013]
- The typical plan is 10 USD per day on one video for 3 days, for example 30 USD of coins spread over three days. [L0501.013]
- Running coins longer than 3 days is not recommended. [L0501.013]
- The setup walkthrough shows a 4-day example ($10 per day for 4 days = $40 total). [L1429.009] Use the 3-day plan as the recommended limit. [L0501.013] The 4-day example applies only as an illustration of the setup screens. [L1429.009]
- A coins boost runs over a 24-hour window from its start time, spreading the budget across that period. [L1429.046]
- Coins only work on videos with original or licensed music, not on copyrighted trending sounds. [L0501.013]

### Coins: what they deliver

- Paid TikTok views cost roughly 2,000 USD per 1 million views at the time discussed. At that rate, 8 million views would cost at least 16,000 USD in ads. This makes organic reach valuable for products with limited budgets. [L0764.023]
- In the cited test, a $100 coins budget generated about 100,000 views, roughly a fifth of the Spark Ads result at the same spend. [L1429.005]
- Coins deliver views more slowly over a roughly 24-hour window and showed no visible harm to organic reach. [L1429.006]

### Reach versus Website conversions

| Measure | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| $50 on Reach | About 50,000 impressions | L1383.002 |
| $50 on Website conversions | About 15,000 to 20,000 impressions | L1383.002 |
| Relative cost | Reach is roughly 2.5 to 3 times cheaper per impression | L1383.002 |
| $25 Reach campaign, test account | About 27,000 to 30,000 views | L1383.003 |

- Choose Website conversions when the ad should generate sales. Choose Reach when the goal is views or an organic push. [L1383.006]
- Do not mix the two goals within the same campaign. [L1383.006]
- The Reach objective has no purchase option or shop button, so it cannot drive sales. Use it only to push views and visibility. [L1383.004]

### Spark Ads: how they work

- Spark Ads run an existing organic video directly from the connected TikTok account, so no new video needs to be produced. [L1376.006]
- Spark Ads boost an existing organic post so it runs as an ad from your own account. Viewers see your profile and earlier videos when they tap through, and a link on the ad lets them buy directly. [L1429.002]
- Spark Ads run under the account's own profile, so viewers can see the followers and buy directly from the ad with a shop-now button. This avoids sending viewers to the profile to find the link. [L1381.026]
- Spark Ads can run without a TikTok pixel or Shopify store link, because the ad uses the authorization code of the organic video. A pixel can be added later if conversion tracking is needed. One seller skipped it for low-budget Spark Ad tests. [L1381.063]
- Spark Ads deliver views fast and can slightly reduce organic reach at times. [L1429.006]

**Identifying a Spark Ad**

- To tell a Spark Ad (a boosted organic post) from a copied ad, open the account behind the ad. A Spark Ad links to the real account that posted the video. A copied ad runs under a different name with no genuine TikTok presence. [L0530.038]

### Spark Ads: authorization codes and authorized posts

**Two routes appear in the sources.** Linking the account in Business Settings makes it selectable as an identity in ad groups. [L1377.070] The authorized-post route runs a Spark Ad without linking the account. [L1383.016] One source warns never to click the option to link your account for Spark Ads. [L1383.014] Choose the authorized-post route when you want to keep the organic account unlinked. [L1383.014, L1383.016]

**Connecting an account (linking route)**

- To use an organic TikTok account for Spark Ads, connect it in the business settings of TikTok Ads Manager. Once connected, it appears in the identity list when you set up an ad group. You can choose it instead of a brand name and logo. [L1377.070]

**Generating a Spark Ad code** [L1381.027]

1. In the TikTok app, open the Profile and go to Creator tools. [L1381.027]
2. Scroll down to Settings, add settings and enable the ad settings. [L1381.027]
3. Open a video that is not copyrighted, tap the three dots. [L1381.027]
4. Slide the bottom menu (Analytics, Save video, Pin, Promote) to the left. [L1381.027]
5. Tap Add settings, then Add authorization. [L1381.027]
6. Generate the code. [L1381.027]
7. In TikTok Ads Manager choose the option to deliver content through Spark Ads, paste the code, and the account is recognized without logging in. [L1381.027]

**Authorized TikTok Post method, without linking the account** [L1383.016]

1. In the TikTok app, open Creator tools and turn on Ad settings. [L1383.016]
2. Open the video you want to run and confirm the music is not copyrighted, otherwise it cannot run. [L1383.016]
3. Tap the three dots on the video, choose Ad settings, then choose Generate code. [L1383.016]
4. Send the code to yourself and copy it. [L1383.016]
5. In TikTok Ads Manager, open the Authorized TikTok Post option and paste the code into the field, then search. [L1383.016]
6. Your account should appear. Select the option Use authorized account, not the option to link your account. [L1383.016]
7. Under Add creative, choose TikTok post and select the video that appears. [L1383.016]
8. Choose whether to duplicate the post, and edit how it appears on the For You page. [L1383.016]
9. Enter the product page URL so viewers who click go directly to the product. [L1383.016]
10. Choose the call to action. Standard is Shop now; Dynamic lets TikTok choose. [L1383.016]
11. Scroll down and click Submit. [L1383.016]

**Upload without the Spark option**

- If you upload a video without selecting the option to use a TikTok account for Spark Ads, the ad runs as a regular TikTok ad. In that case your organic account does not appear on the ad. [L1383.017]

### Spark Ads: volume and budget

**Procedure: scale one winning video into many ad groups** [L1186.026]

1. Pick the best organic video from the first days. [L1186.026]
2. If it reaches roughly 1,000 views on day two or three, set up a Spark Ads campaign for it. [L1186.026]
3. Create one ad group containing only that video with a $25 budget. [L1186.026]
4. Set the payment method to manual and load $25 in advance so the ad spends within minutes. [L1186.026]
5. Duplicate the ad group to create 20 to 30 copies, each with a $25 budget. [L1186.026]
6. Do not add more money to the same video. [L1186.026]

- Pouring repeated Spark Ads money into one video tends to suppress its later organic reach, because organic distribution usually picks up after two to three days. Spend on a video once and let it run rather than repeatedly topping it up. [L1186.027]
- For Spark Ads volume, set up 20 ad groups with one creative in each. With a $100 spend, the cited test generated about 500,000 views, because the approach pushes the post into distribution. [L1429.004]
- Spark Ads were used by one operator on a product with about 50 million views per week. A 50 USD test on Spark Ads was run and then stopped after a few days. [L0819.017]

**Comparison of cited tests at $100**

| Option | Result | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Spark Ads, 20 ad groups, one creative each | About 500,000 views | L1429.004 |
| Coins, one boost | About 100,000 views over roughly 24 hours | L1429.005, L1429.046 |

- The two cited results give different cost-per-view figures: Spark Ads about 200 USD per 1 million views, coins about 1,000 USD per 1 million views. [L1429.004, L1429.005] The figure of about 2,000 USD per 1 million views is the rate the source gave for the time it discussed. [L0764.023] Treat each figure as specific to its test. [L0764.023, L1429.004, L1429.005]

### Spark Ads and organic reach

Sellers disagree on whether Spark Ads reduce organic reach. One advertiser reported that they do. Another saw an organic boost after a small spend ended. [L1381.062] Opinions were mixed and based on small samples. [L0819.017]

- Test Spark Ads on a separate ads account and watch the organic views of the main account before scaling spend. [L1381.062]
- If you run both paid Spark Ads and organic content, keep them on two separate TikTok accounts. One account handles the paid ads and the other stays purely organic. [L1383.007]
- Never click the option to link your TikTok account to deliver Spark Ads. Once linked, the organic account should be considered lost, because the platform tends to limit organic views on accounts used for paid promotion. [L1383.014]
- A seller's other videos can show whether a viral result is repeatable. If they show no sign of the paid-boost pattern, reach likely came from organic posting alone. [L0657.044]

### Judging viral results and sales

- Spark Ads are a candidate explanation when sales arrive in short bursts despite huge view counts. Judging them unlikely just because an account has many followers is weak evidence. Compare the timing of sales with the timing of the views instead. [L1385.018]

## Campaign Setup: Objectives, Targeting and Placements

### Setup order for a website conversion test campaign

1. Open the TikTok ad account, go to Campaigns and click Create. [L1378.001]
2. Choose Custom mode instead of Simplified mode. [L1378.001, L1378.002]
3. Under Conversions, select Website conversions as the advertising objective and click Continue. [L1378.001, L1378.003]
4. Name the ad group after the interest being tested, or "broad" if no interests are used, then continue. [L1378.001, L1378.015]
5. Select the website pixel you created, or create a new one. [L1378.001]
6. Set the optimization event to Complete Payment. [L1378.001]
7. Under Placements, remove Global App Bundle and Pangle so only TikTok remains. [L1378.001, L1378.007]
8. Under Demographics and location, choose the target countries. [L1378.001, L1378.008, L1378.009]
9. Set gender and age (all ages from 18+), leave spending power and audience include/exclude unchanged, and turn on targeting expansion. [L1378.001, L1378.011, L1378.012, L1378.013]
10. Under Budget and schedule, go back to the campaign level, turn on Campaign budget optimization and set the daily campaign budget (example: 50 dollars). [L1378.001]
11. Click Continue, set the start date to the next day at 6 a.m. or midnight, and click Next. [L1378.001, L1378.018]
12. Name the ad, leave Spark Ads off, enter the store name in the ad sign and upload the logo. [L1378.001, L1378.019]
13. Upload the video, add the ad text with a simple call to action, and click Continue. [L1378.001]
14. Add the product page link and click Submit to publish. [L1378.001, L1378.022]
15. After publishing, click the duplicate button on the ad group four times to get five ad groups in total. [L1378.001, L1377.012]
16. Let the campaign run for two days. [L1378.001]

### Entry points and objective

- Two entry paths lead to the same settings. Path A: click Create an ad, choose Website conversions, then select Custom mode instead of Simplified so the full set of options appears. Path B: go to Campaigns and click Create, then select Custom mode. [L1383.001, L1378.002]
- Select Website conversions again inside Custom mode. [L1383.001]
- In the ad group setup, after choosing the Website conversions objective and naming the ad group, the optimization location is set to the website. The store's pixel is then selected in the same section before the optimization event is chosen. [L1378.026]

### Placements

- Remove all placements except TikTok, so the ad runs only on TikTok. Remove Global App Bundle and Pangle. [L1378.001, L1378.007, L1383.010]

### Countries and language

- The countries available for targeting depend on the country where the TikTok ad account is registered, so only options for that registered market appear. [L1378.008]
- German-speaking markets: target Switzerland, Germany and Austria. [L1378.009]
- English-speaking markets: target the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and the UK. [L1378.009]
- Keep the language setting broad, because users may have their phones set to a different language than the one they speak. [L1378.010]

### Age and gender

- Age for broad testing: select all age ranges from 18+. [L1378.012]
- Age for open targeting, default: use 18+. [L1377.009]
- Age for open targeting, larger audience: if the 25+ audience exceeds about 10 million, use 25+, because that group buys more. [L1377.009]
- Age for open targeting, 18 to 24 group: it often gives strong engagement and clicks but weaker purchase conversion. [L1377.009]
- The two age rules differ in when they apply. The broad-testing setup in the handbook uses all ages from 18+. The open-targeting rule uses 18+ as the default and switches to 25+ only when the 25+ audience is above 10 million. [L1378.012, L1377.009]
- Gender: choose based on the product. If most buyers are female, select female, and let targeting expansion reach other genders where TikTok sees potential. [L1378.011]
- Age and gender are the only filters kept on broad setups. Filter both by product. [L1376.030]

### Targeting strategy

- Broad targeting works better on TikTok than specific interest targeting because the algorithm is newer and still optimizing. Let the creative decide which customers it reaches rather than pre-selecting interests. [L0296.008]
- TikTok has always used very broad targeting, so the creative and the message must carry the audience fit rather than the targeting settings. [L0999.055]
- Testing TikTok can reach a younger audience than Facebook. [L0999.055]
- Interest targeting used to perform well on TikTok but now works less well. The recommended setup is completely broad targeting with no interest filters. [L1376.030]
- A broad audience works well only for products with very wide mass-market appeal. Otherwise use targeted interests. [L1440.031]
- Start broad with no interests in the first test, rather than narrowing to specific interests from the beginning. [L1378.014]
- Open targeting is usually the cheapest audience on TikTok, because the platform can show ads to anyone. Stacked interests usually have higher CPMs because they are narrower. Treat stacked interests as a second layer and use them to find a different pocket of buyers. [L1377.010]
- Purchase intention: turn on the TikTok "Purchase intention" option within interest targeting and select broad interests under it. This reaches users who have shown purchase behavior and is meant to attract higher-intent buyers than plain interest targeting. [L1377.008]
- Automated targeting can work for broad, relatable products that appeal to many people, such as simple life-hack or fitness products. Test it as an alternative, but keep it secondary to the open and interest structure for most products. [L1377.011]
- Household income and interest targeting were left at default in the setup shown in the source. These can be tested but were not used as a standard setting. [L1383.012]
- Spending power and audience include/exclude stay at their defaults for broad testing. [L1378.013]

### Audience size and expansion

| Situation | Rule | Ids |
|---|---|---|
| Interest or open audience, target size | At least about 8 to 9 million people | L1377.006 |
| Audience under about 4 to 5 million | Usually shows clearly high CPMs | L1377.006 |
| Interest audience below 8 million | Turn on targeting expansion to widen toward about 10 million | L1377.007 |
| Open or broad, no interests or custom audiences selected | Targeting expansion applies | L1378.013 |
| US broad open audience (18+, all genders, no interests) | Estimated 150 to 200 million reachable people | L1436.091 |

- Smaller audiences tend to produce expensive CPMs and are hard to scale. [L1377.006]
- Expansion lets TikTok reach beyond the chosen interests when the audience is small. [L1377.007]
- Small budgets reach only a small pocket of the broad US audience. This is why separate campaigns are used to find the right pocket. [L1436.091]

### Test campaign structure

- Use 5 to 6 ad groups: two open-targeting ad groups (18+ with no interests), two stacked-interest ad groups, and one hashtag ad group. [L1377.012]
- Split related interests across two stacked-interest ad groups with roughly five interests in each. Keep hashtags in a separate third ad group. [L1377.065]
- Before launching, check that each combined audience reaches at least 8 to 10 million people. [L1377.065]
- Duplicate a finished ad group and change only the audience, so creatives stay identical across groups. [L1377.012]
- The setup order produces five ad groups in total by duplicating the first one four times. [L1378.001]

### Hashtag audiences

- Some TikTok hashtags do not appear as targeting options in Ads Manager, even when they have hundreds of millions of views. [L1374.037]
- Hashtags tied to a brand or a specific product are likely to be excluded. A hashtag may need to exist for some time before it becomes available. [L1374.037]
- The sources differ in emphasis: the hashtag procedure asks for hashtags that describe the product and its niche, while the availability rule warns that brand- or product-specific hashtags are likely to be missing. Use niche-level hashtags and check each one for availability. [L1377.066, L1374.037]

Procedure:

1. Choose hashtags that describe the product and its niche. [L1377.066]
2. Search each hashtag on TikTok without ads and note the ones that appear often in recent videos. [L1377.066]
3. Keep the frequently used hashtags and add them to the hashtag ad group. [L1377.066]
4. Check the audience size and turn on targeting expansion if it is below 8 million. [L1377.066, L1377.007]

### Budget and schedule

- Set the budget with Campaign budget optimization turned on, at campaign level. Example daily campaign budget: 50 dollars. [L1378.001]
- Start date: set it to the next day at 6 a.m. or at midnight, then click Next. [L1378.001, L1378.018]
- Default run hours: start the ad group schedule the next day at midnight and run all day, or run from 7 a.m. to midnight. [L1377.071]
- Narrow the hours only when past data shows that traffic arrives at certain times without producing sales. [L1377.071]
- Ad schedules can be set to run at chosen times instead of running continuously. [L1383.013]
- Let the campaign run for two days before judging it. [L1378.001]

### Naming

- Name each ad group after the interest it tests, so results can be traced to that interest. If no interest is used, name it "broad". [L1378.015, L1378.001]
- Give each video ad a sequential name such as "add 1" for the first video, so every creative can be identified later when comparing results within an ad group. [L1378.027]

### Ad configuration

- Name the ad, and leave Spark Ads off. The option "use TikTok account to deliver Spark Ads" is left off for this test structure. [L1378.001, L1378.019]
- Enter the store name in the ad sign and upload the logo. [L1378.001]
- Upload the video, add the ad text with a simple call to action, and click Continue. [L1378.001]
- Destination: under the link field, add the product page URL, then click Submit to publish the campaign. [L1378.022, L1378.001]

### Comment filters

- Comment filters can be set on ads in TikTok Ads Manager. Use these settings when you run your own ads. [L0706.024]

## Ad Creative and Copy for TikTok Ads

### Ad Performance Weighting: Video Versus Copy

- TikTok ad performance is about 90 percent determined by video content and 10 percent by ad copy. The video carries the conversion weight. [L0204.015]
- TikTok requires video creatives. Images do not work on the platform. [L0577.042]
- Users have already seen the product in the video within the first 3-5 seconds, so the copy's job is to close. [L0204.016]

### Offer and Copy Rules

- Include the product offer or discount in TikTok ad copy in 9 out of 10 cases. The offer in the copy is the final trigger to click the shop button. [L0204.016]
- Keep TikTok ad copy to one line maximum. Longer text will not be visible on mobile. [L0204.017]

### Copy Strategies

The following template is reproduced unchanged:

```
TikTok ad copy strategies (one line each):

**Offer-focused:** [Discount]% off, get yours today | [Discount]% off, limited time only | Buy one get one free, limited time only | Offer ending soon, shop now

**Problem-solution:** Say goodbye to [problem] | Tired of [pain point]? Here's the solution, get yours today.

**Question-based:** Struggling with [problem]? [Product name] is your answer.

**Meme/controversial:** Use punchy, pattern-breaking humor or provocative one-liners that stop scrolling.
```

[L0204.018]

### Native Creative Style

- TikTok ad videos should look like organic TikTok content rather than traditional polished ads. The more native, fun and less salesy the video, the better the performance. Classic Facebook-style ad formats do not work on TikTok. [L1376.004]
- TikTok ads perform best with UGC-style videos that are already native to TikTok. Different creatives should be used per platform. [L1184.040]
- Organic-looking, creator-style videos were outperforming polished ads on TikTok Shop in 2025. Use the top-selling videos as a reference for the format, pacing and hook of your own creatives. [L1479.008]
- GIF-style clips and entertaining content often outperform static material in competitor ads on TikTok. Taglines that grab attention in the first seconds are worth noting and testing in your own creatives. [L0895.031]
- For digital products, the lesson suggested a hook showing someone experiencing a pain point, followed by a transition to the product. This approach is not proven. Check the TikTok Creative Center for competitor creatives. [L0577.046]

**Native clips on TikTok versus Facebook**

| Aspect | TikTok | Facebook |
|---|---|---|
| What is rewarded | Very short, sharp content [L0524.051] | More depth [L0524.051] |
| Native clips as ads | Often underperform on Facebook; work when native and punchy [L0524.051, L1376.004] | Longer problem and solution videos often win [L0524.051] |

### Adapting Organic Posts and TikTok Shop Clips

- Focus on organic growth first, then promote the best-performing organic posts as ads. Ads performed poorly when the posts were not native to the platform. [L1077.020]
- When repurposing an organic video for ads, adjust the text and add an offer with a call to action at the end, such as an instruction to shop now. TikTok ads are judged on views and higher conversion. [L1376.005]

**Procedure: adapting a TikTok Shop video for a Meta ad**

1. Download the video from the source tool only for study, then edit a new cut rather than running the original.
2. Remove all TikTok Shop elements, such as the shop card, the product card and any shop-only buttons.
3. Remove on-screen price overlays that do not match your own selling price.
4. Cut the video down, since the sample testimonial ran almost two minutes and most of it would not be needed on Meta.
5. Keep the hook, the testimonial, the problem and solution, the benefits and the call to action.
6. Add your own call to action and link to your store.

[L0707.022]

**Mistakes to avoid**

- Do not run a TikTok Shop video on Meta unchanged. It still shows shop elements and a price that is not yours. Such mismatches confuse the viewer and can make the ad disconnect from your landing page. [L0707.023]
- Do not keep a video at close to two minutes when the hook and key claims fit in a much shorter cut. Long ads lose viewers before the call to action, so cut all filler and repeat lines. [L0707.024]

**Shop-badge example**

- Short vertical video ads for a seasonal one-size product can show a small TikTok Shop cart badge in one corner. This makes the ad look like it can be bought directly in the feed, which supports impulse purchases. [L0347.038]

### Static-to-Video Conversion

- Once a static creative proves an offer, put that offer into a video ad. Video is more engaging but takes longer to produce. [L0341.023]

### Ad Length

- Keep a TikTok ad under one minute. Short-form ads for TikTok should be quicker and more punchy than longer feed ads. Aim for 30 to 45 seconds when the content allows. [L0344.041]
- The one-minute cap is stated in the source as the limit for Reels and Stories at the time of the course. Check current platform limits before relying on it. [L0344.041]
- A near-two-minute cut is too long when the hook and key claims fit in less time. [L0707.024]

| Format | Target length | Source |
|---|---|---|
| TikTok ad | Under one minute; 30-45 seconds when content allows | [L0344.041] |
| Repurposed TikTok Shop testimonial for Meta | Cut from almost two minutes to the hook, problem and solution, benefits and call to action | [L0707.022, L0707.024] |

### Sourcing Creatives

- TikTok reduces the reach of duplicate content, and the same logic applies to ads that reuse the same video. Fresh creatives are therefore needed for ads. [L1436.025]
- Use creatives uploaded recently, ideally within the last 7 days, that few competitors are using. A video with a good like rate on PPAds is a sign that it is getting strong engagement. [L1436.026]
- A video that has run for more than about 15 to 20 days, or a month, and has gone viral usually gets much less reach when reused in an ad, because TikTok has already analyzed it. [L1436.027]
- Example: a creator video posted three days earlier with about 23,000 to 30,000 views (not yet viral) was reused for ads and scaled successfully, because TikTok had not yet picked it up. [L1436.028]

| Organic video state | Reuse as ad | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Uploaded within the last 7 days, few competitors using it | Preferred | [L1436.026] |
| About three days old, about 23,000-30,000 views, not yet viral | Scaled successfully in the example | [L1436.028] |
| Running more than about 15-20 days or a month, gone viral | Usually much less reach | [L1436.027] |

### Creative Lifespan and Supply

- Creatives on TikTok perform for 1-2 weeks before needing replacement. Plan for consistent creative supply to maintain campaign performance. [L0296.009]
- Creative lifespan on TikTok is about one week, sometimes up to two weeks. [L0637.049]

| Spend plan | Creative supply needed | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Scaling | A steady supply of new creatives per week | [L0637.049] |
| $10k-30k per month | A new creative every two to three weeks | [L0637.049] |

## Testing Structures, Budgets and Automated Rules

### Campaign budget type

- Set the TikTok ad budget type to **Daily**, not **Lifetime**. Lifetime budgets cause spending delays and inconsistent algorithm behavior, especially in high-competition periods such as Q4. [L0309.030]

### Campaign structure: ABO versus CBO

The sources use two budget structures. They differ in where the budget is set, not in what they measure.

| Structure | Where the budget is set | Values in the sources | ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| ABO (ad group budget) | Each ad group gets a fixed amount | $20 per ad group in a 7-15 video test; $20 per ad set on a product with a $10 margin | L1376.003, L1440.029 |
| CBO (campaign budget) | One budget at campaign level, divided by TikTok across the ad groups | $50 per day split across five ads or ad groups; about 50 pounds or 50 Euro per day split across five ads | L1375.001, L0552.025, L1378.017 |

- ABO assigns a fixed budget to each ad set. CBO sets one budget at campaign level, and TikTok divides it across the ad sets. The lesson recommends CBO for the five-ad testing structure. [L1378.016]
- The sources imply a split by test design. Where each video needs a fixed, equal share of spend (7-15 videos at $20 each), use ABO. Where one campaign tests five ads and TikTok should divide the total, use CBO. [L1376.003, L1375.001, L0552.025, L1378.016]
- The five-ad CBO structure is one campaign with five ads, a daily budget of about 50 pounds or 50 Euro split between the five ads, and the same campaign run consistently. [L0552.025, L1375.001] (merged: both sources describe the same structure)

**Setting up CBO**

1. Go to the campaign level, turn on Campaign budget optimization, and set the budget. The example uses a campaign budget of $50 (50 Swiss francs in the Swiss account), spread across all ad sets. [L1378.017]
2. After the campaign is published, a duplicate button appears on the ad group. Click it four times to create five ad groups in total. [L1378.025]

### Budget trick: low campaign cap, high ad-set budgets

**Procedure (use with the warning below)**

1. Create a TikTok Ads campaign and set a campaign budget limit (e.g., $100 for daily spend). [L0309.029]
2. Inside that campaign, create ad sets and set each ad set's budget to $2000-$5000. [L0309.029]
3. The algorithm believes each ad set has more budget than the campaign allows, forcing faster spend. [L0309.029]
4. The campaign-level cap ensures you never exceed your intended daily spend. [L0309.029]
5. To increase overall spend, gradually raise the campaign-level limit in increments (e.g., +$50 at a time). [L0309.029]

**What the trick does and does not do**

- The budget trick compresses the timeline for deciding whether a product is viable. It does not improve results or ROAS. Fast spending answers the question sooner; it does not change the outcome. [L0309.042]
- The result is the same whether you spend $500 gradually over five days or in rapid bursts. Only the timeline changes. [L0309.042]

### Warm-up spend

- TikTok ad accounts often need a daily budget of around 50 pounds or dollars to warm up the pixel. [L0552.024]
- Turning the campaign off early can damage its learning. Keep the same budget running for several days without increasing or decreasing it. [L0552.024]

### Creative testing

**Keep everything except the video identical**

- When testing several creatives, keep the offer, ad copy and audience identical across all ads, so that only the video differs. Otherwise a difference in results cannot be traced to the creative. [L1436.087]

**Creative-led structure (newer approach)**

- With a fully broad audience, the platform finds a pocket of buyers for each creative, so the creative is the variable to test. [L1194.016]
- The older setup (per source) used five ad sets, each with three to five videos and two to three ad copies, duplicated five times with the same creatives. It spread spend across shared assets, so it did not show which single creative was the winner. [L1194.055, L1194.016]
- The newer setup uses 10 ad sets with one unique video each on a fully broad audience. [L1194.055]
- The reset procedure that uses this setup is under "Resetting accounts and pixels". [L1194.015]

**Video and ad-copy test (ABO)**

1. Start with 7 to 15 different videos. [L1376.003]
2. Create one campaign using ad group budgets (ABO, ad-group level budget). [L1376.003]
3. Set the budget at $20 per ad group. [L1376.003]
4. Use only the TikTok placement. [L1376.003]
5. Set age to 25+ (adjust by product and gender). [L1376.003]
6. Use no interest targeting: completely broad targeting. [L1376.003]
7. Place one different video in each ad group. [L1376.003]
8. Use an ad copy built from a short customer-language phrase (four or five words) naming the main benefit, and test several of them. [L1376.003]

**Product test with a budget limit**

1. Choose 4 to 5 interests that correlate with the product, and narrow the targeting further when the product is niche. [L1440.029]
2. Set about $20 per ad set on a product with a $10 profit margin. [L1440.029]
3. When the spend reaches twice the cost per acquisition without a profitable result, switch that interest off and cycle it out. [L1440.029, L0298.041]
4. Spend about $200 to $300 per product with a well-made creative. If nothing works by then, the product is unlikely to take off. [L1440.029]
5. If the product still shows promise, try new creatives or a different marketing angle. [L1440.029]
6. Scale horizontally or vertically once the test works. [L1440.029]

### Evaluation window and daily noise

- Judge TikTok ad performance over a seven-day period rather than day by day. Daily results on low budgets fluctuate and can average out. Short-term swings do not necessarily mean a fault or a glitch. [L0552.022]
- Example: a test with a $50 or 50 Euro daily budget produced five to six sales on the first day, with seven add-to-carts and five checkouts (about 71% from add-to-cart to checkout). On the following day it produced zero sales despite four or five checkouts and add-to-carts. The speaker attributed this to random daily variation. [L0552.023]

### Day-of-week effects

- TikTok performance varies by day of week. Monday-Wednesday typically underperform, and Thursday-Sunday perform better. Adjust expectations and automation rules accordingly. [L0298.040]

### Automated rules

**Setting up rules in Ads Manager**

1. Go to Automated Rules in TikTok Ads Manager (top right). [L0309.031]
2. Select "Manage Rules" or "Create New Rule." [L0309.031]
3. For beginners, use two pre-built rule types: [L0309.031]
   - (a) Control Budget: set a threshold (e.g., "total cost in last 3 days > $X") and an action (turn off campaign or notify). [L0309.031]
   - (b) Enhance Performance: if CTR > 2-3% AND CPC < $1, increase daily budget by $50. [L0309.031]
4. Learn the interface before deploying, as wrong settings can disable profitable campaigns. [L0309.031]

**Kill rules based on break-even**

1. Rule 1: If spend equals 2x break-even cost per purchase with zero sales, pause immediately. [L0298.041]
2. Rule 2: If spend exceeds $80 and ROAS falls below break-even ROAS, pause the ad set. [L0298.041]

### Hour-level waste and bidding

- TikTok can spend budget in low-converting hours, unlike Facebook's delivery algorithm. Check spend by hour when TikTok campaigns run. [L0363.053]
- Manual bidding is not needed on TikTok in most cases. The exception is dayparting blasts later on. [L1440.029]

### Resetting accounts and pixels

**When a reset is justified**

- A reset to a new ad account with a new pixel is a fast fix when CPM and CPC stay far outside benchmarks. A new account showed better CPM and CPC after only $6.60 in spend. [L1194.014]
- This conflicts with the rule not to create a new account for each test. Reset only when CPM and CPC stay far outside benchmarks. Do not reset as routine practice between tests. [L1194.014, L0552.025]

**Reset procedure**

1. Create a new ad account with a new pixel. [L1194.015]
2. Launch 10 ad sets, each with one unique video (or one unique image) and a fully broad audience. [L1194.015]
3. Let them spend, then switch off the underperforming ad sets. [L1194.015]
4. When a winning creative appears, move it into its own campaign and duplicate that same creative into several ad sets. [L1194.015]

## Benchmarks, Diagnosis and Scaling TikTok Ads

### Creative First: The Precondition for Scaling

- TikTok depends heavily on creative and much less on the scaling strategy. Self-scaling, CBO and ABO work mainly because the creatives are strong, not because of the method itself. [L0298.037]
- Before scaling, secure high-quality creatives. Either film original content, or replicate competitor content in your own style rather than copying it directly. [L0298.038]
- Running the same ads that already work for a successful product gives no advantage. A test has to differ from the product's original winning approach in angle, platform or funnel. [L0561.011]
- Scale by producing more distinct video creatives, not by simply raising budget. Scaling budget too aggressively with too few creatives stops results quickly. Lower competition is also a reason to focus on creatives. [L1376.002]

### Benchmarks: CPM, CPC, CTR and Conversion

| Metric | Reference or target | Context | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPM | Typically $10-$15 | Costs are rising year over year | L0296.006 |
| CPM scale trigger | Below $10 | Part of the scale-readiness gate | L1375.006 |
| CPC scale trigger | Below $1 | Part of the scale-readiness gate | L1375.006 |
| CTR | Aim for 1.5% | Standard target | L0774.039 |
| CTR, acceptable | About 0.8% | Acceptable when traffic and store conversion are good, because TikTok CPMs are much lower than Facebook CPMs | L0774.039 |
| CTR, very good | About 0.7-0.8% | Stated as very good on TikTok | L1436.031 |
| CTR, scale trigger | Above 1.5% | Part of the scale-readiness gate | L1375.006 |
| Store conversion rate | Above 1.5% to 2% | Part of the scale-readiness gate | L1375.006 |

**Note on CTR sources:** The sources differ. L0774.039 and L1375.006 use 1.5% as a target and scale trigger. L1436.031 describes about 1.52% as rare. Use 1.5% as the bar for scaling decisions, expect that many ads will sit below it, and accept about 0.8% when CPM is low and the store converts well. [L0774.039, L1375.006, L1436.031]

**Note on the transcript figure:** L1436.031 reads "0.7.8 percent" in the transcript, so treat the exact figure as approximate. [L1436.031]

### Diagnosing Add-to-Cart Without Sales

- When TikTok traffic produces an add-to-cart rate of about 10% to 12% but almost no purchases, the audience is often the problem rather than the page. [L1345.098]
- Excluding a younger group that browses without buying (for example 18 to 24) can lower add-to-cart volume while raising the purchase conversion rate. [L1345.098]
- Judge audiences by purchase conversion, not by the number of add-to-carts. [L1345.098]

### Scale-Readiness Gate

Start scaling when all of the following hold: [L1375.006]

1. CPC is below $1. [L1375.006]
2. CPM is below $10. [L1375.006]
3. CTR is above 1.5%. [L1375.006]
4. The store is making sales with a conversion rate above 1.5% to 2%. [L1375.006]

Before scaling, check the claims in the ads against platform policy. Do not wait for the first sales to find out. [L0638.054]

### Scaling Methods

**CBO scaling procedure**

1. Launch a CBO campaign at a $250-$300 budget. [L0298.039]
2. Create 4 ad groups (ad sets). [L0298.039]
3. Place your best-performing creative in each ad group. [L0298.039]
4. Set up automated rules to manage performance. [L0298.039]
5. If profitable, scale by self-scaling (for example 250 → 350 → 500 → 700), verifying profitability after each increase. [L0298.039]

**Same-day budget increase procedure**

1. On a day when an ad set performs well, raise its budget that same day. [L1469.038]
2. Check results within about three to four hours. [L1469.038]
3. If results stay good, keep the increased budget and continue. [L1469.038]

**Duplication**

- To scale an ad that works, duplicate the ad set into a CBO campaign with a budget of $51 instead of $50. The speaker's experience was that a $51 budget bids better against competitors. [L1469.036]
- Open targeting usually performs well on TikTok. When a particular interest is working, duplicate it to reach the right audience. [L1469.039]
- Duplicate winning creatives as well. [L1469.039]

**Cost cap**

- A cost cap works well for scaling TikTok ads once a winning creative and audience have been identified. [L1469.037]

**Targeting for new CBOs**

- Scaling can mean launching new CBOs with the same broad targeting. [L1375.006]
- Alternatively, test interest targeting by filling the ad group audience instead of leaving it blank. [L1375.006]
- Sources differ on the default: L1469.039 says open targeting usually performs well, while L1375.006 recommends testing interests. Use open targeting as the default, and test interests as a separate step. [L1375.006, L1469.039]

**New countries**

- When ads meet the metric targets and the market is narrow, such as only the US, test additional countries like Canada, Australia and New Zealand, or entirely different markets. [L1375.007]

### Spend Ceilings

- Spend on TikTok ads alone reached about $1,000 per day in the source. Going higher became difficult without a different strategy. [L0637.064]
- Products priced below $60 held up better at higher spend than products priced above $60. [L0637.064]
- Plan a second channel or a new creative strategy before exceeding about $1,000 per day. [L0637.064]
- The same level appears in euros in another unit: about 1,000 euros per day, consistently, for winning products in a niche. The source notes that this scale was limited by the niche. [L1440.023]
- Treat the two figures as the same order of magnitude, since the currency differs between the units. The dollar figure applies to the US-dollar context, and the euro figure applies to the euro context of its source. [L0637.064, L1440.023]

### Multi-Account Fallback

- Running several TikTok ad accounts in parallel lets a seller move spend to a backup account when one is restricted. [L0638.053]
- This is a fallback for account bans. It is not a sanctioned way around policy violations, so the underlying policy issue still has to be fixed. [L0638.053]
- On TikTok, a strong product with strong creatives tends to perform even on a new ad account. Weaker products depend heavily on the standing and history of the account. [L0638.055]
- When testing across accounts, judge the product and creative, since these are the most consistent variables. [L0638.055]

### Ad Restrictions and Prohibited Claims

- TikTok can flag and ban ads or products that make before-and-after claims or weight-loss claims. This often happens within a week or two of launch. [L0638.054]
- Check the claims against the platform policy before scaling, not after the first sales arrive. [L0638.054]
- If an account is restricted, the backup-account fallback applies, but the policy issue must still be fixed. [L0638.053]

## Instagram Reels and Trial Reels

### Account setup and first weeks

- Create the Instagram account, ideally as a business account. [L1186.030]
- Reels content is organic. A business account gives access to analytics and the option to boost posts, and a personal account is not required. [L1186.029]
- New accounts can show zero views for days or weeks before a video takes off. Keep posting consistently rather than abandoning the account. A watermark suppresses only the single video it is on, not the whole account. [L1186.031]
- Growth on any platform depends on regular video posting, so post Reels consistently. [L0915.002]
- When starting, follow accounts similar to your own to see what they post and to find inspiration. Use Instagram's suggested-accounts feature (the plus icon next to a followed account) to find more. [L0915.014]

### Reach expectations and platform value

- Reels can deliver more views than TikTok on new accounts. In the owner's experience, conversion was higher on TikTok, possibly because the emotional content connects more with TikTok viewers. [L1077.021]
- Instagram Reels is useful for brand building and for reaching viewers who need to see credibility before buying. [L1077.021]
- An Instagram following is valued more than an equal TikTok following. For problem-solving products, Instagram may bring more sales, and going viral there is about as easy using the same concept. [L1429.034]
- Follower counts are not interchangeable between platforms. Reach comparison:

| TikTok followers | Approximate Instagram followers (similar reach) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| about 30,000 | 5,000 to 10,000 | [L1379.001] |
| 100,000 | 15,000 to 20,000 | [L1379.001] |

### Cross-posting TikTok videos to Reels

- Instagram can take four to five videos per day, and reposting existing TikTok videos there can produce views. [L0352.044]
- The routine example uses three per day, reposting each day's TikTok videos on Instagram the next day and keeping the same daily count. The two figures do not conflict: four to five is the reported daily capacity, and three is the example routine. [L1186.030, L0352.044]
- Videos that did not go viral on TikTok sometimes perform on Instagram. [L0352.044]
- Cross-posting does not fix a weak angle. In one case, a late cross-post of TikTok content reached only about 500 followers and did not convert sales. [L0764.046]
- Repurpose strong TikTok videos to Reels. [L1077.021]
- Re-uploading a clip to a personal account with a trending sound set to zero was not restricted in the reported case, including after hundreds of uploads. Restriction risk is still possible, so check account notices after each new upload type. [L0795.036]

#### Procedure: moving a TikTok video to Reels with a trending sound

1. Download the TikTok video without watermark using SnapTik. [L0795.033]
2. Upload the file to Instagram Reels. [L0795.033]
3. Open Instagram's audio library and choose a trending sound. [L0795.033]
4. Add that sound and lower its volume to 0. [L0795.033]
5. Keep the video's own audio (the original TikTok sound) audible. [L0795.033]
6. The trending sound is used only to signal the format to Instagram, so it does not need to match the TikTok audio. [L0795.033]

Note on conflicting audio advice: the detailed procedure keeps the original TikTok audio audible under a muted trending sound. [L0795.033] The shorter routine says to keep the video unchanged but replace the original audio with a trending Instagram sound. [L1186.030] Use the detailed procedure when the original audio matters to the video; the sources do not say which applies in other cases.

#### Caption and reply prompt

- For Reels, write a short description with trending hashtags, and end it with a prompt that invites a reply, such as asking viewers to comment a number or post a funny answer. [L0795.034]
- Contest-style prompts such as "funniest comment wins" attract many jokes unrelated to buying intent, so judge comments by quality rather than count. [L0795.034]

### Downloading and removing watermarks

- To reuse your own TikTok videos, save them with a TikTok video downloader such as SnapTik, then upload the files to Instagram. This avoids re-filming content that already exists. [L0352.056]
- Remove the TikTok watermark before posting to Reels, because watermarked videos get suppressed. In one test, a watermarked repost got almost no views. The same video without the watermark reached a few thousand views, compared with a few hundred for other posts. [L1186.028]
- Third-party watermarks reduce reel performance. This includes TikTok watermarks and a brand logo placed in a corner, so remove them before uploading. [L0796.010]
- Posting content you did not create, or without the rights to it, is a serious flag for Instagram. If Instagram suspects it, the account can be taken down immediately. [L0796.016]

### Upload quality and format

- Upload videos in the highest resolution available, because Instagram can compress uploaded files. Edits is recommended for this. [L0796.005]
- InShot is a mobile video editor that can be used to export reels. Export at 1080 resolution where possible. [L0796.006]
- Instagram favors high-quality video, so low-quality videos get less distribution. Film and edit with quality in mind. [L0796.015]
- Reels longer than 3 minutes hurt reel performance. Longer reels can still work below that limit. [L0796.014]
- Test several formats before you know what works for your page, such as a reel of about 2.5 minutes, shorter reels and carousel posts. Let the results guide which formats you keep. [L0796.025]
- When publishing a carousel, add a song, because carousels with music can also appear in the Reels tab. This gives the carousel an extra discovery path. [L0796.026]

### Edits app

#### Recording and editing

- Record in the Edits app only for footage you can easily reshoot. For time-sensitive or non-repeatable shots, film with the phone's regular camera, because a long in-app recording can be lost if the phone overheats or crashes. [L1453.010]
- The Edits camera has a green screen function, a timer, and speed settings, along with the usual camera controls. [L1453.016]
- Timeline layers: Original audio, video clips, Text, Captions, Overlay, Sound FX, and Cutout each get their own timeline track. Each track can be toggled on or off to preview the video without that element. [L1453.018]
- Basic clip editing: drag the clip edges to trim, and use slip to shift the visible portion within a clip without changing its length. [L1453.019]
- Overlay adds a second clip on top of the main video, like picture-in-picture. Add it from the Overlay option on the timeline. [L1453.020]
