2. Send outreach DMs and track replies. From 50 DMs, expect roughly 30 replies, 20 who want the product, and 10 who post on Instagram. [L0915.022]
3. Watch which creators engage with the brand on their own, without prompting. These are the genuinely interested ones. [L0915.022]
4. Invite the genuinely engaged, usually smaller, creators into paid partnerships. [L0915.022]
5. For a challenge or campaign, choose the paid creators from the pool of people already gifted and engaged with the brand. [L0915.022]
6. Secure usage rights before running any creator content through paid media such as Facebook ads. [L0915.022]

### Gifting outreach messages and offers

- Common mistake: a custom cushion brand sent a short email offering a free custom-designed cushion in exchange for showing it on Instagram. The email had only a website link and gave no details about what the brand wanted, the product options, or the deliverables. Creators receive many such emails every day and will rarely do gifted campaigns for an unknown brand, so generic gifting outreach like this is ignored. [L0783.010]
- Template for a gifting offer:

```
Hi [CREATOR NAME],

I saw your [SPECIFIC SERIES OR VIDEO] and loved [SPECIFIC DETAIL]. My name is [YOUR NAME] and I work on creator partnerships at [BRAND].

We would like to send you [GIFT PRODUCT] for your next [PROJECT]. In return, we are looking for one Instagram story and one TikTok post showing how you use it. Please let me know whether you are interested, and feel free to ask any questions before deciding.

Best regards,
[YOUR NAME]
```
[L0783.013]

- Formula for a gifting offer: the creator's name, a specific reference to their work, the gift and what it will be used for in their project, and the exact return asked (for example one Instagram story and one TikTok post). Stating the gift and the expectation together lets the creator judge the offer in one reading. [L0783.014]
  - Example 1: Hi Lena, your upcycling series on small bathrooms is great, and we would like to send you an oak wall panel for your next project. In return we would love one Instagram story and one TikTok post. [L0783.014]
  - Example 2: Hi Sam, your cookware reviews are exactly the style of our customers, so we would like to send you our new cast-iron pan. We are looking for one Instagram reel and one story in return. [L0783.014]
- Gifting procedure for influencer outreach:
  1. Find the creator's PO box address in their Instagram bio or YouTube description. [L1214.038]
  2. Send a product personalized for them, such as a version with their name or a cutout of their photo. [L1214.038]
  3. Include a short note saying the gift is from you, with your social media handle. [L1214.038]
  4. Do not ask for promotion. Smaller creators often promote the gift for free as a goodwill gesture. [L1214.038]

### Seeding relationships before any request (older advice, Source B 2021-22)

- Seed your product to major influencers in your niche, including websites, YouTube creators, Instagram and TikTok creators, larger businesses, magazines, blogs and forums. Send the product and ask for honest feedback. [L0768.016]
- Older advice: when seeding influencers, do not ask for anything in return and do not request a post. Build a real relationship first, because transactional requests for posts rarely lead to results. This applies to seeding established influencers, and it conflicts with the gifting offer format above, which states the return asked. Use the seeding rule when there is no relationship yet and the aim is trust. Use the offer format when the deliverables are defined and the creator is being asked to produce content. [L0768.017, L0783.013, L0783.014, L1214.038]

### Non-posting losses

- About 20 percent of influencers receiving product did not post. Plan for this loss and test enough influencers to find reliable ones. [L0790.064]
- Read this figure as the loss among influencers who already received product. The funnel figures are higher for cold outreach: about 50 percent of creators who asked for product did not post, and about 80 percent of all DMs did not lead to a post. [L0790.064, L0915.017]

### Selecting creators for paid work

- Gifting cannot guarantee coverage, so use it to find genuinely interested creators. Those who engage organically are the best candidates for paid collaboration. [L0915.018]
- For a challenge or campaign, choose creators from the pool of people already gifted and engaged with the brand. They are more authentic and need less briefing on brand image and voice. [L0915.019]
- Do not pick creators only because they are viral at the moment. Choose creators who genuinely invest in the brand. [L0915.021]
- Content produced by campaign creators can be pushed through paid media such as Facebook ads, but only if you have the usage rights to that content. [L0915.020, L0915.022]

### Selling at cost instead of free product

- If free products are not feasible, offer an influencer the product at cost in exchange for shout-outs and links. For example, a $1,000 paddle board can be offered at $500. This is older advice from Source A (2021). [L0671.100, L0671.237]
- Influencer marketing is rarely done with free products. Instead, sell the product to influencers at cost, so you lose no money and still get exposure. This is older advice from Source A (2020). The 2020 source treats at-cost sales as the usual approach. The 2021 source treats it as a fallback when free product is not feasible. [L1277.116, L0671.100, L0671.237]

### Shipping and packaging

- Influencer marketing works best when the product ships quickly, since slow shipping damages the influencer's reputation. [L1184.047]
- A custom box can be designed for the product by a freelancer on Fiverr for about $5 to $10, then quoted by a supplier at about $0.50 per box for around 100 units, which costs about $50. Creators showing the custom box in their videos build a stronger brand impression than plain shipping. [L1382.057]

### Launch seeding with multiple creators and markets

- Launch sequence with untapped-market creators:
  1. Pick three or four influencers in an untapped market, such as certain European countries, Australia or New Zealand. [L1213.039]
  2. Send each influencer a brief specifying the posting day, time and the points to mention. [L1213.039]
  3. First video: the influencer uses the product without introducing it, which creates a rumor and vibe around it. [L1213.039]
  4. Second video: announce the launch date and offer a discount, such as 20%, to people who sign up to the email list before launch. [L1213.039]
  5. Use a signup form on the Shopify store to collect email, name and optionally phone number in exchange for an incentive of 10% to 20% off. [L1213.039]
  6. Let the influencer announce a time-limited sign-up discount, for example valid one to two hours. [L1213.039]
  7. Warm up the new email list with benefit-driven emails before the launch date. [L1213.039]
  8. Sell at launch while stock lasts, then plan the next hype once stock and customization are ready, often 10 to 30 days later. [L1213.039]
- Case: a pre-launch influencer campaign for a product not yet released built a large email list through a signup offer, then sold 20K to 60K per day on launch day. Sales were stopped once stock ran out so existing orders could be fulfilled. [L1213.040]
- Launching with several mid-size creators in the same region at the same time makes a product look widely discussed. Pick three to four creators with roughly 10K to 200K followers each, because their audiences overlap, with about 10 percent of one creator's followers also following another. Their combined posts reach people that no single creator would reach alone. [L1213.083]
- Test a product that works in the US with US influencers, then launch it in a European country such as France with a local influencer. This approach was used in 2020 and produced sales. This is older advice. [L1214.042]
- Case, Mary Roost (multivitamin supplement brand): the brand gained a large TikTok push for its multivitamin hair growth products through a gifting campaign. It sent out large amounts of product and offered affiliate commissions to people who posted videos, without paying flat fees to creators. The campaign targeted several audience groups with separate creators: a health-focused mom, a fitness and supplements enthusiast, a health-field expert giving a scientific explanation, and a younger woman reporting fast hair growth. Once the topic trended and TikTok Shop offered affiliate links, buyers and more creators joined in, creating a domino effect. The campaign showed that it does not cost much: sending product and contacting creators can be enough to start. [L0505.004]
- Principle: a gifting campaign can target several audience segments at once by selecting one creator per segment, each speaking to that segment's specific interests or concerns. Pairing product gifting with affiliate commissions motivates creators to post without flat-rate fees. [L0505.005]

## Pricing, Budgeting and Negotiation

### Fee drivers

#### Audience size and engagement

- Follower count alone does not set an influencer's fee. A larger audience usually commands a higher price, but that link is not reliable, so audience size must be weighed against the other factors. [L0785.001, L0793.001]
- Engagement rate often matters more than follower count. Example: an account with about 500,000 followers and a 20% engagement rate can ask for more than an account with 1 million followers and a 5-6% engagement rate, because its audience is more active and more likely to buy. Engagement rate is a strong signal of what a creator can charge. [L0785.002, L0793.002]
- Price the whole package, not audience size alone. Niche fit, content quality, engagement rate and the campaign's brand objective together determine what is fair and justified. [L0785.005, L0793.005]
- For UGC that the creator posts on their own account, follower count and engagement rate significantly raise the price. The engagement rate on the creator's Instagram or TikTok account should be above 4-5%. If the brand only uses the video itself, follower count and engagement matter little. [L1402.006]

#### Niche and expertise

- Creators who serve a narrow niche or are true specialists charge more, because few creators cover that niche and the market is less saturated. Confirm that the creator's niche and expertise level match what you are budgeting for. [L0785.003, L0793.003]
- Influencers who are one of only a few covering a specific task usually charge more. True specialists in their domain charge even higher rates. [L0793.003]

#### Content quality and track record

- Content quality can justify a higher fee. Relevant factors are production value, brand alignment, how long the creator has worked as an influencer, how much content they have produced, and how well they produce it. [L0785.004, L0793.004]
- A creator with a proven track record, high engagement and a recognised name in the industry, who works in content full time, will usually ask for a higher fee. Leaders in their niche, such as a well-known tech creator, can command a premium because their expertise adds to the collaboration's success. [L0785.010, L0793.006]
- A fair fee is a judgment across audience size, engagement, niche expertise, content quality and the brand's goal. Weigh all of these before deciding what is justified. [L0785.005, L0793.005]

#### Usage rights

- Define the usage term clearly: state the exclusivity and the usage rights you need for the content. Exclusive use, or the right to repurpose content across channels and ads, raises the fee. [L0793.006]
- Price exclusive usage rights, and the right to reuse content in paid ads or across several channels, separately. Charge a higher fee than for organic use on one channel. Write the granted rights into the contract. [L0793.007]
- Document in writing which rights are granted to whom. [L0793.006]
- Royalty alternative: a content creator who makes ad material for a brand can be paid about 3% of the revenue the creative generates in paid ads, instead of a flat fee. This works only when the brand can attribute ad revenue to that content. [L0789.055]

#### Deliverables and campaign complexity

- Define deliverables in detail: the exact scope of posts, stories, costs and creative work the creator must deliver. Each additional element raises the compensation. [L0785.009, L0793.008]
- Assess campaign complexity when pricing. Low-effort campaigns leave room to negotiate a lower fee. Campaigns that need photographers, videographers or specific locations justify higher compensation. [L0785.008, L0793.006]
- Price UGC by use case. Videos for paid ads need higher production quality and justify a higher budget. Organic TikTok content can use lower production quality if it is engaging and attention-grabbing. [L1402.005]
- The platform or company used to source the creator is a major price factor, alongside the use case and the creator's reach. [L1402.007]

#### Pricing procedure

1. Define the usage term clearly: state the exclusivity and the usage rights you need for the content. Exclusive use or the right to repurpose content across channels and ads will raise the fee. [L0793.006]
2. Negotiate the terms openly with the influencer so both sides are satisfied, and document in writing which rights are granted to whom. [L0793.006]
3. Assess the campaign's complexity: low-effort work leaves room to negotiate the price, while high effort such as photographers, videographers or specific locations requires higher compensation. [L0793.006]
4. Define the deliverables precisely (posts, stories, creative work). Each additional element should increase the compensation. [L0793.006]
5. Evaluate the track record: well-known leaders in their niche who make their living from this work charge more, because their expertise contributes to the success of the collaboration. [L0793.006]
6. Negotiate the final compensation with all of these points factored in, and check that the price fits your budget. [L0793.006]

### Market benchmarks

- Influencers charge anywhere from about $50 to about $1 million per collaboration. Before reaching out, determine where your budget sits within that range. [L0793.009]
- Know the market benchmarks for audience size, engagement rate, content quality and your niche before negotiating. Without them you risk overpaying or underpaying. [L0793.012]
- Adjust the market rate for campaign-specific factors such as the influencer's expertise, the complexity of the work and any exclusive rights. Reflect these adjustments in the contract. [L0793.013]

#### Reported rates by creator size and platform

Sources disagree on the rates for small creators. Each row below states the condition under which that figure applies. Rates depend on reach, engagement, recent performance, platform and whether the creator is paid in cash or in product.

| Creator profile | Platform | Reported rate | When it applies | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Celebrity-level creator | Any | Can reach about $500,000 per post | Large reach; small creators with real engagement deliver similar reach for much less | L0528.007 |
| Personal trainer, 300,000 followers, more than 10,000 likes and hundreds of comments per post | Instagram | $100 per post | Real, high engagement relative to follower count | L0528.007 |
| About 100,000 followers in a niche | Instagram | About $5,000 | Niche creator at this audience size | L0661.058 |
| Smaller Instagram creators | Instagram | Free merchandise, or about $50-$300 | Smaller audience, lower engagement | L0661.058 |
| Micro-influencer | Any | $50-$100 per influencer | Tight budget; with $100-$200 you can hire 2 micro-influencers as an alternative to Meta or TikTok ads | L0296.024 |
| Many creators still building an audience | Any | Free product, or about $100 per post | Early-stage creators as a low-cost source of photos and video | L0790.090 |
| 100,000-500,000 followers | Any | Often an upfront payment of about $50-$100, depending on reach | Upfront payment may be needed at this size | L1213.049 |
| Smaller creators | Any | Free product in exchange for a review | Sometimes the only payment needed for small creators | L1213.049 |
| TikTok creator | TikTok | About $50-$200 per post, depending on reach | Creators whose recent posts performed well often charge less | L1214.037 |
| TikTok creator, about 50,000 followers | TikTok | At least $200 for a paid collaboration | Paid collaboration at this size | L1379.010 |
| TikTok creator, about 10,000 followers | TikTok | About $100-$200 | Creator may accept this range | L1379.010 |
| Reported TikTok price range | TikTok | 20 to 45 | Unit (currency or per-thousand-views basis) is not stated; verify before use | L1379.011 |
| New freelance UGC creator | Fiverr | Lower prices | While still building the review record; suitable for small test budgets | L1426.050 |

- Platform changes the price. Instagram creators with a similar follower count often ask for more than TikTok creators. Compare offers per platform before budgeting, and plan a higher rate for Instagram than for TikTok. [L1379.050]

### Budget sizing

#### Budget procedure

1. Assess the overall marketing budget and set a reasonable portion for influencer marketing without compromising the strategy or the business. [L0793.018]
2. Prioritise influencers within that budget. If an influencer is out of reach, choose another who fits both budget and goals. [L0793.018]
3. Research industry standards for audience size, engagement rate, content quality and your niche so you know the usual rates. [L0793.018]
4. Adjust the market rate for expertise, campaign complexity and exclusivity, and reflect this in the contract. [L0793.018]
5. Communicate openly about the budget and any constraints during negotiation. [L0793.018]
6. Show flexibility through long-term collaboration, mutual promotion or affiliate options. [L0793.018]
7. Emphasise the mutual benefit, especially the unique value your brand brings to the influencer's audience. [L0793.018]
8. Discuss a long-term partnership, in which the rate can be lowered for an extended period. [L0793.018]

#### Sizing rules

- The influencer budget should be only a reasonable portion of the total marketing budget. Size it so that it does not compromise the overall marketing strategy or the business. [L0793.010]
- Never choose an influencer whose price is outside your budget, even if you strongly want them. Look for an influencer who fits both your budget and your campaign goals. [L0793.011]
- Test with smaller creators before committing large budgets. A high fee for a large influencer can return far less than expected: one reported $15,000 post returned about $2,000 in sales. [L1214.040]

### Flat versus performance pay

- Flat fee: pays a fixed amount per deliverable. Use it when the deliverables and usage rights are fixed in advance and the brand cannot attribute sales to the content. [L0793.006, L0793.007]
- Royalty: about 3% of the revenue the creative generates in paid ads. Use it only when the brand can attribute ad revenue to that content. [L0789.055]
- Small fixed payment plus affiliate commission: works when the budget is limited. The creator earns a base amount for the post and more for each sale, which aligns their incentive with yours. [L1379.054]
- Affiliate commission for micro-influencers: the offered range is 6-7%. [L0226.005]
- Worked example: a kayak seller offers a local kayaker with a blog or Instagram account 3-5 free kayaks plus a 6% affiliate commission per referral. The creator profits from promoting to their niche audience without large upfront costs. [L0226.006]
- Flat rate for all creators: if a brand pays one flat rate to all creators, for example $500 per creator, state in the brief or negotiation that there is no room to negotiate. [L0579.025]

### Story versus feed pricing

- Story placements are usually much cheaper than feed posts for the same creator. For accounts with roughly 30,000-50,000 followers, a story post is often the better buy for predictable reach. [L1379.003]
- Story posts give predictable reach near the creator's average story views. A feed or TikTok post can go viral but depends on video quality. [L1379.034]
- Choose story posts when consistency matters. Choose feed posts when you want high variance. You can also negotiate both. [L1379.034]

### Seasonal rates

- Creators charge more during the fourth quarter and around holidays. Negotiate and book posts before the season. [L1379.036]

### Negotiation tactics

#### Opening and concessions

- Start with a low offer and increase only if the creator pushes back. Creators who work with you once often accept lower rates the next time. [L1379.012]
- Open communication about your budget and any constraints often leads influencers to come down in price, especially when they want to work with the brand. [L0793.014]
- Negotiate the terms openly so that both sides are satisfied. [L0793.006]
- Ask for the creator's rate directly. For a paid Instagram post, contact the account by direct message and ask for the creator's rate for a post that shouts out your store. [L0528.014]
- For industry event sponsorships, ask for the costs first, because some are expensive and others are affordable. [L0528.014]

#### Non-cash and incentive offers

- Non-cash offers such as long-term collaboration, mutual promotion or affiliate marketing show flexibility and can bridge a gap in the fee. [L0793.015]
- Micro-influencers can be offered a combination of incentives:
  - free products;
  - affiliate commissions of 6-7%;
  - exclusive coupon codes for their followers;
  - free content creation help (guides or product reviews);
  - interviews featuring their expertise. [L0226.005]

#### Mutual value and partnership

- If your brand gives the influencer's audience unique value, the influencer may be more willing to work with you and adjust their rates. Emphasise this mutual benefit in the negotiation. [L0793.016]
- Long-term partnerships lower the cost per collaboration. Influencers value regular income, and the brand gains a reliable partner who keeps working with them over time. [L0793.017]

## Briefs, Contracts and Usage Rights

### Why the Brief Comes First

- An influencer brief should tell a creator the brand voice, the type of video wanted and the goal of the content from the first contact. This matters most with creators the brand has not worked with before, who need more guidance. [L0579.001]
- A precise brief at the start reduces the number of edit rounds and revision loops later. The more the creator understands before filming, the fewer changes are needed. [L0579.002]
- Sending complete information before filming is the most reliable way to avoid wasted time, keep the creator aligned with the brand and get a video that matches what the brand wants. [L0579.027]
- A brief must clarify expectations: the key message, the target audience and the brand tone, for example family friendly with no swearing, luxury and polished, or playful with bright colours. Doing this upfront prevents videos that clash with the brand. [L0579.004]
- The fee must always appear in the brief. It is normally agreed before the brief is sent, which happens once the collaboration and the rate have been discussed. [L0579.024]

### Brief Structure

Build an effective influencer brief in this order: [L0579.008]

1. **Campaign overview:** campaign name, goal, purpose, key dates and deadlines for deliverables. [L0579.008, L0579.009]
2. **Brand background:** tone of voice, target audience, demographics and interests that inform the video. [L0579.008, L0579.010]
3. **Key messaging:** the core message, any call to action, and the specific points the creator must mention. [L0579.008, L0579.011]
4. **Content guidelines:** format ratio, whether on-screen text is allowed, required video length, and rules such as no swearing. [L0579.008, L0579.012]
5. **Content freedom parameters:** a springboard of video types and options, example content, and room for the creator to brainstorm and add their own ideas. [L0579.008, L0579.013]

Section-level rules:

- The campaign overview states the campaign name, the goal, the purpose, and the key dates and deadlines for each deliverable. The creator needs this from the first message. [L0579.009]
- The brand background section defines the tone of voice, the target audience, and the audience's demographics and interests, so the creator can film for the right viewers. [L0579.010]
- Key messaging names the core message and any call to action, and lists specific points the creator must mention, such as a product's number of blades or settings. [L0579.011]
- Content guidelines set concrete rules: the format ratio, whether on-screen text is allowed, the video length (for example 30 seconds), and language limits (for example no swearing). Be as specific as the brand needs. [L0579.012]

### Brief Template

Fill every placeholder and keep the section order.

```
1. Campaign overview
Campaign name: [CAMPAIGN NAME]
Goal: [GOAL]
Purpose: [PURPOSE]
Key dates and deadlines: [DATES]

2. Brand background
Tone of voice: [TONE, e.g. playful, luxury, family friendly]
Target audience: [AUDIENCE]
Demographics and interests: [DEMOGRAPHICS, INTERESTS]

3. Key messaging
Core message: [MESSAGE]
Call to action: [CTA or none]
Must mention: [SPECIFIC POINTS, e.g. number of blades or settings]

4. Content guidelines
Format ratio: [RATIO]
On-screen text: [ALLOWED / NOT ALLOWED]
Video length: [LENGTH, e.g. 30 seconds]
Language rules: [e.g. no swearing]
Other required rules: [RULES]

5. Content freedom
Springboard options: [VIDEO TYPES, e.g. day in my life, get ready with me, tutorial]
Example videos from other creators: [LINKS]
Creative freedom: the creator may use their own voice and approach within the rules above and can propose ideas before filming.

6. Deliverables
- [NUMBER] x [PLATFORM AND FORMAT, e.g. TikTok post with paid media behind it]
- [NUMBER] x [e.g. Instagram grid post]
- [NUMBER] x [e.g. Instagram story]

7. Timeline
- [DATE]: first edit or draft due
- [DATE]: client feedback and changes
- [DATE]: content live

8. Creative
Main talking point: [POINT]
Tone and message: [CREATIVE LINE]

9. Usage rights
Usage period: [PERIOD, e.g. 6 months from the date of the first social post]
Territory: [e.g. worldwide]
Channels and formats: [e.g. brand social accounts, brand and third-party websites, product pages, email marketing, digital ads; computer and mobile]
After the included period: [extra fee per month or none]

10. Fee
Fee: [AMOUNT, e.g. $500 per creator]
Negotiation: [agreed / no room to negotiate]
```
[L0579.026]

### Creative Freedom and the Springboard

- Set firm rules where the brand needs them, but leave the creator room to keep their own voice, since that voice is why their audience follows them. Give tighter guidance at the start and loosen it once the creator understands the brand. [L0579.003]
- Give the creator a springboard instead of a shot-by-shot script: offer one video type or a choice of types (for example day in my life, get ready with me or tutorial), and include example videos from other creators whose look fits the brand. [L0579.005]
- A rigid shot-by-shot list of what to film limits the creator and reduces the chance of getting content that performs. Brands that control every detail often miss trending, high-performing content. [L0579.007]
- Content freedom gives the creator a brainstorming space. If an idea drifts from the brief, redirect it with a reason and a starting point instead of rejecting the creator's idea outright. [L0579.013]
- Brands that want great content should trust the creator's expertise, since the brand hired them for their skills and the style that caught the brand's eye. Keep main points specific but flexible. [L0579.014]

### Deliverables and Timeline

- List deliverables at the top of the brief with the exact number of each piece, for example one Instagram grid post, one TikTok post with paid media behind it, and one Instagram story. Anything not listed can be disputed later. [L0579.017]
- Leaving a piece of content out of the deliverables list, such as the Instagram story, leads to the creator saying they did not know it was expected. Listing every piece removes that argument. [L0579.018]
- Streamline execution by setting dates for idea approval, first draft, final edits and posting. Approving the idea early saves the creator the most time. The dates may shift during production, but the creator must know them from the start. [L0579.006]
- The timeline sets three dates: [L0579.019]
  1. The first edit or draft due date.
  2. A feedback window for client changes.
  3. The go-live date.
  
  Allow more than the minimum time for edits when the deadline is tight. [L0579.019]
- Example: in a sample influencer timeline, the first edit was due on 4 Nov, client feedback on 5 Nov and the post went live on 9 Nov. The course treats a window this short as tight, so allow more time for edits whenever the schedule permits. [L0579.028]
- If the creator needs a physical product before filming, make the first-edit date depend on the product's arrival and say so in the timeline, for example as "first edit (pending product arrival)". This stops the creator from being held to a date they cannot meet. [L0579.029]

### Platform Format and Testimonial Videos

Write the influencer brief and choose the content format using each platform's audience and content style: [L0480.030]

1. Identify the target audience's demographic and the content style that works on the platform. [L0480.030]
2. Pick the format that fits the audience, such as short video on TikTok, visual posts and stories on Instagram, or long-form tutorials and reviews on YouTube. [L0480.030]
3. Write the brief around that format so the content fits the audience you are trying to reach. [L0480.030]

Produce video testimonials with individual reviewers in this order: [L0334.036]

1. Work with each reviewer individually, not with a generic script. [L0334.036]
2. Send a template or brief listing the topics the reviewer must cover, such as premium natural ingredients or high bioavailability. [L0334.036]
3. Specify the lighting and other production requirements. [L0334.036]
4. Spend time crafting the review, because the more time spent on the brief and the review, the better the result. [L0334.036]

- Video testimonials work best when the brief tells the reviewer exactly which product claims to make, so the brand's differentiators appear in every review. Give reviewers a template that covers all required claims and production details. [L0334.037]
- When a product launches in a new market, put that launch next to the main product feature in the creative section. The creator then covers both the feature and the goal of making the market aware of the launch. [L0579.031]

### Gifting and Creator Relationships

- Start creator collaborations with a gifting stage: send product to many creators, then build relationships with those who respond well and continue with them. [L0579.015]
- Creators feel connected to a brand through their direct contact there. A good relationship with that contact makes creators more likely to post stories and to keep the brand voice in their content. [L0579.016]

### Negotiation and Written Agreement

Negotiate and document an influencer collaboration in this order. Once the influencer shows interest, the steps are the same: [L0782.010, L0792.007]

1. Open a transparent, two-way dialogue covering compensation, content requirements, timelines, contract terms and anything else specific to the deal. [L0782.010, L0792.007]
2. Document everything in writing, including compensation, scope of work, deliverables, payment terms and all expectations. A phone or video call alone is not enough. [L0782.010, L0792.007]
3. Provide the resources they need, such as the product, a photographer or samples, or pay for them. [L0782.010, L0792.007]
4. Share brand information, service details and the content you create, so their content stays true to their own style while matching your brand and both sides share the same objective. [L0782.010, L0792.007]
5. Respond quickly and stay available to questions, concerns and collaboration issues so the campaign runs smoothly. [L0782.010, L0792.007]
6. Send a written brief covering the project, campaign, outline, overview and costs. [L0782.010, L0792.007]
7. Thank the creator and aim for a long-term relationship, even if you pay them or send free product. [L0782.010, L0792.007]

Rules for the agreement:

- Every influencer deal must be written down before work starts, including compensation, deliverables, payment terms and expectations. A phone or video call is never enough, and every point, including pay, deliverables and payment terms, must be sent to the creator. Verbal or call-only agreements leave room for disputes. [L0782.011, L0792.008]
- Use a short written creator brief that explains the full project: the campaign, the outline, an overview of the work and the cost. Send it in writing with the rest of the agreement. [L0782.012]
- For products priced above about $30 to $40, use a written agreement with an influencer. Without one, some keep the product and never post, and you have no proof or way to get the product back. [L1213.053]
- Brand information lets a creator stay true to their own style while adjusting slightly to your brand. Sharing it is what makes the final content align with your message. [L0792.009]

### Small-Deal Contract and Approval

Contract steps for a simple post deal: [L0790.063]

1. Send the influencer a short contract: a one-page, three-paragraph digital agreement confirming the product and the post. [L0790.063]
2. Ship the product and confirm it was received. [L0790.063]
3. Receive the photo and caption for approval before the post goes live. [L0790.063]
4. Confirm the post includes your company name in the first eight words of the caption. [L0790.063]
5. Track whether the post was published and how long it stays visible. [L0790.063]

- Approve a new creator's first photo and caption before it goes live. Once a micro-influencer has proven reliable, per-post approval can be dropped so that a brand can keep a pool of about 1,000 creators available. [L0790.098]

### Post Duration and Visibility

Sources give different minimum durations. Use the value that matches the deal:

| Situation | Duration | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Ideal: post stays on the feed, since new followers scan the profile | At least 30 days | L0790.059 |
| 30 days not possible | Anything beyond a seven-day window is considered acceptable | L0790.059 |
| Pay per post for very short durations, such as two hours | Not recommended: does not build lasting brand value | L0790.060 |
| Sponsored deal with a written agreement that keeps the video online | Several weeks or months; one deal ran about six months with three to five posts | L1379.035 |

- Ask influencers to keep the post on their feed for at least 30 days, because new followers scan the profile. [L0790.059]
- Brands that pay per post for very short durations, such as two hours, do not build lasting brand value. Prefer influencers who will keep the content visible over time. [L0790.060]
- Include a written agreement that keeps the video online for a set period, such as several weeks or months, because some creators delete posts shortly after being paid. One deal in this context ran for about six months with three to five posts. [L1379.035]
- For a sponsored deal, one good review video is usually enough, because a creator with a steady audience already gets a consistent number of views. Requesting three uploads per creator is not necessary. [L1379.033]

### Promotion Brief

- Prepare a written promotion brief with the exact story slides, coupon details, shipping terms and posting schedule, because influencers do not know how to promote on their own. Use a cheat sheet listing the templates and questions for the VA to follow. [L0789.054]

### Ownership, Usage Rights and Renewal

Clarify usage rights in this order: [L0784.005]

1. Clarify who owns the creator's content. [L0784.005]
2. Specify the usage duration in the agreement. [L0784.005]
3. Specify the platforms where the content will be posted. [L0784.005]
4. Credit the creator in the caption of every post that uses the content. [L0784.005]
5. If the usage should continue, reach out to the creator before the term ends and agree on a renewal at an additional fee, ideally with a renewal option already written into the contract. [L0784.005]

Usage rights clause, to fill in the bracketed placeholders:

```
USAGE RIGHTS CLAUSE (fill in the bracketed placeholders)

Usage term: The brand may use the Content for [number] months, starting on the date the first post containing the Content is published on the Creator's social media account. When the term ends, the brand must stop using the Content unless both parties agree in writing to a renewal. Any renewal requires an additional fee of [amount] for each extra [period, e.g. month or 30 days].

Ownership: [State who owns the Content and what license the brand receives to use it under the terms of this clause.]

Territory: [e.g. Worldwide].

Formats and media: All digital and electronic media and formats, including but not limited to: the brand's own social media accounts; websites, including the brand's site, third-party websites, and e-commerce product pages; other digital transmission or delivery methods, including email marketing and digital advertisements. This covers use on computer and mobile device platforms.

Credit: The brand will credit the Creator in the caption of each post that uses the Content.

Renewal: [Describe the renewal option, the notice period, and the renewal fee.]
```
[L0784.007]

- A usage term can be renewed with a short extension instead of a new contract. For example, a 30-day extension can be agreed with the creator before the current term expires. The renewal option and its fee should already be written into the original agreement. [L0784.025]

### Crediting Creators

- Always credit the creator in the post caption when reposting their content. This is a low-cost way to build goodwill and trust with the creator. [L0784.006]

### Paid Usage and Boosted Posts

- If the brand plans to boost the creator's TikTok post as a paid ad, state that paid media is behind the post in the deliverables list. This tells the creator in advance that the video will run as an ad. [L0579.030]

### Supplier and Third-Party Video Permission

- Before using supplier videos on social media, confirm the supplier has given permission. Download the video from the supplier's Instagram only with their consent. [L0806.073]

### UGC Brief Prompt

Use this prompt to generate a UGC brief from the brand voice conversation:

```
Using our brand voice and brand guidelines, create a UGC content brief for [PRODUCT NAME]. Include a background on our target consumer [short description], do's and don'ts for the vibe of the content, the filming style, and suggested locations. Keep the brief short and ready to send to a UGC creator together with our brand guidelines document, which includes colors, fonts and style.
```
[L0992.021]

Send a UGC brief to a creator in this order: [L0992.022]

1. Generate a UGC brief from the brand voice conversation that covers the target consumer background, do's and don'ts for the vibe, filming style and locations. [L0992.022]
2. Add the brand guidelines document with the colors, fonts and style. [L0992.022]
3. Send both to the UGC creator so they can produce content that matches the brand. [L0992.022]

## Running and Optimizing Influencer Campaigns

### Campaign Setup and Objectives

**Campaign procedure.** The two Source C versions of this procedure are merged here. Each step lists the ids it draws on.

1. Define one specific objective for the campaign: a new product launch, an upcoming sale, brand awareness, or a new product promotion. [L0787.002, L0868.001]
2. Tell the influencer the objective so both sides understand the goal. [L0787.002, L0868.001]
3. Request a draft of the influencer's content before anything is published. [L0787.002, L0868.001]
4. Review the draft and confirm it matches the campaign objective before publication. [L0787.002, L0868.001]
5. Create the content together with the influencer, as a joint post published alongside their own posts. Agree in advance on what will be posted and which results it should generate, and confirm both sides are aligned on the message and intended result before the campaign goes live. [L0787.002, L0868.001]
6. Publish across your own social media and the influencer's social media at the same time. [L0787.002, L0868.001]
7. Analyze the results, document what worked, and use the insights to choose future influencer collaborations that resonate with your audience. [L0787.002, L0868.001]

**One clear objective per campaign.** Every influencer campaign needs one clear, specific objective before it starts. Typical objectives are a new product launch, an upcoming sale, or promoting new products. Without a defined objective, the influencer's content has no direction and the campaign cannot be measured properly. [L0868.002]

**State the objective explicitly.** The objective must be communicated to the influencer so they understand what the brand is trying to achieve and which product or sale is involved. The influencer should know the specific objective before content is created. [L0868.003]

**Review every draft against the objective.** Never let influencer content go live without first reviewing a draft. Check the draft against the campaign objective, not only for general quality, and confirm its message serves the chosen goal (brand awareness, sales, or a specific product) before it goes live. [L0787.003, L0868.004, L0868.005]

**Co-create the post.** Creating the post together with the influencer, and agreeing on the message and intended result before launch, keeps the content aligned with the campaign goal. This shared understanding reduces the risk of off-message posts. A joint post also gives the brand control over the campaign message. [L0787.004, L0868.006]

**Respond quickly during the campaign.** Answer influencers quickly and handle their questions and scheduling issues in time. Slow or unavailable brand contacts make the campaign feel badly run to the creator, which can hurt both the result and the working relationship. [L0782.016]

### Coordinated Posting and Timing

**Post on both channels at once.** Publishing the same campaign simultaneously on your own channels and the influencer's channels maximizes reach and impact. Coordinated posting across both audiences works better than posting on only one side, and running both channels together is more successful than either alone. [L0787.005, L0868.007]

**Protect the measurement day of a major post.** For a major influencer post:
- Do not run other promotions on the same day.
- Do not let other influencers post on that date.
- Ask the influencer to post within their own two-hour window so traffic can be measured clearly. [L0790.057]

**Approve the first post with a new influencer.**
- Approve the photo and caption before publication.
- Require your company name in the first eight words of the caption.
- Approve all photos and captions for high-priced products. [L0790.058]

**Seasonal window.** The period between Black Friday and Valentine's Day is a strong season for influencer marketing. The influencer receives a product, a script and a coupon code to drive sales. [L1194.051]

**Scale with micro-influencers in bulk.** The goal was about 1,000 micro-influencers available to post at any time. Micro-influencers work best in bulk because each one reaches a small, targeted audience. [L0790.046]

### Promo Scheduling and Story Frameworks

**Five-story Instagram promotion framework.** Each campaign runs over five stories, in this order:
1. Introduce the product, its benefits and the problem it solves, framed as a personal story, such as answering questions about where the product came from. [L0789.041]
2. Demonstrate the product in use, such as showing how to apply a cream or use a hair tool. [L0789.041]
3. Share a coupon code for a limited number of buyers, such as 50 discount codes, plus any free-shipping offer, and mention scarcity. [L0789.041]
4. Ask the influencer to show how to apply the coupon code on the website, by screen recording or on a smartphone. [L0789.041]
5. Repeat the coupon code and remind followers of the deadline. [L0789.041]

Timing of the follow-ups:
- 24 hours later: post a story saying the coupon has sold out and promise another batch later. [L0789.041]
- 24 hours after that: post a story announcing an extra batch of 30 codes, a last-chance message, and extra value such as a bonus. [L0789.041]

**Story script template.** Adapt the wording to the product.

```
Story 1: 'Hey guys, I got a lot of questions about this. People kept asking where I got this. I got it from this brand. It does [benefit] and it helped me with [problem]. This is the product, here is what it does and which issues it solves.'
Story 2: The influencer demonstrates the product in use, for example applying a cream or using the hair tool, on camera.
Story 3: 'Hey, a lot of you have been asking, and I have good news. I reached out to the brand and got a discount code for the next 50 buyers. You get 50 percent off with my code, plus free shipping on orders above [amount]. Enjoy.'
Story 4: Screen recording or smartphone video showing how to go to the website and enter the coupon code.
Story 5: 'Just a reminder, here is the coupon code again.'
Follow-up after 24 hours: 'A lot of you have asked for this coupon. Sorry, it has expired. We will have to wait for the next batch, but I will keep you posted if I can get another one.'
Another follow-up after 24 hours: 'Good news, I got 30 extra codes and I cannot get any more. If you missed it last time, this is your last chance, plus extra value from the brand.'
```
[L0789.042]

**Serial progress videos.** A creator posting a daily check-in on a product's results brings viewers back to follow the next update. This format works best for products where results can be shown over several days. [L0784.026]

### Discount Codes and Exclusive Offers

**Follower-only codes.** Exclusive coupon codes or special offers available only to an influencer's followers create a sense of privilege and special access. This increases redemption rates and strengthens follower loyalty. [L0226.043]

**Limited batches.** The five-story framework uses small, capped batches (50 codes, then 30 extra) and announces sellouts and deadlines to create scarcity. [L0789.041, L0789.042]

### Organic-to-Paid Engagement Posts

**Growing a Facebook or Instagram page with a promoted post.** This is the Source A 2024 approach.

1. Find trending memes or content seen on Facebook, Twitter or Instagram and adapt it to the target customer's audience. [L0666.014]
2. Publish it as a post on the Facebook business page. [L0666.014]
3. In Meta Ads Manager, create a new campaign with the goal set to Engagement. [L0666.014]
4. Choose "use existing post" in the ad builder and select the published post. [L0666.014]
5. Set a daily budget of about 3 to 5 dollars and narrow targeting to the ideal customer (age range, gender, location, interests). [L0666.014]
6. Let it run for a few days, then set the budget to zero and turn the campaign off, since engagement can continue for months. [L0666.014]

### Partnership Ads, Spark Ads and Whitelisting

**Spark Ads boost content designed to convert.** A Spark Ad can give an early boost to a video designed to convert, and organic reach may then take over. Videos can be posted organically first and promoted later, or created from the start for promotion. [L0352.047]

**Spark Ads procedure (TikTok).**
1. Have an influencer create and post content featuring your product on their own TikTok page. [L1374.026]
2. Ask the influencer to whitelist that specific post. This requires only the authorization code for that one post, not their account login. [L1374.026]
3. Run the influencer's post as a Spark Ad from your ad account. [L1374.026]
4. Keep your own organic posts separate from the Spark Ad to avoid damaging their organic reach. [L1374.026]

**Do not Spark-boost your own winning organic posts.** Spark Ads run on the same brand page can kill organic reach. Run Spark Ads from an influencer's post or from a separate page, not from your own successful organic posts. [L1374.027]

**Spark Ads are TikTok-only.** Spark Ads can only run on TikTok placements. If a campaign also uses placements such as Pangle or Audience Network, Spark Ads require a separate campaign limited to TikTok. [L1374.028]

**Partnership ads.** Partnership ads run a collaborator's post as a paid ad. They need the other account's permission before they are set up, and the ad runs through the partner's post under that account's identity. [L0865.036]

**Your own character page versus creator whitelisting.** Running ads from your own character page avoids paying a creator revenue share and removes dependence on a page owner who can withdraw or renegotiate. Creator whitelisting runs ads from a real creator's account, where you have no control over that account. The trade-off of a character page is that you carry all page and account risk yourself. [L1475.004]

**Whitelist pages for video ads.** Whitelist pages also work for video ads, especially UGC. A video that looks like a real person testing the product feels native and gets watched rather than scrolled past. [L1476.027]

**Matching faces.**
- When a UGC video shows a face, pair it with a whitelist character of similar look, such as the same gender and similar hair.
- With several UGC videos featuring different people, use different whitelist pages and match each page to its UGC face.
- A similar look is acceptable. A copy of a real creator's face is not. [L1476.028]

### Handling Audience Saturation

**Move to paid and UGC when an audience is saturated.** Influencer partnerships depend on the audience. When one influencer's audience is saturated, shift to paid ads and UGC to reach new people. [L0789.050]

### Repurposing Creator Content

**Why repurpose.** Reusing creator content reduces production cost, since the video already exists. It also increases reach and authenticity, because the audience sees different people with different experiences instead of the same brand voice every time. [L0784.008]

**Organic videos from unpaid creators.** When a product becomes a trend, creators often post organic videos about it without compensation. If people spontaneously talk about the product, the brand can ask to reuse those videos, as long as the rights are agreed in writing first. [L0784.009]

**Case: a viral candida cleanse product on TikTok.** The brand that drove the movement worked with several creators, each taking a different angle. The lesson does not give the brand's figures or say which creators were paid, but many creators posted without compensation. Five example videos:
1. A creator tried the viral cleanse and posted a daily check-in, with day 4 as one update. [L0784.010]
2. A creator made a comedic video with a funny trending audio about sugar cravings going away. [L0784.010]
2b. The second creator's video was trend-based with no voiceover, using a trending audio. [L0784.010]
3. A creator unboxed the product and walked through her expectations. [L0784.010]
4. Another daily check-in on day 4, which viewers returned to follow. [L0784.010]
5. An instructional video about what to eat and which practices to follow. [L0784.010]

Lesson: when customers organically join a conversation, the brand can repurpose those videos on its own social channels after getting rights. [L0784.010]

**Choose candidates by engagement.** Check engagement metrics, both among followers and among non-followers, to see which content performs best with the broader audience. [L0784.011]

**Prefer evergreen content.** Choose video that still makes sense when shown years later. Avoid renewing rights to trend-based videos, because they lose relevance once the trend ends. [L0784.012]

**Check brand fit before reuse.** Confirm each creator video matches the brand's values and aesthetic before reusing it. The question is whether the video represents how the brand wants to be seen. [L0784.013]

**Re-publish on other platforms.** A UGC video can be reused on another platform by changing the title, description or thumbnail, since these affect click-through rate. The video itself can stay the same. [L1214.052]

### Long-Term Partnerships and Scaling

**One creator over many one-offs.** A long-term partnership with one creator usually delivers more value than many short one-off collaborations with different creators. The relationship produces more connected and authentic content. [L0783.001]

**Ambassador deals and the fade-out.** Long-term ambassador deals can keep producing sales while a creator stays popular, because their audience keeps trying to copy them. Expect the partnership to lose value when the creator's personal brand fades, and plan the budget for that window. [L1214.059]

## Affiliate and Ambassador Programs

### Recruiting Affiliates

#### Where to Find Affiliates

- Start with your Dream 100 prospect list and look for potential affiliates there. [L0202.007]
- Search Google directly for additional affiliates in your market. [L0202.007]
- Evaluate whether each candidate is relevant to your market and products. [L0202.007]
- Reach out by email (using templates) or by phone call. [L0202.007]
- Present your affiliate program offer. [L0202.007]
- Affiliate partners sometimes run offers as banner ads, which you can find during Dream 100 outreach or through searches on forums and Google. [L0288.001]
- A prospect who already runs affiliate deals on a site, YouTube channel or other platform can be added to your affiliate program. They earn a commission per sale and gain new offers to share with their audience. [L0525.010]
- Use an affiliate or commission plan to reward influencers and buyers who promote the product with a referral code, to keep fans engaged after the first purchase. [L0789.052]
- Wholesale accounts such as hotels, cafes and shops can share the product with their own followers, which is a free channel for reaching buyers. Ask each new wholesale partner to promote the product and to let you show their logo on the website. [L1016.076]

#### Finding Content Creators via Google

**Principle**

- Affiliate content creators produce material for the information-gathering stage of the buyer journey (reviews, how-to guides, top-10 lists) rather than commercial-intent keywords, because substantial content performs better with research-phase audiences. [L0215.004]

**Search procedure**

1. Search Google using research-stage keywords: "best [product type]" and "top 10 [product type]" to locate content creators reviewing or comparing products in your category. [L0215.005]
2. Examine the results for review and comparison guide websites. [L0215.005]
3. Click through to these sites to identify which products they recommend and whether they use affiliate links. [L0215.005]

**Mapping the full landscape**

- Test multiple search term variations on Google, such as "best [product]", "top 10 [product]" and related modifiers, to identify all affiliate review and comparison sites active in your product category and geographic market. This comprehensive mapping reveals the full landscape of potential affiliate partners. [L0215.013]
- To map the landscape, search with these variations:
  1. "best [product type]"
  2. "top 10 [product type]"
  3. "[product type] reviews"
  4. "[product type] comparison"
  
  For price-sensitive categories, also search "best [product type] under $[price]" (e.g., "best headphones under $200"). Review the first 2-3 pages of results for each search to identify all major affiliate publishers in your niche. [L0215.020]

**Evaluating candidates**

- Look for reviews comparing multiple products (typically 7 or more), with detailed feature breakdowns, score ratings, and pros/cons for each product. High-effort, comprehensive content indicates a serious publisher worth approaching; thin comparison pages are lower priority. [L0215.014]
- Major media publications (e.g., New York Times, PC Magazine) frequently rank in "best [product]" searches but typically do not use visible affiliate offers due to editorial policies. Focus outreach on independent review sites and content creators where you can confirm active affiliate links, rather than spending effort on large publishers. [L0215.015]

**Confirming an active affiliate link**

1. Hover your mouse over the "See Price" button or product link and read the URL shown in the bottom-left corner of the browser. [L0215.016]
2. If the URL is unclear, right-click the link and select "Inspect" or "Inspect Element". [L0215.016]
3. In the HTML code, locate the `href=` attribute containing the full destination URL. [L0215.016]
4. Look for an affiliate tag parameter in the URL (e.g., "tag=rtings" for Amazon or a similar pattern for other platforms). [L0215.016]
5. If a tag parameter is present, the link is active. If the URL ends at the product ID with no additional parameters, it is not an affiliate link. [L0215.016]

- Affiliate links contain a tag parameter in the URL that identifies the affiliate partner and tracks commissions. Amazon affiliate links use the format `tag=storeidentifier`. Links without this parameter are not affiliate links. [L0215.006]
- In Amazon affiliate links, the text after `tag=` is the affiliate's identifier and activates the affiliate commission tracking system (e.g., `tag=rtings`). [L0215.007]

**Outreach template: message to a potential affiliate** [L0215.017]

```
Hi [Name],

I came across your [article title/topic] and was impressed by your thorough analysis of [number] products in this category.

I noticed you're currently promoting products through [their affiliate program, e.g., Amazon Associates]. I sell [product category or specific products from their review], and I can offer you commission rates that are competitive with or better than what you're earning through [their current program].

[Add one of these based on your situation:]
- I carry the exact same products you reviewed.
- We offer similar high-quality products that fit perfectly with your audience.
- Our products align with the criteria you outlined in your review.

Would you be open to discussing a partnership? I'm happy to share details about commission rates, cookie duration, and partner support.

Looking forward to connecting.

[Your Name]
```

- When contacting a content creator you have identified, propose a partnership by mentioning that you sell the same or comparable products and offer affiliate rates that may be better than or competitive with their current Amazon or alternative program rates. [L0215.008]

**Negotiation**

- After pitching a potential affiliate, expect negotiation. They may accept your terms, request adjustments to commission or cookie duration, or decline. Treat each conversation professionally regardless of outcome, since affiliate relationships matter and a rejection today may become a partnership later. [L0215.019]

#### Recruiting in Facebook Groups

**Procedure**

1. Go to Facebook and search for groups focused on affiliate marketing. [L0215.010]
2. Join established affiliate-marketing communities that permit merchant recruitment posts. [L0215.010]
3. Post your affiliate offer in the group. [L0215.010]
4. Respond to interested affiliates who comment or send direct messages. [L0215.010]
5. Share your affiliate program details with qualified partners. [L0215.010]

**Groups (as listed in the source, 2021-22; member counts may be outdated)**

| Facebook Group | Members | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Affiliate Marketing | 45,000+ | General affiliate recruitment and promotion |
| I Am Affiliate | 6,500+ | Work-at-home and digital advertising community |
| Affiliate Niche Builders | Active | Niche-specific affiliate partnerships |
| Affiliate Pro Community | Active | Professional affiliate network |

[L0215.011]

- Before posting, check the group's pinned posts or description to confirm that merchant recruitment posts are allowed. Some groups restrict posting frequency, require specific formatting, or prohibit direct links; violating these rules can result in post removal or removal from the group. [L0215.021]

**Post template** [L0215.018]

```
Hi everyone,

We're recruiting affiliates to promote [product category] to their audiences.

**Affiliate offer details:**
- Product category: [Specific type, e.g., over-ear headphones, fitness trackers]
- Price point: $[price range]
- Commission: [X]% per sale
- Cookie duration: [X] days
- Tracking platform: [Affiliate software name, e.g., Refersion, Impact]

If you think your audience would be interested, send me a DM and I'll get you all the details to get started.

Thanks!
```

- When posting an affiliate offer in a Facebook group, include: the product type or vertical, the retail selling price, the affiliate commission rate you are offering, the cookie duration and tracking system details, and a clear call-to-action directing interested affiliates to message you for program information. [L0215.012]

#### Affiliates Who Buy Traffic

- Some affiliates buy their own paid traffic and treat the program as a business. They judge a program by whether the commission leaves them profit on offers that convert, not by the size of the catalog. [L0719.048]

### Commission Rates and Cookies

#### Rate Ranges and Benchmarks

| Source | Figure | Context |
|---|---|---|
| Source A (2020) | 5-10% standard | Set toward the lower end unless the affiliate promotes you heavily [L0961.070] |
| Source A (2020, older) | 3-7% | Used by some stores; affiliate programs were used rarely and depended on the store's profit [L1088.087] |
| Source A (2023) | 5% or 7% | Per sale made through the partner's link [L0528.012] |
| Source A (2023) | Up to 30% | Can be considered, but affiliates are hard to win early because a new store has no reputation [L0934.052] |
| Source A (2022) | About 8-10% plus a free product | Needed to recruit influencers or sites through an affiliate app, because a link alone generates no sales [L1113.068] |
| Source C | 10-15% of revenue | Per sale from a unique link; track with Shopify Collabs or another affiliate platform [L1213.050] |

- Where sources disagree, the values apply to different situations: 5-10% (2020) and 5-7% (2023) fit standard programs, 8-10% plus a free product (2022) fits recruiting through an app where a link alone brings nothing, up to 30% (2023) fits only a case where an affiliate is won with a strong offer, and 10-15% (Source C) fits a revenue-based ambassador setup. Source A's 2020 and 2022 advice is older. [L0961.070, L0528.012, L0934.052, L1113.068, L1213.050, L1088.087]

#### Tiered Rates by Partner Status

- Affiliate commission structure: 6% for new affiliate partners, 7% for long-term partners who have consistently performed. [L0226.007]
- Long-term influencer partners earn passive revenue: articles they wrote years ago continue generating income through affiliate commissions and ad placements. Paying 7% commission to experienced partners versus 6% to newcomers acknowledges the compounding value from evergreen content. [L0226.044]

#### Setting the Rate by Promotion

- Set affiliate commissions based on how the affiliate promotes you, such as email to their list, sidebar placements, articles, social media or a footer link. The more prominent the promotion, the higher the justified rate. [L0961.071]

#### Cookie Duration

- Cookie duration is stated in every offer (e.g., "Cookie duration: [X] days") and must be included in outreach and group posts. [L0215.018, L0215.012]

#### Timing

- Affiliate programs work best once a store has steady sales and history. Early affiliate traffic is usually a small share of total traffic. [L0970.124]
- Expect few positive responses from bloggers and YouTube creators until the store has an established sales history. [L0970.123]
- Affiliates are hard to win early because a new store has no reputation; paid sponsored placements, such as a blog post or sidebar image on relevant sites, tend to get results faster in the beginning. [L0934.052]

#### Payment Logic

- The store pays nothing until link clicks turn into sales. [L0528.012]

### Affiliate Software and Setup

#### Refersion

- Refersion integrates directly with Shopify and can run affiliate and influencer programs. It has been used successfully for this purpose. [L0803.079]
- Affiliates who log into Refersion can browse all available banners in the Creatives section, select whichever they want at any time, and test different versions to see what drives more clicks. They do not need to request new assets or wait for custom creation. [L0288.011]

#### Referson / Shopify app

- The Referson app on Shopify runs an affiliate program, where you choose the commission percentage and cookie duration. It works well when your margins allow commissions. [L0961.072]

#### Shopify Collabs and other platforms

- Track affiliate and brand-ambassador deals with Shopify Collabs or another affiliate platform. [L1213.050]

#### Shopify listing partners (complementary stores)

- Shopify stores that are not direct competitors but sell complementary products can list your product for you, with no product data required from you. You then fulfill the order through your supplier and pay them an affiliate-style cut, so this works best for products where you can afford an affiliate fee. [L0869.010]

#### Tracking links and tags

- Use the tag parameter in affiliate URLs to identify the partner and track commissions (see Finding Content Creators via Google above). [L0215.006, L0215.007]

### Banners and Creatives

- Partners with banner ads place image-based advertisements across website headers, sidebars, or other locations. [L0288.001]
- Create banner ads either tied to specific products or as general business-wide promotions. General business banners work well for affiliate placements where partners earn a commission whenever their visitors buy anything from you. [L0288.005]
- You create and provide all banner creatives. Affiliate partners do not create banners for themselves; they expect ready-made, professional options they can immediately use on their sites. [L0288.008]
- Affiliates can choose and test banners in the Refersion Creatives section at any time, without requesting new assets. [L0288.011]

### Tiers and Brand Ambassadors

#### Affiliate and Ambassador Commissions

- Affiliate or brand-ambassador deals pay about 10% to 15% of revenue from each sale generated through a unique link. Track these with Shopify Collabs or another affiliate platform. [L1213.050]
- Formula: Commission = 15% of the revenue from orders placed through the influencer's link. Example: 100K followers with 2% buying gives 2,000 buyers whose purchases form the revenue base. [L1213.051]

#### Upgrading Tiers

- Upgrade affiliates from a Gold to a Platinum ambassador tier once they reach a sales threshold. The upgrade motivates them to bring more sales. [L1213.052]

#### Micro-Influencer Affiliate Program

1. Find small influencers who are active on TikTok or Instagram. [L1439.025]
2. Gift them one product. [L1439.025]
3. They promote it on their platforms. [L1439.025]
4. They receive a commission for every sale made through their channel. [L1439.025]

### Referral Programs

- A referral program lets existing customers refer family and friends, who both get a discount such as a set percentage off. It works better early on than recruiting affiliates. [L0804.058]
- Referral programs can provide customers with ready-made social posts or emails to share with friends and followers. This turns existing customers into a channel that spreads the offer. [L1234.007]

### Brand Ambassadors and Loyalty

- The hourglass funnel turns new buyers into brand ambassadors who are happy to recommend the store. Their referrals bring higher quality traffic back to the top of the funnel, which converts into more customers. [L0676.008]
- Use an affiliate or commission plan to reward influencers and buyers who promote the product with a referral code, to keep fans engaged after the first purchase. [L0789.052]

### Affiliate Apps and Incentives

- An affiliate app only works when you recruit influencers or sites with a strong offer, such as a free product and a commission around 8 to 10 percent, because a link alone generates no sales. [L1113.068]

### Affiliate Partnerships with Complementary Brands

- Outreach to magazines, blogs and authority websites you already have a relationship with: invite them to become affiliates and ask whether they would write a review as an affiliate. [L0768.018]
- Affiliate partners can be asked to add your product to their recommended product list, not only to write a review. This placement on existing lists of trusted sites is a separate step from the review request. [L0768.025]
- Find indirect competitors in your niche (e.g., drum lessons if you sell drum kits): [L0251.026]
  1. Identify indirect competition products related to your niche. [L0251.026]
  2. Search Google for "best [related product/service]." [L0251.026]
  3. Visit top results and look for "Partner Program," "Affiliate Program," or a similar link in the footer. [L0251.026]
  4. Email them directly with your store information and ask about affiliate terms. [L0251.026]
  5. Negotiate the commission structure (fixed dollar or percentage per sale). [L0251.026]
  6. Get a unique affiliate link and promote it on relevant product pages. [L0251.026]

## Paid Placements, Sponsorships and Joint Promotions

### Why Creators Sell Ad Space
- Content creators and large-scale platforms earn revenue by placing advertisements across their websites, YouTube channels, Instagram feeds and audio podcasts. [L0183.003]
- Offer advertisers a cost-free seven-day evaluation period to check whether the placement delivers measurable results before they sign a binding agreement. This appeals to most companies actively searching for additional advertising opportunities. [L0183.003]

### Testing a Placement Before You Commit
Procedure for each prospect that runs paid ads:
1. Complete your Dream 100 Worksheet, identifying people and companies in your niche across all influencer categories.
2. Work through the list and segment out only those that run paid ads.
3. Locate an "advertise" or "contact us" button on their site, or contact them directly via their preferred social channel.
4. Send your outreach message proposing a free one-week trial.
5. During the trial week, track traffic using UTM parameters in Google Analytics to measure sales generated.
6. After one week, review your Google Analytics data for that traffic source to see sales and revenue.
7. Compare the cost of the ad to the sales generated and decide whether to sign a contract. [L0183.007]

### Advertising Early, Before Relationship Building
- Take advertising opportunities with Dream 100 prospects early and directly, without waiting to complete relationship building, provided the cost is within budget. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0202.004]
- Paid advertising can be offered before you reach the 10-engagement threshold. If a site shows an advertise-with-us option, you can buy ad space right away, and the purchase makes the owner aware of your business. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.030]

### Booking Advertising on a Partner Site
Procedure:
1. Find the advertise-with-us link, which is often in a footer or on a contact page of a forum, blog or website.
2. Submit the contact form with your details.
3. Wait for the rate card, which lists prices per placement, such as a banner ad or a sidebar ad.
4. Compare the prices with your budget.
5. If you can afford it, start the booking conversation and buy the placement. If you cannot, keep engaging in other ways and return to it once it fits your budget. [L0525.032]

*Older advice, 2021-2022.*

### Banner Ads on Forums and Blogs
- Forums and blogs often sell banner ad space. You pay the owner to display your banner, which places your brand in front of the same audience every day. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.012]

### Podcast and YouTube Sponsorships
- You pay for a sponsored episode or a sponsor mention, often read at the start of the episode. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.015]
- Podcasters and YouTubers in your niche should be added to the Dream 100 list as well. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.015]
- A sponsored YouTube video or podcast episode can stay online and rank for three to five years, delivering traffic and brand awareness long after it is published. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.016]
- Sponsorships like this do not necessarily have to be expensive. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.016]
- Example: a seller of wine coolers can add wine podcasts to the Dream 100 list and offer to sponsor an episode. Thousands of wine enthusiasts may hear that episode over the years, so the sponsorship reaches a relevant audience. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.017]
- Pitch two placements to the same partner in one outreach, such as a podcast guest slot and a guest blog post, because one contact can open two traffic sources. [L0528.027]
- Influencer traffic works better through advertising on niche authority blogs or websites than through paying random individuals in the niche, because authority sites bring more relevant readers. [L0597.010]

### Paid and Free Product Promotion
- Paid product promotion: some prospects openly publish rates for mentioning your product in a video or sending an email blast to their list. You pay the rate for the placement you choose, so the cost depends on what they offer. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.006]
- Free product promotion: the prospect promotes your products to their audience or email list at no cost, usually because they like them. In return you promote their channel, business or content to your audience, for example with a recommendation or a blog post about them. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0525.005]

### Flat Fee Versus Commission
- A flat-fee ad placement can be cheaper than a commission deal. Example: a banner that costs a couple hundred USD per month but brings over 10,000 USD in monthly sales. Pay for placement first when you can afford it. *Older advice, 2020.* [L0961.073]

### Product-for-Post and Celebrity Video Deals
- A sponsored YouTube video can be paid in product, for example a board valued at up to $800 sent to a smaller creator with high views and engagement. In return the creator makes a video, posts it to the channel and gives a shout-out naming the brand. [L0528.013]
- A celebrity can be paid to record a video that is sent to you rather than posted on their channel. You then post it on your own social media and website, so the celebrity's name and face lend credibility to your store. [L0528.015]

### Endorsements and Specialist Reviews
- Endorsements from recognized authorities or celebrities in your market, such as PGA Tour golfers endorsing golf products, provide credible third-party approval. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0295.008]
- A specialist such as a chiropractor or doctor can review the product on camera; a 30 to 40 second review is enough. Pay the specialist and use the review on the site, landing pages and social media. [L0871.055]
- Only ask a specialist for a review if the product quality is good, since their name will be attached to the product. A simple product with a clear problem is a good fit for this approach. [L0871.056]

### Meme Pages and Repeating Promotions
- Paid placements on TikTok meme pages can be used as a repeating promotion for a product, run about every one to two months. [L0819.026]
- Launch a new batch when the audience gained from the previous batch has been used up and the follower base starts to recycle. [L0819.026]
- Meme pages can post paid content for brands without issue, while influencers may refuse if their followers expect them to appear in the video. Use meme pages to repurpose UGC. [L1214.053]

### Joint Promotions and Collaborations
- Joint promotions let you get your message in front of another creator's audience while they reach yours. Most markets are large enough that this mutual exchange works without taking customers from each other. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0478.026]
- Joint promotion formats include content collaborations, giveaways and competitions. A podcast can be sponsored for one episode, which places your link and product in front of its listeners. *Older advice, 2021-2022.* [L0478.027]
- Collaborate on social media with suppliers, blogs, forums and Facebook groups in your niche by tagging them or working together on posts, which brings the right reach and followers early. *Older advice, 2021.* [L0801.129]

### Free Resources for Influencers
- Offer influencers a free training course, guide or educational resource to promote to their audience. This works as an alternative to affiliate commissions: influencers build credibility by offering exclusive free value, their followers gain access to the resource, and you gain traffic and backlinks. [L0226.045]

### Lead Magnet Placements
- Lead magnet traffic can come from blog banner ads, sponsorships of Facebook groups and forums, Facebook ads aimed at people interested in the niche or its events, and influencer posts. Test these placements with a free offer instead of only using direct discount offers. [L1076.008]
- The lead magnet must match the site, community or influencer where it appears. An offer that fits the audience gets opt-ins, while an off-topic offer gets clicks that never convert to sales. [L1076.009]

## Planning UGC and Choosing Sources

### What UGC Is and Why It Matters

- UGC stands for user-generated content: videos filmed by a real user or creator on a phone, with no professional studio. Such content is often more trusted than polished brand production, so it is a common format for high-performing video ads. [L0707.028]
- Polished ad-style videos made for TikTok ads got almost no views in the referenced case. Reading the feedback and the zero-view results showed the format was wrong. Switching fully to a UGC style fixed the problem. [L0821.018]

### When to Invest in UGC

- Do not spend £120 or more on UGC creators until cheaper ad tests have shown sales. Use image ads or basic videos first. Pay for expensive UGC, such as Billow-style professional creators, only after product-audience fit is proven. [L0308.024]
- Outsource full scripted creative production only for products already proven as winners, or for brands with inventory and data. Do not invest in this production for pure dropshipping tests, because clips and footage are easy to source for those. [L0638.040]
- Buy UGC from marketplaces such as below.app, or hire local creators, only once the product has sales and the store is scaling. In the early phase, use supplier photos instead. [L0661.061]
- Hire UGC creators or an agency once the product shows sales traction and you cannot make your own videos. [L1171.044]
- Outsourcing video creation makes sense once money is available but time is scarce. An external creator team trained to produce converting hooks and calls to action usually beats cheap freelance marketplace creatives, which often lack hook and call-to-action skills. [L1376.016]
- Validate a product with proof of concept before spending heavily. [L1376.017]

**Scale-up trigger: owned creatives through UGC**
