1. Reach the product's first sales of around $1,000 to $2,000. [L1171.043]
2. Send the product to content creators or freelancers. [L1171.043]
3. Ask them to market the product using different marketing angles than the competitors. [L1171.043]
4. Use the resulting videos as your own creatives. [L1171.043]

### Test Cheaply First

- For a fast test, find the product on Amazon with fast delivery (one to two days), order it, and film UGC as quickly as possible. Fulfilling from Amazon speeds up UGC testing. [L0950.049]
- Test an unproven product with cheaper options before paying for established creators. Look for cheaper UGC creators on Fiverr or film your own videos first. [L0950.048]
- Freelance video creation on Fiverr can deliver two to three videos for about 30 to 50 in the lesson's example. Use this option to produce original creatives for testing. [L0638.041]
- UGC-style TikTok ad videos from Fiverr sellers who research TikTok, YouTube, AliExpress and Alibaba can cost about 20 to 30 USD or less per video. Ask the seller about their research and content before placing an order. [L0363.026]
- When outsourcing ads or graphics to freelancers, keep control of the ad copy. Give the designer the core benefits, the offer, and the direction, because graphic designers are not e-commerce experts. [L0950.050]

### Bootstrap Your Own Content

- Film your own videos first. A product can be shown by you, a friend, or in a product order from a store, which gives free creative while you test. [L0398.045]
- A long-form UGC video of about six minutes, where a presenter explains how the product works, is mostly seen on affiliate-marketing products. Film a version yourself with friends, or use a UGC marketplace such as Billo or Fiverr. [L1216.034]
- Creators can film their own videos with a small set of products from bulk orders instead of you paying for production. [L1376.017]
- If a supplier offers free products in exchange for content, accept. You get the product and can use the content for product pages and social media. Post it on Facebook, Instagram and YouTube with the product name. [L0808.052]
- Seasonal products often struggle to get on-season footage once the season has ended, so collect footage in advance. [L1077.053]

### Source Creators at Low Cost

**Procedure: find low-cost creators**

1. Find creators in your niche on Instagram with roughly 3,000 to 50,000 followers. Many of them will film a single video without a large fee. [L0398.045]
2. Use a creator-discovery tool such as Modash to find creators with a high engagement rate. [L0398.045]
3. Message promising creators directly on Instagram. [L0398.045]
4. Order content through a UGC marketplace that lets you chat with creators, and ask for raw clips rather than a finished video. [L0398.045]
5. Use your own footage, a friend, or a product order from a store to produce free creative while you test. [L0398.045]

**Procedure: find TikTok creators**

1. Search the niche keyword on TikTok, for example fishing. [L0561.034]
2. Open the accounts that appear and check their views. [L0561.034]
3. If the largest accounts are too expensive, scroll down until views drop off and hire smaller creators with the same niche. [L0561.034]
4. Small creators are usually cheaper. [L0561.034]

### Cost Benchmarks

Figures mix GBP and USD and are not converted here. Compare only within one currency, and check live prices before you order. [L0308.025, L1077.030, L1402.017, L0637.043]

| Option | Cost as stated | Conditions | Source ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single UGC video, 30 seconds | £120 | Single video | L0308.025 |
| 60-second UGC | ~£300 | Stated as 4 videos of 15 seconds each | L0308.025 |
| High-quality ad creator with team (Billow-style) | £3,500 per month | Full team, for proven products | L0308.025 |
| Billo UGC, one 30-second video | ~£130 | Considered too expensive for a new brand | L1077.030 |
| Billow, 15-second video, one creator | $99 base | Total changes live with every option, so check after each change | L1402.017 |
| Known UGC agency, established product | ~$119 per video | Established product | L0950.048 |
| Average UGC video | $40 to $300 | Depends on platform and factors above | L1402.008 |
| Long-term UGC contract | $250 to $700 per month | At least three videos per day; depends on skill | L1214.048 |
| Fiverr UGC-style TikTok video | ~$20 to $30 or less | Check seller research first | L0363.026 |
| Fiverr, two to three videos | ~30 to 50 | Lesson example | L0638.041 |
| Early tests | Free or ~$10 to $20 | Early testing phase | L0637.043 |
| Paid creators | ~$10 per creative | Budget before hiring | L0637.043 |
| Upwork skilled labour | Cheaper than Billow-style team | Alternative to premium teams, no figure given | L0308.025 |

Where the figures differ, the spread reflects the level of service. A full team at £3,500 per month is different from a long-term per-creator contract at $250 to $700 per month, and a single video at £120 is different from an average of $40 to $300 per video. [L0308.025, L1214.048, L1402.008]

### Compare Sources

#### Freelance Marketplaces: Fiverr and Upwork

- Fiverr is a freelancer marketplace where UGC creators can be found by searching UGC. Buyers can review past work, and prices are described as fair. [L1402.011]
- Fiverr and Upwork can be used to hire video creators. [L0321.018]
- Fiverr and Upwork can be used to hire video editors and freelance UGC creators when footage and story already exist. [L0561.036]
- Upwork offers a cheaper skilled-labour alternative. [L0308.025]
- Fiverr and training a TikTok creator were suggested as sources of UGC talent. [L1214.054]
- Freelance marketplace creatives often lack hook and call-to-action skills. [L1376.016]

#### Platform Marketplaces: Billow, Billo and below.app

- Billow (also spelled Billo or Bilo in the sources) is a complete UGC platform. You define a video order, pay, and then choose from creators who apply. The speaker uses it for ads and says it offers the most options of the platforms shown. [L1402.014, L1077.030, L1214.054]
- Billo UGC is an alternative for long-form videos, along with Fiverr. [L1216.034]
- Bilo was once a recommended UGC source, but its quality was described as dropping after it grew. [L1214.054]
- A UGC marketplace that lets you chat with creators is useful for requesting raw clips. [L0398.045]
- below.app is a UGC marketplace, to be used only once the product has sales. [L0661.061]

#### TikTok Creator Marketplace and TikTok Creative Center

- TikTok Creator Marketplace (creatormarketplace.tiktok.com) lets brands run campaigns that creators apply to. It is used to get UGC made by creators who respond to a brand brief. [L1402.009]
- The TikTok Creative Marketplace requires a TikTok business account. [L0637.042]
- Top-performing ads in TikTok Creative Center often use UGC-style videos made by creators or agencies. Many promote dropshipping products from AliExpress, so they are useful leads for sourcing. [L0706.019]

#### X/Twitter, LinkedIn and Facebook Groups

**Procedure: find UGC creators on Twitter (variant A)**

1. Search for ugc or ugc creator. [L0561.035]
2. Sort results by Top. [L0561.035]
3. Use the advanced search to narrow results. [L0561.035]
4. Contact the creators who post UGC services directly. [L0561.035]

**Procedure: hire a UGC creator on Twitter (variant B)**

1. Open the Twitter search bar and type a keyword such as UGC. [L1214.047]
2. Switch to the Latest tab to see recent posts. [L1214.047]
3. Open promising profiles and check their work, such as an Etsy shop, YouTube channel or TikTok account. [L1214.047]
4. Review their past UGC videos for editing quality. [L1214.047]
5. Message them to offer a paid collaboration. [L1214.047]

**Procedure: find UGC creators on Twitter (X) (variant C)**

1. Search for UGC content creator. [L1402.013]
2. Open profiles of people who offer content creation services. [L1402.013]
3. Check their posts and their Media tab to see past work. [L1402.013]
4. If the work fits, send them a direct message to agree on terms. [L1402.013]

Other social and sourcing channels named in the source are X/Twitter hashtags such as #ugc and #ugccreator, LinkedIn job posts, and Facebook groups for local actors. [L0637.042]

#### Agencies and Full Production

- Companies found by searching for UGC content creator on Google are a UGC option. Shop around and compare them. [L0561.039]
- Outsourced video production for Facebook ads can work in this order:
  1. Hand the Facebook and Google ad management to an agency. [L0349.031]
  2. The agency sends scripts to content creators. [L0349.031]
  3. The creators shoot the videos based on those scripts. [L0349.031]
  4. An agency editor cuts the footage into finished ads. [L0349.031]
- Hire an agency to produce UGC once the product shows sales traction and you cannot make your own videos. [L1171.044]

#### Local Creators, Micro-influencers and Models

**Procedure: local platform production**

1. Send the product to a local platform that creates custom videos from user-generated content. [L0492.047]
2. Hire several models to show unboxing, use and comfort. [L0492.047]
3. Find an influencer from the target audience to show how to use the product. [L0492.047]
4. Use the resulting videos as social proof for paid ads. [L0492.047]

**Procedure: micro-influencer footage**

1. Identify micro-influencers who create content you would like to use. [L1077.029]
2. Reach out to them with an offer. [L1077.029]
3. Send merchandise in return for video footage and b-roll that you can use on your own social accounts. [L1077.029, L1077.053]
4. Confirm you have secured the footage rights before relying on the partnership for content. [L1077.029]

Micro-influencers can be given merchandise in exchange for video footage and b-roll for the brand's own accounts. [L1077.053]

## Commissioning UGC Creators

### Sourcing creators on marketplaces

- Four platform routes appear in the sources: Upwork, Fiverr, the TikTok Creator Marketplace and Billow. An agency that sources creators on incense.com is a fifth route. [L0637.044, L0644.031, L1402.010, L1402.012, L1402.015, L1127.030]
- The marketplace named Billow is spelled "Billo" in one source and "Billow" in another. [L0995.052, L1402.015]

#### Hiring a UGC creator on Upwork

1. Post a job describing the new e-commerce project and the number of creatives needed.
2. Send all applicants a Google Form with questions on expectations, salary and experience.
3. Shortlist the answers, which removes about half of the applicants.
4. Interview the rest via Zoom.

[L0637.044]

#### Working with a freelancer on Fiverr

1. Find a UGC creator on Fiverr with relevant experience, such as a journalism background.
2. Send the product and allow about a week for the creator to receive it before filming.
3. Send the creator a script or a clear steer on the angle before filming starts.
4. Review the footage and test it against the existing hooks and angles.

[L0644.031]

1. Search for UGC on Fiverr.
2. Scroll through the freelancers offered.
3. Choose the freelancer whose style fits your product, reviewing their past work.
4. Start working with them.
5. If the result is good, continue the collaboration long term.

[L1402.012]

#### Sourcing on the TikTok Creator Marketplace

1. Open creatormarketplace.tiktok.com and create an account to get full platform access.
2. Create a campaign and enter the store and product information.
3. Wait for creators to apply to the campaign.
4. Approve the creator you want to work with.
5. Ship the product to the creator.
6. Receive the UGC video.

[L1402.010]

#### Ordering a video on Billow

Billow offers a video ad, TikTok short, product showcase or honest review, priced at about $119 for one quoted order. [L0995.052]

1. Create an account on the Billow website.
2. Click Get a video.
3. Select an existing product you used before, or create a new product.
4. Choose the video type: video ad, TikTok short, product showcase, or honest review.
5. Choose how many creators should work on the product.
6. Check the final price, which updates after every change, and adjust the settings.
7. Choose the format: portrait, landscape, vertical, or square.
8. Choose whether to add subtitles, animations, or your own pictures.
9. Set the preferred creator age so it matches your target customer.
10. Set the preferred creator gender; for a product for women only, deselect male and keep female.
11. Choose the creator interests that fit the product.
12. Add additional notes for the creator.
13. Click Next step and complete the payment.
14. Within 2-3 days, creators apply to the task.
15. Filter the applicants and choose the creator you like most.
16. Within 1-2 weeks after the creator receives the product, you get the finished video.

[L1402.015]

Billow order options:

- Get a video
- Product (existing or new)
- Video type (video ad, TikTok short, product showcase, honest review)
- Number of creators
- Format (portrait, landscape, vertical, square)
- Subtitles
- Animations
- Added pictures
- Preferred creator age
- Preferred creator gender (deselect a gender to exclude it)
- Creator interests
- Additional notes
- Next step (payment)

[L1402.016]

| Billow stage | Timing |
|---|---|
| Creators start applying after payment | 2-3 days |
| Finished video arrives after the creator receives the product | 1-2 weeks |

[L1402.018]

#### Using an agency

- An agency can research the product and store, write scripts and send them to creators found on incense.com. Creator fees are paid separately from the agency fee. [L1127.030]
- An agency can write briefs or scripts for creators, who then shoot the ad videos, so the store owner only reviews the finished videos. This moves content production out of the owner's hands once the store is scaling. [L0694.049]

### Writing the brief and script

- Give ad creators a detailed, well-written ad script before outsourcing video. The script should surface the problem, give the solution, educate, create curiosity and build desire. Fiverr creators are often generalists rather than ad copywriters, so a great script gets great videos and a poor one wastes money. [L0308.026]
- Send the script before the product ships. A creator needs about one week to receive the product before filming, so writing and sending the script during that wait lets filming start as soon as the product arrives. [L1426.023, L1426.051]

### Raw scene clips

- Ask creators for raw 3-5 second scene clips, not a finished 60-second video. Each scene is quick to record, which makes the work cheap for creators and gives you more material to assemble. [L0398.046]

Creative brief math:

- One 60-second brief is split into 12 scenes of about 5 seconds each: 3 hook scenes, 3 product-introduction scenes, 3 benefit scenes and 3 CTA scenes. [L0398.047]
- Choosing one of 3 hooks, one of 3 intros, one of 3 benefit clips and one of 3 CTAs gives 3 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 81 combinations. [L0398.047]
- About 20 high-quality videos can be picked from these combinations, so a $60 creator fee works out to about $3 per video. [L0398.047]

Raw clip request template:

```text
Subject: Raw clips for [PRODUCT NAME]

Hi [CREATOR NAME],

We would like to work with you on [NUMBER] short scene videos for [PRODUCT NAME]. Please do not send a finished 60-second video. Instead, record separate raw clips of about 3-5 seconds each, one scene per clip, with no editing and no music.

Please record these scenes:
- 3 hook scenes: [HOOK ANGLE 1], [HOOK ANGLE 2], [HOOK ANGLE 3]. Keep the first moment strong and simple.
- 3 product-introduction scenes: the product in your hand, an unboxing or first use of [PRODUCT NAME].
- 3 benefit scenes: show [BENEFIT 1], [BENEFIT 2] and [BENEFIT 3] in use. Speak or show the benefit clearly.
- 3 call-to-action scenes: you holding the product and saying [CTA LINE, e.g. shop now or check the link].

For each scene, use a plain background and keep the phone steady. Send all clips separately so we can combine them ourselves.

Thank you,
[YOUR NAME]
```

[L0398.048]

- Some UGC creators now charge more for raw clips, because the brand does the editing and the creator's output becomes more valuable. Agree on a clear fee for the number of raw clips before the shoot. [L0398.049]

### Matching creators to the audience

- Audience demographics matter in UGC because people relate to people who look like them. If you target Gulf countries, consider whether the creator's ethnicity and accent match the audience. Test both approaches and measure performance. [L0308.027]
- Match the creator's age and gender to the target customer so viewers can relate to the person showing the product. For a female-only product, exclude male creators. [L1402.020]
- When the product cannot be sourced in your own market, hire creators in the target country so the content looks local and relatable. Creators in the same market are easier to brief for raw scenes. [L0398.050]
- Hire creators from the country you are targeting and use a local accent or voice. In one lesson, UK-accented UGC for UK customers brought most sales. [L0773.054]

Case: a UK-accented creator for a UK audience

A store where about 90% of buyers came from the UK added TikTok UGC made by a creator with a British accent, and sales rose sharply. The seller then offered a simple digital user guide, made with ChatGPT and one or two images, as a free gift with purchase, listed at 19.95 so the free gift looked valuable. Earlier buyers who had missed the guide bought it once they heard about it, and the seller then gave it to them free as extra service. Reviews were five stars, and the seller had at one point reported a conversion rate of 11.11%. The seller planned to run the same ads on Facebook and to add picture ads. [L0774.054]

- For organic growth on Instagram or TikTok, hire a creator to produce several videos you can post on your own account. Relatable people using the product help the audience connect with the store. [L1402.004]

### Vetting creators

- Freelance sites such as Fiverr often produce poor-quality UGC. Vet candidates with a sample or test video before committing, and expect many misses before you find a good creator. [L1077.031]
- Reviews alone do not guarantee video quality. A freelance video seller with thousands of five-star reviews delivered three unusable videos. Test a seller with a small order before committing. [L1107.021]

### Contracts, volume and rights

- Set UGC work as a daily output over a month, for example at least three videos per day, so the creator can calculate total volume and quote a price. Negotiate after the first month based on quality. [L1214.049]
- Hire creators to make videos you post on your own accounts, since their own feeds may be weak. Talented creators with low views can be better value than popular ones. [L1214.050]
- Hire a mediocre creator, train them for a few weeks, then work with a top creator at roughly a quarter of the price. Long-term contracts usually bring better rates. [L1214.051]
- When paying influencers for video, commission clips you can run as paid ads, not one-off posts on their own channel. Secure the right to use the footage in your own campaigns before the video is made. [L1017.042]

### Group chats, content calendars and audits

- Create a group chat for UGC creators who deliver on a regular schedule, for example two videos per month each. The group lets creators network with like-minded creators, which makes the partnership more valuable to them. [L0576.024]
- JotForm can serve as a content calendar and creator management system. Creators submit content through a form that is open only on set days, such as Tuesdays and Fridays, so submissions stay organised. [L1457.014]
- Run a content audit before outsourced content goes live, so that off-brand posts, weak messages or compliance risks are caught. Start new hires by having them produce test TikToks, review them, then give them posting rights. [L1077.032]

## Producing Your Own UGC and AI Content

### Planning and Principles

- Own UGC is the starting point when no budget exists. Film it yourself first, then move to paid creators once the product shows consistent profit. [L0308.028, L1219.049, L1030.024]
- Phone footage is usually good enough when testing a product early. Shoot the product from several angles: held up, a slow slide across a surface, and slow zooms, so the editor has enough material for the narrative. [L0344.049]
- Customisation costs time and money because each custom UGC video needs creator credits or production. Spend on it only after the original product shows consistent profit. [L1030.024]
- Custom content performs better than existing content on TikTok, so prioritise your own videos over reused viral clips. [L1377.024]
- Custom content recorded by the owner on a phone, with simple scripts and no studio, performs better than stock drop-shipping footage, because viewers relate to a normal person explaining the benefit. [L0871.053]
- Authentic creator footage filmed on a phone outperforms polished company production, because viewers trust a regular person more than a brand. [L0707.012]
- Strong video ads combine three things: showing how the product works, using UGC as social proof, and a first 5 seconds that grab attention. The opening sets the base for the rest of the video. [L0777.011]

### Filming Yourself and Solo Shoots

- Shoot solo when no helper is available: hold the product in one hand, operate the phone with the other, and prop the phone on a towel or flat surface for static shots. Ask a partner to hold the product or the phone only for shots that need two hands. [L1403.035]
- A UGC video can be shot by one person in an ordinary room such as a bedroom or bathroom when no studio is available. A plain surface is acceptable, because the goal is to show the product clearly, not to produce a clean product-photo backdrop. [L1403.029]
- If there is no budget for paid UGC, the creator can film the product personally, add a voice-over and short text overlays. Reusing other people's content is possible but not advised. [L0561.037]
- Warehouse or packaging videos with your own logo add a layer of trust for customers. A freelancer can create this kind of corporate video. [L0950.047]
- Customer or staff-filmed product videos can serve as user-generated content. Film real use, explain the product's feel and fit, and post them on the store and on YouTube. [L0801.130]
- Point-of-view (POV) style content works well on Instagram for product marketing. Learn this format before running paid creator campaigns. [L1367.013]
- Clients often find it useful to be shown a real video of a procedure from the business itself, such as a dentist's own footage of a treatment, because it adds credibility to ads. [L0440.048]

### Outsourced Filmmakers, Photographers and Creators

- Own creatives can be produced quickly with photographers and videographers, for example sourced from China or Fiverr, who shoot product photos and videos. Show the product in hand or in use rather than only the face. [L1345.087]
- A product bought from Amazon can be used for sample shots if it is cheap enough. Express shipping can deliver a product to the UK within two to three days for filming. [L1345.088]
- A product shown being used by a creator in a reaction or try-on video usually converts better than a brand-made ad, because buyers respond to the face and reaction, not only the product. [L1379.028]
- Creator reaction or try-on workflow:
  1. Send the product to the creator first. [L1379.029]
  2. Let the creator film a reaction or try-on video. [L1379.029]
  3. Ask for a private draft and review the video before it is published. [L1379.029]
  4. Add any missing product details in the review before posting. [L1379.029]
- If the person on camera does not match the target audience in age or style, outsource the on-camera part or the voiceover to a script writer or creator instead of filming it yourself. Record the script anyway, because the voiceover is still the timing reference for the edit. [L1403.034]

### Partnering and Exchanging Shoots

- Partner with friends in your network who match your target audience demographic, and exchange UGC shoots for free. [L0308.028]

### Scripting and Shot Structure

- Ask for a UGC piece about the product built on the problem-agitate-solution framework, then refine the output through follow-up prompts before passing it to creators or clients. [L0353.045]
- Create short, exaggerated reaction clips of the presenter using the product in different settings, such as at a desk, in the bath, or at a friend's place. Use the funniest or most surprising clip as the ad hook and keep the others as alternative openings for testing. [L1403.037]
- The answer to "how would you describe the brand to a friend" contains the sales language buyers use without prompting and the order in which they rank benefits. Use these exact phrases and benefit order in UGC scripts, testimonial copy and word-of-mouth ads. [L1139.012]
- Hooks and benefit scenes: the creator performs an action without speaking on camera, and the voiceover is added in editing. Speaking on camera is needed only for scenes such as a testimonial or a call to action. [L0638.039]
- Speaking to camera: videos where the seller speaks to the camera received fewer hate comments and gave better like-to-view ratios, and viewers trusted the seller more. This made talking-to-camera content useful when the video was clean and good quality. [L0657.013]
- Speaker profile: the speaker should sound like someone who was skeptical before and only changed their mind after trying the product. [L0707.012]
- Naming a personal insecurity: testimonials that describe a personal insecurity remind the viewer of their own insecurity and how it makes them feel. Selling works by solving a problem or insecurity the buyer already feels, so the speaker should name it openly. [L0707.013]

#### Modular 60-Second Script Workflow

| Step | Action | Ids |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Divide a 60-second script into scenes: for example five hooks of five to six seconds, several benefit scenes, and two to three call-to-action scenes. | L0638.038 |
| 2 | Write a creative brief for each scene with the exact action the creator should perform. | L0638.038 |
| 3 | Have the creator record the full 60 seconds once. | L0638.038 |
| 4 | Record voiceover and captions as separate files. | L0638.038 |
| 5 | Combine hooks, benefits, and calls to action in different orders to produce 10 to 20 different videos from one recording. | L0638.038 |
| 6 | Test the combinations in the market and keep the best performers. | L0638.038 |

### Voiceovers, AI Voices and Audio

- If you are uncomfortable with your own voice, use AI voice generators such as 11 Labs, with voices such as Adam or Bella. [L0308.028]
- 11 Labs: AI voice generator for UGC videos. It mimics UGC cheaply by combining found footage with natural-sounding voiceovers, and is an alternative to hiring creators. [L0308.029]
- Voiceovers should match the audience's accent. For an Australian audience, an Australian voiceover tested better than an American one, and an American voiceover did not beat a self-recorded voice. [L1427.053]

### Sourcing Footage and B-Roll

- Source footage from TikTok, Instagram, or AliExpress product videos where available. [L0308.028]
- Use footage of the product, such as supplier or AliExpress clips, for product introductions. For emotional scenes, such as someone looking angry or exhausted, search a stock library by emotion. [L1427.060]
- Reusing other people's content is possible but not advised. Prefer your own footage. [L0561.037, L1377.024]
- Re-shooting a proven competitor video: with the same hook, message, vibe and caption, change only the setting, and optionally the music. [L1377.024]

### Testimonials, Personas and Storytelling Patterns

#### Testimonial Sources and Credibility

- A named, credible person speaking for the product, such as a respected user or expert, carries more weight than an anonymous company voice. Their personal authority can make a claim believable. [L1261.117]
- Let a third party such as a doctor or expert recommend the product in the story instead of the brand claiming its own superiority. This keeps the tone editorial and makes the recommendation more credible. [L0578.021]
- Use testimonials from named, real customers who live in the same town or area as the prospect, quoting a specific outcome they experienced. Local recognition of the customer name gives the claim more weight than the seller's own words. [L1369.035]
- Testimonial clips of real people describing a visible result can be reused as the proof part of a new creative, including clips from ads for other products in the same category. Choose a speaker the buyer can identify with, because that is what the buyer wants to see. [L0901.013]

#### Celebrity, Expert and Everyday Voices

- Bring in other people to see the product through their eyes. Use a celebrity testimonial for a famous endorsement, or an ordinary person's case history or narrative for identification. Their actions and reactions make the performance feel new. [L0330.075]
- Show experts reacting with surprise. Professional or sophisticated people who are impressed by the product add surprise, competition and discovery to the image, and their astonishment is more convincing than the ad's own claim. [L0330.076]
- Use both celebrity testimonials and ordinary people's case histories to reaffirm the benefits. Celebrities give status, while everyday people give the reader an easy identity to share; both show the product from a new angle. [L0330.093]
- Showing envied or admired people in ads can increase desire, because readers want the status or outcome the person represents. Use the buyer's aspirations to select who appears. [L1261.118]

#### Chained Persona Testimonials

- A strong testimonial ad can chain several short creator testimonials, each speaking from a different persona such as a parent, a relative of someone with a specific problem, or a professional. Each persona names a different problem or angle, so one ad covers several viewer segments while the product stays the same. Keep each speaker's story short and tied to one concrete result. [L0707.029]

#### Contrast Testimonial Pattern

Pattern: a relatable person, such as a parent or partner, describes a contrast between age or a condition and how they look or feel, and credits the product as the cause. It works because a third person's visible result feels like proof rather than a sales claim. [L0901.018]

- Example 1: "My husband is fifty, but he keeps up with the kids on weekends since he started this protein mix." [L0901.018]
- Example 2: "My grandma was always cold until she began taking this iron supplement." [L0901.018]

### Faceless and AI-Generated Content

- Faceless UGC-style videos and short viral content can be produced with AI tools, so no creator has to appear on camera. [L0914.014]
- TopView, or similar AI platforms, creates realistic product mockups showing a person holding or using the product. This removes the need to send physical samples to influencers for every visual. [L1459.012]

### AI-Generated UGC Photos

Prompt, paste as-is [L0794.044]:

```
Write 10 image prompts for a UGC-style photo of one person holding my book. Give each prompt a different person (age, gender, natural and varied skin tone), a different camera angle and a different setting, and have the person hold the book up toward the camera. Keep the whole book cover visible and facing the camera, and do not let the person or the frame cut the cover in half. Give every prompt an authentic phone-camera look with soft focus, slight grain and natural colour, without studio gloss. Output one prompt per line, ready to paste.
```

#### UGC Photo Batch Procedure

1. Ask Claude for 10 scene prompts with different people, angles and settings. [L0794.045]
2. Read each prompt and remove any that do not make sense. [L0794.045]
3. Paste 2 or 3 scenes into Book Scene Studio as a test. [L0794.045]
4. Upload the book cover, 1 to 3 angles. [L0794.045]
5. Set the aspect to 4:5 portrait. [L0794.045]
6. Run the test and check that the whole book is visible in each output. [L0794.045]
7. Once the test passes, shoot the full list. [L0794.045]
8. Upload the chosen images to the review platform manually. [L0794.045]

#### Phone-Camera Style Rule

- Stating a phone-camera style in the prompt, such as an older phone model look with slight softness, grain and unedited colour, makes the image read more like a real customer photo than studio gloss. [L0794.057]
- Name the camera style in every shot prompt, and vary the person, angle and setting across at least three UGC variations. [L0794.057]

### Creative Hooks and Attention

- Product-in-use is the key. Show how the product works in the first moments, then support it with UGC as social proof. [L0777.011]

## Customer-Generated Content and Reviews

### Principles: why buyer content matters

- Video reviews are a trust format that few competitors use in many niches, so publishing them can make your trust element stand out. Collect the largest number of reviews in your category as well, and state the count next to any claim about it. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L0411.039]
- Loyal repeat customers can become advocates who bring in new traffic, add credibility, and raise the brand's status in its market. Treat advocacy as a deliberate growth channel, not as a side effect of good service. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L0414.054]
- User-generated content is material created by site visitors, such as reviews and customer questions. It adds unique text to product pages and shows search engines that the store is a trusted source for those products. [L1190.025]
- Customer photos can replace generic supplier images on a product page and make the store look unique. Three customer photos of the same product are enough to start using this on the site and can raise the conversion rate. [L0417.011]
- UGC-style photos of real-looking customers holding the product act as social proof next to reviews. Rotating several variations on the product page or review platform keeps the set fresh. [L0794.047]
- Collect UGC-style reviews from real customers instead of borrowing them from other sites. Real customer photos, videos and text are more trustworthy than copied material. (Older advice, Source A 2020.) [L1111.117]
- Paying customers $2 to $15 in refunds for content can replace creator content that costs $50 to $100 or more per piece. Customer-made content looks raw and native, so it often performs better in ads than polished content ordered from creator platforms. [L0605.037]
- A review without a review badge is still better than no review at all. Use the reviews you can collect even if they do not carry the badge. [L0965.075]

### Setting up the request system

- Set up a video review request system and include it in every review request. Video reviews are ideal, but image reviews are also a strong form of social proof. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L0399.014]
- Brands that use both request types usually ask for a photo first and send a review request afterwards, so the same buyer gets two separate post-delivery emails. The choice between them still depends on the product type and what buyers are willing to share. [L0417.025]
- Ask for testimonials several times and in different formats, such as text, photo and video. More emails and more request types give a higher chance of collecting them. [L1076.058]
- Collect testimonials by following up after each first order, and turn satisfied buyers into sources of quotes. Each new testimonial becomes proof for the next mailing. [L1369.036]
- Collect customer reviews after each sale:
  1. Contact every buyer by phone or email.
  2. Ask for a review.
  3. Ask for a product photo taken with their phone if they are comfortable sharing it.
  4. If not, accept a text-based review.
  5. Place the reviews on the product pages.

  [L0806.074]
- Use a post-purchase review service to collect unique store-level reviews for social proof. Yotpo, Shopify Reviews and Judge.me are recommended, though Yotpo was noted as expensive at the time. (Source A, undated source.) [L1357.036]

### Request timing

Sources give different delays. Each applies to a different setup:

| Source | Timing | When it applies | Units |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source A | Wait a few days after delivery before contacting the customer, then send an automated photo request | Automated photo request after delivery | L0417.008 |
| Source A | 14 to 21 days after the product is received | Review and testimonial emails, giving the customer time to use the product | L1243.039 |
| Source C | Trigger when the tracking app reports delivered, then wait 1 to 2 days | UGC generator flow, so the customer has used the product | L0605.035 |
| Source C | Review request timing set to 28 days | LUX Reviews app setting during import setup | L0477.012 |

- Send one short email to everyone who has already received their product, with the store name and order number in the subject line. [L0965.073]

### Request email templates

Use this template for the photo request after delivery:

```
Subject: Enjoying your [Product Name]?

Hi {{ first_name }},

We noticed your order of [Product Name] has been delivered, and we hope you are loving it!

We would love to see it in action. You can reply to this email with a photo of your [Product Name] in use, or post your photo on Instagram or Facebook using #[StoreHashtag] and tag our page @[StoreHandle]. Photos from our customers may be featured on our website.

Thank you for being part of the [Store Name] community!

[Your Name]
[Store Name]
```

[L0417.009]

- Use a branded hashtag built from the store name, for example #[StoreName], and ask buyers to tag the store page handle, for example @[StoreHandle]. The hashtag and tag give friends who see the post a direct path to the store. [L0417.010]

### Outreach to customers who have not reviewed

- Write one or two sentences in the body asking for feedback on the product and their experience buying from your store, without a link or a photo request. [L0965.073]
- When a customer replies, add the product-specific review to Judge.me as if it came from the customer. If the reply is about the store rather than the product, add it to the general store reviews area in Judge.me. [L0965.073]
- Do not ask customers directly to leave a Google review. If a customer's reply is positive and you want a Google review, thank them and ask them to post the same message on your Google business profile, then link them to it. [L0965.074]

### Collecting photos from buyers

Procedure for an automated photo request:

1. Wait a few days after the customer's order has been delivered before contacting them.
2. Send an automated email asking the customer to share a photo of the product in use.
3. Let the customer reply to the email with the photo or post it on social media with the store hashtag and a tag of the store page.
4. Collect the photos and use them on the website as product images.

[L0417.008]

- Photo requests need the product in the customer's hands, with the face visible and smiling. Reward the photo with a refund or cashback, because this shows the customer is happy with the result. [L0871.054]
- Create at least three different UGC variations for review photos, each with a different person, angle and setting. Varied people holding the product read as real customers and give the review set more credibility. [L0794.046]
- Share customer photos on Facebook and Instagram with the customer's first name, location, the product name and the store name. Posts can be scheduled, for example once per month. (Older advice, Source A 2019.) [L1086.049]
- When customers have sent photos of themselves with the product, use those images in preference to studio shots. Customer images show the product in real use. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L1398.011]
- Recruit creators or customers, for example in gyms, to film first-time product use reaction videos. Prioritize volume of UGC, because it both builds trust and fills the creative pipeline. [L1225.051]

### Fashion niche: Instagram customer photos

Procedure for the fashion store:

1. Build out the Instagram page for the fashion store, which is essential in the fashion niche.
2. Post your own photos of the products.
3. Ask customers to submit their photos of the products they bought.
4. Add a 'shop Instagram' link in the store header so visitors can buy directly from the posted photos.

[L0838.017]

- Customer photos on social media provide social proof and are a major part of the strategy of successful stores. Collecting as many real customer photos as possible is especially valuable in the fashion niche. [L0838.018]
- An Instagram page with about 4,500 genuine followers drove sales when customers were asked to tag the brand. A post from an influencer with about 127,000 followers also brought some sales. [L1439.027]

### Video reviews and video content

- Only ask for a video review from customers who sound very positive during the call. Video requests are not for every customer. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L1011.009]
- Customer video reviews are user-generated content that the business gets to keep and reuse. They can also generate organic traffic when posted to a YouTube channel, which may rank in Google search. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L1012.020]
- Customer video reviews can run as Facebook video ads and as YouTube video ads. They are rarer to collect than written reviews, but they are worth using when available. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L1398.012]
- Video reviews are a trust format that few competitors use in many niches, so publishing them can make your trust element stand out. [L0411.039]

Procedure for turning customer feedback into video content:

1. Ask existing customers for a video review.
2. Collect the videos with a tool such as Video Peel.
3. Edit a video only if it needs editing.
4. Publish it on YouTube and link to the product in the description.

(Older advice, Source B 2021-22.) [L1424.029]

### Post-engagement testimonial campaign

Procedure:

1. Create a post and run it as a post-engagement campaign, which does not show on the store's page feed but can be used in ads.
2. Ask commenters to upload a photo of themselves with the product, or to write a short review if photos feel too hard.
3. Connect the campaign to Minichat so each commenter is sent a gift automatically, such as free shipping or a small coupon.
4. Reuse the post with its comments and photos as social proof in later campaigns.

[L1243.041]

- A store ran a video post as a post-engagement campaign for under one week with a budget of a couple of hundred dollars. The post reached 17,000 views and earned 120 likes, almost 200 comments and 23 shares. The result was presented as strong social proof that could keep working as an evergreen post. [L1243.042]

### Incentives

Sources use different rewards. Each applies to its own setup:

| Source | Incentive | When it applies | Units |
|---|---|---|---|
| Source C | Automatic 15% discount for a review with a picture | LUX Reviews app request | L0477.011 |
| Source C | Refund per submission type (see table below) | UGC generator form | L0605.035, L0605.036 |
| Source C | Discount on the next order for a photo of the customer wearing the product (stated as 50, likely percent) | Selfie-style customer photo campaign | L0519.042 |
| Source A | Gift sent automatically, such as free shipping or a small coupon | Minichat post-engagement campaign | L1243.041 |

- The lesson advises a refund over an extra free item, because an extra free item takes longer to deliver. [L0605.035]
- Reward by submission type, as used in the lesson (adjust for your margins):

| Submission type | Reward |
|---|---|
| Product photo | $2 refund |
| Selfie with the product | $4 refund |
| Video testimonial | $15 refund |

  [L0605.036]
- Some branded products with many creator-style reviews are backed by discounts offered to customers in exchange for reviews, which builds social proof quickly. Before copying this, check platform rules on incentivized reviews, since many marketplaces prohibit them. [L1186.045]

### UGC generator flow

Basic version:

1. Create a JotForm where customers submit their custom content and grant you marketing rights.
2. After the order is delivered, send an email asking the customer for UGC, linking to the form.

[L0604.011]

Full flow, in this order:

1. Trigger the flow when the tracking app reports the order as delivered.
2. Wait 1-2 days after delivery, so the customer has used the product.
3. Send an email saying you want to showcase their happiness to other customers, and ask for a photo, selfie or video testimonial.
4. Offer a reward, preferably a refund on their order, since an extra free item takes longer to deliver.
5. Collect submissions through a form such as Jotform, with a category choice, an email field, a file upload and a consent checkbox.
6. Use reviews directly, but ask for permission before using any content in marketing.

[L0605.035]

- UGC Jotform form structure: first a category field to pick the submission type (product photo, selfie with product, video testimonial), then an email field so submissions can be verified, then a file upload field for the content, and finally a consent checkbox before submission. The form can be cloned from a template and the store name replaced. [L0605.038]
- For a customer selfie with the product, use the caption formula [customer's situation] + [product] = [solution or benefit], and use it as the UGC form's prompt text. It works because the customer sees their own face in a solved situation, which makes them more willing to submit. Examples: `Your cozy evenings + our blanket = warmth without the bulk` and `Your dog's morning walk + our leash = hands-free control`. [L0605.051]

### Consent and marketing permission

Consent checkbox text for using customer content in marketing:

```
Your positive feedback and experience with [STORE NAME] have been invaluable to us. We believe featuring your content on our website and social media channels can show other customers the value and benefits of our products. Tick the box below if you agree that we may use your submitted photo, selfie or video for marketing purposes.

[ ] Yes, I agree that [STORE NAME] may use my submitted content for marketing.
```

[L0605.039]

- Use reviews directly, but ask for permission before using any content in marketing. [L0605.035]

### Supplier review permissions

- Ask the supplier before using their reviews, including paid or influencer reviews. If they approve, add any disclaimer the supplier requires on your store. (Source A 2024.) [L0471.018]

Template for asking a supplier to reuse their reviews (older advice, Source A 2020):

```
Hi [Supplier name],

I noticed your website has reviews for [product name or product number]. We don't have any reviews for your products yet. Would it be okay if we displayed these reviews on our website? Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
[Your name]
```

[L0551.022]

Procedure for sourcing supplier and customer reviews (older advice, Source A 2021):

1. Check the supplier's website for reviews or testimonials already published, and ask the supplier if you may reuse them.
2. After approval, ask suppliers for reviews and images they can share for your product pages.
3. Ask customers for reviews after purchase through a follow-up sequence, and incentivize them to leave one.

[L1279.049]

### Importing reviews

Procedure for importing AliExpress reviews into LUX Reviews:

1. Install the LUX Reviews app, choose the Beginner plan (upgrade to Growth or Unlimited when scaling), start the trial and select take beginner instead.
2. Set store primary language (English), choose star color (brand or gold).
3. Set review request timing to 28 days and the 15% picture-review discount.
4. Drag the LUX import bookmark to the bookmarks bar.
5. On AliExpress open the product, click the bookmark and import to the store product URL.
6. Filter to four stars and up, all countries, translated to English.
7. Import reviews one by one after checking text and picture, then click finish importing.
8. Check the reviews and the product page show the imported count and rating.

[L0477.012]

- Import only supplier reviews rated four stars or higher, from all countries, translated to English, and review each before importing to check the text and pictures look good. [L0477.013]

### Q&A on product pages

- The SMPS Product Question and Answer app lets shoppers ask questions on product pages. The free plan is enough for new stores, and paid plans add an FAQ page. The same developer also offers a Google Shopping feed app for sending products to Google Merchant Center. [L1190.026]

Procedure for handling a product question in the Q&A app:

1. A shopper submits a question on the product page with a name and email address.
2. The store owner gets a notification that a question was asked.
3. Write the answer in the app dashboard, or delete the question if it is not suitable.
4. Publish the answer, which appears on the product page and is emailed to the shopper.
5. Use the dashboard to see the number of questions, the most-viewed questions, and pending questions.

[L1190.027]

- Enter questions that customers ask by phone, live chat, or email into the Q&A app yourself and answer them. Publish those answers on the product page when they would help future shoppers, because the answers also support SEO. [L1190.028]

### Pinterest user content

- About 70% of brand engagement on Pinterest is user-generated, meaning it happens without the brand posting anything itself. Stores should therefore make it easy for visitors to share their products. [L1136.006]
- Customers who save and share products from a store's site can generate traffic and sales without any action from the store owner. A visible Pin It button is the simplest way to enable this passive sharing. [L1136.007]
- Entering pinterest.com/source/ followed by your store domain, for example pinterest.com/source/www.yourdomain.com, shows all pins that users have saved from your website. It is a free way to see who is already sharing your products. [L1136.012]
- Once you have found the users who have pinned your products, comment on their pins, follow their accounts and start a conversation with them. These users have already shown interest in your product, so they are warm potential customers. [L1136.013]

## Using UGC in Ads, Store and Social Channels

### Paid ads: why UGC works

- UGC means real customer material, such as reviews and photos of people using the product. It builds trust and works especially well in retargeting ads, where it answers the doubts of people who already saw the product. [L0648.059]
- Meta favors content that looks natural. Over-produced ads still run but cost more, so real customer photos and videos, or phone-shot footage, often perform better. [L0649.036]
- Use real customer videos or photos in retargeting where possible. A customer describing their experience often outperforms a brand message. [L0649.060]
- Spark Ads from influencer posts tend to outperform regular brand creatives because they look like organic content from a trusted creator rather than a sales message. This lowers viewer resistance and makes the ad feel more credible. [L1374.036]

### Paid ads: where the traffic goes

- Turn collected UGC into paid ads. Cold audiences convert poorly on direct product pages, so send paid traffic to the influencer's profile or to a lead magnet page instead of the product page. [L0789.036]

| Audience | Creative | Send traffic to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cold | UGC video ads with real creators | Influencer's profile or lead magnet page | [L0789.036] |
| Retargeting (people who already saw the product) | Real customer videos or photos | Not specified in the source | [L0648.059, L0649.060] |

### Paid ads: whitelisting and brand pages

- Brand pages perform well with UGC video ads that feature real creators, sourced from TikTok Shop creator programs or official Instagram influencers. [L0906.012]
- Whitelisting means running these ads through a creator or persona page instead of the brand's own page. [L0906.012]
- The brand's page can still host the UGC content, so both approaches are used together. [L0906.012]

### Paid ads: boosting organic content

- Paid traffic such as Coins or Spark Ads on a brand-new account can speed up reaching the right audience during the new account advantage window, which lasts roughly the first one to two weeks. Use this boost only on new accounts. [L1374.031]
- Do not boost old accounts with established organic performance. Boosting old successful organic posts has been reported to kill organic sales. [L1374.031]
- Use organic videos as ad creatives only if they already reached strong views (around 50,000 to 100,000) and carry real social proof. Very new organic videos can lose organic reach when boosted through Spark Ads. [L1377.025]
- Both conditions apply together: the view threshold decides which videos qualify, and the account-age rule decides whether boosting is safe at all. [L1374.031, L1377.025]

### Paid ads: borrowed clips and copyright

- Using UGC clips taken from other brands or TikTok for ads carries a risk of copyright strikes. Keep this short term, such as a couple of weeks at 10 USD per ad set per day (50 USD total), and replace it with your own UGC once the product gains traction. [L0693.047]

### Ad iteration: fixing low-attention ads

- Ads with low attention can be improved rather than discarded. Layer a UGC video with a voice-over or new hooks, because a single hook change can lift attention and sales. [L1426.024]

### Converting winning UGC into other formats

- For books, UGC AI ads produced higher purchase intent and better traction than static image ads in the tests. Static image ads still work, but UGC AI ads are the better default for this product type. [L1030.022]
- Convert a proven UGC AI ad concept back to image ads, in this order:
  1. Confirm the UGC AI concept has produced many purchases and steady profit. [L1030.023]
  2. Build image ads that use the same concept, angle and pain point. [L1030.023]
  3. Run the image ads alongside the UGC AI ads and compare soft and hard metrics. [L1030.023]

### Product pages and testimonial sections

- Place customer photos in a dedicated section on the product page, not mixed into supplier product photos. This section is one of the most important elements for conversion. (Older advice, 2019.) [L1086.048]
- Customer photos also work in blog posts where a product image fits. A standalone customer photo gallery page is a weaker use of the photos than product pages and emails. (Older advice, 2019.) [L1086.050]
- In testimonial sections and product images, use raw UGC photos of real customers in real-life settings instead of high-quality studio shots. Visitors relate more to real people, and the lesson reports that such content converts better than polished lifestyle images. [L0916.029]

### Review proof blocks

- Pattern: place review screenshots from the store, a marketplace or a product page over a blurred version of the product, and show the store URL in the same frame. It works because it puts several genuine reviews in one image while the product remains visible in the background. [L0398.020]
  - Example 1: five screenshots of five-star reviews with the URL of the store at the bottom. [L0398.020]
  - Example 2: three reviews from a marketplace over a blurred kitchen counter with the product. [L0398.020]

### Messenger social proof

- Formula: name a real customer with their location, state that they like the product, and mention one specific benefit. Real names and places increase trust more than generic praise. [L1243.031]
  - Example 1: Maria from Ohio told us this kettle heats up in under three minutes, and she uses it every morning. [L1243.031]
  - Example 2: Dan from Texas wrote that his backpack survived a full semester of daily use. [L1243.031]

### Video bubbles on the website

- Embed a bubble group on the website, as follows:
  1. Create the video campaigns that will be shown as bubbles. [L0951.004]
  2. Group the campaigns together into one bubble group (playlist) per topic. [L0951.004]
  3. Embed the bubble group on the website. [L0951.004]
  4. Customize the bubbles to match the look and feel of the website. [L0951.004]
  5. Update the content later without re-embedding, because embedded bubbles are fully dynamic. [L0951.004]
  6. Reuse any video that is already embedded in email marketing campaigns. [L0951.004]

### Shoppable social galleries

- Add a carousel of social content to the website, as follows:
  1. Pull the content directly from your Instagram or TikTok account onto the website. [L0951.005]
  2. Tag each video with the specific products shown in it. [L0951.005]
  3. Place the carousel on the home page, collection pages or product pages, where it works like an endless scroll for product discovery. [L0951.005]
  4. Let the customer check out from the carousel with a single click. [L0951.005]

### Scaling case: UGC as the main lever

- Starting point: a brand scaled mainly on bottom-of-funnel static ads for about two years, with three UGC videos. [L1476.050]
- Change: UGC video was introduced a couple of months earlier. [L1476.050]
- Result: monthly revenue rose about 5x with both formats combined. [L1476.050]
- Conclusion: UGC is the main scaling lever, while bottom-of-funnel statics help at small scale or on top of existing UGC. [L1476.050]

## Tracking, Measuring and Iterating

### Measuring Influencer Results: Principles and Priorities

- Tracking traffic from influencer partnerships is the most critical step in determining profitability. It shows whether a partnership returns enough to continue long-term. Some influencers become so profitable that they stay active advertising partners for multiple years. [L0183.010]
- Track referrals from brand ambassadors as their own traffic source, separate from paid social and search. This traffic is expected to be of higher quality than cold paid traffic, and it can feed back into the top of the funnel to create more customers. [L0676.019]
- Judge TikTok performance over several posts rather than a single post, because engagement on influencer content can rise and fall sharply: attention spans are short and trends move quickly, so expect results to fluctuate. [L0480.029]
- Organic Instagram posting that reached over 200 followers within a week signals content interest, but it is not sales evidence on its own. [L1016.065]
- A cited survey claims that 86% of businesses using influencer marketing effectively report an immediate or long-term effect on their brand. The source and the exact definition of "effective" are not stated, so treat this figure as a rough indication only. [L0786.013]

### Platform Analytics and Engagement Data

- Check the built-in analytics of the platform for each influencer post:
  - Instagram Insights
  - Facebook Insights
  - Twitter Analytics
  - YouTube Analytics
- Record for each post: comments, shares, likes and interaction rate. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
- Ask each influencer to send their engagement figures (comments, shares, likes, interaction rate) for the campaign posts, so you can compare them with your own platform data. [L0630.001, L0786.002, L0786.004]

### Influencer Platforms and Campaign Analytics

- Influencer marketing platforms such as Influency, Aspire IQ and Tracker provide detailed campaign analytics, including reach, engagement and metrics specific to each collaboration. [L0630.006]
- These platforms are most useful when the whole campaign is managed through them. [L0786.007]
- If the campaign ran through such a platform, pull its analytics for reach, engagement and collaboration-specific metrics. [L0630.001, L0786.002]

### Brand Mentions and Audience Feedback

- Track brand mentions over the campaign period, either with a social listening tool or by manually searching for the brand, keyword, hashtag or campaign name. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
- Survey the audience and collect feedback (surveys, social media polls) to find out where they first heard of the influencer and how they perceive the campaign. [L0630.001, L0786.002]

### Sales, Conversion and Unique Codes

- Track sales and conversion rate for each campaign. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
- Give each creator a unique discount code, ideally built from their name, so that sales can be traced back to that creator. A 25% code was affordable at that brand's margins. Any unique code, even free shipping, serves the same tracking purpose. [L0790.094]
- Coupon codes unique to each influencer track campaign results and strengthen the relationship with the creator. Any coupon works, even free shipping, as long as it is tied to a specific influencer. [L0790.056]
- Use one identical spelling of each creator name across all ads. Consistent creator names allow reports per creator and make creator commission payments easier to match. [L0885.006]
- An influencer post that does not produce a sale can still be valuable if it earns a follower, an email or a visit that can be retargeted. Plan this fallback before paying for the post. [L0790.061]

### Campaign Evaluation Sequence

Measure each influencer campaign in this order:

1. Check the platform's built-in analytics for each influencer post (Instagram Insights, Facebook Insights, Twitter Analytics, YouTube Analytics). [L0630.001, L0786.002]
2. Record comments, shares, likes and interaction rate. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
3. Ask the influencer to send their engagement numbers as well. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
4. Monitor brand and hashtag mentions with a listening tool, or search manually for the brand, keyword or campaign name. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
5. Pull detailed campaign metrics from the influencer marketing platform, if one was used. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
6. Track sales and conversion metrics. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
7. Survey the audience. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
8. Compare before and after the campaign. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
9. Compare results with your other marketing channels. [L0630.001, L0786.002]

### Deciding Which Partners to Repeat

- Use the results and audience insights from each campaign to decide which influencer strategies to repeat. [L0868.008]
- Choose future partners and formats based on what has resonated most with your audience. [L0868.008]
- Use the sequence above on every campaign before deciding, so that comparisons across creators rest on the same measurements. [L0630.001, L0786.002]
- Influencers whose traffic and sales prove profitable can remain active advertising partners for multiple years. [L0183.010]

## Other details

### Creative assets

- Custom YouTube thumbnails and channel cover art can be bought cheaply from freelance designers on Fiverr. The course recommends this over making them yourself. [L1511.013]
- This is older advice (2021 to 2022). [L1511.013]

### TikTok ad testing

Procedure for launching a test campaign:

1. Create a new campaign named after the product plus "testing one" and choose ABO.
2. Create the first ad group named "Open 1" with the external website option and select your pixel.
3. Set the conversion event to complete payments and set placement to TikTok only.
4. Turn off comments and video download.
5. Select the countries (United States and Canada for the standard setup) and the language English.
6. Choose the gender: all, or female for beauty products.
7. Choose the age group: 18+ for open targeting, or 18 to 24 for teen-oriented products.
8. Check the audience size; for open targeting in the US and Canada it is often above 100 million.
9. Set the start to the next day at midnight, with the schedule all day or from 7 a.m. to midnight.
10. Set optimization to lowest cost.
11. Select the identity: brand name and logo, or your own account if it has engaging videos.
12. Upload the creative and add the ad text.
13. Set the call-to-action button to Shop Now and paste the UTM URL.
14. Submit and publish the campaign.
15. Duplicate the ad group to create the other ad groups, changing only the audience.

[L1377.035]

### Pinterest group boards

Procedure for using group boards as a traffic source:

1. Build a strong Pinterest profile with relevant boards so it looks credible when you contact group board owners.
2. Find group boards in your niche, for example through the BoardDeckHQ.com directory, and get access to pin on them.
3. Post your product and content pins to the group boards.
4. Drive traffic from the group board pins back to your store.
5. Retarget the visitors who arrive from the group boards.

[L1136.026]

### Customer collection letters

- Put a real customer testimonial in every letter, including collection letters. An unpaid bill often reflects doubt about value rather than refusal to pay. [L1369.037]
- Use the quote to restate value for the customer. [L1369.037]

### Coaching calls

- Use two one-on-one coaching calls each month. [L0820.044]
- Unused calls do not roll over. Book them before the month ends, because they reset on the first of the next month. [L0820.044]


# 14. SEO and content

## SEO Strategy, Priorities and Timelines

### What SEO and content do for a store

- SEO means making a store's pages appear in the unpaid, organic results of search engines, as opposed to paid search ads for which the advertiser pays per placement. [L0594.001]
- SEO targets Google and Bing. The lesson names Bing as the second major target after Google. [L0594.006]
- Organic Google search means people find the store through unpaid text results, usually on page one. It costs nothing per click, but it depends on the store ranking. [L0586.005]
- Organic search traffic comes when people search for a brand name, a product name or a SKU number and click through an unpaid result. It costs nothing per click but is not directly paid for. [L0676.006]
- Organic traffic is any traffic that does not come from paid ads, including search results, organic social posts and free shopping listings. [L0855.151]
- SEO produces free organic traffic from Google and Bing search results and is the free counterpart to paid search ads. [L0597.009]
- SEO is one of the core traffic sources because it brings in visitors without paying for each click. It is treated as free traffic, although it requires work to build. [L0759.004]
- Content marketing sits between publishing and advertising. You build an audience-owning platform and advertise your own products on it, instead of letting third parties monetize that audience. Owning the channel gives you control over how customers are influenced and serviced. [L0382.001]
- Blog posts keep generating traffic for years after a one-time production cost, while pay-per-click charges for every incremental visit. Content therefore has a long-lasting return on investment. [L0382.002]
- Ranking for keywords that matter to your business works like owning the best retail locations in your industry online. If you hold those search results, competitors are pushed out of them. [L0382.003]
- Organic search traffic is one of the funnel's traffic sources, brings in visitors without paid ads, adds to Google Shopping traffic and works alongside email and retargeting. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0458.049]
- A single piece of content that ranks on the first page of Google can deliver steady monthly organic traffic for years, potentially tens of thousands of visits over time. Judge content cost by this long-term return rather than the short-term price. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0379.019]
- Content marketing is a medium- to long-term traffic strategy. Early on it brings only small amounts of traffic through promotion, and it can lift conversion on the site when the content solves a buyer's problem. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0383.001]
- Content and SEO build awareness at the top of the funnel, so a shopper who later searches a high-value term already knows the brand. This raises the conversion chance on those high-value searches. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0740.017]
- Once SEO is fully built, drive large volumes of top-of-funnel traffic from people with no loyalty to a brand who want the best product, and guide them to your product. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0768.015]
- Low-value generic searches should be targeted through SEO and content marketing rather than by bidding on Google Shopping, because these channels reach that audience more profitably than Shopping ads do. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0740.016]
- Organic search traffic from keywords that problem-aware people type can be won at a much lower cost than paid ads for the same keywords. This makes it affordable to target the problem-aware stage at scale. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1392.010]

### How the search results page is laid out

- On a Google results page for a niche search, the top product listings are Google Shopping product listing ads, the "Sponsored" sections are paid search text ads, and further down come product feed results and organic listings. Only the organic listings are the target of SEO. [L0594.004]

### Ranking factors

- Website search rankings depend on three primary factors: quality backlinks from other domains, quality content on the site, and onsite optimizations. [L0173.001]
- Google's own description names three ranking factors above the rest: quality content, backlinks from other websites, and optimizing the site for the RankBrain algorithm. Other SEO activities can help a bit more, but without these three a site will struggle to rank. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0414.032, L1500.003]
- The two sources phrase the third factor differently. Source A calls it onsite optimization; Source B, citing Google, calls it optimization for RankBrain. Both describe the same area of work. [L0173.001, L0414.032]
- Neglecting any one of the three factors limits search rankings, however well the other work is done. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1500.003]
- SEO work falls into three main categories: on-page SEO, technical SEO, and off-page SEO, which is mainly link building from other websites to your site. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1500.001]
- On-page and technical SEO alone rarely produce strong organic search traffic. They multiply the results of content marketing and link building, so all three should run together. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1500.002]
- Backlinks are a core ranking factor, and deep content earns more links. Building deep content is therefore a prerequisite for reaching the top of Google's organic results. Link building is a separate task that must also be done to generate significant organic traffic. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1461.007]
- Backlinks matter most for very competitive keywords in crowded industries, not for niche e-commerce stores. (Older, 2022.) [L0429.067]
- Read together, the backlink statements apply as follows: the core-factor view (Source B) applies to competitive keywords, and the 2022 crowded-industry view applies to niche stores. [L1461.007, L0429.067]
- Ranking signals include user behavior: bounce rate, time on page and return visits. A good store experience can improve Google Shopping and organic performance. (Older, 2022.) [L0969.083]
- Google evaluates aggregated, anonymized user interaction data to judge whether a result is relevant to a query. Visitors who click an organic result and leave within seconds signal a poor match, so keeping visitors on the page and having them interact further is a ranking lever. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1099.001]
- Google states that it uses aggregated, anonymized interaction data to judge relevance, but it does not publish how much bounce rate or time on page weighs in ranking. Treat both as indicators of relevance and page quality, not as confirmed direct ranking factors. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1099.020]
- Organic traffic depends on many combined factors, so a quick list of tips is not enough. The full SEO material should be studied in depth. (Older, 2022.) [L1092.101]
- Established stores rank better in organic search mainly because they have existed longer, built more links and done SEO work for longer. A newer store can overtake them by applying the same SEO practices consistently over time. (Older, 2022.) [L0963.153]
- Domain authority alone should not decide whether to enter a niche. Checking competitor scores only shows which keyword competition level is realistic for your store. [L1227.030]
- Organic clicks concentrate on the first few Google results, and deeper result pages are rarely visited. Product pages should therefore aim for the top organic positions, not just to be indexed. [L1227.029]
- Clicks concentrate at the top: about three quarters of traffic goes to the top three organic results, and the number one spot takes roughly two thirds of that. Reaching position one matters more than reaching position three. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1461.024]

### On-page SEO

- On-page SEO means optimizing each individual web page so that search engines can understand what the page is about, which context it provides, and which searcher it serves. The goal is to make the page match the search terms it should rank for. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1118.001]
- On-page SEO works through many small adjustments to a page's content and structure that tell search engines which search terms the page should match. It is the first SEO work most sites do after technical SEO is in place, and it should be reviewed even if some of it was already done. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1118.002]
- Product pages need SEO work for the search engine listing and the product description. Collection pages, standard pages and blogs also need SEO work, using the newest SEO guides. (2024.) [L0806.076]
- Apply the SEO optimizations from day one, as part of setting up product pages and the store. They are not a later project. (Older, 2018.) [L1109.061]
- For a new store, plan page titles, URLs and categories before launch, because it is much harder to add SEO structure to a finished site later. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0949.057]
- Do not delay paid ads on a new Shopify store because most URLs show as not indexed. Only the key pages need to be indexed, and indexing duplicate URL variants would hurt search results rather than help them. [L0373.003]
- Outsourcing alt text and meta descriptions to freelancers on Upwork is acceptable, because the writing does not require expert skill. AI tools can speed up the work where you can use them. (2024.) [L0965.081]

### Target the products you sell

- SEO should target the products, brands and SKU numbers you sell, because product pages are what bring organic buyers. Ranking for a broad niche keyword does not produce the same sales. [L0941.076]
- A narrow customer focus simplifies content and SEO planning, because one buyer's interests answer the question of what to publish first. Broad stores with many product types and buyer types often stall because they cannot decide where to start. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0905.014]
- For a nationwide high-ticket dropshipping store, geo-targeted local SEO is usually not worth it, because customers can be anywhere in the country. Local SEO normally covers a location within one state; once the area spans several states it is no longer local SEO. (Older, 2021-22.) [L0879.007]
- Low-margin brand products can still rank organically if the site is set up correctly, which can produce some sales without paid traffic. (Older, 2019.) [L1068.074]
- A new store without traffic data can find its likely best sellers by checking the top product placements in the category pages of established competitor stores. Optimize those product pages first, because top placement usually reflects strong sellers. [L1190.018]
- A store can earn its first sale without any paid ads by ranking organically in Google for long-tail searches such as brand name, product name and SKU number. These rankings can be captured before Google Shopping product listings are set up, and the sale came at zero ad cost. [L1223.006]

### When to start

Sources differ on whether paid traffic or SEO comes first. Each position applies under the conditions below.

| Position | Sources | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| Paid traffic first, organic in the background | L0274.061 (2023); L0801.084 (older, 2021); L1111.119 (older, 2020); L1112.032 (older, 2021) | Paid campaigns can be run profitably; in the early life of a store, money goes to paid traffic for customers and cash flow; blogs follow once the store is profitable from paid traffic, unless the approach is purely long-term SEO; paid can bring early sales while organic develops |
| Free channels and SEO from the start | L0360.058 (2024); L0857.047 (2025); L0713.003 (older, 2021-22); L0853.077 (older, 2021) | Before buying traffic, use free channels; start organic early even while doing other work; SEO runs alongside paid traffic from the start for high-ticket dropshipping; free Google listings are used early, including when relaunching a stalled store |
| Content after validation and supplier approval | L0249.066 (older, 2022); L0962.145 (older, 2021); L0544.010 | Niche validation and supplier approval come first; a tight budget goes to product pages and supplier outreach; SEO and content are an advanced later-stage layer, and reaching initial sales does not depend on them |

- Before buying traffic, use free channels such as SEO on product pages and free Merchant Center listings to bring visitors in. Paid ads can be funded from the profit those visitors generate. (2024.) [L0360.058]
- Start organic SEO early, even while doing other work, because traffic takes a long time to build. (2025.) [L0857.047]
- Free Google product listings can drive traffic without ad spend, so list products there early. Relaunching a stalled store also benefits from these free listings. (Older, 2021.) [L0853.077]
- Do not prioritize getting content written immediately. Start with niche validation and supplier approval, and build content gradually as the store proves profitable. (Older, 2022.) [L0249.066]
- A blog is not needed to get suppliers to approve a new store, so a tight budget should go to product pages and supplier outreach first. Blog content can be added later to build organic traffic over time. (Older, 2021.) [L0962.145]
- SEO and content marketing are an advanced, later-stage layer. Reaching initial sales does not depend on them. [L0544.010]
- Improve store pages and collection pages for SEO as the store grows, since organic traffic builds slowly. Free Google product listings and paid Google Shopping ads give data much faster than SEO. (Older, 2021.) [L0968.067]

### What to prioritize first

- A new store should prioritize product pages over blog content. Blogs and content pages should come only after product pages are optimized and the site is being crawled through Search Console. (Older, 2022.) [L0429.067]
- For a store that has not done SEO yet, improve the collection pages and product pages first, since those are the pages you want people to land on. Build blog content around them afterward. (Older, 2021.) [L0801.085]
- Start SEO work with the top 20% of products, which bring in about 80% of website visits. Find those products in Shopify analytics or Google Analytics and optimize them first. (2024.) [L0965.079]
- Sources agree on the order of the work: product pages come first and blog posts come after. The first step differs by source. [L0594.005, L0245.045, L0962.154]

Sequence A, a Shopify store SEO order (undated):
1. Install the recommended SEO app.
2. Do organic keyword research.
3. Optimize product pages.
4. Optimize collection pages.
5. Optimize standard pages.
6. Optimize blog posts.
7. Promote the content to get early traffic.
