### Advertorial retargeting logic

1. Identify visitors who reached the advertorial but did not click through to the offer page. [L1131.025]
2. Show them an ad that educates them further about the product and explains the benefits. [L1131.025]
3. Include a discount such as 40 percent off or 10 dollars off. [L1131.025]
4. Send the ad click directly to the offer page instead of the advertorial. [L1131.025]

### Site-wide and dynamic retargeting with content

- Use a site-wide retargeting pixel to remind visitors of your store, and use article or content retargeting to drive readers of your content back to your website. [L0643.032]
- Dynamic multi-product ads show several products from your store, with the best-converting products at the front. [L0643.032]

### Email capture from readers

- A content visit does not need to produce a sale, but an opt-in form should be present on the content page to collect leads. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1421.028]

## Abandoned Cart and Checkout Recovery

### Finding Abandoned Carts in Shopify

- Abandoned carts appear in the Shopify admin under the Orders dropdown menu. [L0470.026]
- Abandoned checkouts are listed under Orders > Abandoned Checkouts. The list shows the checkout number, order date, customer, email status and whether the cart was recovered. [L0737.003]

### Nightly Check Routine

Check abandoned carts every night in the Shopify admin (older, 2021). [L0671.018, L0671.294]

1. Open Orders in the admin panel. [L0671.018, L0671.294]
2. Click Abandoned carts. [L0671.018, L0671.294]
3. Note who abandoned which products. [L0671.018, L0671.294]
4. Follow up with each one, or have someone do this for you. [L0671.018, L0671.294]

### Speed and Channel Priority

- Following up on abandoned carts is one of the first automations worth building for a dropshipping store. [L0437.014]
- The follow-up should be sent as quickly as possible after a shopper leaves without buying, ideally within minutes rather than hours. [L0437.014]
- Abandoned-cart recovery works best through direct calls and text messages as soon as possible, while email runs automatically in the background. (2023) [L0470.025]
- A Shopify and Slack integration can send an alert with the customer's name and cart items so you can reach out quickly. [L0470.025]

### Email Follow-Up

- At the very least, send an email to every abandoned cart. Early on, calling them directly is a way to recover more sales (older, 2021). [L0671.019, L0671.295]
- Once the store is established, run abandoned cart follow-up as an automated email flow, for example one built in Klaviyo (older, 2021). [L0671.296]
- The Klaviyo app can run the abandoned cart reminder flow. [L1400.004]

#### Manual Abandoned Checkout Emails (before automating)

1. In Shopify, click Orders. [L0857.043]
2. In the dropdown, click Abandoned checkouts. [L0857.043]
3. Open the records that include customer details and email each customer. [L0857.043]
4. Start with manual emails before automating this step. [L0857.043]

Template for the manual email (replace the bracketed parts before sending):

```
Subject: Quick question about your order

Hi [customer first name], this is [your name], the owner of [store name].com. I noticed you had [items in cart] in your cart but did not finish your order. I wanted to check whether anything stopped you from ordering from our store. If you have any questions or comments that would help us understand why you did not complete the order, please reply. I am happy to help and to do what we can to earn your business.

[Your name]
[Store name]
```

[L0857.044]

### Phone and SMS Follow-Up

#### Call Recovery Procedure (older, 2022)

1. Keep automated follow-up emails as the first step. [L0429.057]
2. Set a delay timer of a few minutes after a cart is started and not completed. [L0429.057]
3. Send an alert (for example through Slack, or Zapier as an alternative) with the customer's name, products and phone number. [L0429.057]
4. Call as soon as possible and ask whether there are questions or problems with the order. [L0429.057]

#### Call Script (older, 2022)

```
Hi [customer first name], this is [your name] from [store name]. I noticed you started an order for [product name] but did not finish checking out. Is there anything I can help with, such as a question about the product, the shipping time or the payment options?
```

[L0429.087]

#### Personal Outreach

- Contact people who left items in their cart and ask what happened, since a direct conversation can turn them into buyers. [L0709.031]
- Personal outreach can recover sales that automated messages miss. [L0709.031]

### Visitors Without Contact Details

- Visitors who start checkout but leave before entering any contact details cannot be followed up personally. Reach them through remarketing ads only. [L0471.058]

### Messenger and Ad Funnel (Day by Day)

#### Tool Stack

- The automated abandoned-cart funnel uses five tools: Facebook, Shopify, an email marketing tool, Minichat as a Facebook Messenger bot, and Zapier to connect Minichat with Shopify. [L1243.016]
- Minichat and Zapier both have free plans. Their paid plans were cited at under 20 USD per month. [L1243.016]

#### Messenger and Social Retargeting

- Keep Facebook and Instagram retargeting set up properly, because influencer visitors who did not buy can be retargeted to convert later. [L0790.070]
- Add Messenger abandoned cart messages to capture visitors who add items but leave. [L0790.070]

#### Funnel Steps

| Day after abandoned cart | Shopper status | Action | Channels |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 to 2 | Has not bought | Reminder that the cart is still waiting. Assume the shopper was distracted, busy or comparing prices. Do not offer a discount yet. | Messenger sequence and Facebook ads |
| 3 to 4 | Still has not bought | Offer the easiest incentive: often free shipping, or 10% off if free shipping is not the lowest-cost option. Include the discount code and a link back to the store. | Messenger, collection ad and email |
| 5 to 7 | Still has not bought | Send the best offer and add scarcity. Use social proof on days 5 and 6. On day 7, make the best discount expire within 12 hours. | Video ads and emails |

Sources: Day 0 to 2 [L1243.020]; Day 3 to 4 [L1243.027]; Day 5 to 7 [L1243.030]

- Reach the shopper through several channels, because many buyers need multiple touchpoints before they purchase and may not check a single channel. [L1243.029]
- Each message should show that the store wants the sale, since competition is high. [L1243.029]

### Offers

- Abandoned cart reminders work better when they include a valuable offer, because the offer gives the shopper a reason to return and finish checkout. [L1399.006]

### Cart Audiences and Exclusions

#### Fallback Without Abandoned Cart Data

- When you have no abandoned cart data, use Facebook retargeting ads to target people who viewed your products or added items to their cart. [L0276.006]
- Combine Facebook retargeting with Google remarketing using the same audience to maximize visibility. [L0276.006]

#### Audience Setup Procedure

1. Create a custom audience of people who visited your cart page. [L0643.028]
2. Create an exclusion audience of people who reached the thank-you, confirmation or checkout-complete page. [L0643.028]
3. Use a generic retargeting image such as your store logo or a range of your products, and not necessarily the exact product left in the cart. [L0643.028]
4. Show a message such as "Did life get in the way? Come back and finish your order." [L0643.028]
5. Optionally, after a while, show a 5 or 10 percent discount code to people who have still not bought, and never to buyers. [L0643.028]

#### Trigger Setting

- For the abandoned-cart campaign, use the Add to Cart event as the trigger when building Facebook audiences. In the collection ad audience settings, select Add to Cart from the viewed product, add to cart and purchase options. [L1243.023]

#### Three-Audience Sequence

Set up these three audiences once so the shopper moves through the funnel automatically. [L1243.024]

| Audience | Added to cart | Excludes | Funnel step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 to 2 days ago, not purchased | nothing | Reminder |
| 2 | 3 to 4 days ago, not purchased | last 2 days | Easy offer |
| 3 | 5 to 7 days ago, not purchased | previous 4 days | Best offer and deadline |

- The lesson's wording for audience 2 was ambiguous, but this table matches the funnel timing it describes. [L1243.024]

#### Expected Results

- Retargeting abandoned cart visitors on Facebook can recapture up to 25 percent of lost sales, on top of the automated abandoned-cart email sequence. [L0643.029]

### Testing and Benchmarks

- The commonly cited average abandoned cart rate is 67%, based on a 2015 study. The presenter estimated the current figure is higher, in the 70s, but gave no source for that estimate. [L1243.002]
- Automated follow-up for abandoned checkouts must be tested. A low answer rate (about 1 in 10 calls answered) is normal. [L0806.079]
- Phone follow-up by hand often does better than automation alone. [L0806.079]

## Capturing Emails and Cross-Channel Follow-Up

### Exit-Intent and Opt-In Capture

- Capturing email addresses from bounced visits, meaning visitors who leave without purchasing, gives a second chance to convert them and reveals customer hesitations and preferences. [L0154.001]
- Collect email addresses from every visitor who reads content or opts in, so you can follow up later. Email follow-up is what makes peak-season sales strong. *(Older: 2018.)* [L1274.012]
- Set up an email pop-up to capture visitors who are not ready to buy. This extends the relationship beyond the visit. [L1136.027]
- A browse abandonment feedback survey is an optional extra channel. It is not a required part of collecting customer feedback. [L0682.028]
- Set up a browse abandonment survey email only if the store already tracks browse abandonment. [L0682.028]

### Lead Magnets

- Run paid ads to a lead magnet landing page with an email capture form. Offer a piece of content or an ebook sample in exchange for the email address. [L0789.037]
- Use this approach to grow the follower base and the email list at the same time. [L0789.037]

### Email Lists and Invisible Audiences

- Audiences fall into two groups:
  - **Email lists:** opted-in subscribers, for example in Klaviyo.
  - **Invisible lists:** platform audiences built from site visits, purchases and social engagement. They include people who never opted in.
- You need both, because only a small share of visitors ever give their email address. [L1204.006]

### Uploading Customer Lists to Ad Platforms

Procedure for adding your Shopify email list to remarketing (2024):

1. Export your customer email list from Shopify. [L0965.046]
2. In both Google Ads and Meta Ads, create a customer list audience from that file. The list may include people who have not bought yet. [L0965.046]
3. Upload the list to both platforms. [L0965.046]
4. In your remarketing ad group, stack the new customer list together with your website visitor audience so both are included. [L0965.046]

Procedure for improving Facebook remarketing performance (*older: 2022*):

1. Set Shopify data sharing to maximum. [L1113.064]
2. Upload the Klaviyo list of opted-in people who have not bought yet to a Facebook custom audience. [L1113.064]
3. Add that audience to your remarketing campaigns. [L1113.064]
4. Check frequency, and reduce spend if the same people see the same ads repeatedly. [L1113.064]

### Syncing Email With Ads

- Sync your ads with your emails so that everyone in the broadcast email audience sees the offer message, including people who do not open email. [L0757.028]
- Post each email promotion or piece of content to Facebook and run it as an ad at the same time. This way the list and the audiences see the same message, which builds the relationship and moves people closer to buying. [L1076.073]
- Run remarketing ads on Meta and Google, and email the visitor audience, to bring back people who visited the store. Use pixel-based audience data to build these lists. [L1115.089]

### Retargeting Visitors and Abandoners

- Retarget visitors who did not buy with ads and email campaigns. Use messages that follow up on the page they viewed. [L1016.045]
- Follow remarketing visitors and abandoned carts from two angles at once: automated emails in Klaviyo and personal outreach by the owner. *(Older: 2022.)* [L1092.100]
- Set up retargeting for visitors who arrive from Pinterest, so they can be reached again after leaving the site. [L1136.027]
- Retargeting is a two-part development stage. *(Older: 2021-2022.)* [L0414.039]
  - Part one: retargeting ads on Google, Facebook and YouTube.
  - Part two: personal communication through email, SMS, push notifications and Messenger.
- Smaller high-ticket businesses often neglect personal communication. *(Older: 2021-2022.)* [L0414.039]
- Three main follow-up strategies exist: retargeting ads, email marketing and SMS marketing. *(Older: 2021-2022.)* [L1497.004]
  - Retargeting ads run mainly on a few networks.
  - Email is the classic follow-up channel.
  - SMS is an older channel that can still deliver strong returns when used well.

### Personal Follow-Up Messages

- Use this formula for personal follow-up: name the product, use the real time the visitor spent on that product page from your tracking tool, then ask one simple question about whether they still want it. The specific detail shows a real person is paying attention, so the message feels personal rather than automated. Keep it short and never reuse a fixed script. [L1472.069]

```
Hi {customer_name}, you spent about 20 minutes looking at the {product_name} yesterday. Are you still interested, or can I answer a question for you?
```
[L1472.069]

```
Hi {customer_name}, I noticed you came back to the {product_name} page several times this week. Would it help if I checked its availability for you before you decide?
```
[L1472.069]

### SMS and Push: Channel Limits

- SMS retargeting works only for customers who tick the consent box to receive SMS. If most customers do not tick it, the channel delivers almost nothing. Do not rely on it as the main recovery channel. [L1216.014]
- SMS retargeting results depend heavily on the market. In the reported experience it worked in the US, Canada and Australia, but not in Switzerland, Germany and Austria. Test the channel per market before relying on it. [L1216.015]
- Sources differ on SMS. The older Source B material calls it a channel that can still deliver strong returns when used well. [L1497.004] Source C limits its use to consenting customers and to specific markets. [L1216.014, L1216.015]
- Push notifications are one of the personal channels listed alongside email and SMS for follow-up. *(Older: 2021-2022.)* [L0414.039]

### Multi-Channel Coordination

- Multi-channel marketing across email, SMS, push notifications and retargeting on platforms such as Google, Facebook, Pinterest and Snapchat works best when each message delivers value. Repeating the same product picture across channels mainly annoys customers. *(Older: 2021-2022.)* [L0949.049]
- Run retargeting ads and personal messages together as one development stage, rather than as separate tasks. *(Older: 2021-2022.)* [L0414.039]
- Keep ad and email messages consistent so that the list and the audiences see the same offer. [L0757.028, L1076.073]

## Promotions, Holidays and Q4 Retargeting

### Offer-based retargeting

#### Two types of deal

- Irresistible deal ads come in two types: offers aimed at one person based on their stage in the customer journey, and offers tied to a holiday or seasonal event such as Black Friday, Christmas, Thanksgiving, Veterans Day or Easter. Event deals can also be niche-specific or global. (older: Source B, 2021-22) [L0799.002]
- For a holiday deal, retarget everyone, including previous customers, with a campaign that runs only for the deal period. Audience position in the funnel does not matter here. (older: Source B, 2021-22) [L0799.016]
- For a specific offer, target product viewers who are near the point of no return. This is generally around 30 days after the product view, so a 14 to 30 day viewer window is the usual target. (older: Source B, 2021-22) [L0799.017]
- If your funnel moves fast, shorten the specific-offer window, for example to 7 days after the product view. High-ticket products usually have longer buyer journeys, so their offers should come later. (older: Source B, 2021-22) [L0799.018]
- Do not offer a discount just because someone viewed a product. A buyer who needs more time may not need a discount to convert, so do not rush the deal and protect profit by timing it to the customer journey. (older: Source B, 2021-22) [L0799.019]

### Deal timing

- Schedule the Christmas promotion in early December. Running it on Christmas Day misses buyers, who have spent their budgets and are not shopping online. [L1224.011]
- Publish holiday content weeks ahead of the event. A holiday blog post published just before the sale is wasted effort, because it will not have time to rank and few people will see it. [L1224.034]
- Run promotion-specific Google and Meta ads only during that promotion's dates, so each holiday has its own creative and a short exposure window. [L1224.024]
- Run retargeting ads from November 24 through the end of Cyber Monday. [L0307.007]
- High-CPM periods are ideal for retargeting, because the warm audience has high conversion intent despite CPM increases. [L0298.050]
- Build the visitor audience early, then spend on remarketing when ad costs rise in Q4. (older: Source A, 2019) [L1110.035]

### Monthly promotions

- Retargeting ads work alongside email to capture additional revenue during holidays and promotions. They are run as a standard part of the promotion plan. [L1097.040]
- During a short seasonal sale, point paid ads at remarketing audiences so people who already visited the store are pushed toward the discount. Use the same offer, coupon code and dates across the emails and the ads so the message stays consistent. [L1105.006]
- Promotion ads are not product-specific like dynamic ads. They push one store-wide deal, bundle or bonus to lapsed contacts. The goal is to re-ignite the reason the shopper searched for the product in the first place. [L1204.005]
- Remarketing to warm audiences costs less than reaching cold traffic, so promotions can run on a small budget if the offer is strong. Good offers in these audiences can produce a very high return on ad spend. [L1204.004]
- Static remarketing ads aimed at older website-visitor lists are not limited to holidays. They also run during regular monthly promotions, showing store products with the current coupon code and linking to the store. [L0623.025]
- During the promotion window, run Facebook and Google remarketing ads to the same audience that receives the promotion emails. This maximizes reach and increases sales from people who have already visited but not bought. [L1205.026]

#### Promotion audience and sequence

- The promotion audience is the catch-all group of people who engaged with the store (website visitors, email opt-ins, Facebook and Google remarketing lists) but have not bought. Promotions are sent to them only after they have gone through abandoned cart emails and dynamic product remarketing ads without purchasing. [L1205.002]

Procedure:

1. Visitor views a product and leaves without buying; add them to Facebook and Instagram remarketing and Google remarketing. [L1205.003]
2. Send them through the email flows, starting with the abandoned cart sequence, and show dynamic product remarketing ads that return them to the product they viewed. [L1205.003]
3. Anyone who still has not purchased after these automations is added to the promotion audience and receives the promotional offers. [L1205.003]

### BFCM and holiday campaigns

#### Standard BFCM campaign

Procedure:

1. Use 5-6 different creatives per campaign. [L0298.050]
2. Prioritize image ads (perform best during holidays). [L0298.050]
3. Highlight discount (e.g., '60-70% Off') and show price comparison (e.g., 'Was 159, Now 89.99, Limited Time Only'). [L0298.050]
4. Run this on warm audience (recent visitors, cart abandoners). [L0298.050]
5. High-CPM periods are ideal for retargeting because warm audience has high conversion intent despite CPM increases. [L0298.050]

Procedure, audience and traffic routing (for the Black Friday to Cyber Monday window):

1. Primary audience (prioritize): People who entered the email sequence (newsletter subscribers). [L0307.007]
2. If primary audience is too small for viable campaign: Expand to hot audiences = anyone who engaged with your brand: [L0307.007]
   - Visited your website
   - Watched 50%, 75%, or 90% of your videos
   - Engaged with your Facebook page (likes, comments, shares)
   - Engaged with your Instagram page
3. Run retargeting ads from November 24 through end of Cyber Monday. [L0307.007]
4. Send all retargeting traffic to the hidden category page (not product pages). [L0307.007]

#### Stacked campaign for a short, high-demand event

- For a short high-demand event such as Black Friday or Christmas, one approach was to stack all retargeting audiences into one ad set, use at least 10 creatives that combine testimonials with offer images, and add roughly 10 to 30 dollars to the budget. [L0646.055]
- The retargeting audience is small, so it needs fresh proof and new offers rather than the same ad shown repeatedly. [L0646.055]

Creative count, two values:

| Campaign type | Creatives | When it applies |
|---|---|---|
| Standard BFCM retargeting campaign | 5-6 per campaign | Each campaign run on the warm audience [L0298.050] |
| Stacked ad set for a short high-demand event | At least 10, combining testimonials with offer images | All retargeting audiences in one ad set for Black Friday or Christmas [L0646.055] |

#### Holiday-specific Facebook audiences (older)

- For holiday Facebook remarketing, target all visitors from the past 180 days instead of only the recently viewed-product carousel used normally. Use creative that is specific to the holiday, such as gift boxes with the offer shown on the image. (older: Source A, 2019) [L0467.062]
- Run holiday-specific Facebook ads to a custom audience of website visitors from up to 180 days ago, in addition to dynamic product ads. Example offers: 10 percent off the entire store for Cyber Monday, or a free water bottle with every purchase. (older: Source A, 2019) [L1110.033]
- Each visitor can see several different holiday offers within about three months when the same offer and creatives as the holiday email campaign are used. [L1224.022]

### Static holiday ads

- Standard remarketing uses dynamic ads, but holiday promotions use static image ads with uploaded images. Each holiday gets its own campaign on Meta and its own display and demand gen campaigns on Google. [L1223.027]
- For Q4 remarketing on Meta, use static remarketing ads, one for each holiday, uploaded as images. Do not use dynamic product ads for these holiday campaigns. [L1285.093]
- For Q4 remarketing on Google, use static display ads and static demand gen ads targeted to the same audience of website visitors from the last 180 days, excluding customers from the last 30 days. [L1285.094]
- Dynamic remarketing ads that show the exact products a visitor viewed should target recent website visitors who have not bought, such as 7-, 30- or 60-day audiences. These audiences form the main group used to bring buyers back during regular promotions. [L623.008]
- Visitors who were last active 30, 60 or 90+ days ago may no longer remember which products they viewed, so dynamic product ads are a weak fit for them. Static ads that show store products and the holiday offer work better for these older audiences. [L623.009]
- Example: A static holiday remarketing ad shows several store products with a holiday logo placed over them. The ad copy states that a promotion is running, names the saving and the coupon code, and links to the store. [L623.010]

Conflict on dynamic ads during holidays:

- Use dynamic product ads alongside holiday static ads on a 180-day custom audience (2019 advice). (older: Source A, 2019) [L1110.033]
- Do not use dynamic product ads for the holiday campaigns; use static ads only (2024-2025 advice). [L1285.093]
- Both approaches appear in the source. The 2019 advice pairs holiday ads with dynamic product ads on the 180-day audience. The 2024-2025 advice drops dynamic ads from holiday campaigns entirely. [L1110.033, L1285.093]

### 180-day audiences and Q4 remarketing

- For Q4 remarketing, target all website visitors from the last 180 days and exclude all customers who purchased in the last 30 days, on both Meta and Google. (2024) [L1285.092]
- Meta (Facebook) ads for the promotion should carry the same message as the emails and be shown to all website visitors from the last 180 days. Exclude all customers from the last 30 days from this audience. (2024) [L1221.006]
- Google Ads for the promotion should carry the same message as the emails and be shown to all website visitors from the last 180 days. Exclude all customers from the last 30 days, and run them as Display Ads and Demand-Gen Ads. (2024) [L1221.007]
- Meta remarketing targets all website visitors from the last 180 days, excluding customers from the last 30 days. Use the same offer and creatives as the holiday email campaign, so each visitor can see several different holiday offers within about three months. [L1224.022]
- Google remarketing uses the same audience as Meta: site visitors from the last 180 days, excluding customers from the last 30 days. Run both Display and Demand Gen ads on this audience, because the two formats add placements for short promotion windows. [L1224.023]
- For Google display and demand gen retargeting, use an audience of all website visitors from the last 180 days and exclude customers from the last 30 days. Run both ad types on the same audience to get more placements for short promotion windows. (2025) [L1287.042]
- Matching the ad message to the email message keeps the offer consistent across channels during the same promotion window. Excluding recent buyers stops the promotion from following customers who just purchased. (2024) [L1221.008]

### Audience and exclusion plans

#### Monthly promotion audience set

| Platform | Audience | Setup | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google Analytics | Website visitors, 7 days | Audience definition, with enable remarketing | Dynamic remarketing |
| Google Analytics | Website visitors, 30 days | Audience definition, with enable remarketing | Dynamic remarketing |
| Google Analytics | Website visitors, 180 days | Audience definition, with enable remarketing | Monthly promotions |
| Google Analytics | Purchasers, 7 days and 180 days | Condition: transactions greater than 0 (requires enhanced e-commerce tracking) | Exclusions and buyer segments |
| Facebook | Website visitors, 7, 30 and 180 days | Audiences > Create custom audience > Website | 7 and 30 days for dynamic remarketing, 180 days for promotions |
| Facebook | Purchasers, 7 days and 180 days | Website Purchase event via the pixel | 7 days as exclusion, 180 days for promotions |
| Facebook | Page engagement, 180 days | Create custom audience > Facebook page, choose the right Page per business | Reaching people Facebook can no longer track on site |
| Instagram | Business profile engagement, 180 days | Create custom audience > Instagram business profile, select the account | Reaching social engagers for promotions |
| Klaviyo | Broadcast list | All subscribers who have not opted out | Monthly promotion emails |

[L1204.009]

#### Holiday remarketing audience plan

| Audience | Ad type | Exclusion | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 180-day website visitors | Static holiday ads | 30-day website visitors | Reach older leads who have not bought |
| 30-day website visitors | Dynamic product ads | Recent customers | Bring back recent visitors who have not bought |

The same structure can be built on both Facebook and Google by creating separate ad sets for the older audience and excluding the newer one. [L0623.011]

#### Email and ad exclusions

- Email promotions go to all contacts except those who purchased in the last 30 days and those currently in an evergreen automation, such as an abandoned cart sequence. The same segment applies whether you use Shopify Email or Klaviyo. [L1224.021]
- Do not run holiday promotions as cold campaigns to people who have never visited the store or joined the list. Promote only to email subscribers and recent site visitors, and exclude recent buyers so they do not see the same discount again. [L1223.029]

### Ad copy and message consistency

- Remarketing ads on Meta and the Google Display Network can reuse the offer, code, and deadline from the promotion's email copy so that the message stays consistent across channels. Build the ad copy from the emails rather than writing it from scratch. [L620.005]
- Prompt for writing remarketing ad copy from the email copy:

```
Using the email copy provided above, write copy for the remarketing ads I will run on Meta and the Google Display Network. Please write a separate version for each platform, and for each include a headline, primary text, and a call to action. Keep the discount code, the 10% discount, the promotion dates, and the delivery-before-Christmas guarantee identical to the emails.
```

[L1286.002]

### Budget math per promotion

#### Small-budget principles

- Holiday remarketing ads can run on a very small budget and still reach many people. Budget is therefore rarely the reason to skip this step. [L623.012]
- Remarketing budget for a small holiday audience is about $5 per day, which makes the ad spend a small cost compared with the email sales it supports. The budget can be scaled with the audience size. [L1223.028]
- Remarketing to warm audiences costs less than reaching cold traffic, so promotions can run on a small budget if the offer is strong. [L1204.004]
- Remarketing to people who have already visited the website is typically the lowest cost advertising, because those visitors are cheaper to reach than new traffic. (older: Source A, 2019) [L1110.035]

#### Budget procedure

1. Count how many people are in each Facebook and Google audience. [L757.033]
2. Decide how many times you want each person to see your ads (frequency). [L757.033]
3. Find the current remarketing CPM for each platform from your historic data. [L757.033]
4. Calculate the budget for each audience and total it per platform. [L757.033]
5. Divide each platform total by the number of promotion days to get the daily budget. [L757.033]

#### Formula

Daily budget = total platform budget / number of promotion days. For a 3-day promotion, divide the Google total by 3 and the Facebook total by 3. [L757.035]

#### Worked example

Small-audience example: seven-day website visitors, 2,000 people each on Google and Facebook, frequency 6. At a $1.50 Google CPM the total is $18 (about $6/day over 3 days), and at a $5.00 Facebook CPM the total is $60 (about $20/day over 3 days). [L757.037]

### Ending promotions cleanly

- Leaving bundle pages, bonus gifts or progress trackers live after a promotion ends sends visitors to dead ends and rewards that no longer exist. Revert every change in the closing procedure. [L1204.054]
- Run promotion-specific ads only during that promotion's dates, so each holiday has its own creative and a short exposure window, and stop them when the window closes. [L1224.024]

#### Further details

- Remarketing ads on Meta and the Google Display Network can reuse the offer, code, and deadline from the promotion's email copy so that the message stays consistent across channels. Build the ad copy from the emails rather than writing it from scratch. [L0620.005]

- Dynamic remarketing ads that show the exact products a visitor viewed should target recent website visitors who have not bought, such as 7-, 30- or 60-day audiences. These audiences form the main group used to bring buyers back during regular promotions. [L0623.008]

- Visitors who were last active 30, 60 or 90+ days ago may no longer remember which products they viewed, so dynamic product ads are a weak fit for them. Static ads that show store products and the holiday offer work better for these older audiences. [L0623.009]

- A static holiday remarketing ad shows several store products with a holiday logo placed over them. The ad copy states that a promotion is running, names the saving and the coupon code, and links to the store. [L0623.010]

- Holiday remarketing ads can run on a very small budget and still reach many people. Budget is therefore rarely the reason to skip this step. [L0623.012]

Set the paid budget for an offer promotion:
1. Count how many people are in each Facebook and Google audience.
2. Decide how many times you want each person to see your ads (frequency).
3. Find the current remarketing CPM for each platform from your historic data.
4. Calculate the budget for each audience and total it per platform.
5. Divide each platform total by the number of promotion days to get the daily budget.
[L0757.033]

- Daily budget = total platform budget / number of promotion days. For a 3-day promotion, divide the Google total by 3 and the Facebook total by 3. [L0757.035]

- Small-audience example: seven-day website visitors, 2,000 people each on Google and Facebook, frequency 6. At a $1.50 Google CPM the total is $18 (about $6/day over 3 days), and at a $5.00 Facebook CPM the total is $60 (about $20/day over 3 days). [L0757.037]

## Retargeting Existing Customers and Repeat Purchases

### Why Existing Customers Are Worth Targeting

- Not retargeting existing customers is a major missed opportunity, because selling to an existing customer is much easier than acquiring a new one (older, 2021-22). Relevant upsells and resells should be promoted through ads to past buyers (older, 2021-22). [L0563.027]
- After a first sale, retargeting and repeat email campaigns bring the same customer back for second and third purchases (older, 2021-22). Repeat sales are cheaper to win than new ones, so their profit margins are usually higher (older, 2021-22). [L0771.041]
- Second and third purchases from existing customers usually generate more profit than the first sale, which makes existing-customer retargeting a key driver of customer lifetime value (older, 2021-22). Combine it with email marketing for the best effect (older, 2021-22). [L0563.030]
- Do not assume existing customers will never buy again. Not all of them will, but some will, so test repeat offers rather than dropping them from campaigns (older, 2021-22). [L0563.032]
- People who already use the product have already decided and rarely read acquisition ads, so repeated acquisition ads for current customers waste budget. [L1261.119]

### Building Customer Audiences

- Leaving existing customers out of retargeting means missing repeat sales. Build a separate customer audience and give it its own campaigns (older, 2021-22). [L1390.004]
- Build a customer list from customer email addresses and names (older, 2021-22). Upload the list to the ad network, which matches it to users on its platform (older, 2021-22). [L0563.028]
- Wait until the list reaches the network's minimum size before using it. Google Display needs 100 people (older, 2021-22). [L0563.028]
- Show ads to this audience only when you have a relevant offer or content for these customers (older, 2021-22). [L0563.028]

**Customer audience procedure (older, 2021-22):**

1. Build a customer list from customer email addresses and names. [L0563.028]
2. Upload the list to the ad network, which matches it to users on its platform. [L0563.028]
3. Wait until the list reaches the network's minimum size before using it; Google Display needs 100 people. [L0563.028]
4. Show ads only when you have a relevant offer or content for these customers. [L0563.028]

### Excluding Customers from Acquisition

- If you have enough volume, build a customer audience and exclude it from new-customer acquisition campaigns (older, 2021-22). Customers also need their own retargeting campaigns matched to their stage in the customer journey, not first-purchase offers (older, 2021-22). [L1390.021]
- Showing first-purchase retargeting ads to existing customers wastes spend, because they rarely buy the same product right away (older, 2021-22). Serve customers separate messages based on where they are in the journey (older, 2021-22). [L1390.022]
- Target only first-time buyers by excluding customers with a purchase frequency above one. [L1243.037]
- Use the same exclusion for the thank-you video so repeat buyers do not receive it again. [L1243.048]

### Timing After Delivery

- Timing for existing-customer ads can range from soon after the first purchase to six months later or longer (older, 2021-22). The right timing depends on the offer, such as an upsell or a reorder (older, 2021-22). [L0563.029]
- The repeat-purchase funnel must start only after the customer has received the product, not when the order is placed. [L1243.035]
- If products have different shipping times, separate the audiences by brand or product so each one is triggered by its own delivery. [L1243.035]

### Goodwill and Thank-You Videos

- Recent buyers get a goodwill video ad on reach and frequency, at around 2 impressions per day for 7 days. The goal is to be seen, not to sell, so conversion objectives are the wrong choice here. [L0649.022]
- The thank-you video ad for customers in the first 7 days is set to low frequency, roughly twice a day per person. [L1076.066]
- Customers from the last 180 days see the same content and promotions over time. [L1076.066]
- Goodwill thank-you ad pattern: a short personal video that thanks the buyer, names the store, and says what to expect next. It works because it builds the relationship after purchase and gets high engagement. [L0649.068]
  - Example one: "Thank you for ordering from us, here is what happens next and how we will look after you." [L0649.068]
  - Example two: "Welcome to the family, here is what to expect from your first week with us." [L0649.068]

**Thank-you video script for first-time buyers.** Recorded by the store owner on camera and posted as a Facebook ad after the product has been delivered. Target only people who have bought once, by excluding purchase frequency above one, so repeat buyers do not receive the thank-you message again. [L1243.048]

```
Hi {first name}, I wanted to take a minute to thank you for your order of {product name}. Customers like you are the reason this store exists, and I hope you love using it. Keep an eye on your inbox, because I have a discount for your next order.
```

[L1243.048]

### Repeat-Purchase Funnel

- Repeat buyers were cited as converting at 60% to 70%, compared with an industry average of 2% to 3% for new customers. Targeting past buyers is therefore presented as the main source of repeat sales. [L1243.036]

**Repeat-purchase funnel procedure:**

1. **Step 1, after delivery:** Have the owner send a short thank-you video through Facebook, then follow up with an email containing a coupon code for the next purchase. Target only first-time buyers by excluding customers with a purchase frequency above one. [L1243.037]
2. **Step 2, 7 to 14 days after delivery:** Run a cross-sell campaign with dynamic product ads. Set up pairings in the product catalog beforehand, such as when a customer buys product X, show product Y. Then send an email that recalls the coupon code from step 1. [L1243.038]

### Cross-Sell and Upgrade Ads

- Set up cross-sell pairings in the product catalog before launch, so that a purchase of product X triggers product Y (older, 2021-22 pairing logic is the same as the current funnel). [L1243.038]
- Example: customers who bought a product a year ago are shown an ad for a newer model, presented as an upgrade to the product they already like (older, 2021-22). Some of them will buy again, so the offer is worth testing (older, 2021-22). [L0563.031]

### Channel Split: Acquisition vs. Retention

- Use paid ads to acquire new customers, and use SMS and email to retarget existing buyers with new products or better offers. [L1431.051]
- Retargeting existing customers avoids paying again to reach them on Facebook. [L1431.051]
- Use retention and reactivation messages separately from the acquisition campaign. [L1261.119]

## Retargeting for Long Buying Cycles and Competitive Niches

### Retargeting for High-Ticket Products with Long Buying Cycles
- High-ticket products usually have longer buying journeys, so follow-up must cover a longer period. Without follow-up for first-time visitors, many will leave and buy elsewhere before they are ready. [L0473.012]
- High-ticket buyers, such as people furnishing a home, may research products up to six months before they buy. Keep paid traffic running in slow periods so these early planners enter your retargeting list and recall your store when they are ready to purchase. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0949.069]
- For some high-ticket products, customers shop months before they intend to buy, so retargeting must keep your brand present through that whole consideration window until they are ready to pay. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1239.010, L1240.010]

### Keeping Paid Traffic Running in Slow Periods
- For high-ticket products with long buying cycles, keep paid traffic running during slow periods. Customers may plan purchases months ahead, and retargeting lists keep your store in front of them until they buy. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0949.047]
- The right level of paid traffic depends on your risk tolerance and long-term view. Some owners cut traffic in slow periods to save money, while others keep it running to build audiences for later. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0949.048]
- Remarketing audiences built during slow economic periods compound in value. Maintaining consistent remarketing metrics during downturns means a higher audience size and message frequency when the economy recovers, which multiplies campaign effectiveness. (Older advice, 2020.) [L0245.038]

### Building Audiences in Slow Periods, Then Activating Them
(Older procedure, 2020.)

1. Collect customer emails through opt-in forms. [L0245.036]
2. Create Google audiences of all website visitors (website visits). [L0245.036]
3. Create Facebook audiences of website visitors and page engagement. [L0245.036]
4. During periods of low purchase intent (economic downturns), build these remarketing lists without aggressive selling. [L0245.036]
5. Once consumer confidence recovers, execute heavy remarketing campaigns to these built audiences via email, Google, and Facebook. [L0245.036]

### Competitor-Aware Retargeting for Resellers
- Resellers who sell other brands' products face competitors selling the same items. Prospects who research in advance see several sellers, and in long consideration periods the seller a prospect saw most during research often wins the sale, not only the seller with the best offer. Retargeting therefore gives a competitive advantage. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1239.009, L1240.009]
- Retargeting brings back visitors who did not buy yet. It is one of the reasons a store wins repeat sales when competitors offer the same MAP price. [L0966.098]

### Retargeting in Ultra-Competitive Niches
- In an ultra-competitive niche, retarget visitors on Google, Facebook, Instagram, Bing and Yahoo with higher bids. Buyers often return days or weeks later, forget which store they researched, and buy from a competitor, so repeated exposure keeps your store in front of them. [L1357.016]

### Private-Label Products
- Remarketing to your own visitors is a main traffic source for newly private-labeled products that Google Shopping does not reach, because shoppers do not search for them. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0968.066]

## Channel Selection and Priorities

### Start with search, then retarget
- Search-based campaigns come before retargeting. Google Search, Google Shopping and Bing are the preferred sources of store visitors because people actively look for the product there. [L1020.005, L1243.001]
- Facebook retargeting starts only after Google Search, Google Shopping and Bing are maxed out. Facebook is a discovery platform, not a search platform, so it is the next channel to add, not the first. [L1243.001]
- Cold Google campaigns target people searching for the product, while remarketing runs on both Google and Meta. This does not change based on whether your audience is more active on Google or Facebook. [L0471.015]
- Retargeting should run across several networks with the same core messages. Using only one channel loses customers whose attention is split across platforms. (2021-22, older) [L0563.023]
- Aim for a subtle, omnipresent presence across relevant networks so visitors meet your ads wherever they go without feeling followed. Reach cold traffic this way, and retarget warm and hot audiences across the same networks so competitors do not dominate attention. (2021-22, older) [L0563.025]
- Scale retargeting to your traffic volume. [L1251.044]

### Channel order
1. Start with Google retargeting, which has the highest priority. Set up dynamic remarketing first, then standard remarketing, then video/YouTube remarketing. Build these audiences before any other retargeting channel. [L0920.013]
2. Add Facebook, Instagram and Bing next, using the same audience logic on each platform rather than separate strategies. [L0920.014]
3. Add the next bottom-of-funnel campaigns: website retargeting on the Google Display Network and retargeting on Shopping. Both target people who have already visited the store. [L0867.004]
4. Keep YouTube low priority until other channels are fully used. (2021, older) [L0247.071, L0962.158]
5. Test TikTok last, and only after the Meta and Google remarketing budgets are fully used. It is not a main revenue source. (2025) [L0837.055]

**Conflicting advice on Facebook dynamic remarketing versus Google remarketing.** The 2021 advice (older) gives Facebook dynamic remarketing ads the remarketing budget before Google remarketing or YouTube placement ads. It says Google remarketing is not worth the added complexity until monthly sales reach the high five or six figures. The undated Source A advice puts Google first without a sales threshold. [L1112.026, L0920.013]

| Situation | Order | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly sales below the high five figures (2021, older) | Facebook dynamic remarketing gets the budget first. Google remarketing is not yet worth the added complexity. | L1112.026 |
| Monthly sales in the high five or six figures (2021, older) | Google remarketing becomes worth the added complexity. | L1112.026 |
| No sales threshold given (undated) | Google retargeting is the highest priority, then Facebook, Instagram and Bing. | L0920.013, L0920.014 |

### Google retargeting
- Google Ads offers several retargeting options, and Facebook (Meta) is the second main retargeting platform. [L1239.007, L1240.007]
- Run retargeting natively inside Google Ads and do not pay for third-party retargeting apps. (2022, older) [L0803.052]

| Format | Role in the setup | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Dynamic remarketing | First Google format in the priority order | L0920.013 |
| Standard remarketing | Second Google format in the priority order | L0920.013 |
| Video/YouTube remarketing | Third Google format in the priority order | L0920.013 |
| Website retargeting on the Google Display Network | Next bottom-of-funnel campaign | L0867.004 |
| Shopping retargeting | Next bottom-of-funnel campaign; run alongside Google Shopping campaigns | L0867.004, L1393.004 |
| RLSAs (remarketing lists for search ads) | Recommended retargeting network (2021-22, older) | L0563.024 |
| Google Ads brand search | Used together with Facebook remarketing | L1251.044 |
| Performance Max | Keeps showing ads to past site visitors across Google surfaces, so visitors are rarely lost | L0871.079 |

- A well-built Google setup with retargeting and Performance Max is a core source of repeat traffic when paired with paid acquisition. [L0871.079]
- Remarketing ads bring back visitors from all traffic sources so they can be converted into sales. [L1393.004]

### Meta: Facebook and Instagram
- Use Meta for remarketing to people who have already visited the store. [L1116.057]
- Use Facebook for remarketing rather than prospecting new audiences. Remarketing is the part of the Facebook budget that works best. (2021, older) [L1090.117]
- Use Facebook ads to re-engage visitors after they leave the store, because most of the profit comes from this once Google brings in the first traffic. (2019, older) [L1069.085]
- Facebook retargeting showed a slightly higher return on ad spend than Google retargeting in 2020, though not by much. Run both rather than choosing one. (2020, older) [L1277.091]
- Remarketing is a high priority and should run on both Google and Meta. A good audience can help conversion and return on ad spend, especially for high-ticket products. (2023) [L1094.055]
- Use Google remarketing alongside Meta, because some visitors never use Facebook or Instagram. Audience Network also shows ads on partner websites and apps. [L0649.049]
- Facebook dynamic remarketing ads get the remarketing budget before Google remarketing when monthly sales are below the high five or six figures. (2021, older) [L1112.026]
- Use carousel ads for the product in Facebook remarketing. [L1251.044]
- Remarketing to non-buyers runs through Google Ads, Facebook, Instagram and email. Each channel can restart the funnel from the store visit. [L0676.015]

**If your target audience has low Facebook usage,** use retargeting campaigns on Google, Instagram or other advertising networks instead of relying solely on Facebook. [L0238.014]

### When Meta is added
| Condition | Action | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Google Search, Google Shopping and Bing are maxed out | Add Facebook retargeting as the next channel | L1243.001 |
| Google has brought in the first traffic | Use Facebook to re-engage visitors who left (2019, older) | L1069.085 |
| Visitors have left without buying | Use Meta to win them back, not to prospect | L1020.005, L1116.057 |

### YouTube and video
- YouTube ads work well for remarketing. Target website visitors from the last seven days and exclude customers. Video production is a barrier, so YouTube is generally lower priority than Google Shopping. (2021, older) [L0247.071]
- A short video, filmed as a selfie or recorded as a screen share, can remarket to visitors who viewed the store in the past seven days without buying. It works well on small budgets. Keep YouTube ads low priority until other channels are fully used. (2021, older) [L0962.158]
- Video/YouTube remarketing comes third in the Google priority order, after dynamic and standard remarketing. [L0920.013]

### TikTok
- Test TikTok remarketing only after the Meta and Google remarketing budgets are fully used. It is not a main source of revenue. (2025) [L0837.055]
- A separate TikTok retargeting campaign is generally unnecessary, because prospecting already reaches people who saw the product. Retarget only with a specific creative built for existing brand audiences, such as a discount-code offer. [L1374.025]
- Adding Google ads to Facebook and TikTok campaigns lets you retarget visitors from those channels who did not buy. This recovers customers who would otherwise never return. [L1213.019]

### Bing
- Retarget on Bing after Google, using the same audience logic as on Facebook and Instagram. [L0920.014]
- Bing search campaigns belong with Google Search and Google Shopping as search-based campaigns to max out before Facebook retargeting starts. [L1243.001]
- Bing is a preferred search source of store visitors. [L1020.005]

### Pinterest
- Pinterest remarketing can add some revenue if your target audience uses Pinterest. It is unlikely to double a business on its own. (2020, older) [L1111.122]

### Recommended networks and coverage claims
| Network | Recommendation | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Google Display Network | Retargeting network | L0563.024 (2021-22, older) |
| RLSAs | Retargeting network | L0563.024 (2021-22, older) |
| Facebook/Instagram | Retargeting network | L0563.024 (2021-22, older) |
| Twitter | Retargeting network | L0563.024 (2021-22, older) |
| Taboola | Retargeting network | L0563.024 (2021-22, older) |
| YouTube | Retargeting network | L0563.024 (2021-22, older) |
| LinkedIn | Add only for strictly B2B businesses | L0563.024 (2021-22, older) |

- The Google Display Network, RLSAs, Facebook/Instagram, Twitter, Taboola and YouTube together are claimed to reach about 99% of internet users. Treat this as a rough coverage target for a broad setup, not a measured figure. (2021-22, older) [L0563.035]
- Google Ads retargeting and Facebook (Meta) retargeting together are claimed to reach nearly 99% of internet users worldwide. (2021-22, older) [L1239.007]
- The 99% claim for Google and Facebook was made without a source and should be verified before it is used in planning. (2021-22, older) [L1240.007]

### Running Google and Meta as one sequence
1. A visitor clicks a Google Shopping product listing ad and visits the store. [L1031.012]
2. The visitor leaves without buying. [L1031.012]
3. The visitor sees Facebook retargeting ads for those products. [L1031.012]
4. Plan Google and Facebook campaigns together as one sequence, not as separate projects. [L1031.012]

- Use Google ads after TikTok or Facebook ads to reach people who visited the site but did not buy, across channels such as YouTube and Google. This creates an omnichannel presence. [L1436.075]

### Tools not worth using
| Tool or approach | Advice | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Third-party retargeting apps | Do not pay for them. Run retargeting natively in Google Ads and Facebook Ads. (2022, older) | L0803.052 |
| ROI Hunter | No longer supported for this purpose. (2022, older) | L0803.052 |
| AdRoll (2019 view) | Described as a straightforward way to start retargeting and often the easiest first tool. (2019, older) | L1275.067 |
| AdRoll (2020 view) | No longer used for remarketing, because Facebook's native tools are simpler. A third-party tool is unnecessary when the platform provides the function. (2020, older) | L1111.123 |

- The 2019 recommendation for AdRoll is older. The 2020 position is the later one: use the platform's native remarketing tools instead. [L1275.067, L1111.123]

## Measuring and Optimizing Retargeting Performance

### Core KPIs

- Retargeting ROAS is revenue from the ads divided by ad spend:

```
ROAS = revenue from the ads / ad spend
```

  [L0360.057]
- Facebook Dynamic Remarketing and Google Remarketing should keep a conversion rate of at least 2.5% as a baseline. These are the warmest audiences and should outperform cold traffic. (Older advice, 2022.) [L0272.041]
- Define business measurables for each horizon: customer count, average order value, cost per acquisition or cost per sale, repeat purchase rate, and number of products sold. Choose the measurables that directly drive revenue and profit figures. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1519.004]

### Sample size and attribution caveats

- With fewer than 300-400 qualified people in the audience, results appear random. Larger audiences show clearer conversion patterns. [L0276.057]
- Retargeting audiences from Google and from Facebook or Instagram can be built from site visitors. Include them when calculating the conversion rate for paid traffic. (Older advice, 2022.) [L0963.138]
- Traffic from days earlier can convert later through remarketing and abandoned cart emails. Do not judge a campaign on the last day's orders alone. (Older advice, 2021.) [L1279.070]
- Mobile shoppers often add products to the cart on a phone and finish the purchase later on desktop. Retargeting brings them back, so mobile traffic should not be judged only by immediate sales. (Older advice, 2019.) [L1275.068]
- If retargeting converts worse than cold-traffic campaigns in an account, the result is unusual and should be investigated: check audience size, lookback windows, and tracking errors. [L0867.006]

### Testing retargeting against cold audiences

- Retargeting is often the cheapest audience, but this does not always hold. One advertiser found that a retargeting audience cost 10 to 20 percent more than a cold audience of similar businesses in a similar niche that competitors had not yet targeted. Test cold audiences against retargeting audiences rather than assuming. [L0643.031]
- Both results apply at once. Warm audiences should outperform cold traffic on conversion rate [L0272.041], but cost per result must be tested, because retargeting can cost more than a cold audience [L0643.031].

### Diagnosing weak results

| Signal | First check | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Retargeting underperforms | How qualified the cold traffic is, and what the copy in the retargeting ads says (older advice, 2020) | [L1277.092] |
| High click-through rate, zero conversions | Traffic quality is usually fine. The bottleneck is the store, typically at product page level. Fix the conversion side before changing the audience. | [L1083.011] |
| Retargeting converts worse than cold traffic | Audience size, lookback windows, tracking errors | [L0867.006] |

- The quality of the remarketing audience depends entirely on the quality of the traffic that creates it. The best remarketers are people who arrived through well-optimized cold traffic campaigns. [L0276.009]
- Better cold traffic, such as traffic from Google Shopping, improves warm and hot retargeting results. Retargeting only works with the quality of the first visits that feed it. [L1083.013]
- Keep Meta ads running for remarketing at a small budget even when they have not yet produced conversions. Remarketing only performs well when the initial traffic was qualified, so weak traffic from Google also weakens remarketing. [L0837.054]

#### Learning from non-buyers

1. Create a custom audience of visitors who did not buy.
2. Retarget them with a short video in which you ask why they did not buy and what would change their mind.
3. Ask them to comment with the reason.
4. Use the answers to improve the product, price or page, so more visitors convert.

[L0643.034]

### Reviewing and improving ads on a schedule

- Track remarketing ROAS and units sold as the retargeting KPIs, because more organic visitors grow the remarketing list. Compare them with the earlier month to see whether the growth is working. [L0941.080]
- Review results across accumulated days rather than the last day's orders, since delayed conversions from earlier traffic also count. [L1279.070, L0941.080]

### Scaling budgets

1. Check that the audience is large enough for the result to mean something. Below 300-400 qualified people, results appear random. [L0276.057]
2. Check the return. A retargeting campaign should reach a ROAS of at least 10 (10x) before its budget is increased. [L0360.057]
3. Keep the Meta remarketing budget small until conversions appear, and only increase it once the campaign has passed the ROAS threshold. [L0837.054, L0360.057]

## Common Mistakes and Operating Rules

### Strategy Principles

Three principles drive remarketing success:

1. Stay consistently visible so customers do not forget you. [L0240.021]
2. Directly address the specific objections or concerns that prevented their initial purchase. [L0240.021]
3. Deeply understand what your target customer wants and why. [L0240.021]

### Product Ad Mix

- Running only dynamic product ads is a common mistake. They fit some visitors but not all, and repeatedly showing a product someone already rejected for 14 to 30 days rarely changes their decision. [L0563.014]

### Ad Angles and Segmentation

- Retargeting works best when ad angles are varied and audiences are segmented by the pages visited and the actions taken on the site. Each ad type can expose the customer to different aspects of the business and its products. [L1239.014]
- Retargeting ads work best when they use different angles and communicate different things about the business and its products. They are a chance to educate customers, not only to bring them back to the site. [L1240.015]

### Repetition and Message Fatigue

- Showing the same retargeting ad again and again over weeks, for example a full month, is one of the biggest mistakes and a common error. Once a customer has seen an ad a few times, repeating it adds little value, so change the angle or message instead. [L1239.013, L1240.014]

### Exposure Limits

- Retargeting visitors for too long and too often wastes budget and annoys people. Limit how long and how frequently each audience sees ads. [L1390.002]

### Operating Rules

1. Do not run only dynamic product ads; combine them with other ad types, because each type fits different visitors. [L0563.014, L1239.014]
2. Segment audiences by the pages visited and the actions taken on the site. [L1239.014]
3. Vary the angle, and after a customer has seen an ad a few times, change the message instead of repeating it. [L1239.013, L1240.014]
4. Use each ad to educate the customer, not only to bring them back to the site. [L1240.015]
5. Limit how long and how frequently each audience sees ads. [L1390.002]
6. Stay visible, address the specific objection that blocked the first purchase, and understand what the customer wants and why. [L0240.021]

## Other details

### Retargeting Principles

- Retargeting covers several ad types. Each type needs its own setup, and audiences should be segmented so every group sees the message that fits where it is in the buying process. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1497.006]

### Retargeting Setup Sequence (Older Advice, 2021-22)

Work through these nine follow-up actions in this order:

1. Set up all required pixels and tracking codes from Google Ads, Facebook and Google Analytics. [L0493.001]
2. Build the relevant retargeting audiences in Google Ads and Facebook. [L0493.001]
3. Plan the retargeting and email strategy before building anything. [L0493.001]
4. Identify email opt-in opportunities across the site. [L0493.001]
5. Review the email list and its segmentation structure. [L0493.001]
6. Plan the email sequences for post-purchase and each opt-in. [L0493.001]
7. Review and update the abandoned cart sequence. [L0493.001]
8. Build the first 30-day master flow. [L0493.001]
9. Replicate the master flow for each new entry point. [L0493.001]

### Meta Account Setup

Set up a new Meta account in this order:

1. Create a free Meta Business Manager at business.facebook.com. [L0649.061]
2. Create a Facebook page for the business. [L0649.061]
3. Create an Instagram page for the business. [L0649.061]
4. Install the Meta pixel on the Shopify store. [L0649.061]
5. Turn on auto advanced matching in the Meta account. [L0649.061]
6. Create the audiences listed below in Business Manager. [L0649.061]
7. Create the campaigns. If no lead generation or testing is running yet, start with hot dynamic, hot static, customers goodwill and promotions. [L0649.061]
8. Fill each ad set with 3-4 ads that look similar to the creative examples. [L0649.061]

### Landing Pages by Audience

- Speak to different target audiences with separate landing pages when they have different needs or experience levels, for example beginner, intermediate and advanced. [L0918.016]
- Match each landing page to the messaging of the ad that brings that audience in. This increases relevance and conversion. [L0918.016]

### Traffic Sources and Affiliate Offers

**Amazon Associate stores**

- Do not send traffic from Google Shopping, Google Performance Max or search ads to an Amazon Associate store. It is not allowed and can get the account banned. [L0923.023]
- Use Amazon Associate stores only for retargeting people who already know your brand, because batch-imported products get almost no organic traffic. [L0923.023]

**Raw affiliate links**

- Never run paid traffic to a raw affiliate tracking link, such as a long ClickBank hop link. Facebook dislikes affiliate promotion and the account can be lost. [L0923.028]
- Instead, write a review or informative blog post on your Shopify store, add the affiliate link there, and retarget the blog post visitors. [L0923.028]

### Display Placements

- Remarketing display ads can appear on unrelated websites because they follow where the visitor goes next. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0968.065]
- Unrelated placements are normal and are not an error on their own. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0968.065]

### Video Production

- Video editing is not a skill a store owner needs to learn. Freelance editors can cut a video cheaply, and at a rate of one or two videos per month the cost stays low. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1424.010]


# 17. Customer service, returns and chargebacks

## Designing the support operation: scope, channels and ownership

### Scope: which channels support covers

- A store's support scope is live chat, inbound phone and email, plus social messaging if the store uses it. At low volume one person can handle all of these. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0834.090]
- Cover three channels: email, live chat on the store, and social media messages and comments. Social media means Facebook page messages, Instagram DMs and comments on TikTok organic videos. [L1358.020, L1360.023]
- Answer direct messages and comments on time. If you run organic TikTok videos, assign someone to answer the comments on them. [L1358.024]
- Staff live chat or another support channel, because new visitors ask questions before they buy. Publish your support hours and an email address so buyers know a real person answers. [L1346.029]
- At launch, let customers reach the store through live chat, email and phone. Their questions show how the business actually works and what needs to be clarified. [L1446.011]
- A customer service role covers live chat, phone calls, and order shipping and tracking. Social media and content writing go to a separate person, because combining them breaks down quickly. [L0970.134]
- Automating about 30% of tickets lowers first response time and cost, and frees the team for complex cases that can lead to sales. Instant self-service answers also beat making customers wait for an agent. [L0752.034]
- TikTok direct messages now transcribe voice memos automatically as they are sent, which makes person-to-person conversations easier to read and follow. [L1504.013]
- A structured customer service setup answers questions quickly, prevents refunds caused by confusion, builds trust in the brand and supports sustainable store growth. [L0911.002]
- Phone volume in a small dropshipping store can be about one or two calls per day, and nearly all of them can be sales-related. At that volume, phone can be an additional task for a freelance assistant who already works at a computer, rather than a full-time role. [L0910.061]

### Scope of post-sale support in a store sale

- A typical post-sale scope for a store sale is about one month of email support plus two calls of at least one hour each over that month. Agree the scope before the deal closes. [L0553.019]
- Pre-selling means the calls and emails a buyer needs before committing to a purchase. Products that need a lot of pre-selling add workload for the owner, so avoid them when building a low-effort store. [L1517.017]

### Who handles what at each stage

- Early on, the owner answers every chat, email and call personally. Quick replies to stock and order questions turn clicks into sales. (Older advice, 2020.) [L1111.132]
- Handle all customer service yourself at first, so you learn which questions customers ask and how to solve their problems. (Older advice, 2019.) [L1110.040]
- The store owner handles customer contact and makes sure customers are satisfied, while the supplier usually stores and ships the product. Returns reduce the total sales figure in the store report. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0771.051]
- Move customer service off the owner's plate as early as possible, even if only part of it is delegated at first. This covers phone calls, emails, online chat and sometimes supplier contact. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1247.002]
- Typical contacts that interrupt an owner are shipping time questions and order-status questions (where is my order), arriving by phone, email and online chat. These are low-value, unpredictable inquiries and should go to a support person. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1247.021]
- A virtual assistant can handle emails and phone calls as order volume grows. (Older advice, 2020.) [L0468.145]
- Hire a virtual assistant working about 4 to 8 hours a day only after you know the questions and answers yourself. (Older advice, 2019.) [L1110.040]
- Owners who run the business from abroad need phone and email coverage, handled personally or outsourced, to keep buyers who are ready to purchase. [L0923.053]

Stage summary:

| Stage | Who handles it | What they need | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch, first weeks | Owner, personally | Answers to every chat, email and call; a list of recurring questions | L1111.132, L1446.011, L1110.040 |
| Low volume | One person, or a freelancer for phone | Chat, phone and email; social media handled separately if used | L0834.090, L0910.061, L0970.134 |
| Growing volume | Split into pre-purchase and post-purchase teams | See the split below | L0263.050 |
| Supplier stage | Supplier stores and ships | Tracking numbers sent to customers | L0771.051, L0910.006 |

- As order volume grows, split customer service into two teams:
  - **Pre-purchase** (sales, inquiry response, incentive-based compensation).
  - **Post-purchase** (fulfilment, returns, support).
  [L0263.050]
- Pre-purchase staff must understand order profitability, discount authorisation limits and real-time stock status before speaking with customers. Without this knowledge, they promise excessive discounts or unrealistic delivery dates, creating losses and operational chaos for the fulfilment team downstream. [L0263.050]

### Workload by price point

- Products priced at $2,000 or more typically require higher levels of pre-sale and post-sale customer support. (2024.) [L0253.004]
- High-ticket products raise the customer service workload, mainly in pre-sale questions and post-sale follow-up. Plan for this before selling products above about $2,000. (Older advice, 2022.) [L0854.083]
- Customer service is central in a business with expensive items, since more support is needed as prices rise. Plan staffing and support around the price and return rate of the niche. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0801.124]
- Customer service volume rises with higher-priced items, so plan support for those products. (Older advice, 2020.) [L0468.145]
- Lower-priced products attract more pre-sale calls, such as customers asking whether an item is in stock. Higher-priced products mean fewer calls, but you need to be prepared to answer or return calls quickly. (2023.) [L0835.051]
- Sources differ on higher-priced products. Some describe a higher overall level of support (L0253.004, L0854.083, L0801.124). Others describe fewer calls but a need for fast replies (L0835.051). Both apply: plan for more total support and faster response time per contact, even if the number of calls is lower.
- Expect a slightly higher volume of inbound support requests for electronics and complex products. A high order value, such as an $8,000 sale, can justify handling that extra support. (Older advice, 2018.) [L1274.017]
- Fewer orders mean fewer tracking numbers, fewer shipping problems and less customer service work. This workload reduction is a main reason to sell higher-priced products. [L0474.006]
- A low-ticket store of $40 to $50 products sourced from China generated high order volume but became a support nightmare. High order count with low-value products is not better than fewer higher-value orders. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0962.127]

### Workload by order volume

- Early on, support contacts in a new dropshipping store start slowly, often with only a few calls and sometimes none on a given day. Workload grows only once sales and momentum build, so early volume is usually manageable. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0909.001]
- At high order volume a store can receive hundreds of customer emails per day. This is a reason to outsource support early. [L1358.019]
- Many customers buy without ever contacting support, so slow replies affect only some of your sales, mainly early on. Sales continue while you handle the backlog. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0909.016]
- The share of buyers who call support before purchasing varies by market. In markets where many customers ask questions first, plan more phone capacity. In others, expect most buyers to purchase without contacting you. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0909.029]
- The early small-volume and later high-volume figures describe different stages of the same store. Both apply: plan for a quiet start and for a large inbox once sales grow. [L0909.001, L1358.019]

### Hours, response windows and coverage

- Buyers who are ready to purchase will leave for a competitor if calls or emails go unanswered for more than a few hours. (2023.) [L0923.053]
- Some customers will not wait for a callback, so slow responses will cost some sales. There is no perfect fix, so treat it as an accepted trade-off while the business is small. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0909.005]
- Pick up a call immediately only when you can take it from a quiet place. Otherwise let it go to voicemail and answer emails or chats in set blocks, such as about half an hour during the day. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0909.004]
- Email is easier to handle in batches, because there is a natural gap between a customer's message and your reply. Answer emails after work or in set blocks during the day. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0909.015]
- Daily coverage routine when working in a far time zone:
  1. Check emails right before going to bed, around 21:00 to 22:00 local time.
  2. Fulfil any orders that came in during the day so they do not wait a full day.
  3. Send tracking numbers, either personally or through a VA.
  4. Check emails again first thing in the morning.

  About 20 minutes at night and a morning check cover the start and end of a normal business day, so suppliers and customers see replies during their working hours. [L0910.006]
- Check a competitor's support quality by searching its store name and URL on Google and reading the reviews. Complaints about unanswered calls or emails show a gap you can close by replying quickly. [L0894.014]
- Do not invite overseas customers outside your shipping area to contact you. Shipping costs often exceed the product price, and such inquiries are frequently fraudulent. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0801.120]

### Setting up support step by step

1. Handle all customer service yourself at first, so you learn which questions customers ask and how to solve their problems.
2. Add answers to frequent questions (shipping times, warranties, stock status) to your website, so fewer people ask.
3. Set up automated post-purchase emails with tracking updates, for example with the AfterShip app.
4. Hire a virtual assistant working about 4 to 8 hours a day only after you know the questions and answers yourself.

(Older advice, 2019.) [L1110.040]

### Keeping support separate for each store

- Keep customer service and support separate for each store, because each store has its own customers and its own problems. Mixing support across stores creates confusion that is hard to undo. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0949.034]

### Support and growth: what to expect

- Good customer service protects reputation and can bring referrals and positive reviews. It will not multiply store traffic or customer numbers on its own, so owners should not expect support to be a major growth driver. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1247.020]
- Customer service is a growth lever. Buyers with a good experience come back, while a bad experience stops repeat purchases. Treat service quality as a core part of building a business that lasts. [L1472.001]
- Fast answers to customer questions, especially before purchase, can raise the conversion rate. Customer support therefore affects sales, not just service. [L1358.021, L1360.020]
- Sources differ on how much support can grow the business. One view says support does not multiply traffic or customers (L1247.020). Another says it raises conversion and repeat purchases (L1472.001, L1358.021, L1360.020). Both apply: expect support to protect and convert the customers you already have, not to bring in new visitors.
- Customer service is a core success factor. E-commerce businesses that offer no service either fail or stay small. Expect to answer phone calls and emails, because the belief that you never have to do this is wrong. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1480.027]
- Long shipping times combined with a poor customer experience caused the 2016 to 2018 approach to fail, even when cheap Facebook ads brought in orders. Consider shipping speed and customer experience alongside traffic. [L1459.019]
- For a newly launched dropshipping store, customer service and shipping are the operational areas where owners most often have questions. Sorting out these two areas early is a common starting point for daily store management. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1499.002]

## Setting up contact points: phone, email, chat and contact page

### Business phone numbers

- Use a dedicated business phone number, not a personal cell number, so business and private calls never mix on the same device. [L0700.002]
- Calls are one contact channel alongside email and chat, and a toll-free number can be obtained so customers can call without paying for the call. [L1093.008]
- A toll-free number makes the store look more established and gives customers an easy way to reach support, which can reduce chargebacks caused by unclear order problems. [L0430.014]
- Customers who call before ordering are checking whether the store responds. A visible phone number builds confidence and reduces hesitation to buy. [L1094.089]

| Option | Note | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Local area code number | Fine to start with | L1094.090 |
| Toll-free number (MightyCall 855 numbers) | Looks more professional later | L1094.090 |
| Google Voice free business number | Does not reveal it is Google Voice when the voice option is turned off | L1094.091 |
| GoDaddy 800 number | Another toll-free option | L1094.091 |
| Grasshopper (commonly used for public business numbers) | Older advice, 2021-22 | L1145.006 |
| JustCall.io or Zintel (used in Australia instead) | Older advice, 2021-22 | L1145.006 |

**Testing the number (older advice, 2021-22)**

1. Call the public phone number from a different phone, such as a partner's or friend's phone. [L1145.007]
2. Confirm that it rings through to the phone you will answer. [L1145.007]
3. If it does not, find and fix the cause before launch. [L1145.007]

**Phone hours and forwarding (older advice, 2021-22)**

- Phone or service hours should match when customers actually call, which often peaks in the evening after work. Extended hours can be a differentiator even if round-the-clock calls are rare. [L0411.028]
- Case: in the first business, the seller offered 24-hour phone support staffed by overseas agents while the seller slept. Almost no calls came at 3 a.m., but many came after work around 6 to 7 p.m. Paying agents to cover those hours was worth it because competitors did not answer calls. The seller forwarded the line to their own phone at night, and calls at that hour were almost never received. [L0411.027]
