- Forward the business number to your personal mobile during the day so you can take calls whenever you are free. [L0909.026]
- Set the number to divert to a prerecorded voicemail when you cannot answer, so callers always get a message instead of silence. [L0909.026]
- Outsource phone support once the store is profitable enough to justify it. [L0934.182, L0970.138]

### Voicemail greetings and phone handling

- Keep the phone number on the website even if you cannot answer every call, and use a voicemail greeting that captures the caller's name, email, phone and reason. [L0934.182]
- A business phone number should be listed on the store, with a voicemail that takes name, phone, email and reason for the call and promises a callback as soon as possible. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0834.091]
- Without a voicemail on the public number, callers reach nothing when you cannot pick up. Set a pre-recorded voicemail that lets callers request a callback. This matters most if you still work a day job during business hours. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L1145.008]
- Most inbound calls are either pre-sale questions from people wanting to order, post-sale questions about shipping dates, or checks that the business is legitimate. A voicemail with a short greeting helps you learn which group is calling. (Older advice, 2020.) [L1111.133]

**Voicemail template, store line (2023)** [L0934.178]

```
Hello, you've reached [store name, e.g. storename.com]. Thanks for calling. Our team is currently away from the desk or helping other customers, so please record a voicemail including your name, email address, phone number, and the purpose of your call. We'll respond as soon as we're able.
```

**Voicemail template, personal-brand greeting (no year given)** [L0941.081]

```
Hi, this is [your name] from [store name].com. Sorry, we are unable to take your call right now. We are either away from the desk or helping another customer. Please leave a voicemail with your full name, email address, phone number and the reason for your call, and we will get back to you as soon as possible.
```

**Voicemail template (2023)** [L0970.137]

```
Hello, you've reached [name] from [store domain]. Thanks for getting in touch. Right now I'm either stepped away from my desk or helping another shopper. Leave a voicemail including your name, phone number, email address, and what you're calling about, and I'll return your call as soon as I can.
```

**Voicemail template (older advice, 2020)** [L1111.131]

```
Hi, you have reached [Store name] at [domain]. We are sorry we cannot take your call right now because we are assisting other customers. Please leave a voicemail with your name, phone number, email address and the reason for your call, and we will get back to you as soon as possible.
```

**Voicemail script, improved (older advice, 2022)** [L1113.039]

```
Hi, you have reached [Your Name] at [Store Name], [your-store-domain.com]. We are unable to take your call right now because we are away from the office or helping other customers. Please leave your name, your email address, your phone number and the reason for your call, and we will get back to you as soon as possible.
```

**Handling customer calls before hiring phone support (2023)** [L0970.138]

1. Set the phone app's default voicemail greeting to the template. [L0970.138]
2. Turn on transcription so each voicemail is sent as text immediately. [L0970.138]
3. When a transcript arrives, call the customer back with the reason and details. [L0970.138]
4. Once the business is profitable, hire someone to answer the phone. [L0970.138]

### Dedicated support email and aliases

- Set up a dedicated support email for the brand and have a virtual assistant reply quickly, so that every customer gets an immediate response to questions or delivery problems. [L0492.037]
- Create the dedicated support email on Google Workspace (formerly G Suite), for example contact@ or info@ followed by the store domain, at about $10 per month. Connect your domain and set this address as the store contact email in Shopify. [L1173.030]
- Use the business email support address for support requests. The team reviews incoming messages Monday to Friday and almost around the clock, and escalates urgent ones to the owner. (Older advice, 2022.) [L0665.087]
- Set a dedicated returns@ alias. It separates return requests from sales and supplier mail while keeping everything in one inbox. Replies should come from the same address the customer wrote to. [L1197.021]
- Let a virtual assistant also send tracking numbers to customers. [L1431.054]
- Use a dedicated business address for the store, not a personal one. Addresses on the contact page are mailing addresses, and the page should say that returns are not accepted there. (Older advice, 2020.) [L1088.073]

**Email signatures and sending rules**

- Every business email must include a signature with the sender's name, the business name, the business phone number and the sender's personal business email address. [L0404.014]
- Set this signature up automatically in Outlook to save time, optionally with a small version of the business logo. [L0404.014]
- New emails to customers or suppliers that are not new orders must be sent only from the staff member's personal business email address, using the same signature as for replies. [L0404.016]

### Response-time standards

| Channel or situation | Target | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Support email, maximum | Reply within 48 hours, typically much sooner | L0934.102, L0934.183 |
| Support email, minimum standard | Reply within 24 hours, ideally within a few hours during business hours | L1259.050 |
| Support email, working-hours standard | Respond within 24 working hours, ideally within a few hours during working time | L1260.052 |
| Live chat, while staff are available | Widget says "We'll reply in a few moments." | L0752.038 |
| Live chat, promised callback when nobody is available | Roughly five minutes, per the contact-capture prompt | L0752.038 |
| Refunds for damaged or defective items | Handle quickly; after-sales service affects feedback score and loyalty | L1259.052 |
| Social comments and Messenger questions | Respond quickly | L1260.053 |

- Email support is non-negotiable: use a professional email address, not only one in the footer, keep a working inbox, and reply to customers within 24 hours, ideally within a few hours during business hours. [L1259.050]
- Email support is non-negotiable: use a professional email address with a working inbox, and respond within 24 working hours, ideally within a few hours during working time. [L1260.052]
- Respond to Facebook and Instagram comments and Messenger questions quickly. Chat support tools such as Tidio can help customers ask questions before purchase. [L1260.053]
- The contact page should promise a clear and quick customer service response. This reduces emails and calls, and it also helps suppliers decide to work with the store. [L0910.020]

### Spam control and lost messages

**Contact form and address spam**

- A support email address shown on the website attracts spam and irrelevant inquiries. Use a contact form instead, with predefined subject lines, which allows auto responses and rules to be applied. [L0752.024]
- Listing a plain support email address on a contact page leads to spam and irrelevant inquiries; use a contact form instead. [L0752.033]
- Contact form in Gorgias: Settings > Channels > Contact Form. Name the form, connect the store, define subject lines, then publish it on the website using the embed code. [L0752.025]

**Spam procedure for contact form submissions**

1. Delete junk emails immediately. [L0253.048]
2. If the same email addresses appear repeatedly, block them in your email provider settings. [L0253.048]
3. Do not mark them as spam; simply delete. [L0253.048]
4. Expect spam whenever you have public contact forms on your store; this is normal. [L0253.048]

**Checking for missing replies**

- For a support email that has not been answered, check your spam folder and that of the customer, because replies from customers and outgoing responses are both prone to spam filters. [L1285.071]
- If no reply arrives within the 48-hour window, follow up and check the spam folder. [L0934.102, L0934.183]
- A support email system can fail silently, so requests may never reach the team. If you have not received a reply after four to five days, send the request again through another channel. (Older advice, 2019.) [L0960.066]
- A helpdesk switch can lose emails, so a supplier or customer who says they sent a message but got no reply may have had it lost. Ask them to forward or resend the email to the new address. [L0807.039]
- Relying only on email notifications for form submissions introduces delays that competitors overcome. Real-time alerts enable faster contact and win high-value deals. [L0284.003]

**Email deliverability**

- Set up the DMARC record for the business domain to increase trust and deliverability, so customers receive order and account emails. In Shopify: Settings > Notifications > Sender email > Email domain authentication. Until it is set up, Shopify sends via a backup store address. [L1327.048]

### Contact page and form content

**Editing the Shopify contact page**

1. Go to Shopify Admin > Online Store > Pages and open the Contact page that Shopify created automatically with the account. [L0509.005]
2. Change the page title to Contact Us. [L0509.005]
3. Keep the theme template set to Contact, which adds a contact form to the page. [L0509.005]
4. Click Save. [L0509.005]
5. Click View Page to check the result. The page is reachable at /pages/contacts. [L0509.005]

- The Contact template adds a form that visitors can fill out, and each submission arrives in your email with the visitor's contact details. At the start, the template alone is enough; more contact channels can be added later. [L0509.006]
- Shopify admin > Pages > Contact us: keep the contact form and add at least two further contact methods, such as hours of operation, a real phone number and an email address or live chat, then save. Google checks that a storefront shows at least two contact methods. [L0724.028]
- The Contact Us page should be detailed and personal, with the owner's name, a clear invitation to email, and the email address, so customers know who to reach after purchase. [L1293.013]
- A support page must show customers how to contact the business. Contact details that are easy to find reduce pre-sale and post-sale uncertainty. [L1130.011]
- Make contact options (email, phone, live chat), shipping destinations and the refund policy clearly visible. Without them, visitors who have a question leave and buy from a larger marketplace instead. [L0390.027]

**Where the contact details go**

- Show customer service contact details, such as a phone number with opening hours, in the header so they are visible on every page. [L0409.047]
- Contact details in the footer (phone, email and postal address) are recommended. Search engines and paid ad platforms such as Meta and Google tend to view a store as more legitimate when contact information is visible, and the details give customers an easy way to reach the store. (Older advice, 2021-22.) [L0681.011]

**Reconciling plain email and contact form**

- Public visitors: use the contact form with predefined subject lines as the main route, because a plain address attracts spam. [L0752.024, L0752.033]
- Visible contact options: the store still needs at least two contact methods on the storefront, and a plain email address can be one of them. [L0724.028, L0390.027]

**Chat-widget wording on the site (2025)** [L0752.038]

```
We'll reply in a few moments.

Thanks for reaching out! Leave your email below and a team member will respond in roughly five minutes.

We'll be back tomorrow.
```

- While team members are signed in and available, the chat widget displays "We'll reply in a few moments." If nobody is available, it switches to the contact-capture prompt. Once business hours end, the greeting becomes "We'll be back tomorrow." Every message should match the brand's personality and tone. [L0752.038]

### Live chat on the store

- A live chat widget on the store gives shoppers a real-time support channel, usually used to answer questions before they buy. [L1007.007]
- The online chat widget appears in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen on all devices. [L0404.012]
- Older advice (2021-22): keep the chat widget at the bottom left or bottom right of the page, because shoppers expect the chat there. [L1298.010]
- Before a chat starts, visitors must enter a name and email address. The owner keeps the contact details even if the chat is not answered in time, and can follow up by email. [L1311.012]
- When visitors start a chat, they are prompted to enter their name and email; the email is captured even if you do not reply immediately, allowing follow-up if the chat is missed. [L0151.006]
- The visitor panel in a chat shows the visitor's email address, how long they have been a customer and their location. Shopify counts any email address stored in the system as a customer, even if that person has never bought anything. [L1311.018]
- Mobile notifications let the owner answer chats while away from the computer, which keeps response times short. Slow answers to pre-sale questions cost sales, so the phone app should be set up from the start. [L1311.004]

### Widget hours and offline status

**Going offline when you cannot answer**

1. Open the chat dashboard. [L0404.011]
2. Click the status drop-down in the top left-hand corner. [L0404.011]
3. Set it to "Offline" when you cannot be online for any reason. [L0404.011]

- During working hours, the chat dashboard must stay open while the staff member is at their computer. Outside working hours, the chat is in Offline mode, so customers leave messages, or the owner monitors the chat. [L0404.012]
- When the live chat agent is on break, hide the chat widget instead of showing an offline status, or route chats to a phone if staff can step in. This keeps the site from looking closed. (Older advice, 2020.) [L1088.072]

**Setting hours: two approaches**

- Keep availability as open as is realistic. While a store is run by one person, reaching as many visitors as possible during waking hours matters more than strict business hours. [L0948.013]
- Use 24/7 when visitors who write outside working hours should still be able to leave their name and email for follow-up. Available hours are 24/7 by default and can be edited to limit when the chat icon appears; keeping 24/7 is recommended. [L1311.025]
- Use a waking-hours window when you run the store alone and want staff only notified by phone. Set the window to the hours you are awake, for example 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM, individually for each day of the week. Chat stays on the store during these hours, and staff are not required to sit at the computer. Changes can take a few minutes to appear on the store. [L0948.012]

**Tidio operating hours**

- Turn on operating hours in Tidio and set the times you are available each day, for example Monday 7:30 AM to 6 PM and Tuesday until 4 PM. Match these hours to your target audience, or outsource replies to a VA if you cannot cover them. [L1297.031]
- Turn on operating hours and set hours per weekday, e.g. Monday until 6 p.m., Tuesday until 4 p.m. [L0477.026]

### Shopify Inbox

**What it is and where it runs**

- Shopify Inbox is the live chat app included with a Shopify account. Its mobile app lets you read and answer chats from your phone while customers browse the store. [L1287.011]
- Shopify has built-in live chat on the storefront, and a Shopify mobile app sends a notification to the seller's phone when a visitor starts a chat, so the seller can reply from anywhere. [L1304.006]
- Older advice (2021-22): Shopify stores do not include live chat by default, so a chat app must be installed. Live chat adds a personalised sales channel next to phone and email, and it demands less staff time than phone calls. [L1298.008]
- Shopify Inbox is a built-in live chat option in Shopify that serves the same purpose as Tidio. [L1360.022]

**Mobile app: which app to use**

1. Install the separate Shopify Inbox app on iPhone or Android (not the main Shopify app). [L0948.015]
2. Open it and log in with the store's Shopify account. [L0948.015]
3. Incoming chats appear as push notifications and open in the app. [L0948.015]
4. Type the reply and press send; it appears live in the storefront conversation. [L0948.015]

- The main Shopify mobile app sends a notification to the seller's phone when a visitor starts a chat. [L1304.006]
- Set up the phone app from the start, so the owner can answer quickly. [L1311.004]

**Inbox settings and conversations**

- In Inbox, a conversation with unread messages shows an unread count in the list, and opening it reveals the full history. Replies can be sent from the admin or the mobile app, and both devices show the same conversation. [L1311.017]
- Before a shopper can send a question, Shopify Inbox can require them to enter their name and contact details. This gives the store a contact to follow up with if the chat is missed, and shoppers can also opt into emails at this step. [L0948.014]
- Keep the customer marketing opt-in option enabled in Shopify Inbox settings, so chat visitors can opt into receiving emails from the store. [L0948.011]
- The first reply can be automated, and it is off by default. When turned on, the message can differ depending on whether the store is marked online or offline. [L1311.026]

**Instant answers and built-in options**

- Instant answers are automatic AI replies to common visitor questions, generated from store content. The suggested shipping question takes its answer from the store's shipping page, and a return policy answer can be turned on the same way. [L1311.022]
- "Track my order" is on by default in the settings for the online store chat. Leaving it on is recommended, because visitors can then check order status through the chat. [L1311.021]
- The Shopify Inbox chat widget offers shoppers quick options such as tracking an order, so simple order-status questions can be handled before a message is typed. Enabling these built-in options reduces the number of routine questions the store owner must answer manually. [L0948.021]

**Enabling instant answers**

1. Open the settings for the online store chat in Inbox. [L1311.023]
2. Confirm that "Track my order" stays on. [L1311.023]
3. Turn on the suggested instant answer for shipping details. [L1311.023]
4. Click Save. [L1311.023]
5. Turn on the instant answer for the return policy. [L1311.023]
6. Click Save again. [L1311.023]
7. Leave the marketing opt-in unchanged. [L1311.023]

- At launch, do not enable instant answers right away. Let real chats come in first, record what customers actually ask, and only then enable automated instant answers for the recurring questions. [L0948.010]
- Instant answers let visitors find answers without sending a message. When the same questions keep arriving, add a new instant answer for each one so the visitor gets the answer right away. [L1311.024]

### Tidio setup

**Installation and setup, version A (as taught)**

1. Install the app and customize the chatbot (name, blue color, avatar image). [L0477.026]
2. Answer the setup questions: main focus = increase sales, number of agents, industry = online store, customers last month. [L0477.026]
3. Choose talk to customers and automate conversations. [L0477.026]
4. Choose greet warmly (recommended when a Klaviyo pop-up already captures emails) or offer a discount in exchange for email. [L0477.026]
5. Set a password. [L0477.026]
6. Turn on the Tidio chat widget in the Shopify theme editor and click save. [L0477.026]
7. Settings: set the online status name to customer support. [L0477.026]
8. Team > Operators: add a VA as chat agent if hired. [L0477.026]
9. Turn on operating hours and set hours per weekday, e.g. Monday until 6 p.m., Tuesday until 4 p.m. [L0477.026]
10. Save. [L0477.026]

**Installation and setup, version B (as taught)**

1. Search for Tidio live chat in the Shopify App Store, click Add app, then Install app. [L1297.029]
2. Name the chatbot, choose the colors, and upload an avatar from unsplash.com. [L1297.029]
3. Set the main focus to increase sales, the number of support agents to 1, the industry to online store, and customers last month to just getting started. [L1297.029]
4. Agree to the terms and select both talk to customers and automate conversation. [L1297.029]
5. Choose to greet visitors warmly, since the Klaviyo pop-up already collects emails. [L1297.029]
6. Set a password and turn the Tidio chat widget on in the Shopify theme editor, then save. [L1297.029]
7. Under Settings, rename the online status message to customer support. [L1297.029]

**Tidio team and tools**

- Tidio is a live chat tool that can be installed on the store so support staff can answer customer questions in real time. [L1360.022]
- Add a VA or other helper as a chat agent in Tidio under Team > Operators, using their name and email, so you do not need to answer every chat yourself. [L1297.030]
- Chat support is recommended; the lesson names Tidio as an app for live chat. Handle refunds for damaged or defective items quickly, since after-sales service affects feedback score and customer loyalty. [L1259.052]

### tawk.to setup

**Widget appearance** (Administration > Chat Widget > Widget Appearance in the tawk.to dashboard; older advice, 2021-22) [L1298.009]

| Field | Default or note |
|---|---|
| Desktop Widget: Width | 350 |
| Desktop Widget: Height | 520 |
| Desktop Widget: Widget Position | Set position |
| Desktop Widget: Minimized Width | Set size |
| Desktop Widget: Minimized Height | Set size |
| Desktop Widget: Top Radius | Set corner radius |
| Desktop Widget: Bottom Radius | Set corner radius |
| Desktop Widget: Attention Grabber | Enabled toggle |
| Mobile Widget | Has its own appearance settings |
| Widget Colors | Header, Header Text, Agent Text, Agent Message, Visitor Message, Visitor Text |

- Enter brand colours as hex codes, then click Save. [L1298.009]
- The attention grabber is a teaser that draws visitors' attention to the chat. Switch it off if it looks weak, and keep one of the available styles only if it draws attention without clashing with the brand. [L1298.011]

**Inbox and staff**

- tawk.to Messaging works as a shared inbox where chats and tickets are stored. Emails sent to the tawk.to ticket address are also delivered to this inbox. [L1298.012]
- Staff and virtual assistants can be added to the tawk.to dashboard so they answer chats from the Shopify app during daily store management. [L1298.013]

### Quick replies, instant answers and chatbots

**Quick replies**

- Quick replies can be saved in Shopify Inbox for frequently asked questions. Pre-created discount codes from the store can be shared directly in the chat, and images can also be sent to shoppers. [L0948.016]
- The Inbox reply box supports quick replies (saved answers), discount codes, product links, image uploads and emojis. Quick replies are useful for repeated answers, and product links help the visitor move straight to the item in question. [L1311.019]

**Tidio chatbots: three bots**

1. Open chatbots and choose the cart abandoned template. Enter the discount, for example 15%, and the coupon code name, for example SAVE15, then save. Tidio creates the coupon in Shopify, so click Save and activate. [L1297.032]
2. Use the product recommendation template without changes and click Save and activate. [L1297.032]
3. Use the AI responder template for order status. Add conversation topics such as "hi where is my order", "hello where is my tracking number" and "when will my product arrive". [L1297.032]
4. Paste the order status reply, which says orders ship in 4 to 7 days of processing, and add your email at the end so customers can write to you. [L1297.032]
5. Click Save and activate and confirm the bot is on. [L1297.032]

## Hiring, briefing and managing support staff and virtual assistants

### When to outsource

- Outsource customer service first, because a constant flow of negative messages can drain the owner, and even major brands receive negative feedback. [L0780.012]
- Outsource customer support early. Answering customer questions can take a lot of time, especially with high order volume, and some days may bring hundreds of emails that overwhelm the owner. [L1360.019]
- Answering customer emails can take three to four hours per day and blocks growth. A virtual assistant (VA) at $3 to $5 per hour can take over this work and return those hours to the owner. [L1127.034]
- Typical daily tasks in an online store are answering live chat, phone and email questions, handling follow-up questions after a purchase, and processing incoming orders with suppliers until they ship. These tasks require human interaction and are usually the first candidates for delegation once they are understood. [L1447.004]
- Outsource customer service only after you have seen call volumes, call times and how many calls turn into sales. A new hire in another time zone should be fully briefed before taking over. [L1277.093]
- Do not outsource phone support until business profit can pay for it. Until then, use a voicemail with a clear message and return calls and emails the next day. [L0941.082]
- Per-call phone answering services are not recommended at the start. The vendor example is only a starting point to see what is possible. [L0941.083]
- Early on, answer live chat from the owner's phone when possible. Consider a paid 24/7 answering service only once the business is profitable and reinvesting profits. [L0967.091]
- Hire your own employees for customer service and other tasks that need care and attention toward customers. Third-party agents have less interest in your customers and often cost about the same as a direct hire. [L1359.014]
- Where sources differ on structure, use direct hires for work that needs care toward customers, and a virtual team for hours and time-zone coverage. [L1359.014, L0962.129, L0852.110]
- Scope of support hours depends on three factors: product price (higher price means fewer sales and fewer support contacts), customer demographic (older customers generate more phone calls), and budget. [L0721.031]
- Product knowledge questions can be handled by general support staff. Pre-purchase questions call for live chat and email coverage, which may give a competitive edge if others avoid it. (Older, 2019.) [L0663.003]
- Prepare customer service before a major sales peak such as Black Friday. In the lesson's case, a team of three VAs was not enough when orders surged, and tickets fell four to five days behind. Train extra helpers in advance, even family or a VA at around 3 USD per hour. [L1363.043]

### Where to find virtual assistants

- onlinejobs.ph is the go-to platform for hiring virtual staff to answer customer queries in real time when the owner is in a different time zone. Job posting, qualifying, hiring and training guidance is covered in the outsourcing module of the course. (2024.) [L0666.006]
- Staff customer support with VAs in regions with reverse working hours, such as the Philippines, to cover different time zones. Hire them through job platforms such as onlinejobs.ph. (2021.) [L0962.129]
- Customer support can be outsourced to a virtual team in the Philippines, which is a major growth step. Support covers live chat, phone and email. (Older, 2020.) [L0852.110]

### Hiring and vetting

- When hiring customer service staff, look for people with similar past experience who can provide a reference. Treat the job as a real position even though it is virtual. (2023.) [L0970.135]
- For a store selling to US customers, the person answering calls should be a native speaker with an American or Canadian accent. Customers then assume the business is a normal domestic company. Accents from some outsourcing regions can reduce trust for this audience. [L0910.060]

### Pay and incentive models

| Role or model | Rate or term | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Overseas customer service specialist | $2-6 per hour; usually little or no extra training, so an affordable first hire [L1129.005] | Source C |
| VA answering customer emails | $3 to $5 per hour [L1127.034] | Source C |
| Extra helper for peak periods | Around 3 USD per hour, or family [L1363.043] | Source C |
| Experienced VA for customer support via onlinejobs.ph | $5 to $8 per hour; cancellable monthly platform fee; candidates pre-screened for quality [L1274.075] | (Older, 2018) |

- Customer service for a VA can be paid by incentive per result rather than by the minute. Per-minute service pricing is less efficient than paying a hired assistant for the same work. (Older, 2022.) [L0854.084]
- Offer a performance bonus of 1% to 2% of the sales the hire closes as an incentive to customer service or sales staff. (2023.) [L0970.136]
- A customer service question about a new store can be delegated to a family member or friend with written answer guidelines. A small commission can be paid if they handle chats that lead to sales. (Older, 2020.) [L0967.092]

### Onboarding a new hire

- Set up the assistant in this order:
  1. Give access to the support mailbox, sales and orders. [L1173.032]
  2. Write standard operating procedures and reply templates. [L1173.032]
  3. Hold a weekly call to review work. [L1173.032]
  4. Update the instructions in one batch rather than sending small changes continuously. [L1173.032]
- When hiring fulfillment or design help, give clear, complete instructions, since vague briefs lead to unwanted results. Schedule calls regularly and do not wait for the assistant to start the conversation. [L1173.033]
- Onboarding a customer service or fulfillment hire (older, 2020):
  1. Document every customer service and fulfillment step for each supplier and each scenario. [L1277.094]
  2. Set up an open communication channel with the new person, such as Slack or Facebook Messenger. [L1277.094]
  3. Expect questions for the first few weeks, possibly up to a month, because the new hire will not know every answer yet. [L1277.094]
  4. Keep answering questions until the process runs smoothly. [L1277.094]

### Scope of the role

- A virtual assistant for customer service handles three areas: visitor questions before purchase, customer updates after purchase, and order processing. Order processing means contacting the supplier to place the order after a customer order comes in. It does not mean taking orders by email from customers. [L1430.002]
- VAs can handle order processing, tracking and routine customer questions without expert skills, since many customers mainly want to hear a real person. Phone support is often the first role to hand off. [L1515.031]

### Phone coverage and time zones

- Responding to customer queries instantly raises conversion. An owner in a distant time zone should outsource real-time responses rather than rely on a night shift schedule, since working through the night is unhealthy over the long term. [L0666.007]
- When operating from a distant time zone, staff phone support first, then email support, with people who work during your customers' business hours (US business hours in the example). Do not answer calls yourself at night. [L1515.032]
- Answering support calls personally at 3 or 4 a.m. because of a time-zone gap is not sustainable. Plan staffing before sales volume grows. [L1515.033]
- Split phone support and chat or email support into separate people only when volume grows beyond what one person can handle within the response targets. [L1111.126]

**Setting up a first phone helper (small business):**

1. Forward the business phone line to the helper's personal mobile. [L0337.005]
2. Pay per answered call instead of a fixed salary. [L0337.005]
3. Greet callers with "Hi, can I help you?" [L0337.005]
4. Take a message and ask the caller's questions. [L0337.005]
5. Tell the caller that a product specialist will call back. [L0337.005]

### Access rights and permissions

- Give VAs access only to the support mailbox and the sales and order data they need, not to the entire personal inbox. Keep the owner's personal inbox separate from customer complaints. [L1173.031]
- A VA can independently approve discounts up to 10%. Any discount above 10%, or any other customer credit, requires owner approval. [L0230.021]

### Inbox labels and email triage

- Colour-code Gmail labels by priority so the assistant knows which emails to handle first. Customer issues get a red label, since they are the most urgent. [L1000.063]
- An overnight inbox may hold around 20 emails, and an urgent $20,000 order could be buried among them. Priority labels make sure the assistant handles that order before routine messages. [L1000.064]
- Keep customer issues and sales inquiries in dedicated Gmail labels, not mixed into the general inbox, so they can be found later. Customer issues get a red label so they are actioned first. [L1000.068]

### Order boards

**Order Processing board (card per order):**

1. Order Sent: record the product name and shipping address, then send the order to the manufacturer. [L1396.016]
2. Once the manufacturer confirms the item is in stock, move the card forward. [L1396.016]
3. If the item is on backorder, notify the customer first and only then move the card to Backorder with a due date. [L1396.016]
4. Move the card to Shipped once fulfilled, and record the tracking number. [L1396.016]
5. Move the card to Claims and Damages when a claim or damage notice arrives, and add notes about its progress. [L1396.016]

- Keep cancelled orders on the board instead of deleting them, because the same customer may call back and the quote information may still be needed. Put a due date on backorders so they are not forgotten. Move cancelled orders to a cancelled list, not deleted. [L1396.017]
- If a replacement item is out of stock, notify the customer that a new item is coming but is temporarily unavailable. Keep the card in the Claims and Damages list with a due date, so the claim stays visible until the replacement ships. Add status notes to the card with each update. [L1396.018]
- Shopify order notes alone are hard to track once there are many backorders. Staff must scroll through each order and cannot see due dates. Track order status on a visual board with due dates on each card. This matters once volume reaches about 30 to 50 orders per month. Keeping important customer details only in individual Shopify orders makes information hard to find as volume grows, and the owner has to scroll through orders and cannot see all pending items together. A separate board for order tracking solves this. [L1396.019, L1396.063]
- Without a shared board, backorders and customer updates get lost. One customer waited since July, and the follow-up depended on memory. Lost notes from calls and chats also cause missed quotes. Record every customer request on a board that everyone can see. [L1396.020]

**Asana order board (automated order flow):**

1. A new order arrives in the store and is automatically added to the first column of the Asana order board, and the help desk sends a notification. [L1473.010]
2. The VA waits for the outside fraud-screening service ClearSale to approve the order. [L1473.010]
3. After approval, the VA forwards the order to the appropriate supplier or places it on the supplier's website and waits for confirmation. [L1473.010]
4. When the supplier confirms stock, the VA charges the customer's card in Shopify, since the card was only authorized at checkout. [L1473.010]
5. The VA moves the card to the confirmed column in Asana. [L1473.010]
6. When the order ships, the VA adds the tracking number in Shopify and updates the status in Asana. [L1473.010]
7. The VA marks the order complete in Asana with a check mark. [L1473.010]
8. If a shipped order later has a problem, the check mark is removed and the card is moved back to the column that matches the new issue. [L1473.010]

**Backorders on the Asana board:**

1. When a supplier reports a backorder, the VA gets the backorder date from the supplier. [L1473.011]
2. The VA records that date in Asana. [L1473.011]
3. The VA moves the order card to the backorder column. [L1473.011]
4. The VA informs the customer about the backorder using a ready reply template in the help desk. [L1473.011]

**Damaged items and returns on the Asana board:**

1. For a damaged item or a return, the VA asks the supplier for their damage or return procedure. [L1473.012]
2. The VA explains that procedure to the customer. [L1473.012]
3. The VA updates the order status in Asana. [L1473.012]

### Standard operating procedures and templates

**Support workflow with a VA:**

1. Create reply templates for the most common messages, such as where is my package, when will it arrive and where is my tracking number. [L0519.040]
2. Translate messages with DeepL (free online tool) when the assistant does not speak the customer's language. [L0519.040]
3. Review the assistant's drafts before sending them, especially for general messages. [L0519.040]
4. Keep separate templates for each target market. [L0519.040]

- Routine questions get a direct reply from the assistant. For unusual cases, the assistant sends the email screenshot to the founder, who dictates the response. [L1432.037]
- Staff have first responsibility for monitoring and answering emails to the business's customer email addresses. The owner monitors these accounts in the staff member's absence. Emails addressed to the owner by name must be forwarded to the owner's personal email. [L0404.015]

[insert business name]
Version 1 (update the number whenever a new version is issued)

How our customer service works
Customer service is one of our core selling points. It keeps sales coming in and brings existing customers back to buy again.

Phone service
Customers are directed to one number, which we promote on our website and in our ads. That number is [insert number].
We advertise that this number provides service during [insert advertised business hours].
Outside those hours, the line either plays a prerecorded message and sends callers to voicemail, which is checked during the next business period, or it forwards to the owner's personal phone.

Call routing
Our phone number is forwarded to different people at different times of day.
Current schedule, based on [insert your time zone] time:
[Insert the time periods showing which person the line is directed to]
If you are busy or unable to take calls during the hours the phone is routed to you, unanswered calls automatically overflow to voicemail or to the owner's personal phone. You do not need to turn the overflow on yourself.
Check voicemail regularly during the periods when you are expected to answer the phone.

How to answer the phone
Answer with a greeting that includes your first name and makes clear that the caller has reached [insert business name].
Examples:
"Hello... welcome to [insert business name], this is [insert your name]."
or
"Good morning, [insert business name], [insert your name] speaking."
Choose whatever phrasing suits you, but always identify yourself and confirm that the caller has reached [insert business name].
Because we treat customers like friends, feel free to ask how they are doing or share a light joke when it fits. We want customers to enjoy speaking with you.

Phone orders
Customers often phone in orders, and you are authorised to take them.
To place an order for a caller while they are on the line:
1 Ask the customer what they want to order.
2 Open our website, add those products to the cart, then go to checkout.
3 Go through the customer's contact details with them: name, email, address and phone number.
4 Click through to the payment page and ask how they want to pay. Phone orders can be paid by credit card or by bank deposit. A PayPal payment cannot be taken from the customer's PayPal account on their behalf.

They must send payment confirmation to [insert business email address] before we ship their order.

Email service

[Your Name]
[Insert business name]
[insert business phone number] | [insert personal business email address]
Set this signature up automatically in your Outlook account to save time. You may add a small version of our business logo to it; a logo file will be provided.

Email responsibilities
• You have first responsibility for monitoring and answering emails sent to [insert business email addresses].
• When you are absent, [insert business owner's name] monitors these accounts.
• If an email to either account is addressed to [insert business owner's name], forward it to [insert business owner's personal email] so they can reply.

Sending emails
When writing new emails to customers or suppliers that are not new orders, use only your personal [insert business email handle] address.
Use the same signature block you use in any [insert business email handle] inbox.

Online chat service
Customers can chat with us live through our online chat widget, provided by [insert name of chat tool, e.g. Zopim, Tidio]. The widget appears in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen on all devices.
Whenever you are at your computer during working hours, you must have the [insert chat tool name] dashboard open and watch for visitors.
Outside normal working hours, chat is set to Offline mode, where customers can leave a message, or [insert business owner name] monitors the chat and handles any customer contact.
If you cannot be online for any reason, set your status to "Offline" using the status drop-down in the top left-hand corner of the dashboard.
[Insert screenshot showing the chat window in offline mode]
The [insert chat tool name] works in both directions: customers can start a chat with us, and we can start one with a customer.
Starting chats is encouraged when you have spare time. It is optional and should only be done when you can handle it properly.
To start a chat, single-click a visitor and type your greeting in the window that opens.
[Insert screenshot showing an open chat box in the software interface]
Treat chats like a phone call: be natural and keep a friendly, upbeat tone.
A good opener is along the lines of: "Hi there, how's your day going? Can I help you with anything today?"
If the customer replies, keep the conversation going. If they do not answer your first message, do not send another, so that customers never feel pestered.

What to say when you don't know the answer
Customers ask all kinds of questions. Most are straightforward, and some are not. We have over [insert number of products] products for sale, and you are not expected to know every one of them.
You will regularly get questions you cannot answer. Our single rule for these moments: never invent an answer.
If you are dealing with a customer by phone, chat or email and need help, do one or more of the following, as relevant:
1 Contact [insert owner's name] through [insert relevant contact methods]. If they are available, they will either answer the question or ask you to pass the customer over.
2 If [insert owner's name] is not immediately reachable, tell the customer you will get back to them shortly, take their contact details, and follow up as soon as you can.
3 If [insert owner's name] is unavailable and you need product information, first check the supplier's webpage. If it is not there, call the supplier and ask. Suppliers are always glad to help.
4 Take your time. It is better to reply once you have the correct information than to answer quickly with wrong information. Customers understand if you need 10 minutes to come back to them.

### Escalation when the answer is unknown

- When you cannot answer a customer's question by phone, chat or email, do one or more of the following, as relevant, in this order:
  1. Contact the business owner through the agreed contact methods. If the owner is available, they will either answer the question or ask you to forward the customer to them. [L0404.009]
  2. If the owner is not immediately available, tell the customer you will get back to them shortly, take their contact details, and reply as soon as you can. [L0404.009]
  3. If the owner is not available and you need product information, first check the supplier's webpage. If the information is not there, call the supplier and ask. [L0404.009]
  4. Do not rush. Reply to the customer once you have the correct information, since a short delay of around 10 minutes is acceptable. [L0404.009]
- To find product information for a customer, the VA follows this order (Source A, undated):
  1. Search Google for the answer. [L1430.004]
  2. If the answer is not found, take the customer's question and contact details, and pass them to a sales rep contact number or email. [L1430.004]
  3. The sales rep then calls the customer back once the needed information is available. [L1430.004]

### Agent training and knowledge base

- Customer service agents are usually the customer's first contact with the company, so improving agent training is typically the first and most powerful step to raise overall satisfaction. [L0401.009]
- Build an internal knowledge base or wiki for agents containing a guide to the brand voice, canned responses for common scenarios such as angry customers and refund requests, and upselling scripts. [L0401.010]
- Support agents hear the most direct customer complaints, so ask the support team for their view on what causes low satisfaction. Their input on customer needs is one of the most useful sources for changing how support is delivered and for improving the wider purchase experience. [L0401.018]
- Check customer questions and contact requests by reviewing chat and phone activity during the first months of a new hire's training, and send corrections privately as needed. Watching the chat app is the simplest way to see the answers given to customers. This helps catch misspellings and rude replies before customers notice. (Older, 2021-22.) [L1396.064]

### Quality rubric

- A quality rubric for support replies defines the key elements a high-quality response must have and gives an objective framework for scoring response quality. Typical criteria are response time, alignment with company policy, brand tone and voice, plus any other elements the business considers essential. [L0401.011]
- Judge the rubric against the actual customer outcome too. A response can score well on tone (for example, playful humor) yet still fail to produce a clear, satisfying interaction. [L0401.011]

### Response times and KPIs

| Channel | Target | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Live chat, first response | Within 30 seconds (older, 2020) [L1111.124] | |
| Email, baseline | Reply within 24 hours; if there is no reply, follow up, because the email may have gone to spam or the wrong inbox [L0359.084] | |
| Email, staffed window | Set window such as 30 minutes (older, 2020) [L1111.124] | |
| Email, too slow | A reply in 5 business days is too slow for an active dropshipping student (Source D 2026) [L1452.009] | |
| Phone | Answer 95% of inbound calls [L1111.124] | |

- The sources give two email targets. Use 24 hours as the baseline rule for every support email and the trigger for a follow-up. Use the 30-minute window where a dedicated person covers the inbox during staffed hours. [L0359.084, L1111.124]
- Track customer support response times and set a target time for every channel, such as tickets, phone calls and live chat. (Older, 2021.) [L0962.128]
- Set KPIs for each support channel: chat response time, email response time and phone answer rate. Where phone support is part of the job, track the percentage of calls converted to sales. (Older, 2020.) [L1111.125]

## Support tone, soft skills and handling difficult customers

### Support mindset and tone

- Customer service drives both repeat purchases and five-star reviews. Reviews act as a trust factor that raises the website conversion rate, so service quality directly affects sales. Communication should always be quick, truthful and friendly, across phone, email, chat and social media. [L0404.017]
- Empathy is the most important skill in customer service (older advice, 2021-22). Understand the customer's situation from their side, listen fully, and reflect back what you heard before you act. [L0909.019]
- Stay friendly and patient, even with rude customers (older advice, 2021-22). Basic courtesy, such as not talking over the customer and not ignoring their message, matters more than any technique. [L0909.020]
- Greet every customer warmly, ask what problem you can solve for them, and build a genuine personal connection. Customers who feel cared for are more understanding when problems appear during the order. [L1472.002]
- Remember details from earlier conversations, such as names and past topics, and use them in later contacts. This familiarity matters most for repeat buyers. [L1472.003]
- Keep a consistently positive tone with every customer, because a competitor selling the same product is often only one click away. Service is what sets a store apart when the product and price are similar. [L1472.004]
- Be empathetic by imagining you are the customer waiting for a product that is four weeks late with no clear date. Frustration is natural in that situation, so acknowledge it in every reply. [L1472.011]
- Even when a delay is caused by a supplier, carrier or processing time outside your control, you remain responsible for solving it. Respond with empathy and focus on the solution. [L1472.005]
- Customers often accept a long wait or a problem as long as you communicate regularly and stay polite. Rudeness is the main thing that makes customers leave, not the problem itself. [L1472.013]
- Service that does not lead to a sale still has value, because it builds goodwill and a human connection. Listening to a customer who needs to talk can keep them loyal for future purchases. [L1472.012]
- Do not sell products you do not carry, but still listen to the customer and help where you can. Being a supportive point of contact can keep the customer loyal even when the sale does not happen. [L1472.061]
- Treat your customers with respect and aim to improve their lives, since the best dropshipping businesses excel at service. Customer relationships are where you can separate yourself from competitors. [L1480.028]

### Chat and proactive contact

- Staff may start chats with website visitors when they have time, but this is optional. [L0404.013]
- If a visitor does not reply to the first message, do not send a follow-up, so customers do not feel harassed. [L0404.013]

### Regional communication styles

- Customer service replies should match each market's communication style. Separate reply templates are needed even within the same language. [L0519.039]

| Market | Typical style | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| Germany | Often more direct, harder to satisfy on refunds | Expect firm refund expectations and answer directly. [L0519.039] |
| Switzerland | Very polite | Write German-language replies without the letter ß; use ss instead. [L1431.064] |
| Swiss German customers | More polite register than German customers | Do not rely on literal machine translation, which can sound disrespectful. [L1431.064] |

### Never guess, and admit what you don't know

- Never guess or make up answers to customer questions. Give information only once it has been confirmed through the owner or the supplier. [L0404.010]
- Never invent an answer to a product or technical question (older advice, 2021-22). If the customer receives wrong information and finds out after delivery, you will have to pay to fix the problem. [L0909.022]
- If you do not know a product detail, do not guess. Tell the customer you will check with the manufacturer and call back with accurate information, then use the answer to update your product page. [L0934.180]
- Admitting when you do not know an answer and following up with the correct information builds trust. Customers appreciate accurate information, and the owner gains a stronger knowledge base in the niche over time. [L1094.093]

Phone reply when you do not know the answer (Source A, 2023):

```
Good question, [customer name]. I don't know the answer at the moment, so I'll consult our team and return your call as quickly as possible. May I have your phone number and email address?
```
[L0934.179]

```
Use this reply on the phone when you do not know the answer to a customer's question. Replace each bracketed placeholder and keep the order of the steps:

That is a great question. I do not have the exact answer right now, but I would like to reach out to our partner at [brand or partner name] so I can get you the correct information. Can I get your name, phone number and email address? I will follow up with you as soon as I have the answer, because I do not want to give you incorrect information.
```
[L1094.092]

#### Handling a question you cannot answer (older advice, 2021-22)

1. Tell the customer you need to check the answer, and do not guess.
2. Offer a callback within a stated time, such as five or ten minutes, or put them on hold if the phone system allows it.
3. Check the answer with your supplier, by phone or on the supplier's website.
4. Call the customer back and give them the confirmed answer.

[L0909.024]

Holding reply:

```
Thanks for asking. I want to confirm that exactly before I answer, so you get accurate information. Could I call you back in five minutes?
```
[L0909.023]

### Voicemail and callbacks

- Sending callers to voicemail loses sales, because callers simply phone the next seller on their list. Customers have said they bought because someone answered the phone, so answered calls are a cheap sales safeguard. [L0337.006]
- Voicemail greeting (older advice, 2021-22):

```
Hello, you've reached [business name]. We are busy right now and cannot take your call immediately, and we don't want you to have to wait on hold. To use our callback service, leave your name and your contact details after the tone, and we will call you back as soon as we can. Thank you for your patience.
```
[L0909.008]

#### Handling a voicemail callback (older advice, 2021-22)

1. Receive the SMS or email notification that a message has been left.
2. Listen to the message and note the caller's name and what they need.
3. Call the customer back as soon as you are able to.

[L0909.009]

### When to call customers

- Avoid calling customers early in the morning. Use the evening and night hours instead, and in most countries keep calls before about 8 p.m. (older advice, 2021-22) [L0909.027]
- Evening callbacks work because customers are usually at home at that time and can actually talk. Calling after a day of work also fits a side-business owner's schedule (older advice, 2021-22). [L0909.028]

### Difficult and angry customers

- Do not return an angry caller's hostility with hostility, and do not block customers in anger. A single heated reaction can turn a fixable problem into a lost customer and a public complaint. [L1472.006]
- Angry customers often vent about problems in their own life, so their anger is rarely about the store itself. Stay calm, train yourself to keep your composure, and still follow your own process. [L1472.007]
- Some customers will stay unreasonable no matter how well you respond, and that is not your fault. As long as you complete your own steps correctly, their reaction does not change the correct response. [L1472.019]
- Do not take personal offense at customers who react badly to a sensible response. Document each step so you can show you handled the situation correctly. [L1472.020]

#### Handling objections that products ship from China

- Some customers object that products come from China. This is rare, and it can usually be handled by giving the tracking number and finding a solution with the customer. [L1347.035]

1. When a customer objects that the product ships from China, first send the tracking number, since customers often ask for it.
2. If they remain upset, point out that many everyday consumer electronics, such as iPhones, are also made or shipped from China.
3. If the problem is serious, offer a solution.

[L1347.038]

## Reply templates and scripts for pre-purchase questions

### Speed and first response before purchase

- Being the first store to answer a pre-purchase question often decides the sale. Fast responses are a direct sales lever, and speed and quality of service can beat competitors who sell the same product. [L0948.001]
- Replying within minutes can raise sales, because a quick answer to a product question can convert a visitor into a buyer. Check messages from your phone so questions are not left waiting. [L0661.049]
- Shoppers who call before buying to check stock or get an answer often choose the store that responds. Answering the phone can win sales that other stores lose. [L0966.094]
- Phone calls from prospective customers, such as asking whether an item is in stock, are a normal part of selling higher-priced products. Answer or return them as soon as possible. [L0835.103]
- Pre-purchase questions from website visitors typically arrive by phone, live chat or email. They are a daily task to automate or delegate. Post-purchase follow-up questions come through the same channels and need the same handling. [L0592.004]
- Shoppers fear buying online and then receiving no answer from customer service. Only promise fast customer service if you can actually reply quickly. [L1207.018]

### Answering known questions in chat

- When an answer is known, give it right away in the chat to close the sale. Shoppers who ask pre-purchase questions should receive a fast reply without extra effort from the store owner. [L0948.018]
- Example: a shopper asks how fast stickers ship, and the store replies "They ship within two to three days." Quick, specific shipping times answer purchase hesitation directly. [L0948.019]
- Most customer service questions are simple and concern delivery time, shipping time or discounts. Prepare clear answers to these first. [L0909.021] *(Older advice, 2021-2022.)*
- Pre-written answers can be stored in the live chat app, so customers get an immediate reply about a specific product, including shipping time and usage. This is useful when you expect repeated questions about one product. [L1428.002]
- Reply to a chat question you cannot answer yet with the following text, then send the answer as a follow-up once it is ready:

```
When a chat question comes in and you don't know the answer yet, respond right away by saying it's a good question, that you're looking into it, and that you'll reply as soon as possible. Once the answer is ready, send it as a follow-up.
```
[L0948.017]

### Handling a question you cannot answer yet

#### Standard procedure (phone or chat)

1. Receive a customer question you cannot answer immediately. [L0276.040]
2. Respond: "That's a great question. I want to make sure you get an accurate answer. May I have your name, email, and phone number?" [L0276.040]
3. Contact your supplier with the customer's exact question. [L0276.040]
4. Collect the supplier's answer. [L0276.040]
5. Reply to the customer with the accurate response. [L0276.040]
6. Update your product page with this information for future customers. [L0276.040]

#### Supplier-verified variant

1. Tell the customer you want to confirm the answer and get the correct information. [L0972.042]
2. Collect their name, email address and phone number if the question came by phone. [L0972.042]
3. Ask your supplier rep the question directly, stating the customer's needs and quantities. [L0972.042]
4. Send the verified answer to the customer. [L0972.042]
5. If the question is likely to come up again, add the answer to the product page as an FAQ or in the description. [L0972.042]

Use this reply when a customer asks a product question you cannot answer yet:

```
That's a great question, and I want to make sure I give you the correct answer. Could you please send me your name, email address and phone number? I will check directly with the manufacturer and get right back to you.
```
[L0972.043]

#### Product question not answerable from the product page

1. Tell the customer you do not have the answer right now, and take their name, phone number and email. [L0805.031]
2. Contact the supplier rep (or email the supplier) with the product model number and the customer's question. [L0805.031]
3. Call the customer back or reply with the answer. [L0805.031]
4. Add the answer to the product page so future customers see it. [L0805.031]

#### Older procedure (2020-2021)

Treat these as older advice. The steps remain valid, but the wording is dated.

Procedure, 2020 *(older)*:

1. Tell the customer that it is a great question and that you want to make sure you give the right answer. [L0852.108]
2. Collect the customer's name, phone number and email address. [L0852.108]
3. Contact the supplier to get the answer. [L0852.108]
4. Add the answer to your website, so future customers can find it. [L0852.108]
5. Reply to the customer with the correct information and try to close the sale. [L0852.108]

Procedure, 2021 *(older)*:

1. Respond promptly: "That's a great question. Let me get you the answer." [L0270.059]
2. Contact the supplier for the answer. [L0270.059]
3. Provide the supplier's answer to the customer. [L0270.059]
4. Capture that information and add it to the product page so future shoppers see the answer without asking. [L0270.059]

#### Principles for supplier questions

- Expect customer questions on products you did not know before. Ask the supplier for the answer, then add frequent questions to the product page. [L0806.083]
- Each store owner needs to build product knowledge in the niche. Questions from customers should be answered by checking with the supplier, then published on the product page. [L0805.032]
- Phone and support answers for product questions should follow a lesson script. A sales phone call should never end without a follow-up: the customer should be called back with an answer rather than left waiting. [L0971.078]

### Responding to pre-purchase hesitation

- Using fear, threats or crime statistics to push a purchase repels most buyers. Instead, let the buyer recognize the need, then show the product points they care about most, such as reliability and ease of installation. [L1366.068]

### FAQ building and product-page content

#### Building the FAQ

1. Answer every customer question by email or phone, then add that question and answer to the FAQ. [L0910.025]
2. Keep building the FAQ over the first months of the store. [L0910.025]
3. Make new customer service staff read and memorize the FAQ during onboarding, because these are the questions they will receive. [L0910.025]
4. Link customers to the FAQ so they can find answers without calling or emailing. [L0910.025]
5. Where possible, add the answer to the product description or to a staff note so the question does not come up again. [L0910.025]

#### What the FAQ page should cover

- The FAQ page should collect the questions customers ask repeatedly. Cover price guarantee, product guarantee, shipping policy, returns and support. If one visitor has a question, many others probably do too. [L1130.012]

#### Preparing support for a team

*The following two units describe the same procedure and are merged here.*

1. List the questions customers are likely to ask, both before and after purchase. [L1358.018, L1360.021]
2. Write a clear, polished answer for each question. [L1358.018, L1360.021]
3. Put the questions and answers into PDFs (compile them into a PDF document). [L1358.018, L1360.021]
4. Let the support team copy and paste the answers to customers. [L1358.018, L1360.021]

#### Turning questions into product-page content

- Turn customer questions into product page updates so future visitors find the answers without calling. [L0934.181]
- Product pages should give customers all information they need before buying, so the store reduces customer inquiries over time. [L0964.111]
- Write detailed FAQs on each product page for every recurring customer question, so the answer is available before the customer has to ask. [L1515.034]
- Write content that answers questions a buyer has before buying, such as whether to offer a phone number, and link those questions to your products. This keeps the blog focused on purchase decisions rather than general interest. [L0382.051]

### B2B and wholesale discount requests

- Standard reply for a B2B or wholesale buyer who wants a discount: create a multi-use discount code named after the business, give it only to that buyer, and set the percent off as the B2B price. [L0472.054]

Reply template:

```
Thank you for your question. That's a great question, and I want to make sure I give you the correct answer. Could you please send me your name, email address and phone number? I will look into this and get back to you with the answer as soon as I have it.
```
[L0472.077]

### MAP discount requests

Procedure for customers who request a discount on products with strict MAP policies:

1. Acknowledge their request professionally. [L0251.036]
2. Explain that the price is set by the manufacturer to protect brand value and that this is industry-wide. [L0251.036]
3. Offer alternative value: same-day shipping if possible, expedited service, or reference other benefits. [L0251.036]
4. If you cannot offer discounts or special terms, maintain confidence in the price and emphasize service quality and expertise. [L0251.036]

### Price-match answers

The rules below apply together. Use the row that matches the situation.

| Situation | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Customer finds a lower price from an unauthorized seller | A price-match guarantee only works against the MAP. Explain that the seller violates the supplier's policy and cannot be trusted to ship the product. A discount that matches what a coupon code already gives can still be offered. [L0964.104] | L0964.104 (2023) |
| Working with a non-MAP supplier | Do not offer a price-match guarantee. [L0969.040] *(Older, 2022.)* | L0969.040 |
| You sell above MAP | Do not have a price-match policy. [L0969.040] *(Older, 2022.)* | L0969.040 |
| A supplier sells below MAP on another platform (for example Wayfair) and refuses to act, and that supplier makes up most of the business | Remove the price-match policy. [L0969.041] *(Older, 2022.)* | L0969.041 |

### Expired promotions

- Honor a legitimately expired promotion when the customer has a real reason for missing it. Decline expired codes requested from old archives or without a reason. [L0834.088] *(Older, 2021.)*

## Order status, tracking and delivery inquiries

### Why tracking and order status matter

- Order tracking systems prevent orders from disappearing due to supplier delays, lost emails in inbox, or operational oversights. This becomes critical as transaction volume grows and when working with new suppliers whose reliability is unproven. [L0292.001]
- Tracking questions are the most frequent support request, so prepare standard replies for the common cases: order not shipped yet, order shipped, shipped but not received, and shipped with an angry customer. [L0405.001]
- Most customer calls are about legitimacy, order status and stock. Detailed product pages, an FAQ and automated tracking emails remove most of these questions. (2021, older advice) [L1112.033]
- An order tracking tool can send tracking information to customers automatically after shipment, which reduces "where is my order" contacts. (2021, older advice) [L1112.034]
- Automatic shipment updates sent through a tracking app reduce customer inquiries about order status. [L0966.093]

### Order status check before every reply

1. Look up the order status in the store admin and fulfillment system before replying to any tracking question. [L0405.033]
2. If the order is not shipped yet, send the not-shipped reply: it is being processed, a tracking email follows once it ships, and orders take about 10-20 days after shipping. [L0405.033]
3. If the order is shipped and the customer is asking about tracking, send the shipped reply with the shipping date, the 3-5 business day tracking delay, the tracking link and a screenshot of the current status. [L0405.033]
4. If the order is shipped and the customer says they got no confirmation emails, send the junk/spam version of the shipped reply and ask them to check junk and spam first. [L0405.033]
5. If the order is shipped but the customer is angry, send the angry reply with the current status, take responsibility for delivery and promise a free reship or full refund if the parcel is lost in transit. [L0405.033]
6. If the parcel is delivered and the customer wants a refund, offer a free reship first unless they ask for a refund on first contact, in which case process the refund without pushing a reship. [L0405.033]
7. If the tracking cannot be found at all and the parcel appears lost, send the lost-order refund reply and confirm the refund is already initiated. [L0405.033]

### Delivery times: processing and transit

Sources give different values for the same stages. Each value applies to the case listed.

| Stage | Value | When it applies | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dispatch of in-stock orders from the warehouse | Within 5 business days from the order date | Warehouse with in-stock items | [L0145.009] |
| Processing before a dropshipped order ships | About 4 to 7 days | Dropshipping store, order not yet shipped; the value to quote in the AI responder and in the not-shipped replies | [L0477.009, L0477.040, L1297.039] |
| Processing example | About 3 days before shipment (Illinois to Philadelphia example) | Single supplier case used to show processing and transit must be separated | [L1472.064] |
| Physical product shipping for dropshipping | 5 to 14 days | General shipping range for physical dropshipped products | [L0911.001] |
| International transit | 10-20 days after shipping (calendar basis) | Used in the not-shipped and shipped templates that say "after shipping" | [L0405.002, L0405.008, L0405.021, L0911.005] |
| International transit | 10-20 business days after processing | Used in the shipped templates that say "after processing" | [L0405.009, L0405.022, L0911.006] |
| Transit to final address | 10 to 20 days from the shipping date | Used in the not-shipped reply that cites the shipping date | [L0911.005] |

- Use one basis for transit time in every template, preferably business days, so customers do not receive conflicting estimates. [L0405.035]
- Present delivery timelines as estimates, and separate supplier processing time from carrier transit time, so a deadline is not promised that cannot be met. When processing takes about 3 days before a shipment from Illinois to Philadelphia, a 5-business-day deadline cannot be guaranteed, so say that upfront. [L1472.064]
- Set expectations with the customer before they become frustrated. [L0911.007]
- Give customers a rough delivery window once a sale is made, such as one to two weeks, based on the parcel's position in the shipping process (for example, cleared customs and on its way), and update it when possible. [L1315.007]

### Tracking numbers and tracking updates

| Stage | Value | When it applies | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| First tracking information appears | Within 24 hours of shipment, sent to the checkout email | Store that sends tracking itself at dispatch | [L0145.009] |
| First tracking information appears | Within 3-5 business days of shipping | Standard Source C replies, shipped and junk/spam versions | [L0405.002, L0405.009, L0405.010, L0405.022, L0405.023] |
| First tracking information appears | 3 to 5 days after shipping (no business-day qualifier) | Shipped reply variant | [L0911.006, L0911.007] |
| Tracking escalation | If no tracking after six business days, contact the support address | Escalation rule in the in-stock template | [L0145.009] |

- Tracking numbers often do not update until the parcel is close to its destination, so customers should be warned not to panic when the status stays unchanged for a while. [L0405.003]
- The tracking number does not show precise updates until the parcel is close to its destination; state this in every shipped reply. [L0405.009, L0405.010, L0405.022, L0911.006]
- Check the status yourself on a public tracking website first, then send the customer a screenshot of the page. [L0911.008]
- Give customers the tracking number when they ask for it, because PayPal and other payment providers may ask for it as proof of shipment. [L1347.034]

#### Tracking tools and apps

| Tool | What it does | Notes | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shopify built-in shipping notifications | Sends tracking numbers entered directly in Shopify to customers | Can replace AfterShip to save its monthly cost (2024) | [L0666.013] |
| AfterShip | Sends automatic updates at each carrier status change (in transit to a city, arriving soon, out for delivery, delivery attempt missed) | Enter a tracking number once; prevents many support contacts; more customization than built-in notifications | [L0666.013, L1515.035] |
| Track123 | Order tracking page app | Every store should have a tracking page | [L1299.024] |
| Track123 configuration | Updates order emails automatically and links the tracking page in the store menu | Lets customers check their order at any time | [L1299.025] |
| CJ Dropshipping app | Linked to Shopify, sends an email with tracking information once a tracking number is generated | Automatic customer email at tracking generation | [L1347.033] |
| Public tracking website (e.g. 17track) | Customer enters tracking number to see package location | Used as the source for screenshots and tracking links | [L0911.008, L0405.022, L0405.023] |

- A tracking page serves existing customers who want to follow their parcel. It also gives prospects a sign that the business provides real tracking numbers, which adds credibility before they buy. [L1130.010]

### Confirmation emails and spam checks

- Confirmation emails for order, shipping and delivery can land in the junk or spam folder, so when a customer says they received nothing, ask them to check those folders first. [L0405.004]
- Automated emails sent by a store or its platform can land in the spam folder. Before reporting a missing confirmation or account email, search both the main inbox and the spam folder for the sender's name. (2025) [L0807.052]
- If support emails seem missing, check the spam folder first, since replies may land there. If you are in the mentor program, also post in the member Slack channel to get attention faster. [L0941.085]

- The standard response to a delivery complaint takes responsibility for the shipment, apologizes for the inconvenience, and then offers a free reship or full refund if the package is lost in transit. [L0405.006]

### Guarantees and refund policy

- A guarantee covering every package should be stated to customers: if a parcel is lost in transit, they may choose a full refund or a free reship, and the store can add a store credit on top of the reship. [L0405.005]
- The default refund policy is that a customer can get either a free reship or a full refund. The preferred first offer is a free reship, but if the customer asks for a refund on first contact, give the refund without pushing a reship. [L0405.007]

### Lost parcels and refunds

- For lost shipments, send the tracking information that shows the item was lost, then keep the customer updated on replacements, when they ship and when they arrive. Most customers only panic when they are not kept informed. (2020, older advice) [L0852.109, L0852.125]
- If the fulfillment platform can no longer track an order and the package is considered lost, issue a full refund and tell the customer it has already been initiated. Do not wait for the customer to ask for a replacement before refunding. [L0911.017]

### Late delivery and delay responses

- When a customer complains about a late delivery, first find the cause before deciding on a remedy. Possible causes are outdated product page delivery times, slow order submission, or a supplier that took longer than usual, and each has a different fix. (2021, older advice) [L0853.018]
- If a supplier never ships a paid order and the customer becomes upset, a partial refund such as 5% combined with a firm delivery date can settle the situation. The exact remedy depends on what went wrong. (2021, older advice) [L0853.019]
- For delivery questions, promise only what the supplier and carrier can deliver. Contact the store team when a customer needs a quote instead of guessing a price. (2022, older advice) [L1281.118]

### Delivery promises and Christmas

- Setting delivery times that are too short for the real transit time is over-promising. Shorter estimates may raise conversion, but customers who receive the parcel later than promised lead to complaints and chargebacks. Set the estimate to what the fulfillment center can reliably meet and improve it as the setup matures. [L1327.026]
