### Origin and trust after purchase

- Customers who do not know their parcel is shipping from China become more anxious when they discover it later, so hiding origin on tracking and emails protects trust after the purchase. [L1315.006]

### Tracking from day one

- For dropshipping with physical products, shipping can take 5 to 14 days, so customers will often ask where their order is. Plan customer service for these tracking questions from the start. [L0911.001]

## Order changes, cancellations and out-of-stock handling

### Order states and what can still change

| Order state | Change possible? | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Not yet processed by fulfillment, not shipped | Quantity, variant, items and shipping details can usually still be changed, and cancellation is possible | Make the change or cancel now |
| Processed by fulfillment, in transit or shipped | Changes are usually impossible | Offer the replacement or return route for the situation |

[L0405.014, L0405.016, L0405.018, L0911.020]

Once an order has been processed by fulfillment, changes to quantity, variant, items or shipping details are usually impossible. The requested change should still be made as soon as possible if it is still allowed. [L0405.014]

### Payment authorisation and capture timing

#### Order flow from authorisation to tracking

1. The customer places the order and receives a confirmation email with a credit card pre-authorisation. [L0145.007]
2. Supplier stock is verified automatically. [L0145.007]
3. If the item is unavailable or on backorder, the pre-authorisation is voided and the customer is notified by email immediately. [L0145.007]
4. If the item is available, charges are processed and the order is submitted for shipment within 5 business days. [L0145.007]
5. Tracking information is emailed within 24 hours of shipment. [L0145.007]
6. If tracking has not been received within 6 business days, the customer may contact orders support. [L0145.007]

#### Order confirmation email

```
Order confirmation emails send immediately upon checkout, indicating your order is in our system and your card is pre-authorized. We immediately contact suppliers to verify stock availability. Backordered or unavailable items trigger authorization reversal and email notification to you. Items available for shipment within 5 business days proceed through charge processing and dispatch to the warehouse.
```
[L0145.008]

#### Capture only after stock is confirmed (older advice, 2021)

Process orders as follows: pre-authorise the payment when the order comes in but do not charge yet. Confirm the items are in stock with the supplier, then process the charge. If an item is out of stock, contact the customer with the expected wait time and charge only if they still want it. [L1112.035]

This 2021 advice is older. It matches the 2025-era flow above, which also charges only after availability is confirmed. [L1112.035, L0145.007]

If a customer orders while a supplier stock is unfinished, do not forward the order until stock is confirmed. Verify stock, then capture payment. [L0964.110]

### Unconfirmable orders

#### Cancelling an order that cannot be confirmed

1. Call the number on the order and email the customer about the attempts. [L1285.069]
2. If there is still no response before processing, cancel the order. [L1285.069]
3. Send a cancellation email that lists the email and call dates and explains that the order was cancelled. [L1285.069]
4. Consider adjusting product pricing in the meantime. [L1285.069]

```
Hi [Customer name], we contacted you by email on [dates] and called you on [dates] about your order [order number]. We did not hear back before we needed to process it, so unfortunately we have cancelled the order. If you still want the product, please reply or order again through our store.
```

### Cancellations before shipment

#### Cancelling an order that has not shipped

1. Open the order on the fulfillment platform and check whether it has shipped. [L0911.020]
2. If it has not shipped, cancel it on the fulfillment platform and refund the customer's payment. [L0911.020]
3. Confirm to the customer that the order is cancelled and that the refund will be credited to their credit card within 5 to 7 business days. [L0911.020]
4. If it has already shipped, do not promise a cancellation. State the shipping date and that the order is in transit. [L0911.020]
5. Explain that the store's refund and returns policy can be used once the order is delivered, and link the refund and returns policy page. [L0911.020]

- Quote 5 to 7 business days to the customer, depending on the bank. [L0405.017, L0911.013, L0405.029, L0911.020]
- Shopify's "Cancel and refund" screen may show up to 10 days. Tell the customer that timeframe, and expect refunds to usually arrive faster than the stated maximum. [L0972.040]

Use the 5 to 7 business day figure in customer messages. Use the Shopify figure as the outer limit. [L0405.017, L0972.040]

#### Cancelling an unshipped order in Shopify

1. Open the order in Shopify Orders. [L0972.040]
2. Click Cancel and refund. [L0972.040]
3. Check the refund timeframe Shopify displays, which may say up to 10 days, and tell the customer about that timeframe. [L0972.040]
4. Expect refunds to usually arrive faster than the stated maximum. [L0972.040]

Refunds are credited only to the original credit card used for the purchase. [L0145.011]

#### Do not promise cancellation after shipping

Do not promise to cancel an order after it has shipped. Offer the store's return or refund policy instead, which the customer can use after delivery. Cancellation promises for shipped orders lead to disputes and chargebacks. [L0911.015]

#### Cancellation fee model (differs from the return-policy model)

```
Cancellations initiated after 48 hours incur a $20 administrative fee regardless of whether the order has shipped. If already shipped, the buyer covers return postage. Refunds are credited only to the original credit card used for the purchase.
```
[L0145.011]

Two models are documented:
- Fee model: a $20 administrative fee for cancellations after 48 hours, shipped or not. For shipped orders, the buyer pays return postage. [L0145.011]
- Return-policy model: no cancellation once shipped; the customer starts a return after delivery under the store's refund and returns policy. [L0405.018, L0911.014]

The sources do not say which model is preferred. Use the one that matches the store's written policy, and state it the same way in every reply.

### Asking why customers cancel

- When a customer cancels, ask the real reason instead of only refunding. The answer can reveal product, price or experience barriers that affect conversion. [L1016.068]
- Handle cancelled orders as a learning opportunity:
  1. Contact the customer and ask why they cancelled. [L1357.040]
  2. If they bought from a different retailer, ask what you could do better and use that to win the next sale. [L1357.040]
  3. If they bought from a brand you do not carry, contact that brand as a possible new supplier. [L1357.040]
- After a cancellation, work in this order:
  1. Look for ways to improve the customer experience so the customer is more likely to return. [L0920.030]
  2. Find new suppliers so you can fill future orders for that product. [L0920.030]
- Without an automated cancellation system (older advice, 2020), handle cancellation and refund requests manually and respond quickly. Offer an updated ship date and alternatives before issuing a refund. [L1277.096]

### Out-of-stock: listing and customer notice

#### Keep out-of-stock products visible (older advice, 2022)

Do not remove out-of-stock products from the store. Either label them as out of stock with an expected availability date, or accept orders if you are willing to backorder and notify customers of the timeline. [L0249.070]

#### Stock problem on an existing order

Suppliers sometimes run out of stock of products that are still listed for sale. When a customer orders such a product, the order must go through the out-of-stock process rather than being shipped late without notice. [L1119.011]

#### Early warning email (2023)

```
Thanks for placing your order. Our warehouse confirmed that this product is on backorder. The next delivery lands on [date], and we could dispatch the item to you on [date]. If you'd rather keep the order open, be aware that all online sellers source [brand]'s products from the same place, so the backorder applies at other shops too. If you need the product sooner, we suggest [similar product], which is comparable because [reason], with a price gap of [amount]. You can: 1) wait for the item on [date], 2) switch to [similar product], or 3) cancel the order.
```
[L0964.103]

Send this email so the customer has time to consider before replying. [L0964.103]

### Out-of-stock: handling the order

#### Standard out-of-stock handling

1. Ask the supplier when the product will be available again. Also ask whether a faster special order is possible and whether it costs extra. [L1119.009]
2. Contact the customer as soon as possible. Tell them the product is not immediately available and how long the wait will be, then ask whether they are willing to wait. [L1119.009]
3. If the customer is undecided about waiting, offer an authorised discount by refund if they wait. [L1119.009]
4. If the customer cannot wait, look for a similar product that is in stock and suits their needs. If needed to close the sale, offer an authorised discount on the similar product. [L1119.009]
5. If the customer will neither wait nor accept a similar product, cancel the order in Shopify. If payment was already captured, refund it. [L1119.009]
6. If the customer is willing to wait, confirm with the supplier that you want to backorder the product, and ask the supplier to ship immediately once the product is back in stock. [L1119.009]
7. If the supplier requires partial or full payment to place a backorder, consult the business owner and get authorisation before confirming any payment. [L1119.009]
8. Once a backorder is placed, email the customer to confirm the order is on backorder and give the expected arrival date. [L1119.009]

#### No response to an unavailable-item email

1. If a customer does not answer emails about an unavailable item, try calling and texting. [L0857.041]
2. If there is still no reply and the item is unavailable, cancel and refund. [L0857.041]

#### Offering alternatives: two price values

- Procedure from 2025: when an item is out of stock with no clear delivery date:
  1. Tell the customer about the stock problem. [L0857.040]
  2. Offer similar alternatives at about the same price. Example: between 800 and 1,200 dollars for a 1,000 dollar order. [L0857.040]
  3. If the customer wants a more expensive available item, send a Shopify draft order for the difference. [L0857.040]
  4. If the customer declines, cancel the order and refund it. [L0857.040]
- Rule for supplier failures: offer 2 or 3 alternative products that match the original in size, color, quality and price and are in stock and ready to ship now. Ask whether they want to swap their order for one of them. [L1407.007]

Use the 800 to 1,200 band in the 2025 procedure when the customer's order value is the reference. Use the "match size, color, quality and price" standard when the customer must receive a like-for-like product. [L0857.040, L1407.007]

#### Supplier cannot fill the order

```
Hi {customer name}, I am following up about your order {order number}. We recently ran into a problem: our supplier is currently out of stock on this product and has no estimated restock date, [or: our supplier is not responding to us and we are unable to fulfill this order for this specific product]. We would like to offer you two or three alternative products that are similar in size, color, quality and price and that are in stock and ready to ship right away: {alternative product 1}, {alternative product 2}, {alternative product 3}. Would you be willing to swap your order for one of these in-stock items? Please reply with your choice and we will ship it to you as soon as possible.
```
[L1407.006]

Orders placed before you learned of a supplier problem are the first ones to fix. Those customers are already waiting and can be offered a swap. [L1407.008]

#### Supplier stock and payment on backorder

- Do not confirm any supplier payment for a backorder without the business owner's authorisation. [L1119.009]
- Discounts must be authorised by the business owner. [L1119.010]

### Discounts, partial refunds and extra payment

- Only offer discounts that have been authorised by the business owner. A discount for waiting can be given as a refund, and a discount for a similar product can be used to close the sale. [L1119.010]
- To ask a customer for extra payment (for example, the price difference on an upgrade):
  1. Create a draft order in Shopify with the amount you need. [L0857.042]
  2. Send it to the customer from Shopify so they can pay by the link. [L0857.042]
- Offer the 50% OFF replacement purchase only through the discount link used in the template for in-transit orders. [L0405.028, L0405.016]

### Product test orders and pre-order follow-up

When an order came from a short product test, tell the customer directly. Offer a pre-order option so they can keep the item. The following email is the 2025-26 template for that case.

```
Subject: Thank you for your order - important update about [Product name]

Hi [Customer name],

Thank you very much for your order of [Product name] (order number [Order number]). We really appreciate your trust in us.

We need to tell you something important: this order was part of a short product test to find out whether the product sells before we buy it in larger quantities. Your payment of [Order amount] will be refunded in full to your original payment method. You should see the refund within [Refund timeframe].

If you would still like to receive this product, please reply to this email and tell us. We will then place you on a pre-order list, and the expected delivery is around [Expected delivery window]. You will be the first to know if anything changes, and you can cancel at any time before shipping.

Thank you for your patience and understanding.

Best regards,
[Your name]
[Store name]
[Support email]
```
[L1017.029]

### Gifts for delayed orders

- Gifts from Amazon: do not ship free gift items directly from Amazon to the customer, because the Amazon origin is visible. Have the items shipped to yourself, repackage them, and include a note for the customer. [L0972.041]
- When a product is out of stock but already ordered, a gift of a different slow-selling design keeps the customer happy until the stock arrives. Once the stock comes in, resend the item the customer originally bought. [L1439.032]

## Backorders, made-to-order items and shipping-delay communication

### Setting expectations before the sale

- Keep accepting orders for an out-of-stock item whose restock is a few weeks away, and add a note at the top of the product description with the estimated restock date. [L0247.096]
- Put delayed-shipping information prominently in the product description, not only in checkout. State assembly requirements, shipping duration and installation responsibility upfront. [L0270.034]
- Tell customers the exact date an out-of-stock product will be back, both on the product page and right after the order. Customers accept a wait when they know what is happening and are far less likely to email later asking where the product is. [L0942.014]
- A customer whose item is delayed should be told on the website and by email that the item is backordered, with the expected ship date. *(Older advice, 2020.)* [L0468.144]
- When a product is backordered, show the expected date on the product page and offer a deposit option so customers can order now. *(Older advice, 2019.)* [L1069.086]
- Make the lead time visible before checkout, and confirm it by email after the order. The risk of a chargeback or complaint rises when a customer does not know a product is built to order. [L0965.071]
- Be transparent with customers and suppliers about production and delivery lead times, because customers often expect immediate fulfilment that production cannot provide. Communicate realistic timelines from the start. [L1438.032]
- Customers who order unique products they cannot find locally usually accept a shipping delay of up to about two weeks. Their tolerance is much lower for products needed for a fixed occasion. [L0766.009]
- Products must be delivered before the promised date to avoid chargebacks. Avoid selling products tied to fixed dates unless delivery is guaranteed in time. [L1184.050]
- Avoid supplier routes with three- to five-week shipping, because long shipping times caused many refunds. [L1108.031]
- Avoid launching during holidays that delay shipping. Late orders lead to complaints and payment disputes, which can put a Stripe account and a Facebook account at risk. [L1127.035]

### Confirmation emails and made-to-order follow-up

Follow-up procedure for made-to-order sales:

1. After the order is placed, contact the customer by phone or email to thank them.
2. Confirm that the product is made to order.
3. State the estimated manufacturing and delivery time.
4. Check that the customer understands and accepts the lead time.

[L0806.081]

Email the customer after the sale to confirm the lead time before the order goes to the supplier, so the customer is not surprised by a delay. [L0856.083]

Thank you for your order. You should have received your order confirmation already. We just want to confirm that this product is made to order, and the estimated delivery is [ETA]. Please reply to confirm you are aware of this.
```

Complaints about delayed shipping should be answered with the lead time. If a supplier delays the order, inform the customer proactively before the shipment date. [L0856.086]

Keep customers informed about their order at all times. Shopify's automated emails cover much of this, but you must contact the customer directly in many cases. [L1119.008]

### Backorders: first contact, escalation and revised dates

Escalation procedure when a backordered product has caused problems:

1. Update the product page with a notice above the Add to Cart button that states the backorder and the expected date.
2. Send a confirmation email right after each purchase and ask the customer to confirm that they are willing to wait.
3. Stop paid ads for backordered products.
4. Restructure the store so the most profitable in-stock products appear first.
5. Run only a small, tight Google Shopping campaign with the best-margin in-stock products until inventory is no longer a problem.
6. Keep looking for and following up on new supplier approvals in the meantime.
7. When stock returns, remove the notices and follow-up emails, restore ad spend on the other products, and rebuild the best sellers.

[L0359.081]

Procedure when a customer's backorder has a slipped supplier date:

1. Call each customer who placed the order first.
2. If the customer does not answer, leave a voicemail and say an email will follow.
3. Explain the new ship date and the reason, and offer to cancel the order or keep it.
4. If the customer keeps the order, process it when stock arrives; that customer is first on the list.
5. Send the follow-up email to everyone, even those who were reached by phone.
6. Do not cancel all orders without first trying to keep them.

[L0359.082]

2. When a supplier reports a backorder, contact the customer with the expected ship date.
3. Ask whether the customer is willing to wait for the exact product, and optionally offer a small discount (for example 5 percent) for waiting.
4. If the customer will not wait, offer the closest in-stock alternative that can ship within 48 hours.
5. If the customer declines both options, refund the payment.

```
Hi [CUSTOMER NAME], this is [YOUR NAME] from [STORE NAME]. We see you just placed an order for [PRODUCT NAME]. This product is currently backordered, and I'm sorry about that. It's going to be back in stock on [ETA DATE]. If it's about [TIME UNTIL STOCK], we can ship it to you first out the door when the shipment comes in. Would you be willing to wait? If the wait is longer, the earliest date it can ship is [SHIP DATE], and we would make you the same offer then. Please know this ETA is the same no matter where you order this product, because it applies to every seller. If you need it sooner, we have a similar product, [ALTERNATIVE PRODUCT NAME], that can be shipped within 24 to 48 hours with a [PARTIAL REFUND AMOUNT] partial refund. If you'd rather keep your order, we'll make sure you get updates and ship it as soon as possible. Which option would you like?
```

[L0852.034]

- For long backorders, you can leave the card uncharged until the product is ready and ask whether the customer wants to wait. Customers generally accept this when they are informed. [L0942.015]
- If the payment is only pre-authorized, there is nothing to refund when the customer declines. If it is already captured, refund the full amount right away. [L0468.139, L0468.138]
- Customer communication is key, and it is what separates a decent store from a great one. Keep customers informed about delays, replacements, ship dates and arrival dates. *(Older advice, 2020.)* [L0852.107]
- When delivery is delayed, keep the customer updated with each revised estimated arrival date. You can add a helpful extra, such as an installation video or a related article, in a postscript. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0968.098]
- Shipping delay communication: be proactive, give regular status updates, explain that the expected date is the same for everyone, and offer a similar in-stock product as a replacement if possible. A free gift is a nice extra, not a substitute for clear communication. *(Older advice, 2022.)* [L0969.038]
- Selling without stock and leaving customers unaware leads to angry follow-up messages after two weeks. Tell customers about the delay automatically at the time of ordering. [L0492.040]
- When a customer will not wait for an out-of-stock product, offer a different design from the slow-selling stock as a gift. Most customers accepted this and waited for their full order. [L0492.039]
- If customers ask about delayed delivery, reply promptly and explain the situation, such as high demand after a viral video or shipping slowdowns. Customers who receive a timely explanation are often understanding. [L1444.049]
- Send proactive updates about delays before customers complain, for example a short email saying the order is still late and you are monitoring it. Proactive communication prevents most anger. [L1472.008]
- Keep the customer informed at every step when delays occur, and address concerns before the customer gets angry. Frequent, honest communication reduces the number of complaints even when the delay is unavoidable. [L1472.010]

Quick update email for an order that the supplier is taking longer to process:

```
Subject: Quick update on your order {order_number}

Hi {customer_name},

I wanted to give you a quick update on your order for {product_name}. Our supplier is taking longer than expected to process it, and I am actively monitoring the shipment. I will send you your next update by {next_update_date}.

Thank you for your patience and understanding. If you have any questions in the meantime, just reply to this email.

{your_name}
{store_name}
```

[L1472.009]

### Out-of-stock and delay notices

Handling out-of-stock items or long shipping times:

1. Send a confirmation email as soon as the problem is known, with a clear apology.
2. State the realistic shipping time, which in the example was two to three weeks.
3. Offer an immediate refund if the customer does not want to wait.
4. Answer all customer messages promptly and keep the tone respectful and honest.

[L0519.036]

Informing customers about a long shipping time up front in the operator's German market led to almost no refunds. Staying silent while customers expected fast shipping led to angry emails, refund requests and ultimately the store being shut down. [L0519.037]

Out-of-stock update email (the example gives a delivery window of 2 to 3 weeks):

```
Subject: Update on your order [Order number]

Hi [First name],

Thank you for your order of [Product name]. We just found out that this item is currently out of stock, and we are sorry for the inconvenience. Your order is expected to arrive within 2 to 3 weeks. If you would prefer not to wait, reply to this email and we will refund your payment right away.

Warm regards,
[Store name] Customer Care
```

[L0519.038]

Delay email that offers two choices, a full refund or a wait of about 15 days:

```
Subject: Your order is delayed

Thank you very much for your order. Due to huge demand we are currently out of stock, and we are very sorry for the delay. You have two options: you can request a full refund, or you can wait about 15 days for your order to arrive. Simply reply to this email with your choice, and we will take care of it immediately. Thank you for your patience and for choosing [BRAND NAME].
```

[L0492.038]

Note on the wait windows: the 15-day window in the email above and the 2 to 3 weeks in the other out-of-stock notices come from different stores. Use the realistic date from your supplier in every case.

Digital product delay email for a short fulfilment-system delay:

```
Subject: Thank you for your order

Hi [FIRST NAME],

Thank you very much for your order of [PRODUCT NAME]. We are currently experiencing a short delay in our fulfilment system, and we apologise for the wait. Your digital guide will be sent to [CUSTOMER EMAIL] within two to three days, and sooner if possible. Thank you for your patience, we hope you enjoy it.

Kind regards,
[SHOP NAME] Team
```

[L1131.064]

A seller scaled a mini-winner product last year. The supplier could not ship on time because a flammable lighter item was held in customs, leaving nearly 200 orders unshipped and forcing resends until the third attempt. The seller emailed every customer to say the delivery was delayed, not a scam, and the delivery took nearly six weeks, but only two chargebacks occurred. [L0352.023]

Shipping delays from slow suppliers such as AliExpress are manageable in the early stage if you communicate actively with customers. Regular back-and-forth emails keep most buyers patient. Note that the same long routes were also linked to many refunds, so this applies to early-stage stores with active messaging, not to routes with three- to five-week shipping. [L0352.024, L1108.031]

### Made-to-order lead-time changes and compensation

Handling a made-to-order product whose lead time grows (for example from 4 to 6 weeks to 10 to 12 weeks) and customers cancel. *(Older advice, 2021.)*

1. Show the current lead time on the product page.
2. Tell affected customers the delay comes from the supplier's warehouse inventory, so cancelling and ordering elsewhere gives the same wait.
3. Offer a gift that costs under 100 dollars but has high perceived value to the customer, to keep the order.
4. If there is no suitable gift, offer a partial refund of about 100 dollars to the original card.

[L1279.091]

Handling a made-to-order collection on the store. *(Older advice, 2022.)*

1. Create a separate collection called Made to Order, or custom made, for these products.
2. Keep the products also in the main collections.
3. Show the lead time next to add-to-cart and send the follow-up confirmation after purchase.

[L1281.081]

Compensation options by situation:

| Situation | Option | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Customer declines a backorder but payment is still uncaptured | Nothing to refund; offer a 48-hour alternative | [L0468.138, L0468.139] |
| Customer waits for an exact product | Optional discount, for example 5 percent | [L0468.138] |
| Customer will not wait for an out-of-stock design | Gift from the slow-selling stock | [L0492.039] |
| Lead time grows and customer cancels | Gift under 100 dollars, or partial refund of about 100 dollars if no suitable gift | [L1279.091] |
| Late Q4 order | 50 percent refund or another gift | [L1220.015] |
| Alternative product can ship sooner | Partial refund amount to the customer | [L0852.034] |

### Split shipments and multiple sources

- When one order ships from two warehouses, send an automated email through Klaviyo after the order is placed. Say that one item is in stock closer to the customer, and include tracking for the item that ships first. [L0524.029]
- A split order from two suppliers ships as two parcels, which raises shipping cost compared with one supplier shipping the same items together. Accept this cost or consolidate the catalogue to one fulfilment source. [L0524.030]

### Carriers and payment delays

- For a delayed freight delivery, check the shipping company's online reviews before deciding whether to keep using it. Note expected delivery times on the shipping policy page. One-off delays are not a reason to change carrier. *(2023.)* [L0964.105]
- For an order paid by PayPal e-check, the payment may take two to three weeks to clear or may not clear at all. Tell the customer the order will ship when the e-check clears. *(2023.)* [L0964.106]

### Supplier slowdowns, seasonal peaks and Q4 cutoffs

- During a supplier slowdown such as Chinese New Year, some organic orders still come in, so customers should be told in advance about expected delays. This prevents refund requests caused by silence about shipping times. [L0780.045]
- Procedure for a product that goes viral a few days before Christmas:

1. If a product goes viral a few days before Christmas and customers place orders unlikely to arrive by the holiday, accept the orders.
2. Send follow-up emails to every customer confirming their order and shipping timeline.
3. Update them throughout fulfillment with tracking.
4. Even if products arrive after December 25, consistent communication reduces chargebacks and improves customer satisfaction.

[L0309.036]

- In Q4, customers who buy about 5 days before Christmas hoping for delivery in time often file chargebacks when the product arrives late. This is a major Q4 risk for dropshipping stores. [L1220.014]
- Procedure for setting a Q4 cutoff and handling late orders:

1. Work out the last order date that still delivers before Christmas, based on supplier and shipping times.
2. State the delivery risk clearly on the store and in emails.
3. If an order will arrive late, email the customer early and explain the plan.
4. Offer a compensation option such as a 50% refund or another gift.
5. Use this plan to avoid chargebacks.

[L1220.015]

Where the two Q4 sources differ: the viral-product procedure accepts late orders and relies on communication after December 25, while the cutoff procedure sets a last order date based on supplier and shipping times. Use the viral procedure for unplanned demand spikes close to the holiday, and the cutoff procedure for planned Christmas promotions. [L0309.036, L1220.015]

### Long backorders and cash

A seven-figure store with about 3 million dollars in annual sales handled 300 to 500 orders per month. COVID pushed orders to about 1,000 per month, and many orders went on backorder. The store saved about 500 to 700 of those customers by asking them to wait, but the backorders stretched for months while normal costs and owner pay continued. Customers grew tired of waiting and asked for refunds, and the owner realized the account might not cover both supplier bills and refunds, so the owner asked for help in a panic. *(Older advice, 2021-2022.)* [L1200.023]

## Writing shipping, returns, refund and warranty policies

### Before you start: supplier terms and policy basis

- Base the store's return policy on each supplier's return policy. If a supplier allows 30-day free returns, the store can offer the same. If a supplier allows no returns, mark those products on the site as not eligible for returns. [L0551.072]
- Read the signed supplier approval documents. They state each supplier's return terms, and the store's return policy is set around them. [L1113.040]
- Your return window must match what the supplier allows. Read the supplier's agreement documents before you set the policy, and show any longer supplier window on the product pages. [L0855.132]
- Return responsibility for heavy items depends on each supplier's policy, which you learn when the supplier approves you. (Older advice, 2019) [L0663.067]
- If suppliers charge return shipping or restocking fees, state those fees in the shipping and returns policy and base the policy on the supplier's terms. (Older advice, 2019) [L1275.033]
- Return policies differ between brands. The store's returns policy should summarise all supplier policies, and each supplier's policy should be noted in the retailer paperwork. (Older advice, 2020) [L1111.128]
- Before listing a brand, verify its return process. Brands with supplier-level support and clear policies reduce return and warranty problems. (Older advice, 2020) [L1111.134]
- Expect higher return rates in some niches, and avoid those niches when choosing products. [L1283.003]
- Compare your return policy with the top two or three competitors in the niche. A policy with refunds within 30 days without a reason, a restocking fee (for example 15% to 20%) and customer-paid return shipping is acceptable if competitors do the same. You can set the fee lower to stand out. [L0805.029]
- To set return shipping fees, look at the return policies of your top future competitors and model yours on them. Choose whether to charge actual cost or a fixed amount. [L1285.068]

### Shipping policy content

- The shipping policy must be specific enough for a reviewer to understand within a minute. It should state when orders ship after purchase (a range is acceptable), the average transit time, and the shipping cost, including whether shipping is free. [L0377.010]
- Vague shipping policies are a known cause of compliance problems. Avoid any wording that could be read as misleading. [L0377.011]
- Use this template for the shipping policy text:

```
Once your purchase goes through, you'll get an order confirmation email. We dispatch every order within [X] days of placement and send you an email with the tracking number as soon as it leaves us. Across the United States, every order ships free through [carrier(s) you typically use]. Choose free shipping and transit takes [X] to [Y] business days. If the store offers faster options, add this line: customers who need quicker delivery can pick [upgraded delivery option] at checkout, and those expedited rates are calculated live at checkout. If the store ships internationally at no charge, add this line: every international order ships free, and with free international shipping transit runs [X] to [Y] weeks.
```
[L0377.012]

- Reference figures from the lesson's US example: dispatch within 3 days, US transit of 3 to 5 business days, international transit of 1 to 3 weeks, carrier USPS. [L0377.012]
- If actual average shipping times are not yet known, check competitors' shipping pages to estimate transit times. The policy can be updated later. It only needs to exist and be accurate from the start. [L0377.013]
- A high-ticket dropshipping store usually does not ship internationally. Publish the international shipping paragraph only if the store actually ships abroad. A store that ships worldwide should state the international transit time in weeks. [L0377.027]
- The shipping page should list the expected shipping time for each supplier or brand, because suppliers ship at different speeds. Update these times as they become clear, for example after a few weeks of order data. [L0910.026]
- Shipping time should be stated in the store's policies, along with contact methods, the return policy and product descriptions, because missing details are a common reason for a store review. (2023) [L0855.139]
- Keep store policies short and clear, not long legal texts. The lesson's policies are only a few sentences each. [L0377.017]
- Many shoppers do not know a new store. Write the shipping policy (cost, delivery time, carrier) and the returns policy in plain English, and make them better than competitors' policies. [L0894.012]
- The contact page must offer at least two different ways to reach the business, such as a phone number and a business email. A contact form may be added, but it does not replace the two methods. [L0377.009]
- Until dedicated support mailboxes exist, use support@ followed by your domain (for example support@yourdomain.com) in the policy templates. Replace it with the real mailbox once it exists. [L1048.013]

### Shipping and returns page placement

- Shoppers read the shipping policy before they spend a lot of money, so it must be easy to find and complete. Place shipping information where buyers look before ordering. [L1130.008]
- The returns and exchange page answers what happens if the buyer is unhappy, which buyers ask before purchasing. Keep it visible before checkout to reduce hesitation. [L1130.009]
- The shipping page can link to the returns policy so customers find return terms next to delivery information. A short shipping statement with a link to the returns page reduces questions. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L1264.012]
- Leaving the return policy off the page leaves shoppers worried about damaged or unwanted items. State easy returns clearly on the page. [L1207.017]
- Most merchandise sold by mail ships subject to return. Return rights are a standard part of direct response selling, and a clear return policy removes the buyer's risk. [L1261.122]
- Do not open the returns and exchanges policy by default, especially a harsh one. Place it in an expandable section for curious buyers, because a long multi-step return process can scare off undecided visitors. [L1016.036]
- Pre-footer trust column: use a clear header such as "Easy returns" and link it to the returns policy page once that page exists. Until then, leave the link empty. [L1309.057]
- Policy pages such as shipping or terms are needed before they are linked in the pre-footer. In the example, a temporary link to terms of service was used and should be replaced with the correct page later. [L1309.058]
- Publish the shipping policy and the returns policy on the store, and make sure everyone handling orders has read both before working on them. [L1291.027]

### Free shipping, add-ons and accessories

- A free standard shipping offer on all products is a common store policy. Expedited shipping or white glove delivery can be offered as paid add-ons. [L1283.058]
- Conditional free shipping is set up by creating separate shipping profiles on the Shopify shipping page, each with the criteria that must be met for it to apply. [L1283.059]
- Accessories with flat-rate shipping should be sold only as add-ons to a main product. Do not list accessories as standalone products or include them in ads and product feeds. [L1283.060]
- When offering free shipping, a customer return means the shipping cost already paid may not be recovered. Design the return policy around each supplier's return rules, not a single store-wide policy. [L0837.042]
- Advertising free shipping while charging customers for return shipping is acceptable if the return costs are clearly disclosed in the policy. Clarity in advance prevents complaints about shipping. (Older advice, 2019) [L1275.034]

### Return window

- Return windows should always have an end date, because unlimited free returns make it impossible to tell when a product is profitable. Match the store's return window to the supplier's policy, for example 30 days when the supplier allows 30 days. (Older advice, 2019) [L1069.093]
- US average return window for physical products is about 30 days. Supplier windows can be 14, 30, 60 or up to 180 days. (2023) [L0855.131]
- No general US legal return period exists for ordinary products that the store must offer. This is general information, not legal advice. (2023) [L0855.138]
- A UK retailer may be required to offer a 14-day return policy for consumer goods, so check local rules before setting the policy. The US has no equivalent blanket rule for most products. (Older advice, 2022) [L0963.135]

Return window values by source. Each applies to the case stated:

| Window | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 30 days | Standard window for a new dropship store, because it usually follows supplier return policies. Adjust later once supplier policies are known. | [L1048.020] |
| 30 days | Store-wide default when suppliers share similar terms; exceptions only for extreme outliers (2023). | [L0970.131, L0251.008] |
| 30 days from delivery | Source B general window for most items in new condition. | [L0556.019] |
| 30 days from delivery | Australian caravan parts retailer, change-of-mind returns in original condition (older, 2021 to 2022). | [L0893.022] |
| 30 days from purchase date | Source D sample policy template, where the window counts from the purchase date. | [L1250.005, L1250.028] |
| 30 days, with a 14-day window for one supplier | General store policy at 30 days; a supplier with a 14-day window gets the 14-day window stated on its product pages and is listed as an exclusion. (2023) | [L0470.082] |
| 7 days | Furniture brand, Source B (older, 2021 to 2022). | [L0556.019] |
| 14 days | Mirror brand, Source B; no returns once installed (older, 2021 to 2022). | [L0556.019] |
| 3 days from delivery | Shopify default example in the lesson, with an option to extend for weekends or holidays. This conflicts with the 14-day text in the lesson's template and must be aligned. (2026) | [L1327.050, L1327.051] |
| 14, 30, 90, Unlimited or Custom days | Options in the Shopify return rules settings. | [L1250.010] |

- Return windows differ by brand. A general 30-day window applies to most items in new condition, but a brand can have its own window. [L0556.019]
- For a 30-day window, the Source D template reads "You have [number of days] days from the purchase date to initiate a return." Choose the start point (purchase date or delivery) and state it in the policy. [L1250.005, L1327.050]
- Match the store's return window to the supplier. When suppliers differ, use the window in the store's general policy and show the exception on product pages. [L0855.132, L0470.082]
- Customer can return within 30 days on the store-wide default, with a 10% restocking fee and customer pays return shipping (example brand structure). [L0972.046]

### Return conditions and eligibility

- Returned items must go back in original packaging with all parts. [L0556.019]
- A returned item must be unused, kept in the state it arrived in, and still in its original packaging. Any return needs a receipt or other proof of purchase. [L1250.005]
- Change-of-mind returns can be accepted even when special packaging has been opened, as long as the product itself is in original condition. Record this condition because it determines whether a return is accepted. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0893.050]
- For change-of-mind returns, the store's policy should copy the supplier's policy for gently used products that customers simply change their mind about, because the store cannot send the item back to the supplier under different terms. (2023) [L0855.137]
- Return conditions to state in the policy: [L0539 student input] "New, unused, in original packaging, all accessories included" is the example condition set. [L0539.001]
- Return wording for a dropshipping store reads: "Items must be returned in their original condition." [L0855.133]
- Record the return conditions as one clear rule set per supplier when they differ. [L0893.021]

### Non-returnable items and excluded products

- Typical exceptions to change-of-mind returns include sanitation products that were opened or installed, electronics unless in sealed original packaging, items sold by the metre, specially ordered items, and installed, modified or used items. Free freight included in the price can be deducted from the refund. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0893.023]
- Bidets and toilets (personal hygiene products) cannot be returned once opened or installed. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0556.019]
- Food and flowers (perishables), gift cards, and health and personal-care products cannot be sent back. This is the Source D sample exclusion. [L1250.005, L1250.028]
- If a product is an ingestible, a hygiene item, a pre-owned good or a final-sale item, the return policy must state that. These categories are often excluded from standard refunds, so the exclusion must appear on the policy page and not be left for the buyer to discover. [L1188.057]
- Refunds apply only to full-price items. Discounted goods are not refundable in the sample policy. [L1250.005]
- A supplier with a no-return policy should be matched on your store. Add a note to each product page from that supplier stating it is not eligible for returns unless the item arrives defective or damaged, using the supplier's exact wording. (2023) [L0835.099]
- Products that the supplier does not take back must be marked as non-returnable on the policy page and on each product page. This prevents disputes when a customer later asks for a return. (Older advice, 2018) [L1085.074]
- Suppliers without a return policy can still be sold, but the product pages and the return policy page must state that those products are not eligible for return. (Older advice, 2022) [L1113.043]
- If a supplier refuses returns for a product, either mark the product as not eligible for returns on its page, or ship the product to a fulfilment centre you control if you want to sell it. (Older advice, 2021) [L0801.122]
- If a supplier refuses returns for damaged items, do not accept returns for those products either. State the exclusion in the return policy and also on that supplier's product pages. (2025) [L0667.023]
- When some suppliers accept no returns, state that clearly on their product pages where customers see it before buying. (Older advice, 2021) [L0968.099]
- Products from suppliers that do not accept returns should be excluded from the return policy. Add a note on those product pages and in the shipping and returns tab that the items are not eligible for returns. (Older advice, 2021) [L0962.125]
- Products from suppliers that accept no returns must be named as not eligible for return on the shipping and returns page and on their product pages. (Older advice, 2022) [L0963.134]
- Changing their mind on a no-return product: "This item is not eligible for returns unless it arrives defective or damaged. [Use the supplier's exact return wording]" [L0835.100]

Exclusion wording template:

```
This item is not eligible for returns unless it arrives defective or damaged. [Use the supplier's exact return wording]
```
[L0835.100]

```
Exclusion: products from [Supplier name] are eligible for return only if they arrive defective or damaged.
```
[L0835.101]

- Procedure for adding a no-return policy for a supplier that does not accept returns (older, 2018):
  1. Update the shipping and returns policy page with a note listing the affected supplier or products.
  2. Add the same note to every product page from that supplier, in the shipping and returns tab.
  3. Use wording such as "This product is not eligible for returns; all sales are final."
  [L1085.073]
- Procedure for a non-returnable brand (2025):
  1. Keep your general return policy for all brands.
  2. Add an exception at the bottom of the policy stating that products from the non-returnable brand are not eligible for return.
  3. On each product page of that brand, replace the standard return text with a statement that the product is not eligible for return.
  [L0837.043]
- Follow the procedure in [L0837.043] when a brand has no returns. [L0837.042]
- Do not use a general no-return rule for a supplier whose terms are otherwise general. Put the exclusion only on that supplier's pages. [L0968.100]

### Restocking fees

- Restocking fees and return shipping costs depend on each supplier's return policy. Customers usually pay return shipping, but this varies by supplier. (Older advice, 2021) [L0247.093]
- A restocking fee should match the supplier's restocking fee, not be added on top of it. The purpose is to avoid losing money on returns, not to make profit from them. (2025) [L0972.044]
- Restocking fees and return terms can differ per brand. Show them on the general return policy page, and optionally in expandable sections on each product page. (2025) [L0972.045]
- Use this structure for a brand-specific return policy (2025):

```
Our return policies vary by brand. Please see the list below for the return policy of each brand.

Brand A products can be returned within 30 days. A 10% restocking fee applies, and you are responsible for return shipping costs.

Brand B products can be returned within 60 days. A 20% restocking fee applies, and you are responsible for return shipping costs.

Replace the brand names, return windows and fees with the exact terms from each supplier.
```
[L0972.046]

- Restocking fee values by source. Each applies to the case stated:

| Fee | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 10% to 15% of order price | Charged only if the top 2 to 3 competitors charge it; otherwise omit to remain competitive (2024). | [L0253.007] |
| 15% to 20% | Acceptable if competitors do the same (2024). | [L0805.029] |
| 15% | Large items (Source B, 2021 to 2022, older). | [L0556.020] |
| 15% | Steam shower or bathtub that fails local inspection, unit still in original packaging (older, 2021 to 2022). | [L0556.021] |
| 25% | Same steam shower or bathtub when it was opened, or opened and assembled (older, 2021 to 2022). | [L0556.021] |
| 10% (normally) | Australian caravan parts retailer, refund on request (older, 2021 to 2022). | [L0893.022] |
| 10% or 20% | Brand structure examples (Brand A and Brand B). | [L0972.046] |
| 5% or 10% | Lower fee used to beat a competitor's 15% (2023). | [L0964.101] |
| None | Source D Shopify default; Source D sample policy; new dropship store default. | [L1327.050, L1048.018, L1048.020] |

- Restocking fees can also apply to damaged packaging, to inspection and testing of appliances, and to items with multiple components. Expect fees beyond the standard percentage in these cases. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0893.025]
- If a store charges no restocking fee, state this clearly and make it prominent in the refund policy. Google views a zero-dollar restocking fee favourably. [L0724.018]
- If a customer asks for a return fee receipt, a restocking fee can be charged and documented in the return policy so that customers can see it before buying. (2023) [L1094.096]

### Return shipping and who pays

- For a non-defective return, the customer normally pays the return shipping fee. Damaged or defective items are replaced at no cost to the customer. Returns should stay a very small share of total sales. (2021) [L1279.090]
- Return shipping costs are always charged to the customer. (2024) [L0253.007]
- Customers usually pay return shipping. For a damaged item, the customer does not pay for the return. (Older advice, 2019) [L0663.066]
- Free returns are the default for stores of this kind, and customers pay for return shipping on almost all stores. Restocking fees are the alternative. (2023) [L0964.101]
- If a supplier offers free return shipping, absorb the cost and do not charge the customer. Otherwise, the customer pays. (2023) [L0251.008]
- For damaged or defective returns, the supplier should pay the return shipping. Supplier applications may ask who pays, and the answer is the supplier. (2023) [L0855.134]
- If a store-caused problem (wrong or defective item) occurs, the store can cover all return shipping and refund the original shipping cost. Keep the store-caused case separate from buyer's remorse. [L0539.006]
- Store covers all shipping for defective or wrong items. [L1048.018]
- Heavy products: the refund policy must state that a customer who requests a refund pays the shipping cost to send the item out and the return shipping, even if the original order had free shipping. This can be about 35 dollars each way for heavy products. State this on the shipping page, in the order confirmation and in the terms. [L0910.031]
- Shipping cost for the return: "Customer is responsible" for buyer's remorse; "Store covers all shipping" for defective or wrong items (example input). [L0539.001]
- For a buyer's remorse return, the customer can be made responsible for return shipping, and the restocking fee terms must be stated. [L0539.006]
- For warranty claims, the customer returned the faulty item to the seller at their own cost. The seller paid to send the repaired or replacement item back once a manufacturing fault was confirmed. If no manufacturing fault was found, the customer paid the freight for the item's return. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0893.048]
- Free return postage in the Source B example was limited to 3 months for spare parts and 12 months for other items. If no manufacturing fault was found, the customer paid the freight back. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0893.024]
- Source D sample: the customer pays return postage, and that postage is not reimbursed. [L1250.005, L1250.030]
- Shopify return rules: return shipping cost is set to "Customer provides return shipping" or "Flat rate return shipping". [L1250.010]
- Shopify default: the customer pays for return shipping. [L1327.050]

### Prepaid return labels

- If prepaid return labels are used, the policy should state whether the label cost is deducted from the refund. [L0539.007]
- Example input: "Yes, cost deducted from refund." [L0539.001]
- Exchanges use prepaid shipping labels in the default settings for a new dropship store. [L1048.018]

### Refunds, timing, cancellations

- The refund timeframe should be a fixed number of business days counted from when the item is received and inspected, for example within 7 business days. Stating the start point of the clock prevents customers from expecting refunds on the day the return is shipped. [L0539.003]
- Sample refund rule (Source D): approved refunds go back to the original payment method within 5 to 7 business days after the returned item is inspected. [L1250.029, L1250.005]
- Partial refunds may apply to items not in original condition, damaged items, or returns after the window. [L1250.029]
- Refund wording from the lesson: "If you're unhappy with your products for any reason, we refund the full amount minus shipping. To ask for a refund, email [business email] or phone [phone number]. [Add restocking fee, if any.] [Add brands or products that cannot be returned, if any.]" [L0377.014]

```
If you're unhappy with your products for any reason, we refund the full amount minus shipping. To ask for a refund, email [business email] or phone [phone number]. [Add restocking fee, if any.] [Add brands or products that cannot be returned, if any.]
```
[L0377.014]

- The lesson's sample policy refunds the full product price minus the original shipping charges and tells customers to request this by email or phone. [L0377.014]
- The refund policy must state any restocking fee and any brands or product types that cannot be returned, because a reviewer checks for these. [L0377.015]
- The refund and return policy should answer: what the refund policy is, how a customer requests a refund, how returns work for damaged items, and how a customer starts a return. [L0377.016]
- Source B's example refunded the original shipping cost for store-caused returns and did not refund it for remorse returns. The 2025 template in Dropship defaults: store refunds original shipping cost for defective or wrong items. [L1048.018]
- Default refund policy settings for a new dropship store: the customer pays for return shipping, the store pays for defective or wrong items and refunds the original shipping cost, orders canceled before shipping receive a full refund, and exchanges use prepaid shipping labels. [L1048.018]
- Cancellation policy: full refund if canceled before shipping. [L0539.001, L1048.018]
- Original shipping cost policy: the original shipping cost is refunded for store-caused returns. [L0539.001, L0556.021]
- For a steam shower or bathtub that fails local inspection, the return is the purchase price minus the original shipping fee, the return shipping fee and a 15% restocking fee if it is in original packaging. If opened or assembled, the restocking fee rises to 25%. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0556.021]
- Refund disputes are best prevented with clear product page wording about returns. Keep the wording specific to the supplier and product type. (2020) [L0664.072]
- A refund dispute can happen when a return promise is inconsistent (see Consistency). [L0567.031]

Return address and RMA:

- The RMA process: a customer starts a return and receives an RMA number. The return address is provided after the return is authorised. [L0167.020]
- Procedure: after you receive an RMA number, send the item only to the return address you are given, quoting the RMA number. [L0724.017]
- If returns go to a third-party warehouse instead of the business address, the refund policy must state that the return address is provided after the return is authorised. Google may flag a policy that does not clearly name the return address when it differs from the business address. [L0724.016]

Template for a warehouse return address:

```
Once your return has been approved and you have received an RMA number, we will provide you with the exact return address of the warehouse facility. Please send your item only to that address, quoting your RMA number.
```
[L0724.017]

- Include this summary table at the top of the refund policy page, titled "Returns and Refunds at a Glance":

| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Restocking fee | None (state explicitly if zero) |
| Return window | [your return window] |
| Refund timing | [your refund timeline, stated clearly] |
| Return method | RMA required |
| Return address | Provided after RMA authorization, may differ from business address |
| Shipping costs | [exact cost, or free shipping] |

[L0724.019]

### Damage reports and defective items

- Set the two damage report windows separately in the returns policy, because the carriers' claim periods differ. (2023) [L0539.002]
- Damage reports for shipments by UPS or FedEx must be filed within 48 hours by the customer. For all other carriers the damage report window is 15 days. [L1048.019]
- Conflict on UPS and FedEx: the Example for high-ticket products sets freight (LTL) damage reports at 48 hours after delivery and small parcel shipments via UPS or FedEx at 15 days after delivery. The Shopify default sets UPS or FedEx at 48 hours and all other carriers at 15 days. Check the carrier's claim period before you publish, because the two sources do not agree on UPS and FedEx. [L0539.002, L1048.019]
- Damage report window by carrier type (applies to the high-ticket template):
  - Freight (LTL): 48 hours after delivery. [L0539.002]
  - Small parcel (UPS or FedEx): 15 days after delivery. [L0539.002]
- Each area of a competitor's return policy has its own terms: seller errors (wrong or damaged product, incorrect photo), the window for reporting damage, warranty terms, and change-of-mind returns. Record each separately. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0893.021]
- Restocking fees and damage: damage to the product can void the return entirely. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0556.020]
- For a quality or damage claim, the customer provides photo or video evidence. State that a refund is not granted simply for disliking a product; the customer can leave a review instead. [L0639.037]
- The 30-day money-back guarantee applies, with photo or video evidence required for quality or damage claims. [L0639.037]
- Keep screenshots of the terms of service, shipping policy and refund policy pages. They serve as evidence in a chargeback dispute. [L0352.021, L0352.061]
- Put a specific refund cutoff in the refund policy, such as no refunds after 14 days from delivery, and state it in the terms of service as well. [L0352.061]
- Publish clear terms of service, a shipping policy and a refund policy with specific conditions, such as no refunds after a set number of days. [L0352.021]

### Exchanges

- Exchanges are only offered for defective or damaged items. The customer must send details of the issue and proof of damage. The customer pays return shipping, which is non-refundable in the sample policy. [L1250.030]
- Replacements happen only for defective or damaged products. The customer emails the contact address describing the problem and attaches proof of damage. [L1250.005]
- Exchange shipping: "Customer responsible for return and reshipment costs" is the example input. [L0539.001]
- Exchanges use prepaid shipping labels in the default settings for a new dropship store. [L1048.018]
- Template for returns and exchanges:

```
Returns and Exchanges

We accept returns and exchanges within [X-day] days for unused products in their original packaging. If you are not satisfied with your purchase, contact us at [email/contact info] to start a return. We will guide you through the process and issue a refund or an exchange once we have received and checked the returned items.
```
[L1250.035]

### Warranty text and guarantees

- Show each brand's warranty on its product pages in an expandable section that is unique to that brand. (2024) [L0471.033]
- Warranty blurb for product pages (older, 2020): "We offer a [warranty length] warranty on all [Brand] products. This warranty is limited to [scope, for example parts only] and covers [short description of what it includes]." Place it directly under the warranty statement on each product page of that brand. [L0961.051]

```
We offer a [warranty length] warranty on all [Brand] products. This warranty is limited to [scope, for example parts only] and covers [short description of what it includes].
```
[L0961.051]

- Warranty on a product's warranty tab: replace the manufacturer's email address with your own business email so customer questions reach your company. The manufacturer still handles warranty claims, so redirect customers to them only when a claim is needed. (2026) [L0808.001]
- Source B's warranty example (older, 2021 to 2022): 12 months on appliances and 3 months on spare parts from purchase. [L0893.024]
- Items that are impractical to send back, such as an installed refrigerator, may have their warranty handled on site by an authorised service agent instead of a return. Note this exception separately, since it changes the returns process for bulky or installed products. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022) [L0893.049]
- The product guarantee page should explain how the guarantee works, when a product counts as not effective, and how long the guarantee lasts. Because each supplier may have different terms, the page can list the guarantee for each supplier's products. [L1130.007]
- Using example return and warranty terms without changing them to match your own returns policy and each supplier's policy will cause problems. Terms must be verified and adjusted before use. [L1291.026]

### Blanket policy versus supplier exceptions

Sources disagree on whether to match each supplier individually or use one blanket policy with exceptions. Each applies in the case stated:

- Match each supplier individually: "Don't create uniform policy; match supplier policies individually." (Older advice, 2020) [L0268.027]
- Use one blanket policy with exceptions only for suppliers that do not accept returns. (2021 onwards) [L0671.104, L0671.241]
- Use one general policy for most suppliers and give unique policies to suppliers whose terms differ. (2023) [L1283.001]
- Use one standard 30-day return policy for the store and add exceptions only for extreme outliers. This keeps the policy simple. (2023) [L0970.131]
- Use a blanket return policy built from the average of your suppliers' return policies. (Older advice, 2022) [L0963.134]
- Set your return and shipping policy as an average of the supplier policies. Do not copy each supplier's policy into the store. (Older advice, 2021) [L0962.124]
- For a store with several brands, use one general return policy that works for all suppliers, or add a separate return policy tab on each product page for a brand with different terms. (2023) [L0855.136]

When each applies:
- Use the blanket policy when most suppliers share similar terms, and show exceptions separately. [L1283.001, L0801.121]
- Use an individual supplier policy when supplier terms differ widely, such as a supplier with no returns or a supplier with a 14-day window. [L0470.082, L0268.027]

- Supplier return terms differ in windows, restocking fees and return shipping. Because of this, a blanket policy can sometimes cost around $100 on a single return. (Older advice, 2021) [L0671.105, L0671.242]
- Main shipping and return policy covers most products. Any supplier with stricter terms gets its own policy on the product page, and those exclusions are also listed in the main policy. (Older advice, 2021) [L0801.121]
- If a supplier refuses returns for a product, mark the product as not eligible for returns on its page, or ship it to a fulfilment centre you control. (Older advice, 2021) [L0801.122]
- Write one general return policy that fits most suppliers. List the exceptions on the returns page with footnote markers, and repeat them on the product pages of the affected suppliers. (Older advice, 2021) [L0968.100]
- Build the return page this way (2023):
  1. Put the general return policy at the top and add the note "some exclusions apply".
  2. Below it, list each supplier or brand the general policy does not cover.
  3. Under each listed supplier, state its specific return policy.
  Place a product-level return policy on the product pages of those unique suppliers.
  [L1283.001]
- Use one general return policy when most suppliers share similar terms, and give unique policies to suppliers whose terms differ. [L1283.001]
- If a supplier's agreement states that no products are returnable, you can still sell their products by setting a separate policy for that supplier that marks the products as non-returnable. Expect higher return rates in some niches. (2023) [L1283.003]
- A store policy based on the supplier's policy: "Base your return policy on your suppliers' return policies." (2020) [L0551.072]
- Older advice (2019) return policy procedure for the returns page:
  1. On each brand's product page, show that brand's return policy in the returns tab (for example, Company A policy equals 15 days).
  2. On the returns page, state the general store return policy at the top.
  3. Below it, list each supplier's return policy separately, including any unique exceptions.
  4. For a supplier that accepts no returns, state on its product pages and on the returns page that its products are not eligible for return and all sales are final.
  5. Repeat the same wording everywhere a policy appears so customers are not confused.
  [L0663.030]
- Return policies must match across all pages. Inconsistent policies between the product page and the returns page confuse customers. (Older advice, 2019) [L0663.031]
- Keep a separate policy for each supplier when supplier terms differ. The supplier-specific wording goes on each supplier's product pages. [L0247.094]
- Principle (2021, older): create one combined shipping and returns policy that covers most suppliers. Suppliers whose terms differ get their own policy text on the policy pages and in the product page tabs. [L0247.094]
- Products from non-returnable brands and suppliers are excluded from the general policy and stated separately (see Non-returnable items). [L0962.125, L0963.134]
- A customer-facing returns template that works for all suppliers: "If your item arrives damaged or defective, we will replace it or refund it, and we will cover the cost of shipping the replacement or the return. If you want to return an item that is not damaged or defective, you may return it within 30 days of delivery; you are responsible for the return shipping cost, and a restocking fee may apply. Items must be returned in their original condition." (2023) [L0855.133]

```
If your item arrives damaged or defective, we will replace it or refund it, and we will cover the cost of shipping the replacement or the return. If you want to return an item that is not damaged or defective, you may return it within 30 days of delivery; you are responsible for the return shipping cost, and a restocking fee may apply. Items must be returned in their original condition.
```
[L0855.133]

- The sample wording above is for a dropshipping store. The customer-facing returns policy must not contain the word "dropshipping" or legal jargon. [L0855.133, L0539.004]

### Shopify return rules and settings

- Settings > Policies > Manage return rules: turn return rules on with the toggle (Turn off appears when they are active). Choose the return window: 14 days, 30 days, 90 days, Unlimited or Custom days. Choose return shipping cost: Customer provides return shipping or Flat rate return shipping. Optionally enable Charge restocking fee and define final sale items. [L1250.010]
- Settings > Policies > Return and cancellation rules (Defaults): set the return window to 3 days starting from when the item is delivered, with the option to extend the window to account for weekends or holidays. Make the customer pay for return shipping. Leave the restocking fee off, and note the rule applies only to items purchased after the rule is turned on or updated. [L1327.050]
- Return rules are enabled on the Policies page and let you set return fees, return shipping and define final sale items. Enable them before launch if you want to control returns in the store. [L1167.034]
- Return rules in Shopify only apply to orders placed after the rules were turned on or last updated. The written return policy page must be updated separately whenever the rules change. [L1250.011]
- Shopify's return rules page shows a summary, for example returns accepted for 30 days and no final sale items. The written return and refund policy must repeat the same return window and final-sale rule, otherwise customers see conflicting terms. [L1250.042]
- A return window set to 3 days in Shopify must be matched in the written return policy. The template text in the lesson says 14 days, so the policy text and the Shopify rule disagree if left unchanged. Edit the policy text after setting the rule so the customer sees one consistent return window. [L1327.051]
- Publishing a generated policy with the example numbers unchanged is a common error. Every placeholder and figure, such as the return window, processing days and delivery days, must be replaced with what the store really offers. [L1250.031]
- Settings > Policies: Shipping policy and Refund and return policy pages. The refund policy initially shows as "no policy set". [L1048.017]
- Conditional free shipping profiles: see Shipping and free shipping. [L1283.059]

### Google Merchant Center requirements

- In the Merchant Center return steps, the return method options are "By mail" with a return label, "Download and print" label, or "Customer's responsibility" for the customer to pay return shipping. Choose the option that matches the return policy on the website. If the store charges no restocking fee, select "No cost" for the restocking fee. [L0729.016]
- The Merchant Center return window can include a holiday extension, but add one only if the website's return policy states it. If the policy has no extension, keep the standard return window so the Merchant Center setting matches the website. [L0729.020]
- The refund policy must state the return address clearly when it differs from the business address (see Refunds). [L0724.016]
- The refund policy summary table ("Returns and Refunds at a Glance") is placed at the top of the refund policy page (see Refunds). [L0724.019]
- Product returns do not directly hurt Google SEO, and they have no direct effect on search rankings. (Older advice, 2022) [L0963.136]

### Chargebacks and support

- A visible support policy with a stated response time signals that complaints will be handled. This reassures customers before they buy and reduces the urge to dispute a charge with their bank. [L1250.039]
- Support and feedback template: "Our team is here for you. Questions, feedback or complaints about products or services can be sent through [email or contact form]. We aim to answer within [X] business days and will work to settle any problem to your satisfaction."

- Keep the refund and return policy clear and specific so the policy and screenshots of the pages can be shown as evidence in a dispute (see Damage reports). [L0352.021, L0352.061]

### Consistency across pages and emails

- Keep the return promise consistent across all emails and match it to the real policy. One email stated a 30-day money-back guarantee while another claimed 100% money back. That conflict creates a potential refund dispute. [L0567.031]
- Repeat the same wording everywhere a policy appears so customers are not confused. [L0663.030]
- Keep the refund and return policy consistent with the Shopify return rules, the Merchant Center setting and the product pages. Shopify rules apply only to new orders, so update the written policy whenever the rules change. [L1250.011, L1327.051, L0729.016]
- Clear product page wording about returns prevents refund disputes. Keep it specific to the supplier and product type. [L0664.072]
- Policy pages (shipping and terms) must exist before they are linked. Replace a temporary link with the correct page. [L1309.058]
- Keep the exact wording for a no-return supplier on every page that mentions it. [L0835.099, L0835.100]

### Compliance check and AI-generated drafts

- Procedure for checking the Contact Us page (after updating it in Shopify, Online Store > Pages > Contact Us):
  1. Copy the full page content and run it through Google Gemini to confirm it is compliant, in addition to the policy pages.
  2. Apply any changes Gemini recommends.
  3. Ask Gemini to re-check the page.
  [L0167.022]
- A policy that does not say where the item should be sent is flagged as unclear. The policy should explicitly state that the return address is provided after the return is approved through an RMA (return merchandise authorization). [L0167.020]
- An AI writing tool such as ChatGPT can generate a complete returns and exchanges policy when given the store's specific terms in a structured prompt. The output is then pasted directly into the Shopify refund policy page. [L0539.009]
- Pasting the generated policy into Shopify with unfilled bracket placeholders or unchecked example values leaves customers with contradictory or meaningless terms. Check every value against the actual store process before publishing. [L0539.008]
- Procedure: creating the shipping policy with an AI prompt (Settings > Policies > Shipping policy):
  1. Copy the full shipping policy prompt from its copywriter role line to the end.
  2. Paste it into ChatGPT or another AI tool.
  3. Enter the store name.
  4. Enter the support email in the format support@yourdomain.com.
  5. Set the shipping region to Continental United States only for a US business.
  6. Keep the default handling time of 3 to 5 business days, transit time of 3 to 7 business days and total delivery time of 7 to 12 business days.
  7. Leave the shipping partners at their default.
  8. Set the freight option to yes for large and heavy products.
  9. Delete the white glove delivery field unless it is confirmed available for your niche.
  10. For out of stock or custom orders, enter that customers are contacted with updated timelines.
  11. For delays, enter that customers are proactively notified when delays occur.
  12. Send the prompt, copy the generated policy and paste it into the Shipping policy in Shopify.
  13. Click Publish.
  [L1048.016]
- Procedure: creating the refund and return policy with an AI prompt (Settings > Policies > Refund and return policy):
  1. Click the Refund and return policy, which initially shows as "no policy set".
  2. Copy the full refund page prompt from its copywriter role line to the end.
  3. Paste it into ChatGPT or another AI tool.
  4. Enter the store name.
  5. Enter the support email in the format support@yourdomain.com.
  6. Set the return window to 30 days.
  7. Keep the restocking fee at none.
  8. Keep the defaults for return shipping, defective or wrong items, cancellation, damage reports and exchanges as listed below.
  9. Send the prompt and wait for the full output.
  10. Copy the generated policy and paste it into the policy section in Shopify, then save it.
  [L1048.017]
- Default settings for a new dropship store (refund policy): the customer pays for return shipping; the store pays for defective or wrong items and refunds the original shipping cost; orders canceled before shipping receive a full refund; exchanges use prepaid shipping labels. [L1048.018]
- For a new store, keep most refund and return settings at the default values, since the store is still choosing suppliers. Change them over time to match each supplier's actual return and cancellation policy. [L1048.021]
- The standard return window for a new dropship store is 30 days, because it usually follows supplier return policies, and the restocking fee is set to none. Adjust both values later once actual supplier policies are known. [L1048.020]
- Prompt for a plain-language returns and exchanges policy (use verbatim; the student inputs are filled in before sending):

```
Act as a senior eCommerce customer-experience writer. Draft a plain-language Returns & Exchanges Policy for a Shopify store that sells high-ticket goods sourced from domestic suppliers. The copy should ease buyer worry, state expectations openly, read as an established and dependable business, stay simple to follow, avoid legal jargon, never use the word “dropshipping,” and feel fair and centered on the customer. Voice: professional, reassuring, transparent, supportive, confident. Use short section headers and brief paragraphs. Length: 400 to 650 words. Skip filler, exaggeration, and boilerplate. It should read like a genuine brand's own page.

Include these sections: Policy Overview; Return & Exchange Eligibility; Return Window; Return Shipping Responsibility; How to Start a Return or Exchange (RMA Process); Damaged or Defective Items; Cancellations; Refund Processing Time; Our Error vs. Customer-Initiated Returns; Exchanges Process; Final Reassurance Statement.

Student inputs to fill in:
Store Name: [Example: Coastal Ridge Living]
Support Email Address: [Example: support@coastalrideliving.com]
Return Window: [Example: 30 days from delivery]
Condition Requirements for Returns: [Example: New, unused, in original packaging, all accessories included]
Restocking Fee: [Example: None]
Who Pays Return Shipping for Buyer's Remorse: [Example: Customer is responsible]
Who Pays Return Shipping for Defective/Wrong Item: [Example: Store covers all shipping]
Original Shipping Cost Policy: [Example: Original shipping cost is refunded]
Refund Processing Time: [Example: Within 7 business days after item is received and inspected]
Cancellation Policy: [Example: Full refund if canceled before shipping]
Damage Reporting Window for Freight (LTL): [Example: 48 hours after delivery]
Damage Reporting Window for Small Parcel (UPS/FedEx): [Example: 15 days after delivery]
Exchange Shipping Policy: [Example: Customer responsible for return and reshipment costs]
Do You Use Prepaid Return Labels? (Yes/No): [Example: Yes, cost deducted from refund]
