```
Final instruction: Using the details above, write a complete Returns & Exchanges Policy that feels fair and professional, reduces hesitation on high-ticket purchases, makes the brand feel safe to buy from, can be pasted straight into Shopify, and is unique each time it is generated. Use no placeholders. Give no explanations. Include no notes or headings such as "Policy Generator." Output only the finished policy copy.

Before writing, confirm every student input is filled in. If one is missing, request it instead of inventing a value. Apply the exact input values for the return window, condition requirements, restocking fee, shipping responsibility, refund time, cancellation rule, damage reporting windows, and exchange shipping, and place each one in the section where it belongs. Keep the Final Reassurance Statement to two or three sentences that include the support email address.
```
[L0539.001]

- Reference: the prompt's required sections and student inputs are set out in [L0539.001]. Use the input values exactly; do not invent a value for any missing input. [L0539.001]
- A high-ticket returns policy should state the refund timeframe as a fixed number of business days from receipt and inspection (see Refunds), and keep the copy between 400 and 650 words with short section headers. [L0539.003, L0539.004]
- High-ticket buyers hesitate most when they cannot see the cost and effort of a return. The policy should answer who pays return shipping, whether a restocking fee applies, and how the original shipping cost is treated. Clear answers lower purchase anxiety more than long reassurance text. [L0539.005]
- Shipping-policy text with a template is in [L0377.012]. Return policy text templates are in [L0377.014] and [L1250.005]. [L0377.012, L0377.014, L1250.005]

Source D sample returns and refund policy template (replace every bracket with the store's real term):

```
Return and Refund Policy

At [Your Store Name] our goal is that you're happy with what you bought. If something isn't right for you, we'll help. The rules are set out below.

1. Eligibility
- A returned item must be unused, kept in the state it arrived in, and still in its original packaging.
- You have [number of days] days from the purchase date to initiate a return.
- Any return needs a receipt or other proof of purchase.

2. Non-returnable items
Food and flowers (perishables), gift cards, and health and personal-care products cannot be sent back.

3. Refunds
- After we get your return, we check it and let you know where it stands. Approved refunds go back to the original payment method within 5-7 business days.
- Partial refunds: some cases qualify, such as items not in original condition, damaged goods, or goods sent back after the [number of days]-day window has closed.

4. Exchanges
- Replacements happen only for defective or damaged products. Email [your contact email] describing the problem and attaching proof of damage.

5. Return shipping
- Mail the product to [Your Return Address].
- The customer pays return postage, and that postage is not reimbursed.

6. Sale items
- Refunds apply only to full-price items; discounted goods are not refundable.

7. Contact
For questions about returns, refunds or exchanges, write to [your contact email]. We're glad to help with any concern.
```
[L1250.005, L1250.028, L1250.029, L1250.030]

- Sample refund and exchange rules are repeated in the template above. Replace every bracket with the store's real value before publishing. [L1250.031, L1250.005]

### Returns policy template

```
Returns
You have 14 days from the day you receive your item to request a return. [Set the number of days to match the return window in Settings > Policies > Return and cancellation rules.]
To qualify, the item must be in the condition you received it: unworn or unused, with tags still attached, and in its original packaging. You also need the receipt or proof of purchase.
To start a return, contact us at {Business email}. Returns must be sent back to the original shipping address.
If we accept your return, we will send you a return shipping label and instructions on how and where to ship the package. Items sent to us without a return request first will not be accepted.
For any question about returns, you can reach us at {Business email}.

Damages and Issues
Please check your order when it arrives. If the item is defective or damaged, or if you received the wrong item, contact us right away so we can review the problem and make it right.

Exceptions / Non-Returnable Items
Some items cannot be returned. These include perishable goods (such as food, flowers or plants), custom products (such as special orders or personalized items), and personal care goods (such as beauty products). We also do not accept returns of hazardous materials, flammable liquids or gases. If you have questions about a specific item, please get in touch.
We cannot accept returns on sale items or gift cards.

Exchanges
The quickest way to get the item you want is to return the one you have and, once that return is accepted, place a separate order for the new item.

European Union 14-Day Cooling Off Period
Despite the above, if the goods are shipped into the European Union, you may cancel or return your order within 14 days, for any reason and without giving a justification.
As stated above, the item must be in the condition you received it: unworn or unused, with tags, and in its original packaging. You also need the receipt or proof of purchase.

Refunds
We will notify you once we have received and inspected your return, and tell you whether the refund has been approved. If approved, the refund goes automatically to your original payment method within 10 business days.
Your bank or credit card company may need some time to process and post the refund. If more than 15 business days have passed since we approved your return, contact us at {Business email}.
```
[L1327.057]

### Return window and Smart SEO setup

- The Source D template uses a 14-day return window from receipt, and tells you to set the number of days in Settings > Policies > Return and cancellation rules to match it. [L1327.057]
- Source A's Smart SEO example uses 30 days as the window, so the number entered must match your actual policy, not the example. [L1337.017]

Setting the return policy in Smart SEO:

1. Turn on the return policy option. [L1337.017]
2. Enter the country where returns apply. [L1337.017]
3. Enter the return window in days, for example 30 for a 30-day return policy. [L1337.017]
4. Enter the return method, such as return by mail. [L1337.017]
5. Enter the return fees: free returns, or the customer pays for return shipping, matching your actual policy. [L1337.017]
6. Save. [L1337.017]

### Subscription, pre-order and try-before-you-buy cancellations

```
Some items in our store may be offered as a subscription, a pre-order or try before you buy. This cancellation policy explains how you can change or cancel these types of purchases.

Subscriptions
A subscription delivers items to you repeatedly, according to the subscription duration and frequency you choose. Your payment details are stored securely, and you will be charged for each delivery unless you choose to pay in advance.
Some subscriptions renew automatically at the end of their duration. If you do not want to renew, you can cancel.
You can change or cancel a subscription at any time. Your order confirmation emails contain links to your order, and you can manage your subscription from there.
See our returns policy for more details on returns and refunds.

Pre-orders
When you buy a pre-order, you are purchasing an out-of-stock or soon-to-be-available product that is not yet in inventory. We may collect no payment or a partial deposit at checkout, store your payment method, and then fulfill the order and charge the full or remaining amount at a later date.
You can cancel a partially paid pre-order that has not yet been fulfilled. Once an order has been fulfilled, it can no longer be cancelled, but you can request a full or partial refund.
See our returns policy for more details on returns and refunds.

Try Before You Buy
When you buy a try before you buy item, we authorize your payment method before fulfilling the order. You have a set amount of time to decide whether to keep the item.
Once that period has passed, if you have not returned the item, we will charge your payment method the full amount.
```
[L1327.061]

### Clear return terms in high-return markets

- In markets with a strong habit of buying and returning items, such as the UK, a fashion brand should make its return policy firm and clearly visible before checkout. [L1438.057]
- Customers in such markets expect easy returns, so the policy needs to be stated plainly rather than left implied. [L1438.057]

### Cancellation rights for pricing errors

- Use a written return and exchange policy that states you have the right to cancel and not fulfill an order when a pricing mistake was made. [L1472.021]
- Put this in your terms before any pricing error happens. [L1472.021]

#### Further details

- Use one general return policy, typically the policy most suppliers share, such as a 30-day return for undamaged products. Place outlier brand policies below the general policy on the shipping and returns page, including non-returnable or extended-return brands. [L0471.034]

## Processing returns, refunds and exchanges

### Return policy, ownership and who pays

- Publish a clear return policy that states a return address and who pays return shipping; then refuse fraudulent claims, because a clear policy makes refusal defensible. [L0335.038]
- Set your return policy at least as competitive as those of your competitors. [L1113.041]
- Return responsibilities follow the supplier agreement made at approval, not who ships the order. Check that agreement, and ask the supplier if the return process is not stated. [L0803.018]
- If you ship on your own account and a customer returns an item, create the return label through your carrier and send it directly to the customer. Whether the item goes back to the supplier warehouse depends on the supplier's return policy. [L0803.019] *(older: 2022)*
- Many suppliers do not accept returns, so set up return addresses on your side for customers returning items, and record these addresses in the accounts sheet. [L1000.058]
- Do not set up a process that requires shipping returned items to yourself and reselling them. It is messy; match the supplier's policy and keep exclusions in your general return policy. [L0835.102] *(older: 2023)*
- Do not use a personal home address as the return address when using Buy with Google, because the address is shown to the customer and returns can go there if they do not contact you first. Consider carefully whether to use Buy with Google at all. [L1090.120] *(older: 2021)*
- Keep unsold returned items on a list. An assistant can offer them to customers at a lower price when the product is in stock again. [L1000.059]

### Change-of-mind returns and category rules

- Returns are accepted in three categories: change of mind, damaged in shipping, and faulty or under warranty. If a return claim fits none of these, inform the person responsible for returns before deciding. [L1291.016]
- A change-of-mind return is only possible when all of the following apply: the claim is made within 7 days of delivery; the customer pays and arranges the return shipping; the return is for store credit only (no refunds are offered); and the goods are in their original packaging. Requests outside these conditions go to the person responsible. [L1291.017]
- A change-of-mind claim must be submitted within 7 days of the order being delivered. [L1291.018]
- Processing an approved change-of-mind return:
  1. Once the claim is approved, give the customer the return shipping address, which is the original supplier.
  2. Notify the supplier that a return is coming.
  3. Do not let the customer use or receive the store credit until the supplier confirms the goods arrived in good order.
  4. After the supplier confirms safe delivery, process any re-order from the customer in the normal way.
  [L1291.019]
- Store credit from a change-of-mind return cannot be approved or used until the supplier has confirmed that the returned goods were received in good order. [L1291.020]

### Supplier return workflows (RMA)

- A return requires an RMA number, which the customer requests from the store before sending the item back. Questions about a product's return policy are answered within 24 hours, and refunds go to the original credit card used for the order. [L0556.022] *(older: 2021-22)*
- Benchmark: a competitor's return process typically issues a return authorisation within 2 business days, and where the item qualifies for a free return it also sends reply-paid postage details. Record this response time as a benchmark for your own process. [L0893.026] *(older: 2021-22)*

**Standard supplier flow, version A** (procedure with a 30-day label window):
1. The customer emails the store requesting a return.
2. You contact the supplier with the order number and the return request.
3. The supplier issues a return shipping label, usually within a return window such as 30 days stated in the supplier agreement.
4. Attach the label to the package; the carrier picks it up and returns it to the supplier warehouse.
5. After the supplier receives the item, refund the customer or exchange the product.

[L0469.103] *(older: 2021)*

**Supplier flow, version B** (customer pays return shipping by default):
1. Customer initiates a return request with your company.
2. Contact the supplier with the customer order number and return reason.
3. Request a return shipping label from the supplier via email.
4. Provide the return shipping label to the customer.
5. Customer ships the product back to the supplier (customer typically pays return shipping unless the supplier policy specifies otherwise).
6. Supplier refunds your company.
7. You refund the customer or offer store credit based on customer preference.

[L0251.007] *(2023)*

**Supplier flow, version C** (supplier label, refund after receipt):
1. The customer emails the store with a return request at the address listed on the returns policy page.
2. The store acknowledges receipt of the request.
3. The store asks the supplier for a return shipping label for that order number.
4. The supplier sends the label, and the store emails it to the customer.
5. The customer attaches the label, the package is picked up, and it is shipped back to the supplier.
6. The supplier refunds the store, and the store then refunds the customer.

[L0667.024] *(2025)*

**Supplier flow, version D** (drop-shipped item, broken):
1. The customer emails the store to report a broken item and asks for a refund or return.
2. The store emails the supplier and asks for a return shipping label.
3. The supplier sends the return label to the store.
4. The store sends the label to the customer, who ships the item back.
5. The item returns to the supplier's warehouse.
6. The supplier refunds the store, and the store refunds the customer.

[L0853.058] *(older: 2021)*

**Supplier flow, version E** (customer requests, brand label, direct to warehouse):
1. Customer requests a return.
2. Contact the brand and request a return shipping label.
3. The brand sends the label to the customer.
4. The customer ships the item to the supplier's warehouse.
5. The customer is refunded.

[L1111.127] *(older: 2020)*

**Standard supplier flow, version F** (item goes directly to warehouse):
1. Customer asks for a return.
2. Retailer contacts the supplier with the order number.
3. Supplier sends a return shipping label to the retailer.
4. Retailer sends the label to the customer.
5. Customer ships the item back, and it goes directly to the supplier's warehouse.
6. Supplier credits the retailer, and the retailer refunds the customer.

[L1283.002] *(2023)*

**Generic flow** (summary of the seven-step pattern):
1. The customer requests a return.
2. You notify the supplier.
3. The supplier sends a return shipping label.
4. The customer ships the item back.
5. You refund the customer, and the supplier refunds you.

[L0247.092] *(older: 2021)*

- Supplier return request email (use for each return; replace the bracketed fields):

```
Subject: Return authorization request, order [order number]

Hi [supplier rep name],

A customer from order [order number] would like to return [product name]. Could you please issue a return authorization number for this return and send the return shipping label directly to the customer?

Thank you,
[your name]
[store name]
```

[L1002.058] *(older: 2019)*

- For suppliers with different return policies, keep one catch-all shipping and returns template for suppliers that share a policy. Create a separate template for a supplier with its own policy and show it in the shipping and returns section of that supplier's product pages. [L1002.059] *(older: 2019)*

### Supplier-side problems: proof, reshipping and missing labels

- Handling refunds and returns with a supplier:
  1. Collect proof that something went wrong, such as the product is broken, incorrect or not delivered.
  2. Ask the supplier for a refund or a free reship when proof exists; good suppliers will do this.
  3. If the product is returned, confirm the return address and contact details before reshipping.
  4. Reship costs are lower than shipping a new parcel from China, so reshipping is often the better option.
  5. Contact the supplier in parallel with answering the customer, without making a definite promise to the customer yet.
  6. Ask the supplier once for their refund policy and publish a link on your store so customers can see the terms.

  [L0780.032]
- When a supplier cannot deliver a return label or the logistics are not working, use this wording. Present it as a planned process, not as a free giveaway, so customers do not learn that they can skip returns and word does not spread through the same postcode:

```
Sure, absolutely, we will refund you now. At the moment our logistics are not working for us, so we will refund you in this instance and send your return label once the process is working again.
```

[L0552.002]
- If a customer says they have no return label and asks what to do with the item, suggest they gift it to someone who could benefit from it, or donate it to a local charity or shelter. Customers usually respond well to this, and it turns the refund into a positive story for the brand. [L0552.003]

### Refund timing and confirmation

- Refunds are confirmed to the customer by email, and the money is credited to the original credit card within 5 to 7 business days of the refund being processed. Tell the customer this timeframe in every refund reply. [L0911.012]
- Timing conflict: the Source C-sourced material uses 5 to 7 business days for card refunds, while the brands in the Source D 2026 examples promised 5 to 10 business days, depending on the bank's processing time. Use 5 to 7 business days as the standard in replies when your card processor and bank data support it; otherwise use the 5 to 10 business day window, and put the same refund window in your refund policy and in replies. [L0911.012, L0405.025, L1164.024]
- Refund-timing wording used by the Source C examples: "5-7 business days, depending on your bank or card issuer." [L0405.025, L0405.026]
- Refund process after a supplier return: the supplier refunds the store, and the store then refunds the customer. Refund the customer only once the supplier has received the item or confirmed the goods. [L0667.024, L0469.103, L1291.019]

### Refund emails and reply templates

- Refund reply template for a delivered order where the product quality is poor. Replace the bracketed fields:

```
Hello [NAME],

Thanks for reaching out, I'm happy to help.

I'm sorry the [PRODUCT] did not live up to your expectations. We aim to give every customer a great experience with [STORE NAME], but we don't always succeed. Our refund policy still applies, and we want to make this right for you.

I have issued a full refund for your order. You should see a confirmation email shortly. The money should return to your credit card within 5-7 business days, depending on your bank or card issuer.

You are welcome to keep the [PRODUCT].

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any other questions or concerns.

Best wishes,
[AGENT NAME]
[STORE NAME] Customer Support Representative
```

[L0405.025]

- Refund reply template for a delivered order where the delivery time was unsatisfactory:

```
Hello [NAME],

Thanks for reaching out, I'm happy to help.

I'm sorry the delivery time did not meet your expectations. We aim to give every customer a great experience with [STORE NAME], but we don't always succeed. Our refund policy still applies, and we want to make this right for you.

I have issued a full refund for your order. You should see a confirmation email shortly. The money should return to your credit card within 5-7 business days, depending on your bank or card issuer.

Please feel free to keep your [PRODUCT].

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any other questions or concerns.

Best wishes,
[AGENT NAME]
[STORE NAME] Customer Support Representative
```

[L0405.026]

- Shorter reply template for a shipping-time complaint (single paragraph; replace the bracketed fields):

```
Hi [customer name], thanks for getting in touch, happy to help. I'm sorry the shipping duration didn't meet your expectations. We aim to give every customer a great experience, yet we don't always get it right. Still, our refund policy stands, and I want to resolve this for you, so I've issued a complete refund for your order. A confirmation email should arrive soon, and the amount should return to your credit card within five to seven business days. You're welcome to keep the [product name]. Hopefully this helps. Should you have further questions or concerns, don't hesitate to reach out. Best wishes, [agent name], [store name] Customer Support Representative
```

[L0911.011]

- Structure for a reply to a delivered order with unhappy product quality (structure only; write the text in your own words): thank them and say you are happy to help; apologise that the product did not meet expectations; say the store aims for a great experience but sometimes falls short; state that the store stands by its refund policy and wants to make it right; confirm a full refund has been processed and that an email confirmation will arrive shortly; say the charge should return to the credit card within 5-7 business days, depending on the bank; tell the customer they may keep the product; invite further questions; sign off as the store customer support representative. [L0405.012]
- Structure for a reply to a delivered order with unhappy shipping time (same structure as above, with the complaint about shipping time): thank them and say you are happy to help; apologise that the shipping time was not satisfactory; say the store aims for a great experience but sometimes falls short; state that the store stands by its refund policy and wants to make it right; confirm a full refund has been processed and that an email confirmation will arrive shortly; say the charge should return to the credit card within 5-7 business days, depending on the bank; tell the customer they may keep the product; invite further questions; sign off as the store customer support representative. [L0405.013]
- If an order has been delivered and the customer is unhappy with it, you can issue a full refund and let the customer keep the product, so no return is required. Tell the customer the refund has been processed and that the card credit can take 5 to 7 business days. [L0911.019]

### Partial refunds and keep-the-item deals

- Partial refunds in Shopify (procedure; *older: 2019*):
  1. Go to the order details in Shopify.
  2. Locate the refund section.
  3. Click "Partial refund" (not "Full refund").
  4. Enter the refund amount (for example, $100 off the full product price).
  5. Confirm the refund.

  Do not accidentally select the full refund option. [L0243.025]
- When a customer asks for a return, try to offer a deal to keep the item first, since that is easier than sending it back. [L1113.042] *(older: 2022)*
- For a refund request without a defect, charge the customer for return shipping. Alternatively, offer a partial refund of around 30 to 50 percent so the customer keeps the item. [L0352.026]
- When negotiating a refund where the customer keeps the item, aim for break-even so the seller does not lose money on the order. A 50 percent refund was used in practice. [L0352.027]
- Return shipping for a US customer typically costs about 15 to 20 USD, which often exceeds the value of a cheap product. Quote this real cost to the customer when explaining why a return is not worth it. [L1128.005]
- Handling a return request when return shipping is high:
  1. Apologise and explain that shipping the item back to the US is expensive, quoting a realistic rate of about 15 to 20 USD.
  2. If the mistake was yours, send a free replacement.
  3. If the customer is not at fault, offer a replacement in which the customer pays only shipping, for example about 7 to 8 USD, while you cover the product cost.
  4. If the customer insists on a refund and does not want a replacement, offer a partial refund that is lower than the sale price by the return shipping cost, and let the customer keep the product.

  [L1128.006]
- Example: for a product sold at 50 USD where return shipping would cost the customer 20 USD, offer a partial refund of 30 USD and let the customer keep the item, avoiding the trip to the post office and the wait for the return. The seller stated this may not be the best method, and customers accepted it with mixed reactions. [L1128.007]
- For a low-cost product where return shipping costs 15 to 20 USD, a replacement with the customer paying about 7 to 8 USD for shipping was accepted by most customers. Partial refunds drew more complaints. Lead with the paid-shipping replacement option. [L1128.027]
- When you handle return and replacement emails yourself, read the customer's first message to judge whether they will accept paying for shipping. Offer a paid-shipping replacement to those who seem willing, and a free replacement or a refund to those who do not. [L1128.028]
- Landed cost of a cheap item shipped to the US: supplier price (about 2 to 3 USD) + shipping to the US (about 5 USD) = about 7 to 8 USD. If the customer pays about 7 to 8 USD for shipping on a free replacement, the seller's cost is covered. [L1128.029]

### Store credit and exchange-first returns

- When customers request refunds, offer store credit instead. Store credit keeps revenue on your books, retains the customer within your ecosystem, and lets you fulfil their purchase need with an alternative product or brand you control, maintaining the sale. [L0309.011]
- Return credit options in Loop: store credit delivers a gift card code by email once the return is set up, while a refund to the original payment method is issued minus applicable fees. Refund timing varies. [L0955.032]
- Choose the model that fits the return type:
  - Change-of-mind returns under the 7-day rule are store credit only. [L1291.017]
  - Loop's exchange-first model offers refund or exchange, with bonus credit on refunds. [L0955.033, L0955.034]

### Exchange-first logic in Loop (Checkout Plus)

- Customer return flow with Checkout Plus:
  1. The customer enters the order number and zip code.
  2. Loop detects that the customer is covered for a free return.
  3. The customer selects the return reason and the item to return.
  4. The summary page removes the handling fee for a customer who opted in.
  5. The customer submits the return and chooses store credit or a refund to the original payment method.
  6. The customer buys a label from the preferred carrier, and the label is billed to the brand's FedEx or USPS account.
  7. The customer attaches the label and ships the item back.

  [L0955.031]
- Exchange-first return logic in Loop:
  1. The shopper selects the item to return.
  2. The shopper gives a reason, such as too big, too small or did not like it.
  3. The shopper chooses refund or exchange.
  4. If the shopper wants a refund, Loop offers bonus credit to shop again now.

  [L0955.033]
- A bonus credit of about $5 or $10 for shopping again, added on top of the refund value, can turn a refund into an exchange. The credit works across the full catalogue. [L0955.034]
- Shoppers who want an item in a different size are more likely to exchange than to refund. This is why the return reason question comes before the refund-or-exchange choice. [L0955.035]
- Shoppers who pay for free returns in Loop's model are not charged the handling fee at return. Those who did not opt in pay the handling fee on return. [L0955.036]

### Cross-border returns

- Returns from a customer in another country are usually sent to a local return centre, and the customer pays return shipping. This applies in the UK, the Netherlands and elsewhere. [L0660.034]
- Global return solutions are lacking in dropshipping. Returning a product to a facility where it can be handled matters most for fashion, because fashion return ratios are higher. [L0780.033]
- Returns from overseas dropshipping suppliers are very hard to process. Some stores absorb the cost of a return instead of chasing the supplier, especially when the return is requested after the order has already shipped. [L1315.060]
- Refund process for a customer who requests a refund:
  1. Check whether the customer is in the same country as the store's target market.
  2. If yes, ask the customer to send the product back so it can be resold.
  3. If no, which is the usual case, tell the customer to keep the product.
  4. Refund the customer if the reason for the request is valid.

  [L1439.029]

### Refund abuse and requests outside policy

- Most customers do not abuse refund policies. The minority who do is small, and generous service tends to pay off in brand goodwill. Design the service policy around the honest majority, and handle the few abusers with stricter rules only when they become a real cost. [L0552.004]
- Refund abuse without returning the item is a risk mainly for low-priced items, such as those under about $50. For expensive products it was not seen in practice. [L0970.133] *(2023)*
- Responding to a return request outside the policy:
  1. Send a polite first email that explains the policy.
  2. Include a screenshot of the return policy page and a link to it.
  3. If the customer stays unreasonable, consider accepting the return.

  [L0962.126] *(older: 2021)*
- Customers ask for returns of unopened product during a recall, and they get frustrated when refused. Define a clear recall and unopened-product return process before it is needed. [L1164.022]

## Damaged, defective, wrong or missing items and sizing problems

### Packaging check and photo evidence

- Have customers examine the packaging when items arrive and record any visible damage while signing for delivery. For damaged goods, they email photos to the returns address. [L0145.010]

```
Examine packaging when items arrive and document any visible damage while signing for delivery. For damaged goods, email photos to returns@YOURWEBSITE.com and we'll file an insurance claim on your behalf.
```
[L0145.010]

- For a non-working product, asking for evidence such as a short video showing the defect before accepting the return filters out claims that are not genuine. Many customers will not complete the extra step, which lowers refunds while the policy stays clear and fair. [L0955.052]
- Seller errors, such as a wrong item, a damaged item or an incorrect product photo, are handled under the competitor's seller-error rules. Record these separately from change-of-mind terms, because the customer is not charged in these cases. [L0893.046] (older advice, 2021-22)
- One competitor allowed 30 days from delivery to report a damaged item. This is a separate window from its change-of-mind period, so record each reporting window as its own value in the risk reversal column. [L0893.047] (older advice, 2021-22)

#### Photo request to the customer (damage in transit)

1. Apologize to the customer and ask for photos of the damage. [L1279.089] (older advice, 2021)
2. Ask the customer to take a photo right away, with a smartphone or camera, that clearly shows the damage to the product or the packaging. [L1291.021]
3. Ask the customer to email the photos to the company email address. [L1291.021]

#### Supplier photo request

- Ask the customer for a photo of the damage, then send the photo to the supplier and ask for a free replacement. [L0352.025]
- Send the photos to the supplier, which decides whether to ship a replacement part, a whole replacement item or a reshipment. [L1279.089] (older advice, 2021)

### Refusing delivery

- Add a clear instruction to the delivery notification, delivery page and shipment page on your website that the customer must refuse delivery if any damage is visible. [L1472.015]
- If the customer refuses the shipment and notes the damage on the packing slip, the carrier returns the item to the shipper. [L1472.015]
- Refusal and acceptance are two different paths. Where the customer accepted the shipment, the supplier may ask for photos as proof, and there is usually a short window for such claims. [L1472.015]
- Your documentation and refusal instructions must match: when damage is visible, the sign-for-delivery step (documenting damage and accepting the parcel) and the refusal step (refusing the parcel so it returns to the shipper) can both be used, depending on what the customer chooses. [L0145.010, L1472.015]

#### Procedure: damaged item where the customer refused delivery

1. Add a clear instruction to the delivery notification, delivery page and shipment page on your website that the customer must refuse delivery if any damage is visible. [L1472.015]
2. If the customer refuses the shipment and notes the damage on the packing slip, the carrier returns the item to the shipper. [L1472.015]
3. Email the supplier right away with the order details and the damage, and request a replacement. [L1472.015]
4. If the customer accepted the shipment instead, the supplier may ask for photos as proof, and there is usually a short window for such claims. [L1472.015]
5. Reply to the customer politely and apologetically, without blaming them, and tell them you are handling it. [L1472.015]
6. Act on the issue as soon as it happens, because fast action shortens the replacement lead time; in one case the issue was resolved within a day. [L1472.015]

Customer email template for a refused damaged delivery:

```
Hi {customer_name},

I am very sorry that your {product_name} arrived damaged, and I understand how frustrating that is. Thank you for refusing the delivery and noting the damage, which was exactly the right step. I have already contacted the manufacturer and am requesting a replacement as quickly as possible. I will keep you updated at every step.

Thank you for your patience and understanding.

{your_name}
{store_name}
```
[L1472.016]

- Damage in transit is never the store owner's fault, but the owner must still resolve it and replace the item quickly. Customers who are told they can refuse delivery and who are handled politely usually accept the outcome. [L1472.017]

### Supplier replacements and refunds

#### Who bears the cost

- Defective products should be refunded or replaced by the supplier, not by the store owner. In over 10 years of operation, no supplier has refused such a request on thousands of orders, but you should still ask your suppliers. [L0551.073] (older advice, 2020)
- Defective or damaged goods are the supplier's responsibility, and the replacement is shipped by the supplier rather than the dropship store. [L0626.004]
- When a working product confuses the buyer during setup, the customer contacts the retailer, not the supplier, so the store must budget for that support. Only defective or damaged items go back to the supplier, which ships a replacement. [L0626.003]
- Even when a supplier accepts no returns, confirm in writing that damaged or defective items qualify for a refund or replacement. Then state the no-return rule clearly on each affected product page so the customer knows before buying. [L0664.087] (older advice, 2020)

#### Procedure: product differs from the description (older)

1. Identify the problem: for example the product differed from the description on the site. [L0468.143] (older advice, 2020)
2. Contact the supplier and ask whether it will replace the item, ship the correct product or refund. [L0468.143] (older advice, 2020)
3. Decide case by case whether to offer a refund, replacement or the correct product. [L0468.143] (older advice, 2020)
4. Document the outcome in the supplier notes. [L0468.143] (older advice, 2020)

#### Procedure: cross-border returns and refunds

1. For damaged products, refund the customer and let them keep the item. [L0678.034]
2. For size complaints, point them to the size guide on the store. [L0678.034]
3. Make sure the store has a detailed size guide. [L0678.034]
4. If the mistake was the seller's own, refund the customer. [L0678.034]

Note: step 1 (refund and keep the item) differs from the supplier-replacement rules above. Use it where the cross-border policy applies; elsewhere the supplier replacement applies. [L0678.034, L0626.004]

#### Procedure: damaged or non-working items (supplier refund)

1. Ask the customer for a photo or proof of the fault. [L1219.054]
2. Refund the customer if the fault is confirmed. [L1219.054]
3. Request the refund from the supplier, for example CJ, because the product did not meet the promise. [L1219.054]

Note: this procedure refunds the customer, while the supplier-replacement procedures ship a replacement. Choose the path that matches the customer's preference and the supplier's answer. [L1219.054, L1279.089, L1472.015]

#### Procedure: AliExpress shortcut

1. For a damaged item, ask the customer for a photo of the damage. [L0352.025]
2. Send the photo to the supplier and ask for a free replacement. [L0352.025]
3. For AliExpress, email them with a screenshot of the customer message and they usually refund automatically with free returns. [L0352.025]
4. If needed, offer the customer a discounted second item as the replacement. [L0352.025]

#### Disputed removal of the damaged unit

Procedure for a damaged-delivery dispute where the supplier shipped a replacement but did not remove the damaged unit and the customer wants removal:

1. Ask the supplier to share the removal cost. [L0971.047]
2. Offer the customer a partial refund of $50 to $100 so they can have the old unit hauled away. [L0971.047]
3. Keep the relationship with the supplier intact. [L0971.047]

### Carrier insurance and claims

#### Insurance rules

- Confirm that the supplier insures shipments, because insurance is what lets you file a claim for an item damaged in transit. After the claim pays out, the value can be recovered. [L0667.022]
- Shipments should be insured. For a damaged item, a customer claim supported by the insurance can allow the item to be disposed of rather than shipped back. [L0970.132]
- Every shipper used should insure its packages, so rely on shipping insurance for transit damage. [L1279.089] (older advice, 2021)
- For a damaged item, the shipping insurance covers the loss, whether the supplier shipped on their account or yours. For a change-of-mind return, the customer's return is governed by your return policy. [L1285.067]
- Shipping damage that happens in transit counts as a shipping issue rather than a customer return. Whether the customer pays for return shipping and whether there is a restocking fee are policy decisions set by the competitor benchmark. [L0805.030]
- Lost or damaged parcels are covered by carrier insurance. [L0276.053]

#### Package protection

- Package protection covers lost, damaged and stolen parcels during delivery, as well as a free return. This coverage helps keep the customer relationship intact after a delivery problem. [L0955.037]
- US merchants offer and use package protection more widely than Australian merchants, where trust in the national carrier is high. Australian brands are still raising awareness of it. [L0955.038]

#### Customer claim message

```
If your order arrives damaged, please contact us at [support email] within [number] days of delivery with photos of the damaged box and the product. We will file a claim with the shipping carrier on your behalf. Once the claim is approved, we will ship you a replacement item.
```
[L0667.091]

#### Full procedure: damaged or defective order in shipping or at the factory

1. Ask the customer to take a photo right away, with a smartphone or camera, that clearly shows the damage to the product or the packaging. [L1291.021]
2. Ask the customer to email the photos to the company email address. [L1291.021]
3. If the customer has opened the packaging, ask them to put back everything they removed and reseal it. [L1291.021]
4. If the packaging is damaged, ask the customer to photograph the damage, then open it carefully and inspect the product. If the product is fine, the process ends here. If the product is damaged, ask them to photograph the damage to the item and then reseal the packaging. [L1291.021]
5. Contact the relevant supplier by phone or email to report the damage, and email the photos to the supplier. [L1291.021]
6. If the supplier booked the shipping, ask the supplier to arrange a replacement and to collect the damaged product if it wants to. The supplier may ask the customer to dispose of the damaged item, which is acceptable. [L1291.021]
7. If your business booked the shipping, first ask the supplier to replace the item with you booking the shipping again. If the supplier refuses because you booked the shipping, ask the supplier to prepare a replacement for dispatch, then arrange shipping as normal. [L1291.021]
8. File an insurance claim with the shipping carrier following its instructions. [L1291.021]
9. Keep the customer updated throughout the whole process. [L1291.021]

- Keep the customer informed at every stage of a damaged-in-shipping claim, from the first photo request until the replacement or insurance outcome is known. [L1291.022]
- If a customer reports damage after using the product for several weeks, there is no fixed rule, so decide case by case. [L1279.089] (older advice, 2021)

### Warranty eligibility

- All products carry a 2-year warranty, so faulty items within that period can be checked for a warranty claim. [L1291.023]

#### Procedure: is a faulty product eligible?

1. Ask the customer how they have been using the product and what the fault is. Note down their answers. [L1291.024]
2. First contact the relevant supplier to confirm the warranty claim process. [L1291.024]
3. If the supplier agrees the circumstances qualify, ask who honours the warranty: the supplier or the original manufacturer, if these are separate entities. [L1291.024]
4. If the supplier is responsible, ask the supplier to replace the product. If the supplier wants to collect the faulty product, contact the customer and ask them to get it ready for pickup. [L1291.024]
5. If the original manufacturer is responsible, the customer may need to lodge the warranty claim directly with the manufacturer. Get the manufacturer's contact details and give them to the customer. [L1291.024]
6. If either side disputes the process or the status of a warranty claim, inform the responsible person and ask for guidance on the next step. [L1291.024]

- Warranty disputes about the process or the status of a claim must be escalated to the person responsible for guidance before any further action. [L1291.025]

### Missing parts and late shipments

- For lost or damaged items, the carrier insurance applies. [L0276.053]
- For missing parts, the ideal outcome is that the customer accepts a replacement shipment. The alternative is a partial refund proportional to the missing items. [L0276.053]
- For late shipments, use the replacement or refund approach. [L0276.053]
- In all scenarios, respond immediately. Customers accept problems when they hear from you quickly. [L0276.053]

### Heavy items

- For very heavy items, around 150 pounds for some appliances, returning the product is impractical for the buyer. The better fix is to have the supplier pick up the damaged unit and ship a replacement as soon as possible, rather than asking the buyer to dispose of it. [L1472.066]
- Note the conflict: for a damaged unit the supplier may allow the customer to dispose of it, which is acceptable for standard shipments. For very heavy items, use the supplier pickup and replacement from L1472.066 instead. [L1291.021, L1472.066]

### Sizing and fashion returns

#### Decision rule

- For a size problem, refund the customer and let them keep the item instead of paying for a return. The refund is cheaper than the return shipping. [L1431.053]

#### Procedure: fashion sizing returns

1. Ask the customer to send proof that the item is too big or too small. [L1161.016]
2. Once the proof is received, decide based on the situation whether to refund the money or send a replacement in the correct size. [L1161.016]
3. Make the choice that makes more sense for the store at that moment. [L1161.016]

#### Footwear and other sized products

- Sizing issues cause a significant share of refunds in footwear. Communicate sizing clearly on the product page and with the supplier to reduce returns. [L1439.031]
- For wrong-size shoes, check the customer's centimeter measurement and the size shipped. If the supplier sent the wrong size, refund the customer. [L1219.055]
- For clothing and other sized products, expect refunds from sizing issues and plan for them. Treat sized products as having a higher refund rate than standard items. [L1172.050, L1172.051]
- Stretch fabrics can reduce the impact of small fit differences, but sizing remains the most important factor for returns. [L1172.051]

#### Choosing products

- Placing the size chart in three places on the product listing still did not stop buyers from choosing the wrong size. Clear size guidance alone is not enough, so pick products that need little or no size selection. [L1128.032]

### Size guides

- Make the size guide accurate and communicate sizing clearly on apparel products. This keeps wrong-size orders from becoming the store's fault. [L1171.047]
- For clothing and other sized products, provide a detailed size chart with all measurements, agree the numbers with the supplier and check the sizes used in the target country. [L1172.050]
- A no-refunds policy can be added to the landing page, but a good size guide on the store is essential, because a missing size guide is a strong reason for customers to return items. [L0678.035]
- For size complaints, point the customer to the size guide on the store, and make sure the store has a detailed size guide. [L0678.034]

## Reducing return and refund rates

### Set the return target and measure it correctly

- Two metrics are in use, and they are not the same. A **return rate** is the share of orders sent back. A **refund rate** is the share of sales refunded. The targets below use different ones, so check which one a benchmark measures before comparing. [L0467.005, L0253.009]
- For premium products sold at premium prices, a return rate of 1 to 2 percent is normal and a good target. Some niches run higher, but 2 percent is a safe planning ceiling. (Older advice, 2019.) [L0467.005]
- For refunds, aim for under 1 percent over a long period, calculated over the whole period and not per 10 items. Damaged items that need a replacement are excluded from this calculation. [L0253.009]
- Track the refund rate per product as a quality measure, because a low refund rate suggests strong product satisfaction. In one example store, about 410 orders were placed without a single refund. [L0492.041]
- Track returns and cancelled orders, and sales discounts, each as a separate percentage of gross sales every month, so a rise in returns is not hidden inside the sales total. In the example store, returns and cancelled orders of 237,813 equalled about 13 percent of gross sales of 1,826,410, and sales discounts of 34,197 were about 1.9 percent. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022.) [L1046.056]
- For fashion, check the net sales after returns before deciding whether a product is viable. [L0693.055]

**Benchmarks at a glance**

| Benchmark | Figure | Applies to | Status | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Normal return rate | 1 to 2%, 2% planning ceiling | Premium products at premium prices | Older (2019) | L0467.005 |
| Long-run refund rate | Under 1%, excluding damaged replacements | Products generally | 2024 | L0253.009 |
| Established fashion brand | About 1 in 5 orders (return or size change), about EUR 30,000 to 35,000 per year | Fashion, established brand | Undated | L0660.031 |
| Fashion brand, typical | About 20 to 25%, varies by month and volume | Fashion brand with accurate ads, strong imagery and a quality product | Undated | L1438.030 |
| Apparel, high | 35 to 40% per year | Low-priced markdown and impulse apparel | Older (2019) | L0467.006 |
| Holiday gifts, high | 40 to 45% | Low-priced markdown and impulse gifts | Older (2019) | L0467.006 |
| Apparel, example | Over 30% (Victoria's Secret) | Apparel | Older (2020) | L0245.064 |
| Store example | About 13% of gross sales (returns and cancellations) | Example store | Older (2021 to 2022) | L1046.056 |

### Choose niches and suppliers by return risk

- Research the expected return rate for your niche before committing. Start with brand reviews on Google, and look up supplier names on retailer sites for reviews. (Older advice, 2020 and 2022.) [L0245.064, L0249.069]
- Look for patterns of complaints about damage, quality inconsistency and defects. [L0249.069]
- Before signing a supplier, check its brand reviews for complaints about damage, wrong colours, or items that differ from the photos, because these signal a high return rate. [L0667.025]
- A supplier with a high return rate is a product quality problem. Stop selling its products rather than covering the losses with restocking fees. [L0667.026]
- Skip any niche where high returns are expected. Returns cost shipping, support time and revenue at the same time. (Older advice, 2019.) [L0663.004]
- Avoid building a store around products where delivery and returns depend on slow or unreliable chains, because a poor customer experience leads to disputes and loss of repeat customers. (Older advice, 2019.) [L0357.063]
- Avoid niches where customers have strong emotional attachment and tight deadlines. A late or failed delivery can ruin an event and cause severe complaints. Products that must arrive by a fixed date carry much higher service risk. [L0766.005]
- Avoid mattresses, bed sheets and pillows for dropshipping unless the seller is a brand with very high margins. Feel, softness and stiffness cannot be shown on a website, so these personalised items have very high return rates that cost time, labour and money. [L0766.013]
- Products with high return rates or that customers often ask about, such as electronics and apparel, should be avoided, since they need more support and return handling. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0801.123]
- A store with a physical showroom can reduce returns by helping customers choose the right product in person. It can sell online only the brands whose return policies allow it. (Older advice, 2021.) [L0801.125]
- For fashion, returns are common and can be acceptable if sales exceed returns. [L0693.055]
- Sizing-dependent fashion creates high return rates because customers expect Amazon-level return policies. Dropshipping cannot sustainably support sizing-dependent products. [L0209.038]

### Product types with specific refund risks

**Low-priced and impulse products**

- Low-priced markdown products and impulse purchases drive very high reported return rates. Premium products bought after more thought return far less often. (Older advice, 2019.) [L0467.006]
- Very cheap novelty items, around $13 or less, are less likely to be returned, because customers often do not bother sending back a low-value product. Check this against your own return rate before relying on it. [L0655.027]
- The two observations do not conflict. Items under about $13 are returned less often because return shipping is not worth the effort. Low-priced markdown and impulse purchases are returned more often. Apply the $13 rule only after checking your own rate. [L0655.027, L0467.006]
- Gimmicky products carry high refund risk because buyers are often disappointed by the product's real quality. Plan for refund handling and dispute management from the start. [L1211.016]

**Digital products**

- Refund requests for a digital product are a direct signal of low content quality, and they show where the product needs to improve. [L0513.044]
- Make sure the content is accurate and useful before launch, because poor content is what triggers refunds. [L0513.044]

**Assembly-heavy products**

- Include supplier videos showing assembly time, and photos of what the packaged goods look like when delivered. Set customer expectations upfront to reduce returns and complaints. (Older advice, 2022.) [L0249.067]

**Fashion and footwear**

- Some buyers wear fashion items for a weekend and return them with the tags still on, which causes chargebacks. Plan return rules for clothing with this in mind. [L1214.030]
- Bracketing (buying several sizes to keep one) and wardrobing (buying for a single use and returning) push return costs up. Strategic friction in the return policy or at purchase filters out customers who return for no reason without breaking loyal relationships. [L0955.004]
- Categories where the product may differ from the photos, such as jewellery or clothing with sizing or quality variance, cause refund-risk hesitation. [L1208.007]
- For shoes, state clearly on the product page that stock is limited and that returns are not accepted. This discourages buying one pair to send back for another size. Expect that some wrong-size cases will still need a refund. [L1219.007]
- Sizing issues can cause returns, especially for shoes and footwear. Plan refunds into the margin. [L1439.030]

**Electronics**

- Electronics carry a high risk of chargebacks and disputes when quality is poor. Test a new electronic product with the first week of customers, collect reviews and ask about quality before increasing spend. [L1218.029]

### Describe the product so the customer knows what arrives

- Accurate product descriptions and photos, plus staff notes that explain exactly what is in the product, reduce refund requests because customers know what they are buying. Clarity before purchase is the first refund preventer. [L0910.033]
- Sell only what fits the promises you make. Congruent purchases reduce buyer's remorse, refunds and chargebacks. [L0378.097]
- The brand with a typical 20 to 25 percent return rate credited its low returns to accurate product advertising, strong product imagery and a quality product that customers do not want to send back. [L1438.030]

### Set expectations on the sales page

- State customer service speed and the returns policy on the sales page, for example "fast customer service" and "easy returns", so the buyer knows who will help if something goes wrong. [L0919.045]
- Visible support lowers the fear of being left alone with a bad purchase. Place it next to the guarantee and secure checkout messages in the risk-removal section. [L0919.045]
- Reply to customer questions and complaints quickly to keep returns low. One store had no refunds because support was fast and problems were fixed for the customer. [L1439.028]
- A money-back guarantee shown on the product page must match the refund process you actually operate. Make sure customer support can process it without extra conditions the buyer was not told about. [L1188.036]
- A money-back guarantee needs fast, clear refund handling, because the guarantee is part of the offer and affects trust and conversion. [L0871.082]

### Choose the return policy: who pays for return shipping

Sources disagree on this. Each position applies in different conditions.

| Position | When it applies | Ids |
|---|---|---|
| Customer pays return shipping | Free returns raise the return rate and encourage return culture, especially when competitors offer fast delivery together with free returns. | L1438.029 |
| Customer pays return shipping (fashion, multiple markets) | Paid returns are now common in fashion, and customers in several countries accepted them after a switch from free returns. | L0660.032 |
| Customer pays a fee | About 64% of brands charged return fees to some extent in surveys cited for 2025. Shoppers accept fees when the process is easy. | L0955.002, L0955.003 |
| Seller pays return shipping | Use a full refund guarantee with seller-paid return shipping as the answer to dissatisfaction, and refund within the stated trial period. Customers who know the return route is simple are more likely to order. | L1369.102 |
| Free replacement, no questions | A policy that says no returns are needed and the product is replaced for free reads as a strong guarantee and can lift conversion. | L0577.069 |

- Shoppers accept return fees when the return process is easy. A fee combined with a hard, slow process damages the relationship. Free returns still make sense for loyalty or VIP customers and to attract first-time buyers. [L0955.003]
- Many consumers do not know how expensive returns and shipping are, so they abuse free returns when they are unaware. Making the cost of a return visible is part of keeping abuse down. [L0955.005]
- Surveys cited for 2025 found that in a survey of 1,000 consumers worldwide, about 70% said they would pay for a convenient, premium return experience. [L0955.002]
- Clear refund shipping costs deter buyers who would otherwise order and return, so some low-intent orders are lost on purpose. This is accepted because returns cost more than the lost sale. [L0910.032]
- Check reviews for a brand's products across websites to judge its return rate before deciding on a free-return policy. [L0964.102]
- Free returns can increase the return rate, so decide the policy against your own measured return rate, not on principle. [L1438.029, L0964.102]

### Choose refund windows and guarantee lengths

Sources disagree on length. Each applies in different conditions.

| Guarantee | When it applies | Ids |
|---|---|---|
| 14 days, money back | Unopened products or items with manufacturing defects. Show it prominently in Q4 to build confidence without triggering chargebacks, if the terms are clearly stated. | L0309.010 |
| 30 days, money back | Common standard. Must match the refund process you actually run. | L1439.030, L1188.036 |
| 30 days, with free return | Pair with a stated free-returns policy. | L0919.026 |
| 30 days, reminder | Remind buyers of free returns or the 30-day guarantee where product may differ from photos. | L1208.007 |
| 90 days, money back | Full refund if the product is returned within 90 days of receipt. State it on the page. | L1194.047 |

- A 90-day guarantee gives buyers a full refund if they return the product within 90 days of receiving it, and it should be stated on the page. [L1194.047]
- For approval or trial offers, most people are honest when they receive a product on approval, and losses from trials that are not paid for are very small. Offering approval or return rights rarely costs more than it earns in trust and sales. [L1261.121]
- Before offering a trial with a payment or return condition, check the cost of processing returns and the share of trials that are never paid for. Build those costs into the cost per customer. [L1261.123]
- Do not charge restocking fees if the main competitors do not charge them. [L0667.025]

### Remove the buyer's risk

- Risk reversal removes the buyer's fear of losing money. Common tools are a 30-day money-back guarantee with a free return, a 100% refund if not satisfied, and a stated free-returns policy. [L0919.026]
- A money-back guarantee works because buyers are loss averse: they fear losing money more than they value gaining a product. Reducing the downside of a purchase increases conversion more than merely highlighting the upside. [L1209.026]
- A returns policy that says no returns are needed and the product is replaced for free reads as a strong guarantee and can lift conversion. [L0577.069]
- Display the 14-day money-back guarantee prominently during Q4 to build confidence, provided the terms are clearly stated. [L0309.010]

### Build the return allowance into the margin

- Build a return allowance into the margin so refunds do not push individual sales into loss. Set the allowance from your expected return rate. [L0436.010]
- Plan refunds into the margin, because sizing issues can cause returns, especially for shoes and footwear. [L1439.030]
- Include the cost of processing returns and the share of trials that are never paid for in the cost per customer. [L1261.123]
- Returns are unavoidable in e-commerce, but they can be reduced, and reducing them is a core task. Plan for returns as a normal part of the business and work to minimise them. (Older advice, 2021 to 2022.) [L1480.026]
- Plan for refund handling and dispute management from the start, particularly for gimmicky products. [L1211.016]

### Keep the customers who return less

- Attract customers who want to wear the product for a long time and keep coming back, rather than customers who buy for a one-time occasion. Long-term customers are less likely to return items. [L1438.031]
- Accurate advertising, strong product imagery and a quality product that customers do not want to send back are the main reasons the brand with a 20 to 25 percent return rate gave for its lower returns. [L1438.030]

## Fraud screening and risky orders

### Shopify fraud analysis levels

- Shopify Payments ranks the fraud risk of each order through fraud analysis. Medium or high risk orders should be checked before they are shipped. [L0360.060]
- Shopify Fraud Analysis scores orders for fraud risk. Use it to review suspicious orders before fulfilling them and to reduce chargebacks. [L1095.011]
- Shopify's built-in fraud analysis flags high-risk orders, which usually have a reason to be high risk. Do not process flagged orders without first contacting the customer. [L0934.099]
- Shopify's fraud analysis rates orders low, medium, or high. A high rating is almost always fraud. A medium rating needs a check of the reason shown plus verification of the customer. [L0856.088]
- Shopify includes risk tools that flag orders likely to be fraud. Use them to reduce stolen-card chargebacks, which are a separate risk from delivery disputes. (Older advice, 2019) [L1086.064]
- The level scales differ between sources. Both are given below, and the 2019 scale is marked as older. [L0467.003, L0856.088]

| Source | Levels | Meaning and action | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024 | Low, medium, high | High is almost always fraud. Medium needs the shown reason checked and the customer verified. Check medium and high orders before shipping. | L0856.088, L0360.060 |
| 2019 (older) | No risk, moderate risk, probably fraudulent | Levels are based on card activity Shopify sees across its network. Probably fraudulent orders are not processed. | L0467.003 |

### Daily checks of new orders

1. Open each new order and read the fraud analysis risk rating that Shopify shows. [L0360.061]
2. For a medium or high risk order, contact the customer by phone or email before shipping. [L0360.061, L0360.060]
3. For any order you are not comfortable processing, call the phone number the customer entered before shipping. (Older advice, 2019) [L0467.002]
4. Check the order status and the fraud tool's reason regularly. Do not assume an order went through. [L0807.040]

### Verifying flagged orders by phone and email

#### Routine for medium and high risk orders (2024)

1. Check the fraud analysis risk rating that Shopify shows for each new order. [L0360.061]
2. For a medium or high risk order, contact the customer by phone or email before shipping. [L0360.061]
3. If the customer does not reply, cancel the order and send nothing, since fraudulent orders often use fake phone numbers. [L0360.061, L0960.079]

#### Routine for flagged orders (2023)

1. Call the customer to find out why the order was flagged. [L0934.100]
2. Confirm the identity and details. [L0934.100]
3. Process the order only if the risk is resolved. [L0934.100]
4. Decline the order if the customer cannot be verified. [L0934.100]

#### Chargeback prevention routine (2019, older)

1. Read the risk level that Shopify assigns to the order. [L0467.002]
2. For any order you are not comfortable processing, call the phone number the customer entered before shipping. [L0467.002]
3. If nobody answers or calls back, treat the order as a major red flag and do not ship it. [L0467.002]
4. Optionally add fraud protection, either Shopify's native option or the ClearSale app, so that fraud chargebacks on orders marked safe are covered by the provider. [L0467.002, L0467.004]

#### Routine for Shopify-flagged orders (2020, older)

1. Shopify fraud protection flags an order as high risk. [L1111.129]
2. Call the phone number the customer provided. [L1111.129]
3. If the number is disconnected or no one answers, treat it as a likely fraud case. [L1111.129, L0960.079]
4. If the customer answers and confirms, ask why the shipping and billing addresses differ. [L1111.129]
5. For large orders, request proof of billing address, such as a photo of a billing statement. [L1111.129]
- Orders that do not pass Shopify's built-in fraud protection must be checked before they are shipped. Contact the customer and try to verify the order by any means before you decide. (Older advice, 2020) [L0961.052]
- A phone number that goes unanswered after a suspicious order is a further warning sign. (Older advice, 2019) [L0960.079]

#### High-fraud orders: request for card and ID (2025)

1. Do not ship the order immediately. [L0472.049]
2. Email the customer, thank them, explain that a fraud alert was raised, and ask them to reply with a copy of the card used at checkout and a photo of their driver's license or ID. [L0472.049, L0472.078]
3. Ship only once both are received and the name on the card matches. [L0472.049]
4. Do not accept an order flagged "high fraud" without verification, even when the shipping address matches the billing address. A mismatched billing address and card holder is a warning sign. [L0472.050]

Email template (2025):

```
Hi [Customer name], thank you for your order with [Store name]. Our system has placed a fraud alert on this order. Sometimes these alerts are wrong, for example because an address was entered incorrectly, but before we ship your order, please reply to this email with a copy of the card you used at checkout, showing your name on the card, and a photo of your driver's license or ID. Once we have both, we can confirm that you are the cardholder and process your order. Thank you for your patience.

[Your name]
[Store name]
```

[L0472.078]

#### Declined or voided orders (2025)

- A fraud tool can void a transaction without telling the customer, even when the payment processor marks the order as safe. Check the order status and the fraud tool's reason regularly. [L0807.040]
- Handle an order flagged as fraud by the tool as follows:
  1. Find the exact reason the fraud tool gives for the decline. [L0807.041]
  2. Decide whether the flag looks justified, especially if the payment processor marked the order safe. [L0807.041]
  3. If it looks wrong, contact the customer and explain that the order was flagged for a reason, without blaming them. [L0807.041]
  4. Ask for verification, such as proof of address or ID, that matches the flag. [L0807.041]
  5. Process and ship the order again once verification arrives. [L0807.041]

### Suspicious order patterns

- Suspicious orders often come from emails that ask to pay with an unfamiliar method, such as QuickBooks, and to ship through the buyer's own carrier. Treat this as a likely scam, especially when the buyer wants expensive items shipped to a family member or a vacation home. [L0472.052]
- Fraudsters often enter fake phone numbers and do not answer calls. (Older advice, 2019) [L0960.079]

### Bots testing prices

- Bots that add the cheapest product to the cart repeatedly are often Google or Meta testing checkout prices against the product feed. Ignoring them is usually fine. [L0472.053]

### High-fraud regions

- For orders from high-fraud regions, such as the UAE, use Shopify's fraud protection tools, require strong payment confirmation, and remain cautious. (Older advice, 2020) [L0245.062]
- Shipping costs to these regions often equal or exceed the product price, which makes the orders uneconomical. (Older advice, 2020) [L0245.062]

### Fraud tools and chargeback insurance

- Shopify's native option and the ClearSale app are the two ways to transfer fraud-chargeback risk away from the merchant. [L0467.004]
- ClearSale independently verifies orders and covers the chargeback if an order it marked as safe turns out to be fraud. (Older advice, 2019) [L0467.004]
- ClearSale is a fraud-screening app for e-commerce orders. It reviews transactions to reduce fraudulent orders and chargeback losses. [L0984.005]
- ClearSale reimburses the money if an order it approved is later found fraudulent. One host did not use it personally. [L0804.093]
- Chargeback insurance services such as ClearSale pay out only when the provider approved the order as safe and it then turned out fraudulent. They do not cover all disputes. (Older advice, 2022) [L0969.037]
- Chargeback insurance services work with Shopify. The lesson pointed to one such tool without using it personally. [L0934.101]
- Rely on Shopify's built-in fraud protection and review any order it flags as high risk, including the reason. Some members also used the third-party chargeback app Signifyd early on, then stopped once they could spot risky orders themselves. [L0470.081]
- Some stores rely only on Shopify's built-in notifications and skip third-party fraud apps, while others use paid fraud tools. Choose based on your chargeback risk. (Older advice, 2021) [L0968.101]
- A chargeback on a stolen credit card is usually lost by the merchant if the order was shipped and no evidence can counter the claim, so the business absorbs the loss. Fraud protection and careful order checks reduce this exposure. (Older advice, 2019) [L0467.001]

### Cancelling when in doubt

- If you think an order might be fraud, treat it as fraud and cancel it. This rule of thumb prevents losses from suspicious orders. (Older advice, 2020) [L0961.053]
- If the customer does not reply to verification, cancel the order and send nothing. [L0360.061]
- If nobody answers or calls back, do not ship the order. [L0467.002]

## Preventing chargebacks and protecting the payment account

### Chargeback causes

- Late fulfillment and customers who believed the product was not authentic or not as described were the main causes in one documented case. Some customers also disputed charges after the brand owner publicly called the seller a scammer. [L0351.009]
- A low-quality product can lead to high chargebacks. Enough of them can get the payment processor to shut the account down, even after the store reaches high sales. Check quality before scaling. [L0335.034]
- Selling a seasonal product outside its season increases chargebacks, because buyers dispute orders for items they do not need in the current weather. Plan the sales window so the product is sold only while its season matches the buyer's need. [L0347.032]
- Dropshipping models with long delivery times and difficult returns carry more chargeback risk, because customers who wait weeks often dispute payments. (Older, 2019.) [L0357.056]
- Customers file chargebacks through their bank or card issuer, not through Shopify. The merchant receives a notification and can respond with evidence, but the card network or the bank decides the outcome. (Older, 2019.) [L1086.062]
- Chargebacks stay rare when products arrive quickly, the store responds to customers, and the product matches what the customer expected. Most chargeback losses come from delays and unclear product expectations. (Older, 2019.) [L1086.065]
- A chargeback can be lost even after delivery if a stolen card was used to order an item shipped to a reachable address. Prevent this with fraud prevention measures on the store, because evidence submitted after the dispute is often not enough. (Older, 2021.) [L1112.036]
- Higher order volume brings more returns, complaints and chargebacks, especially on Shopify Payments or Stripe. Products with thin margins become a risk as sales grow. [L0440.052]
- Orders paid with credit or debt carry higher chargeback risk. The store's economic exposure is higher during a downturn, when customers are panicking. [L1440.048]
- In fashion and streetwear, younger UK buyers (about 21 to 30) converted very well, but refunds and chargebacks were much higher with them. Older UK buyers were easier to sell to. [L1440.047]
- A supplier dispute or a quality problem can raise the PayPal dispute rate. Changing suppliers can therefore cause temporary spikes in disputes. [L1440.049]
- Most German buyers pay with PayPal. Poor customer support leads to many chargebacks in Germany. [L1184.049]
- Chargebacks rise during peak and holiday seasons. A single chargeback can threaten a small merchant. [L1231.047]
- Unsupported health claims may pass for a while, but they eventually cause trouble with platforms. When the promised result does not happen, customers become angry and more likely to return the product or dispute the charge. (Source B course, 2021-22.) [L0416.018]

### Chargeback rate thresholds

The sources give different figures because they describe different contexts. Use the reference that matches your account and payment method.

| Reference point | Value | When it applies | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Visa and Mastercard expectation | Below 1%, meaning no more than about 1 chargeback per 100 orders. Above that, card networks issue warnings and the processor may close the account. (Older, 2020.) | General card network rule | [L0468.140] |
| US Stripe and PayPal accounts | About 1% dispute rate described as the point of risk for holds or closure | US accounts, account-specific | [L1512.030] |
| Hong Kong accounts | Up to 6% described as tolerated (account-specific, verify before relying on it) | Hong Kong accounts only | [L1512.030] |
| Reserve case | 3.36% chargeback rate over the last 90 days led Shopify to place 10% of payouts in reserve | Shopify Payments store that had unfulfilled orders charged back | [L1327.017] |
| Example ratio | 17.5% for the period without alert prevention | Lesson example, not a benchmark | [L0351.012] |
| Occasional chargebacks | Two chargebacks across more than 1,000 orders | Treated as a normal cost of business that sales volume covers | [L0910.036] |
| Shopify shutdown trigger | Three chargebacks in one week | Can get a Shopify store shut down | [L1299.030] |

- The chargeback rate is disputes divided by orders. Raising average order value spreads the same number of disputes over more revenue, which is the main practical way to bring the rate back below 1%. [L0351.002]
- Keep chargeback rates low. A high chargeback ratio is one of the main triggers for a merchant account to hold a reserve. (Older, 2021.) [L0671.107, L0671.244]
- Excessive chargebacks can cause a payment provider to stop supporting a store. (Older, 2020.) [L1088.074]

### Account holds and closures

- Shopify rarely closes stores. Closures mostly happen for prohibited products or serious chargeback problems. (Older, 2021.) [L0671.106, L0671.243]
- Account closures for chargebacks are rare. They usually follow from unanswered customers, missed shipments or repeated fraud. To stay within the limits, respond to customers, ship on time and avoid prohibited products. (Older, 2020.) [L0468.141]
- Three chargebacks in one week can get a Shopify store shut down. Shopify may ban the store immediately, without refunding the money it holds. [L1299.030]
- A wrong Disputifier setup can let chargebacks through, which can lead to this situation. [L1299.030]

**Case: Stripe hold.** A seller's Stripe account was placed on a 30-day hold. The seller contacted customers early to resolve complaints, and the disputes were resolved quickly. About 20 days after the hold, the money was released, the dispute rate fell, and no further holds followed. [L1512.053]

**Case: PayPal hold.** A seller with PayPal holds at about 27,000 USD in volume uploaded fulfillment documents when requested, and the funds were released about a week later. The store also found that PayPal made up only about 5% of its payments. The seller paused PayPal for a few days and saw no drop in conversion. Judge holds against how much a payment method actually contributes to sales. [L1512.054]

### Prohibited products

- Products on Shopify's prohibited list, such as supplements, can cause the processor to cancel the account and hold funds. Check the prohibited products list on Shopify's legal page before listing a product. (Older, 2020.) [L0468.142]
- Avoid unsupported health claims. They create platform trouble and lead to angry customers who dispute charges. (Source B course, 2021-22.) [L0416.018]

### Responsiveness and proactive communication

- Not replying to customer emails is the most common cause of chargebacks. Answer every message quickly, reassure the buyer and show empathy. A customer who receives no answer will often dispute the charge. [L0352.022]
- Ignoring customers who ask where their order is leads to chargebacks. Even a reply that only explains a delay keeps the customer from disputing the payment. [L0661.050]
- Contact the customer as soon as a delay is known. Most chargebacks from legitimate customers can be avoided this way, because the frustration that leads to disputes is prevented. [L0360.059]
- Most chargebacks may be prevented with better communication: clear product descriptions, accurate shipping times and a friendly, responsive contact channel. Angry customers who dispute a payment often have unrelated problems, but the store controls what it communicates before the dispute. [L0910.037]
- Unanswered customer tickets make customers angrier. This raises the share of refunds. A rising share of refunds leads to a rising share of chargebacks, so the damage grows faster than sales. (Source B course, 2021-22.) [L0632.013]
- Chargebacks and refunds mostly happen when customers are not answered in time. A fast email reply with a discount code for the next order protects against chargebacks, even with long shipping. [L0820.031]
- Put in the shipping and refund policies that customers must contact the store before filing a chargeback. Keep records of all customer emails. A bank can use a screenshot of the customer's email and an unanswered reply as evidence. [L1381.052]

### Terms checkbox and evidence

- Turn on the terms and conditions checkbox in the checkout area, so customers must agree before checkout. Link it to your terms pages using inline HTML. [L1231.046]
- A recorded terms checkbox and a screenshot of it are evidence to include in a chargeback response. They may not win every dispute. [L1231.047]
