- For orders that were shipped as planned, enter the tracking number as evidence to win the dispute. Keeping proof of shipment is what makes this possible. (Source A course, 2024.) [L0360.062]

### Disputifier, Disputely and RDR settings

**Disputifier**

- Disputifier is an app that blocks chargebacks and helps handle disputes when orders go wrong. Set it up before the store starts scaling. [L1299.029]
- A wrong setup can let chargebacks through. [L1299.030]

**Disputely**

- Disputely is a chargeback monitoring and dispute tool. It connects to the store, sends chargeback alerts and fights disputes to recover funds. The lesson presents it as one of the cheapest options. Its billing page lists alert types RDR, CDRN and Ethoca, with prices of $16.00 and $25.00 per alert. [L0351.010]
- Each chargeback costs about $30 in total. Fighting a chargeback with Disputely costs about $20 to $30. The merchant pays these fees even when the chargeback is won. [L0351.011]
- The Disputely dashboard shows the chargeback ratio over time, chargebacks prevented, and the true cost of avoided chargebacks. [L0351.012]
- The Disputes view lists each case with a status such as Enriching or Evidence Ready and a countdown to the deadline. The tool submits evidence automatically about 5 days before the deadline, so review cases and add notes or extra evidence before that point. [L0351.016]

**RDR setting**

- In Disputely Billing, the RDR (Rapid Dispute Resolution) alert setting must show Not active. When it is Not active, the automatic actions read: No refunds will be issued and no subscriptions will be canceled. [L0351.013]
- If RDR stays active, customers can be refunded automatically even after the order has shipped, when the order is seen as not fulfilled fast enough. The merchant then loses the ad spend, the cost of goods and the sale. [L0351.014]

**Procedure: stop automatic RDR refunds**

1. Open the Disputely billing page and check the RDR alert status. [L0351.015]
2. Write an email to Disputely support asking them to disable RDR on your account. [L0351.015]
3. Wait for confirmation, then check that the RDR alert shows Not active and that the automatic refund action reads No refunds will be issued. [L0351.015]

### Pre-dispute refunds and early resolution

- Automatic refunds triggered by RDR are a loss, not a protection, so keep RDR at Not active. [L0351.013, L0351.014]
- Mitigator sends signals before a chargeback is filed to a Stripe or Shopify Payments account. This allows earlier resolution. Third-party gateways with better merchant protection were reported to cost around 400 to 500 (period and currency not stated). Their lower acceptance rate can reduce conversion, so they fit mainly when holds or disputes already occur. [L1512.046]
- Replying quickly with a discount code, before a customer opens a dispute, is the earliest form of resolution available. [L0820.031]

## Responding to chargebacks and payment disputes

### Core principles for every dispute

- Submit far more evidence than seems necessary, such as courier proof of delivery, email threads, order pages, packing slips and the website's policies. The aim is to persuade the payment provider to decide in your favour. [L0350.001]
- Never accept a chargeback. One seller who contested every dispute with delivery evidence reported winning far more disputes than losing them, even with a high chargeback rate. [L1381.060, L1381.051]
- Save the responses from past cases that worked, because they show which evidence to submit and which wording is persuasive. Reuse them as a guide for similar disputes. [L0350.004]
- Answer every customer message, and prepare response templates for each situation. A chargeback is usually lost when a customer messaged and received no reply, because no action was taken. [L1219.053]
- Customer service for chargebacks should not follow a fixed template. First stop the shipment, then decide the next step based on whether the customer responds and whether the chargeback was intentional. [L0856.085]
- Chargebacks can still be lost even with proof of delivery, a customer signature, order emails and shop messages. The case may still be lost if the card was stolen. [L0472.051]
- Chargebacks are relatively rare. With proof of delivery (a tracking number showing delivery), a store is typically in a good position to dispute a claim that the product was not received. [L0971.021]
- Contested chargebacks were won in roughly 50 to 60 percent of cases when the seller had clear policies and responded well. Winning depends heavily on documentation and prompt replies. [L0352.019]

### Ownership and first customer contact

- Assign all chargebacks and payment disputes to one dedicated support team, which also handles high-risk customers in the lesson's setup. That team owns each case from the first customer contact through to the final evidence submission. [L0350.025]
- Check email regularly and respond quickly to any customer who raises a problem or threatens a chargeback. [L0639.038]
- Ask what went wrong and offer a fix first, such as a replacement or a resend. [L0639.038]
- Contact the customer in ways that can be documented, such as email, not only by phone. [L0466.060] *(older: 2018)*
- Keep records of every contact attempt, including unanswered calls and voicemails. [L0466.060] *(older: 2018)*
- On PayPal, if the case has not yet become a chargeback, first try to settle the customer's problem directly, for example with a replacement order or a partial refund. Customers who are satisfied with that outcome often close the case themselves. [L0350.003]
- When a customer stops answering about an incomplete order after a partial shipment, treat it as a warning sign and do not assume the chargeback is lost. Submit proof of delivery such as tracking, and keep all outreach documented. [L0466.071] *(older: 2018)*

### Identify the dispute before you respond

- Chargebacks usually come from three claims: the customer says the order was fraudulent, never arrived, or arrived broken. Each claim needs different evidence, so answer the specific complaint rather than a generic one. [L1381.059]
- Non-receipt disputes differ from fraud claims, where a card was stolen. Identify which kind of chargeback you face before deciding how to respond. [L0466.061] *(older: 2018)*
- The dispute reason shown in the customer's message tells you what evidence to submit. [L0350.024]
- A delivery status can mislead, for example when a parcel is delivered back to the sender. Read the tracking carefully before responding. [L0350.024]
- A sudden cluster of PayPal disputes, such as six in one day shortly after a supplier change, signals that the product or fulfilment being shipped does not match the listing. Check what is actually being delivered before handling the disputes one by one. [L0694.047]

### Matching the ticket and the order

- A customer can have several tickets. Check that the ticket you attach to a chargeback response matches the disputed order before you submit it. [L0350.017]
- Use the customer's details to find their ticket and related correspondence in Gorgias or your email platform. [L0350.015, L0350.005, L0350.018]
- For a ClearPay/AfterPay dispute, the view shows the customer's message, a dispute ID, the merchant order number, the order amount and the dispute amount. Match these against the order in Shopify before you prepare the response, to confirm you are answering the right dispute. [L0350.028]
- In Shopify, the home dashboard counters, such as '1 chargeback to review' and '3 high risk orders to review', are the starting point for finding open chargebacks that still need a response. [L0350.026]

### Evidence and file rules

**Shopify files**

- Shopify accepts only files in.png,.jpg or.pdf format, each smaller than 2 MB. [L0350.009]
- 'More actions' > 'Print packing slips' produces the packing slip PDF. [L0350.007]
- 'More actions' > 'Print order page' produces the order page PDF with customer details, shipping and billing addresses, order total and payment information. Both are used as evidence. [L0350.007]
- Leave the packing slip file name as it is. [L0350.005]

**Response section labels in Shopify**

| Section label | What to upload or write | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 'Add a screenshot of customer interactions' | PDF of the Gorgias ticket | L0350.008 |
| Shipping section | Packing slip | L0350.008 |
| 'Add an additional document that supports your case' | Order page PDF, tracking or other proof | L0350.008 |
| 'Explain why you feel this order was not fraudulent' | Written investigation findings | L0350.008 |

**ClearPay, AfterPay and Klarna files**

- Everything entered in a ClearPay, AfterPay or Klarna dispute, including attachments, is shared with both the merchant and the consumer. Write the note and choose the files with that in mind. [L0350.022]
- Shipping fields (transport carrier, tracking number and shipping date) are used by the platform to verify that the package was sent. Enter them exactly as they appear in Shopify and the 3PL records. [L0350.030]
- Upload supporting documents such as order pages, packing slips, tracking information and email correspondence. [L0350.021]

**PayPal files**

- Attach all evidence under the 'Attach a file' section, such as previous customer interactions, the order page and tracking information. [L0350.018]

**Record keeping**

- Keep clear records of the policy so it can be shown in a dispute. [L0664.071] *(older: 2020)*
- Keep a record of every refund and its reason. [L1128.030]

### Shopify chargeback response

**Deadlines and set-up**

- Every Shopify chargeback shows a response deadline. If you do not respond, Shopify submits the evidence it holds to the customer's bank on your behalf on that deadline date. [L0350.010]
- Example: a Shopify chargeback for $462.00 showed a deadline of 27 May 2023 at 9:00 am to submit evidence and dispute it. Missing that date means the bank receives only what Shopify has on file. [L0350.011]
- Shopify gives roughly one to two months to contest a chargeback. Example: a 74.81 dollar chargeback had a deadline of November 16 at 3:30 p.m., after which Shopify sends available evidence to the bank automatically. [L1381.050]
- To find chargebacks needing action, go to 'Chargebacks to review' in the middle menu and change the right-hand drop-down to 'Needs Response'. [L0350.006, L0350.005]

**Full procedure (detailed version)**

1. Log into your Shopify account. [L0350.005]
2. Click 'Chargebacks to review' in the middle menu and change the filter in the right-hand drop-down to 'Needs Response'. [L0350.005]
3. Select the order on the chargeback order page. [L0350.005]
4. Find the customer in Gorgias or your email platform, using the customer details. [L0350.005]
5. Read the customer's emails, if they wrote in, to see where the order stands. Confirm the ticket relates to this specific order, because a customer can have several tickets. [L0350.005]
6. If the customer did not write in, create an email chain with them. Use the subject line 'URGENT: [Brand] - Order #[order number]' and the macro 'CHARGEBACK - No Ticket', amending the wording where needed. [L0350.005, L0350.015]
7. Add the tag 'chargeback' to the ticket. [L0350.005, L0350.015]
8. Send and close the ticket. [L0350.005]
9. Print the ticket and save it as a PDF to submit as evidence. [L0350.005]
10. On the Shopify order page, click 'More actions' and select 'Print packing slips'. [L0350.005]
11. Save the packing slip as a PDF and leave the file name as it is. [L0350.005]
12. Go back to the Shopify order page, click 'More actions' and select 'Print order page'. Save it as a PDF. [L0350.005]
13. Click 'Submit response' on the order page to start the dispute. [L0350.005]
14. In 'Add a screenshot of customer interactions', upload the PDF of the Gorgias ticket. [L0350.005]
15. Upload the packing slip in the shipping details section. [L0350.005]
16. In 'Add an additional document that supports your case', upload the order page PDF and any other proof, such as tracking information. [L0350.005]
17. In 'Explain why you feel this order was not fraudulent', write the findings of your investigation. [L0350.005]
18. Read through all uploaded documentation to check the correct information is included. [L0350.005]
19. Click 'Submit response'. Shopify then sends all evidence and shows a purple-blue status box while the bank decides. [L0350.005]

**Short procedure (alternative version, delivery-status based)**

When the order was delivered or is still in transit, a shorter response can work:

1. Never accept the chargeback. [L1381.051]
2. Open the chargeback and click Submit response. [L1381.051]
3. Read the customer's complaint carefully. [L1381.051]
4. If the order was delivered, upload a screenshot of the delivered status to the customer's address. [L1381.051]
5. If the order is still in transit, upload a screenshot of the tracking status and copy the tracking number, then state the date the customer is expected to receive it. [L1381.051]
6. Write half a paragraph to a paragraph saying you did not commit fraud, shipped the order and that the customer received it or is expected to. [L1381.051]
7. Attach the screenshot and tracking number as an additional document. [L1381.051]

*Note: L0350.005 (full, with Gorgias ticket and packing slip) and L1381.051 (short, delivery screenshot) are two versions from different sources. Use the full version for fraud claims, where the bank asks whether the order was genuine, and the short version for quick non-receipt or in-transit cases. [L0350.005, L1381.051, L1381.059]*

**Written explanation (Shopify)**

- The written explanation should prove the order was not fraudulent. Include that shipping and billing addresses match, that there was only one payment attempt, the date the fulfilment centre dispatched the order, the delivery date, and that the customer never contacted you before the chargeback if that is the case. [L0350.012]
- Write the explanation with the findings of your investigation, stating what you are currently doing to resolve the situation. [L0350.005, L1381.051]

**Decision timeline**

- After a Shopify response is submitted, the bank takes about 75 days to reach a decision on the chargeback. [L0350.013]

### PayPal dispute response

**Navigation**

- The menu item 'Response required' lists all disputes that need an answer. Cases sit in three subcategories depending on status: 'Response required', 'Under review' and 'Awaiting other party's response'. [L0350.018, L0350.020]
- Open a case, click 'Respond', then use the paperclip icon to reach the messaging tab, where the message box and the 'Attach a file' section are used. [L0350.020]

**Procedure**

1. Log into your PayPal account. [L0350.018]
2. Click 'Response required' in the menu. Cases sit in three subcategories depending on status: 'Response required', 'Under review' and 'Awaiting other party's response'. [L0350.018]
3. Select the case and click 'Respond'. [L0350.018]
4. Use the customer's details to search for them in Gorgias or your email platform. [L0350.018]
5. Read the customer's email correspondence, if they wrote in, to see where the order stands. [L0350.018]
6. If the customer did not write in, create a new ticket in Gorgias with the subject line '[Brand] - Order #[order number], following up on your PayPal dispute'. Follow up on their issue (delayed order, lost in transit or faulty item) and ask why they opened the dispute and how you can help resolve it. [L0350.018]
7. Depending on the case, either snooze the ticket or close it, then wait for the customer's reply. [L0350.018]
8. Print the ticket using the three dots at the top right and save it as a PDF, leaving the file name as it is. [L0350.018]
9. Go back to the PayPal portal, click 'Respond' to open the inquiry and read the issue shown. [L0350.018]
10. Click the paperclip icon to open the messaging tab. [L0350.018]
11. Write your message in the box, address it to the customer (not PayPal) and sign it with your company name, in email style. [L0350.018]
12. Attach all evidence under the 'Attach a file' section, such as previous customer interactions, the order page and tracking information. [L0350.018]
13. Proofread the message to confirm it includes all relevant information, then send it with the attachments. [L0350.018]
14. The case now waits for the customer. When they reply, it reappears under 'needs your attention' and you must respond again. [L0350.018]

**PayPal message template**

Use this as the message to the customer in the PayPal messaging tab. [L0350.019]

```
Hello [Customer name],

I'm sorry to hear you believe an unauthorized charge was made on your order. Going through our records, I can't find any messages from you about this matter. We therefore handled your order within our usual shipping window. The tracking details confirm it arrived on [delivery date]. The order lists the same address for shipping and billing, and only one payment attempt was made. I've attached all the relevant documents for your reference. If any of this doesn't match your own records, please tell us and we'll look into it right away.

Thank you,
[Brand name]
```

[L0350.019]

### ClearPay, AfterPay and Klarna dispute response

**Navigation and procedure** *(Klarna disputes follow a very similar process)*

1. Sign into your ClearPay or AfterPay account. [L0350.021]
2. Click 'Disputes' in the left-hand menu. [L0350.021]
3. In the right-hand drop-down, select 'needs response' to list all open disputes that need an answer. [L0350.021]
4. Click 'Review Detail' to look at the order in depth. [L0350.021]
5. Read the customer's message at the top of the dispute description and note their name. The message states the reason for the dispute, for example 'PRODUCT_NOT_RECEIVED'. [L0350.021]
6. Search for the customer's details in your email platform to find any related correspondence. [L0350.021]
7. Investigate the complaint to find where the issue is and what stage the resolution is at. [L0350.021]
8. Click the dispute, click 'Challenges Dispute' on the ClearPay/AfterPay/Klarna page, then click 'Next'. [L0350.021]
9. Fill in the shipping information: 'Transport Carrier', 'Tracking Number' and 'Shipping Date', found in Shopify and the 3PL. Upload supporting documents with 'Browse File' or 'Update Case Document', such as order pages, packing slips, tracking information and email correspondence. [L0350.021]
10. Fill in the note section with what the investigation found, explaining how you will resolve the issue and where the order or problem currently stands, then press submit. [L0350.021]

**Worked example**

- Example: a ClearPay dispute for a 45 GBP order claimed 'PRODUCT_NOT_RECEIVED'. The parcel had been returned to sender because of an incorrect address, and the tracking 'delivered' status referred to the return. The response should explain this and attach the tracking confirmation. [L0350.023]

**After submission**

- After a ClearPay or AfterPay challenge is submitted, the platform runs its own internal investigation and then notifies the merchant of the outcome. The merchant does not decide the result directly, so the evidence submitted is what the platform reviews. [L0350.029]

### Follow-up emails to customers

**When the customer did not write in first**

- The questions in the follow-up email are meant to find out why they disputed the payment. Ask whether they had any contact about the order, whether all items arrived, and for photos of any problem on arrival. Their answers give you the reason to build your evidence around. [L0350.027]
- Use this email when the customer has not reached out first. Subject line: 'URGENT: [Brand] - Order #[Order number]'. Adjust the wording to fit the situation before sending. [L0350.014]

```
Hello [Customer first name],

I'm getting in touch because I see you've opened a chargeback on your [Brand] order and told your bank the transaction was fraudulent. Customer care and satisfaction are very important to us, and we'd like to understand what happened and fix it.

We have no record of any contact from you about this, so could you help me clear up a few points? Here's what I'd like to ask:

- Have you been in touch with [Brand] about a problem with your order?
- Were all of your items delivered safely, as the tracking number shows [if relevant: to your local post office on [date]]? [Tracking link]
- If anything was wrong when the order arrived, could you send photos of the problem?

I look forward to hearing from you so I can help resolve this.

Best regards,
[Agent name]
[Brand]
```

[L0350.014]

**Offering a fix before money**

- If the customer still wants money back after a fix is offered, offer a partial refund of about 20%, or up to 50%. [L0639.038]
- Offer a full refund only if the customer escalates publicly on social media or another platform, where a dispute can cause more harm. [L0639.038]

### Cost of losing a dispute

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Amount reversed | Full order amount, including taxes and shipping | L1381.049 |
| Fee on top of order amount | Platform deducts a fee on top of the full order amount, so a lost case costs more than the order value | L0350.002 |
| Bank fee passed to store | $15 per chargeback | L1381.049 |
| Shopify response window | Roughly one to two months | L1381.050 |
| Bank decision after response | About 75 days | L0350.013 |

*Note: the sources give different fee figures. L0350.002 describes a fee on top of the full order amount without a fixed value, while L1381.049 gives a fixed $15 per chargeback. Check the fee shown on your own platform statement, and use the $15 figure only where it matches what you see. [L0350.002, L1381.049]*

- A lost case costs more than the order value, because the platform deducts a fee on top of the full order amount. [L0350.002]
- A chargeback reverses the full order amount including taxes and shipping, and the bank passes a fee of 15 dollars to the store per chargeback. [L1381.049]

### When to refund instead of fighting

**Refund when you were at fault**

- Refund the order instead of fighting a chargeback when the customer was left without a response or shipment. The chargeback may be handled as a refund when you were at fault. [L0804.092]
- Refund a customer rather than let them file a chargeback, because a bank dispute is harder to recover from. A refund keeps the customer and the account in better standing. [L1141.027]
- Refund customers who threaten a chargeback with a valid reason, because chargebacks can lead to holds and blocks on your payout account. [L1219.056]

**Fight when the request has no valid reason**

- Fight chargebacks from customers who ask for a refund without a valid reason. [L1219.056]
- Submit everything for every chargeback, even fraud claims, since many are won. [L0804.091]

**Procedure: fight a chargeback that is not your fault**

1. Gather the Shopify receipt. [L0804.091] *(2023)*
2. Gather the supplier invoice. [L0804.091] *(2023)*
3. Gather the tracking number and proof it was delivered to the address. [L0804.091] *(2023)*
4. Submit everything for every chargeback, even fraud claims, since many are won. [L0804.091] *(2023)*

**Procedure: non-returnable item (older)**

Responding to a customer demanding a refund for a non-returnable item: [L0664.071] *(older: 2020)*

1. Confirm the item is marked as non-returnable on the product page. [L0664.071] *(older: 2020)*
2. Send the product page screenshot and the order details to the customer or the bank. [L0664.071] *(older: 2020)*
3. Keep clear records of the policy so it can be shown in a dispute. [L0664.071] *(older: 2020)*

**Limits of recovery**

- If a customer used their own card, received the product, and then filed a chargeback, the dispute is hard to win through the bank. Small claims court is a possible but limited option for recovering the money. [L1112.037] *(older: 2021)*
- A buyer who already received a refund from the seller can still open a platform dispute and get a second refund, with the amount pulled from the seller's account. Check whether a platform dispute is open before refunding, and keep a record of every refund and its reason. [L1128.030]

**Policies and terms as evidence**

- Attach screenshots of the terms of service, shipping policy and refund policy that show the customer agreed to them. [L0352.020]
- Shopify forwards chargeback evidence to the bank, but whether you win depends on what you did before the dispute. A chargeback can be contested on Stripe or PayPal if you replied to the customer and have evidence. [L1219.052]

### Non-delivery claims and older guidance

**Procedure: contest a non-delivery chargeback (older)**

- A chargeback claiming non-delivery can usually be won with tracking that shows the item was delivered, so submit the shipping information and tracking proof to the bank. [L0466.059] *(older: 2018)*
- To contest a non-delivery chargeback, upload evidence such as a tracking number that shows the order was delivered. The bank or card network then decides whether the merchant keeps the money or the customer is refunded. [L1086.063] *(older: 2019)*

**Procedure: non-delivery and partial shipment (older)**

1. Submit all documentation to the bank or card company, including shipping information and tracking showing delivery. [L0466.060] *(older: 2018)*
2. Contact the customer in ways that can be documented, such as email, not only by phone. [L0466.060] *(older: 2018)*
3. Email the customer about any outstanding item, with its status and options such as shipping it later or a partial refund. [L0466.060] *(older: 2018)*
4. Keep records of every contact attempt, including unanswered calls and voicemails. [L0466.060] *(older: 2018)*

**Procedure: contest a chargeback (Source C)**

To contest a chargeback: [L0352.020]

1. Check whether the customer already emailed and answer those messages if possible. [L0352.020]
2. Open the dispute form that Shopify provides. [L0352.020]
3. Submit proof that the order shipped, including tracking. [L0352.020]
4. Attach screenshots of the terms of service, shipping policy and refund policy that show the customer agreed to them. [L0352.020]
5. For damage claims, state that items are quality checked and shipped in good condition. [L0352.020]

**Procedure: Source C response flow**

1. Check email regularly and respond quickly to any customer who raises a problem or threatens a chargeback. [L0639.038]
2. Ask what went wrong and offer a fix first, such as a replacement or a resend. [L0639.038]
3. If the customer still wants money back, offer a partial refund of about 20%, or up to 50%. [L0639.038]
4. Only offer a full refund if the customer escalates publicly on social media or another platform, where a dispute can cause more harm. [L0639.038]
5. If a chargeback is filed, submit the shipping details, a tracking number, an order screenshot, the refund and return policy, and email chats showing that the transaction was approved and the customer was contacted. [L0639.038]
6. In the chargeback response, state the evidence and explain what you are currently doing to resolve the situation. [L0639.038]

## Automation, help desk and self-service tools

### Self-service and proactive support principles

- Omni-channel support brings customer touchpoints from email, social media, phone and SMS into one platform. This lets you serve customers on their preferred channel and move a conversation to a faster channel, such as from email to SMS. [L0401.013]
- Self-service resources (FAQ pages, knowledge bases and chat) let customers find answers themselves. The source states that 88% of customers prefer self-service because it is quick and hassle-free. Self-service also reduces repetitive tickets in the inbox. [L0401.014]
- Proactive support means reaching out before customers contact you, for example with live chat campaigns while they browse the site, or with direct messages to social media followers. This creates chances to answer questions, offer discounts and build happier customers. [L0401.015]
- A shopper who cannot get a fast answer about product fit, shipping or account changes often leaves the store without buying. Instant automated replies across the whole buying journey can keep these visits from ending in lost sales. [L0753.001]
- Self-service quick responses should cover frequent questions that can be answered without a human, so the support team is not distracted from more significant issues. [L0752.010]

### Support channel hierarchy and tool choice

- Start with the chat and automation add-on features (flow builder, quick response flows), then the help center, then the contact form. Tickets that still reach the contact form and could have been solved by the flow builder or quick response flows are handled by rules and auto responses. [L0752.028]
- Use quick response flows for questions with one fixed answer, where one click gives the reply. Use the flow builder only when the right answer depends on a customer detail such as days since the order, region or product, because it asks follow-up questions and branches. Both can run in the same chat widget. [L0752.040]

### Gorgias Automate and the automation ratio

- Gorgias Automate can automate up to 30% of support tickets on average, which lowers first response time and cost. Some brands report higher rates, but 30% is the planning figure. [L0752.001]

### Gorgias AI agent

- Gorgias is a conversational AI platform for e-commerce stores, built both to answer support questions and to drive sales through one-to-one chat conversations. Its AI agent works as an automated front-line team member. [L0753.002]
- AI chatbots can handle customer service 24/7. The stated purpose is to reduce refunds and increase customer satisfaction. [L1459.013]
- AI reply generators inside a live chat app can handle standard customer questions automatically, which reduces response time for common requests. [L1416.008]
- Routine requests, such as changing a shipping address or modifying a subscription, can be resolved automatically by the AI agent without a human handling them. This shortens response times for simple inquiries. [L0753.005]
- When the AI agent hands a conversation over to a human agent, the human sees the full customer history, profile and order data already in the same place. The human can answer personally without asking the customer to repeat information. [L0753.008]
- Quality control of a Gorgias AI support agent runs in this order:
  1. Gorgias runs rigorous quality checks on the agent. [L0753.006]
  2. The store's own team reviews the agent, so that responses are accurate and match the brand voice. [L0753.006]

### Quick response flows

- Quick response flows are set up under `Automation > Quick response flows` (Automation Add-on). Up to 6 buttons can be displayed in the chat widget with common questions. A click gives an instant answer. If the customer needs more help, a ticket is created for an agent. [L0752.008]
- Buttons appear in the order set in the list. Add new flows with `+ Add Quick Response Flow`. [L0752.008]
- Build quick response flows in this order: [L0752.009]
  1. Analyze the first 30 to 45 days of tickets after launch to find the questions asked most often. [L0752.009]
  2. Pick the six most frequent questions. Examples include product mineral-based check, vegan and cruelty-free status, how to create an account, how to pick the right shade, track and manage orders, and return policy or flow builder questions. [L0752.009]
  3. Create one quick response flow per question in `Automation > Quick response flows`. [L0752.009]
  4. Use all six button slots as soon as the brand has enough recurring questions. [L0752.009]

### Finding the most frequent customer questions

Follow these steps to find the questions that quick response flows and flow builder logic should cover: [L0752.020]

1. Review the historical ticket backlog and aggregate the most common questions. [L0752.020]
2. For a new brand without history, list the typical questions: [L0752.020]
   - subscription changes
   - shipping and return policy
   - discount codes and how to get a discount
   - loyalty program
   - restock dates for out-of-stock items
   - changing or cancelling an order
   - return fees
   - product sizing
   - product differences versus competitors
   - ingredients
   - product usage
3. Check the FAQ pages of brands in the same industry for inspiration. [L0752.020]
4. Trigger chat for out-of-stock products so customers ask about restock timing and get an answer. [L0752.020]

### Order management flows

- Order management flows are set up under `Automation > Order management flows` (Automation Add-on). They let customers act on their order from the chat widget. [L0752.011]
- Customers can use order management flows to:
  - view tracking information
  - get responses for unfulfilled orders
  - return orders
  - cancel orders
  - report an order issue
  [L0752.011]
- It is highly recommended to have both quick response flows and order management flows turned on. [L0752.011]
- Returns in the order management flow can link out to a return portal (for example Loop Returns) instead of sending an automatic reply. Returns are accepted only if the order was delivered less than 30 days ago under that brand's return policy. [L0752.013]
- Order cancellation through a chat flow is very difficult with a 3PL, so the cancel order flow was turned off in the example brand. [L0752.014]
- If the cancel flow is enabled, it can be set to trigger by order status (still processing fulfillment, unfulfilled or pending delivery), with a response text for each status. [L0752.014]
- The report order issue flow lets the customer choose from scenario options such as "I didn't get my refund" or "I'd like to reorder some items". Each scenario can be built out for self-service. [L0752.015]

### Order status checks and tracking

- To check an order, the shopper enters their email address and receives a six-digit code. The code unlocks the order so they can see and change it. [L0752.012]
- For orders that have not been packed or sent out yet, the system displays a special note to manage expectations about shipping dates or holdups. A sample note reads: `Your order has not been packed and shipped yet. Processing usually takes one to two days.` [L0752.012]
- Orders still waiting to be fulfilled generally need 24 to 48 hours to be processed. [L0752.012]
- After the customer enters their email and the six-digit code, the track order view shows:
  - the fulfillment count (for example 1 of 1)
  - the carrier (for example USPS)
  - the tracking number
  - a status timeline such as In transit or Out for delivery, with date, time and location
  - the shipping address
  [L0752.041]
- Unfulfilled orders show the custom message instead of a timeline. [L0752.041]
- At high order volume, automate order tracking and review requests with a dashboard, and check it daily to make sure nothing gets missed. (Older advice, 2020.) [L1277.095]

### Flow builder

- The flow builder supports multiple choice, free text reply collection, file upload, and an automated answer as the end step. The flow ends after the final answer. [L0752.017]
- The conditional pattern asks a condition (for example, days since order), and each answer leads to a different automated response. The customer gets the right policy answer without an agent. [L0752.016]
- Return-window example, as described in the source:

| Step | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Question | "How many days has it been since you placed your order?" | [L0752.016] |
| Answer "More than 30 days" | Reply that free returns and exchanges are only offered within 30 days | [L0752.016] |
| Answer "30 days or less" | Reply that returns or exchanges can be started, with a link to the return portal | [L0752.016] |

- The same logic works for regional shipping policies or product guidance. [L0752.016]
- Shipping-policy example, as described in the source:

| Step | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Question | "Which region are you in?" | [L0752.016] |
| Answer "United States" | Reply with the US shipping time and cost | [L0752.016] |
| Answer "International" | Reply with the international shipping time and cost, with a link to the shipping policy | [L0752.016] |

- Recommended flow builder use cases beyond returns are product recommendations, size guides, warranty policy, shipping policy and subscription management. [L0752.019]

Return-window reply template (US store example), full text:

```
Question to the customer: How many days has it been since you placed your order? Answer 'More than 30 days' reply: Sorry, we can only offer free returns and exchanges within 30 days of ordering for customers in the US. Answer '30 days or less' reply: You can start your return or exchange here: [return portal link]. Replace the 30-day window and the region with your own return policy.
```

[L0752.039]

Subscription management flow template, full text:

```
Subscription management flow template for the flow builder. Ask 'How can we help with your subscription?' with these options: 'Change frequency', 'Change products', 'Update delivery details', 'Change payment info', 'Cancel subscription'. Each option leads to an automated answer or a link to the relevant page. Use the flow builder to add the conditional logic that follows each choice.
```

[L0752.018]

### Help center

- The help center is set up under `Settings > Channels > Help Center` in Gorgias. You can create multiple help centers. Setup fields are: [L0752.021]
  - email to integrate with
  - subdomain
  - help center name
  - connection to a Shopify store
- Help center content is organized in categories (for example Products, Returns, Orders & Shipping, Account), each with articles. Each category has a title, image and description. [L0752.021]
- Top action buttons can include Track order, Return order, Cancel order, Report issue and Get more information. [L0752.021]
- Configuration options include: contact form on or off, chat widget on or off, appearance, preferences, header elements such as navigation links back to the main site, and publishing on a chosen subdomain. [L0752.023]
- Link the help center in the website footer and possibly the header. [L0752.023]
- Build many help center categories and articles rather than few. More articles improve self-service. [L0752.022]
- Articles can be referenced in chat support responses to push customers into the self-service flow. [L0752.022]

### Rules and auto-close

- Rules are set up under `Automation > Rules`. They are triggered in the order listed. Create rules with Create Rule. [L0752.026]

| Rule type | What it does | Example names | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Auto reply | Sends an automatic answer for matching inbound messages | `(Auto Reply) Send tracking information email` (order status or tracking requests); `(Auto Reply) Automate return request emails` | [L0752.026] |
| Auto close | Sets ticket status to closed and adds a tag when the message body or subject contains defined keywords | `(Auto Close) Auto-close spam emails` | [L0752.026] |
| Auto tag | Tags messages | `(Auto Tag) Identify social questions and leads`; `(Auto Tag) Identify intents and sentiments` | [L0752.026] |

- Auto close rules suit social mention tickets (for example from Instagram tracking) that need no agent response. When the ticket is created and the body or subject contains set keywords, the ticket is closed and tagged automatically. [L0752.027]

### Chatbot setup in other tools

- Tidio chatbots can be set up with three automations:
  1. Cart abandoned: set a coupon name (for example `save 15`) and a discount value (for example 15), click save, check that the coupon is created in Shopify, then save and activate. [L0477.027]
  2. Product recommendation: use the template as is, then save and activate. [L0477.027]
  3. AI responder: add a conversation topic for order status, such as "where is my order" or "when will my product arrive", with a prepared reply. Add your email address, then save and activate. [L0477.027]

### Reference resources for support questions

- The Source A Help Desk Database was listed as a new resource in the December 2020 coaching call, presented as a reference for customer support questions. The lesson gives no further detail. (Older advice, 2020.) [L0426.003]

### Zendesk caveat

- Zendesk is not recommended for most small stores. It becomes very expensive over time and creates lock-in, which makes switching costly as more data piles up. (Older advice, 2022.) [L1281.078]

### AI reply drafting

- AI can help draft email replies, but customers should not be handed to AI to talk to directly. Human review remains necessary for live conversations. [L1287.010]
- Compose.ai is a free Google Chrome extension that writes email replies, including customer support answers, in Gmail. Install it from the Chrome extension store. A blue button then appears in the reply field. [L1428.006]
- Compose.ai can write replies in languages other than English. Ask in the instruction for the reply in the target language, for example French or German. The app interface can also be set to German. Check the language quality yourself before sending. [L1428.009]

Writing an email reply with Compose.ai in Gmail:

1. Install the Compose.ai Google Chrome extension. [L1428.007]
2. Open the email you want to answer and click reply. [L1428.007]
3. Click the blue Compose.ai button on the right side of the reply field. [L1428.007]
4. Type a short instruction of what the reply should say, for example the main point or the fact to communicate. [L1428.007]
5. The tool reads the incoming email, detects its topic and writes a short reply. [L1428.007]
6. Choose one of the suggested versions by clicking it. [L1428.007]
7. Review the text and click send. [L1428.007]

- Example input for a customer asking where an order is: state that the product is on its way and that delivery takes about two weeks. Compose.ai turns this short instruction into a complete, polite reply. [L1428.008]

### Third-party tool support

- Problems with a third-party software tool should be taken to that tool's official support channel, not to individual users who offer to help in direct messages. Community members who redirect you to a support channel are the safer path. [L1442.007]

### Reassurance email flow

Reassurance email flow built in Klaviyo (set up in Shopify) to reduce disputes and refunds: [L1128.004]

1. Right after fulfillment, email the customer that the order has shipped and will arrive in about 7 to 14 days, sometimes up to 20 days. [L1128.004]
2. After 7 days, send a second email confirming the product is on its way and that everything is fine. [L1128.004]
3. After about 3 weeks, send a third email asking whether the product has arrived. If not, ask the customer to contact you so the issue can be checked together. [L1128.004]

## Post-purchase communication and customer gratitude

### Order and shipping confirmation

- A post-purchase email assures the customer that the brand is legitimate, gives order updates, and can introduce cross-sell or upsell items. It is a good place to add a social media link to grow the following. [L0607.038]
- *Older advice (Source A, 2021):* Confirm to the customer that the order was received, even when stock verification takes longer because of weekends or holidays, so the customer does not doubt the payment. [L0834.089]
- State the shipping time clearly in the order confirmation, because customers ask about shipping most. A store that ships within 48 hours should say so, and should email customers when the order is dispatched and when tracking updates arrive. [L1076.055]
- Customers in this model value fast shipping, being kept informed about their order, and small surprises. Use these three points deliberately in the post-purchase experience. [L1437.006]
- Fast shipping and fast support build repeat buyers. One brand used two-day shipping and quick customer support to encourage repeat purchases. [L1431.052]

### Access and onboarding for new buyers

- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* The purchase confirmation email should contain a login link and all details needed to access the product, so it must be sent immediately after payment to the address given at checkout. [L1491.002]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Many access complaints come from buyers checking a different mailbox than the one used at checkout, so the confirmation appears to be missing. Always check the checkout email address first. [L1491.003]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Store a dedicated support address in the welcome and confirmation emails and direct all access problems there, so buyers have one clear channel for help. [L1491.005]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Moving a legitimate sender's email from spam to the inbox tells the mail provider to deliver future messages from that sender to the inbox. Tell buyers to do this so later order, access and service emails are not missed. [L1491.004]

**Onboarding steps for a new buyer after a successful purchase** (older, Source B, 2021-22) [L1491.001]

1. Open the inbox of the exact email address used at checkout and look for the purchase confirmation.
2. If it is not there, check the spam or junk folder.
3. If it is in spam, move it to the inbox.
4. Open the confirmation and use the login link and access details it contains.
5. If access still fails, contact the support address and describe the problem.

**Welcome email template** (older, Source B, 2021-22):

```
Subject: Welcome, your access is ready

Hi {first_name},

Thank you for your purchase of {product_name}. Your order is confirmed and we are glad to have you with us.

To get started, check the inbox of {purchase_email} for the email with your order details and login link. If you do not see it within {minutes} minutes, check your spam or junk folder.

If you find the email in spam, move it to your inbox. This makes sure future emails from us reach you.

The email contains your login link and all the details you need to access your purchase. If you have any trouble accessing anything, reply to this email or contact {support_email}, and we will help you as quickly as we can.

Best regards,
{sender_name}
```
[L1491.006]

### Post-purchase email machines and expectations

- Post-purchase machines reduce buyer remorse and increase customer lifetime value by confirming the purchase, setting expectations, building relationships, and encouraging repeat purchases and referrals. They coordinate phone calls, video ads, and email sequences. [L0240.017]
- The goal of post-purchase machines is to raise customer lifetime value, reduce buyer remorse, and earn sales, testimonials and referrals. Buyer remorse is common when competition is high, so reassurance after purchase matters. [L1076.054]
- Avoid sending only sales pitches after purchase. Long-term success depends on happy customers. [L1076.060]

### Avoiding buyer remorse

- To reduce buyer remorse and maximize post-purchase customer lifetime value, underpromise on delivery times and product characteristics in your post-purchase communications. Then overdeliver by meeting those promises faster or with unexpected value, such as bonuses, premium packaging, or exclusive content that customers would love but never expect. [L0240.023]
- Add extras such as digital files or unexpected perks after purchase. [L1076.060]

### Thank-you messages and gratitude

- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* A standard order confirmation email does not count as gratitude. The thank-you must go further and be overt and personal. [L0406.006]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Thank every new customer as a permanent part of the business, not only the first hundred customers. Making it a routine practice is worth it as the business grows, and it also encourages reviews. [L0406.007]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Say thank you whenever a customer takes an action you want, not only on the first purchase. Gratitude works best as a permanent routine in the business rather than a short campaign. [L0406.032]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Small and medium online stores have an advantage because large e-commerce companies rarely send personal thank-you messages. Customers do not expect personal gratitude from large brands, so it stands out when a small store does it. [L0406.004]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* The most effective way to get customers to refer others is an unusual post-purchase experience that surprises them, prompting them to talk or post about it on social media. Pre-purchase factors such as a working, good-looking site and good service still matter, but post-purchase gratitude is the focus. [L0406.003]
- Thank-you messages should feel like personal communication from one person to another, not a mass-produced mailing. This applies to both handwritten notes and video messages. [L0406.022]

### Thank-you videos

- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Bonjoro is an affordable online tool for recording video thank-you messages with a webcam or phone camera and sending them as personal emails. The recipient watches the video directly inside the email. [L0406.009]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Video thank-you messages are rare for customers, so they create a strong wow moment and set the store apart from competitors. Doing them manually requires formatting and compressing video files, which is time-consuming, so a dedicated tool is worth using. [L0406.013]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Thank-you videos should be authentic and quick, recorded wherever you are, not overproduced. Customers value seeing a real person who appreciates their support. [L0406.014]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* A pre-recorded generic video can be personalized through email placeholders such as the customer's first name, which email tools insert automatically. The customer sees a personal address from a real person, while the video itself is recorded only once. Example: the video says "Thanks for supporting us," and the email subject and greeting include the customer's name. [L0406.015]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* A thank-you video should thank the customer, give useful tips for using the product, and explain how to get support. Invite customers to contact customer service if they get stuck or have questions. [L0406.017]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Video thank-you emails sent through Bonjoro get a good open rate, and recipients often share the videos with others. The video thank-you can therefore reach people beyond the single customer. [L0406.030]

### Handwritten thank-you notes

- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Decide when the note is sent. The timing options are below. [L0406.019]

| Option | When it is sent | Arrival | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Right after the order | Immediately after ordering | About 1 to 3 days later | Standard shipping |
| After expected delivery | At the expected delivery date, e.g. day 7 for a 7-day shipping time | After the customer receives the order | Delivery is slow |

[L0406.019]

- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Do not sign handwritten notes with a generic "From the team" line. Sign with a real person's name and job title, such as owner or sales manager, so the note feels personal. [L0406.021]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* A low-cost option for businesses with few customers is to write short handwritten notes yourself and post them with a stamp, an envelope, paper and a pen. This is cheap and still effective, and it can be done before any online tool is needed. [L0406.023]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Scribeless is an online service that uses AI to turn typed text into a handwritten-looking note, including natural human imperfections. It can print and post the note for you, or you can print and mail it yourself. Pricing is about $2 per message and depends on message volume. [L0406.011]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Handwritten notes mailed by hand when a store had only a few customers were photographed and shared by recipients. Some later buyers said a friend who had received such a note had referred them, showing that a simple handwritten note at low cost can produce referrals. [L0406.033]
- *Older advice (Source A, 2021):* Handwritten thank-you cards make the most sense when buyers are likely to reorder for their own clients, such as interior designers, especially after an earlier interaction. Automated thank-you emails can be sent through Klaviyo. [L0834.128]

### Follow-up, support and first-product success

- Following up with customers after purchase, for example with a call or a check that they are happy, builds relational and reputational capital. Satisfied customers then recommend the business, which supports trust and conversion. [L0390.029]
- Help buyers succeed with the first product, because satisfied buyers are the main source of later purchases. A buyer who gets results is more likely to buy the next product from you. [L0378.099]
- Good customer support, reliable shipping times and clear emails build the loyalty that brings repeat purchases and referrals, especially when new products are added to the same store. [L0871.081]

### Repeat purchases

**Consolidate component (repeat purchases) steps** (older, Source B, 2021-22) [L0414.043]

1. Map the consolidate pathway for each product: what the second and third purchases are, which can be a different product, such as an accessory for the first order or a complementary product later.
2. Define what the customer must know before the second or third purchase, and whether education is needed first.
3. Set the timing for the next offer. It depends on the original purchase and may be two weeks, two months or six months.
4. Choose the delivery mechanism, such as email marketing or another channel.

### Loyalty programme and referrals

- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Mention the loyalty program in personalized post-purchase touchpoints, such as a thank-you video message or a post-sale support call. Explain that points are earned and can be turned into a discount on a future order. [L0956.010]
- *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):* Thanking customers, showing gratitude, and following up after the sale with a post-sales support call each make customers more likely to recommend a store on their own. A referral reward adds an extra push on top of these steps rather than replacing them. [L1234.019]

## Post-sale calls, reviews and customer feedback

### Why post-sale contact matters

- Most e-commerce stores see only about 1%, 5% or 10% of customers leave a review. A structured post-sale call program can raise the review rate to roughly 50% or more. [L1011.001]
- Post-sale calls serve two goals at once. They make the customer feel looked after by checking that their needs are met and their questions answered, and they bring in reviews and feedback for the business. [L1011.002]
- Post-sale calls reveal what customers expect, want, or would like improved. This can be information the business did not have before. [L1011.003]
- A customer who receives an unexpected, helpful follow-up call is more likely to talk about the business and to buy again. Sending upsell messages before or just after the call strengthens this effect. [L1011.004]
- Reviews will not come on their own. The business has to ask for them actively, most effectively by phone. Relying on passive hope is not an effective approach. [L1012.009]
- Asking customers for feedback on the business reveals improvement opportunities and is often a core part of conversion rate optimization. It also makes customers feel they have input, which increases their mental investment and the chance they buy again. [L1052.001]
- Customer feedback will not arrive on its own. Ask for it proactively, every time you want to learn something about the business. [L1052.002]
- Feedback can point to website usability problems, content gaps customers want filled, weak customer service, or issues with how products are delivered. Targeted customer answers show where the business can grow. [L1052.003]
- Track customer feedback and queries to find weak points that are not visible in analytics. Be proactive about shipping delays or site issues. [L1259.053]
- After-sale service (refunds, returns, damages and defects) shapes the feedback score and loyal customers. Be proactive about shipping delays and monitor customer feedback for product or page issues. [L1260.054]
- Request reviews from happy customers consistently, and track the number of reviews relative to sales volume. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.130]

### Timing the contact

Sources give different timing rules. Choose the rule that matches your own delivery times.

| Rule | Source | Applies when |
|---|---|---|
| Call 7 days after purchase by default, adjusted to typical shipping duration. If items normally ship in 14 days, call on day 14 so the customer has received the order. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* | [L0203.008] | Default; adjust to your shipping duration |
| Call on day 10 after purchase if deliveries normally take 7 days. The exact timing depends on the store's own shipping times. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* | [L1011.005] | Standard delivery of about 7 days |
| Schedule the follow-up call 3-5 days after delivery confirmation. | [L0286.035] | Delivery is confirmed |

- Call each customer once the product should have arrived. [L1011.005]
- When delivery status is available, base the review call on confirmed delivery. If it is not available, use the store's typical delivery time. For example, call 10 days after purchase when orders usually arrive within 7 days. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.023]

### Who makes the calls and how the routine runs

- Assign the calls to yourself, using calendar reminders, or to a customer service virtual assistant (VA) who performs them during gaps between inbound support calls. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0203.007]
- Making the calls yourself gives you a much better understanding of your market and customers. The insights can improve other marketing, content ideas, and emails that answer common questions. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.020]
- Run the post-sale review call as a routine for every new customer, rather than picking only customers who seem likely to review. The consistent routine raises the review rate; a selected sample does not. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.022]
- Do not place the review call to customers known to be unhappy. About 95% or more of customers are usually not disgruntled, so the call is safe to make to most of the customer base. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.017]

**Setting up the review multiplier call system** *(older advice, 2021-22)* [L0399.013]:

1. Decide whether you or your customer service team makes the calls.
2. Share the call script with the team.
3. Have the team schedule calls to customers at the appropriate time after purchase, to collect reviews.

### Review call process

**Review collection process, in order** *(older advice, 2021-22)* [L1011.007]:

1. Develop a call script first, based on a template and adapted to your own circumstances.
2. Offer the customer several ways to leave a review.
3. Ask customers who are very positive for a video review.
4. Have your team manage the process.
5. Track which reviews were gained, and follow up with customers who committed to a review but have not left one.

**Delivered-order review follow-up, Trello workflow** [L0286.025]:

1. Identify delivered orders not yet reviewed in Trello's "Delivered/Pending Review" list.
2. Call the customer and ask about product experience and satisfaction.
3. Request specific content: text review, product photo, or video.
4. If the customer hesitates, offer an incentive (discount code, gift card, or item).
5. Collect the content and confirm the incentive via follow-up email.
6. Move the card to "Reviewed" and document in a Trello comment the content type and date.

**Scheduled follow-up call, review and testimonial** [L0286.035]:

1. Schedule a follow-up call 3-5 days after delivery confirmation.
2. Call the customer and ask about product experience, quality, and satisfaction.
3. Request specific content: text review, product photo, video, or testimonial.
4. If the customer declines, offer an incentive (discount code, gift card, or physical item).
5. Collect the content via email or directly document the response.
6. Send an incentive confirmation and thank-you message.
7. Add a Trello comment with the completion date and content type received.

### Review call script

Use the script as a guide to content only, and speak in your own natural language. Fill the [brackets] before the call. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)*

```
1. Greeting: Hi [customer first name], this is [agent name] from [store name]. I am calling to thank you for your order of [product name].
2. Check-in: I just wanted to make sure it arrived in good condition and that it is working the way you expected. Are you happy with it?
3a. If the customer is happy: That is great to hear. Feedback from customers really helps us serve you and others better. Would you be willing to leave us a quick two-minute review? Then send the text review link [review link]. If you like, you can also leave a short video or send a photo with the product. Our video review tool [VideoPeel link] makes that a few clicks on your phone.
3b. If the customer is not happy: Thank you for telling me, I am sorry about [issue]. Let me fix that now: [resolution options]. Once it is sorted, would you be open to sharing your experience in a review?
4. Close: Thank you for your time and for being a [store name] customer. You will get a short follow-up email with the review link [and reward details, if any].

Follow-up email: send it within [number of hours] of the call. Restate the thank-you, include the text review link and the video or photo link, and state any reward terms [e.g. 10% off a future order or store credit for a text review; a larger reward for a video or photo review].
```
[L1012.025]

- Use the call to mention other retention programs, such as loyalty and referral programs, so customers learn about them while they are already positive about the business. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.021]

### Review options and rewards

- Offer four review options during the call: dictating the review over the phone, emailing the review text to the business, following a review link from the review app to post it online, or recording a video review. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.008]
- Ask customers who are very positive for a video review. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.007]
- For a post-purchase customer testimonial, send an email within 24 hours of purchase offering a refund in exchange for a video testimonial submitted through a form. The form must collect first and last name, the video upload, and a checkbox giving permission to use the content in ads. [L0789.034]
- Offer an incentive when a customer hesitates or declines, as in the procedures above. Do not offer incentives in a way that makes the review inauthentic. See the integrity rules below. [L0286.025, L0286.035, L0243.044]

### Review request emails and messages

**Review request, short delivery check (Source A, 2024)**. The note in this template says to keep the message to one or two sentences, to include no link to a review app, and not to ask for a photo or video [L0965.072]:

```
Subject: [store name] order #[order number]

Hi [customer name],

I see your order arrived on [delivery date]. I would really appreciate any feedback on the product and your experience ordering from [store name].

Thank you,
[your name]

Notes: Keep this message to one or two sentences. Do not include a link to a review app, and do not ask for a photo or video.
```
[L0965.072]

**Review request, follow-up after delivery (Source A, 2024)** [L1115.107]:

```
Hi [customer first name], I saw that your order was delivered, and I wanted to make sure it arrived in good condition and matches what you expected. Please reply and let me know how your experience was, since I am the owner of [store name] and your feedback reaches me directly. If you are happy with it, would you mind leaving a review here: [review link]? If you know anyone who might like our products, we would be glad to take care of them as well. Thank you, [your name]
```
[L1115.107]

**Review request, delivery check with photo request (Source A, 2020, older)** [L1111.130]:

```
Hi [Customer name], I just saw that your order was delivered, and I wanted to check in. I hope you are loving it. Is everything okay with your order? If you are happy with it, would you be willing to leave a short review, and send photos or a video if you have them?
```
[L1111.130]

**Review request, after-delivery conversation (Source A, 2024)** [L0292.009]:

```
Hi [customer first name], I wanted to follow up on the [product name] you received a few days ago. I'm curious-how are you enjoying it? How was your experience with us? [Listen to response] That's wonderful to hear! Since we're building our reputation, I'd really appreciate if you could leave us a review on our site. Would you also be willing to send us a photo with the product? Thank you so much for your business.
```
[L0292.009]

**Personal review request email procedure (Source A, 2024)** [L1115.071]:

1. Send a personal email to each customer after delivery, not an automated one.
2. Ask whether the product matches what they expected and whether their experience was good.
3. Ask for a review by linking to the review page.
4. If the customer replies with a positive experience but leaves no review after a set period, you may use that email as a review on the store, with permission.

- The sources give two different approaches to the review link in the request message. The 2024 Source A template [L0965.072] says to include no link, and the 2024 Source A template [L1115.107] includes the review link. Both are recorded here; the sources do not state which applies in which situation. [L0965.072, L1115.107]

### Review request channels and volume

- Review requests can reach customers through post-purchase email automation, phone calls, text messages, or photo submission requests. Phone calls generate the highest engagement and personal connection, which is especially valuable in the early stage when building social proof. Email automation handles volume; calls handle relationship-building. [L0292.011]

### Review counts and content

- Minimum review count to launch: 10 reviews in total, with 6 to 7 of them image-based. Image reviews convert significantly better than text reviews. [L0321.032]
- Only use reviews that belong to the store, such as existing reviews from the supplier with permission. Never copy reviews from competitor sites. [L1088.075]

**Increasing review count with CSV import (not recommended)** [L0321.033]:

1. Import initial reviews from AliExpress or Amazon via Riview or Loox app.
2. Download the CSV file of imported reviews.
3. Copy individual reviews and duplicate them 10x within the CSV.
4. For example, take 10 reviews and duplicate each 10 times to create a list of 100 reviews.
5. Re-import the expanded CSV into the app.
6. Customers see the higher review count and trust the product, even though they rarely check beyond the first 10-20 reviews.

- This procedure is documented here as the source gives it, but it produces copied, fabricated reviews. It conflicts with the honest-review rules and must not be used. [L0321.033, L0243.044, L1088.075, L1188.058]

### Authentic reviews and review integrity

- Build product reviews honestly, without fabrication. When a customer makes a purchase, follow up relentlessly to request a review. Authentic customer reviews build market credibility faster than hiding "no reviews yet" or creating fake reviews. *(Older advice, 2019.)* [L0243.044]
- Changing reviewer names, genders, or avatars on borrowed or template reviews to make them look real turns them into made-up testimonials. Use only real reviews with the names or initials the customer actually gave. [L1188.058]
- Look at the reviews on the product page for negative or suspicious entries. Identify reviews from people who did not buy the product, which are often posted by competitors or haters. Remove or do not approve those reviews, and keep genuine feedback visible. [L0657.043]

### Review dates

- Review dates can be omitted if you are concerned that older reviews make the product look outdated. Alternatively, keep dates visible, because they show product longevity and an established sales history. The sources give both options; choose by the product's situation. [L0253.005]

### Ratings and platform risk

- Meta may ask buyers about their experience about a week after purchase and collect a rating. If the store's ratings fall below a threshold, the ad account can be banned. This risk is mostly seen with very high-volume stores that have many poor ratings. The source does not give the threshold. [L0649.053]

### Post-sale feedback surveys

- A post-purchase survey should contain about five questions. One to three questions also work, but five balances getting people to engage against making the survey too long to finish. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1052.004]
- Survey questions must be relevant to customers, answerable by them, and produce meaningful feedback on what the business actually wants to learn. Rotate the questions over time as your open questions change. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1052.005]
- Ask only a few questions per call so the caller is not burdened. [L0682.006]

**Set up the post-purchase feedback system, in this order** *(older advice, 2021-22)* [L1052.017]:

1. Create a post-purchase survey using a tool such as Google Forms, SurveyMonkey, GoSurvey, or Typeform, with about five questions chosen from a template list or written yourself.
2. Set up an automated email that sends the survey to customers at your chosen point after purchase.
3. Define the reward for responses and set up the thank-you message, either a template email or a video.

### Survey tools

| Tool | Cost and use | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Google Forms | Free and fully adequate. Available with Google Workspace and set up in Google Drive. | [L1052.006] |
| SurveyMonkey | Further option. | [L1052.006] |
| GoSurvey | Further option. | [L1052.006] |
| Typeform | Paid tool; can also be used for on-site surveys and quizzes. | [L1052.006] |

*Older advice, 2021-22.*

### Thanking respondents

- Thank every customer who responds to the survey, ideally with a personal message. Even a short email reply saying the response was seen and naming the reward is enough. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1052.012]

**Thank-you follow-up process** *(older advice, 2021-22)* [L1052.014]:

1. Receive the survey response, which includes the respondent's name and email.
2. Trigger the thank-you message for that person, either a pre-recorded Bonjoro message or a reply email.
3. Mention that the reward is available and where to claim it.

### Call-based customer questions

**Customer service survey during calls** *(older advice, 2021-22)* [L0682.005]:

1. Let the caller first get their problem solved or receive the information they called for.
2. Then say you have a couple of quick questions that are asked of everyone who calls.
3. Ask whether they noticed anything not working on the site; if yes, ask what it was.
4. Ask whether they looked at other sites while researching the product; if yes, ask which ones.
5. Ask which of those they liked better and why, and what they liked about them.
6. Record the answers in the Q&A tracking sheet.

- Asking questions during a pre-purchase call is especially valuable because the buying decision is still fresh in the caller's mind. Ask only a few questions per call so the caller is not burdened. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0682.006]

### Tracking reviews and feedback

- Record every customer who was called, who had a conversation, and who promised a review, and whether the review was actually posted. Follow up with customers who committed but have not yet left the review. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.013]
- Track the number of reviews relative to sales volume, and request reviews from happy customers consistently. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.130]
- Use a Q&A tracking sheet (Google Sheets, or any tool such as Trello or Asana) to record customer service answers, especially when virtual assistants handle service. It must be built into the customer service SOPs, and access must be given to the right people. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L0682.021]
- Document each completed review in Trello with a comment that records the content type and date. [L0286.025, L0286.035]

### CSAT: measurement and analysis

- CSAT data is in Gorgias under the Statistics section, in the Satisfaction view. It shows a chronological list of tickets, including ratings of 4 stars or lower. The Satisfaction dashboard has a CSV download button to export all CSAT scores. [L0401.005]
- CSAT ratings alone have limited value. The written customer comments, especially negative ones, explain what to change in customer service. [L0401.008]
- CSAT is shaped by what happens before and after purchase, not only by support. Clear product descriptions set expectations; good product photography, faster and more reliable shipping, free shipping for eligible customers, and a helpful post-purchase experience all raise satisfaction. [L0401.012]
- When a customer gives a low CSAT score without an explanation, proactively reach out and ask for written feedback. This reveals why the rating was given, what the customer expected, and how to prevent lower scores in the future. [L0401.007]

**Review negative CSAT responses in this order** [L0401.004]:

1. Read and audit the low-rated responses, not just the positive ones.
2. Identify recurring themes, such as long wait times, confusing information, or unresolved product issues.
3. Tally how many tickets mention each recurring issue.
4. Rank issues by tally count, since the more tallies an issue has, the higher its impact on satisfaction.
5. Fix the highest-impact issues first, for example through agent training or automation for faster replies.

### Acting on feedback

- Post-sale calls reveal improvement points that may not have been known before. Use them to adjust customer service, product information, and delivery communication. [L1011.003, L1259.053]
- Insights from calling customers yourself can improve other marketing, content ideas, and emails that answer common questions. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1011.020]
- Feedback can point to usability problems, missing content, weak customer service, or delivery issues. Act on the answers that recur across customers. [L1052.003]

## Abandoned carts, leads and sales follow-up

### Who follows up, and how fast

- Sources differ on who makes the follow-up call. Each applies to the setup it describes:
  - The owner personally messages every email lead when the store is new and traffic is low. The message asks what they are interested in, offers to answer questions, and shows you want their business. This closes more sales and reveals what customers want. [L0201.012]
  - The store owner or a customer service rep can make the follow-up call to an abandoned checkout. It should happen as soon as possible after the abandonment. The goal is to ask whether something went wrong and fix it, not to push a sale. (Source B, 2021-22; older advice.) [L1522.042]
  - A VA handles the callbacks in this setup:

    1. Abandoned cart alerts are sent to Slack as soon as a cart is abandoned.
    2. The VA calls the customer back right away.
    3. The VA asks whether the customer had any difficulty or questions and tries to recover the sale.

    The owner did not measure the exact recovery rate. [L1473.013]

### Abandoned checkouts: where to find them and what to send

- In Shopify, go to Orders > Abandoned Checkouts to see every cart that was started but not completed. Follow up manually with every person on this list. [L0208.010]
- Abandoned carts are the easiest sales to win, so following them up raises conversions without spending on ads. [L0255.064]
- Use Shopify's cart recovery email, which has a button that sends the reminder to the customer. Keep the default button and send it to all customers who entered an email address and did not complete the purchase. Template:

```
Email to send to customers who started checkout but did not finish, to be sent from the Shopify abandoned-checkout recovery email with its button: use the cart recovery email in Shopify, which contains a button to send the reminder to the customer. Keep the default button and send it to all customers who entered an email address and did not complete the purchase.
```

  [L1216.011]
- Include a contact address in every abandoned cart email so shoppers with questions can reach you before they leave the checkout. [L0567.030]
- You can offer a discount in the abandoned cart email, for example 5% off. The source says this is promotional use and does not violate MAP restrictions on advertised pricing. (Source A, 2020; older advice.) [L0268.028]
- Bot-generated abandoned-cart emails can be annoying. In 2020 no simple fix was known, so keep checking your tools for an option to block them. (Older advice.) [L1277.097]

### Contact timing rules

- Customer service must not contact customers after 8 pm in their time zone. For an abandoned cart, wait until the next morning to send the message or make the call. [L0964.108, L0964.109] (Source A, 2023.)
- Abandoned-cart calls or texts happen only during daytime, using the customer's time zone. [L0964.109]

### SMS and text messages

- Do not automate SMS text messages to customers for marketing or abandoned cart recovery. One operator faced significant legal liability for automating customer text outreach. [L0286.020]
- Sources differ on texting. L0964.109 allows calls or texts to abandoned carts during daytime in the customer's time zone. L0286.020 forbids automated texts. Both apply together: manual texts, sent only in the daytime window, never automated. [L0964.109, L0286.020]

### Live chat, phone and service leads

- Live chat and phone questions usually come from buyers who want to place an order or need a few answers to finish the purchase. Missed calls and chats cost real sales, so cover them as soon as traffic arrives. (Source A, 2019; older advice.) [L0467.064]
- For service clients, invite prospects to call or visit the office. In-person or live selling produced a much higher success rate than email, which mostly serves to introduce the operator. (Source C.) [L0440.053]
- High average order values, around 2,000 dollars and above, bring more customers who want to order by phone. Answer the phone yourself first and hire help later. (Source A, 2024.) [L0806.082]

### Personal video follow-up

- The purpose of a video follow-up is to open a conversation, not to close the sale immediately. Once the lead replies, answer their specific concern, whether it is a question, a discount request, or a delivery date. [L1049.012]
- Use the same Loom method for other lead inquiries, such as whether a product is in stock or a request for a bulk order quote. Pull up the relevant product, record a short video, and send the link. [L1049.014]

### Phone orders

1. Add the product to the cart.
2. Collect the name, shipping address, billing address and payment method.
3. Enter the order into the checkout with the customer's email.
4. Process the order like a web order and follow it up the same way.

[L1283.061] (Source A, 2023.)

## Reputation management and complaint handling

### Principles of reputation work
