- Poor reviews and complaints are inevitable at scale: one complaint in a thousand customers is normal. [L0790.071]
- Respond honestly, and interact with critics while the audience is still small enough to do so. [L0790.071]
- Public negative comments cannot be fully prevented, so the practical response is to resolve each customer's complaint quickly and directly. Consistent service reduces the number of unhappy buyers over time. [L0492.067]
- Happy customers refer other customers, while unhappy customers search out every public channel to complain. [L1472.014]
- Customers judge a brand by how the retailer treats them. Suppliers approve retailers only if they will treat customers fairly, because a retailer represents the brand's name and must protect its reputation. [L1422.012]

### Response standard and speed

- Answer complaint emails quickly. Acknowledge the customer's frustration and offer a concrete solution such as a refund or fix. Response speed is part of the solution and prevents disputes. [L1141.028]
- Reply to negative reviews within 24 hours. Acknowledge the specific problem, state the action taken and give a direct contact route. [L1164.025]
- Trustpilot shows a company's reply rate and reply time. The example brand replied to 99% of negative reviews, typically within 24 hours. Use these figures as the benchmark for your own response standard. [L1164.023]
- Update customers proactively about shipping delays, before they have to ask. [L0637.022]
- Reply fast to Facebook comments, DMs and Messenger messages. Fast replies signal good business practice to Meta and can help move the business up a tier. [L0637.022]

### Triage of negative reviews

- Older advice (Source A, 2021), still valid as a sequence. Handle a negative review as follows: [L0968.097]
  1. Decide whether it comes from a real customer, a competitor or a troll. [L0968.097]
  2. For a real customer with a fixable problem, try to fix it calmly. [L0968.097]
  3. For fake or unjustified reviews, request removal. [L0968.097]
  4. For customers who cannot be satisfied, stop engaging and focus on good customers. [L0968.097]
- The business cannot edit or delete reviews itself. Its only direct action on a review is a reply. [L0694.038]
- Removal, as described in step 3 above, applies only to fake or unjustified reviews. [L0968.097, L0694.038]

### Reply templates

Reply to negative reviews and complaint emails with this template, filling in the brackets:

```text
Hi [Customer name], thank you for your review. We are sorry about [the specific issue, e.g. the unexpected charge, the difficulty cancelling your subscription, the wrong order]. We understand how frustrating that is, and it is not the experience we want for you. We have reviewed your order and [the action taken, e.g. cancelled your subscription, processed a full refund of [amount] for order [order number], refunded the remaining balance]. The refund should appear on your original payment method within [5-10] business days, depending on your bank's processing time. You are welcome to keep [the package you received] as a gesture of goodwill. If you have any other questions, contact us at [support email] or reply directly to our email and we will help. Kind regards, [Agent name], [Title]
```

[L1164.026]

### Trustpilot: analysing the profile

1. Read the star rating, the review count and the AI review summary. [L1164.015]
2. Filter the reviews to 1, 2 and 3 stars to find product flaws and service problems. [L1164.015]
3. Export or copy the filtered low-star reviews into a CSV file. Ask an AI assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT to run a full gap analysis of the complaint themes. [L1164.017]
4. Interpret the pattern:
   - When low-star reviews focus on cancellations, unexpected recurring shipments and refunds rather than the product itself, the product is probably acceptable. The real gap is service and subscription handling. [L1164.016]

### Trustpilot: handling a negative profile

Procedure for a negative Trustpilot profile created about your store: [L0694.038]

1. Check whether the business has claimed the profile. An unclaimed profile can be claimed by opening a new profile and proving ownership. [L0694.038]
2. Accept that reviews cannot be edited or deleted by the business. You can only reply to them. [L0694.038]
3. Send customers to your review page by email, so that new reviews improve the rating and the profile looks better. [L0694.038]

### Subscription and cancellation complaints

- Making cancellation hard is the most damaging pattern. This includes routing customers to a promotion instead of cancelling, or refusing to change an order after it is placed. Offer a self-service cancellation and order-change path. [L1164.020]

### Public comments and ad moderation

- Leaving comments unfiltered can damage an account. A comment section full of complaints or negative remarks can kill momentum and sales, so filter comments before a video goes viral. [L1429.038]
- Procedure for moderating comments on the page: [L1431.055]
  1. Hide negative or inappropriate comments on the page. [L1431.055]
  2. Assign a moderator to the page to handle comments. [L1431.055]
  3. Reply to customer messages quickly using prepared templates. [L1431.055]
- Respond to comments and messages on Facebook, Instagram and Messenger when running social ads, because these are often pre-purchase questions. [L1259.051]
- Ignoring negative comments on ads and leaving them unanswered led to bad reviews piling up and the Facebook page being blocked. Answer comments and address complaints promptly. [L1131.046]
- Procedure for filtering comments on every promoted video: [L1444.050]
  1. Add a list of banned words to the comment filter, and add words specific to your product. [L1444.050]
  2. If a comment gets through the filter, add variations of the same word to the filter. [L1444.050]
  3. If the same person posts many variations of comments, block that profile. [L1444.050]
- Older advice (Source B, 2021 to 2022): reply to every genuine YouTube comment, including those expressing disagreement, because replies count as engagement. Ignore trolls or answer them lightly, and never argue. [L1511.014]

### Imitators and public notices

Template for a notice to customers when imitators appear:

```text
Draft a tactful notice to customers explaining that imitators are appearing, that our brand is the original, and that we have no partner ties with them. Anyone buying from us is buying from the genuine brand. Phrase it delicately so it does not come across as boasting.
```

[L0353.046]

### Consumer complaint services

| Platform | What it mainly contains | How to use it | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yelp | Mostly complaints | Public review platform, mainly used to complain | [L1472.062] |
| Google Reviews | Both good and bad reviews | Can go either way | [L1472.014, L1472.062] |
| Better Business Bureau | Mainly complaints | Limited value for building trust; resolve issues directly before they reach it | [L1472.063] |

- Focus your reputation effort on the platforms where your customers are most active. [L1472.062]
- Prioritise resolving issues directly with the customer before they reach any public channel. [L1472.063]
- When a customer files a complaint with a consumer complaint service:
  - Reply once through that service, in a calm and factual way. [L1472.067]
  - Keep a copy of every message. [L1472.067]
  - Write the reply as if the customer will read it, because the service forwards it to the customer. [L1472.067]
  - Do not argue about fault. [L1472.067]

### Case: a complaint service filing after a pricing error

A store sold an appliance priced at about $1,000 too low because its price update was late. When the order came in, the store emailed the buyer that the item was out of stock. The buyer insisted on receiving the product and filed a complaint with a small business complaint service. The store offered a full refund, apologised again, and stopped the exchange. The complaint went off the web after about 30 days with no further action. [L1472.018]

### Recovering customers and turning complaints into improvements

Procedure for customers who left a negative review or complaint: [L1377.068]

1. Contact each customer who left a negative review or complaint. [L1377.068]
2. Apologise and say the problem was a mistake on your side. [L1377.068]
3. Offer a $5 to $10 credit or a small free product to rebuild trust. [L1377.068]
4. Ask the customer for feedback through a short survey about the product and delivery. [L1377.068]

### Mistakes that cause lasting reputation damage

- Collecting customer payments without sending the orders to the supplier, then closing the store, leads customers to complain to the supplier and damages its online reputation. [L1422.011]
- Ignoring negative comments on ads and leaving them unanswered led to bad reviews piling up and the Facebook page being blocked. [L1131.046]
- Making cancellation hard, through promotion redirects or refusing order changes after placement, is the most damaging service pattern. [L1164.020]

## Documentation, record-keeping and operational safeguards

### Order and communication records

- Contact the customer first in any refund or dispute, then the supplier or carrier. Keep records of all communication, because they serve as chargeback evidence. [L0856.087]

### Evidence for disputes

- Keep complete records of every order, shipment and refund in Shopify. These records are the evidence needed to win a buyer appeal, and refund requests from platforms such as Facebook can be contested with them. [L1128.011]
- Keep detailed records of tracking numbers, supplier legal names, locations (including exact China addresses) and company names. Payment processors require these in compliance investigations. [L0324.023]

### Supplier information

- Do not share customer email addresses with suppliers without caution. Suppliers will likely use them for marketing, and customers did not consent to receive supplier communications. [L0245.063]
- Send customers only the supplier's order email and return policy. The company does not create its own supplier contracts. Sign the supplier's agreement and return it right away. *(Older: Source A 2021.)* [L0834.092]
- As the store owner, you handle customer complaints and payment disputes, not the supplier. Agree return and payment terms with the supplier in advance. [L0660.033]
- Set the defective return allowance on a supplier application to 100 percent, because a defective product is always replaced. [L0855.135]

### Supplier relations and escalation

- If a supplier does not respond after a few days, keep following up until you get a yes or no answer. [L0855.140]
- When an order is lost or damaged, do not yell, curse or send hostile emails to the supplier, even if the fault is theirs. Work through the problem calmly and respectfully. Suppliers who are treated with disrespect will not give you special treatment, even if you sell a lot. [L0939.013]
- If you cannot reach the decision maker at a supplier, ask the receptionist to connect you to a sales representative. Sales representatives have more product knowledge than call-center staff. [L0941.084]

### Insurance

- The sources differ on whether general liability insurance is required or only usual.
  - Optional view: general liability insurance is optional and not needed to open a business. It can be considered based on business assets. Get quotes from a large insurer or from the insurer already used for a home policy. [L0941.086]
  - Usual-type view (older): general liability insurance is the usual type for an online store. *(Older: Source A 2020.)* [L1277.098]
- Be cautious with insurance brokers, and review what you are actually charged over time, since premiums can rise a lot after the first year. *(Older: Source A 2020.)* [L1277.098]
- Limited liability insurance becomes more sensible once you have assets to protect. Consult a professional before deciding. *(Older: Source A 2020.)* [L1277.099]

### Sales tax and payouts

- Enable sales tax for each state before taking orders from that state. An order placed before tax is set up may need to be cancelled and redone, and refunds can cost real money, as in one case that cost 40 USD. *(Older: Source A 2021.)* [L1090.118]
- A refunded or cancelled order can create a negative pending payout in Shopify. After logging in, check the options shown in Shopify Payments before paying out the balance. *(Older: Source A 2021.)* [L1090.119]

### Refund exposure and cash reserves

- Letting backorders stretch for months while income continues to be spent on normal costs and owner pay can leave no money for refunds or supplier bills. Track refund exposure from pending orders against the cash set aside for them. *(Older: Source B 2021-22.)* [L1200.024]

### Sensitive files and AI-accessible folders

- Dragging personal or financial documents into an AI-accessible folder exposes them to the agent and creates real risk. [L0366.006]
- Keep such files outside the agent folder and out of any folder Codex can open. [L0366.006]

## Other details

### Payment, collections and chargebacks

**Unpaid invoice after shipment (older advice, Source A 2021).** If a customer does not pay an invoice after shipment, follow these steps:
1. Call the customer. [L0247.095]
2. Text the customer. [L0247.095]
3. Check the tracking record to prove delivery. [L0247.095]
4. Message the customer through LinkedIn or Facebook if they still do not respond. [L0247.095]

**Pending PayPal payment.** For a customer whose PayPal payment is pending, check the notification for a reason first. If none is shown, contact PayPal support. [L0964.107]

**Chargebacks and refunds in the sales plan.** Refunds, chargebacks and lifetime value often get too little attention during the front-end sale. Include them in every sales plan and report them with each offer. [L0378.098]

**Chargeback risk from test orders.** When placing a dummy test order on a competitor's store, contact their support first, say the order was placed by mistake, and request cancellation or a refund. Expect refusal, often with a claim that the order has already shipped. Some testers then consider a chargeback, which carries risk and should not be the default. [L0501.038]

**Benchmark from a store with low disputes.** A founder working from Thailand reported more than 1,000 orders with two chargebacks and fewer than one refund per month. The details are in the case study below. [L0910.057]

**Collection letters: persuasion and threat in turn.** Alternate persuasion with the threat of loss in a collection series. A strong threat frightens some debtors into paying, but it angers others, so follow it with a persuasive letter that restores goodwill before the next threat. [L1369.098]

**Collection letters: appeal to honesty.** Formula: remind the debtor of an honest trait he is proud of, such as paying one's debts, and then say that his account reflects that trait. Why it works: a debtor who sees himself as honest is more likely to pay than one who feels accused. [L1369.099]
- Example one: Most of our customers pay their accounts promptly because they value their word, and we are confident you are one of them. [L1369.099]
- Example two: Our records show your history of paying on time, and this one invoice is simply waiting for your confirmation to close. [L1369.099]

**Collection letters: amount, date, consequence and benefit.** Formula: state the exact amount owed, the specific date by which payment must arrive, the consequence if it does not, and the benefit of paying now. Why it works: a precise deadline and consequence are more likely to prompt action than a general reminder. [L1369.100]
- Example one: Your balance of 25.00 dollars is due by the 17th. If payment is not received by then, your account will be recorded as overdue in our credit file. [L1369.100]
- Example two: Your invoice of 340 dollars is due by the 30th. Paying by then keeps your account in good standing and lets you order next month without a hold. [L1369.100]

**Collection letters: specific threats.** Threats in collection letters must be specific: state the amount, the deadline date and the exact next step, such as a transfer to the legal department. A vague warning is easy to ignore. [L1369.101]

**Collection letters: before and after record.** In a payment reminder, show the debtor the exact current entry on his account and the entry it will become if payment does not arrive by a set date. A visible before-and-after record makes the consequence concrete. Keep the consequence limited to actions you are legally entitled to take. [L1369.123]

### Shipping, delivery and checkout costs

**Charging for shipping.** Do not charge customers for shipping unless it is for an upgraded service, such as expedited shipping or white glove delivery. If free shipping margins are insufficient for specific suppliers, stop running ads to those products and rely only on organic traffic. (Source A 2023) [L0251.017]

**Shipping cost as an expense.** Shipping costs are an expense that comes out of gross profit, and they are not reduced by the store's own margin. (Older advice, Source A 2021) [L0834.093]

**Default offer: free standard delivery.** Offer free standard delivery by default and let customers upgrade to white glove delivery or white glove with assembly. This model has worked well compared with charging for every delivery option. (Older advice, Source A 2021) [L0853.096]

**Checkout transparency.** Use a checkout that shows shipping costs and fees clearly to avoid shock at checkout, since customers who do not expect extra costs may abandon or return. [L0950.072]

**Residential or commercial address.**
- Customers may be asked whether an address is residential or commercial by using a Shopify app or native option if available. If none exists, contact Shopify support to check. (Source A 2024) [L1115.072]
- For delivery questions about residential versus commercial addresses, check Shopify support for an app or native option before making changes to checkout. (Source A 2024) [L1115.073]

**Customer accounts.** Customer account login is usually enabled, but most stores see little use because purchases are one-off or infrequent. (Source A 2024) [L1115.074]

**Installation.**
- When a customer needs installation for a product, avoid taking on installation liability directly. Build a network of local installers in major cities and refer customers to them. (Source A 2023) [L1094.094]
- For a product that is basic furniture or not regularly installed by professionals, the freight-to-third-party-receiver model is not the norm. Ask the supplier about their standard delivery process first. (Source A 2023) [L1094.095]

### Supplier quality and supplier relations

**Invoices and wholesale prices in packages.** Suppliers do not include invoices or receipts with wholesale prices in packages. The product box will show the brand name (normal, expected) but never the internal wholesale cost. (Source A 2022) [L0249.068]

**Supplier approval before selling their products.** Suppliers request approval before allowing you to sell their products. Explain that your store is not yet live, demo products are on the site to show suppliers what their product pages will look like, and you will launch on [specific date]. This is standard practice and fully disclosed. (Source A 2024) [L0253.035]

**Reporting MAP pricing violations (procedure, older advice, Source A 2019).**
1. Find a competing store selling the supplier's product below the MAP price. [L0243.024]
2. Use Loom to record a brief 20-second video stating the competitor's name, product, price, and that they are violating MAP policy. [L0243.024]
3. Email the Loom video to your supplier contact at customer service. [L0243.024]
4. The supplier will typically correct the violation quickly if they enforce MAP policy. [L0243.024]

**Supplier mismatch case study.** The founder of a store with a printed fashion item ordered the product after a video call showed the item. The founder asked the supplier for a factory photo or video, but the supplier said photos would slow production, and no sample was ever sent, even though one had been promised. The supplier then shipped a lower-quality product: the printed item was sent in place of a woven product. [L0694.039]
- Within one day the store received six PayPal disputes, and more followed the next day. [L0694.039]
- The founder spent many hours on customer service. A Trustpilot profile was opened by someone else with negative reviews, and the store was labelled as a scam. [L0694.039]
- The supplier threatened to close the account if the founder opened a dispute and did not apologise. [L0694.039]
- The founder decided to stop working with this supplier, postponed the planned relaunch from the 15th to around the 19th while checking the price with new factories, and planned to redesign the store and hire a virtual assistant. [L0694.039]
- Lesson: the founder should have requested a photo or video from the factory before the first order, and should not have ordered bulk or trusted a supplier that refused to show the product. [L0694.039]

**Early product example.** A first product ran for about one month, with the first ad launched on 7 January, and produced about 11,000 EUR in revenue. This shows that a single well-chosen product can carry an early store while other markets are tested. [L0694.040]

**Customer service staff and virtual assistants.**
- A customer support virtual assistant who handles chat, phone calls, email, and Zendesk tickets reduces seller dependence. If staff are willing to stay with the new owner, tell the buyer, because buyers highly value continuity. (Source A) [L0554.029]
- A founder working from Thailand built a dropshipping business with over 500,000 dollars in sales in about 2.5 years, reportedly without answering calls or emails in real time. At the start he worked late nights and early mornings, calling suppliers and answering emails himself. [L0910.057]
- He then added a visible phone number, an FAQ, personal product notes, a clear shipping page and detailed shipping-time emails, which reduced contact volume significantly. [L0910.057]
- He hired a native English-speaking virtual assistant to answer calls for a flat 150 dollars per month, and he uses a shipping-tracking app and a Gmail scheduling and reminder tool. [L0910.057]
- Over more than 1,000 orders, he had two chargebacks and fewer than one refund per month. [L0910.057]

**Fulfilment model comparison.** On FBA, Amazon handles most returns, refunds and customer calls, so the seller only answers occasional questions by email. Customer service load is much lower than running a dropshipping store. (Source A) [L1153.077]

### Customer communication

**Message templates.** A ready-made PDF of customer service message templates covers the common situations. Adjust the store name, product name and customer service agent name in each template before sending it to customers. [L0911.004]
- The PDF is grouped into four scenario types: tracking inquiries, returns and refunds, order modification or cancellation, and refunds for lost orders. [L0911.004]

**Reply structure.** Every customer reply follows the same frame: a greeting that thanks the customer and offers help, the order status with the specific facts, the expected timeframe or the action taken, a closing line that asks if they have further questions, and a sign-off with an agent name, store name and role. [L0911.018]
- Pattern formula: Greeting + Status fact + Timeframe or action + Closing + Signature. [L0911.018]
- Example for a delayed order: Hi Sam, thanks for reaching out, happy to help. Your order left our supplier on March 3 and is now with the carrier. Expect delivery within 7 to 10 business days. Let me know if anything else comes up. Best, Emma, Customer Care at [store name]. [L0911.018]

**Response window for student or community messages.** Answer student or community messages within a fixed window after the morning business checks, because members in other time zones may start their day while the operator is still in the middle of the workday. Schedule this as its own short block rather than answering whenever a message arrives. [L1181.028]

**Opening a support ticket.** When you open a support ticket, include your name, your goals and whether you are new or experienced, so the right helper can be assigned and help faster. [L1323.012]

**Customer service as a differentiator.** Customer service can be a differentiating part of the offer, and buyers expect service close to what they would get in a physical store. A distinctive service level such as extended phone hours can win sales when competitors do not offer it. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22) [L0411.026]

**Customers referred from another marketplace (procedure, older advice, Source A 2020).**
1. Reply by email, acknowledge that Amazon referred them, and offer to help. [L0961.054]
2. Offer to answer their question on a recorded video call, using FaceTime, Skype or a similar tool. An audio-only recording is acceptable if they are not comfortable on camera. [L0961.054]
3. At the start of the call, ask how they found your store. [L0961.054]
4. Answer their question and give practical advice. [L0961.054]
5. End the recording with a call to action that points to your store. [L0961.054]
6. Embed the recording on your About Us page and on the product pages for those products. [L0961.054]
7. Run a remarketing ad to visitors of your site, so they remember you before buying elsewhere. [L0961.054]

**Template: email reply to a customer referred by another marketplace (older advice, Source A 2020).**

```
Hi [Name], thanks for reaching out about [product]. Amazon sent you to us for support, and I would be glad to help. Would you be open to a short recorded video call so I can walk you through it? If you would rather not be on camera, an audio call works too. Before we start, could you tell me how you found us?
```
[L0961.055]

**Business mindset and service quality.**
- Poor customer service is a symptom of low business confidence, appearing alongside doing business only for money and running a business on plans that never get executed. Fixing the owner's confidence and self-alignment is part of improving service quality. (Source A) [L0701.041]
- A competitive business should turn setbacks into advantages, so each problem becomes a chance to improve. Track each setback and record what it reveals about the customer experience or supply chain. (Source A) [L0920.029]
- Speaking directly with real people who have bought the product is the most important way to make progress. These conversations reveal the bottleneck so it can be identified and solved. (Source D 2026) [L1042.015]
- Good customer service and product quality can make shoppers buy from a dropshipping store even when many stores sell the same product. Satisfied customers also promote the store to others. (Source C) [L1213.077]
- Scaling a product with poor quality or service makes unhappy existing customers see the ads and share complaints. Since iOS limits tracking, you cannot fully hide ads from past buyers even when they are excluded. (Source C) [L1213.036]

### Customer targeting

**Aim for the right buyers.** Aim to attract the right buyers rather than the most buyers. Customers who do not fit the product create a poor business, complaints, and extra costs. [L0378.100]

**Pain-point research.** Find out what the product solves, what customers say in reviews, and what problems they face in daily life, to build a precise customer avatar. [L1158.020]

**Customer conversations before private label.** Before private labeling a main product, the store should already have a substantial sales history, many customer service interactions and ongoing contact with customers. These provide the data needed to find differentiation. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22) [L1155.005]

### Platform support, accounts and policy compliance

**Support channels for a training program.** Support is available through the private, members-only Facebook group, where questions are answered by the instructor and experienced high-ticket dropshippers, and by email to support@dropshipbreakthrough.com (the link is in the page header). Before posting, search the group for the question, as it may already be answered. (Older advice, Source B 2021-22) [L1496.009]

**Shopify theme and app support.**
- Shopify Support for theme edits: contact Shopify directly for a theme question, such as where to place a Klaviyo embed code in the Dawn theme, since Shopify built the theme and can give the exact location. (Source A 2024) [L0856.090]
- Store and product issue support: email the support address with the theme version used. The developers can locate code added elsewhere, including custom code, that changed a setting. (Source A 2024) [L0856.091]
- Send technical Shopify questions to the support address of the course provider, which routes to the developer team. This is not the coach's area of expertise. (Source A 2023) [L0964.112]
- When business email support is needed, contact the store's support address and describe the page and the problem. The team then routes the request to the right designer or developer. (Source A 2022) [L1092.098]
- For a support problem with Google Search Console or other tools, email the support team with the exact error message, since the team may already have a fix from earlier cases. (Older advice, Source A 2021) [L1090.121]

**Unplanned Shopify theme code error (procedure, Source A 2024).** Use this when red error lines appear in the theme editor after removing a third-party app's JavaScript.
1. Find the extra or missing bracket or line that was removed. [L0971.036]
2. If unsure, post a job on Upwork for a Shopify developer describing the exact red error. [L0971.036]
3. A five-minute fix is typical; a budget of about $20 is usually enough. [L0971.036]

**Bulk price changes.** Shopify bulk edit and product export are the approach for price changes in bulk. No repricing app is used by the team. (Source A 2024) [L0971.077]

**Digital content protection.** When content is copied, first message the copier once to remove it. If there is no response, file a DMCA takedown with the host, for example Shopify for a Shopify store. (Older advice, Source A 2022) [L0969.039]

**Store name collisions.** If another store uses the exact same name and sells the same products, change the store name and buy a new domain to avoid consumer confusion. (Older advice, Source A 2022) [L0969.094]

**Advertising account restrictions.** Ad accounts and business assets can be restricted when the landing page or creatives break platform policy, for example with before and after claims or weight loss claims. Audit the landing page and creatives against the policy before launching or reusing creatives. (Source C) [L0638.049]

**Google Merchant Center.**
- Google Merchant Center policy violations caused by automated bot scrapes can be contested. Request a manual review, then ask for the domain to be whitelisted so it is reviewed manually before suspension. (Older advice, Source A 2022) [L0665.088]
- Merchant accounts can be suspended if the account is set up from abroad while listing a US address. If this happens, appeal and provide the correct details. (Older advice, Source A 2022) [L0665.089]

**Facebook account bans due to ID issues.** Submit the ID review in Meta Business settings. It usually takes 24 to 48 hours. If it does not work, contact the account seller or a support provider. (Source C) [L0773.052]

**Pinterest.** Pinterest's support team can help with account bans, restrictions and ad insights. The phone number on the business account is used for support, not verification. Do not follow Pinterest's general marketing advice for campaign decisions, because it is not aimed at direct response selling. (Source C) [L1134.036]

### Ads and click quality

**Click-through rate threshold.** Do not scale ad spend when click-through rates fall below 2%. A low CTR indicates poor product-market fit and will exhaust budget without converting traffic. (Source C) [L0324.024]

**Click fraud.** A third-party click fraud service tested at the time was not worth the cost. The author cancelled after 30 days and does not recommend it. Use Google's Invalid Click analysis and account audit first. (Source A 2024) [L0856.089]

### Marketplace delivery commitments (Google Shopping Actions)

Older advice, Source B 2021-22.

**Joining Shopping Actions.** Joining Shopping Actions requires the merchant to state specific delivery time frames for orders and to keep them. Other marketplaces use the same kind of delivery commitment. [L0738.010]

**Delivery reliability before joining.** Before joining, check that you can deliver within the stated time frame at least 90% of the time. Example: if you promise delivery in 7 days, at least 90% of orders must arrive within 7 days. If you cannot, do not join, because suspension will follow. [L0738.011]

**Seller score.** The seller score is driven by buyer feedback on delivery times, return rates and cancellation rates, each with thresholds. A poor seller score is hard to recover from. [L0738.016]

**Retailer Standards score.** The Retailer Standards score is calculated from order defects such as late deliveries and high cancellation rates. A merchant must deliver 20 items to receive a score the following month, and the score is checked on the first day of each month. [L0738.027]

**Defect trends.** Late deliveries and a high order cancellation rate both lower the Retailer Standards score. Check the defect trends in Merchant Center regularly so that problems are corrected before the monthly score is set. [L0738.028]

**Daily order check.** The Shopping Actions Today's Snapshot in Merchant Center flags orders as due today when they are pending shipment, missing tracking information or have wrong tracking information. Clear these flags daily, because late or untracked orders reduce the Retailer Standards score that determines Shopping Actions visibility. [L0738.040]


# 18. Legal, tax, banking and payments

## Business Structure: Sole Proprietor, LLC, S-Corp and Entity Strategy

### Why a Legal Entity Matters

- An LLC (Limited Liability Company) is a separate legal entity that protects personal assets from business liabilities and looks more professional to suppliers than a sole proprietorship. Form an LLC unless you genuinely have nothing to protect. [L0118.001]
- A sole proprietorship has no legal separation from its owner, so personal assets such as bank accounts and property are exposed to business liabilities. A separate legal entity limits liability to the business assets only. [L0698.003]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* A sole trader is personally liable for business debts. In a dispute, personal assets such as a house could be claimed to settle them. [L0702.003]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* A proprietary limited company or LLC is separate from its owner. The owner is usually both director and shareholder. If the company cannot pay its debts, it can be wound up without the director generally being liable. [L0702.004]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Limited liability does not cover illegal conduct. A director can still be held liable if the company or the director acts illegally. [L0702.005]
- Liability protection holds only if business and personal funds are not commingled. [L0429.009]
- Commingling funds across unrelated LLCs makes separate businesses look like one entity. This weakens the LLC's liability protection and makes a later sale of one business much messier. [L1092.011]
- Lawsuits against the business target the business and not the owner personally. [L1085.076, L1274.047]

### Choosing a Structure

#### Structure Overview (US Terms)

| Structure | Separation from owner | Setup and cost | Suits | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sole proprietorship | None. Personal assets are exposed to business lawsuits. | No formation filing. The owner can trade under their own name immediately. | People with little to lose. Owners with a home, several vehicles, retirement savings or significant cash should avoid it. | [L0703.001, L0703.002, L0698.005] |
| LLC | Separate legal entity. A lawsuit reaches only assets the LLC owns, such as business bank funds and equipment. | Inexpensive and easy to set up. Commonly about $100. | The most common first structure for online sellers. | [L0703.003, L0270.027, L1085.076] |
| LLC taxed as S corp | Same liability protection as the LLC. The S corp is a tax election, not a separate entity type. | Election is filed with the IRS. The one-time setup cost is small once the business is profitable. | Once profit justifies payroll setup and accounting costs. | [L0703.004, L0703.012] |
| C corp | Separate legal entity. | Used when bringing in shareholders, seeking investment or going public. | Businesses seeking outside investment. Most small business owners use an LLC, the most popular structure. | [L0969.034, L0272.042] |

#### Sole Proprietorship

- Trading under your own name is the fastest and cheapest way to start. It is a reasonable starting point but is usually replaced by a company structure once revenue grows. [L0698.005]
- A sole proprietorship is not a separate legal entity, so all business profit is reported on the owner's personal tax return. Choose the structure with this in mind before you start selling. [L1344.001]
- The owner's name is the business name, even if the website domain differs. [L0969.033]
- A sole proprietorship has a higher tax burden. The owner cannot use as many write-offs and cannot split pay between salary and distributions. [L0698.004]
- Some states require registration even for sole proprietors. Upfront cost is lower, but there is no liability protection. [L0270.065]
- *Older advice (2021):* A sole proprietor operating under a business name may not need a DBA on day one. Many stores launched without one and later formed business entities as they grew. This is general experience, not legal advice. [L0968.024]
- *Older advice (2020):* A new store can start as a sole proprietorship with an EIN and no state sales tax certificate. When sales grow, the owner can form an S corporation and obtain the state sales tax certificate at the same time. [L1111.180]
- *Older advice (2019):* Starting as a sole proprietor using personal accounts is a valid option while you test the business. Once sales come in, a business structure can be set up with an accountant. [L1275.062]

#### LLC

- Forming an LLC typically costs about $100. [L0270.027, L1085.076]
- *Older advice (2021):* An LLC can be formed in a state other than where you live, through an accountant or yourself using an online filing service such as LegalZoom. [L0968.020]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* In the US, the LLC is the most commonly chosen structure. It is quick to form, often possible entirely online, and separates the company's assets from the owner's personal assets, unless the owner breaks the law. [L1405.009]
- *Older advice (2022):* Lean approach to entity setup in the US: form a cheap online LLC and optionally elect S-corp tax treatment. A sole proprietorship can be used first and an LLC formed later. Consult an accountant or tax professional for a personal situation. [L0969.005]
- An LLC is optional at launch, and a sole proprietorship can work initially. Once the business is making money, consult an accountant about forming a separate entity. [L0247.103]
- Form an LLC early and elect S-corporation tax treatment, which gives asset protection and tax benefits. Start as a sole proprietor only if the business is brand new, and form the LLC as soon as sales begin. [L0667.076]

#### S Corp and C Corp Elections

- An LLC can be elected to be taxed as an S corporation. This decision affects tax obligations. [L0249.074, L0469.051]
- Confirm the S-corp election with a tax professional before filing. [L0469.051]
- An S corp is not a separate entity type but a tax election. An existing LLC is taxed as an S corporation by filing an election form with the IRS. The owner keeps the same liability protection while gaining the S-corp tax treatment. [L0703.004]
- An LLC taxed as an S corporation offers tax advantages and separates personal liability from the business. This structure is commonly used by US-based dropshippers. [L0471.060]
- Consider an S-corp election after formation to reduce self-employment taxes. [L0270.027]
- Under an S corp or LLC, different pay structures are possible that can reduce taxes. [L0698.004]
- In the US, the main difference between an LLC and an S corp is how business profits are taxed. An accountant should compare both for the owner's personal situation. [L1405.010]
- *Older advice (2019):* An S corporation is the structure the presenter uses for protection and tax benefits. The right legal entity depends on your situation, so confirm it with an accountant or attorney. [L0663.060]
- *Older advice (2022):* Form your business as an LLC elected to be taxed as an S corp. Use a C corp only if you plan to seek outside investment. [L0272.042]
- *Older advice (2022):* An LLC can be elected to be taxed as an S corporation, which the lesson presented as a way to save on taxes. This is an example structure only and not tax or legal advice. [L1092.007]
- *Older advice (2022):* A C corporation is generally used when bringing in shareholders, seeking investment or going public. Most small business owners use an LLC, which is the most popular structure. [L0969.034]

### When to Start Simple and When to Upgrade

#### Timing Advice Compared

Sources agree that a sole proprietorship is a valid start and that the structure can be upgraded later. They differ on how early to form the LLC.

| Advice | Ids |
|---|---|
| Start as a sole proprietor for speed, then move to an LLC or corporation as soon as the business makes money. | [L0698.006] |
| Sole proprietorship can be used at the start. Set up a corporation with an accountant once the business earns money. *(Older, 2021.)* | [L0962.122] |
| An LLC is optional. Many people start as a sole proprietor, then form an LLC or S corporation once the business is making money. *(Older, 2021.)* | [L0671.109, L0671.246] |
| A business can start as a sole proprietor, and an LLC can be formed later once the business is established and earning money. *(Older, 2022.)* | [L1092.014] |
| Start as a sole proprietor and form an S corp only after the business is profitable. Entity formation is optional and not needed before contacting suppliers. *(Older, 2020.)* | [L1088.077] |
| Common path: start as an LLC and later elect S-corp taxation once the store earns enough profit to justify the payroll setup and accounting costs. | [L0703.012] |
| Form an LLC early and elect S-corp taxation. Start as a sole proprietor only if the business is brand new, and form the LLC as soon as sales begin. *(2025.)* | [L0667.076] |
| *Older advice (2021-22):* In the US, do not run a store as a sole proprietor. | [L1405.008] |

- The timing decision depends on personal risk and sales level. Whether to form an LLC or S corp early or wait is a personal choice. *(Older advice, 2018.)* [L1274.047]
- The sales level and risk exposure decide when a sole proprietorship stops being suitable. Owners with significant assets should avoid it from the start. [L0703.002]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* The right structure depends on personal circumstances such as existing self-employment, other jobs, investments and personal assets. A local accountant or lawyer should confirm the choice, especially outside the US and Australia. [L1405.007]

#### Revenue and Profit Thresholds

| Measure | Threshold | What applies | Ids |
|---|---|---|---|
| Annual profit | Below about $50,000 per year | Operating as a sole proprietor under your own name is simplest. | [L1126.027] |
| Annual profit | From about $100,000 per year | Look at tax-saving structures. At a 30% rate, tax on $100,000 would be about $30,000. | [L1126.027] |
| Monthly store revenue | Above roughly 5,000 to 10,000 USD | A company setup is recommended. It also helps with funding, business credit, banking and tax handling. *(Source C.)* | [L1512.009] |

- Profit thresholds and revenue thresholds are different measures. Use the profit figure for tax-structure decisions and the revenue figure for the company decision in the Source C source. [L1126.027, L1512.009]

#### Upgrade Procedures

*Older procedure (2020): Business setup path used by the coach.*

1. Start as a sole proprietor. [L1277.104]
2. Get an EIN. [L1277.104]
3. Once revenue arrives, consult an accountant. [L1277.104]
4. Set up an S-Corp with that accountant, and consider separate LLCs or S-Corps for each unrelated niche network. [L1277.104]
5. Confirm all of this with your own accountant or lawyer, since the coach is not one. [L1277.104]

*Source C procedure for a beginner's company path.*

1. Check whether Shopify Payments can be opened with personal documents, which may make a company unnecessary at first. [L1512.038]
2. If a company is needed, form a basic company in your home country, not abroad. [L1512.038]
3. After you have proof of concept, plan a better overseas setup for scaling. [L1512.038]

- *Older advice (2018):* You can start as a sole proprietor and later convert to an LLC or S-Corp, typically once the business is profitable. The expert did exactly that and paid an accountant to set up the S-Corp after sales started coming in. [L1274.046]

### Structuring Multiple Stores

#### Related Versus Unrelated Stores

- Related stores can sit under one LLC when they may later be sold as a network, especially when they cross-promote and share a remarketing pixel. Unrelated niches should be placed in a separate LLC. [L0471.059]
- Stores are related if they target the same audience, share suppliers, or compete directly or indirectly. Unrelated niches should each sit in their own LLC. *(Older, 2022.)* [L1092.009]
- Run separate niches under separate businesses. A closely related niche can share an LLC, while an unrelated niche should get its own LLC so finances stay separate. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0803.063]
- Building a network of stores under one LLC works for stores selling related products. Keep stores in separate LLCs when they operate in unrelated product types, so funds are not commingled. *(Older, 2021.)* [L0801.146]
- Put related stores that are cross-promoted or would be sold together under one LLC or S corp. *(Older, 2022.)* [L1113.046]
- Test: ask whether you would compete with store A if you kept store B. If yes, keep them in one entity. Create a new LLC for unrelated businesses. *(Older, 2022.)* [L1113.046]
- Run related stores in the same niche under one parent company, and open an unrelated niche under a separate business entity. Related stores can operate as DBAs under the parent company. *(2023.)* [L0835.113]
- Businesses that would be sold together should share one LLC, one EIN, one bank account and one resale certificate. Unrelated businesses should be set up as separate entities. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0963.120]
- An Amazon store and a Shopify store can share one LLC if they are related. Decide based on whether a future buyer would buy them as a bundle. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0963.122]
- Related stores that are cross-promoted to the same customers can be sold together as one listing. *(2024.)* [L1285.073]
- Group related stores under one LLC or S corp and form a separate entity for each unrelated category. This keeps stores easy to sell individually, since selling one store can compete with related ones. *(Older, 2021.)* [L1279.077]
- Operate a dropship business under a separate entity from other businesses, such as Etsy or Amazon, if you may sell that business later. Commingled finances make the parts harder to sell separately. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0665.098]
- Each store can be run under its own business entity so stores can later be sold separately. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0665.128]
- Mixing funds and expenses means the businesses are effectively one business, so decide whether that is what you want. *(Older, 2021.)* [L1090.124]
- Do not register an LLC under the name of a niche-specific website, because it ties the company to one niche and makes it hard to expand. Create a new entity for other stores and use DBAs for the store names. *(2023.)* [L0835.114]
- One LLC can run several businesses under different trade names. A single LLC can be kept as a long-term vehicle for future projects. Each business does not need its own LLC. *(Older, Source B 2021-22.)* [L1415.019]

#### Conflict: One Umbrella Entity or One Entity per Store

- Sources agree that related stores can share an entity. They differ on whether each store should have its own entity.
- *Shared entity:* related stores under one LLC when they may be sold as a network or cross-promoted. [L0471.059, L1285.073]
- *Separate entity per store:* each store under its own business entity so stores can be sold separately. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0665.128]
- Apply the shared entity when you plan to sell a network as one asset. Apply separate entities when you plan to sell stores individually. [L0471.059, L0665.128, L1279.077]

#### Single Entity Mechanics

- All stores can be run through one business entity with one EIN and one sales tax permit. Use one bank with sub-accounts for each store to see the money per store. *(Older, 2020.)* [L0852.094]
- Keep the company that holds the bank accounts and credit card, and that appears on supplier forms, as the company that operates the websites. *(Older, 2019.)* [L0960.059]
- An existing LLC can be used to run the stores as a business name, so a new company is not always needed. *(Older, 2019.)* [L0960.060]
- An EIN is tied to the business entity, not to one store. One entity can run many stores, so changing niche or rebranding does not require a new entity. *(Older, 2021.)* [L0968.025]
- Under one S corp, one entity can run several Shopify stores under different domain names, with each store linked to the corporation. A formal DBA filing for each domain was not needed in that setup. *(Older, 2018.)* [L1085.077]
- One S-Corp can own all of your stores. *(Older, 2018.)* [L1274.048]
- An existing registered company can sell online under a DBA. *(Older, 2021.)* [L1279.076]
- Keep the entity if possible instead of forming a new one and closing the old one, even if the business name no longer matches the niche. Choose a neutral name where a rename is needed. *(Older, 2022.)* [L1281.072]
- An older LLC can be reused for a new store only if it has a generic name. An LLC named after an unrelated former business should not be used. *(2024.)* [L1285.074]
- To open a new store name, buy a domain and create a Shopify store under the new name while the operating company remains the S corp. Check with a lawyer or accountant whether a DBA or separate entity is needed. *(Older, 2019. Not legal advice.)* [L0467.072]

### Naming the Entity

#### Generic Names

- Do not name the LLC after the store brand. Use a generic business name such as "AK Stores LLC" or "AK Shopping LLC". This allows you to own multiple stores under one LLC, keeps accounting clean and makes future sales easier. [L0118.002]
- Example: AK Stores LLC could own ShakaSurfboards.com initially, then add ShakaPaddleboards.com under the same LLC. [L0118.003]
- Form the LLC with a broad, general name rather than a store-specific name, such as "DD Stores LLC". *(Older, 2021.)* [L0270.012]
- Use a general, non-niche-specific LLC name so future related stores can be placed under the same entity. A narrow name makes it harder to add stores later. *(Older, 2022.)* [L1092.008]
- Name legal entities with broad, non-store names, because one entity can later run several stores. *(Older, 2020.)* [L1088.078]
- Name the parent company generically, for example with your initials plus "Stores, Inc.", rather than after one domain. This lets the same company own future stores. *(Older, 2019.)* [L1002.069]
- Keep the company name generic and let each store name carry the niche. Stores built in the same niche can sit under one company. The store name, not the company name, is the part tied to the niche and domain. *(2023.)* [L1114.067]
- The company name is mostly seen by banks and business contacts, while each store carries its own brand name. *(Older, 2018.)* [L1274.048]
- Give the LLC a generic name that is not the store name, for example a pattern like "X Stores LLC" or "X Enterprises LLC", so it can hold several stores over time. The exact wording matters less than the name being general. [L0695.003]
- Pick a vague LLC name such as a set of initials plus "Stores" or "Enterprises", so the same entity can own several stores. *(2023.)* [L0804.097]
- Use a neutral business name, such as initials with the word "Stores" or "Inc", before the niche is decided, because it appears on bank accounts and supplier applications. *(Older, 2022.)* [L1281.071]
- Do not name the company after the store. A separate company name, such as the owner's initials plus "Stores LLC", makes it easier to open additional stores later. *(Older, 2021.)* [L0834.080]
- Entity name examples: "ER Stores LLC" and "Online Stores LLC". *(Older, 2022.)* [L0249.073]
- Use the entity name for tax documents and bank accounts only. [L0249.073]
- The business name does not need to relate to your domain or niche. [L0249.073, L0429.010]
- Choose a different entity name rather than the store URL, so several related niche stores can be run under the same entity. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0429.010]
- Example: a business entity "AK Stores Inc" owns the stores "Antons-Paddleboards.com" and "Antons-Kayaks.com". *(Older, 2022.)* [L0272.043]
- The LLC name should differ from the store domain. This separates the legal entity from the brand. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0272.043]
- Business names used for an LLC or EIN do not have to match the store names. The LLC or S corp owns the websites, so the legal entity name can differ from the brand. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0854.086]
- The name on the LLC paperwork must match the name used for the tax ID and the submitted address. *(2024.)* [L0971.068]

#### DBAs (Doing Business As)

- A DBA is usually needed when the LLC name differs from the store name, although this varies by state. Consult local requirements. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0272.044]
- Register the DBA in the state where the LLC is registered. The existing sales tax certificate usually covers e-commerce sales in that state. *(Older, 2020.)* [L0468.160]
- Use a DBA when the store name is close to the LLC name or is general. Form a new LLC when the new store is unrelated. *(2023.)* [L0804.097]
- Check your original business setup with the person who helped create it before adding a DBA or reseller certificate to an existing LLC. Advice on legal or tax structures should come from an accountant or lawyer. *(Older, 2018.)* [L1085.079]
- Choose an LLC over a DBA if you are fully committed to the business and plan to form an entity eventually. Form it early. Both DBA and LLC are fine for supplier approval. *(2024.)* [L1285.072]
- Running an online store as a DBA under an existing LLC with the same EIN and bank account is possible if the businesses are related. *(Older, 2021.)* [L1090.124]

### Registered Agent, State and Address

#### Choosing a State

- Form the LLC in the state where you live. You need only one LLC per state. [L0118.004]
- *Alternative:* Choose the US state for your LLC. Texas is business-friendly. A virtual address through a UPS store or PO box can serve as the official business address, so you do not have to use your home address. *(Older, 2021.)* [L0834.078]
- *Alternative:* Choosing a state to form your company in is a personal decision. Texas is described as business friendly, and Delaware and Nevada are commonly used alternatives. *(Older, 2018.)* [L1274.049]
- Wyoming's tax benefits are mainly relevant to non-US residents forming a US company. A US resident should generally form the company in their own state, since Wyoming or Delaware give no clear advantage there. *(Source C.)* [L1512.023]
- An LLC can be formed in any state, but forming it in another state usually does not remove the obligation to pay tax in the state where you live. Check tax rules with a professional before relying on a different state. *(Older, 2019.)* [L0960.061]
- An LLC formed in Wyoming while physically operating in Florida: assume a nexus in the state of operation and confirm with a tax professional. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0969.028]

#### Registered Agents and Legal Address

- A registered agent is the person who receives legal paperwork for a business. A registered agent is needed when you set up a business in a state where you do not live. A legal service can provide one. *(2023.)* [L0835.115]
- A registered agent must be located in the state where the LLC is registered. An LLC outside your state needs a local registered agent who forwards mail. *(2024.)* [L0971.068]

### Before the First Sign-Up

- Settle the business structure before any supplier, platform or ad account sign-up, because those accounts use the registered business details. Get an EIN and a sales tax certificate only when they are needed for your situation (US context). [L0393.003]
- You do not need an LLC or business license before contacting suppliers. You can start as a sole proprietor, then hire an accountant to set up a corporation after revenue starts. *(Older, 2020.)* [L0268.045]
- A business structure is not required to get approved by suppliers. Starting as a sole proprietor is valid, and an LLC or S corporation can be added later. *(Older, 2018.)* [L1085.075]
- Entity formation is optional and is not needed before contacting suppliers. *(Older, 2020.)* [L1088.077]
- *Conflict:* Many US suppliers prefer to deal with a company structure such as an LLC or S corp rather than a sole proprietor. This is an additional reason to form one. *(Older, Source B 2021-22.)* [L1405.011]
- Australian suppliers generally do not care whether you trade as a sole trader or through a company, so the early choice does not limit supplier approval. *(Older, Source B 2021-22.)* [L1405.015]
- An EIN can be used for more than one business in the view presented, but confirm this with an accountant before relying on it. *(Older, 2021.)* [L1090.123]
- Get an EIN as part of the setup path. [L1277.104]
- Running a store under your own name typically requires being at least 18 years old. A younger founder would normally need an adult to sign the accounts and agreements. Confirm the rules for your country or state before opening business accounts. *(Older, 2022.)* [L0803.100]

### Structure by Country

#### United States

- The usual US business forms are a sole proprietorship (trading as yourself), an LLC and an S corp. The last two are legal entities. [L0698.015]
- *Conflict:* A sole proprietorship can be used at the start, and an LLC can be formed later. [L0698.006, L0962.122]
- *Conflict (older, 2021-22):* A sole proprietorship gives no separation between the business and the owner. The owner is personally liable, and personal assets such as a home can be seized to pay business debts. Do not run a US store as a sole proprietor. [L1405.008]
- Sole proprietorship, LLC and S corp differ mainly in liability and tax treatment. Use the LLC and S-corp options above for the relevant decision. [L0698.015, L0703.003, L0703.004]

#### Australia

- *Older advice (2021-22):* In Australia the two structures are the sole trader and the Proprietary Limited company (Pty Ltd). [L1405.012]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* A sole trader can be set up in minutes. A Pty Ltd costs about $800 to $2,000 to establish and requires an accountant. [L1405.012]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* In Australia, a sole trader is personally liable for business claims. A company director's personal assets are protected if the business operates legally. Liability protection and tax treatment are the two main differences. [L1405.013]
- *Older advice (2021-22). Recommended path for most Australian beginners:*
  1. Start as a sole trader to keep setup cheap and fast. [L1405.014]
  2. Once the business earns meaningful revenue and liability exposure grows, switch to a Pty Ltd company with an accountant's help. [L1405.014]
  3. If you already own a Pty Ltd, use it from the start. [L1405.014]

#### Sole Trader and Company Basics (Source B, Older)

- *Older advice (2021-22):* A sole trader has no legal separation from the owner. [L0702.003]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* The choice between sole trader and company has no universal right answer. It depends on liability exposure, tax situation, cash available and cost. Advice from an accountant is recommended when tax is complex. [L0702.008]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Starting as a sole trader is a valid low-cost choice, and it is easy to convert to a company later. Many owners do this when cash is limited and convert once the company's cost is financially justified. [L0702.011]

#### Other Countries

- Most other countries use different names but the same two-tier choice between trading as an individual and forming a company. [L0698.015]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Outside the US and Australia, a local accountant or lawyer should confirm the structure choice. [L1405.007]

### Company Path for Beginners (Source C)

- Check whether Shopify Payments can be opened with personal documents. If so, a company may be unnecessary at first. [L1512.038]
- If a company is needed, form a basic company in your home country, not abroad. [L1512.038]
- After you have proof of concept, plan a better overseas setup for scaling. [L1512.038]
- At about 100,000 USD monthly revenue, the advice was to consider Dubai for tax savings. Hong Kong was recommended for payment stability if the seller lives at home. Both need a home-country basic company for tax reporting. [L1512.039]

#### Further details

- When structuring multiple stores, consult an accountant or lawyer about whether to use one LLC for all stores or separate entities; benefits of separate entities include asset protection from lawsuits and cleaner separation if selling a store later. [L0245.065]

## Forming the Entity and Registering the Business

### Order of registration

- Choose the legal form first: sole proprietor, LLC or S-Corp. The sales tax certificate is needed only where the seller must collect sales tax. [L0532.002, L0532.003]
- Form the LLC before you apply for the EIN. The EIN application uses the LLC name. [L0695.010, L0118.010]
- Register the business early, even before it earns money, because the LLC, EIN and any sales tax certificate will be needed anyway. This avoids later delays and makes the business look more professional to suppliers. [L0695.017]
- The business name and the store name can differ. A business name is often generic and not tied to one niche. [L0941.092, L0251.015]
- Do not set up ad accounts until supplier products are on the store. While waiting for the EIN or company paperwork, work on supplier research and niche understanding. [L0962.121]

#### Full procedure: US LLC with EIN and sales tax certificate (older sources marked)

1. Decide between sole proprietorship and LLC. Choose an LLC unless there is almost nothing to lose. [L0695.008]
2. Choose a generic LLC name that is not the store name. [L0695.008]
3. Form the LLC online in the state where you are located, using LegalZoom's $0 basic option plus the state filing fee (no more than $97). Decline all upsell offers. [L0695.008, L0695.006]
4. Confirm with LegalZoom, or the chosen service, that the LLC name is available and belongs to you. [L0695.008]
5. Apply for an EIN on the IRS website using the "Apply for an EIN" option. Answer the questions, which usually takes 5 to 10 minutes. You receive a 9-digit number. [L0695.008]
6. Only if your state has sales tax: search Google for "[your state] sales tax certificate", open the state's.gov sales and use tax registration page, choose to register online, and enter the LLC name. [L0695.008, L0695.013]
7. Download the PDF that shows your sales tax certificate number. If none is offered, the certificate is sent by mail. [L0695.008, L0695.015]
8. Use the LLC name, EIN and sales tax certificate when registering with suppliers. [L0695.008]

#### Other sequences in the sources

| Sequence | Source | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Form LLC → get EIN → register for sales tax certificate if required in your state | [L0118.010] | Canonical order used in the sources |
| Choose structure → apply for EIN and sales tax certificate if needed | [L0393.002, L0532.002] | Structure must come first |
| Form LLC → get EIN (usually during formation) → open bank accounts → apply for sales tax certificate once the niche is picked | [L0803.062] (2022, older) | Bank opens before sales tax |
| Form LLC → apply for EIN online in a few minutes, without calling the IRS → keep EIN and sales tax certificate under the LLC name | [L1115.030] (2024) | Keep all numbers under LLC name, not store name |
| Structure → free EIN from the federal government → seller's permit in home state → business bank account using LLC info and EIN → business PayPal linked to the bank, with auto sweep enabled by PayPal support | [L1415.005] (2021-22, older) | Includes PayPal step |
| Register company with state → EIN → sales tax permit → business checking and savings → business credit card | [L0966.106] (2025) | Pre-launch order for the store |

#### Step-by-step details (per step)

- The EIN can usually be requested at the same time as the LLC, or right after the state approves it, depending on the filing service. [L0468.149] (2020, older)
- The EIN is a unique tax number for the business and is needed for Stripe, Mercury and most platforms. [L1127.004]
- Use the EIN as the business tax number for Stripe, Mercury and other platforms. [L1127.002]
- Open the business bank accounts only after the LLC and EIN are in place. [L0693.001]
- Entity, tax ID and bank setup should be done before supplier applications. Suppliers ask for the business name, business structure, registration and tax numbers. Missing these can delay progress by about a week while government registrations are processed. [L1405.006] (2021-22, older)
- Keep the EIN and sales tax certificate under the LLC's name, not the store name. [L1115.030]

### Choosing the legal form

- Sole proprietor or LLC: choose an LLC unless there is almost nothing to lose. [L0695.008]
- Before the EIN and sales tax certificate, get an accountant's advice on the structure that fits you, and track every business expense from the start so all deductible costs can be written off. [L1344.023]
- Describe the business as "online retail" or similar. No physical location is required in the formation documents. [L0268.047] (2020, older)
- An S-corp can be set up with an accountant after the EIN and LLC are in place. Many owners set up the EIN, LLC and S-corp as a package. [L0468.164] (2020, older)
- Converting a sole proprietorship to an LLC (DBA, EIN, bank accounts): consult a CPA or the state where the DBA was registered. One call did not give the steps. [L0805.053] (2024)

### Forming an LLC: DIY, services and fees

- Forming an LLC means filing articles of organization with your state. This is a formal registration step separate from any federal number. It can usually be done without a paid service, although many online ads push paid helpers. [L1415.017] (2021-22, older)
- You can form a business entity yourself. Paying someone is optional, and many owners pay only after the business is making money. [L1112.061] (2021, older)
- An LLC and EIN can be set up directly online for little cost. Third-party formation services often charge about $99 and then upsell extra services. [L0855.123] (2023)
- An LLC filed online through LegalZoom costs about $99 and is optional. It keeps business and personal funds separated from the start. [L1275.061] (2019, older)
- Do not pay a service just to obtain a document you can file yourself. Compare quotes before paying. [L0468.151] (2020, older)
- A service that forms LLCs for a monthly fee charges only the state filing fee. Typical formation services add a markup of roughly $100 to $150 on top of it. [L0960.062] (2019, older)
- Forming a business entity directly through a local government website typically costs about $100 to $300 at most. [L0698.008]
- Paying third-party intermediaries to form a legal entity abroad can be far more expensive than the official government registration website. Use the government portal whenever it is available. [L0698.009]
- Use the official state website to apply for a business entity or the state's reseller certificate. A virtual address can be used where needed for business documents. [L0964.115] (2023)
- Formation services usually handle the state filing for you. Confirm with the service what is included. [L1113.048] (2022, older)
