2. After the product videos (creatives) are found, send the report within 24 hours. [L1355.002]
3. After the campaign is launched, report at the 24-hour mark for Day 1. [L1355.002]
4. Report within 24 hours after Day 2. [L1355.002]
5. Report within 24 hours after Day 3. [L1355.002]
6. Continue reporting every 24 hours after that until told otherwise. [L1355.002]

- Missing a daily report costs money and removes the support team's control over the test, so all required reports must be submitted before moving on to the next step. Do not proceed to a later phase while earlier reports are outstanding. [L1355.006]

### Tracking setup

- Inventory tracking is commonly disabled even for live stores because continuously checking stock across all products is impractical. Enable it only if you maintain an active inventory management system. [L0036.030]
- An automation that writes the recovery date when a paid order comes in captures sales made when nobody on the team could call, such as at night or during time off. This keeps the sheet accurate without someone updating it manually. [L0737.012]
- Set up the sheet and automations early, even when one person handles everything, so the data is available for month-over-month improvement. Tracking is worth doing from the start rather than after the team grows. [L0737.017]

### Planning that feeds daily work

- Older advice from 2021-22: turn each priority into the full list of tasks needed to achieve it within six months, and mark recurring tasks as weekly so they are entered once. These task lists then feed the daily to-do list, and the 90-day rocks are derived from them. [L0447.016]
- Older advice from 2021-22: the priority task lists in the planner feed the daily to-do lists for the owner and the team, so one plan aligns everyone on the same top priority each day. [L0447.026]

### Changelogs

#### Why every change is logged

- Keep a running changelog of every change made to the store and its marketing, because over months you forget what was tweaked and why sales moved. Without this record, teams repeat failed tests and cannot tell which change caused a rise or drop in sales. Review it regularly so past experiments stay available when a similar idea comes up again. [L0410.001]
- Record every platform change in a log together with the date, the platform, the exact change, the expected result, and a baseline measured before the change. Fill in the result and its date later so each change can be judged on its own. [L1509.002]
- Compare results against a 90-day trailing baseline rather than a single day, because one day of data is too noisy to show whether a change worked. Write the baseline into the log next to the change so the comparison is fixed in advance. [L1509.003]
- A change logged without a baseline or a numeric expected result cannot be evaluated later. Always define the target metric and its current value before making the change. [L1509.004]
- Keep a dedicated record of every ad, supplier and store change so you can explain what moved the metrics. (Older advice from 2022.) [L0803.093]
- Keep a file of every letter, variant and result, because the record is what lets you repeat winners and avoid losers. A seller who loses the file must rebuild its knowledge from scratch. [L1369.108]

#### Setting up the changelog spreadsheet

Procedure:
1. Open the master Google Docs changelog template from the provided link; it is read-only, so click File and then Make a copy to get an editable version in your own Google Drive. [L0410.002]
2. Alternatively, use File and Download to save it as Excel or CSV and open it in any spreadsheet software. [L0410.002]
3. For each change, fill the columns: Date (date the change was implemented), Platform (where the change was made, e.g. Google Ads or Shopify Email), Change (what was changed), Expected Results (a hypothesis of the outcome, stated as a number where possible), Additional Notes (anything you will need to remember later, such as starting budget or baseline). [L0410.002]
4. When the experiment ends, enter the Result Date (the end date of the test) and the Results (what actually happened). [L0410.002]
5. Compare the result with the expected result, then decide whether to stop the change or to adjust it and log the adjusted version as a new experiment row. [L0410.002]

Changelog template column layout (Google Docs / spreadsheet):

| Column | Name | Content |
|---|---|---|
| A | Date | Date the change was implemented |
| B | Platform | Platform where the change was made (e.g. Google Ads, Shopify Email) |
| C | Change | Description of the change |
| D | Expected Results | Hypothesis of the outcome, e.g. a target ROAS or open-rate increase |
| E | Additional Notes | Anything relevant to remember later, e.g. starting budget, baseline figure |
| F | Result Date | End date of the experiment (e.g. two weeks after the start date) |
| G | Results | What actually happened, entered as a number |

[L0410.003]

#### Log structure and example entries

Log structure (one row per change, dates as Excel serial numbers):

| Date | Platform | Change | Expected Result | Additional Notes | Result Date | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 45733.0 | Shopify Email | Opt-in bribe changed from % off to quiz | Increase revenue per opt-in | 90 day trailing revenue per opt-in = $80 | | |
| 45701.0 | Meta Ads | Updated creative for remarketing ads | Increase CTR | 90 day trailing CTR = 5% | | |
| 45691.0 | Meta Ads | Launched Advantage+ Shopping Campaign | >10x ROAS | Starting budget of $20/day | | |
| 45660.0 | Google Ads | Launched Demand-Gen Remarketing Campaign | >10x ROAS | Starting budget of $10/day | | |
| 45653.0 | Instagram | 3x weekly posts using AI-generated images & copy | 5x monthly engagement on organic posts | Current engagement = 100/month | | |
| 45630.0 | Shopify | Offer extended warranties | Sell 5 extended warranties/month | NA | | |
| 45611.0 | Shopify Email | Replaced email profile picture with moving.gif | Increase open rates by 5% | 90 day trailing open rate = 45% | | |
| 45553.0 | Google Ads | Launched YouTube Remarketing Ads | >10x ROAS | Starting budget of $10/day | | |

[L1509.001]

Example of a Google Ads test logged in the changelog: on 18 September, YouTube remarketing ads were launched on Google Ads for the first time. Expected result: a return on ad spend above 10X, meaning more than $10 back per $1 spent. Additional note: starting budget of $10 per day. Result Date: two weeks after the start. Actual result: 5X ROAS, below the expected 10X, so the test was iterated instead of kept as is. [L0410.004]

Example of an iteration logged as a new row: after the first YouTube remarketing test returned 5X ROAS, the video ads in the campaign were swapped and the test was logged again as a new experiment with the expected result of over 10X ROAS. The note in the new row referenced the 5X result of the original test, so the link between the two experiments stayed visible. [L0410.005]

#### Deciding after a test and before repeating an idea

- When a test fails to reach its expected ROAS, decide between two options: turn the campaign off, or change its structure, targeting, or ads and run it again as a new logged experiment. Either way, record the decision so the same idea is not retested without knowing the earlier outcome. [L0410.006]

Use the changelog in team meetings before a new idea is accepted:
1. When someone proposes a change, search the log for earlier tests of the same element or platform. [L0410.014]
2. If a matching test exists, read its Expected Results, Result Date and Results. [L0410.014]
3. Only propose the idea again if the earlier outcome is recorded as a different setup or was never run, and log the new attempt. [L0410.014]

### CRO test boards (older advice, 2021-22)

- Trello boards can track every CRO test in one place, with columns for future tests, current tests, completed tests, insights and notes. Trello is easy to share with virtual assistants and team members, who often already know it. [L1364.039]
- The tool does not decide success, so a spreadsheet with the same columns or another project tool such as Asana or Basecamp works equally well. Pick the tool that keeps all tracking in one place and is quick to use. [L1364.044]

Structure of a CRO test tracking board:

| Column | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Future Tests | Test ideas planned but not started |
| Current Tests | Tests running now |
| Completed Tests | Finished tests, with sub-lists Winning Tests and Failed or Inconclusive Tests |
| Insights | Ideas for further tests drawn from results |
| Notes | Loose ideas and reminders not related to a current test |

[L1364.040]

Contents of each test card:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Description | What is being tested and the exact change |
| Duration | How long the test will run |
| Notes | Specific data points or other points worth recording |
| Attachments | Exports from Google Analytics, Google Ads or Shopify with data linked to the test |

[L1364.041]

Test card workflow:
1. Create a card for each planned test in Future Tests with its description, duration and attachments. [L1364.042]
2. When the test starts, move the card to Current Tests. [L1364.042]
3. Set a calendar reminder for the end date and review running tests in a weekly to-do session. [L1364.042]
4. When the test ends, move the card to Completed Tests and update it with results, comments and any additional attachments. [L1364.042]
5. Decide whether the test is winning or failed or inconclusive. [L1364.042]
6. Copy the card into the matching winning or failed sub-list. [L1364.042]
7. If the test produced insights, add a card to Insights describing them, to feed future test ideas. [L1364.042]

### P&L and bookkeeping

#### Starting the P&L with Claude Code (Source E 2025-26)

Procedure:
1. Open Claude Code project and type "execute this project". [L0218.009]
2. Answer onboarding questions in one message: brand name, accounting software (Xero/QuickBooks/MYOB/spreadsheets), monthly revenue ballpark, and primary priority (e.g., margin visibility, ad ROI, cash forecasting). [L0218.009]
3. Review and approve the generated CFO_DECISION_LOG.md, MEMORY.md, and DATA_INVENTORY.md files. [L0218.009]
4. Drag Xero P&L export into folder. [L0218.009]
5. Ask iterative questions to improve formatting or analysis. [L0218.009]

- Claude Code is preferable to Claude Cowork for initial P&L projects. Pass the Xero transaction export and classification prompt directly to Claude Code rather than Cowork; it handles larger datasets and maintains better file organization. [L0218.019]

#### Operating expenses in the P&L

- Operating expenses are entered on a 30-day (monthly) basis, then multiplied by three to create a 90-day total that aligns with the 90-day revenue figures. [L0222.017]
- Include only fixed operating expenses, meaning costs that remain constant regardless of revenue level. Examples: employee salaries, rent, warehouse costs, subscriptions to Shopify, Klaviyo, Gorgias, and other software. Exclude variable expenses that fluctuate with sales volume. [L0222.018]
- Example monthly operating expenses: $25,000, which equals $75,000 for a 90-day period ($25,000 × 3). [L0222.019]

#### Scaling and fixed costs

- Scaling example: selling 50 products per month at 1,000 USD each gives 50,000 USD in revenue. Fixed costs stay roughly the same at about 30 USD (Shopify plus domain), so they barely increase as volume grows. [L0759.027]

#### When to upgrade bookkeeping

- Older advice from 2021-22: start with the main goal of making sales and more sales; bookkeeping should not be perfected before the business has revenue to account for. Only move to proper accounting once questions about cash flow or money in the bank become important, or once you can afford to pay someone or have the time to set it up yourself. [L1516.001]
- A practical threshold for upgrading from a DIY bookkeeping setup to professional accounting is roughly 10,000 to 20,000 in monthly revenue. The figure is in the course's currency; the German course copy states it in euros. Above that level the business is considered real and should be run more seriously. [L1516.002]
- Scaling a dropshipping business means taking on bigger problems, which need better tools and different, more advanced help than the starter setup provides. The starter tools are not wrong, they are simply not suited to a business that is just getting started. [L1516.003]
- A spreadsheet is recommended while the store has low order volume. When revenue grows, you have a bookkeeper or accountant, and the extra cost is justified, switch to a paid accounting tool such as Xero.com, which the author describes as the one used once the business had an accountant. [L1202.021]

Decide when to upgrade from a basic bookkeeping setup to proper accounting (older advice, 2021-22):
1. Upgrade once questions about where the money goes or why the bank balance does not match the P&L keep coming up. [L1516.020]
2. Upgrade when cash flow becomes important to you. [L1516.020]
3. Upgrade when you have the money to hire someone for bookkeeping, or the time to set it up yourself. [L1516.020]
4. If you are unsure, upgrade when monthly revenue reaches 10,000 to 20,000. [L1516.020]
5. Upgrade when the business moves into a growth phase with full financial systems. [L1516.020]

Until one of these applies, put the focus on getting sales. [L1516.020]

#### Who does the books (older advice, 2021-22)

- When a store grows, a fractional CFO or a better accountant can provide a finance plan and budget, and can advise on financial issues that do not matter at the starter stage. [L1516.009]
- Hiring a cheap bookkeeper from freelance marketplaces such as Upwork, Fiverr or general online job boards is risky, because poor work is often not visible for many months. A business owner without accounting skills usually cannot inspect the work, and a clean-up by experienced professionals later costs far more than good work would have. [L1516.010]
- When hiring an external bookkeeper, choose someone who has proven experience with e-commerce businesses, ideally with dropshippers, rather than an unknown freelancer. Specialists in e-commerce accounting exist, and a business owner who has run an e-commerce store themselves may offer this service. [L1516.011]
- Professional e-commerce bookkeeping typically costs at least a few hundred dollars per month, which is the minimum a reputable bookkeeping company charges for this type of work. [L1516.012]
- If the owner dislikes doing the books or lacks the time to do them, a done-for-you e-commerce bookkeeping service is a reasonable option once the business has grown. Choose a provider that specializes in e-commerce and can show it works with many dropshippers. [L1516.019]
- Bookkeeping is needed for the owner to understand performance and solve problems. The main goal of the books is clarity about what is happening in the business, not a formal record for its own sake. [L1516.015]
- Outsourcing bookkeeping to a trained VA is allowed and encouraged when the owner purchases a course, as long as the course is used in the business for the assistant's training. [L1516.014]
- Once manual tracking is established, you can delegate order profit entry to a virtual assistant. Full automation with Zapier-style automations is possible but is an advanced setup; if you are not comfortable with such tools, hire someone to build it. [L1201.003]

Budget-conscious alternative to hiring an agency or freelancer (presented as far better than hiring an unknown cheap freelancer):
1. Hire a virtual assistant who already has some bookkeeping experience. [L1516.013]
2. Give the assistant access to a DIY e-commerce bookkeeping course that the business owner has purchased or has free access to. [L1516.013]
3. Have the assistant learn the bookkeeping process from the course and apply it to the business. [L1516.013]

Options compared:

| Option | Who does the books | Cost named | Main risk named |
|---|---|---|---|
| Done-for-you e-commerce bookkeeping service | Specialist firm | At least a few hundred dollars per month | Low when the firm has proven e-commerce experience |
| Cheap freelancer from Upwork, Fiverr or online job boards | Unknown freelancer | Low | Poor work often shows only months later, and the clean-up by professionals costs a lot |
| Virtual assistant with some bookkeeping experience, trained with a DIY e-commerce bookkeeping course | Virtual assistant under the owner's supervision | Not stated | Depends on the assistant's skill and training |

[L1516.021]

#### Financial review cadence (older advice, 2021-22)

- Review the financial reports every month, because the monthly picture is what allows decisions before problems compound. Reports should be reviewed alongside the cash position, not only the sales figures. [L1046.045]
- An outside bookkeeper or advisor who knows ecommerce can translate the reports into clear actions. Where an advisor is not affordable, a self-taught bookkeeping course can also provide the same reports. [L1046.046]
- Financial analysis is built in layers: first understand the profit and loss, balance sheet and cash flow, then address cash flow, supplier and profit problems in turn. Each analysis answers some questions and raises new ones. [L1046.047]

### Profit allocation

#### Reinvest before taking profit

- Early profits from a drop shipping store should be reinvested, not taken out, so that you can work through the full cycle of finding a winner, testing, scaling, creating unique content, and eventually moving toward a private label or bulk-buying brand. Take profit out only once you have a second store running and enough experience to do so without taking a personal financial hit. [L1215.025]

#### 90-10 rule for budget and time (Source A 2024)

- Follow the 90-10 rule monthly: allocate 90% of time and budget to proven, repeatable methods that drive revenue. Allocate 10% to experimental channels or strategies. If an experiment works, move it to the proven 90%; use the freed 10% for new tests. [L0253.015]

#### Paying yourself (older advice, 2021)

Procedure:
1. Calculate your personal monthly expenses. [L0801.150]
2. Pay yourself a fixed salary from the business account, for example 500 dollars per week, once the business is running. [L0801.150]
3. At the end of each month or quarter, check the net profit left in the business. [L0801.150]
4. Decide a distribution based on goals and the profit available, for example distributing 150,000 dollars at the end of a quarter when net profit passes 200,000 dollars. [L0801.150]
5. Keep some profit in the business and avoid drawing the entire balance. [L0801.150]

- Set distributions from goals, not from what is left in the account. Tie a quarterly or monthly distribution to a target net profit so you do not overdraw the business. [L0801.151]

#### Planning sheet (older advice, 2021-22)

- A two-tab spreadsheet works for planning: one tab holds the Profit First allocations from revenue, and the other holds the strategic planning with current team, staff pay, remaining budget, and max and target capacity. The lesson used a spreadsheet for this, and the owner should update it with real numbers. [L1334.025]

### Hiring thresholds tied to revenue (older advice, 2021-22)

- A new expense can be funded by raising revenue or by raising that expense's allocation percentage. This forces a check on whether the expense, such as a software tool or a hire, is necessary. [L1200.034]
- Tie each hire or large expense to a revenue threshold, so growth is paid for before it is committed. For example, a new staff member should be added only once real revenue reaches a set level that covers their cost. [L1200.035]
- Staff share benchmarks differ by source:
  - About 35% of real revenue: observed in one established dropshipping company that used this method. [L1200.037]
  - 30%: the figure used in the lesson's example. [L1200.037]
  - Use 35% or 30% only as a reference point. The right staff percentage depends on the business's actual payroll and should be set from its own numbers. [L1200.037]

### Reviewing metrics

- Every e-commerce store should have someone who asks each month what revenue can be reached next, comparing the latest month and the upcoming quarter, so growth opportunities are not missed. [L0463.005]
- Review the changelog regularly so past experiments stay available for comparison. [L0410.001]
- Compare each change against its logged baseline and expected result, using the 90-day trailing figure. [L1509.003, L1509.004]
- Review the monthly financial reports alongside the cash position. [L1046.045]

## Preparing a store for sale or shutdown

### Making a store sellable without the owner

- A buyer acquires a business, not a job. The store must run on its own without your daily involvement, so document all critical processes in standard operating procedures and remove yourself from essential functions. [L0231.010]
- Most buyers do not want a 40-hour-a-week job. Hire a team and step out of daily operations before selling. The team also shows which tasks still need documentation. [L0554.031]
- A store that runs without the seller, with documented SOPs, training documents, and processes, is worth more, because the buyer can take over the daily work without you. [L0554.030]
- Services that depend on the seller reduce valuation. A service tied to the product can add value if a team runs it, but some buyers dislike the extra complexity. [L0554.033]
- Portfolio investors want passive income, so virtual assistants (VAs) who run the site without the owner matter a lot to them. Buyers who want to tinker will prefer a more hands-on setup. [L1468.038]
- A store can be sold while it is still early. List it with its key details and either a price or a "best offer" note in a for-sale channel so buyers can make offers. [L0360.083]

### Documentation and SOPs

- Document all processes as SOPs before listing. Clear documentation lets a buyer take over with confidence. Missing documentation makes buyers hold back money or discount the price. [L1468.037]
- SOPs and a documented, trained team (for example VAs) raise a store's attractiveness, especially to newer buyers. They can decide between a completed sale and no sale. [L0553.020]
- Document critical processes in SOPs so the buyer can run them without you. [L0231.010]

### Building and handing over the team

**Procedure: prepare a store team for sale** [L0553.022]

1. Hire and train new VAs about 3 to 6 months before selling so they can run the operations.
2. Document SOPs.
3. Hand over the trained team and processes to the buyer as part of the sale. Do not try to train after the sale closes.

- Using VAs to run day-to-day operations makes a store more attractive, because the owner does not need to be involved. This raises buyer interest and can improve the multiple. [L0553.023]
- VAs usually transfer with the business. If they do not, you must train replacement hires before closing. Buyers will contractually require you to handle the handover and may hold back part of the payment until training is complete. [L0553.021]
- You can write a sale-linked bonus into each VA's contract: each gets 1% of the profit when a site is sold. This aligns the team with the long-term value of the business. [L1437.031]

**Case: owner-dependent production** [L1468.039]

A seller's wine-glass store made about $1,000 per month in net profit. The owner said it needed about two hours per week. However, the product was hand-made by a family member working 30 to 40 hours per week. This made the business dependent on one unpaid producer who might not transfer, so a buyer would discount it.

### Contracts with staff and suppliers

- Formal written contracts with VAs and suppliers are not required to sell a business. They are helpful because they define expectations and protect both parties during the transition. [L0231.026, L0231.030]
- Contracts with staff and suppliers are not required for a sale, but they add buyer confidence. A contract may be needed before a kickback arrangement with a supplier counts as profit. [L0554.032]

### Notifying suppliers and staff

- Tell your suppliers that you are selling. Clarify what terms the new owner expects, so they understand the changes before the handover. [L0231.019]
- Inform your staff of the pending sale as early as your circumstances allow. Most buyers retain existing employees, which eases continuity concerns. [L0231.020]

### Post-signing handover

- After the asset purchase agreement is signed, the broker's team can migrate the accounts and run the handover. The level of help depends on what the buyer and seller each want. [L0553.044]
- Some sellers prefer that the broker does not touch the accounts. Less experienced sellers are guided step by step. [L0553.044]
- Cross-border handovers, such as a buyer in another country who needs a local company, are handled case by case and can take months. [L0553.044]

### Valuation factors

- A store's valuation is based on profit and success. More suppliers, more revenue, and better profit mean a higher sale price. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.136]
- A buyer will not trust a P&L that is only typed into a spreadsheet. The seller must prove the figures with proper accounting records, so accounting must be upgraded well before an exit. The higher the expected sale price, the more important this proof becomes. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1516.007]
- Dropshipping businesses can be sold for six, seven, or even eight figures, so a buyer will expect audited, verifiable financial records before paying that kind of price. *(Older advice, 2021-22.)* [L1516.008]

### Portfolio buyers

- Portfolio buyers typically set up a separate LLC for each acquisition. This compartmentalizes liability and lets them manage tax reporting independently. [L0231.025]
- Portfolio buyers want stores that keep running without the seller. They often keep the existing team and systems for a while after purchase rather than shutting everything off at once. Continuity in the first months after the sale is part of what the buyer pays for. [L0554.056]

### Sale channels and brokers

- Store sale options depend on age and profit. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.135]

| Store profile | Route |
|---|---|
| Under one year old, modest net profit | Member marketplace listing [L0962.135] |
| Over one year old, significant net profit | Offer to a broker such as Empire Flippers [L0962.135] |

- Selling a store means transferring its ownership inside Shopify. The store can be sold with or without a full supplier set. *(Older advice, 2021.)* [L0962.137]

### Closing a store instead of selling

- If a store cannot be actively managed for a long period, such as 18 months, it is better to sell it and restart later than to let it sit idle. *(Older advice, 2019.)* [L1069.074]

**Procedure: shut down a store you no longer need** [L0804.102]

1. Export all products and data with Rewind backups or the product CSV export.
2. Stop paying for the store once the export is saved.
3. Contact any supplier you approved with, thank them, and explain that the store is closing.

## Other details

### Owner role and team growth

- *Older advice (2021-22):* Growing the team multiplies positive impact by improving team members' lives through meaningful work, enhancing customer service, and creating broader community benefit. [L0107.007]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Sustainable growth comes from repeatedly identifying and reducing weaknesses over time, not from a single fix. [L0443.007]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Assign someone on the team to monitor the online spaces your customers use. They are a steady source of pain points, desires and market research for your avatars. [L0907.018]
- Running a store passively through a virtual assistant is not permanent. The assistant may quit or stop answering, and competitors may add bundles or redesign their sites, so the store must keep being monitored and improved. [L0826.017]
- Case: a dropshipping store started in 2014 made its first sale within a few weeks of opening, by Christmas. [L1473.036]
  - It ran as a side business while the owner worked as a bookkeeper, and it helped pay off about 70,000 in debt built up with a husband from buying a house, in just under two years. [L1473.036]
  - After the owner quit the bookkeeping job, the store tripled its revenue in the first full-time year. [L1473.036]
  - The owner still worked about 50 hours a week on customer service, orders and fires, and only removed themselves from business operations in 2018, about four years after starting. [L1473.036]
  - The turning point was a pregnancy in 2017. The owner built the business system and found a virtual assistant within about three months. [L1473.036]
  - Training lasted two weeks, after which customer service and order management were handed over. The owner later could travel for months while the business ran, working on the business rather than in it. [L1473.036]
  - The owner later hired a second assistant and raised pay after one year. [L1473.036]

### Delegation and done-for-you services

- Done-for-you services are listed at the bottom of the members area page and can be booked at any time. [L1496.014]
  - Most of them carry an extra fee and are optional. [L1496.014]
  - They suit those who want faster progress or who dislike tasks such as website design, product uploads or market verification. [L1496.014]
- Done-for-you store building typically takes two to five business days, depending on team workload. Ask for the team's current turnaround before committing. [L0806.095]

### Working setup and tools

- Use a screen split or external monitor for supplier and product research so you do not switch between windows constantly, which saves time. [L0665.110]
- Do not open a normal chat or create a new Cowork task without first selecting the project. Work started outside the project does not get the project's files, instructions or memory. [L1506.013]
- Downloaded course files belong in one dedicated folder inside the project location. You can then drag them into a chat to install skills or to reference them. [L1506.014]

### Business identity and accounts

- Use the exact same email address for the Google Merchant Center account, Google Analytics, Google Ads and the other Google products. This lets Google link them and confirm domain ownership automatically. [L0728.001]
- Set the same time zone across all Google products so data shows consistently everywhere. [L0728.001]
- *Older advice (2021):* Use an existing store's customer support email, at the store's own domain, for business email. Avoid email from another business domain. [L0834.107]

### Store build and technical checks

- *Older advice (2021-22):* When implementing image optimization, start with the high-priority pages and products you want to rank most, then gradually work through lower-priority pages. This staged approach makes the task manageable without needing to optimize everything at once. [L0301.031]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Clicking through every link on a page by hand is too time consuming on pages with dozens of outgoing links. Use a link checker extension or outsource the scan instead. [L0332.022]
- Build single-product stores, add relatable products at the bottom of the page, and use upsells in the cart as a way to grow average order value. [L0577.064]

### Offers and average order value

- Quantity discounts (buy one, buy two, buy three) can outperform a complex bundle for a first test. [L0773.041]
  - They are simple to set up. [L0773.041]
  - They lift average order value without needing to pick related products. [L0773.041]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Consistency drives upsell results. Keep offering the upsells across all three channels every time, rather than trying once and stopping. [L1409.027]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Upsell action items: [L1409.029]
  1. Decide which on-site upsell positions to use (product page, cart page, post-purchase).
  2. If no post-purchase upsell exists yet, add one; keep existing product-page upsells and add later upsells in the sequence.
  3. Add an upsell email sequence for each core product from the planner list into your email system.
  4. Customize the email templates with your specific products.
  5. Pass the script and instructions to the customer service team and discuss the planner list with them, so they offer the related upsell when a customer calls about a core product.

### Product research and validation

- Find someone already achieving the results you want, then model their process instead of reinventing it. Starting from a proven model can compress years of trial and error into a short period. [L0523.044]
  - Test and improve the model only after it makes money. [L0523.044]
- Product review workflow used by the team: [L0530.027]
  1. Watch the TikTok video and judge whether it is good.
  2. Read the comments for buying intent.
  3. Check the seller's account for upload dates and posting consistency.
  4. Open the store on mobile and desktop and review structure, product page and payment options.
  5. Estimate cost and selling price.
  6. Score the product and decide whether to test it.
- Spending more does not beat a competitor's higher budget if your targeting is sharper. [L0664.066]
  - *Older advice (2020):* A focused store with a few thousand dollars a month can outperform a competitor spending tens of thousands by cutting weak products. [L0664.066]
- Roughly 80% of sales often come from about 20% of products. Focus effort on identifying and adding the few suppliers whose products drive most of the revenue. [L0835.125]
- Validation and profit timing:
  - A store that passes all validation tests can usually become profitable. [L0806.092]
  - How large it grows (hundreds of thousands, millions or more in annual sales) is learned over the first year or two. [L0806.092]
  - Profit does not appear in the first week or the first six months. [L0806.092]

### Competitor signals

- When a competitor switches off a large number of active ads, for example 22 to 30 ads after about three weeks of running, this can signal a stock problem around the holiday rather than a failed product. [L0694.014]
  - If the product meets your criteria, the wait for stock may be worth it. [L0694.014]

### Product range and rebranding

- Launch a new product regularly to give existing customers a reason to buy again. [L0790.083]
  - The target was one new product per month, though one per quarter may be enough in some niches. [L0790.083]
- Keep a stable store with the same products over time. A single winner can keep a business running, and the goal is to keep the store alive by reselling and upgrading the best product, not chasing one-off hits. [L1440.052]
- Rebrand a store with a mixed product line: [L0806.094]
  1. Remove the products that do not fit the target niche.
  2. Change the domain name and logo in Shopify.
  3. Keep the remaining products and rename the store to match the niche (for example a carport store).
  4. Keep the removed products only for a future second store if there are enough suppliers to justify it.

### Sub-niches and multi-niche stores

- *Older advice (2022):* Use the same workflow for multiple sub-niches. Build keyword silos for each sub-niche in one store rather than separate stores. [L0665.107]
  - One store is easier to rank with one keyword silo. [L0665.107]

### Launch sequence and growth

- *Older advice (2021):* Start paid traffic and suppliers right away instead of waiting to build content first. Make money from paid traffic, then reinvest that money into content and SEO. [L0801.158]
- *Older advice (2022):* A store can grow to seven-figure revenue if it stays focused on one niche, becomes a leading store there, and keeps scaling ad budgets. [L0803.074]
  - The main limit is how far the owner pushes, not the product. [L0803.074]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* A customer multiplier funnel consists of about six to seven main actions plus some smaller supporting actions. [L0482.004]
  - The main actions work best when they all run together, one after another, to move customers toward a second purchase or toward new customers. [L0482.004]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Follow-up is the practice of keeping prospects who visited but did not buy, and customers who already bought, engaged so they move toward a second or third purchase. [L1497.001]
  - Its value builds over time as traffic sources bring in many top- and middle-of-funnel visitors. [L1497.001]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* High-ticket stores need far fewer orders than low-ticket stores for the same profit. [L0771.052]
  - Five saunas a day can be fulfilled by one owner in a few hours. [L0771.052]
  - Equal profit from 40 USD items needs hundreds of orders and a team. [L0771.052]

### Copy, direct mail and product arguments

- *Older advice... no year given:* When one argument works for one buyer group, apply it to every group with the same need. For example, use it for all gas companies within several hundred miles, then for all stove makers within 500 miles. [L1369.107]
  - Expanding a proven argument to new segments is faster than inventing a new one. [L1369.107]
- Test changes to the product itself, such as the screening of coal, the cooking time of coke or the size of oven charges, to stay ahead of competitors. [L1369.109]
  - Improving the product keeps the argument for it strong over time. [L1369.109]
- Study proven direct mail and letter-writing references and apply their principles to your own mailings on a regular basis. [L1369.110]
  - A systematic study routine produces better results than relying on instinct alone. [L1369.110]

### Store updates and course materials

- A major update to the outsourcing and automation module was in preparation, replacing all existing trainings with new strategies and tools. [L0373.015]
  - Existing material still works. [L0373.015]
  - Users who want the newest tools should wait about one week before going through that module. [L0373.015]
- Store updates in the training are published in one place, so the member login always shows the latest version. [L1283.026]
  - Announce significant updates in the team announcement channel with a link to the changed lesson. [L1283.026]

### Owner income and reinvestment

- An online business can be scaled far beyond a salary because revenue is not tied to hours worked, and it can run from any location. [L0863.009]
  - This makes it a stronger base for reinvesting income into other assets than a fixed-salary job. [L0863.009]
- A large share of business income can be reinvested. The lesson cites 80% of earnings invested from 2013 until COVID. [L0863.011]
  - The reinvestment should be spread across diversified assets such as index funds and stable stocks, with only a small part in speculative assets. [L0863.011]

### Income beyond the own stores

- Monthly income for a freelancer who serves multiple dropshipping stores = monthly fee per client × number of clients. Example: 150 dollars × 10 clients = 1,500 dollars per month. [L0910.054]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* Skills gained from running your own store, such as paid traffic management, can be sold as a service to other store owners who will pay for them. [L1014.010]
  - Early client work of this kind can grow into a separate income stream alongside the own stores. [L1014.010]
- *Older advice (2021-22):* When the same questions and problems keep coming from clients, package the answers into a structured course or program instead of repeating one-on-one advice. [L1014.011]
  - Courses can deliver the same knowledge to more people in less time, and one-on-one coaching can continue alongside. [L1014.011]

### Personal environment and idea generation

- Being in a different environment or culture, even within your own country, shifts how your brain works and generates new ideas. Visit other places, meet people who do things differently, and bring back what you learn. [L1343.033]

### Case studies: store design and launch

- Case: a jewelry store was the sixth product tested after several earlier products without a winner, and it was launched when buyers wanted to show identity. [L1131.057]
  - Ads pointed to a collection page with about 20 designs of an African map necklace, priced at 30 with a buy-one-get-second-free offer, so two cost 30 instead of 60. [L1131.057]
  - A later collection of African country necklaces let buyers choose their country free with the map necklace. [L1131.057]
  - The store made about 60,000 in revenue within two months. [L1131.057]
  - The store was closed after two months because the operator lacked ads experience. Money went into unprofitable ads, the daily budget was raised from 5 to 100 dollars in one step, which got the ad account blocked, and negative comments were left unanswered, which led to the Facebook page being blocked. [L1131.057]
- Case: a student's store sold a mix of unrelated products, including hair wax, pet grooming gloves, men's jewelry, pet accessories, hats, car accessories and a bathroom apron. Its traffic came from a Facebook ad for a baby hammock sleeping bed. [L1346.034]
  - The homepage showed unrelated lifestyle photos. The product pages used default featured images and had no reviews, no urgency, no estimated delivery dates, no live chat link and no social media accounts. [L1346.034]
  - The reviewer judged the store to look like a burner store. [L1346.034]
  - Recommended changes: choose one product type, theme the site around it, replace the images, add a review system, scarcity counts, urgency offers, estimated delivery, a live chat link, tabbed product pages, a fuller footer and active social media accounts. [L1346.034]
  - The lesson gives no sales figures or results for the store. [L1346.034]


# 21. Phone sales

## Deciding whether phone sales belong in your store

### Price bands where calls matter

| Price level | What to expect | Source ids |
|---|---|---|
| Up to about $1,000 without phone capacity | Keep the average price in a lower range, around $1,000. This is older advice from 2019 and 2021. | L0356.010, L1112.071 |
| About $1,000 to $2,000 | Products generally convert with phone support, so have a team or staff ready to answer or return calls quickly. | L0667.073 |
| About $1,000 to $2,000 (listing) | High-ticket items above this range are worth listing, because a short phone call can close the sale. | L0934.108 |
| Above about $1,500 to $3,000 | Expect many inbound calls that check the business is legitimate before buyers order. | L0667.073 |
| Above roughly $2,000 | Many buyers call before ordering, so expect inbound sales calls. List these products and return calls quickly. | L1081.018, L0934.184 |

- The sources give different thresholds, so apply the one that matches your situation. The 2025 source puts conversion with phone support at $1,000 to $2,000 and expects heavy inbound calls above $1,500 to $3,000 [L0667.073]. The 2023 sources put the listing threshold at $1,000 to $2,000 [L0934.108] and at roughly $2,000 [L0934.184]. Older advice from 2019 and 2021 points to around $1,000 as the ceiling without phone support [L0356.010, L1112.071].
- Use the lower end of each range if you are unsure whether you can handle calls, and the higher end only when you have capacity to answer them [L0667.073, L0934.108, L0934.184].

### Phone as a trust signal

- A visible phone number tells customers they could call if needed, even when few customers actually call [L0359.105].
- Phone calls matter for trust even when few customers call, and the few who call usually buy [L0359.105].
- Keep a working phone number on the store and answer customer calls promptly, because phone responsiveness affects conversions for higher-priced items. This is older advice from 2020 [L0468.176].

### Inbound calls as a buying signal

- A phone call on the store is usually a buying signal, not a waste of time [L0910.007].
- Over about 2.5 years, more than 90 percent of calls either led to a sale or came from existing customers [L0910.007].
- Many shoppers call a store before buying, and those who get an answer tend to buy from that store [L0966.095].
- Answering the phone quickly and reliably is a competitive advantage [L0966.095].
- Answering the phone or returning calls generates significant sales volume that competitors miss. Customers are often surprised that a human answers and frequently place orders as a result. For established businesses, this represents millions in annual revenue [L0251.027].
- Phone calls before purchase are a normal part of selling products above about $1,500 to $3,000, because buyers check that the business is real [L0667.074].
- Calls decrease as the store builds reviews and credibility over time [L0667.074].

### Capacity you need before taking calls

- A store with high-priced products needs someone who can answer customer phone calls. Without that capacity, keep the average price in a lower range [L0356.010].
- For high-ticket products, the store owner should be willing to handle phone calls and extra emails, since that is part of how higher order values are closed [L0359.106].
- Only enter the $1,500 to $3,000 price range if you are willing to take these calls [L0667.074].
- Return calls from high-ticket buyers quickly [L0934.108, L0934.184].
- Respond to or call back high-ticket callers quickly [L0934.108].

### High-ticket offers and live selling

- Changing the selling environment is needed for high-ticket offers, because few people will buy a very expensive product from a sales letter alone [L0523.064].
- Move high-ticket offers to a phone call, direct mail or a live event [L0523.064].
- An 8,000 USD buy button is unlikely to be clicked from an email, while a booked phone appointment makes the sale far more likely [L0523.064].
- A phone conversation gives live feedback, so the salesperson can answer objections and help the prospect decide on the spot [L0523.065].
- Listeners pay closer attention to a voice than to a page [L0523.065].
- Use phone sales for offers that are too costly to close online [L0523.065].

### Decision: phone work or lower prices

1. Check whether you can answer and return calls quickly and reliably. If yes, you can consider products in the higher bands above $1,000 [L0667.073, L0966.095, L1112.071].
2. If you cannot, keep prices in the lower band around $1,000 and do not move into high-ticket niches [L0356.010, L1112.071].
3. If you want a hands-off business with no phone sales, do not pick niches with an average price above roughly $2,000 [L1081.018].
4. If you enter the $1,500 to $3,000 range, expect calls from buyers checking legitimacy and accept that they decline as reviews grow [L0667.073, L0667.074].

## Choosing a business phone number and provider

### Why a separate business line

- Business numbers signal professionalism to suppliers and customers and keep business calls apart from personal calls. [L0122.001, L0664.084]
- A dedicated business number receives less spam than a personal cell number, and business calls are easier to recognise and prioritise. [L0122.002]
- Use a business phone line and business address on the store, not personal details. A business line also allows a phone team to handle inbound and outbound calls. [L0852.111]
- Each store needs one phone number that belongs only to the business. Show it on the contact page or in the header. [L1092.088]

### Toll-free numbers

#### Prefixes and rules

| Country | Prefix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| US | 800, 888, 877, 866, 855, 844, 833 | Each prefix is assigned by a Responsible Organization (RespOrg) under FCC rules. [L1198.004] |
| Australia | 1300 | Equivalent of the US toll-free number. [L1198.003] |

- Toll-free numbers in the formats 800, 855 or 866 look more professional on store websites and work especially well for supplier-facing stores. [L0122.006]
- Older advice (2019) lists 888 or 855 for customer calls. A phone line may be a Google number or a toll-free number. [L0960.043] *(older advice, 2019)*
- For callers in the same country, a toll-free number is free. International callers pay charges. [L1198.003]
- The provider forwards calls to any mobile or landline you choose, so callers hear an ordinary phone call. [L1198.003]
- Toll-free numbers are portable. You can move one to a different provider without changing the number. [L1198.004]

#### Vanity numbers

- Do not pay extra for a memorable or vanity number if the number only appears on your website and in supplier emails. The digits after the prefix do not matter for this use, and a plain number with a toll-free prefix looks just as professional. [L1198.010]

### Providers

#### Mighty Call / MightyCall

- MightyCall is a business phone system for handling calls. [L0518.002]
- Entering the code `dropship50off` at checkout gives 50% off for the first 3 months. [L0518.002]
- Mighty Call provides a toll-free business number with an app that rings the owner's cell phone and transcribes voicemails. It suits a single business number shown in the site header or on the contact page. [L1092.087] *(source 2022)*
- If Mighty Call does not work in a country such as Australia, Google Voice is a workable alternative for a business phone line. [L1092.090] *(source 2022)*

#### Grasshopper

- Grasshopper (grasshopper.com) is a US option for toll-free and vanity numbers. It has desktop and mobile apps, call forwarding and voicemail transcription. [L1198.006]
- Pricing at the time of recording: plans from $26 per month for a business line, and up to $75 off an annual plan. [L1198.006]

**Setup steps**

1. Open grasshopper.com and click Try Free. [L1198.007]
2. Go to Types of Numbers and select Toll Free Numbers. [L1198.007]
3. Pick a random number or specify your digits, then choose a plan. [L1198.007]
4. Download the desktop and mobile apps. [L1198.007]
5. Configure your settings, which the setup guides you through. [L1198.007]
6. Place the number on your website and in supplier communication. [L1198.007]

#### Zintel

- For an Australian business number, Zintel (zintel.com.au) sells 1300 numbers for about $10 per month. [L1198.008]
- Sign-up takes under 5 minutes. There is no lock-in contract, and you can cancel at any time. [L1198.008]

#### JustCall

- JustCall costs about $20 per month and lets you buy numbers in over 70 countries. Calls are answered through desktop and mobile apps from anywhere. [L1198.009]
- Example: a US number can be answered from the UK or Thailand, which suits a business run from abroad. [L1198.009]
- At the time of recording the provider advertised 70% off the first month. [L1198.009]

#### Google Voice

- Google Voice is a workable business phone line where Mighty Call does not operate, for example in Australia. [L1092.090] *(source 2022)*
- Google numbers are an accepted option for a phone line. [L960.043] *(older advice, 2019)*

## Setting up the line: voicemail, greetings, hours and routing

### Routing calls by time of day

- The phone number is directed to different people at different times of the day, based on the business time zone. [L0404.004]

### Overflow to voicemail or personal phone

- Unanswered calls overflow automatically to voicemail or the owner's personal phone, so no manual switching is needed. [L0404.004]
- Staff must check voicemail regularly during their answering periods. [L0404.004]

### After-hours handling

- Outside advertised business hours, the phone line plays a prerecorded message and goes to voicemail. [L0404.005]
- Voicemail left after hours is checked in the next business period. [L0404.005]
- Alternatively, outside advertised business hours the call diverts to the owner's personal phone. [L0404.005]

### Staff answering rules

- Staff must always state their first name and the business name when answering a call. [L0404.005]

### Ringing several devices

- Google Voice can be installed on multiple phones logged into the same Google account so that calls ring on several devices. [L0971.073]

### Answering service

- Older advice (Source B, 2021-22): Most number providers offer an answering service. When a call is missed, it plays a pre-recorded greeting that names your business and asks for a message. The service then notifies you of the message by email or app so you can call back as soon as possible. [L1198.005]

### Voicemail transcripts

- Quo's automatic voicemail transcripts convert incoming messages to text, enabling faster responses to customer and supplier inquiries without listening to full recordings. [L0122.007]
- Example (Quo Starter plan): The Quo Starter plan includes voicemail transcripts, which turn each voicemail into text. A caller asking whether a product is in stock can be answered from the transcript later, so a sale is not lost while the owner is busy. [L0338.007]

### Recorded voicemail greeting

Current version (Source A, 2023):

```
Hello, you've reached [store name, e.g. storename.com]. Thanks for calling. Our team is currently away from the desk or helping other customers, so please record a voicemail including your name, email address, phone number, and the purpose of your call. We'll respond as soon as we're able.
```
[L0934.103]

Older version (Source A, 2021):

```
Thanks for reaching out to [store name]. Our team is either away from the phone or busy assisting another customer at the moment. Leave a voicemail stating your name, email address, and question, and we'll call back as quickly as we can. Alternatively, send us a message at [support email address].
```
[L1090.140]

### Missed-call text reply

```
Hi, this is {store_name}, and I'm sorry I missed your call. I'm helping other customers right now, so I'll reply by text or phone as soon as I can. If your call is urgent, you can reply to this message with your order number and a short note about what you need.

{your_name}
```
[L1472.068]

## Showing the number and using phone calls to action

### Why phone contact matters

- For expensive products, a phone-based call to action can convert better than the buy-now button for many buyers, because they want to speak to a sales or customer service person before committing. Test "Call today" with the phone number in the copy against the buy-now button. Keep the buy-now button as the default option. [L0461.014]
- Business buyers often want to call before they order, to confirm stock or negotiate a volume discount. If you sell B2B, put a phone number on your website. [L0769.006]
- Visitors who call before ordering are usually close to buying. Leaving the number off can lower conversion. [L1088.085]
- A visible phone number builds trust, and callers are often ready to buy. [L0960.042]
- Older advice (2019 to 2022): Source A (2019) recommends a phone number at any price point, including products with an average order value around $500. Source B (2021 to 2022) limits the rule to expensive products. Use both: for high-ticket products, show the number prominently; for lower-priced products, the number still builds trust, so it does no harm to include it. [L0960.042, L0461.014, L1371.038]

### Showing the number on the site

#### Header and contact page

- Show a business phone number in the website header with a "Call us today" heading. High-ticket buyers want to speak to someone, and Google Shopping and similar marketing channels require a visible phone number. [L1371.038]
- Keep the phone number on the website even if you cannot answer every call. [L0934.107]

#### Trade (B2B) page

- B2B buyers usually want to talk on the phone and ask for bulk pricing. Make a phone contact visible on the trade page. [L0961.016]

### Handling calls you cannot answer

Follow these steps when the store cannot answer every call:

1. Keep the phone number on the website. [L0934.107]
2. Set up a voicemail greeting that collects the caller's details. [L0934.107]
3. Return every missed phone call on the same day. [L0961.016]
4. Outsource phone support later, when the store earns enough to justify it. [L0934.107]

### Offering a choice of channels

- When customers can choose between writing, calling or visiting a store, the phone option is the one most people use. In one test, 70 percent of inquiries for a sample came by telephone. [L1261.052]
- Offer the phone option as a primary response channel, since people find it easier than writing. [L1261.052]

### Testing phone-based calls to action

| Element | Control | Test variant |
|---|---|---|
| Call to action | Buy-now button (default, stays) | "Call today" with phone number in the copy |
| Product type | Expensive products | Test first here [L0461.014] |

Run the test on expensive products first. Keep the buy-now button as the default option whatever the result. [L0461.014]

## Answering inbound calls

### Greeting and first contact

- Answer every inbound call with a person, not a machine. Do not use AI to answer sales calls. A person should answer, even if they do not know every product answer right away. [L0808.039]
- Use this phone greeting, adjusting the wording to match how formal your company is. Use the same structure for opening chats, and make sure the staff member knows the next question to ask after the greeting. [L1396.009]

```
Hello, thank you for calling [company name], this is [your name]. How can I help you today?
```
[L1396.009]

- Staff with little phone experience should practice this greeting until it feels natural. [L1396.009]

### Understanding what callers want

- Inbound callers usually want to confirm that the business is legitimate, or check whether a product is in stock before ordering. The phone line therefore also answers pre-purchase questions. [L0700.003]
- Most incoming calls concern stock or shipping times. The real question is usually whether the store can be trusted. [L0910.008]
- Most early calls to a store are simple checks, such as "is this a real business" or "is this product in stock". [L1092.089]
- Answers should reassure the caller that a real person will help if something goes wrong. [L0910.008]

### Building trust on the call

- A phone number builds trust, and calls often convert to sales. [L1092.089]
- Ask what the caller's specific concerns are first. [L0253.049]

Trust-concern script (Source A, 2024, older advice):

1. Ask what their specific concerns are.
2. Respond: "We are an authorized retailer for [Brand Name]. We have been since [year]."
3. Ask which product they're interested in.
4. Say: "Our website is hosted on Shopify. All of your payment information is completely secure."
5. Offer: "You can also purchase directly on our website without speaking to us if you prefer. Or, if you ever have questions, you can reach me directly at [your email]."
6. Your goal: build confidence by proving you are legitimate and authorized. Most callers are satisfied once someone picks up the phone.

[L0253.049]

### Answering questions about physical locations

- If a customer asks whether they can visit a store or pick up in person, answer as follows (Source A, 2022, older advice):

```
We do not have physical locations. We ship directly from our suppliers' warehouses to customers, and those warehouses are not open to the public.
```
[L0803.032]

### Handling missed calls and voicemail

- Calls to a store should always be answered by someone who can handle the common questions, because an unanswered call can mean a lost sale. [L0910.013]
- Check voicemail and return calls promptly. [L0910.013]

### Treating callers as real prospects

- Treat each inquiry as a real prospect of a salesperson, and give them the full story rather than cutting the conversation short. [L1261.054]
- A prospect who has already shown interest is worth more effort than a cold one. [L1261.054]

## Callbacks, unknown answers and call logging

### Promising accurate callbacks instead of guessing

- When you do not know a product detail, do not guess. Tell the customer you will check with the manufacturer team and call back with accurate data. [L0934.105]
- Answer unknown technical questions by promising a callback with accurate data, not by inventing an answer. This keeps trust and lets you collect the caller's contact details for follow-up. [L0934.185]
- A correct answer given hours later is better than an instant guess or no answer. Callers accept a follow-up within about 12 hours when they receive a correct answer. [L0808.041]

### Collecting caller details

Three phrasings for the moment you cannot answer at once. Each is a complete script from a different year.

Source A, 2026:

```
Thank you for calling [Company Name], this is [Your Name]. That is a great question, and I want to make sure I give you the correct answer. Could I get your name, phone number and email address? I will get back to you with the answer as soon as possible. [Optional: I will follow up by [email/text] within [timeframe].]
```

[L0808.040]

Source A, 2024:

```
Thank you for calling, that is a great question and I do not have the answer right now. Let me contact our supplier and confirm the answer with you, and I will get back to you as soon as possible. Can I have your name, phone number and email address, please?
```

[L0805.067]

Source A, 2023:

```
Good question, [customer name]. I don't know the answer at the moment, so I'll consult our team and return your call as quickly as possible. May I have your phone number and email address?
```

[L0934.104]

### Handling unknown product questions

Pre-sales product question, 2024 procedure (Source A):

1. Ask for the customer's name, phone number and email.
2. Tell them you will check and call them back.
3. Call the brand contact about the product detail.
4. Call the customer back with the answer.
5. Send the answer by email and add the new detail to the product page.

[L0971.042]

Phone first, email second: call suppliers for an answer and follow up by email only if they do not answer. [L0971.043]

Phone or chat question you cannot answer, 2020 procedure (Source A, *older advice*):

1. Take the caller's name and phone number or email address.
2. Tell them you don't know yet, but will find the answer and follow up as soon as possible.
3. Ask the supplier the question.
4. Add the answer to the website, so future visitors also see it.
5. Contact the lead with the answer and follow up for the sale.

[L1277.113]

Note: the 2020 version does not name a channel for asking the supplier. The 2024 version calls the brand contact first and uses email only as the fallback. [L0971.042, L0971.043, L1277.113]

### Stock questions

Stock question you are not sure about, 2022 procedure (Source A, *older advice*):

1. Tell them you need to confirm with the warehouse before answering.
2. Take their name and phone number and write them down, even if the call drops.
3. Check inventory through the weekly stock sheet, the dealer portal or by contacting the supplier.
4. Call the customer back with the answer as soon as possible.

[L1113.038]

### Evening and gap-time callbacks

*Older advice (Source B, 2021-22):*

- In most countries it is considered acceptable for businesses to call customers until about 8 p.m. Evening callbacks are therefore a practical option when daytime calls are not possible. [L0909.010]
- At the start you may only have about two or three callbacks to return each day. A single half-hour block in the evening is usually enough to clear them. [L0909.011]
- Short gaps such as lunch breaks, a few minutes away from work, or a commute can be used to make callbacks. Calling while commuting is possible even on public transport. [L0909.012]
- A callback in the evening often feels to the customer like extra attention, which can build trust and improve the chance of a sale. Unexpected out-of-hours service is a useful way to create a memorable experience. [L0909.013]

Callback timing at a glance:

| Option | When to use it | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Evening block, until about 8 p.m. | When daytime calls are not possible; about 2-3 callbacks a day at the start, one half-hour block | [L0909.010, L0909.011] |
| Gap time: lunch, short breaks, commute | To make short callbacks during the day | [L0909.012] |
| Within about 12 hours | After you have a correct answer for the caller | [L0808.041] |

### Logging unclosed calls

- Log every inbound sales call that does not close with the call date and a follow-up date. Many callers who promise to call back never do, so the follow-up must come from you. [L0949.030]
- A Google Sheet with columns for call date, emailed or not, and next follow-up date is enough to track early leads without a CRM. *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22).* [L0949.032]

### Daily follow-up review

- Review the follow-up list every morning, either yourself or through a team member, and contact each lead on its scheduled date. This recovers many leads that would otherwise be lost. *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22).* [L0949.031]
- Check the sheet daily to see who needs a reply. *Older advice (Source B, 2021-22).* [L0949.032]
- When a prospect calls in response to an offer, they have already been persuaded enough to take action, so follow up the inquiry quickly while interest is fresh. Delay and forgetting reduce the value of each inquiry. (Source C) [L1261.053]

### Feeding answers back into product pages

- Use the answers you learn from customer calls to update the product pages on your store, so future visitors get the information without calling. [L0934.106]
- Add the new detail to the product page as the last step of the 2024 procedure. [L0971.042]
- Add the answer to the website as step 4 of the 2020 procedure, so future visitors also see it. *Older advice (Source A, 2020).* [L1277.113]

## Selling high-ticket and B2B buyers by phone

### Qualifying high-ticket buyers

- Use this sequence on a qualified lead call for products with an average order value of $5,000 or more [L0268.044, L0268.071]:
  1. Ask why they want the product, where it will go, when they need it, and what they will use it for [L0268.044, L0268.071].
  2. Decide whether they are a real buyer by checking for a confirmed need and a real timeline [L0268.044, L0268.071].
  3. Offer service enhancements such as expedited delivery or white glove delivery instead of discounts [L0268.044, L0268.071].
  4. Show that you want to earn the business through service, not price cuts [L0268.044, L0268.071].
  5. If call volume becomes unmanageable, hire a VA to handle calls [L0268.044].
- Expect more pre-sale questions and inbound calls for high-ticket items, such as those priced at $10,000 and above or at $1,000 to $2,000. These products can still be sold, but expect more contact before the sale [L0808.043].
- Before pitching a high-ticket B2B lead, qualify in this order [L1315.063]:

  | Step | Question | Purpose |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | Who holds the authority over the budget? | Identify the economic buyer |
  | 2 | What is the need the buyer is trying to meet? | Establish the need |
  | 3 | Where are they now? | Establish the current state |
  | 4 | Where do they want to be? | Establish the target state |
  | 5 | What is the impact of not reaching that goal? | Establish urgency and cost of inaction |

### Avoiding discount tactics

- Do not use loss-leader pricing or a discount-focused strategy for products of $5,000 or more [L0268.084].
- Discounts signal desperation to customers with serious buying intent [L0268.084].
- Focus on service enhancements such as white glove delivery and expedited shipping [L0268.084, L0268.044].
- Verify genuine customer need and timeline, and show business credibility [L0268.084].
- Price questions from buyers often close the sale, but this requires constant commitment and fast responses. Older advice from 2019 (Source A) states that high-ticket products of about $5,000 and above can sell well when someone answers live chat and the phone quickly and responsively [L1110.031].

### Phone as a sales channel

- Selling by voice on the phone is an effective way to close high-ticket sales. The chance of a sale rises significantly when customers can speak to the business [L1371.039].
- Plan staff capacity for phone sales before entering the high-ticket or bulk segment. Calls will reveal product questions that you can then answer on the website [L1277.114].

### Concierge-style selling

- High-ticket buyers are often over 50 and sometimes in their 60s or 70s. They value personal attention and clear answers to their questions. A concierge-style approach works best with this group [L1472.044].
- Concierge-style phone sale for an expensive product [L1472.046]:
  1. Answer every question the buyer has about the product, and pay attention to their specific needs [L1472.046].
  2. Create a draft order in your system and send it to the customer, so they can pay without going through the normal checkout for the first order [L1472.046, L1472.047].
  3. For repeat orders, keep the conversation going by email, text or voice memos, and send another draft order when they are ready [L1472.046, L1472.065].
  4. Keep the buyer updated on any back-order delays until the product arrives [L1472.046].
- A personal concierge approach can turn a single high-ticket buyer into a steady source of revenue over time. Draft orders avoid friction in checkout for buyers who prefer a personal sale [L1472.047].

#### Case: concierge sale with draft orders

- A store sold products priced between $2,000 and $9,000, with the most expensive variant at $9,000 [L1472.048].
- One buyer called with many questions about her purchase. The store answered each one attentively and sent a draft order, so she did not have to go through checkout for the first order [L1472.048].
- Two months later she placed a second order after only a few emails of prior contact, with no draft order needed. Over those two months she brought in about $13,000 in sales [L1472.048].
- A separate $9,000 order was back-ordered for three months. The store kept her updated on the status until it was delivered [L1472.048].

### Multi-person B2B buying

- High-ticket B2B purchases involve several people [L1315.064]:

  | Role | Description |
  |---|---|
  | Economic buyer | Controls the money |
  | Lead decision maker or product owner | Leads the decision on the product |
  | Functional buyers | For example, head of purchasing |

- Get in front of the key decision maker and build relationships with the others [L1315.064].
- Expect the buyer to need strong proof and security for the purchase [L1315.064].

### Long sales cycles

- High-ticket products can require around 20 touch points before purchase. Expect a long sales cycle and plan a sequence of follow-ups rather than expecting a sale after one contact [L0949.033].

### Direct mobile numbers and repeat business

- Giving a high-value buyer your direct mobile number can turn a one-time purchase into repeat business. The buyer may later text or send voice messages to request a new draft order [L1472.065].
- Accept the channel the buyer prefers, including voice memos, and respond reliably [L1472.065].

## Taking orders over the phone

### Staff authorisation and payment limits

- Staff are authorised to take customer orders over the phone and place them on the website for the customer. [L0404.003]
- Phone orders are limited to credit card or bank deposit payment. [L0404.003, L0404.002]

| Rule | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Who takes phone orders | Staff | L0404.003 |
| Payment methods allowed | Credit card or bank deposit | L0404.003, L0404.002 |

### When phone sales matter

- Older advice (2021): most sales come through the website rather than the phone. [L0834.094]
- Older advice (2021): phone calls are typically used to close bulk orders, for example 10 items for an office. A discount is offered, and the sale is then placed over the phone. [L0834.094]

### Taking the call

1. Answer the customer's product or stock question. [L1283.062]
2. If they want to buy, add the item to cart in the store. [L1283.062]
3. Collect the customer's name, shipping address, billing address and payment method. [L1283.062]
4. Enter the details as if the customer were checking out, using their email. [L1283.062]
5. Process and follow up the order like any other online order. [L1283.062]

The sources also give a fuller version of the call:

1. Ask the customer what they would like to buy. [L0404.002]
2. Open the website, put those products in the cart, then go to checkout. [L0404.002]
3. Collect the customer's contact details with them: name, email address, delivery address and phone number. [L0404.002]
4. Move on to the payment page and ask which payment method they prefer. Phone orders can be settled by credit card or by bank deposit. [L0404.002]
5. If the customer is paying by credit card, ask for the card numbers, type them into the checkout page, then click finish to complete the purchase. [L0404.002]

### Routes for entering the order

The sources describe two routes. Phone quotes are sent as draft orders, and direct orders are entered through normal checkout. [L1000.043, L0470.044, L1283.063]

#### Normal checkout

- Take phone orders by entering them through the normal online checkout, asking the customer for the same information as on the site. No separate POS system is needed for this. [L0470.044]
- A phone-only order can be placed through the normal checkout in the back end, so the order record matches a customer-placed web order. [L1283.063]

#### Shopify draft orders

Creating an order for a customer by phone in Shopify:

1. Click "Create order" in the Orders section, which creates a draft order. [L1302.009]
2. Add the products the customer wants. [L1302.009]
3. Apply any discounts. [L1302.009]
4. Send the customer a link so they can complete checkout themselves. [L1302.009]

### Channel attribution

- Phone quotes are sent to customers as draft orders in Shopify. [L1000.043]
- When the customer buys from a draft order, the sale is attributed to the phone channel, not to the online store, Facebook or Pinterest. [L1000.043]
- Because of this attribution, the phone sales commission can be tracked by channel. [L1000.043]

| Sale placed via | Attributed channel | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Shopify draft order bought by the customer | Phone | L1000.043 |
| Online store, Facebook, Pinterest | Their own channel | L1000.043 |

### Referral questions

- Ask about referrals only if they are part of the sales workflow. [L1283.063]
- Referral status does not change the process. [L1283.063]

## Quotes and quote follow-up

### Handling quote requests

A call within three minutes of the form submission creates a strong impression, and the speed and personalisation set you apart from slower competitors. [L0284.012]

Use this opening script as an example:

```
Hi, this is [name] from [company]. I saw your request for [specific need-e.g., playground setup]. We're working on a quote and will follow up later today. Let me confirm your contact details.
```

[L0284.012]

For high-value custom orders, follow this call sequence:

1. Introduce yourself and your company source.
2. Acknowledge the specific need they requested, showing you reviewed their submission.
3. Confirm the action you are taking on their behalf.
4. Verify contact information for follow-up.
5. Express enthusiasm about working together.

This builds credibility, separates you from generic outreach, and increases conversion on B2B and custom product quotes. [L0284.013]

B2B prospects often submit requests to several vendors at once to compare pricing. Set up Zapier to send immediate Slack alerts when Wufoo or Typeform quote requests arrive, then call the prospect within minutes. The first vendor to respond with a qualified quote typically wins the order. [L0286.040]

### Product-specific questions before quoting

Before quoting or selling certain products, ask for the details that the product category requires, not a generic set. Examples include:

- whether the customer has space to install the item,
- a photo of that space,
- the customer's zip code,
- any regulation that applies to the product.

Keep a separate question list for each product category or brand so staff do not need to remember them. [L1396.071]

### Quote task cards (older advice, Source B 2021-22)

When a call or chat asks for a quote, handle the pending task as follows:

1. Create a card with the customer name and the item, both together, so cards are easy to find.
2. Record the contact information, the product, any shipping needs such as inside delivery or installation, and the shipping address.
3. Send the request to the manufacturer.
4. When the manufacturer replies, move the card to Quote Received and note the extra cost, for example that inside delivery costs $100.
5. Send the customer the quote, move the card to Quote Sent, and attach a screenshot or copy of the invoice or email.

[L1396.021]

Creating several cards for the same item made it hard to see which customer each card belonged to. Always record both the customer name and the item name in the card title. Without this, staff must open each card to find the right customer. [L1396.022]

### Follow-up sequence after every quote (older advice, Source B 2021-22)

Run this sequence after every quote, with a due date set on each step:

| When | Action | Units |
|---|---|---|
| Next day | Check that the customer received the quote email. | L1396.024 |
| After 3 days | Send the warranty information for the product. | L1396.024 |
| After 1 week | Send a message explaining why to buy from you, such as financing, price matching and other benefits. | L1396.024 |
| After 1 month | Offer a free consultation with an expert to check whether the product fits the customer's needs. | L1396.024 |

Give each follow-up message a real benefit, such as warranty details, reasons to buy, or a free expert consultation, instead of only asking whether the customer has decided. Many quotes stay open because the customer is missing information or budget options, so each new message should add value to the conversation. [L1396.029]

### Follow-up email templates (older advice, Source B 2021-22)

**Day after the quote.** Adjust the wording as needed:

```
Hi [customer's title and last name], this is [your name] from [company name]. I wanted to check whether you got the quote request you made for [item name]. If there is anything else we can help you with, just let us know. Best regards, [your name].
```

[L1396.025]

**Three days after the quote.** Send this so the customer receives useful information rather than just a request for a reply:

```
Hi [customer's title and last name], we are attaching the warranty details for your [product name]. You will find them [attached or listed below]. If there is anything further we can do for you, please tell us. Best regards, [your name].
```

Change the warranty details to match each product or brand. [L1396.026]

**One week after the quote.** Use this to outline why buying from your company makes sense:

```
Hello [customer name], this is [your name] from [company name]. Many customers pick us for [product name] for these reasons: [list your financing options, price match policy, support, and other advantages]. Let us know if there is anything else we can assist with. Warm regards, [your name].
```

[L1396.027]

**One month after the quote.** Use this to offer help rather than pressure:

```
Hi [customer name], this is [your name] from [company name]. Would you like a consultation with an expert to see whether [product name] fits your needs? If you prefer a lower-priced option that fits your budget, we can also look at alternatives with you. Kind regards, [your name].
```

[L1396.028]

### Recovering open quotes (older advice, Source B 2021-22)
